translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This is an invocation that begins an act by seeking Allah’s blessing and help, while affirming trust in His all-encompassing compassion and mercy.

translation: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: Every form of perfect praise and gratitude is due to Allah alone, for He is the Creator, Sustainer, and Master of every realm and all that exists.

translation: The Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah’s relationship with creation is founded upon vast, encompassing compassion and continual mercy, which He bestows and sustains according to His wisdom.

translation: Master of the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: God alone possesses absolute authority and judgment over the Day of Resurrection, when every person will be held fully accountable for their deeds and receive the outcome they deserve.

translation: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
interpretation: This is a declaration of sincere devotion to Allah: worship is directed exclusively to Him, and reliance for every need is placed upon Him alone. It combines the servant’s commitment to obey Allah with recognition that no strength to worship or face life’s trials exists except through His aid.

translation: Guide us to the straight path.
interpretation: This is a supplication asking Allah to grant us clear knowledge of the truth, steadfastness in following it, and protection from ways that lead away from His guidance.

translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed Your blessings—not those who have incurred wrath, nor those who have gone astray.
interpretation: This is a prayer to be guided along the way of those who faithfully received and lived by God’s favor, while being protected from knowingly rejecting the truth or losing the right path through ignorance and error.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’an’s mysterious opening letters; their ultimate meaning is known to Allah, while their presence points to the divine nature of the Qur’an, composed from the very letters known to human speech yet beyond human imitation.

translation: This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-conscious.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as wholly true and free from uncertainty in its divine origin and message. Yet its guidance is most fully received by those who are mindful of God, sincerely seek truth, and are willing to live according to it.

translation: Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: True faith is not merely an inward claim: it is trust in realities beyond human perception, expressed through steadfast prayer and generosity from the blessings God has entrusted to a person. Thus, the believer combines devotion to God with compassionate responsibility toward others.

translation: And those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and who have certainty in the Hereafter.
interpretation: They are distinguished by accepting the revelation given to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ together with the authentic revelations granted to earlier prophets, recognizing their shared divine source, and by possessing firm conviction that life does not end with death but culminates in resurrection, judgment, and the lasting consequences of one’s deeds.

translation: Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.
interpretation: True success belongs to those who follow the guidance granted by their Lord, for it directs them to what is right and leads them to lasting well-being.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
interpretation: This describes people whose persistent rejection and inward resistance have become so entrenched that admonition no longer benefits them; their refusal is not due to a lack of guidance, but to their deliberate unwillingness to accept it.

translation: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a veil; and for them is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: Because they persistently reject the truth and refuse to respond to guidance, their hearts and hearing become closed to it, while the veil over their sight signifies their inability to perceive its signs clearly; this deliberate spiritual blindness leads to severe punishment.

translation: Among the people are those who say, “We believe in Allah and the Last Day,” yet they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the contradiction of those who profess faith outwardly while denying it inwardly. True belief is not merely a claim on the tongue; it must be sincere in the heart and reflected in one’s conduct before Allah.

translation: They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves, though they do not perceive it.
interpretation: The hypocrites outwardly claim faith while concealing disbelief, imagining that their words and conduct can conceal their reality from Allah and mislead the believers. In truth, Allah is never deceived; their deception only harms themselves by deepening their hypocrisy and leading them toward its consequences, even though they remain unaware of their self-deception.

translation: In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.
interpretation: Their inner corruption—such as doubt, hypocrisy, and refusal of the truth—grew worse because they persisted in falsehood and deceit, leading them to a painful punishment.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Do not spread corruption in the land,” they say, “We are only reformers.”
interpretation: This exposes the self-deception of those who cause harm while presenting themselves as agents of good. Their claim of reform does not change the reality of their actions; genuine reform is measured by obedience to God and the resulting justice and well-being, not by self-proclaimed intentions.

translation: Indeed, they are the corrupters, but they do not realize it.
interpretation: Those who cause corruption while believing themselves to be reformers are deceived about their own actions and remain unaware of the harm they spread.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Believe as the people have believed,” they say, “Should we believe as the foolish have believed?” Indeed, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who reject sincere faith while mocking the believers as intellectually inferior. In reality, true foolishness lies in allowing pride and prejudice to prevent one from recognizing and following the truth; yet their self-deception keeps them unaware of their own condition.

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, “We believe”; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, “Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who present themselves as believers for worldly advantage while privately aligning with the forces opposed to faith. Their claim that they were merely mocking reveals their contempt for believers and the self-deception underlying their duplicity.

translation: Allah repays their mockery and leaves them to persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This means that Allah responds to their hypocrisy and mockery by allowing them to continue in their rebellion and confusion, so their deliberate rejection becomes a cause of further misguidance and eventual punishment.

translation: Those are the ones who have traded guidance for misguidance; their trade has brought them no profit, nor were they rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse portrays those who knowingly abandon divine guidance as merchants making a ruinous exchange: they choose error in place of truth, gaining nothing in return and losing the ability to reach the right path.

translation: Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire; then, when it illuminated all around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, unable to see.
interpretation: This portrays those who outwardly approach guidance but inwardly reject it: they may briefly experience the clarity and security of faith, yet through their insincerity and persistence in denial, they lose that light and become spiritually unable to recognize or follow the truth.

translation: They are deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will not return.
interpretation: This describes people who have rejected guidance: although they possess the faculties to hear, speak, and see, they use them neither to receive truth nor to express or follow it, and therefore remain unable to return to the right path.

translation: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, within it are darknesses, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, fearing death; and Allah encompasses the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a parable for those who confront divine revelation with inner rejection: its warnings and proofs overwhelm them like darkness, thunder, and lightning, so they try to shut themselves off from what exposes their disbelief. Yet their avoidance cannot protect them, for Allah fully surrounds them with His knowledge and power.

translation: The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Whenever it lights their way, they walk in it; but when darkness falls upon them, they stand still. Had Allah willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: This portrays the hesitant condition of those who encounter divine guidance without truly embracing it: they advance when its benefits are clear and convenient, but halt when faith demands patience, sacrifice, or steadfastness. The warning that Allah could remove their hearing and sight emphasizes that their ability to perceive and respond is a mercy, not something they may take for granted, while affirming His absolute power over them.

translation: O people, worship your Lord who created you and those before you, so that you may become mindful of Him.
interpretation: This verse calls all humanity to worship Allah alone, grounding that command in His role as the Creator of every generation. Recognizing that existence is entirely dependent on Him should lead a person to devotion, obedience, and awareness of accountability before Him; through such God-consciousness, one is protected from wrongdoing and guided toward righteousness.

translation: He is the One who made the earth a resting place for you, the sky a canopy, and sent down water from the sky, bringing forth fruits as provision for you. So do not set up equals to Allah while you know.
interpretation: Allah reminds you that every essential means of life—the earth you inhabit, the sky that shelters you, the rain that revives the land, and the food it produces—comes from Him alone. Since His sustaining power is evident and none shares in it, worship and devotion must be directed exclusively to Him, without attributing partners or rivals to Him.

translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it and call upon your witnesses besides Allah, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse presents the Qur’an as a divine revelation and challenges those who doubt it to produce even one chapter comparable to it, while summoning any supporters or authorities they can rely on besides Allah. The challenge exposes the inability of human beings to replicate its distinctive combination of meaning, eloquence, guidance, and spiritual power, thereby affirming that it was revealed to the Prophet by Allah rather than authored by a human being.

translation: But if you do not—and you will never be able to—then guard yourselves against the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: Since those who reject the Qur’an cannot meet its challenge, they are warned that persistent disbelief has a grave consequence: the Hellfire prepared for them, whose terrifying fuel signifies the severity and inescapability of its punishment.

translation: And give glad tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with fruit from them as sustenance, they will say, “This is what we were provided with before,” though it is given to them in resembling forms. And they will have purified spouses therein, and they will remain there forever.
interpretation: This verse promises that genuine faith expressed through righteous action leads to a complete and everlasting life in Paradise: its blessings are continually renewed yet familiar in their goodness, its relationships are free from every impurity and harm, and its joy is secured by eternal permanence.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not refrain from presenting an example—even that of a mosquito or something above it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. But those who disbelieve say, “What does Allah intend by this example?” Through it He leads many astray and guides many; yet He leads astray through it only the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: Allah’s wisdom is not measured by the apparent smallness or greatness of an example. Even a mosquito can reveal a profound truth when considered with humility. The parable becomes a means of guidance for those who sincerely seek the truth, while the same sign exposes the arrogance and rebellion of those who reject it; thus misguidance is attributed only to those who persist in disobedience.

translation: Those who break Allah’s covenant after affirming it, sever what Allah has commanded to be maintained, and spread corruption on the earth—it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse portrays true loss as the consequence of knowingly abandoning one’s obligations to Allah, breaking sacred commitments, cutting off relationships and responsibilities that should be upheld, and causing harm in the world. Such actions destroy a person’s moral and spiritual well-being, even if they appear to bring worldly advantage.

translation: How can you deny Allah when you were lifeless and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again, and then to Him you will be returned?
interpretation: The verse rebukes disbelief by directing attention to the unmistakable stages of human existence: nonexistence or lifelessness, worldly life, death, resurrection, and return to Allah for judgment. The One who brought you into being and has power over life and death is therefore fully deserving of worship and obedience, and resurrection is not beyond His power.

translation: He is the One who created for you everything on the earth; then He turned to the heaven and fashioned them into seven heavens. And He has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah created the earth and all that it contains for human benefit, then ordered and perfected the heavens in their multiple levels. His complete knowledge encompasses every part of creation, showing that its existence and arrangement are the result of deliberate wisdom and perfect power.

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, “Indeed, I am placing upon the earth a successive authority.” They said, “Will You place upon it one who will spread corruption there and shed blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You?” He said, “Indeed, I know what you do not know.”
interpretation: The verse reveals that humanity has been entrusted with a role of stewardship on earth, carrying the responsibility to establish justice and obedience to God despite the capacity for corruption and violence. The angels’ question reflects their awareness of humanity’s destructive potential, while God’s response teaches that His wisdom encompasses purposes and qualities beyond what creation can perceive, including the capacity of human beings to learn, choose righteousness, and fulfill a divinely intended trust.

translation: And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He presented them to the angels and said, “Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: This verse signifies that God granted Adam a distinctive capacity for knowledge, understanding, and expression. By teaching him the names, God demonstrated the human potential to comprehend and classify creation, while showing the angels that their knowledge is limited to what God has taught them. The challenge calls them to recognize that true merit lies not in assumption or status, but in knowledge granted by God.

translation: They said, “Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You alone are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: This is an expression of complete humility before God: the angels acknowledge that their knowledge is limited and entirely dependent on His teaching, while His knowledge is absolute and His wisdom governs all that He reveals and decrees.

translation: قال الله: «يا آدم، أخبرهم بأسمائهم». فلما أخبرهم بأسمائهم قال: «ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض، وأعلم ما تُبدون وما كنتم تكتمون؟»
interpretation: يبين الله بهذا أن علمه محيط بكل ما غاب في السماوات والأرض، وبكل ما يظهره الخلق وما يخفونه في نفوسهم. وقد أظهر لملائكته فضل آدم فيما علّمه إياه، ليتبين أن الحكمة الإلهية في استخلافه قائمة على علم شامل لا يحيطون به.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they all prostrated except Iblis; he refused, acted arrogantly, and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that obedience to God requires humility and submission, whereas pride can lead a being to reject divine command even after recognizing it. Iblis’s refusal was not due to ignorance, but to arrogant self-preference, which placed him among the disbelievers.

translation: And We said, “O Adam, dwell—you and your wife—in Paradise, and eat freely from it wherever you both wish. But do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: This verse portrays God’s generous provision for Adam and his wife, granting them unrestricted enjoyment of Paradise while setting one clear boundary as a test of obedience. The prohibition of even approaching the tree emphasizes that faithfulness sometimes requires avoiding not only the forbidden act itself but also the paths that lead toward it. Violating God’s command is described as ظلم because it wrongs the soul by placing it outside the bounds of guidance and obedience.

translation: Then Satan caused them both to slip from it and drove them out of the state in which they had been. And We said, “Go down, some of you enemies to others; and on earth you will have a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time.”
interpretation: The verse portrays humanity’s departure from the original state of security through Satan’s deception and disobedience, while establishing earthly life as a temporary arena in which human beings must contend with one another and live under moral responsibility until their return to God.

translation: Then Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the One who repeatedly accepts repentance, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: After Adam’s lapse, God taught him words of sincere repentance and turned toward him with forgiveness. The verse shows that repentance is a divine gift and that whoever returns to God honestly will find Him ever-willing to forgive and encompass with mercy.

translation: We said, “Go down from it, all of you. Then, whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.”
interpretation: Human life on earth is accompanied by divine guidance; whoever sincerely follows it is granted inner security, protected from fear concerning what lies ahead and grief over what has passed, even while facing the trials of worldly life.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and reject Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This warns that knowingly rejecting faith and denying the clear signs of God leads to the enduring punishment of Hell, where such people will have no end to their stay.

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you, fulfill My covenant, and I will fulfill your covenant; and fear Me alone.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of His favors and calls them to honor the covenant by obeying Him and remaining faithful to His guidance. In return, He promises to fulfill what He has pledged to them, so their deepest reverence and awe must be directed to Him alone.

translation: And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what you already possess; do not be the first to disbelieve in it, and do not trade My signs for a small price. And be mindful of Me alone.
interpretation: This verse calls the People of the Book to recognize the Qur’an as confirming the truth that remains in their revealed scripture, and warns them not to reject it out of pride, rivalry, or fear of losing worldly authority and benefit. Divine guidance must not be concealed or exchanged for temporary worldly gain; true reverence is shown by obeying God and giving His truth precedence over every other concern.

translation: Do not mix the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know it.
interpretation: This is a warning against deliberately distorting what is true by blending it with falsehood or withholding it for personal gain, status, or fear. Knowing the truth creates a responsibility to present it honestly and not mislead others through concealment or manipulation.

translation: Establish the prayer, give the zakat, and bow with those who bow.
interpretation: This commands believers to uphold prayer faithfully, fulfill their duty of giving zakat, and join the community of worshippers in humble obedience to God, emphasizing both personal devotion and shared acts of worship.

translation: Do you enjoin righteousness upon others while forgetting yourselves, even though you recite the Scripture? Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who call others to goodness while neglecting to practice it themselves. True guidance requires sincerity and personal obedience; knowledge of revelation increases a person’s responsibility to live by what they teach, and abandoning that duty is a sign of heedlessness.

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is burdensome except for the humble—
interpretation: When facing hardship or obeying God, a person should rely on steadfast patience and sincere prayer. These practices may feel difficult to one distracted by worldly concerns, but they become a source of strength and obedience for those whose hearts are humbled before God.

translation: Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return.
interpretation: They are mindful of standing before Allah and returning to Him for judgment, so this certainty gives them the humility, patience, and devotion needed to remain obedient to Him.

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you, and that I favored you above all peoples.
interpretation: Allah commands the Children of Israel to recall His abundant blessings and recognize that their distinction came from His grace, especially through the prophets, revelation, and covenant He granted them; this favor required them to remain faithful and obedient, not to take pride in lineage alone.

translation: And beware of a Day when no soul will avail another in the slightest; no intercession will be accepted from it, no ransom will be taken from it, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This warns that on the Day of Judgment each person will face the consequences of their own deeds. Family ties, influence, pleas, or wealth will not save anyone from divine judgment; true security therefore lies in faith, obedience, and righteous action before that Day arrives.

translation: And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. In that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Children of Israel that their deliverance from Pharaoh’s brutal oppression was a profound divine favor, while the suffering they endured was a severe test of faith and steadfastness. It also exposes the cruelty of tyranny, which sought to destroy their future by killing their sons and humiliating their women.

translation: And when We parted the sea for you, saving you and drowning the people of Pharaoh while you watched.
interpretation: This verse recalls God’s decisive rescue of the Children of Israel: He opened a path through the sea for them, while Pharaoh’s tyranny and pursuit ended in destruction before their very eyes. It teaches that divine deliverance can come through what appears impossible, and that witnessing God’s power should lead people to gratitude, faith, and freedom from oppression.

translation: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلةً، ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون.
interpretation: يذكّر الله بني إسرائيل بميثاقه مع موسى حين واعده لمناجاته أربعين ليلة، ثم يبيّن انحرافهم بعد غيابه باتخاذ العجل معبودًا، وأن هذا الفعل كان ظلمًا عظيمًا لأنه شرك بالله ونقض للعهد بعد ظهور آيات التوحيد.

translation: Then We pardoned you after that, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: Despite your grave wrongdoing, Allah restored His mercy to you, giving you an opportunity to recognize His forgiveness and express gratitude through sincere faith and obedience.

translation: And when We gave Moses the Scripture and the criterion, so that you might be guided.
interpretation: God reminds the Children of Israel that the revelation given to Moses was both a source of divine instruction and a clear criterion distinguishing truth from falsehood, so that they could follow the path of guidance rather than their own desires.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf as an object of worship. So turn in repentance to your Creator and put yourselves to death. That is better for you in the sight of your Creator.” Then He accepted your repentance. Surely He is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Moses commanded the Israelites to repent sincerely from their worship of the calf, and “put yourselves to death” refers to the severe expiation prescribed for those involved—those who had not participated were to execute the guilty among them. This demonstrates the gravity of associating partners with God, while God’s acceptance of their repentance reveals that His mercy remains open even after a grave sin when repentance is genuine.

translation: And when you said, “O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah plainly,” the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the Israelites for demanding to see Allah physically as a condition of faith, revealing their stubbornness and lack of proper reverence. The thunderbolt that struck them was a warning that the unseen cannot be subjected to human demands, and that faith requires trusting Allah’s revelation rather than insisting on direct sensory proof of His essence.

translation: Then We brought you back to life after your death, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: After the Israelites were struck down, Allah restored them as an act of mercy, giving them another opportunity to recognize His power and respond with sincere gratitude and obedience.

translation: وأظلَلْنا عليكم الغمام، وأنزلنا عليكم المنَّ والسلوى؛ كُلوا من طيِّبات ما رزقناكم، وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون.
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن الله أحاط بني إسرائيل برعايته، فوفّر لهم الظلّ والطعام الطيّب دون استحقاقٍ منهم، ثم وجّههم إلى الانتفاع بنعمه في طاعته. غير أن جحودهم وتجاوزهم لم ينقصا من ملك الله شيئًا، بل كان وبالهما عائدًا عليهم؛ لأن العبد لا يضرّ الله بمعصيته، وإنما يظلم نفسه بإهدار النعمة واستحقاق العاقبة.

translation: And when We said, “Enter this town and eat from it freely, wherever you wish; enter the gate prostrating, and say, ‘Relieve us of our burdens.’ We will forgive you your sins, and We will increase the reward of those who do good.”
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel that His blessings were accompanied by obedience: they were granted provision, but commanded to enter humbly, seek forgiveness, and submit to Him. Their forgiveness was linked to sincere repentance and obedience, while those who excel in righteousness would receive an even greater reward from Him.

translation: But those who did wrong replaced the word they had been told with another, so We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the heavens because of their defiance.
interpretation: This warns that deliberately altering or mocking God’s commands, rather than submitting to them sincerely, turns disobedience into a cause of divine punishment.

translation: And when Moses prayed for water for his people, We said, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Then twelve springs burst forth from it; each group of people knew its drinking place. “Eat and drink from Allah’s provision, and do not go about the land spreading فساد.”
interpretation: When the Israelites were in need, Allah provided them water through Moses and arranged it in a clear and orderly way, giving each group its own spring. This sign teaches that provision comes from Allah, while people must receive it with gratitude and use it without causing corruption, harm, or disorder in the earth.

translation: And when you said, “O Moses, we cannot endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us some of what the earth grows—its herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions.” He said, “Would you exchange what is better for what is inferior? Go down to a town, and there you will have what you have asked for.” And humiliation and poverty were imposed upon them, and they incurred the wrath of Allah. That was because they used to reject Allah’s signs and kill the prophets unjustly. That was because they disobeyed and transgressed.
interpretation: This passage reproaches a people who, after receiving a sufficient and honored provision, became dissatisfied and sought lesser alternatives out of craving and ingratitude. Moses’ response teaches that the problem was not the food itself but the attitude of devaluing divine favor and preferring worldly variety to a provision granted with special care. Their humiliation, hardship, and divine anger are presented as the consequences of persistent disbelief, rebellion, and grave injustice—including the killing of prophets—rather than as the result of a single request. The verse therefore warns that repeated refusal of guidance can turn freedom and blessing into degradation when people continually transgress against God’s commands.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians—whoever truly believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—shall have their reward with their Lord; no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse establishes that salvation is tied to sincere faith in Allah, belief in the Last Day, and righteous action, not merely to belonging to a religious group by name. In its original context, it assures that those among the communities mentioned who genuinely followed the truth revealed to them and lived righteously would receive their reward from Allah, free from fear and sorrow.

translation: And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you: “Hold firmly to what We have given you, and remember what is in it, so that you may become mindful of God.”
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel that their covenant required sincere, steadfast adherence to the revealed scripture, not merely accepting it outwardly. The raising of the Mount emphasizes the seriousness of this obligation, while remembering its teachings means keeping them present in thought and practice; this leads to taqwa—living with awareness of Allah and obedience to Him.

translation: Then you turned away after that. Had it not been for Allah’s فضل and mercy upon you, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: After witnessing the covenant and its clear signs, you still turned away from obedience. Yet Allah’s grace and mercy spared you from immediate ruin and gave you the opportunity to repent; without them, your rejection would have led to true loss in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: And you surely knew those among you who transgressed concerning the Sabbath, so We said to them, “Be apes, despised and humiliated.”
interpretation: This verse warns that deliberately violating God’s commands, even through evasive schemes, can lead to disgrace and severe punishment when accompanied by defiance and arrogance.

translation: So We made it a deterrent for those before it and those after it, and an admonition for the mindful.
interpretation: The punishment was established as a lasting warning: those who witnessed it and those who came afterward should recognize that deliberately violating God’s commands brings disgrace and consequences, while reverent awareness of Him leads people to heed such warnings.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow,” they said, “Do you take us in mockery?” He said, “I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that divine commands are not to be met with ridicule or suspicion, and that a believer should respond to them with seriousness and trust. Moses rejects mockery because treating sacred matters lightly is a form of ignorance, while his response also shows that a person entrusted with guidance must clarify that Allah’s command is true and purposeful, even when its wisdom is not immediately apparent.

translation: They said, “Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is.” He said, “He says it is a cow neither old nor young, but middle-aged between the two. So do what you are commanded.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that excessive questioning, when a command is already clear, can make obedience more difficult; the proper response is to accept God’s guidance and carry it out without needless hesitation.

translation: They said, “Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what color it should be.” He said, “He says: It is a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to those who look at it.”
interpretation: The Israelites continued to demand unnecessary details instead of obeying promptly, and they were told that the cow must have a vivid, beautiful yellow appearance. The verse teaches that excessive questioning, when not motivated by sincere understanding, can make a simple command more difficult, while also showing the importance of obeying God’s instructions precisely.

translation: They said, “Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is. Indeed, the cattle all seem alike to us, and surely, if Allah wills, we will be rightly guided.”
interpretation: Their repeated questioning shows reluctance to obey until every detail was specified, while their words “if Allah wills” acknowledge that true guidance depends on God and express their hope of reaching the right command.

translation: He said, “He says: It is a cow neither trained to plough the earth nor used to water the fields; sound and without any marking.” They said, “Now you have brought the truth.” So they slaughtered it, though they scarcely did so.
interpretation: This verse concludes the Israelites’ repeated questioning about the cow, showing how their insistence on unnecessary details made a simple command increasingly difficult. Once the specified qualities were given, they recognized the truth and fulfilled the command, though only with great reluctance.

translation: And when you killed a person and disputed with one another concerning it, Allah was bringing to light what you had concealed.
interpretation: This verse exposes how concealment and mutual blame cannot hide wrongdoing from God: although the people involved tried to obscure the truth of the killing through dispute, God brought their hidden actions into the open.

translation: So We said, “Strike him with part of it.” Thus Allah brings the dead to life and shows you His signs, so that you may understand.
interpretation: Allah demonstrated His power by restoring the slain person to life through a part of the cow, making the truth of the murder manifest. This sign also teaches that the resurrection is entirely within Allah’s power, and that His signs are given so people will reflect, recognize the truth, and submit to it.

translation: Then, after that, your hearts became hardened, like stones—or even harder. For among stones are those from which rivers burst forth; among them are those that split open and water flows from them; and among them are those that fall down in awe of Allah. And Allah is not heedless of what you do.
interpretation: The verse rebukes hearts that remain unmoved by divine signs and admonition, portraying them as harder than stones: even stones yield water or respond with awe, whereas a hardened heart refuses faith, repentance, and humility. It warns that Allah fully knows such persistent conduct and will hold people accountable for it.

translation: Do you then hope that they will believe you, while a group of them used to hear the word of Allah, then knowingly distort it after understanding it?
interpretation: The verse cautions against expecting sincere acceptance from those who deliberately alter divine guidance after recognizing its meaning. Their obstacle is not lack of understanding, but conscious distortion driven by resistance or self-interest; therefore, faith cannot be presumed merely because truth has been clearly presented to them.

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, “We believe.” But when they are alone with one another, they say, “Why do you tell them what Allah has revealed to you, so that they may use it against you in argument before your Lord? Will you not understand?”
interpretation: The verse condemns the hypocrisy of concealing or selectively withholding revealed truth out of fear that it may be used as evidence against them. It shows that knowledge of divine truth carries a responsibility to accept and uphold it consistently, rather than adapting one’s speech to suit different audiences.

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal?
interpretation: The verse warns that no hidden intention, secret statement, or openly expressed act escapes Allah’s knowledge. Therefore, concealing disbelief, wrongdoing, or deception cannot protect a person from accountability before Him.

translation: Among them are unlearned people who know the Scripture only through wishful notions, and they do nothing but speculate.
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who claim to follow divine revelation without genuinely understanding it, relying instead on hearsay, imagined beliefs, and unsupported assumptions; true knowledge requires sincere learning rather than conjecture.

translation: So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, “This is from Allah,” in order to obtain a small price by it. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who knowingly fabricate religious teachings and falsely attribute them to Allah for worldly gain. Their wrongdoing lies both in deliberately producing falsehood and in benefiting from misleading others; such manipulation of revelation brings severe divine punishment.

translation: And they say, “The Fire will never touch us except for a limited number of days.” Say, “Have you made a covenant with Allah? For Allah never breaks His covenant. Or are you saying about Allah what you do not know?”
interpretation: They falsely comforted themselves with the claim that punishment would be brief, without possessing any promise from Allah to support it. The verse teaches that salvation cannot be based on wishful claims or inherited assertions; only a genuine covenant from Allah can guarantee it, and speaking about His judgment without knowledge is a grave falsehood.

translation: Yes indeed! Whoever earns evil and is encompassed by his sin—those are the companions of the Fire; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: This affirms that salvation is not secured by mere claims or affiliation; rather, a person who deliberately persists in wrongdoing until sin wholly surrounds and defines him, without repentance, faces the enduring consequence of the Fire.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—they are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: True faith is demonstrated through righteous action, and those who unite sincere belief with obedience to God are promised everlasting life and security in Paradise.

translation: And when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: “Worship none but Allah; show kindness to parents, relatives, orphans, and the needy; speak graciously to people; establish prayer; and give zakah.” Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you were refusing.
interpretation: This covenant presents faith in Allah as inseparable from ethical responsibility: honoring parents, caring for the vulnerable, treating people with gracious speech, and maintaining prayer and charitable giving. The reproach at the end shows that knowing these obligations is not enough; their value is realized only through sincere adherence, while turning away from them is a breach of the covenant.

translation: And when We took your covenant: “Do not shed one another’s blood, nor expel one another from your homes.” Then you acknowledged it, bearing witness.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel that they had expressly accepted the obligation to preserve one another’s lives and homes. Their acknowledgment made them witnesses against themselves, so violating these duties was not merely ignorance or error but a deliberate betrayal of the covenant with Allah.

translation: Then you are those who kill one another, drive a group of your own people from their homes, and support one another against them in sin and hostility. Yet if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Scripture and reject part of it? The reward of those among you who do this is nothing but disgrace in this worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment. Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse condemns selective obedience to divine law: people cannot uphold a command when it serves their interests while violating another command when loyalty, hostility, or worldly advantage leads them otherwise. Genuine faith requires submitting to the whole guidance of revelation, especially when it restrains injustice toward one’s own community. Such deliberate contradiction brings humiliation in this life and severe accountability in the Hereafter, for Allah fully knows every action and the motives behind it.

translation: Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world in exchange for the Hereafter; so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: They knowingly chose temporary worldly gain over obedience to God and the eternal life to come; therefore, in the Hereafter, they will face punishment without relief or any protector able to save them.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture and followed him with messengers. We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear signs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. So, whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, did you act arrogantly? Some you denied, and some you killed.
interpretation: This verse rebukes the persistent rejection of divine guidance when it conflicts with personal desires. It reminds the Children of Israel that God repeatedly sent revelation, supported His messengers with clear proofs, and granted Jesus particular signs and divine aid; yet many responded not with humility but with arrogance—denying some messengers and killing others. Its central warning is that faith requires submitting to God’s truth even when it challenges one’s preferences, rather than accepting revelation selectively according to desire.

translation: And they said, “Our hearts are wrapped in coverings.” Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.
interpretation: They used the claim that their hearts were closed as an excuse for refusing divine guidance, but the real barrier was their deliberate disbelief; as a consequence, they were deprived of spiritual receptivity and believed only rarely and superficially.

translation: When a Book from Allah came to them, confirming what they already had—although before that they had been seeking victory over the disbelievers—then, when what they recognized came to them, they rejected it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse condemns the deliberate rejection of truth when it becomes clear, especially when a person recognizes its authenticity but refuses to follow it out of arrogance, envy, or attachment to personal interests. Previous claims of loyalty to revelation and appeals for divine support do not benefit those who deny the truth once it arrives.

translation: How evil is that for which they have sold themselves: that they should disbelieve in what Allah has revealed, out of envy that Allah should bestow His فضل upon whichever of His servants He wills. Thus they incurred wrath upon wrath, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns knowingly rejecting divine revelation because of resentment toward the people Allah chooses to receive His favor. Such envy turns disbelief into a deliberate moral rebellion, bringing compounded divine displeasure and humiliation rather than honor.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Believe in what Allah has sent down,” they say, “We believe in what was sent down to us,” while they reject what came after it, although it is the truth confirming what they have. Say, “Why, then, did you kill Allah’s prophets before, if you are believers?”
interpretation: This verse exposes the inconsistency of claiming faith in one’s own revelation while rejecting the later revelation even though it confirms the truth already present in it. True faith is not selective or driven by communal allegiance; it requires accepting God’s guidance when it comes, and the history of killing prophets demonstrates that mere religious claims are worthless when a person refuses obedience to God’s messengers.

translation: And Moses certainly came to you with clear signs, then you took the calf as an object of worship after him, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse reproaches the Israelites for abandoning the decisive evidence brought by Moses and turning to idol worship after his departure, showing that such conduct was deliberate injustice despite the truth having been made clear to them.

translation: And [remember] when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you: “Hold firmly to what We have given you and listen.” They said, “We hear and we disobey.” And their hearts were made to absorb the love of the calf because of their disbelief. Say, “How evil is what your faith commands you to do, if indeed you are believers.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction between claiming faith and deliberately rejecting God’s covenant. True faith requires sincere listening, steadfast obedience, and freedom from devotion to anything that competes with God; their attachment to the calf revealed that their professed belief had become an excuse for disobedience rather than a source of submission.

translation: Say, “If the abode of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you, apart from all other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the emptiness of claiming a special entitlement to salvation without sincere faith and obedience. A person who is truly certain that the Hereafter belongs exclusively to them would not fear death, yet such certainty cannot be established by mere assertion; it must be proven by truthfulness before Allah.

translation: But they will never wish for it because of what their hands have sent ahead; and Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Their refusal to wish for death exposes the contradiction between their claim to exclusive closeness to God and their awareness of the wrongdoing they have committed; God knows their deeds and the reality of their hearts.

translation: You will surely find them the most eager of all people for life—even more than those who associate partners with Allah. Each of them wishes to live for a thousand years, but even such a long life would not save him from the punishment. Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: The verse portrays an intense attachment to worldly life that stems from fear of what awaits beyond it. Yet prolonging life cannot shield a person from divine judgment; what matters is not how long one lives, but how one lives, for Allah fully knows every deed.

translation: Say: “Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel—indeed, he brought it down upon your heart by Allah’s permission, confirming what came before it, and as guidance and good news for the believers.”
interpretation: This verse declares that hostility toward Gabriel is ultimately hostility toward the divine revelation he faithfully delivered. Gabriel brought the Qur’an to the Prophet’s heart only by Allah’s command, and its message confirms the truth preserved in earlier revelation, guides people to faith and right conduct, and gives believers hope of Allah’s mercy and reward.

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel, and Michael—then surely Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse declares that rejecting or opposing any of Allah’s angels or messengers is ultimately opposition to Allah Himself, because they convey and serve His command. By singling out Gabriel and Michael, it emphasizes that no distinction or selective belief is acceptable; whoever adopts such hostility places themselves among those opposed by Allah.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you clear revelations, and none reject them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: These unmistakable revelations leave no legitimate excuse for rejection; disbelief in them arises not from a lack of clarity, but from a willful departure from obedience to God and resistance to the truth.

translation: Is it not that whenever they make a covenant, a group of them casts it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe.
interpretation: The verse censures the repeated violation of divine and human covenants by some of the Children of Israel, indicating that such betrayal is rooted in the absence of genuine faith: true faith obliges a person to honor commitments even when doing so conflicts with personal desire.

translation: And when a messenger from Allah came to them, confirming what they already had, a group of those who had been given the Scripture cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, as though they did not know.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن بعض أهل الكتاب أعرضوا عن الوحي الذي جاء به الرسول، مع أنه وافق أصول الحق التي كانت في كتبهم وأقام الحجة عليهم. وكان إعراضهم إعراضًا متعمدًا، إذ تعاملوا مع كتاب الله كأنهم يجهلون قيمته وما يقتضيه من الإيمان والاتباع.

translation: They followed what the devils recited during Solomon’s reign. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils did, teaching people magic—and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Hārūt and Mārūt. Yet they taught no one without saying, “We are only a test, so do not disbelieve.” Still, people learned from them the means by which they could separate a man from his wife. But they could not harm anyone through it except by Allah’s permission. They learned what harmed them and did not benefit them, although they certainly knew that whoever acquired it would have no share in the Hereafter. How evil was that for which they sold themselves, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse exposes the false claim that Solomon’s authority came from sorcery: Solomon was innocent of disbelief, while the devils were guilty because they promoted magic and misled people. The mention of Hārūt and Mārūt presents their teaching as a trial accompanied by an explicit warning, not as an approval of magic; those who pursued it nevertheless chose a harmful path, even using it to destroy marriage. Its effects cannot occur independently of Allah’s permission, yet seeking and practicing it remains spiritually ruinous, because it brings harm without true benefit and forfeits one’s share in the Hereafter. The verse therefore warns that knowledge or power pursued in defiance of divine guidance becomes a means of self-destruction.

translation: Had they believed and been mindful of Allah, a reward from Allah would have been far better—if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere faith and reverent obedience to Allah lead to a reward far superior to any worldly gain, including the fleeting benefits people may seek through sinful or deceptive practices. It urges people to recognize that true benefit lies in trusting Allah and living according to His guidance.

translation: O you who believe, do not say, “Rāʿinā,” but say, “Unẓurnā,” and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Believers are instructed to use clear, respectful words when addressing the Prophet, avoiding expressions that could be twisted into disrespect or insult. They should listen attentively and obey, while those who knowingly reject faith and persist in denial face a painful punishment.

translation: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the rejection or envy of people must not be allowed to obscure the truth that every blessing of guidance and revelation comes from Allah’s mercy and choice. He grants His favor according to His wisdom, not according to the wishes of those who oppose it, and His abundant grace is not limited by anyone’s resentment.

translation: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or equal to it. Do you not know that Allah is capable of all things?
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah may replace a revealed ruling with one more suitable to His servants’ circumstances, or with one equivalent in benefit and guidance. Such change occurs by His wisdom and authority, not because of deficiency or contradiction; Allah alone determines revelation and is fully capable of every matter.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have no protector or helper besides Allah?
interpretation: This verse calls people to recognize Allah’s complete authority over all existence and to place their ultimate trust in Him, for no one besides Him can truly protect them from harm or grant them victory.

translation: Or do you wish to question your Messenger as Moses was questioned before? Whoever exchanges disbelief for faith has surely strayed from the right path.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to burden the Messenger with demands and objections arising from stubbornness, as earlier people challenged Moses. True faith requires sincere submission to divine guidance, whereas rejecting it after receiving it is a departure from the straight path.

translation: Many of the People of the Scripture wish to turn you back into disbelievers after your faith, out of envy from within themselves, even after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that hostility may arise not from uncertainty about the truth, but from envy and resentment. They are therefore instructed not to answer such opposition with vengefulness; instead, they should respond with patience, pardon, and restraint, trusting that Allah has full power to establish justice and bring about His decree.

translation: Establish the prayer and give the zakat. Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worship is not confined to inward belief: it must be expressed through faithful prayer and generosity toward others. Every good deed sincerely offered is preserved with Allah and will be found by the servant as lasting reward, while Allah’s complete awareness of all actions calls for sincerity and constancy.

translation: And they say, “None will enter Paradise unless they are Jews or Christians.” These are merely their wishful claims. Say, “Bring your proof, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that salvation belongs exclusively to a particular religious label, exposing it as an unfounded wish rather than a truth supported by revelation or evidence. It calls those who make such claims to provide clear proof, teaching that entry into Paradise cannot be established by mere affiliation or assertion.

translation: Indeed, whoever submits himself to Allah and is excellent in conduct will have his reward with his Lord. No fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: True salvation belongs not to claims or affiliations, but to sincere submission to Allah expressed through righteous action. Whoever entrusts themselves wholly to Him and lives with excellence may be assured of His reward and protected from the fear and sorrow that accompany ultimate loss.

translation: The Jews say, “The Christians have no valid standing,” and the Christians say, “The Jews have no valid standing,” even though they both recite the Scripture. Likewise, those who have no knowledge speak in the same manner. So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed.
interpretation: The verse condemns religious partisanship that leads people to deny one another while possessing revealed Scripture. Mere association with a sacred tradition does not protect a person from ignorance when revelation is used to justify rejection, rivalry, or injustice; the ultimate judgment of conflicting claims belongs to Allah, who will distinguish truth from falsehood on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who prevents Allah’s name from being mentioned in His mosques and strives to ruin them? Such people have no right to enter them except in fear. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who obstruct worship and remembrance of Allah or seek to destroy the sanctity and proper function of places of worship. Their aggression is a grave injustice, and the warning that they should enter only in fear signifies that they have forfeited any claim to security or honor in those sacred places; their worldly humiliation and ultimate punishment correspond to the harm they deliberately cause to devotion and the worshippers.

translation: To Allah belong the east and the west. So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah is not confined to any direction or place; all directions belong to Him, and His knowledge, authority, and care encompass everything. Thus, when a person sincerely turns to Him—especially when unable to face the prescribed direction—Allah receives and knows that devotion.

translation: And they say, “Allah has taken a son.” Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing offspring to Allah, affirming that He is exalted above all human-like qualities. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him and is subject to His command, so none can be His child or share in His divinity.

translation: مُبدع السماوات والأرض، وإذا قضى أمرًا فإنما يقول له: كن، فيكون.
interpretation: يبين الآية أن الله تعالى هو الخالق المبدع للسماوات والأرض، وأن قدرته المطلقة تجعل تحقق ما يريده لا يحتاج إلى وسيلة أو زمن؛ فإذا أراد أمرًا وقع بمجرد قضائه له.

translation: Those who have no knowledge say, “Why does Allah not speak to us, or why does a sign not come to us?” In the same way, those before them said what they said. Their hearts are alike. We have made the signs clear for people who are certain.
interpretation: The verse exposes a recurring attitude of spiritual arrogance: people demand extraordinary proof or direct speech from God while refusing to respond to the guidance already given. Their repeated demands arise from hearts alike in doubt and stubbornness, whereas those who sincerely seek certainty recognize that God’s clear signs are sufficient for anyone willing to believe and reflect.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner, and you will not be held accountable for the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: God consoles the Prophet that his mission is to convey the truth, offer hope to those who believe and warn those who reject it; he is not responsible for the disbelief or ultimate fate of those who refuse the message.

translation: The Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their way. Say, “Indeed, Allah’s guidance is the true guidance.” And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or helper from Allah.
interpretation: This verse teaches that religious truth is not determined by seeking the approval of others, but by adhering faithfully to the guidance revealed by Allah. The warning against following their desires applies to abandoning divine knowledge for conformity or compromise; it is a warning to remain sincere and steadfast, not a justification for injustice or hostility toward people of other faiths.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it as it ought to be recited; they truly believe in it. But whoever disbelieves in it—it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: True engagement with revelation is not merely verbal recitation; it is to read it faithfully, understand its guidance, and follow it sincerely. Such honest adherence leads to genuine belief, whereas rejecting the truth after it has been made known deprives a person of the ultimate success.

translation: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you, and that I favored you above all peoples.
interpretation: Allah calls the Children of Israel to recall His blessings and recognize that their distinction was a gift carrying the responsibility of gratitude, obedience, and faithfulness to His covenant—not a guarantee of merit independent of their deeds.

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will avail another in anything, no ransom will be accepted from it, no intercession will benefit it, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This warns that on the Day of Judgment each person will face responsibility for their own deeds; neither worldly relationships, payment, appeals, nor external assistance can rescue anyone from God’s judgment. Only sincere faith and righteous deeds can benefit a person by God’s permission.

translation: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commandments, and he fulfilled them, He said, “I am making you a leader for humanity.” Abraham said, “And from my descendants?” He said, “My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: This verse shows that spiritual leadership is a divine trust granted to Abraham after he faithfully completed every test and command entrusted to him. His request that this honor extend to his descendants is answered with a condition: lineage alone does not qualify anyone for God’s covenant. Those who persist in ظلم—wrongdoing, injustice, or rebellion—are excluded from such divinely sanctioned leadership, regardless of their ancestry.

translation: And when We made the House a place of return for humanity and a sanctuary of safety, [saying], “Take the standing-place of Abraham as a place of prayer.” We entrusted Abraham and Ishmael, “Purify My House for those who circumambulate it, those who remain there in worship, and those who bow and prostrate.”
interpretation: The verse presents the Kaaba as a divinely appointed center to which people continually return, finding spiritual orientation and protection there. By linking prayer to Abraham’s station and commanding its purification, it teaches that worship must be grounded in sincere devotion, reverence, and a sacred space kept free for those who seek God through pilgrimage, remembrance, prayer, bowing, and prostration.

translation: And when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this a secure land and provide its people with fruits—those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.” He said, “As for whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then I will compel him toward the punishment of the Fire—and what a wretched destination.”
interpretation: Abraham’s prayer seeks security and provision for the inhabitants who live by faith, while Allah clarifies that worldly sustenance may also be granted to those who reject faith as a temporary respite, not as a sign of approval or lasting success. Every person is given a limited opportunity in this world, but disbelief ultimately leads to accountability and the severe consequence of the Fire.

translation: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, they prayed: “Our Lord, accept this from us; indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: As Abraham and Ishmael built the sacred House, they did not rely on the greatness of their deed or their own righteousness; instead, they humbly asked God to accept it. This teaches that acts of worship should be accompanied by sincerity, humility, and hope in God’s acceptance, while trusting that He hears every prayer and knows the intentions behind every deed.

translation: Our Lord, make us submissive to You, and from our offspring raise a community submissive to You. Show us our rites, and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This supplication teaches that true faith is wholehearted submission to God, a gift to be sought not only for oneself but also for one’s descendants. It asks God to clarify the acts of worship and their proper observance, while acknowledging that returning to Him requires His acceptance and mercy.

translation: Our Lord, raise among them a messenger from them who will recite to them Your verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Surely, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This is a supplication that God send a messenger from among the descendants of Abraham and Ishmael: one who conveys His revelations, teaches divine guidance and sound understanding, and purifies people from disbelief, corruption, and immoral character. The fulfillment of this prayer is seen in the mission of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, whose authority and wisdom proceed from God’s might and perfect wisdom.

translation: And who would turn away from the way of Abraham except one who has made a fool of himself? Indeed, We chose him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.
interpretation: The verse portrays sincere devotion to Abraham’s pure monotheistic faith as the path of sound judgment, while rejecting it is self-inflicted folly because it means abandoning the truth despite its clarity. Abraham was honored by God in this life for his wholehearted submission, and that divine favor is completed in the Hereafter by his place among the righteous.

translation: When his Lord said to him, “Submit,” he replied, “I have submitted to the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: This portrays true faith as willingly surrendering oneself entirely to God’s command, as Abraham did, recognizing Him as the sole Lord and Creator of every realm.

translation: And Abraham instructed his sons, and Jacob as well: “My children, indeed Allah has chosen this way of life for you, so do not die except in a state of submission to Him.”
interpretation: Abraham and Jacob urged their descendants to hold firmly to the divinely chosen path of submission throughout their lives, because true success lies in remaining devoted to Allah until death, not merely in claiming faith by ancestry or words.

translation: Or were you witnesses when death came to Jacob, when he said to his sons, “What will you worship after me?” They said, “We will worship your God and the God of your fathers—Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac—the One God, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: This verse reminds people that true faith is not inherited merely by lineage, but is a conscious commitment to worship the one God and submit to Him. Jacob’s final concern was the spiritual direction of his children, and their answer affirms the same monotheistic devotion upheld by their righteous forefathers. Mentioning Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac emphasizes the continuity of their message: sincere submission to God, rather than attachment to names, ancestry, or worldly identity.

translation: That was a community that has passed away. They shall have what they earned, and you shall have what you earn; and you will not be questioned about what they used to do.
interpretation: The deeds of earlier generations belong to them alone and neither benefit nor burden those who come after them. Each person and community is accountable before God for their own faith and actions, so lineage, historical affiliation, or claims about past people cannot replace obedience and responsibility in the present.

translation: And they say, “Be Jews or Christians, and you will be rightly guided.” Say, “Rather, [we follow] the way of Abraham, inclining wholly to the truth; and he was not of the polytheists.”
interpretation: True guidance is not attained by belonging to a religious label or by imitating a community, but by following Abraham’s sincere devotion to God alone. His way rejects every form of associating partners with God and calls people to pure, undivided monotheism.

translation: Say, “We believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: This verse commands believers to affirm the common divine origin of all authentic revelation and to honor every prophet without rejecting or elevating some while denying others. True faith embraces the guidance granted to Muhammad and the earlier messengers alike, while complete submission belongs to Allah alone.

translation: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا، وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق، فسيكفيكهم الله، وهو السميع العليم
interpretation: إن آمن أهل الكتاب بالإيمان الحق الذي جاء به النبي ﷺ، بما يوافق توحيد الله وسائر أصول الهدى، فقد سلكوا طريق الرشاد؛ أما إعراضهم فليس عن طلب حق، بل هو مخالفة وانقسام عن الحق. وفي ذلك تطمين للنبي ﷺ بأن الله سيتولى كفايته ودفع أذى المعاندين، فهو يسمع أقوالهم ويعلم نياتهم وأعمالهم.

translation: The coloring of Allah—and who is better than Allah in coloring? And it is Him alone that we worship.
interpretation: Allah’s true mark is the faith and way of life He instills in people, which distinguishes them through sincere devotion and righteous conduct; no identity or spiritual path is better than the one shaped by Allah, and worship belongs to Him alone.

translation: Say, “Do you argue with us about Allah, while He is our Lord and your Lord? We have our deeds, and you have your deeds, and we are sincerely devoted to Him.”
interpretation: The verse rejects disputation over God based on claims of exclusive religious privilege: Allah is the Lord of all, and each person is accountable for their own deeds. What distinguishes true devotion is sincere submission to Him, not empty argument or inherited claims.

translation: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians? Say, “Are you more knowledgeable, or is Allah?” And who is more unjust than one who conceals testimony received from Allah? Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse rejects the attempt to claim the earlier prophets and their descendants as belonging exclusively to later religious identities. It affirms that Allah knows their true faith and history better than those who make such claims, and condemns knowingly suppressing or distorting divine testimony. The warning emphasizes that no concealment, misrepresentation, or denial of truth escapes Allah’s knowledge.

translation: That was a community that has passed away. It shall have what it earned, and you shall have what you earn, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do.
interpretation: Past peoples are accountable for their own beliefs and deeds, while you are accountable for yours; lineage, association, or claims of belonging to them cannot replace personal faith and righteous action.

translation: The foolish among the people will say, “What has turned them away from the direction of prayer they used to face?” Say, “To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whoever He wills to a straight path.”
interpretation: Allah foretells and dismisses objections to the change of the qiblah, teaching that sacred direction is established by His command rather than by any inherent sanctity of a particular place. Since all directions belong to Him, true obedience lies in following His guidance with submission, and He grants the straight path to whom He wills.

translation: وهكذا جعلناكم أمةً وسطًا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدًا. وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن يرتدّ على عقبيه، وإن كانت هذه المسألة لشاقة إلا على الذين هداهم الله. وما كان الله ليُضيع إيمانكم؛ إن الله بالناس لرؤوف رحيم.
interpretation: جعل الله المسلمين أمةً وسطًا، أي قائمة على الاعتدال والعدل والحق، لتشهد على الناس بإبلاغ الرسالة والالتزام بها، ويشهد الرسول على أمته. وكان تحويل القبلة اختبارًا يكشف صدق الاتباع من التراجع، مع أن الأمر شقّ على النفوس، إلا أن الهداية جعلته يسيرًا على المؤمنين. ويطمئن الله من صلّى إلى القبلة الأولى بأن أعماله وإيمانه محفوظة لا تضيع، لأن رحمته ورأفته بعباده تقتضيان ألا يبطل طاعتهم.

translation: We certainly see you turning your face toward the sky. So We will surely turn you toward a direction of prayer that pleases you. Turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that this is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: Allah responds to the Prophet’s longing by establishing the Kaʿbah in Makkah as the qiblah, showing that the direction of worship is determined by divine command rather than human preference. Turning toward it unites believers everywhere in obedient worship, while those familiar with earlier revelation can recognize the truth of this command; Allah remains fully aware of their responses and deeds.

translation: Yet even if you brought those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your direction of prayer; nor are you to follow their direction of prayer. Nor would some of them follow the direction of prayer of others. And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would surely be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that rejection rooted in stubbornness or sectarian attachment is not overcome merely by presenting further proofs. The established direction of prayer signifies the distinct obedience revealed by God, so the Prophet is commanded to remain firmly faithful to divine guidance rather than yield to the conflicting demands and desires of those who oppose it. Once truth has become clear, abandoning it to please others is injustice, because it replaces God’s guidance with human preference.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons, yet a group of them knowingly conceal the truth.
interpretation: Those among the People of the Scripture who possess sincere knowledge can recognize the truth of the Prophet through the signs and descriptions preserved in their revelation, as clearly as a person recognizes his own child. Nevertheless, some of them deliberately hide or deny this truth despite knowing it, showing that rejection may arise not from lack of evidence but from pride, envy, or attachment to worldly interests.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.
interpretation: This is a firm reassurance that what God has revealed is certain and originates from Him, so the believer must hold to it with confidence rather than allowing uncertainty to unsettle faith.

translation: For everyone there is a direction toward which they turn. So compete with one another in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that differences in direction, circumstance, or religious practice must not distract believers from their essential duty: hastening toward righteousness. Since all people will ultimately be gathered before Allah, the true measure of a person is not outward affiliation alone but sincere obedience and the good deeds pursued for His sake.

translation: Wherever you go forth, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, this is certainly the truth from your Lord, and Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This command affirms that facing the Kaaba is a divinely established direction of worship, binding wherever one may be. It also reminds believers that Allah fully knows their actions and intentions, so obedience to this direction should be sincere and mindful.

translation: Wherever you go out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it, so that people will have no argument against you—except those among them who are unjust. So do not fear them, but fear Me, and so that I may complete My blessing upon you and perhaps you will be rightly guided.
