interpretation: The command to face the Sacred Mosque establishes a shared direction of worship through which the believers’ obedience and distinct religious identity are made manifest. Any objections raised against this command by those who persist in wrongdoing have no legitimate weight; therefore, the believer must not be intimidated by people, but must remain devoted to God alone, trusting that sincere obedience leads to the completion of His blessings and to guidance.

translation: Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive mission of the Messenger: to convey God’s revelation, purify people’s hearts and conduct, teach them divine guidance and sound judgment, and open for them knowledge beyond what they could attain on their own. True guidance therefore joins learning with moral transformation.

translation: So remember Me, and I will remember you; be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful.
interpretation: Allah commands believers to keep Him present in their hearts and lives through remembrance and obedience, promising them His care, mercy, and favor in return. Gratitude requires recognizing His blessings and using them rightly, while denying or neglecting them is a form of ingratitude.

translation: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse teaches believers to meet trials and responsibilities with steadfast self-control and sincere prayer, for Allah grants His support, care, and guidance to those who remain patient and devoted to Him.

translation: And do not say of those who are killed in the cause of Allah, “They are dead.” Rather, they are alive, but you are unaware.
interpretation: Those who sincerely sacrifice their lives for Allah are not truly lost or annihilated; they possess a special life and honor with their Lord beyond the limits of worldly perception. Human beings cannot sense this reality through ordinary means, so they must not judge their state by the outward appearance of death.

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits. So give glad tidings to the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse teaches that trials are an inevitable part of life and may touch people through fear, deprivation, financial loss, bereavement, or reduced prosperity. These tests do not signify abandonment by God; rather, they reveal and cultivate steadfastness, trust, and faithful perseverance. Those who endure without losing their devotion and respond to hardship with patience are promised glad tidings from God.

translation: Those who, when calamity befalls them, say, “Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.”
interpretation: They face loss and hardship with faith that their lives, possessions, and circumstances are entrusted to Allah and ultimately return to Him. This conviction gives them patience, humility, and hope, rather than despair or rebellion, because they trust in Allah’s wisdom and await His recompense.

translation: Upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and it is they who are rightly guided.
interpretation: Those who endure their trials with faith and steadfastness are honored by Allah with divine praise, mercy, and guidance that keeps them firm upon the right path.

translation: Indeed, Ṣafā and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or makes ʿUmrah, there is no blame upon him for going back and forth between them. And whoever does good voluntarily—indeed, Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah establishes the movement between Ṣafā and Marwah as a sacred rite of pilgrimage, honoring the devotion and perseverance associated with it. The wording “there is no blame” removes any hesitation about performing this rite, while affirming that every voluntary act of goodness is fully known and rewarded by Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal the clear proofs and guidance We have revealed, after We have made them clear to people in the Scripture—Allah condemns them, and those who condemn also condemn them.
interpretation: This warns that knowingly hiding revealed truth after it has been clearly explained is a grave betrayal of knowledge and a cause of exclusion from Allah’s mercy, deserving condemnation from all who reject such injustice.

translation: Except those who repent, reform themselves, and make clear the truth; those—I will accept their repentance. And I am the Ever-Relenting, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Those who had concealed the truth can receive Allah’s forgiveness through sincere repentance, correcting their conduct, and openly clarifying what they had hidden. Allah welcomes such repentance and shows them His abundant mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers—upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.
interpretation: This verse declares that persistent disbelief until death places a person under complete and lasting rejection: they are deprived of Allah’s mercy, condemned by the angels, and repudiated by humanity. It also indicates that repentance and faith must occur before death, because once a person dies in disbelief, that state is no longer reversed.

translation: They will remain therein forever; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: This describes the unending severity of the punishment: those condemned to it will neither experience any reduction in suffering nor receive delay or relief from it.

translation: And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This affirms that all true worship belongs exclusively to the one God, whose absolute oneness is joined with boundless compassion and mercy toward His creation.

translation: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض، وتعاقب الليل والنهار، والسفن التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس، وما أنزله الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها، ونشر فيها من كل دابة، وتصريف الرياح، والسحاب المسخَّر بين السماء والأرض، دلائل واضحة على قدرة الله وحكمته ووحدانيته لقوم يتدبرون بعقولهم.
interpretation: تلفت الآية نظر الإنسان إلى انتظام الكون وتنوع مظاهره النافعة، لتبين أن هذا النظام الدقيق والحياة المتجددة لا يمكن أن يكونا بلا خالق مدبر؛ وإنما يهتدي إلى دلالتهما من يستخدم عقله في التأمل، فيزداد يقينًا بقدرة الله ووحدانيته وحكمته.

translation: Among the people are those who take rivals besides Allah, loving them as they should love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. If only those who commit wrongdoing could see—when they behold the punishment—that all power belongs entirely to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: Some people direct to created beings a devotion and love that belong solely to Allah, treating them as equals in worship and obedience. True believers, however, place Allah above every rival, desire, and attachment, so their love for Him is deeper and governs their lives. The wrongdoers will recognize the absolute power of Allah only when punishment becomes visible, but that recognition will then come too late to benefit them.

translation: When those who were followed disown those who followed them, and they see the punishment, and all ties between them are severed.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the people who were blindly followed will renounce responsibility for their followers, while the followers will find no protection or connection remaining between them. This reveals that worldly authority and imitation cannot save anyone from accountability before God.

translation: Those who followed will say, “If only we had another chance to return, we would disassociate ourselves from them just as they have disassociated themselves from us.” Thus Allah will show them their deeds as sources of regret for them, and they will not emerge from the Fire.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who blindly followed others will realize that their allegiance brought them nothing but ruin. They will wish for a return to worldly life so that they could reject those leaders and influences, yet this wish will be impossible. Their former choices and deeds will then appear before them as the very cause of their anguish, while their punishment will have no end because they did not turn away from falsehood before death.

translation: O mankind, eat from what is lawful and wholesome on the earth, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse teaches that believers should seek sustenance that is both religiously lawful and good in its nature, while avoiding the gradual path by which Satan leads people from permissible desires into disobedience. It also warns that moral corruption often begins with seemingly small steps, so one must remain vigilant about the choices and influences that shape one’s life.

translation: He only commands you to evil and indecency, and to say about Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: Satan’s influence is confined to inviting people toward sinful and shameful acts and toward making unfounded claims about God; therefore, one must reject such impulses and speak about divine matters only with sound knowledge.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,” they say, “Rather, we follow what we found our forefathers following.” Even if their forefathers understood nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: This verse condemns the blind imitation of inherited customs when they conflict with divine guidance. Truth is not established by ancestry or tradition; it must be accepted through sound understanding and guidance from Allah, even when that requires departing from the practices of previous generations.

translation: The example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who calls out to what hears nothing but a shout and a cry. Deaf, dumb, and blind—they do not understand.
interpretation: Those who reject faith are likened to animals that hear sounds without grasping their meaning: they may hear the message of revelation, but because they refuse to reflect and respond, its guidance does not reach their understanding or hearts.

translation: O you who believe, eat of the wholesome things We have provided for you, and give thanks to Allah, if it is truly Him that you worship.
interpretation: True worship requires receiving Allah’s lawful and wholesome blessings with gratitude, recognizing that they come from Him, and using them in obedience rather than heedlessness or excess.

translation: He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is compelled by necessity—without desiring it or exceeding the limits—there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah prohibits these specific foods because of their impurity or association with false worship, yet His law accommodates genuine necessity: a person facing unavoidable danger may consume only what is needed to preserve life, without seeking the forbidden or exceeding the essential limit. This exception reflects Allah’s mercy and forgiveness.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and sell it for a small price—they consume nothing but fire into their bellies. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that deliberately hiding revealed truth for worldly benefit is not a minor act of dishonesty but a corruption of one’s religious trust. The temporary gain is portrayed as fire because it carries a consequence that destroys rather than nourishes, while being denied Allah’s speech and purification signifies complete deprivation of His mercy and moral cleansing on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Those are the ones who purchased error in exchange for guidance and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. How persistent they are in facing the Fire!
interpretation: They knowingly chose misguidance over divine guidance and the punishment of the Hereafter over God’s forgiveness. The closing expression is a rebuke expressing amazement at how audaciously they persist in the path that leads them to the Fire, despite its terrifying consequence.

translation: That is because Allah has sent down the Book in truth; and indeed, those who differ concerning the Book are in profound opposition.
interpretation: The revelation was given as a clear and truthful standard, so disputing it through denial, distortion, or division places people in a state of deep estrangement from the truth and from one another.

translation: Righteousness is not merely that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. Rather, righteousness belongs to those who believe in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Scripture, and the prophets; who give wealth—despite their love for it—to relatives, orphans, the needy, travelers, those who ask, and for the freeing of captives; who establish prayer and give zakāh; who honor their pledges when they make them; and who remain steadfast in poverty, hardship, and times of conflict. It is they who have been true, and it is they who are mindful of God.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true righteousness is not defined by outward religious orientation alone, but by the harmony of sound faith, sincere worship, generous service, moral responsibility, and steadfastness through trial. Genuine belief becomes visible in a person’s willingness to part with what they love for the sake of others, uphold commitments, support the vulnerable, and remain patient in hardship and danger. Such people are truthful because their inner convictions are confirmed by their actions, and they are mindful of God because their entire conduct is shaped by accountability before Him.

translation: O you who believe, prescribed for you is the law of equal retribution regarding those killed: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But if the victim’s brother grants any pardon, then the matter should be pursued with fairness, and compensation should be paid to him with excellence. This is a mitigation and mercy from your Lord. Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes justice in cases of unlawful killing by requiring proportionate legal retribution under lawful authority, while rejecting vengeance and unequal retaliation. It also opens the door to mercy: the victim’s family may pardon the offender or accept fair compensation, which must be sought and given honorably. The warning against transgression forbids exceeding the limits of justice after pardon or settlement, showing that the law’s purpose is to protect life, restrain revenge, and balance accountability with mercy.

translation: And there is life for you in legal retribution, O people of understanding, so that you may become mindful of God.
interpretation: The prescribed justice of equal retribution protects society by deterring murder and preventing cycles of revenge; those who reflect understand that upholding this justice preserves life and encourages obedience to God.

translation: Prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and he leaves wealth, is a bequest for parents and close relatives in a fair manner—a duty upon the mindful.
interpretation: The verse directs a person facing death, if possessing substantial wealth, to make a just and reasonable provision for parents and close relatives through a will, without favoritism or harm. Such care for family rights is presented as an obligation of those who are conscious of God.

translation: Whoever changes it after hearing it, the sin is only upon those who change it. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse warns that deliberately altering a valid bequest after learning its terms is a serious injustice, and that the one who makes the alteration bears its sin—not the person who made the bequest—because Allah hears every statement and knows every intention and action.

translation: But whoever fears that a testator has committed an injustice or wrongdoing, and then reconciles between them, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: If a person notices that a will contains unfairness or sinful bias and works sincerely to correct the matter and restore justice among those affected, he is not blameworthy for intervening; rather, Allah forgives such efforts and shows mercy to those who seek reconciliation and fairness.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، فُرض عليكم الصيام كما فُرض على الذين من قبلكم، لعلكم تتقون.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن الصيام عبادة مفروضة على المؤمنين، وقد عُرفت في شرائع سابقة، وأن غايتها تربية التقوى في القلب؛ فيتعلم الصائم ضبط شهواته، ومراقبة الله، والامتثال لأمره، فينعكس ذلك على سلوكه خارج وقت الصيام.

translation: For a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or traveling, then let them make up an equal number of days later. And for those who are able to fast only with great difficulty, there is a ransom: feeding a needy person. Whoever voluntarily does more good, it is better for them; and fasting is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: God establishes fasting as a manageable, counted obligation while showing mercy to those whose illness or travel prevents them from observing it, allowing them to complete the missed days later. Those unable to fast except with serious hardship may instead feed a needy person for each day, and voluntary generosity brings additional benefit. Yet when a person is capable, fasting itself is spiritually better because its discipline and devotion fulfill the purpose of the command.

translation: The month of Ramadan is the month in which the Qur’an was revealed, as guidance for humanity and clear proofs of guidance and the criterion between truth and falsehood. So whoever among you witnesses the month must fast it; and whoever is ill or travelling may fast an equal number of other days. Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you, so that you may complete the prescribed period, glorify Allah for guiding you, and perhaps be grateful.
interpretation: This verse establishes Ramadan fasting as an act of devoted obedience while affirming that worship is not meant to become unbearable. The allowances for illness and travel express Allah’s mercy, and making up the missed days preserves the discipline and completion of the obligation. The month’s deeper purpose is to receive the Qur’an as guidance, recognize its clear distinction between truth and falsehood, magnify Allah for that guidance, and respond to it with gratitude.

translation: And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I answer the call of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be guided.
interpretation: Allah assures His servants that He is near to them through His knowledge, mercy, and readiness to answer their sincere prayers. This nearness calls them to turn to Him directly, obey His guidance, and place their trust in Him. True guidance comes when supplication is joined with faith and a willing response to Allah’s commands.

translation: It has been made lawful for you, on the nights of fasting, to be intimate with your wives. They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them. God knows that you were betraying yourselves, so He turned to you in mercy and pardoned you. So now be intimate with them and seek what God has prescribed for you. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread; then complete the fast until night. But do not be intimate with them while you are secluded in worship in the mosques. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make His signs clear to people, so that they may become mindful.
interpretation: This verse establishes fasting as an act of disciplined devotion whose boundaries protect both its spiritual purpose and the believer’s well-being. It permits marital intimacy during the night, portraying spouses as garments for one another—offering protection, closeness, comfort, and concealment—while forbidding intimacy during the daytime fast and during devotional retreat in the mosque. The gradual clarification of the times for eating, drinking, and abstaining shows that worship is governed by clear limits rather than unnecessary hardship. By warning believers not even to approach God’s limits, the verse calls them to conscientious self-restraint and awareness of God, so that fasting becomes a means of attaining genuine piety.

translation: And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, nor offer it to the authorities so that you may consume a portion of people’s wealth sinfully while you know.
interpretation: This verse forbids taking or transferring wealth through any unlawful means, including bribery, deceit, false claims, and manipulation of authorities. It warns that knowingly using legal power or public judgment to seize what belongs to others remains sinful, even if it is made to appear legitimate.

translation: They ask you about the new moons. Say, “They are markers of time for people and for the pilgrimage.” Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs; rather, righteousness is to be mindful of God. Enter houses through their doors, and be mindful of God so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Islam directs people toward practical signs and proper means in organizing their lives, while correcting superstitious customs that have no foundation in true righteousness. Real piety is not found in outward rituals or unconventional acts, but in reverent obedience to God. “Entering through the doors” also conveys the broader principle of approaching matters through their proper, honest, and lawful means, with God-consciousness as the path to success.

translation: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله الذين يقاتلونكم ولا تعتدوا ۚ إن الله لا يحب المعتدين
interpretation: يأذن الله للمؤمنين بقتال من يباشر قتالهم دفاعًا عن النفس والدين، لكنه ينهى عن تجاوز حدود العدل بالبدء بالعدوان أو استهداف من لا يقاتل أو ارتكاب الظلم؛ فالقوة لا تبرر التعدي، والله لا يحب المعتدين.

translation: And kill them wherever you encounter them, and drive them out from wherever they drove you out. Persecution is worse than killing. Do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there; but if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hostile persecutors who had expelled the believers and continued waging war against them; it is not a command to kill people merely for holding a different faith. It permits the believers to repel aggression and remove those responsible for their persecution, while affirming that persecution and preventing people from practicing their faith is more grievous than the killing that occurs in lawful defense. Even at the Sacred Mosque, fighting remains prohibited unless the opposing side initiates combat; only then may the believers respond proportionately.

translation: But if they desist, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: If those who oppose the truth abandon their hostility and wrongdoing, Allah will forgive what they have done and show them mercy, opening the way for repentance and reconciliation.

translation: Fight them until there is no persecution and devotion is wholly to Allah. But if they desist, then there is to be no hostility except against the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse permits fighting only to end persecution and coercion that obstructs people from freely following their faith, not as an unlimited command to attack others. Once the aggressors cease their persecution, fighting must also cease; continued hostility is unjust and applies only to those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: The sacred month is for the sacred month, and sacred things are subject to fair retribution. So whoever transgresses against you, then respond against them in proportion to the transgression they committed against you. And be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The verse establishes that even when defending oneself against wrongdoing, one must not exceed the limits of justice. Any response must remain strictly proportionate to the harm committed, without oppression, revenge, or excess. Reverence for Allah requires restraint and fairness, and those who maintain this consciousness can rely on His support.

translation: And spend in the way of Allah, and do not cast yourselves into destruction with your own hands. And do good; surely Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: This verse teaches that believers should devote their resources to what serves Allah’s cause and should not deliberately bring about their own ruin through reckless actions or neglect of their responsibilities. They are to act with wisdom, balance, and excellence, for Allah loves those whose conduct is beneficial and good.

translation: Complete the Hajj and the ‘Umrah for Allah. If you are prevented, then offer whatever sacrifice is readily available, and do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice. Whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the scalp must compensate by fasting, giving charity, or offering a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever performs the ‘Umrah followed by Hajj must offer whatever sacrifice is readily available; but whoever cannot find one must fast three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned—these are ten complete days. This applies to those whose families do not reside near the Sacred Mosque. And be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Hajj and ‘Umrah must be performed sincerely for Allah and completed according to their requirements, while also allowing genuine hardship to be met with regulated compensation. A pilgrim prevented from reaching the sanctuary offers a sacrifice and remains under the restrictions of pilgrimage until its proper time; illness or a scalp condition permits removal of the hair, provided the prescribed expiation is given. The allowance for tamattu‘—performing ‘Umrah and then Hajj in the same season—carries an offering, or fasting when one cannot provide it: three days during the pilgrimage and seven afterward. The ruling concerning the offering applies to those living outside the Sacred Precinct, and the closing warning teaches that these concessions do not lessen the duty of obedience, reverence, and careful observance of Allah’s limits.

translation: The pilgrimage is during well-known months. Whoever undertakes the pilgrimage in them must abstain from sexual relations, sin, and disputation during the pilgrimage. Whatever good you do, Allah knows it. And take provisions, for surely the best provision is mindfulness of Allah. So be mindful of Me, O people of understanding.
interpretation: The verse teaches that pilgrimage is not merely a physical journey but a disciplined act of worship requiring control of desire, speech, and conduct. Its true preparation is not only material provision but taqwa—constant awareness of Allah—which should guide the pilgrim’s behavior and choices throughout the journey.

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. Then, when you depart from ʿArafāt, remember Allah at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and remember Him as He has guided you, for indeed, before that you were surely among those astray.
interpretation: The verse teaches that lawful worldly effort, including trade, does not contradict sincere worship during pilgrimage, provided that the heart remains devoted to Allah. After standing at ʿArafāt, pilgrims are directed to remember Allah at the sacred site of Muzdalifah, recognizing that their rites and guidance are gifts from Him and responding with gratitude and obedient remembrance rather than relying on their own understanding.

translation: Then depart from where the people depart, and seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: After completing the standing at ʿArafah, believers are commanded to join the wider community in the prescribed rites rather than distinguish themselves through pride or self-importance, and to accompany their worship with sincere repentance, trusting in Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: فإذا أتممتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كما تذكرون آباءكم، بل أشدَّ ذكراً. فمن الناس من يقول: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا، وليس له في الآخرة من نصيب.
interpretation: توجّه الآية إلى أن تُستثمر العبادة في ترسيخ ذكر الله، وألا ينصرف القلب بعد أداء المناسك إلى التفاخر والاهتمامات الدنيوية كما كان الناس يتفاخرون بآبائهم. وتذمّ من يحصر دعاءه في متاع الدنيا، لأن هذا القصر يكشف غفلةً عن المصير الأبدي ويحرم صاحبه من نصيب الآخرة.

translation: And among them are those who say, “Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: This supplication teaches the believer to seek a balanced form of goodness: lawful well-being and blessing in worldly life, together with faith, righteousness, and salvation in the Hereafter, while recognizing that true success ultimately depends on being protected from the consequences of sin and disbelief.

translation: Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: Each person’s outcome is determined by what they have sincerely done, and nothing of their deeds is overlooked; Allah brings every account to completion with perfect justice and without delay.

translation: And remember Allah during the appointed days. Whoever hastens to leave after two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever stays longer, there is no sin upon him—provided he is mindful of Allah. And be mindful of Allah, and know that to Him you will all be gathered.
interpretation: The verse teaches that pilgrims may either depart from Mina after two days or remain longer, and neither choice is blameworthy when made within the prescribed rites and with sincere God-consciousness. The true measure is not the length of one’s stay, but obedience to Allah, remembrance of Him, and awareness that everyone will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: Among the people is one whose speech impresses you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents.
interpretation: The verse warns that eloquent speech and solemn claims of sincerity do not prove a person’s righteousness; someone may present himself as sincere while concealing deep hostility, so his true character is revealed by his conduct and its consequences rather than by his words alone.

translation: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to spread corruption therein and destroy crops and offspring. And Allah does not love corruption.
interpretation: This describes a person whose persuasive words conceal harmful intentions: once given power or left unchecked, he works to damage society, livelihoods, and future generations. The verse warns that true righteousness is measured by the effects of one’s actions, and that God rejects every form of destruction and corruption.

translation: And when it is said to him, “Fear Allah,” pride seizes him, driving him further into sin. Hell is sufficient for him—and what an evil resting place!
interpretation: This depicts a person whose arrogance prevents him from accepting sincere admonition: instead of abandoning wrongdoing out of reverence for Allah, he becomes more attached to sin. Such obstinate pride leads to the severe consequence of Hell.

translation: And among the people is one who offers his very self, seeking the pleasure of Allah; and Allah is Most Kind to His servants.
interpretation: This describes the sincere believer who willingly sacrifices his desires, comfort, possessions, and even life in obedience to Allah, seeking only His approval rather than worldly recognition. Allah, in His mercy and gentleness, does not let such devotion go unrewarded.

translation: O you who believe, enter into Islam wholeheartedly and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to embrace Islam completely—both in faith and in conduct—without selecting only what suits their desires. They should remain vigilant against Satan’s gradual temptations, which lead a person away from obedience and unity, because his hostility is clear and deliberate.

translation: But if you falter after the clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that knowingly departing from clear divine guidance is a serious lapse, while reminding them that God cannot be overcome or evaded and that His dealings—whether through warning, judgment, or mercy—are governed by perfect wisdom.

translation: Do they await anything but that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, with the angels, and the matter be decided? And to Allah all affairs return.
interpretation: The verse warns those who reject faith that they should not expect endless delay in accountability. It portrays the decisive manifestation of divine judgment, accompanied by the angels, when the final decree is carried out; then all matters will return to Allah, the ultimate Judge and Sovereign.

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them. And whoever exchanges Allah’s blessing after it has come to him—surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that receiving clear divine guidance is a profound blessing that carries the responsibility of accepting and preserving it. Deliberately rejecting, distorting, or replacing that blessing after recognizing its truth exposes a person to Allah’s severe punishment.

translation: The life of this world has been made alluring to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe. But those who are mindful of God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And God provides for whom He wills without measure.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly attractiveness can deceive those who reject faith into judging believers with mockery and contempt, yet this apparent advantage is temporary. On the Day of Resurrection, true honor and superiority will belong to those who remained mindful of God, while His provision—both worldly and everlasting—is granted according to His wisdom, without limit or calculation.

translation: Mankind was one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and He sent down with them the Scripture in truth, so that it might judge between people concerning that over which they differed. Yet none differed over it except those who had been given it, after clear proofs had come to them—out of jealous hostility among themselves. Then Allah guided those who believed, by His permission, to the truth concerning which they differed. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: Humanity’s original unity did not endure because people differed over truth and guidance. Allah therefore sent prophets and revealed Scripture to establish the standard by which disputes are judged, promising reward to those who follow it and warning those who reject it. The verse teaches that the gravest disagreements often arise not from lack of evidence, but from envy, rivalry, and the desire to preserve one’s own position after the truth has become clear. Those who sincerely believe and seek guidance are enabled by Allah to recognize the truth amid such disputes and remain upon the straight path.

translation: Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without experiencing what befell those who passed away before you? They were afflicted by hardship and suffering, and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, “When will the help of Allah come?” Surely, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is tested through severe hardship, fear, and distress; such trials do not mean that Allah’s support has been withdrawn. Rather, steadfastness amid them prepares believers for deliverance, which comes at the time appointed by Allah and is always near in His wisdom.

translation: They ask you what they should spend. Say: “Whatever good you spend should be for parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and stranded travelers.” Whatever good you do, surely Allah knows it well.
interpretation: This verse teaches that charitable spending should begin with those who have a rightful claim upon one’s care—especially parents and close relatives—and extend to vulnerable people such as orphans, the poor, and travelers in need. It also assures that no act of goodness is overlooked by Allah, whether or not people recognize it.

translation: Fighting has been prescribed for you, though it is hateful to you. Perhaps you dislike something while it is good for you, and perhaps you love something while it is bad for you. Allah knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse teaches that human judgment is limited: an obligation may feel difficult or unwelcome while carrying a greater good, and something desired may conceal harm. In its context, the prescribed fighting refers to the legitimate duty of defending the community against aggression under divine guidance, not to unrestricted violence. Believers are therefore called to submit to God’s wisdom, fulfill their responsibilities with restraint, and trust that His knowledge encompasses consequences beyond their own understanding.

translation: They ask you about fighting during the sacred month. Say, “Fighting in it is a grave matter; but barring people from Allah’s way, denying Him, preventing access to the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it are graver in Allah’s sight. Persecution is graver than killing.” They will not cease fighting you until they turn you away from your religion, if they are able. Whoever among you turns away from his religion and dies while disbelieving—their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the companions of the Fire, remaining there forever.
interpretation: The verse acknowledges that fighting during a sacred month is a serious violation, yet places it within the larger reality of persistent persecution: obstructing faith, denying God, barring worshippers from the Sacred Mosque, and forcibly expelling its people are even more grievous. It therefore responds to an accusation of wrongdoing by exposing the greater oppression that preceded it, while warning believers that those who abandon faith and die in disbelief forfeit the spiritual value of their deeds and their ultimate reward. The passage is not a license for indiscriminate violence; it addresses hostile persecution and emphasizes that the sanctity of religion, worship, and freedom of faith must not be violated.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, those who emigrate, and those who strive in the cause of Allah—it is they who hope for Allah’s mercy. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere hope in Allah’s mercy is grounded in faith demonstrated through sacrifice: leaving what hinders obedience and striving for His sake. Such deeds do not make a person independent of divine grace; rather, they place the believer among those who rightly hope for it, trusting that Allah forgives shortcomings and responds with mercy.

translation: They ask you about intoxicants and gambling. Say, “In both is great sin, and some benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.” And they ask you what they should spend. Say, “Whatever is beyond your needs.” Thus Allah makes the revelations clear to you so that you may reflect.
interpretation: Allah directs people to judge practices by their overall moral and social consequences: even when intoxicants and gambling offer temporary or limited benefits, the harm and sin they produce outweigh those benefits, making them worthy of abandonment. In financial giving, He teaches moderation and generosity by encouraging a person to give from what remains after meeting legitimate needs, so that reflection leads to both moral discipline and care for others.

translation: في الدنيا والآخرة. ويسألونك عن اليتامى، قل: إصلاح شؤونهم خير، وإن خالطتموهم فهم إخوانكم. والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح، ولو شاء الله لأعنتكم؛ إن الله عزيز حكيم.
interpretation: يبين الله أن رعاية اليتامى ينبغي أن تقوم على الإصلاح الحقيقي لمصلحتهم، لا على استغلال أموالهم أو التشدد في معاملتهم؛ فمخالطتهم في المعيشة جائزة حين تكون بروح الأخوة وحفظ الحقوق، والله وحده يعلم صدق النيات ويميز من يسعى إلى نفعهم ممن يفسد عليهم، وقد شرع ذلك بحكمة ورحمة دون أن يكلّف الناس ما يشق عليهم.

translation: Do not marry polytheist women until they believe. A believing bondwoman is better than a polytheist woman, even though she may impress you. And do not marry polytheist men until they believe. A believing bondman is better than a polytheist man, even though he may impress you. They invite to the Fire, while Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission. He makes His signs clear to the people so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith must take precedence over attraction, social status, freedom, or worldly appeal in marriage. A marriage bound to polytheism can draw a person toward values opposed to devotion to God, whereas genuine faith provides the spiritual foundation that leads toward divine forgiveness and Paradise; therefore believers are instructed to wait for faith rather than allow outward admiration to override religious commitment.

translation: They ask you about menstruation. Say, “It is a discomfort, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are purified. Then, when they have purified themselves, go to them as Allah has commanded you. Indeed, Allah loves those who constantly repent and loves those who purify themselves.”
interpretation: The verse establishes that menstruation is a temporary state requiring abstention from sexual intercourse until the bleeding has ended and purification has taken place; it does not command separation from women in any other form of companionship or care. Intimacy may then resume within the lawful boundaries ordained by Allah. Its conclusion teaches that bodily purification and sincere repentance are both acts beloved to Allah.

translation: Your wives are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation as you wish. Send ahead good for yourselves, remain mindful of Allah, and know that you will meet Him. And give glad tidings to the believers.
interpretation: The verse permits intimacy with one’s wife in whatever position one wishes, provided it is within the lawful place of marital intercourse. It also reminds spouses to approach marriage responsibly, seeking what benefits them in the Hereafter through righteousness, restraint, and obedience to Allah, knowing that they will ultimately stand before Him.

translation: Do not make Allah a pretext in your oaths to keep you from doing good, being mindful of Him, or making peace among people. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Do not use an oath sworn by Allah as an excuse to abandon righteous deeds, piety, or reconciliation. If an oath conflicts with what is good, it must not become a barrier to obeying Allah and repairing relations, for Allah hears the oaths people utter and knows their intentions.

translation: Allah does not hold you accountable for thoughtless utterances in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: Allah does not blame a person for an oath uttered casually or without real intention; accountability concerns deliberate commitments arising from sincere intent and inner resolve. His forgiveness and forbearance show that He does not hasten to punish, giving people the opportunity to correct themselves and fulfill their obligations.

translation: For those who swear to abstain from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. Then, if they return to them, surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse regulates a husband’s oath to avoid marital relations: he may not leave his wife suspended indefinitely, but is given four months to reconsider. If he ends the estrangement and resumes the marriage, he is not condemned for what occurred, for Allah forgives and shows mercy.

translation: And if they resolve upon divorce, then surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: When spouses reach a firm decision to end the marriage, they must recognize that Allah hears their words and knows their intentions and conduct; therefore, divorce should be approached with sincerity, justice, and accountability before Him.

translation: Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual cycles. It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they truly believe in Allah and the Last Day. Their husbands have the greater right to take them back during that period, if they genuinely seek reconciliation. Women have rights comparable to the obligations owed to them, according to what is fair and honorable; yet men have a degree of responsibility over them. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a waiting period after divorce so that pregnancy may be known and reconciliation may remain possible. It requires honesty about pregnancy and permits the husband to restore the marriage during this period only when his intention is genuine reform, not harm or manipulation. The reciprocal rights and duties of spouses are to be governed by fairness and customary decency, while the degree given to men is understood as an added responsibility and legal role within the family, not a license for oppression or the denial of women’s rights.

translation: Divorce may be pronounced twice; then either retain [your wife] honorably or release her with kindness. It is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they cannot uphold the limits set by Allah. If you fear that they cannot uphold Allah’s limits, then there is no blame upon either of them regarding what she gives up to obtain her release. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not transgress them. Whoever transgresses Allah’s limits—it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that divorce is not meant to be used impulsively or as a means of harm: after two revocable divorces, the husband must either preserve the marriage with honorable treatment or end it with dignity and fairness. Financial rights already granted to the wife may not be reclaimed as a form of pressure, except when the marriage has become so untenable that both spouses fear they cannot fulfill their duties and the wife willingly offers compensation to secure separation. By setting these boundaries, Allah protects both parties from injustice and commands that marital decisions be governed by restraint, kindness, and respect for one another’s rights.

translation: But if he divorces her, she is not lawful for him thereafter until she marries another husband. Then, if that husband divorces her, there is no blame upon the two of them if they return to one another, provided they believe they can uphold Allah’s limits. These are the limits set by Allah, which He makes clear to people who know.
interpretation: After a final divorce, the former spouses cannot simply resume their marriage as before; she must first enter a genuine marriage with another man, not a contrived arrangement intended to make her lawful again. If that marriage ends, they may remarry only when both sincerely believe they can fulfill the rights and responsibilities Allah has ordained, for His rulings are protective boundaries to be understood and respected rather than manipulated.

translation: When you divorce women and they have nearly reached the end of their waiting period, then either retain them honorably or release them honorably. Do not retain them to cause harm and transgress, for whoever does that has wronged himself. Do not take Allah’s verses as a joke. Remember Allah’s blessing upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, by which He admonishes you. Be mindful of Allah and know that Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse commands that divorce be handled with sincerity, dignity, and justice: a husband may reconcile only with the genuine intention of maintaining a sound marriage, or he must let the woman go without manipulation or harm. Using reconciliation merely to prolong suffering or control her is oppression and a violation of Allah’s guidance, whose seriousness believers must remember through gratitude, obedience, and awareness that Allah knows every intention and action.

translation: When you divorce women and they have reached the end of their waiting period, do not prevent them from marrying their former husbands if they mutually agree in a proper manner. This is an admonition for whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is purer and more wholesome for you; Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: The verse forbids families or guardians from using social pressure, resentment, or control to obstruct a divorced woman from returning to her former husband when both freely consent and the relationship can be restored honorably. It establishes that her marriage decision must be respected, while reminding believers that obedience to Allah’s guidance is more beneficial than acting on personal judgments or desires.

translation: Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for those who wish to complete the nursing period. The child’s father shall provide them with food and clothing according to what is reasonable. No soul is burdened beyond its capacity. Neither a mother nor a father shall be harmed on account of the child. The heir bears the same responsibility. If both parents wish to wean the child by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by another woman, there is no blame upon you, provided that you pay what you have agreed to in a fair manner. Be mindful of Allah and know that Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes a just and compassionate framework for caring for a child after separation or within the family: the mother’s nursing, the father’s financial duty, and the child’s welfare must all be protected without either parent using the child to harm or pressure the other. The nursing period may be completed for two years, or ended earlier through genuine mutual agreement and consultation, while alternative nursing is permitted when arranged fairly. Every obligation is measured by ability, and all parties are reminded that their treatment of one another and their fulfillment of these responsibilities are known to Allah.

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days. Then, when they have reached the end of their waiting period, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in a proper manner. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a widow must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days after her husband’s death before entering a new marriage. During this period, she refrains from remarriage and observes the prescribed mourning, allowing time for grief and ensuring clarity concerning pregnancy. Once the period ends, she may make lawful decisions about her life and marriage in a dignified and recognized manner, and the verse reminds the community that Allah knows their conduct and intentions.

translation: There is no blame upon you for indirectly expressing your desire to marry women or for keeping that desire concealed within yourselves. Allah knows that you will think of them, but do not make secret promises with them, except to speak in a decent manner. And do not resolve to عقد the marriage until the prescribed period reaches its end. Know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him; and know that Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse permits a man to convey, through dignified and indirect words, his interest in marrying a woman who is observing a waiting period, while recognizing that such thoughts may naturally arise. It forbids secret arrangements, intimate promises, or any commitment that could compromise the waiting period, allowing only honorable speech. The marriage contract must wait until the prescribed term has fully ended, teaching that private intentions are known to Allah and must therefore be governed by restraint, reverence, and respect for lawful boundaries; His forgiveness and forbearance leave room for sincere repentance and self-control.

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or stipulated for them a bridal gift. Yet provide for them—a provision according to the means of the affluent and according to the means of the poor—a fair provision, an obligation upon those who act with excellence.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a divorce before marital relations and before a dowry has been fixed carries no sin in itself, but it must not be carried out without consideration for the woman’s dignity and welfare. The husband is required to give her a suitable parting gift in keeping with his financial capacity, making kindness and generosity the standard even when the marriage ends.】【。

translation: And if you divorce them before you have touched them, while you have already stipulated for them a bridal gift, then half of what you stipulated is due—unless they waive it, or the one in whose hand is the marriage bond waives it. And to waive it is nearer to righteousness. Do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed, Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that when a marriage ends before consummation and a dowry was specified, the wife is entitled to half of that dowry, while allowing either party to relinquish their right voluntarily. It directs both spouses to act with generosity and goodwill rather than treating the legal entitlement as an occasion for hostility, reminding them that righteousness is shown through forgiveness and that Allah is fully aware of their conduct.

translation: Be mindful of all the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devout obedience.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to guard the prayers by performing them consistently and properly, giving particular care to the middle prayer, and to stand before Allah with humble, attentive obedience rather than distraction or heedlessness.

translation: But if you are in fear, then pray on foot or riding. And when you are secure, remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know.
interpretation: Even in circumstances of danger, prayer is not abandoned; it is performed according to one’s ability, whether walking or mounted. Once safety returns, worship should be restored to its proper form, with gratitude and remembrance of Allah, recognizing that every form of guidance and knowledge comes from Him.

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives should make a bequest for their wives: provision for one year, without being turned out. But if they leave of their own accord, then there is no blame upon you for what they reasonably do with themselves. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a safeguard for widows, ensuring that they are not deprived of housing and financial provision immediately after their husbands’ deaths and may remain for up to a year without being forced out. If they choose to leave, they are free to manage their lives in a proper and honorable manner, and others are not blameworthy for allowing this. The ruling reflects Allah’s protection of the vulnerable while affirming wisdom, dignity, and personal choice.

translation: And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is fair—a duty upon the God-conscious.
interpretation: Divorce should not leave a woman without dignified support; she is entitled to a reasonable provision suited to the circumstances, and fulfilling this obligation reflects true piety and moral responsibility.

translation: Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you, so that you may understand.
interpretation: Allah clarifies His guidance and rulings in a clear way so that people will use their reason, recognize the wisdom behind them, and live according to what He has revealed.

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in their thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, “Die,” then He brought them back to life. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that life and death are entirely under Allah’s command, and that fleeing from a divinely decreed fate cannot ultimately avert it. By restoring those who had died, Allah demonstrated His power over resurrection and reminded humanity that every blessing—including life itself—is a favor from Him, deserving gratitude and obedience rather than heedlessness.

translation: And fight in the cause of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This commands believers to struggle in Allah’s cause under His guidance, with sincere intentions and disciplined conduct, while remembering that Allah hears every word and knows every motive and action.

translation: Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over? Allah withholds and gives abundantly, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Allah describes sincere charity and spending for His sake as a “loan” even though everything already belongs to Him, promising to repay it with multiplied reward. The verse teaches that wealth and provision are in Allah’s control: He may restrict them or expand them as a test, so believers should give generously and trust His promise, knowing that all will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to one of their prophets, “Appoint for us a king so that we may fight in the cause of Allah”? He said, “Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you?” They said, “Why should we not fight in the cause of Allah, when we have been driven from our homes and separated from our children?” But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away—except for a few of them. And Allah knows the wrongdoers well.
interpretation: The verse reveals that sincere commitment is proven by obedience when sacrifice becomes real, not by confident words beforehand. The Israelites claimed readiness to fight after suffering oppression, yet most abandoned their pledge when the duty was imposed; thus Allah identifies their desertion as wrongdoing and shows that He fully knows the difference between genuine resolve and empty claims.

translation: And their prophet said to them, “Indeed, Allah has appointed Saul as your king.” They said, “How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than he, and he has not been granted abundant wealth?” He said, “Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physical strength. Allah grants His kingdom to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.”
interpretation: Legitimate leadership is not established by wealth, status, or people’s claims of entitlement; it is granted by Allah according to wisdom. Knowledge and sound capability are greater qualifications for authority than material abundance, while Allah’s choice is based on His complete wisdom and knowledge.

translation: And their prophet said to them, “The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord and remnants of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The return of the Ark, bearing sacred remnants and divine tranquility, was a miraculous confirmation that God had chosen Saul to lead them. It reassured the believers that his authority came from God rather than from wealth, lineage, or human preference.

translation: And when Saul set out with the troops, he said, “Indeed, Allah is testing you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is truly of me—except for one who takes only a handful with his hand.” Yet they drank from it, except for a few of them. Then, when he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said, “We have no strength today against Goliath and his troops.” Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said, “How often a small group has overcome a large group by Allah’s permission. And Allah is with those who remain steadfast.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine testing reveals the sincerity and discipline of faith: victory is not granted to those who merely claim allegiance, but to those who restrain themselves when obedience becomes difficult. The few who endured the test understood that strength does not depend on numbers or material power; reliance on Allah, steadfastness, and certainty of accountability before Him can enable a faithful minority to overcome a stronger force by His permission.

translation: And when they went forth to confront Goliath and his troops, they said, “Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make our feet firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
interpretation: This prayer teaches that true courage in the face of overwhelming opposition is grounded in reliance on God: believers seek steadfast patience, firmness in action, and victory for the truth rather than trusting solely in their own strength.

translation: So they defeated them by Allah’s permission, and David killed Goliath. Allah granted him kingship and wisdom and taught him whatever He willed. Had Allah not restrained some people through others, the earth would surely have been corrupted; but Allah is full of فضل toward all worlds.
interpretation: The verse teaches that victory comes by Allah’s permission, even when carried out through human courage and effort. David’s triumph became the means through which Allah granted him authority and wisdom, showing that power is rightly joined to moral and intellectual guidance. It also establishes that Allah preserves the earth from widespread corruption by opposing forces of injustice with forces that restrain them; this protection is an expression of His encompassing favor toward creation.

translation: These are the verses of Allah that We recite to you in truth, and surely you are among the messengers.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the revelation conveyed to the Prophet is the truth, and confirms his genuine mission as one of His appointed messengers.

translation: Those messengers—We have favored some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and some He raised in rank. We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. Had Allah willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after clear proofs had come to them. But they differed: some believed and some disbelieved. Had Allah willed, they would not have fought one another; but Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: Allah has honored all His messengers while granting some distinct virtues, signs, and degrees according to His wisdom. The clear proofs brought by the messengers were sufficient to guide people, yet later generations fell into conflict because of their differing responses—some submitting to faith and others rejecting it. Their disputes and violence were not beyond Allah’s power to prevent, but He allows human choices to unfold within His will, thereby revealing the consequences of faith, denial, and division.

translation: O you who believe, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there will be neither trade, friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers—they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to use the wealth and blessings entrusted to them in acts of charity and obedience before death and the Day of Judgment, when worldly means of rescue will disappear. No wealth can purchase salvation, no relationship can secure it, and no intercession can benefit those who reject faith; their wrongdoing lies in denying the truth and failing to fulfill their duty to God.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursī encompasses the heavens and the earth, and preserving them does not weary Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse establishes Allah’s absolute oneness, perfect life, and complete sovereignty. His sustaining care is constant and never interrupted by weakness, drowsiness, or sleep. All creation belongs to Him, and no one can intercede independently of His permission. His knowledge encompasses every aspect of creation, while created beings know only what He chooses to disclose. The vastness of the heavens and the earth remains entirely within His dominion, and maintaining them causes Him no fatigue; therefore, He alone deserves ultimate worship, trust, and reverence.

translation: There is no compulsion in religion. The right path has become distinct from error. So whoever rejects false deities and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold, which will never break. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Faith is meaningful only when embraced freely and consciously, not imposed by force. Since truth has been made clear from falsehood, a person must turn away from every power or object of devotion that rivals Allah and place complete trust in Him. This commitment gives the believer an unbreakable bond of guidance and protection, while Allah fully knows and hears the sincerity of every heart.

translation: Allah is the Protector of those who believe: He brings them out of darknesses into the light. As for those who disbelieve, their protectors are false deities; they bring them out of the light into darknesses. They are the companions of the Fire; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: The verse portrays faith as a divinely guided movement from the many darknesses of disbelief, confusion, and moral deviation into the single light of truth and guidance. Allah leads believers through this transformation, while those who reject Him entrust themselves to false authorities and desires that draw them away from truth into increasing error. Their final ruin is a consequence of choosing those false loyalties instead of divine guidance.

translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because Allah had granted him sovereignty? When Abraham said, “My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death,” he replied, “I give life and cause death.” Abraham said, “Then indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.” Thus the one who disbelieved was confounded. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of prideful argument when worldly authority leads a person to challenge divine truth. Abraham distinguishes Allah’s absolute power over life, death, and the order of creation from the ruler’s merely figurative claim, then confronts him with an undeniable sign that lies beyond human control. His inability to respond reveals that rejection of truth is not caused by lack of evidence, but by injustice and arrogant refusal to submit; therefore such people deprive themselves of divine guidance.

translation: Or consider the one who passed by a town lying in ruins, with its roofs collapsed, and said, “How will Allah bring this to life after its death?” So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him. He asked, “How long have you remained?” He replied, “I remained for a day, or part of a day.” He said, “Rather, you have remained for a hundred years. Look at your food and drink—they have not spoiled. And look at your donkey. We have made you a sign for the people. Look at the bones, how We raise them up and then clothe them with flesh.” When this became clear to him, he said, “I know that Allah is capable of all things.”
interpretation: The verse presents a direct demonstration that resurrection is entirely within Allah’s power: He preserves what normally perishes while allowing the body and bones to be restored before the observer’s eyes. The man’s initial question is answered not by argument alone, but by an experience that transforms uncertainty into certain knowledge of Allah’s ability to bring the dead back to life.

translation: And when Abraham said, “My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.” He said, “Do you not believe?” Abraham said, “Yes indeed, but so that my heart may be reassured.” He said, “Then take four birds, draw them close to you, then place a part of them on each mountain; afterward call them, and they will come to you swiftly. And know that Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
interpretation: Abraham’s request was not born of doubt in Allah’s power, but from a desire for deeper inward certainty and tranquillity. Allah answered him through a visible sign: the scattered parts of the birds were restored and returned at His command. The verse teaches that faith may seek increased reassurance without denying belief, while affirming that Allah’s power is absolute and His acts are governed by perfect wisdom.

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears, with a hundred grains in each ear. Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Sincere charitable giving for Allah’s sake is never diminished; its spiritual reward may be multiplied far beyond the amount given, according to Allah’s wisdom, generosity, and knowledge of the giver’s intention and deed.

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders of their generosity or harm—they will have their reward with their Lord. No fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: True charity is preserved by sincerity: the giver should not remind the recipient of the favor or cause them pain through reproach, humiliation, or any other injury. Such giving is for Allah alone, so its reward remains secure with Him, and the sincere giver is granted reassurance and freedom from regret in the Hereafter.

translation: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurt. And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: Giving is only virtuous when it preserves the recipient’s dignity; a gracious word or overlooking a fault is better than charity that is later spoiled by reproach, humiliation, or harm. Allah has no need of anyone’s charity and patiently gives people time to act with sincerity and kindness.

translation: O you who believe, do not nullify your charitable deeds by reminders of your generosity and hurtful words, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people while believing neither in Allah nor in the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth stone covered with soil: a heavy downpour strikes it and leaves it bare and hard. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that charity is accepted only when it is offered sincerely for Allah’s sake and accompanied by respect for the recipient. Reminding others of one’s generosity or causing them emotional harm strips the deed of its spiritual value, just as rain washes the thin soil from a smooth stone, leaving nothing behind. Acts performed for reputation rather than faith may appear substantial to people, but they yield no lasting reward with Allah.

translation: And the likeness of those who spend their wealth seeking Allah’s pleasure and strengthening their souls is that of a garden on elevated ground, struck by abundant rain, so it yields twice its produce. If abundant rain does not reach it, then a drizzle suffices. And Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: Sincere charity, offered for Allah’s pleasure and with inner conviction rather than ostentation or compulsion, is like a garden planted in a favorable place: abundant blessings make it flourish greatly, yet even modest blessings are enough for it to produce. In the same way, a sincere act of giving bears lasting spiritual reward regardless of whether the outward circumstances are abundant or limited, because Allah fully knows the intention and deeds behind it.

translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it and every kind of fruit for him, then be overtaken by old age while he has weak offspring, and a fiery whirlwind strikes it and burns it up? Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you so that you may reflect.
interpretation: الله يضرب مثلاً للعمل الصالح الذي يُفسده صاحبه بالرياء أو المنّ والأذى؛ فكما أن احتراق الجنة عند حاجة صاحبها إليها خسارة مؤلمة، كذلك يكتشف الإنسان يوم القيامة ضياع أعماله حين يكون أحوج ما يكون إلى ثوابها، ولذلك ينبغي أن يخلص عمله ويحفظه من أسباب الإبطال.

translation: O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. Do not deliberately choose the inferior of it to spend, when you yourselves would not accept it except by overlooking its defects. And know that Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to give from wealth that is lawful, wholesome, and genuinely valuable, rather than offering what they themselves consider defective or undesirable. Charity should reflect sincere respect for those who receive it, not an attempt to dispose of inferior goods; Allah has no need of anyone’s giving, but He praises and rewards generosity offered with integrity.

translation: Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Satan instills fear of losing wealth in order to discourage generosity and obedience, and he urges people toward every shameful act. Allah, by contrast, assures those who give and obey Him of forgiveness for their sins and abundant provision and reward. His bounty is limitless, and He knows the sincerity, needs, and deeds of His servants.

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He wills; and whoever is granted wisdom has certainly been given abundant good. Yet none take heed except those possessed of sound understanding.
interpretation: True wisdom is a profound divine gift that enables a person to discern truth, act rightly, and recognize the lasting good in obedience to God; only those who use their intellect with humility truly benefit from it.

translation: Whatever you spend of wealth or make of vows, surely Allah knows it; and the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: Every act of spending and every vow is fully known to Allah, including its purpose and sincerity. Therefore, good deeds should be offered seeking His pleasure, while those who persist in injustice cannot rely on anyone to protect them from its consequences.

translation: If you disclose your charitable giving, it is commendable; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, that is better for you, and He will erase some of your sins. Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: Giving charity openly is permissible and good when it encourages others or serves a beneficial public purpose, but concealing it is better when doing so protects the recipient’s dignity and preserves the giver’s sincerity. Charity offered purely for Allah’s sake becomes a means of forgiveness, while Allah knows both the outward act and the inner intention behind it.

translation: Their guidance is not your responsibility, but Allah guides whom He wills. Whatever good you spend is for your own benefit, and you do not spend except seeking the Face of Allah. Whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: You are responsible for sincerely conveying the truth and giving for Allah’s sake, not for controlling people’s faith or securing their acceptance. Charity is ultimately an investment in your own nearness to Allah, and every sincere gift will be fully rewarded without any loss or injustice.

translation: For the poor who are confined in the way of Allah, unable to travel through the land; the unaware may think them self-sufficient because of their restraint. You will recognize them by their distinctive signs; they do not ask people persistently. Whatever good you spend, surely Allah knows it well.
interpretation: This verse directs charity toward dignified people whose devotion or circumstances have prevented them from earning a livelihood, yet who preserve their self-respect and do not burden others through persistent begging. Their need may be hidden beneath modesty, so believers are urged to look beyond appearances and give with attentiveness and sincerity, knowing that Allah fully recognizes every charitable act.

translation: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, privately and openly, will have their reward with their Lord; no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse praises those who give sincerely and consistently for the sake of God, whether their charity is hidden or public and whether given at any time. Their reward is assured with Him, and their trust in His promise brings them security from future fear and sorrow over what has passed.

translation: Those who consume usury will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch. That is because they say, “Trade is only like usury,” while Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury. Whoever receives admonition from his Lord and then desists may keep what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns to it—those are the companions of the Fire; they will remain therein forever.
interpretation: The verse condemns usury as an unjust gain that exploits people and corrupts the moral purpose of wealth, rejecting the claim that it is equivalent to lawful trade.
