Trade involves the exchange of goods, effort, and risk by mutual agreement, whereas usury secures an increase on a debt without sharing the borrower’s hardship or loss. Allah therefore distinguishes clearly between permissible commerce and forbidden financial exploitation. Whoever sincerely abandons usury after receiving this warning is not required to undo what occurred before the prohibition, while continuing or returning to it is presented as a grave spiritual danger whose consequence is the Fire.

translation: Allah erases usury and causes charitable offerings to grow. Allah does not love anyone persistently ungrateful and sinful.
interpretation: Allah removes blessing from wealth acquired through usury, so that its apparent increase ultimately leads to loss, while He blesses charity and causes its benefit and reward to increase. The verse warns that knowingly persisting in usury, denying Allah’s guidance, and engaging in sin places a person among those whom Allah does not love.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord. No fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: True faith is expressed through consistent righteous action and sincere devotion, especially by maintaining prayer and fulfilling the duty of zakah. Such people are assured of divine reward, security from the terrors of what lies ahead, and freedom from sorrow over what they have left behind.

translation: O believers, be mindful of Allah and give up whatever remains of usury, if you are truly believers.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to abandon all outstanding usurious claims, making sincere faith inseparable from obedience to Allah’s prohibition of riba. It calls them to relinquish unlawful financial gain out of reverence for Allah, rather than continuing to benefit from it while merely claiming belief.

translation: But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, then you may have your principal sums—you will neither wrong nor be wronged.
interpretation: This is a grave warning against persisting in usury: those who abandon it may reclaim only the original capital, without demanding an increase or suffering an unjust loss. Justice requires that neither party exploit nor be exploited.

translation: And if the debtor is in hardship, then grant him respite until ease. But if you remit it as charity, that is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: This verse teaches that financial dealings must be governed by mercy and justice: a debtor who genuinely cannot repay should be given time until their circumstances improve, while voluntarily forgiving the debt is an even greater act of generosity and righteousness.

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse calls people to remain conscious of Allah by remembering the inevitable return to Him, where each person will receive the complete and exact consequence of their deeds. Allah’s judgment will be perfectly just: no good deed will be diminished, no sin will be increased beyond its due, and no one will be treated unfairly.

translation: O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. Let a scribe record it between you with justice, and let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the debtor dictate, and let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it. If the debtor is foolish, weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice. Call upon two witnesses from among your men; and if two men are not available, then one man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, the other may remind her. Let the witnesses not refuse when they are called. Do not become weary of writing the debt, whether small or great, along with its term. That is more just in the sight of Allah, more upright for testimony, and more likely to prevent doubt between you. However, if it is an immediate trade that you conduct among yourselves, there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. Yet take witnesses when you conclude a sale. Let neither scribe nor witness be harmed; if you do so, it is sinful disobedience on your part. And fear Allah; Allah teaches you, and Allah knows all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive ethic for financial dealings: rights are protected by clear documentation, defined deadlines, honest dictation by the party who owes, and reliable testimony. Responsibility is adapted when a person lacks the capacity to speak for himself, while those who record or testify must remain impartial and must not be pressured or harmed. The allowance for ordinary immediate transactions reflects practical ease, not a relaxation of justice. Beneath these procedures is the principle that preserving trust and preventing disputes are acts of obedience to Allah, whose knowledge and instruction should govern every contract.

translation: And if you are traveling and cannot find a scribe, then a pledge in hand may serve as security. But if some of you entrust others, then let the one who is entrusted fulfill the trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony; whoever conceals it—surely his heart is sinful. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that financial dealings must be protected by trustworthy measures, while making clear that documentation and collateral are safeguards rather than substitutes for faithfulness. When trust is given, fulfilling it becomes a religious duty before Allah, and concealing truthful testimony is not merely an outward wrongdoing but a corruption of the heart for which a person is accountable.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills; and Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse establishes Allah’s absolute ownership and complete knowledge of both outward actions and inward realities. It warns that hidden intentions and deliberate inner choices are not beyond His judgment, while affirming that forgiveness and punishment remain subject to His wisdom and authority—not to anything that escapes His knowledge or power.

translation: The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. All believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers, saying, “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” And they say, “We hear and obey. Our Lord, we seek Your forgiveness, and to You is the final return.”
interpretation: This verse portrays true faith as wholehearted acceptance of divine revelation: belief in Allah necessarily includes belief in the unseen realities and all messengers without rejecting or ranking any of them in respect of their truth. Such faith is expressed through willing obedience rather than mere acknowledgment, while remaining accompanied by humility, repentance, and reliance on Allah in anticipation of the final return to Him.

translation: God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It will have the reward of what good it has earned, and it will bear the consequence of what evil it has acquired. Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not place upon us a burden as You placed upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s commands and trials are measured with perfect justice according to each person’s capacity, and that every person is accountable for their own choices. It also teaches believers to turn to God with humility, asking that their honest mistakes and forgetfulness not be treated like deliberate wrongdoing, that they be spared unbearable obligations and hardships, and that divine pardon, forgiveness, mercy, protection, and support accompany them in resisting rejection of the truth.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: Alif, Lām, and Mīm are among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters; their precise meaning is known to Allah alone, and their opening placement directs attention to the Qur’an’s extraordinary revelation through the ordinary letters of human speech.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah alone deserves worship: He possesses perfect, everlasting life and continuously sustains, governs, and preserves all creation, while He Himself depends on nothing.

translation: He has sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: God affirms that the Qur’an is a true revelation from Him and that it confirms the original divine guidance contained in the Torah and the Gospel, showing that the prophets’ messages share one source and essential truth.

translation: Previously, as guidance for humanity, and He sent down the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Almighty, Possessor of retribution.
interpretation: Allah’s revelations have consistently served as guidance and as the decisive standard distinguishing truth from falsehood. Rejecting His signs after they have been made clear is not a minor error, but a grave act deserving punishment; Allah’s absolute power ensures that no such rejection escapes His just reckoning.

translation: Indeed, nothing at all is hidden from Allah, whether on earth or in heaven.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses every matter in existence, whether visible or concealed, so nothing escapes His awareness or occurs outside His perfect knowledge.

translation: هو الذي يصوّركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء، لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن تكوين الإنسان وتقدير صفاته وهيئته في رحم أمه واقع تحت مشيئته وعلمه وحكمته، فلا شريك له في الخلق والتدبير؛ ولذلك يستحق وحده العبادة، فهو العزيز الذي لا يُغلب، والحكيم الذي يضع كل أمر في موضعه.

translation: It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise and clear—they are the foundation of the Book—and others that are allegorical or open to interpretation. As for those whose hearts are inclined to deviation, they pursue what is allegorical in it, seeking discord and seeking to impose their own interpretation. Yet none knows its ultimate interpretation except Allah. And those firmly grounded in knowledge say, “We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.” But only people of sound understanding take heed.
interpretation: The Qur’an contains clear teachings that establish its essential guidance, alongside passages whose full reality or intended details are not accessible with certainty. The verse condemns the misuse of such passages by people who seek confusion or support for their desires, and presents sincere scholarship as humility: affirming the entire revelation, accepting what is clear, and refraining from forcing uncertain matters into claims beyond human knowledge.

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Your presence. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This is a humble prayer asking God to preserve the heart’s faith and steadfastness, since guidance is a continual gift that can be lost through pride, doubt, or turning away. It also asks for divine mercy to sustain obedience and renew spiritual strength, acknowledging that every blessing is granted by God alone.

translation: Our Lord, surely You will gather all people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah never breaks His promise.
interpretation: This is a declaration of certainty in the Resurrection and the final gathering, affirming that God’s promised judgment is unavoidable and that His word is completely trustworthy.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth and their children will never avail them against Allah in the least. It is they who are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly possessions and family status cannot protect a person from divine judgment when faith is rejected. Their inability to help reflects that ultimate security comes not from material means or lineage, but from sincere faith and obedience to Allah.

translation: Like the manner of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent denial of divine signs and deliberate wrongdoing follow the same destructive pattern seen in earlier nations. Their worldly power could not protect them from accountability; Allah’s punishment is severe for those who knowingly reject truth and persist in sin.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve: “You will be defeated and gathered to Hell—what an evil resting place.”
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject the truth and persist in opposition will ultimately suffer defeat in this world and be brought together for punishment in the Hereafter, where Hell will be their wretched and permanent abode.

translation: There has already been a sign for you in the two forces that met: one force fighting in the cause of Allah, and the other disbelieving. They saw them as twice their number with their own eyes. And Allah supports with His victory whomever He wills. Surely in that is a lesson for those who possess insight.
interpretation: This verse directs believers to recognize in the encounter between the two forces that victory and strength do not depend solely on apparent numbers or material power. Allah may grant support to those who strive in His cause, making the outcome a visible sign of His power and a lesson for people of sound discernment: they should trust Him, remain steadfast in righteousness, and not be deceived by outward worldly calculations.

translation: Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up stores of gold and silver, fine horses, livestock, and crops. That is the enjoyment of the life of this world, while with Allah is the finest return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly attractions naturally appear appealing, but their pleasure is temporary and limited; therefore, a person must not let attachment to wealth, family, status, or possessions distract from seeking Allah, whose reward and final return are far better.

translation: Say, “Shall I inform you of something better than all that? For those who are mindful of Allah are gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, abiding therein forever, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of His servants.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the lasting reward prepared for those who remain conscious of Allah is far superior to the temporary attractions of worldly life: eternal bliss, purified companionship, and—greater than all of these—the pleasure and acceptance of Allah. His complete sight of His servants affirms that He knows their faith, intentions, and deeds and rewards them with perfect justice and mercy.

translation: Those who say, “Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: This portrays sincere faith as inseparable from humble repentance: believers rely on God’s mercy, acknowledge their need for forgiveness, and seek His protection from the consequences of sin.

translation: The patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, those who spend [in charity], and those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn.
interpretation: This describes people whose faith is reflected in steadfastness during hardship, sincerity in speech and conduct, humble obedience to God, generous care for others, and private repentance—especially in the quiet moments before dawn, when they sincerely seek God’s forgiveness.

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and so do the angels and those endowed with knowledge—He upholds justice. There is no deity except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the oneness of Allah is established by His own testimony and confirmed by the angels and people of knowledge. His unity is inseparable from His perfect justice: He governs all things with fairness and wisdom, possessing absolute power without ever acting unjustly.

translation: Indeed, the religion accepted by Allah is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of mutual transgression. And whoever rejects Allah’s signs—surely Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse establishes that true religion is sincere submission to Allah and obedience to His revealed guidance. It explains that the disputes of the People of the Scripture arose not from a lack of evidence, but from envy, rivalry, and injustice after the truth had become known. Therefore, rejecting Allah’s clear signs is a grave act for which accountability before Him is certain and swift.

translation: So if they argue with you, say, “I have submitted my face to Allah, and so have those who follow me.” And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, “Have you submitted yourselves?” If they submit, they will be rightly guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey the message. And Allah sees His servants well.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the truth of faith is sincere submission to Allah, demonstrated by the Prophet and those who follow him, not victory in argument. The invitation is extended to all people, whether they possess earlier revelation or not, while guidance remains their choice. The Messenger’s responsibility is to communicate clearly, whereas Allah knows every person’s response and judges them with full awareness.

translation: Indeed, those who reject the signs of Allah, kill the prophets without right, and kill those among people who command justice—give them news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that denying divine guidance becomes especially grave when it is joined with violent opposition to those who convey it and those who call society to justice. Such people are condemned because they suppress truth and righteousness through persecution and murder; the painful punishment is a fitting consequence of their deliberate rebellion against Allah and their oppression of His servants.

translation: They are the ones whose deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth has deprived their deeds of any lasting spiritual reward or benefit, both in worldly life and in the Hereafter, and no one will be able to protect them from the consequences of their choice.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, being invited to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them, then a group of them turns away, refusing?
interpretation: The verse censures those who claim to follow divine revelation yet reject its judgment when it conflicts with their desires or interests. True faith requires willingly submitting disputes to Allah’s revealed guidance, whereas turning away from it exposes a contradiction between one’s religious claim and one’s conduct.

translation: That is because they say, “The Fire will never touch us except for a few numbered days,” and what they used to fabricate deceived them regarding their religion.
interpretation: They were misled by the false belief that punishment would be brief and limited, relying on claims they had invented rather than sincere obedience to God. Their self-deception made them complacent about wrongdoing and the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: How will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly claims, excuses, and false hopes will have no value on the Day of Judgment. Every person will stand before God and receive the complete consequence of their deeds with perfect justice, without anything being withheld from them or added to their account.

translation: Say: “O Allah, Sovereign of all sovereignty, You grant authority to whom You will and take authority away from whom You will; You honor whom You will and humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Surely You are powerful over everything.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that all power, authority, honor, and humiliation ultimately belong to Allah and unfold according to His wisdom. Human beings may possess influence temporarily, but it is granted and withdrawn by Him; therefore one should not be arrogant when favored, despair when deprived, or seek dignity through rebellion against Him. The affirmation that all good is in His hand directs the believer to trust His decree while asking Him for beneficial authority, lasting honor, and protection from the misuse or loss of blessings.

translation: You cause the night to enter into the day, and You cause the day to enter into the night; You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living; and You provide for whom You will without measure.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah alone governs the continual transformation of creation and the alternation of its conditions. Just as He brings life from death and death from life, He can change circumstances in ways beyond human expectation, and His provision is granted by wisdom and generosity rather than being limited by any worldly measure.

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as protectors instead of the believers. Whoever does so has no connection with Allah whatsoever—unless you fear harm from them and thus act cautiously. Allah warns you to beware of Him, and to Allah is the final return.
interpretation: The verse forbids believers from giving their ultimate loyalty, protection, and intimate allegiance to those who oppose the faith in a way that undermines the community of believers. It does not prohibit justice, kindness, or peaceful dealings with non-believers; rather, it permits cautious concealment or guarded conduct when believers face genuine danger. The warning that Allah knows and judges these loyalties calls believers to place obedience to Him above fear of people, while remembering that everyone will ultimately return to Him.

translation: Say, “Whether you conceal what is within your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. Allah is Powerful over all things.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that God’s knowledge encompasses not only outward actions but also the thoughts, intentions, and feelings hidden within people; therefore, no secret can escape His awareness or judgment, because His power extends over all existence.

translation: On the Day every soul will find whatever good it has done brought before it, and whatever evil it has done as well; it will wish that there were a great distance between itself and that evil. Allah warns you about Himself, and Allah is Most Compassionate toward His servants.
interpretation: The verse portrays the unavoidable encounter with one’s deeds in the Hereafter: good will be present as a source of comfort, while evil will become so distressing that its perpetrator will long to be utterly separated from it. Allah’s warning is therefore a merciful call to turn away from wrongdoing before that day, for His compassion is shown by giving people the opportunity to repent and reform.

translation: Say, “If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: Love of Allah is not merely a claim of the heart; it is proven by following the Messenger ﷺ in faith, worship, character, and conduct. Such sincere following brings the servant Allah’s love and becomes a means for the forgiveness of sins, for Allah is abundant in forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Say, “Obey Allah and the Messenger.” But if they turn away, then surely Allah does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah is inseparable from obedience to His Messenger; turning away from this command is not a minor act of disobedience, but a rejection of faith that places a person outside Allah’s love.

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of عمران (Imran) above all worlds.
interpretation: Allah declares that He selected these honored individuals and families for distinction among humanity, granting them revelation, faith, righteousness, and the responsibility of guiding others. Their elevation is not merely a privilege of lineage, but a divine trust reflected in their obedience and service to the truth.

translation: Descendants, one from another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: They were a righteous lineage whose faith and virtue were connected across generations; Allah knows the sincerity of their hearts and hears their prayers and words.

translation: When the wife of ʿImrān said, “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, wholly devoted to Your service, so accept it from me. Indeed, You alone are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: This expresses the sincere dedication of an unborn child to God’s worship and service. The mother entrusts her vow to God, seeking His acceptance while affirming that He hears her prayer and knows the sincerity of her intention.

translation: When she gave birth to her, she said, “My Lord, I have given birth to a female”—and Allah knew best what she had given birth to—“and the male is not like the female. I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge in You for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”
interpretation: This verse portrays Mary’s mother surrendering her expectations to Allah’s decree: she had hoped to dedicate a son to sacred service, yet Allah chose a daughter whose role and honor would surpass what she had imagined. Her naming of Mary and her prayer for protection show her entrusting the child and her future descendants to Allah, seeking that they remain safeguarded from Satan and devoted to righteousness.

translation: So her Lord accepted her with gracious acceptance, caused her to grow in a beautiful manner, and placed her under the care of Zechariah. Whenever Zechariah entered the sanctuary to visit her, he found provision with her. He said, “O Mary, where has this come from?” She said, “It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.”
interpretation: Allah honored Maryam by accepting her devotion, nurturing her spiritually and physically, and placing her in the care of a righteous guardian. The provision found with her was a sign of Allah’s special care and of His ability to sustain His servants through means beyond ordinary expectation. Maryam’s answer affirms that all provision ultimately comes from Allah, who grants it freely and abundantly according to His wisdom, without being limited by human calculation.

translation: Thereupon Zechariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord, grant me from Your grace a righteous offspring. Surely, You are All-Hearing of prayer.”
interpretation: Having witnessed Allah’s special provision for Mary, Zechariah was inspired to turn to Him with humble hope. His prayer shows that righteous children are a divine gift, and that no circumstance prevents Allah from answering a sincere supplication.

translation: Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: “Indeed, Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, and he will be a leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”
interpretation: This verse announces to Zakariyya that his son Yahya will be distinguished by faithfulness to Allah’s revelation, moral purity, leadership in righteousness, and prophetic integrity; his mission will affirm the truth of the divine word brought by the prophets.

translation: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?” He said, “Thus does Allah do whatever He wills.”
interpretation: Zakariyya’s question expresses astonishment at the fulfillment of a seemingly impossible promise, not rejection of it. The response teaches that Allah’s creative power is not constrained by ordinary causes, age, or human impossibility; His will is sufficient to bring about what He decrees.

translation: He said, “My Lord, appoint for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gestures. And remember your Lord abundantly and glorify Him in the evening and at dawn.”
interpretation: Zakariyya’s temporary inability to speak was a divine sign confirming the promised miracle, while directing him to respond not with ordinary speech but with abundant remembrance and praise of Allah at all times, especially at the beginning and end of the day.

translation: And when the angels said, “O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse declares Mary’s exceptional honor before God: He selected her for a noble mission, purified her in faith and character, and granted her a distinction surpassing that of all other women of her time and, according to the encompassing wording, of all worlds.

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow.
interpretation: Mary is instructed to devote herself wholly to God through persistent worship and humble submission, joining the community of worshippers rather than treating her spiritual distinction as a reason for separation or pride.

translation: That is from the news of the unseen, which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens to determine which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they argued.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet’s knowledge of Mary’s guardianship and the dispute among her caretakers came through divine revelation, not personal observation or human instruction. By mentioning these hidden events, Allah establishes the truth of the Prophet’s message and shows that He alone discloses the unseen as He wills.

translation: When the angels said, “O Mary, God gives you good news of a word from Him: his name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, honored in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near to God.”
interpretation: The verse conveys God’s announcement to Mary of the miraculous birth and distinguished mission of Jesus. He is called a “word from Him” because he comes into existence by God’s command, without a human father. His honor in this world and the Hereafter signifies his noble status, truthfulness, and lasting recognition, while being among those brought near to God indicates his exceptional spiritual rank and closeness through devotion and obedience.

translation: And he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This signifies that Jesus will be granted an extraordinary sign by speaking while still an infant, and that his speech and conduct in adulthood will reflect wisdom, truth, and righteousness; his life will remain under God’s guidance and among His devoted servants.

translation: She said, “My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?” He said, “Thus does Allah create whatever He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”
interpretation: Mary’s question expresses wonder at how a child could be born without the ordinary human cause, while the reply teaches that Allah’s creative power is not limited by natural processes. His decree is sufficient for existence, so the miraculous birth occurs by His will and command.

translation: And He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel.
interpretation: God grants Jesus profound knowledge of revelation and sound judgment, teaching him both the earlier Torah and the Gospel entrusted to him so that he may guide people according to divine truth.

translation: And [I have come] as a messenger to the Children of Israel, saying: “I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. I fashion for you from clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah’s permission. I heal the blind from birth and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah’s permission. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Surely in this is a sign for you, if you are believers.”
interpretation: This verse presents Jesus as a messenger whose extraordinary miracles—giving life to a clay form, healing incurable conditions, reviving the dead, and disclosing hidden matters—were not independent powers but signs granted and enabled by Allah. They were intended to lead the Children of Israel to recognize the truth of his mission and believe in Allah, rather than to regard Jesus as divine.

translation: And confirming the Torah that came before me, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: Jesus affirms the divine origin of the Torah while bringing a limited easing of its legal restrictions by Allah’s permission. The sign granted to him is evidence of his mission, and therefore he calls his people to God-consciousness and obedience to the revelation he conveys.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize Allah as the one Lord of all and to devote their worship exclusively to Him. Such sincere worship is the sound and direct way that leads to faith, guidance, and righteousness.

translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from them, he said, “Who will be my helpers in the cause of Allah?” The disciples said, “We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we are Muslims.”
interpretation: When people reject the truth despite clear signs, the faithful are called to support Allah’s cause by standing with His messenger and upholding obedience to Him. The disciples respond with sincere belief and openly affirm their submission, showing that true faith entails both conviction and committed support for the truth.

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed and followed the Messenger, so record us among those who bear witness.
interpretation: This is a prayer of sincere believers affirming faith in divine revelation and obedience to God’s Messenger, asking God to count them among those whose testimony to the truth is proven through faithful commitment and righteous conduct.

translation: They plotted, and Allah planned; and Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: When people devise schemes against the truth, Allah brings their designs to nothing and carries out His decree in a way they cannot overcome. His planning is perfect, just, and victorious, unlike the deceitful plotting of those who oppose Him.

translation: When Allah said, “O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself, and purify you from those who disbelieve. I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you differed.”
interpretation: This verse declares Allah’s protection and exaltation of Jesus: He will rescue him from the plots and accusations of the disbelievers, while granting his sincere followers enduring ascendancy over falsehood in proof and authority until the Day of Resurrection. The ultimate judgment belongs to Allah, who will then distinguish the truth from the disagreements that arose concerning Jesus and his message.

translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This warns that persistent rejection of the truth brings consequences both in worldly life and in the Hereafter, where no ally or protector will be able to rescue the disbelievers from God’s judgment.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will grant them their rewards in full. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Those who combine sincere faith with righteous action will receive their complete recompense from Allah, while those who commit injustice are deprived of His love and approval.

translation: That is what We recite to you of the verses and the Wise Reminder.
interpretation: Allah presents these revealed accounts as clear signs of His truth and as a wise reminder meant to guide people, correct their understanding, and lead them toward faith and obedience.

translation: Indeed, the likeness of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be,” and he was.
interpretation: Jesus’s miraculous birth does not make him divine, for Adam was created without either a father or a mother. Both are signs of Allah’s absolute power: He creates as He wills, and His command alone is sufficient for existence.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt.
interpretation: What has been revealed by God is certain truth, grounded in His perfect knowledge and authority; therefore, remain firm in faith and do not allow doubt to unsettle your acceptance of it.

translation: So whoever argues with you about him after the knowledge that has come to you, say: “Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us earnestly pray and invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”
interpretation: After clear knowledge has been established, continued dispute over the truth of Jesus is no longer a sincere search for guidance but obstinate denial. The verse therefore directs the Prophet to propose a solemn mutual invocation of Allah’s judgment, entrusting the matter to Him and asking that His curse fall upon whoever knowingly lies.

translation: Indeed, this is certainly the true account; and there is no deity except Allah. Indeed, Allah is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This affirms that the account revealed by Allah is the unaltered truth, and that the truth of the events described points to the exclusive worship of Allah alone. His absolute might ensures that His decree cannot be overcome, while His perfect wisdom places everything in its proper measure and purpose.

translation: But if they turn away, then surely Allah is All-Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: Their refusal to accept the truth does not escape Allah’s knowledge; He fully knows those who knowingly reject guidance and spread corruption, and will judge them accordingly.

translation: Say: “O People of the Scripture, come to a word of justice between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides Allah.” But if they turn away, then say: “Bear witness that we are Muslims, submitting to Allah.”
interpretation: This verse establishes the fairest foundation for dialogue among revealed communities: sincere devotion to Allah alone, freedom from every form of idolatry, and refusal to grant human beings the absolute authority that belongs only to God. If others reject this foundation, believers are to remain firm in their submission to Allah while responding with clarity and dignity.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason?
interpretation: The verse rebukes the People of the Scripture for claiming Abraham as belonging exclusively to their religious communities, even though the revelations that define those communities came after his time. It calls them to recognize that Abraham preceded those labels and to abandon sectarian dispute in favor of clear reasoning and acknowledgment of the truth.

translation: Here you are, arguing about matters of which you have some knowledge; so why do you argue about matters of which you have no knowledge? Allah knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: The verse censures speaking with certainty about matters beyond one’s knowledge, especially disputing unseen or historical truths without reliable evidence. Human understanding is limited, so one must submit claims to what Allah has revealed rather than follow conjecture or personal assumption.

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was upright, devoted to God, and was not among the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse establishes that Abraham’s faith preceded and transcended the later religious identities attributed to him. He followed pure monotheism with sincere submission to God, so those who claim him should be measured by adherence to his worship of the One God, not by labels that arose after him.

translation: Indeed, the people who have the strongest claim to Abraham are those who followed him, this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Protector of the believers.
interpretation: True kinship with Abraham is established by sharing his faith and following his path, not merely by ancestry or claims of affiliation. The Prophet and all sincere believers are closest to him because they uphold his devotion to God, and Allah supports, guides, and protects those who believe.

translation: A group of the People of the Book wish to lead you astray, but they lead only themselves astray, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be deceived by those who deliberately seek to turn them away from faith and truth. Such efforts ultimately harm the deceivers themselves, because their hostility and misguidance distance them from guidance while they remain unaware of their own loss.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in Allah’s signs while you yourselves bear witness?
interpretation: The verse reproaches the People of the Scripture for knowingly rejecting God’s clear signs, despite possessing the knowledge and testimony that should lead them to recognize their truth.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who knowingly distort or obscure revealed truth by blending it with error, emphasizing that awareness of the truth makes its concealment a deliberate moral wrongdoing.

translation: And a group of the People of the Scripture said, “Believe in what was sent down to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and reject it at its end, so that they may turn back.”
interpretation: This describes a deliberate scheme to create doubt among the believers: to outwardly accept the revelation in the morning and then renounce it by evening, hoping that people would think the faith was unreliable and abandon it. The verse exposes this as calculated deception rather than sincere searching for truth.

translation: ولا تصدّقوا إلا من اتبع دينكم. قل: إن الهدى هو هدى الله، خشيةَ أن يُعطى أحدٌ مثل ما أُعطيتم، أو أن يحاجّوكم عند ربكم. قل: إن الفضل بيد الله، يؤتيه من يشاء، والله واسع الفضل والعطاء، عليم بمن يستحقه.
interpretation: يكشف الله أن هذا الكلام يعبّر عن خوف أهل الكتاب من أن يمنح الله غيرهم من الهداية والفضل مثل ما منحهم، أو أن يمتلكوا حجة يحتجّون بها عليهم يوم القيامة. ويقرّر أن الهداية والفضل ليسا امتيازًا موروثًا ولا ملكًا لجماعة، بل هما بيد الله يختص بهما من يشاء وفق علمه وحكمته؛ لذلك لا يجوز حصر الحق في أتباع جماعة لمجرد انتمائهم إليها.

translation: He grants His mercy exclusively to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: Allah’s mercy is a supreme gift bestowed according to His wisdom, and His boundless generosity is not limited by human expectation or merit.

translation: Among the People of the Scripture are those who, if you entrust them with a heap of gold, will return it to you; and among them are those who, if you entrust them with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you persistently demand it. That is because they say, “We are under no obligation concerning the unlettered,” and they knowingly attribute falsehood to God.
interpretation: The verse exposes the moral corruption of those who invent a religious excuse for betraying the rights of people outside their own community. Their dishonesty is not merely a personal failing but a deliberate distortion of divine law; it also makes clear that the Qur’an does not condemn all People of the Scripture alike, since it distinguishes between the trustworthy and the treacherous among them.

translation: Indeed, whoever fulfills his covenant and is mindful of God—then surely God loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: True righteousness is shown by honoring one’s commitments while remaining conscious of God; such integrity and reverence are qualities that earn His love.

translation: Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a small worldly gain—those will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will neither speak to them nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them; and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that knowingly betraying one’s covenant with Allah or using solemn oaths deceitfully for worldly benefit is a grave moral and spiritual crime. Such gain is insignificant compared with the loss of divine acceptance, mercy, and salvation in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, among them is a group who twist their tongues while reciting the Scripture, so that you may think it is part of the Scripture, though it is not part of the Scripture. They say, “It is from Allah,” though it is not from Allah, and they knowingly attribute lies to Allah.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who deliberately distort divine revelation—whether by altering its wording, its recitation, or its meaning—in order to make human claims appear divinely authorized. It warns that knowingly presenting falsehood as God’s word is not a harmless error but a grave act of deception and a lie against Allah.

translation: It is not for any human being that Allah should give him the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood, then he would say to the people, “Be servants to me instead of Allah.” Rather, he would say, “Be devoted servants of the Lord, because you teach the Scripture and because you study it.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that true prophets never claim worship or ultimate allegiance for themselves; their knowledge and authority direct people exclusively toward Allah. A person becomes ربّانيّ (devoted to the Lord) by grounding faith and conduct in the revealed Book, teaching it with sincerity, and continually studying it—so that learning produces humble obedience to Allah rather than personal glorification.

translation: Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted?
interpretation: This verse affirms that no true messenger of God would call people to worship or deify angels or prophets, because doing so would contradict submission to God alone. Attributing such a command to a prophet is therefore an accusation of disbelief against the very faith he was sent to establish.

translation: And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: “Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you must surely believe in him and support him.” He said, “Do you affirm this and accept My binding covenant upon you?” They said, “We affirm.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.”
interpretation: This verse portrays the unity of the divine message and the solemn responsibility borne by God’s prophets: revelation is not meant to be treated as isolated or competing traditions, but as a continuous truth whose later confirmation must be recognized and supported. Their covenant establishes that genuine fidelity to earlier scripture requires welcoming the messenger sent by God, while the formal questioning and witnessing emphasize the seriousness and binding nature of this commitment before Him.

translation: So whoever turns away after that—those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: After affirming this solemn covenant, anyone who knowingly abandons it and refuses to remain faithful to its implications has departed from obedience to God and is therefore counted among the transgressors.

translation: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعًا وكرهًا وإليه يرجعون
interpretation: يستنكر الله على الناس أن يطلبوا منهجًا غير منهجه، فالكون كله خاضع لأمره وسننه، طوعًا ممن آمن واستسلم، وكرهًا ممن جحد؛ إذ لا يملك أحد الخروج عن سلطانه، وسيعود الجميع إليه للحساب.

translation: Say, “We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets by their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that true faith accepts the one divine source and the authentic revelation granted to all of Allah’s prophets, without rejecting any messenger because of religious partisanship. The believers affirm their unity in submission to Allah while recognizing that revelation continued through successive prophets.

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God accepts only sincere submission to Him—the way of faith and obedience He has revealed—and that deliberately turning to another path after the truth has become clear leads to ultimate loss in the Hereafter.

translation: كيف يهدي الله قوماً كفروا بعد إيمانهم، وشهدوا أن الرسول حق، وجاءتهم البينات؟ والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن من عرف الحق وشهد بصدق الرسول وقامت عليه الأدلة، ثم رجع إلى الكفر عناداً واختياراً، فقد ظلم نفسه وأعرض عن أسباب الهداية؛ ولذلك يُحرم التوفيق إليها ما دام متمسكاً بهذا الظلم والإعراض.

translation: Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.
interpretation: They are deserving of being deprived of Allah’s mercy and condemned by the heavenly and human creation because of their deliberate rejection of the truth.

translation: They will abide therein forever; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be granted respite.
interpretation: This portrays an unending punishment with no reduction in severity and no delay or opportunity for relief, emphasizing the permanence and utter finality of their consequence.

translation: Except those who repent thereafter and reform themselves—for indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Those who sincerely turn back from their wrongdoing and demonstrate their repentance by correcting their conduct may receive Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed, then increase in disbelief—their repentance will not be accepted; and they are the ones who have gone astray.
interpretation: This warns that repeatedly turning away from faith and deepening in rejection until death makes repentance unacceptable—not because God’s mercy is limited, but because such a person remains insincere and does not truly return to faith before it is too late. They are thereby deprived of guidance and have chosen a path of grave error.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers—never would the equivalent of the earth’s full weight of gold be accepted from any of them, even if he offered it as ransom. For them is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith cannot be postponed until death, nor can punishment then be escaped through wealth or any attempted ransom. Once a person dies in persistent disbelief, material possessions and worldly allies have no power to secure forgiveness or deliverance from God’s judgment.

translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love. Whatever you spend—Allah is fully aware of it.
interpretation: True righteousness is reached through sincere generosity: giving for Allah’s sake from the possessions one values, rather than only from what is easy or unwanted. Allah knows every act of spending and the sincerity behind it, so the verse calls believers to sacrifice what they love in trust that their devotion is known and rewarded.

translation: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, except what Israel forbade for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, “Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse refutes the claim that certain dietary restrictions were part of the original divine law before the Torah. It clarifies that the prohibition arose from Israel’s personal vow or self-imposed abstention, not from an earlier universal revelation, and challenges those making the claim to verify it directly from the Torah. Thus, truth in religious debate must be established by authentic scripture rather than unsupported assertion.

translation: So whoever fabricates lies against Allah after that, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: After the truth has been made clear, inventing claims and attributing them to Allah is a grave injustice, because it distorts divine guidance and misleads others.

translation: Say, “Allah has spoken the truth.” So follow the way of Abraham, inclining wholly toward truth; and he was not among the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to affirm Allah’s truth and adhere to Abraham’s sincere, undivided devotion to Him, free from every form of associating partners with God.

translation: Indeed, the first House established for humanity was surely that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for all worlds.
interpretation: This verse declares that the Sacred House in Bakkah—Makkah—was the earliest sanctuary appointed for the worship of God and the benefit of humanity. Its blessing lies in the spiritual good, mercy, and acts of worship connected to it, while its role as guidance is embodied in the call to affirm God’s oneness, turn to Him in devotion, and follow the path of faith that reaches beyond any single people or nation.

translation: In it are clear signs, including the Station of Abraham. Whoever enters it shall be safe. Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by all people who are able to find a way to it. And whoever denies it—surely Allah is Self-Sufficient, independent of all worlds.
interpretation: The Sacred House contains manifest signs of Allah, among them the Station of Abraham, reminding people of Abraham’s devotion and obedience. Allah has made pilgrimage obligatory for those who possess the physical, financial, and practical ability to undertake it, while the promise of safety emphasizes the sanctity and protection associated with the Sanctuary. Whoever rejects this obligation or refuses its truth does not diminish Allah in any way, for He has no need of His creation, whereas all people remain dependent upon Him.

translation: Say, “O People of the Scripture, why do you reject the signs of Allah, while Allah is witness to all that you do?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who knowingly deny or conceal the truth conveyed by Allah’s revelations. Their rejection cannot escape divine knowledge: Allah observes their actions and will hold them accountable for how they respond to the truth.

translation: Say, “O People of the Book, why do you obstruct those who believe from the way of Allah, seeking to make it appear crooked, while you yourselves bear witness? Allah is not unaware of what you do.”
interpretation: This verse reproaches those who knowingly oppose faith and mislead believers by distorting the truth, despite possessing knowledge of its reality. It warns that religious authority does not excuse such conduct, for Allah fully knows their intentions and actions and will hold them accountable.

translation: O believers, if you obey a group of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back into disbelievers after your faith.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to surrender their religious convictions to the influence of those among the People of the Scripture who seek to mislead them, but to remain steadfast in the guidance and faith they have received.

translation: How can you disbelieve while Allah’s verses are being recited to you and His Messenger is among you? Whoever holds fast to Allah has certainly been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse rebukes disbelief when divine guidance is continually present through revelation and the Messenger who teaches and embodies it. It teaches that true protection from error comes from firmly clinging to Allah through faith, obedience, and reliance upon Him; whoever does so is guided to the clear, upright path.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، اتقوا الله حق تقواه، ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون.
interpretation: يأمر الله المؤمنين بأن يجعلوا تقواه منهجًا شاملًا لحياتهم، فيلتزموا أوامره ويجتنبوا نواهيه، وأن يثبتوا على الإسلام والطاعة حتى يلقوه، لأن العبرة بالخاتمة.

translation: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah and do not be divided. Remember Allah’s blessing upon you: when you were enemies, He united your hearts, and by His grace you became brothers. You were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you so that you may be guided.
interpretation: Allah commands believers to remain firmly united around His guidance and not let disputes sever their community. Their brotherhood is a divine gift that transformed hostility into mutual loyalty, and their deliverance from ruin came through faith and obedience; therefore, preserving unity upon revelation is an expression of gratitude and a means of remaining rightly guided.

translation: And let there be among you a community calling to all that is good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. It is they who will prosper.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Muslim community must preserve its moral wellbeing through a dedicated effort to promote truth and virtue and to prevent wrongdoing, with wisdom, knowledge, and sincere concern. True success is promised to those who undertake this responsibility faithfully.

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. For them is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that once truth has been made clear, they must not allow rivalry, prejudice, or attachment to personal opinions to divide them. Deliberately disputing and splitting after guidance has been established is a serious spiritual failure that brings severe consequences.

translation: On the Day when some faces will be bright and some faces will be dark. As for those whose faces are darkened: “Did you disbelieve after your faith? Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment, when people’s outward condition will reveal the spiritual reality of their deeds. The darkened faces signify disgrace and despair, and the question rebukes those who turned away from faith after recognizing it. Their punishment is presented as the just consequence of their persistent denial and rejection of the truth.

translation: As for those whose faces are brightened, they will be in the mercy of Allah, abiding therein forever.
interpretation: Those whose faith and obedience are reflected in their purified state will receive Allah’s mercy and remain in the lasting bliss of Paradise without end.

translation: These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth. And Allah does not intend injustice for all the worlds.
interpretation: Allah’s revelation is presented with absolute truth and fairness, affirming that whatever He decrees or judges is free from arbitrary oppression or wrongdoing toward any of His creation.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: Everything in the universe belongs entirely to Allah and remains under His authority and wisdom. Ultimately, every affair returns to Him for judgment and resolution, so people should place their trust in Him and conduct their lives with accountability before Him.

translation: You are the best community brought forth for humanity: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah. Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The excellence of the Muslim community is not an unconditional privilege; it is a responsibility and a distinction upheld by faith in Allah and active commitment to moral good—encouraging righteousness and resisting wrongdoing. The verse also leaves the door of fairness open regarding the People of the Book: some are sincere believers, while many reject obedience, showing that moral worth is determined by faith and conduct rather than by affiliation alone.

translation: They will never harm you except with some annoyance. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped.
interpretation: تطمئن الآية المؤمنين بأن أذى أعدائهم لن يتجاوز ضررًا عابرًا ما داموا ثابتين على الحق، وأنه إذا وقعت مواجهة صريحة انكسر المعتدون وانهزموا، ولن يجدوا نصرًا أو عونًا ينقذهم من عاقبة عدوانهم.

translation: Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except through a covenant of protection from Allah and a covenant of protection from people. They have incurred the anger of Allah, and misery has been imposed upon them. That is because they used to disbelieve in Allah’s signs and kill the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and transgressed.
interpretation: The verse explains that disgrace and hardship follow a community when it abandons obedience to God, rejects His revelations, violates sacred justice, and commits grave oppression. Its mention of protection through a covenant with Allah and with people indicates that such consequences are not an excuse for indiscriminate hostility; rather, security and dignity remain possible through faithfulness to God’s covenant and through lawful, peaceful relations. The warning is therefore moral and conditional: persistent rebellion and transgression lead to humiliation, while obedience, justice, and respect for divinely established limits are the means of avoiding it.

translation: They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is an upright community who recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night while prostrating.
interpretation: This verse teaches that people should not be judged collectively by the wrongdoing of some among them. Allah acknowledges those from the People of the Book who are sincere, devoted to worship, and responsive to His revelations, making their faith and humble obedience the basis of their distinction.

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and hasten to do good deeds. Such are among the righteous.
interpretation: True righteousness is shown through a living combination of faith, moral responsibility, resistance to wrongdoing, and eagerness to pursue good; those who embody these qualities are counted among the صالحين, the people whose character and actions are sound before Allah.

translation: Whatever good they do, it will never be denied them; and Allah knows the God-conscious.
interpretation: No sincere act of goodness is overlooked or rendered worthless before Allah; He fully knows those who remain mindful of Him and will preserve the reward of their deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—their wealth and their children will never avail them against God in anything. They are the companions of the Fire; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: Those who reject faith should not imagine that worldly resources or family ties can protect them from God’s judgment. Such things may benefit a person in worldly life, but they cannot compensate for disbelief or avert accountability before God; therefore, the disbelievers’ final abode is the Fire, where they will abide eternally.

translation: The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is that of a wind carrying a biting frost that strikes the crops of people who wronged themselves and destroys them. Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: Whatever wealth is spent without faith and obedience to Allah may appear beneficial, yet it is deprived of the lasting reward that gives deeds their true value. Like a freezing wind destroying a harvest, disbelief and wrongdoing nullify the benefit of such spending; this loss is not injustice from Allah, but the consequence of people choosing what corrupts their own deeds.

translation: O believers, do not take as intimate confidants anyone outside your own community; they spare no effort to corrupt you. They wish you hardship. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, while what their hearts conceal is even greater. We have made the revelations clear to you, if you will understand.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to exercise wisdom in granting deep trust and access to those who may be hostile to their faith and well-being: outward signs of malice should not be dismissed, and concealed intentions may be more harmful than what is openly expressed. This is a call to prudent boundaries and discernment, not to injustice or hostility toward people merely because they belong to another community.

translation: Here you are, loving them while they do not love you; you believe in all the Scripture. When they meet you, they say, “We believe,” but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips in rage against you. Say, “Die in your rage.” Indeed, Allah knows well what is hidden in the hearts.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy and deep hostility of those who outwardly profess faith when meeting the believers but secretly resent and oppose them. In contrast, the believers accept the revealed Scripture in its entirety and respond with sincere goodwill. Allah’s command to let the hostile people perish in their rage is a declaration that their concealed hatred cannot harm the truth, while Allah fully knows the malice hidden within their hearts.

translation: If something good befalls you, it grieves them; and if something bad afflicts you, they rejoice at it. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their schemes will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers not to measure their security or success by the reactions of those who harbor hostility toward them. Their envy may make them resent your prosperity and celebrate your hardship, but steadfast patience and consciousness of Allah protect you from being overcome by their plotting. This protection does not mean that trials will never occur; rather, their schemes cannot ultimately defeat or corrupt those who remain patient, act with God-consciousness, and trust that Allah fully knows and governs all their deeds.

translation: And when you departed from your household at dawn, assigning the believers their positions for battle—and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Prophet ﷺ carefully organizing the believers before battle, teaching that reliance on Allah does not replace disciplined planning and responsible leadership. Allah’s perfect hearing and knowledge encompass both their words and intentions, so outward preparation must be joined with sincerity and obedience to Him.

translation: When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their protector; and in Allah let the believers place their trust.
interpretation: The verse teaches that moments of fear and wavering do not mean believers are abandoned. Allah supports and safeguards those who remain under His care, so believers should resist despair, rely on Him sincerely, and continue with steadfastness rather than surrendering to weakness.

translation: Indeed, Allah aided you at Badr while you were in a state of weakness. So be mindful of Allah, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The victory at Badr teaches that success comes from Allah rather than from worldly strength or numbers; therefore, believers should respond to His blessings by obeying Him, relying on Him, and avoiding disobedience.

translation: When you said to the believers, “Will it not be enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?”
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that divine support is sufficient to strengthen them in hardship, teaching that victory and steadfastness come from God, while the promised aid also calls for sincere faith and reliance upon Him.

translation: Yes indeed! If you remain steadfast and mindful of God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels bearing distinctive marks.
interpretation: This verse teaches that steadfastness and God-consciousness are the conditions through which divine aid is sought: believers must remain disciplined and obedient even when confronted unexpectedly, trusting that God can strengthen them through means beyond ordinary human ability.

translation: Allah made it only as good news for you and so that your hearts might be reassured by it. Victory comes only from Allah—the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The divine support granted to believers is a means of encouragement and inner steadfastness, not an independent source of victory. True success belongs solely to Allah, whose might ensures that no force can defeat His decree and whose wisdom determines how and when victory is given.

translation: So that He may destroy a faction of those who disbelieved or humiliate them, causing them to turn back disappointed.
interpretation: This verse teaches that victory and defeat ultimately lie with God: He may weaken the forces of disbelief by destroying some of them or by exposing them to humiliation, leaving their plans frustrated and their hopes unfulfilled.

translation: You have no authority in the matter—whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that ultimate judgment belongs solely to God. Even the Prophet cannot determine the fate of those who have committed wrongdoing; God may forgive them through repentance and mercy or punish them in accordance with their injustice.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: All creation belongs entirely to Allah, so He alone possesses ultimate authority over His creatures and judges them with perfect wisdom and justice. His forgiveness and punishment are governed by His will, while His being repeatedly described as Forgiving and Merciful gives hope that those who sincerely turn to Him may receive His mercy.

translation: O believers, do not consume usury, multiplied and compounded, and be mindful of Allah so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse forbids exploiting people through debt that increases burdens excessively and repeatedly, directing believers to conduct financial dealings with justice and compassion. True prosperity comes from honoring Allah’s limits rather than seeking gain through another person’s hardship.

translation: And guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a warning to protect oneself from the punishment of the Hereafter by holding firmly to faith, obeying God, and turning away from the disbelief and disobedience that lead to it.

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is the path by which a person aligns their life with divine guidance and becomes deserving of Allah’s mercy.

translation: And hasten toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-conscious.
interpretation: This verse urges believers not to delay repentance and righteous deeds, but to actively hasten toward what earns God’s forgiveness and entry into Paradise. Its immense breadth emphasizes the limitless generosity of the reward, while describing it as prepared for the God-conscious points to those who protect themselves from disobedience and remain mindful of God.

translation: Those who spend in prosperity and adversity, restrain their anger, and pardon people—God loves those who do good.
interpretation: True righteousness is shown by generosity in every circumstance and by mastering anger rather than letting it lead to harm, while choosing to forgive others when one has the power to retaliate. Such self-control, mercy, and kindness are qualities beloved by God.

translation: And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and they do not persist knowingly in what they have done.
interpretation: The verse portrays true repentance as arising when a person, after falling into sin or harming themselves, turns back to Allah with awareness and sincere طلب for forgiveness. Their repentance is shown by refusing to knowingly continue in the wrongdoing; thus, Allah’s forgiveness is sought through remorse, seeking pardon, and abandoning persistence in sin.

translation: Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Excellent is the reward of those who strive in righteousness.
interpretation: This promises that those who repent, resist wrongdoing, and persist in obedience will receive both God’s forgiveness for their shortcomings and everlasting bliss; their reward is described as excellent because it comes from sincere, steadfast action accepted by their Lord.

translation: قد مضت من قبلكم سننٌ وأحوالٌ جرت على الأمم، فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كانت عاقبة المكذبين.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن قوانين الله في الأمم ثابتة؛ فمن كذّب الحق وأصرّ على الباطل انتهى إلى الهلاك، ولذلك يُدعَى الناس إلى الاعتبار بتاريخ السابقين وآثارهم ليتجنبوا طريقهم ويستقيموا على الإيمان والحق.

translation: This is a clear explanation for humanity, and a guidance and admonition for those mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse presents the divine message as making truth clear to all people, while its guidance and corrective reminder are especially benefited from by those who remain conscious of God and receptive to moral instruction.

translation: Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers.
interpretation: Believers are urged not to let defeat, hardship, or loss break their resolve or overwhelm them with sorrow. Their true strength and dignity come from steadfast faith, obedience to God, and perseverance, so long as their belief is sincere and lived out.

translation: إن يمسسكم جرحٌ فقد أصاب القومَ جرحٌ مثله، وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس، وليُظهر الله الذين آمنوا، ويتخذ منكم شهداء، والله لا يحب الظالمين.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الهزيمة أو الألم لا يعنيان تخلي الله عن المؤمنين، فالأيام تتعاقب بين الناس بحكمة وابتلاء. ومن خلال الشدائد يظهر صدق الإيمان والثبات، ويُكرم بعض المؤمنين بالشهادة، أما الظلم والعدوان فهما مما لا يرضاه الله، مهما بدا لأهلهما من نصر مؤقت.

translation: And so that Allah may purify those who believe and erase the disbelievers.
interpretation: Allah allows trials to distinguish and refine the believers, cleansing their faith through steadfastness and obedience, while the persistent rejection of truth is ultimately weakened and brought to ruin.

translation: Or did you think that you would enter Paradise before Allah makes evident those among you who strive and those who are steadfast?
interpretation: The verse admonishes believers not to assume that Paradise is attained merely by claiming faith or wishing for it. Its trials reveal, in accordance with Allah’s encompassing knowledge, those who sincerely strive in His cause and remain patient through hardship; such steadfastness demonstrates the truth of their faith and is among the means by which they attain Paradise.

translation: You certainly used to wish for death before you encountered it; now you have seen it while looking on.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who had longed for martyrdom and confrontation with the enemy before the battle, reminding them that true courage is proven when death becomes an immediate reality, not merely when it is desired in words. Having witnessed its dangers, they were to remain steadfast rather than retreat.

translation: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers passed away before him. So, if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah in the least. And Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that faith must be devoted to Allah rather than dependent on the continued earthly presence of any messenger. The Prophet Muhammad’s death or possible killing would not invalidate his message, and abandoning faith afterward would only harm those who abandon it, never Allah or His religion. Those who remain steadfast and grateful for divine guidance will receive Allah’s reward.

translation: No soul can die except by Allah’s permission, at a decreed time. Whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him some of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him some of it. And We will reward the grateful.
interpretation: Death and worldly outcomes occur only within Allah’s determined decree, so believers should not let fear govern their obedience or sacrifice. The verse also teaches that a person receives according to the aim of the heart: seeking only worldly gain may yield a worldly share, while sincere pursuit of the Hereafter earns its reward. Therefore, gratitude and devotion should be directed toward Allah rather than toward temporary benefits.

translation: How many a prophet fought, and with him fought many devoted servants of God. They neither lost heart because of what befell them in the way of God, nor weakened, nor humbled themselves. And God loves those who are steadfast.
