interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere believers may suffer losses and hardship while striving for God, but such trials must not make them despair, become weak, or surrender to humiliation. Their steadfastness reflects true faith, and it is this patient endurance that earns God’s love.

translation: Their only words were: “Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make our feet firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
interpretation: This prayer teaches that true believers respond to hardship by acknowledging both their sins and their own excesses, seeking God’s forgiveness, asking for steadfastness, and relying on Him for victory rather than on their own strength.

translation: So Allah granted them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter; and Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: Allah rewarded their sincere faith, steadfastness, and obedience with blessings in this life, and reserved for them an even greater and everlasting reward in the Hereafter. His love is for those who excel in righteousness and act with sincere goodness.

translation: O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will end up as losers.
interpretation: This is a warning to believers not to follow the direction or counsel of those who reject faith when doing so compromises obedience to God, because such submission can gradually pull them away from the truth and lead to loss in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: True protection and victory come from Allah alone, so believers should place their trust in Him rather than fear or rely upon any power besides Him.

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associated with Allah partners for which He has sent down no authority. Their refuge will be the Fire—and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Allah declares that those who reject faith and attribute partners to Him without any proof will be deprived of inner security and overcome by fear. Their false beliefs cannot protect them, and their ultimate return will be Hell, a fittingly miserable abode for those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: And Allah certainly fulfilled His promise to you when, by His permission, you were killing them, until you lost courage, disputed over the matter, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you loved. Some of you desired this world, while others desired the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them in order to test you; yet He has pardoned you. And Allah is full of فضل toward the believers.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن النصر لا يستمر بمجرد بدايته، بل يرتبط بالثبات والطاعة ووحدة الصف؛ فقد تحقق للمؤمنين ما وُعدوا به حين التزموا، ثم تبدّل حالهم عندما دبّ فيهم الضعف والتنازع وغلب بعضهم طلب الغنيمة على مواصلة الطاعة. وكان انحسار النصر عنهم ابتلاءً يكشف صدقهم ويعلّمهم أن التعلق بالدنيا يضعف الجماعة، ومع ذلك لم يكن ما وقع نهاية علاقتهم بالله، إذ قابل خطأهم بالعفو، وفي ذلك بيان لفضله ورحمته بالمؤمنين حين يرجعون إليه.

translation: When you were climbing, paying no heed to anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind, He repaid you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what had eluded you or what had befallen you. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse depicts the believers’ disorder and retreat in battle, despite the Prophet’s call, as a moment through which Allah disciplined and purified them. The compounded grief awakened them to the consequences of abandoning responsibility and taught them to place their trust in Allah rather than becoming consumed by loss, fear, or worldly outcomes; Allah’s complete knowledge encompasses both their actions and the inner lessons they were meant to learn.

translation: Then, after the distress, He sent down upon you a reassurance—a sleep overcoming a group of you. Yet another group was preoccupied with their own concerns, entertaining thoughts about God that were untrue, like the assumptions of the pre-Islamic age. They said, “Do we have any say in the matter?” Say, “Indeed, the whole matter belongs to God.” They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you, saying, “If we had had any say in the matter, none of us would have been killed here.” Say, “Even if you had been in your homes, those destined to be killed would have gone forth to their places of death.” Thus God tests what is in your hearts and purifies what is within them. And God knows well what hearts contain.
interpretation: The verse contrasts two inner responses to a severe trial: sincere believers received calm and restorative sleep, while others were consumed by fear, self-interest, and distrust of God’s wisdom. Their claim that events would have been avoided if they had controlled the decision reflects a mistaken belief that human planning can escape divine decree. God affirms that His authority encompasses the outcome, while human choices still reveal what lies within people. The ordeal therefore serves as a test that exposes hidden attitudes and cleanses the hearts of those who respond with faith, patience, and submission.

translation: Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two armies met—it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. Yet Allah has certainly pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse teaches that believers may falter under the pressure of fear and temptation because of weaknesses they have acquired, but such a lapse does not place them beyond Allah’s mercy when they return to Him. His forgiveness and forbearance show that He does not hasten to punish repentant servants, while also warning them to guard themselves against the causes of disobedience.

translation: O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers, when they travelled through the land or went forth to battle, “Had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed.” Allah makes this a source of anguish in their hearts. Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: Believers are taught not to respond to death with futile regret or to imagine that remaining behind could have defeated Allah’s decree. Such speech only deepens grief and weakens faith; life and death are entirely within Allah’s power, while people remain accountable for the choices and deeds they make before Him.

translation: And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass.
interpretation: The verse reassures believers that their ultimate gain is not measured by worldly wealth or possessions: whether their life ends through sacrifice in Allah’s cause or by ordinary death, Allah’s forgiveness and mercy are a far greater and lasting reward than anything people can accumulate.

translation: And whether you die or are killed, you will surely be gathered before Allah.
interpretation: Death, whether it occurs naturally or through being killed, does not end a person’s journey; all people will return to Allah for judgment, where their deeds and ultimate fate will be made clear.

translation: So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you. Therefore, pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. Then, when you have resolved upon a course of action, place your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who place their trust in Him.
interpretation: Allah teaches that effective leadership and guidance arise from divine mercy expressed through gentleness, compassion, forgiveness, and sincere consultation. Even when people have made mistakes, they should not be driven away by severity or resentment; rather, they should be treated with kindness, their forgiveness sought from Allah, and their perspectives heard. After thoughtful consultation and a firm decision, one should act with determination while entrusting the outcome to Allah, combining responsible effort with reliance upon Him.

translation: If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse teaches believers that true success and protection come from Allah alone. They must therefore place their trust in Him rather than in their numbers, strength, or worldly means, while remaining steadfast and obedient instead of becoming arrogant in victory or despairing in difficulty.

translation: It is not for any prophet to act treacherously. Whoever betrays shall come on the Day of Resurrection bearing what he betrayed. Then every soul shall be fully repaid for what it earned, and they shall not be wronged.
interpretation: A prophet cannot conceal, misuse, or unlawfully take anything entrusted to him, especially from the public spoils; such betrayal is incompatible with prophetic trustworthiness. The verse also establishes that every act of dishonesty will be exposed and carried by its perpetrator into the Hereafter, where each person will receive the exact consequences of their deeds without any injustice.

translation: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن رجع بسخطٍ من الله، ومأواه جهنم، وبئس المصير؟
interpretation: لا يستوي من جعل غايته طاعة الله وطلب رضاه، فيوفَّق إلى الخير والنجاة، ومن أعرض عن أمره واستحق سخطه؛ فمصير الثاني جهنم، وهي أسوأ ما يُرجع إليه.

translation: They are of varying ranks in the sight of Allah, and Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: People differ in their nearness and standing before Allah according to the sincerity and righteousness of their deeds; nothing they do is hidden from His perfect knowledge.

translation: Indeed, Allah has surely bestowed a great favor upon the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they had been in clear error.
interpretation: Allah’s sending of the Messenger is a profound mercy because he guides people through revelation, cultivates their souls, and teaches them sound understanding and wise conduct. The verse emphasizes that true reform begins with divine guidance: without it, people may possess customs or knowledge yet remain lost in beliefs and actions; through the Messenger, faith and moral purification become the means of their transformation.

translation: What! When a calamity befell you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, “Where did this come from?” Say, “It is from your own selves.” Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: When hardship reaches believers, they should examine their own choices and shortcomings rather than question Allah’s justice. The verse teaches that worldly outcomes occur within Allah’s complete power, while human negligence and disobedience can be causes of painful consequences; therefore, adversity should lead to honest self-accountability and correction.

translation: Whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by Allah’s permission, so that He might make evident who the believers are.
interpretation: The setback and hardships experienced at the battle occurred within Allah’s decree, not outside His knowledge or authority. Through that trial, the sincere believers were distinguished by their faith, steadfastness, and obedience.

translation: And that He might expose those who were hypocrites. It was said to them, “Come, fight in the way of Allah, or defend yourselves.” They replied, “If we knew there would be fighting, we would certainly follow you.” That day they were closer to disbelief than to faith. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, and Allah knows best what they conceal.
interpretation: The verse reveals the hypocrisy of those who withdrew from the believers at a time of danger, using uncertainty about the battle as an excuse while concealing their unwillingness to sacrifice for the truth. Their outward claims of faith were contradicted by their hearts and actions, showing that sincere faith is proven through steadfastness and obedience, especially in hardship. Allah fully knows the motives they hide, and their deliberate preference for safety and worldly interests brought them spiritually nearer to disbelief than to genuine faith.

translation: Those who said of their brothers, while they themselves stayed behind, “Had they obeyed us, they would not have been killed.” Say, “Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the false comfort of those who avoided the struggle and then blamed the fallen for not following their advice. Their claim that obedience could have prevented death is challenged by the reality that no one can repel death when its appointed time arrives; true belief is shown through trust in God and sincere responsibility, not hindsight and discouraging others.

translation: Never think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.
interpretation: The verse teaches that martyrdom for Allah is not annihilation but a transition to an unseen life of honor and sustenance in the presence of their Lord; their true state is greater than what ordinary human perception can perceive.

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that they shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: Those whom Allah has honored are filled with joy over His generous reward and are assured of the blessed destiny awaiting the faithful who remain behind; neither future danger nor past loss can cause them fear or sorrow, because Allah’s promise and acceptance have given them complete peace.

translation: They rejoice in grace from Allah and bounty, and in the fact that Allah does not let the reward of the believers go to waste.
interpretation: This conveys the believers’ deep joy at the divine blessings and generosity granted to them, together with their certainty that every sincere act of faith and obedience is preserved and fully rewarded by Allah, never lost or overlooked.

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after suffering injury—those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse praises the believers who, despite the wounds and hardship they had endured, continued to answer Allah’s and the Messenger’s call. Their reward is especially assured because their obedience was joined with righteous conduct and sincere God-consciousness.

translation: Those to whom people said, “Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them,” only increased in faith, and they said, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.”
interpretation: True faith transforms reports of danger into deeper reliance on Allah: the believers do not deny the threat, but refuse to let fear control them, entrusting their affairs to Him while remaining steadfast and courageous.

translation: So they returned with grace from Allah and bounty, untouched by any harm, and followed what pleases Allah; and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: Those who obey Allah and pursue His approval with sincere courage are granted His care and abundant spiritual reward, even when they face fear or hardship; their true success lies in His favor, which surpasses every worldly gain.

translation: It is only Satan who frightens you through his allies, so do not fear them; fear Me, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that fear of worldly opponents must not overpower trust in God. Satan uses threats and intimidation through those who support falsehood to weaken believers, but sincere faith redirects ultimate awe and obedience to God alone.

translation: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will never harm Allah in the least. Allah intends not to grant them any share in the Hereafter, and for them is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: Do not let the eagerness of those who reject faith distress you, for their rejection cannot diminish Allah’s power or sovereignty. Their persistent choice of disbelief deprives them of the reward of the Hereafter, and they will face a severe punishment as a consequence of that choice.

translation: Indeed, those who have chosen disbelief in place of faith will never harm Allah in the least, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Those who knowingly abandon faith for disbelief do not diminish Allah’s power or authority in any way; their rejection only brings harm upon themselves and leads to a severe punishment.

translation: Let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for them. We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The delay of punishment for those who reject the truth is not an indication of God’s approval or favor toward them; it is a period in which their wrongdoing may deepen, while the final consequence awaiting them is a punishment that disgraces them.

translation: Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the impure from the pure. Nor would Allah disclose to you the unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. If you believe and are mindful of Allah, then you will have a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that trials and changing circumstances serve to reveal the true quality of faith: sincere believers become distinct from those whose faith is corrupted by hypocrisy or disobedience. People are not granted unrestricted knowledge of the unseen; rather, Allah discloses of it only what He wills to the messengers He chooses. Therefore, the proper response is steadfast faith and God-consciousness, for the reward belongs to those who remain sincere and obedient.

translation: And let not those who withhold what Allah has granted them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. What they withheld will be fastened around their necks on the Day of Resurrection. To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse warns that treating Allah’s blessings as possessions to hoard, while refusing the obligations attached to them, is not a source of true benefit but a cause of ruin. Wealth and every gift are temporary trusts, whereas Allah alone remains their ultimate owner; therefore, those who withhold what they should give will face the consequences of their miserliness in the Hereafter, when the very thing they refused to part with becomes a burden and a punishment for them.

translation: Allah has certainly heard the words of those who said, “Indeed, Allah is poor while we are rich.” We shall record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We shall say, “Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the arrogance of those who spoke about Allah with contempt, treating their own wealth as evidence of superiority and mocking the divine call to give. Allah’s hearing and recording signify that no word or crime escapes His knowledge or judgment; the mention of killing the prophets shows that such insolence was accompanied by violent rejection of truth. Their claim of self-sufficiency is therefore revealed as delusion, and the punishment of the Fire is the fitting consequence of denying Allah’s majesty and persecuting His messengers.

translation: That is because of what your own hands have sent ahead, and Allah is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: The consequences you face arise from your own deeds and choices, not from any wrongdoing by Allah; He judges with perfect justice and never wrongs anyone, even in the least.

translation: Those who said, “Indeed, Allah has commanded us not to believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes.” Say, “Messengers before me came to you with clear proofs and with what you have described, so why did you kill them, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: Their demand was not a sincere search for truth but a pretext for rejecting the Messenger. Allah exposes its falsehood by reminding them that earlier messengers had brought clear signs and, in accordance with their claimed condition, the divinely accepted offering—yet they opposed and killed some of them. Thus, the real cause of their disbelief was stubbornness and betrayal, not the absence of evidence.

translation: If they reject you, messengers before you were also rejected, though they came with clear proofs, scriptures, and the enlightening Book.
interpretation: This consoles the Prophet ﷺ that rejection by his people does not indicate any deficiency in his message, for earlier messengers likewise faced denial despite presenting unmistakable evidence and revealed guidance. Truth is not measured by the number of those who accept it, but by the clarity and authority of the revelation supporting it.

translation: Every soul will taste death. You will only be given your rewards in full on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has truly succeeded. The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worldly life is temporary and that death is an unavoidable passage for every person, while complete justice and recompense belong to the Day of Resurrection. True success is not measured by worldly wealth, status, or pleasures, but by being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise; worldly attractions are described as deceptive because they can distract people from preparing for their lasting return to God.

translation: You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves, and you will surely hear much hurtful speech from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah. But if you remain patient and mindful of Allah, that is truly among matters requiring firm resolve.
interpretation: Believers should expect trials involving their possessions, personal well-being, and the hostile words of those who oppose faith. They are called to respond neither with despair nor retaliation, but with steadfastness and God-consciousness, since enduring such tests with moral discipline is a mark of determined faith.

translation: And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: “You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it.” But they cast it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. How miserable is what they purchase.
interpretation: This verse condemns the betrayal of divine knowledge: those entrusted with revelation are obligated to explain its truth openly and honestly, not hide or distort it for worldly advantage. Treating guidance as something to be traded for status, wealth, or approval is a profound loss, because no temporary benefit can compensate for abandoning the responsibility of truth.

translation: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done are secure from punishment. They shall have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against taking delight in one’s deeds while seeking undeserved praise and recognition. Such self-deception and love of reputation do not make a person successful before God; rather, they expose the insincerity of the heart and carry the consequence of painful punishment.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is powerful over all things.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth is under Allah’s ownership, authority, and governance. Nothing lies beyond His power, so all creation depends upon Him and must ultimately answer to Him.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: The vastness and ordered design of the universe, together with the recurring succession of night and day, point discerning minds toward the wisdom, power, and oneness of their Creator.

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, saying, “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
interpretation: This verse portrays sincere faith as a constant awareness of Allah in every circumstance, joined with thoughtful reflection on the order and purpose of creation. Such reflection leads the believer to recognize that existence is not meaningless, to glorify Allah’s wisdom and perfection, and to seek protection from the consequences of living without regard for Him.

translation: Our Lord, surely whoever You admit into the Fire, You have truly disgraced; and the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: This supplication recognizes that entry into the Fire is the ultimate humiliation and consequence of wrongdoing, because it reflects divine judgment and the loss of every means of rescue. No worldly power, ally, or advocate can protect those who persist in injustice from God’s judgment.

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith: “Believe in your Lord,” and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins, erase our misdeeds, and cause us to die among the righteous.
interpretation: This supplication expresses the response of sincere believers to divine guidance: they accept faith when its call reaches them, then acknowledge their need for God’s mercy. Their request for forgiveness, the removal of their faults, and a righteous end shows that true faith is joined with humility, repentance, and hope to remain steadfast until death in the company of the righteous.

translation: Our Lord, grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break the promise.
interpretation: This is a supplication expressing complete trust in Allah’s promise while acknowledging the believer’s need for His mercy and protection from humiliation on the Day of Judgment. The request is not based on doubt in Allah, but on humble dependence upon Him and hope that He will fulfill the promise conveyed by His messengers.

translation: So their Lord answered them: “I will never allow the deed of any worker among you to be lost, whether male or female; you are members of one another. Those who emigrated, were driven from their homes, were persecuted in My cause, fought, and were killed—I will surely erase their sins and admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah; and with Allah is the best reward.”
interpretation: Allah assures believers that no sincere effort made for His sake is overlooked or diminished, regardless of whether the person is male or female. Faithful sacrifice—leaving one’s home, enduring persecution, and striving courageously in His cause—is met with forgiveness and lasting Paradise. The verse therefore establishes that spiritual worth and divine reward depend on sincere faith and deeds, not on gender or worldly status.

translation: Do not let the prosperity and movement of those who disbelieve throughout the lands deceive you.
interpretation: The worldly power, success, and freedom enjoyed by those who reject faith should not mislead believers into thinking that such advantages prove God’s approval or that disbelief ultimately prevails; these are temporary worldly circumstances, not a measure of truth or final success.

translation: A brief enjoyment; then their abode will be Hell—and what a miserable resting place.
interpretation: The worldly prosperity of those who reject the truth is only temporary and insignificant; their ultimate destination is Hell, whose punishment is the worst possible dwelling.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining there forever—a welcoming provision from Allah. And what is with Allah is better for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the fleeting attractions available to people in this world with the lasting honor Allah has prepared for those who live in reverent obedience to Him. Their eternal dwelling is not merely a reward, but a gracious reception from Allah; therefore, the true measure of success is what He grants in the Hereafter, which surpasses every worldly benefit.

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly devoted to Allah. They do not exchange Allah’s verses for a small price. For them is their reward with their Lord. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse honors sincere people among the People of the Scripture who recognize the truth in the revelation given to them and in the Qur’an, submitting humbly to Allah rather than allowing prejudice, status, or worldly gain to prevent them from accepting it. Because they do not distort or conceal Allah’s signs for material benefit, Allah promises them a reward with Him, and His swift reckoning affirms that no act of sincere faith and integrity will be overlooked.

translation: O believers, be steadfast, persevere in steadfastness, remain vigilant, and be mindful of Allah, so that you may prosper.
interpretation: Believers are called to cultivate inner patience, support one another in enduring hardship, remain watchful and committed to their responsibilities, and maintain God-consciousness; through this steadfast discipline, they attain true success.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O humanity, be mindful of your Lord, Who created you from a single soul, created from it its mate, and from the two spread countless men and women. Be mindful of Allah, in whose name you appeal to one another, and honor family ties. Surely Allah is ever watchful over you.
interpretation: The verse establishes that all people share one origin and therefore possess a fundamental human dignity that should prevent arrogance, oppression, and division. Awareness of Allah must govern both one’s dealings with others and one’s treatment of relatives, whose rights are especially emphasized because family bonds arise from the same human origin. Since Allah continually watches over every person, reverence for Him should be expressed through justice, compassion, and responsibility toward others.

translation: Give the orphans their wealth, and do not substitute the bad for the good. Do not consume their wealth by adding it to your own. Indeed, that is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse commands those responsible for orphans to safeguard and return their property faithfully, forbidding them from replacing valuable assets with inferior ones or appropriating the orphans’ wealth for themselves. Such exploitation of the vulnerable is a grave moral offense before God.

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry women of your choice—two, three, or four. But if you fear that you will not maintain justice, then marry only one, or those whom your right hands possess. That is more likely to keep you from injustice.
interpretation: The verse addresses the responsibility of protecting the rights of orphans, particularly in marriage, and prohibits taking advantage of their vulnerability or wealth. It permits marriage to up to four women only on the strict condition that equal justice can be maintained among them; if this cannot be assured, one wife is required. Thus, the permission is limited by the obligation of justice, while the verse’s final principle directs believers away from oppression, neglect, and unequal treatment.

translation: Give women their bridal gifts graciously. But if they willingly give up any part of it for you, then accept and enjoy it with ease and satisfaction.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the bridal gift is a woman’s rightful property, to be given to her freely and without reluctance. A husband may take any portion of it only when she willingly and genuinely chooses to relinquish it, not through pressure, manipulation, or coercion.

translation: Do not entrust those lacking sound judgment with the wealth that Allah has made a means of support for you. Provide for them from it, clothe them, and speak to them words of kindness.
interpretation: The verse instructs guardians to protect wealth from being placed under the control of those unable to manage it wisely, while still using that wealth to meet their legitimate needs for food, clothing, and care. This responsibility must be carried out with dignity and compassionate speech, not with humiliation or neglect.

translation: Test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage; then, if you perceive sound judgment in them, hand over their property to them. Do not consume it extravagantly or hastily, fearing that they will come of age. Whoever is wealthy should abstain, and whoever is poor may take from it in a fair manner. When you hand over their property to them, have witnesses present over them. And sufficient is Allah as an accountant.
interpretation: This verse establishes that an orphan’s wealth is a trust, not an opportunity for exploitation. The guardian must assess both the orphan’s maturity and ability to manage property before returning it, while protecting it from waste or premature appropriation. A wealthy guardian must take nothing, whereas a needy guardian may receive only reasonable compensation for necessary care and management. Witnesses and the reminder that Allah keeps account place the entire process under moral and legal accountability.

translation: For men is a share of what parents and close relatives leave behind, and for women is a share of what parents and close relatives leave behind—whether it is little or much—a prescribed share.
interpretation: This verse establishes that inheritance is a divinely mandated right for both men and women, regardless of the size of the estate; no heir entitled by God’s law may be excluded or deprived because the amount is small or because of customary preferences.

translation: And when relatives, orphans, and the needy are present at the distribution, give them something from it and speak to them kindly.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the distribution of wealth should be carried out with compassion and dignity: vulnerable people who are present should be given a suitable share or provision from what is being distributed, and they should never be humiliated or dismissed, but addressed with gracious and considerate words.

translation: Let those who, if they were to leave behind weak offspring, would fear for them, be mindful of Allah and speak words that are upright.
interpretation: This verse calls people entrusted with the vulnerable—especially orphans—to treat them with the same care and protection they would want for their own children. Their conduct should arise from reverence for Allah, and their words should be truthful, fair, and beneficial rather than manipulative or harmful.

translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will enter a blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse gives a grave warning against taking, wasting, or misusing an orphan’s property. Such wrongdoing may appear to bring worldly gain, but before God it is like consuming fire and will lead to severe punishment unless the injustice is abandoned and rectified.

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, a share equal to that of two females. If there are more than two daughters, they receive two-thirds of what he leaves; and if there is only one, she receives half. Each of his parents receives one-sixth of what he leaves if he has a child. If he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then his mother receives one-third. But if he has siblings, his mother receives one-sixth—after any bequest he makes or debt is paid. You do not know which of your fathers or children is nearer to you in benefit. This is an obligation from Allah. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that inheritance is a divine obligation rather than a matter left to personal preference or changing family expectations. It assigns fixed shares according to the responsibilities and relationships within the family, while requiring that debts and valid bequests be settled first. The different shares are not a measure of human worth; they form part of a divinely ordered system intended to protect relatives’ rights and prevent disputes. Because people cannot know fully who will be most beneficial to them, they are instructed to accept Allah’s wiser judgment concerning the distribution of wealth.

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, then for you is one-fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they may have made or debt. And for them is one-fourth of what you leave if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is one-eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you may have made or debt. If a man or woman leaves an inheritance in the case of kalālah, and has a brother or sister, then each of them receives one-sixth. But if they are more than one, then they share one-third, after any bequest made or debt, without causing harm. This is a commandment from Allah; and Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse establishes measured inheritance rights for spouses and for maternal siblings in a case where the deceased has no direct descendants and no surviving ascendant who takes precedence. The shares are assigned only after legitimate debts and bequests are settled, while bequests must not be used to deprive rightful heirs or cause them harm. Thus, inheritance is presented as a binding divine order that protects family rights, restrains personal manipulation, and balances precise justice with Allah’s complete knowledge and forbearance.

translation: These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: Allah’s commands and boundaries are not arbitrary restrictions but a divinely guided path to true flourishing. Those who submit to Allah and follow His Messenger with sincere obedience attain lasting security and eternal reward, which is the greatest success beyond every temporary worldly gain.

translation: Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, remaining there forever, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting Allah’s guidance and violating the boundaries He has established is not a minor matter: it leads to lasting punishment and humiliation, because such disobedience reflects defiance of divine authority rather than merely an isolated error.

translation: As for those of your women who commit indecency, call four witnesses from among you against them. If they testify, confine them to their homes until death takes them or Allah appoints for them a way.
interpretation: تقرر الآية إجراءً تشريعيًا في المرحلة الأولى تجاه الزنا، فلا تُقبل الدعوى فيه إلا بشهادة أربعة شهود، ثم تُلزم المرأة المدانَة بالإقامة في بيتها إلى أن يشرع الله حكمًا آخر. وفي ذلك تشديد بالغ في إثبات الجريمة وصيانة للأعراض من الاتهام، وقد فُهم السبيل الذي جعله الله لاحقًا على أنه الحكم المبيَّن في سورة النور.

translation: And the two among you who commit it, discipline them both. Then, if they repent and reform, leave them alone. Surely Allah is Ever-Relenting, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that wrongdoing should be met with corrective censure, but not with continued persecution once genuine repentance and reform are evident. It directs the community to recognize sincere change and to end the punishment, reflecting Allah’s readiness to accept repentance and His mercy toward those who amend their conduct.

translation: Allah’s acceptance of repentance is only for those who commit evil out of ignorance, then repent soon afterward. It is they whose repentance Allah accepts. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse assures that sincere repentance remains open to those who fall into sin through human heedlessness or weakness and turn back without delay. Such repentance is accepted because Allah knows the servant’s true condition and intention, and in His wisdom He distinguishes genuine return to Him from repentance postponed until death or made without sincerity.

translation: Repentance is not for those who persist in doing evil until, when death comes to one of them, he says, “I repent now,” nor for those who die as disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن التوبة المقبولة تكون قبل بلوغ الإنسان حال الاحتضار، حين تنكشف له الحقيقة ويزول مجال الاختيار؛ أما من يؤخر التوبة حتى حضور الموت، أو يلقى الله مصرًّا على الكفر، فلا تنفعه توبته المتأخرة، وقد أُعدّ له عذاب أليم.

translation: O believers, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to constrain them in order to take back part of what you have given them—unless they commit a manifest indecency. Live with them honorably; and if you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.
interpretation: This verse establishes that women are not possessions to be inherited or controlled, and that a husband may not pressure his wife merely to reclaim wealth he gave her. Marriage must be governed by dignity, kindness, and fairness, even when affection is diminished. A person should not hastily act on dislike, for patience and honorable treatment may reveal goodness and blessings that were not initially apparent; only clear, serious misconduct constitutes the stated exception.

translation: If you intend to replace one wife with another, and you have given one of them a great amount, then do not take anything back from it. Would you take it through false accusation and manifest sin?
interpretation: The verse forbids a husband from reclaiming the bridal gift or wealth he gave his wife merely because he wishes to divorce her and marry another. Even if the gift was immense, it remains hers; taking it back through pressure, defamation, or fabricated accusations is a grave and evident wrongdoing.

translation: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض، وأخذن منكم ميثاقًا غليظًا؟
interpretation: ينكر الله على الزوج أن يستردّ من زوجته شيئًا مما أعطاها، بعد أن حصل بينهما من القرب والعشرة ما يجعل المال حقًّا ثابتًا لها، وبعد أن التزم لها بعقد الزواج عهدًا مؤكدًا عظيم الحرمة؛ فليس من الوفاء ولا من العدل أن تُنتقص حقوقها أو يُستغلّ الفراق لسلبها مالها.

translation: Do not marry women whom your fathers married, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an obscenity, hateful, and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse forbids a man from marrying any woman who was married to his father, thereby preserving the sanctity of family relationships and preventing a grave violation of parental honor. What happened before this prohibition was revealed is exempted from punishment, while continuing such a practice is condemned as morally abhorrent and destructive.

translation: Forbidden to you in marriage are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers’ daughters, your sisters’ daughters, your foster mothers who nursed you, your foster sisters, the mothers of your wives, your stepdaughters under your care who are born of wives with whom you have consummated marriage—but if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you—and the wives of your biological sons. And it is forbidden to marry two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permanent and temporary boundaries of marriage in order to protect family relationships, lineage, and social dignity. It treats certain blood relationships and equivalent relationships created through breastfeeding as marriage prohibitions, and it also prohibits marrying a wife’s daughter after consummating marriage with her mother, as well as marrying the wife of one’s biological son. The ban on combining two sisters preserves the bonds of sisterhood and prevents marital rivalry within the same family. The reference to Allah’s forgiveness and mercy indicates that these rules are binding from the time they are known, while sincere repentance is accepted for what occurred before the prohibition was understood or observed.

translation: And married women are forbidden to you, except those whom your right hands possess. This is God’s decree upon you. Lawful for you are all others, provided you seek them in marriage with your wealth, desiring chastity, not illicit relations. So for whatever you have enjoyed from them, give them their bridal gifts as an obligation. There is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree to beyond the prescribed gift. Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse establishes that marriage is a lawful, committed bond rather than a license for sexual exploitation or promiscuity. It prohibits taking married women as wives while recognizing the specific historical circumstance of women captives under the laws governing the society at that time, and commands that lawful relationships be entered through a recognized marriage arrangement, with financial responsibility and a required bridal gift. The concluding permission for mutual agreement concerns additional arrangements between the spouses after the obligatory bridal gift, all subject to God’s knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women may marry believing women from among those whom your right hands possess. Allah knows best the reality of your faith; you are all from one another. So marry them with the permission of their guardians and give them their bridal gifts in a fair manner, provided they are chaste, neither openly promiscuous nor taking secret lovers. Then, once they are married, if they commit an indecency, they shall receive half the punishment prescribed for free married women. This permission is for those among you who fear falling into hardship and sin; but to be patient is better for you. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse regulates marriage to believing bondwomen for men unable to marry free believing women, requiring the consent of their guardians, a proper bridal gift, and the preservation of chastity rather than exploitation or illicit relationships. By affirming that faith unites people as members of one human community, it places these women within the moral and legal order of the believers. The reduced penalty mentioned after marriage reflects their distinct legal status in that society, while the closing exhortation teaches that self-restraint is preferable whenever one can avoid the difficulty and temptation altogether.

translation: Allah desires to make clear to you, guide you to the ways of those who came before you, and accept your repentance. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah’s guidance clarifies the lawful and upright path, connects it with the sound ways followed by righteous people before you, and opens the door for you to return from error and sin. His commands and acceptance of repentance are grounded in complete knowledge of human weakness and perfect wisdom.

translation: Allah desires to turn to you in mercy, while those who follow their passions desire that you deviate far from the right path.
interpretation: Allah’s guidance and commands are intended to lead people back to purity and repentance, whereas those governed by unchecked desires seek to draw believers into grave moral deviation and away from obedience to Him.

translation: Allah desires to lighten your burdens, for humankind was created weak.
interpretation: Allah’s laws are established with mercy and consideration for human limitations. Because people are vulnerable to desire, hardship, and error, He provides ease and legitimate concessions rather than imposing obligations beyond their capacity.

translation: O you who believe, do not consume one another’s wealth wrongfully, except through trade conducted by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves; surely Allah is ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to respect one another’s property and dignity: wealth may be exchanged only through lawful dealings based on genuine, willing consent, not through fraud, exploitation, coercion, or injustice. The prohibition against killing yourselves includes forbidding suicide and harming one another, emphasizing that human life is sacred and must be protected under Allah’s mercy.

translation: Whoever does that in transgression and injustice, We shall make him enter the Fire; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately violating God’s prohibitions through aggression and wrongdoing exposes a person to the punishment of Hell, while affirming that bringing such judgment about is effortless for Allah.

translation: If you avoid the major sins from which you are forbidden, We will erase your lesser sins and admit you into an honorable entrance.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincerely refraining from grave sins is a means by which God, out of His mercy, forgives lesser faults and grants the believer a dignified entrance into Paradise. It emphasizes both the seriousness of major sins and the generosity of divine pardon for those who conscientiously avoid them.

translation: Do not desire what Allah has given some of you in preference over others. Men will have a share of what they earn, and women will have a share of what they earn. Ask Allah of His bounty. Surely Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse teaches believers to avoid resentful longing for the particular advantages granted to others, since such comparisons can lead to envy and discontent. Each person—man and woman alike—is accountable for and rewarded according to their own efforts and deeds. Rather than coveting another’s provision or status, one should seek Allah’s bounty through lawful effort, prayer, and trust in His perfect knowledge of what is best for each person.

translation: For each person We have appointed heirs to what the parents and close relatives leave behind. As for those with whom you have made binding agreements, give them their due share. Surely Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: Allah establishes rightful claims to inheritance for those connected to the deceased through family ties, while also requiring that binding commitments and covenants be honored by granting the parties concerned whatever share or due entitlement the agreement gives them. Nothing of these rights is hidden from Allah, whose complete knowledge and witness make their fulfillment a moral and religious obligation.

translation: Men are responsible for the care and maintenance of women because Allah has given some of them advantages over others, and because they spend of their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient and guard in the husband’s absence what Allah has entrusted them to guard. As for those from whom you fear persistent marital defiance, admonish them, then leave them alone in bed, and then strike them; but if they obey you, do not seek any means against them. Surely Allah is Most High, Most Great.
interpretation: The verse assigns men a duty of protection, provision, and responsible leadership within the family—not an unrestricted right of domination—while recognizing righteous women as faithful guardians of the marriage and its trusts. In the case of serious marital defiance, it prescribes a gradual process: sincere counsel, temporary separation in the marital bed, and, only as a final measure, a strictly non-injurious symbolic act that may never involve humiliation, harm, or abuse. Once reconciliation occurs, the husband has no right to continue reproaching or persecuting his wife, and the closing reminder of Allah’s supreme authority restrains him from tyranny.

translation: And if you fear a breach between the two of them, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring harmony between them. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: When serious conflict threatens a marriage, the matter should be entrusted to two fair and trustworthy representatives—one from each family—who seek reconciliation rather than victory for either side. Their sincere effort can become a means through which Allah restores understanding and harmony, while reminding everyone that He knows the true intentions and circumstances of both spouses.

translation: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and show kindness to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Surely Allah does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that sincere devotion to Allah must be reflected in compassionate and responsible conduct toward others. It calls for honoring parents, supporting vulnerable people, maintaining ties with relatives, and extending kindness to neighbors, companions, travelers, and those under one’s authority or care. By ending with a warning against arrogance and boastfulness, it teaches that genuine worship is incompatible with pride, self-importance, and mistreating or looking down on people.

translation: Those who are miserly, urge others to be miserly, and conceal what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty—we have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who withhold Allah’s blessings, discourage others from generosity, and conceal the favors or knowledge entrusted to them. Such conduct reflects rejection of Allah’s grace and leads to a punishment that humiliates those who persist in disbelief.

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day—whoever takes Satan as a companion, what an evil companion he has.
interpretation: This verse condemns charitable spending when it is driven by ostentation rather than sincere faith and devotion to Allah. Such outward generosity has no true spiritual value because it seeks people’s praise while rejecting accountability before Allah; by choosing this path, a person allows Satan to accompany and mislead him, leading him away from sincerity and lasting good.

translation: And what harm would come to them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah had provided them? Allah is All-Knowing of them.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who withhold faith and charity, showing that belief in Allah and the Hereafter, together with spending from His provision, would bring them no loss but rather benefit. Their motives, sincerity, and refusal to act are fully known to Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and grants from Himself a tremendous reward.
interpretation: Allah’s perfect justice means that no person will suffer the slightest injustice: every deed, however small, is fully known and fairly accounted for. Yet His mercy surpasses mere justice, for He increases the value of good deeds and bestows a vast reward from His own grace.

translation: So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these people?
interpretation: The verse portrays the solemn scene of Judgment, when every community’s messenger will testify regarding its response to divine guidance, while the Prophet Muhammad will testify concerning his people. It warns that no one will be able to conceal their rejection or neglect, because their conduct will be confronted with the testimony of those who conveyed God’s message.

translation: On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth had been leveled over them, and they will not be able to conceal a single statement from Allah.
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter humiliation of those who rejected divine guidance: when judgment makes the truth undeniable, they will prefer to be buried beneath the earth rather than face accountability. Yet concealment will be impossible, because Allah’s knowledge exposes every deed, word, and excuse.

translation: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you understand what you are saying, nor while in a state of major ritual impurity—except when merely passing through—until you have bathed. If you are ill, traveling, have relieved yourselves, or have had intimate contact with women, and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Indeed, God is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to approach prayer with conscious understanding and bodily purification, not in a condition that prevents awareness of their words or while affected by major impurity. When water cannot be used or found because of illness, travel, or the stated causes of purification, God provides tayammum with clean earth as a merciful substitute. This ruling shows that purification is required for worship, while divine law also accommodates genuine hardship and repeatedly opens the way to forgiveness.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They purchase misguidance and wish that you too would lose the way.
interpretation: يعاتب الله المؤمنين على حال أناسٍ أوتوا علماً من الوحي، ثم آثروا الضلال على الهدى، ولم يكتفوا بانحرافهم، بل سعوا إلى إضلال غيرهم وصرفهم عن الطريق المستقيم؛ وفي ذلك تحذير من اتباع الهوى ومن التأثر بمن يستعمل العلم لإبعاد الناس عن الحق.

translation: Allah knows best who your enemies are. Allah is sufficient as a Protector, and Allah is sufficient as a Helper.
interpretation: Believers should not be deceived by the schemes or apparent strength of those who oppose them, for Allah fully knows their hostility and is enough to safeguard, support, and grant victory to those who rely on Him.

translation: Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their proper places and say, “We hear and we disobey,” and, “Hear—may you not be made to hear,” and “Rāʿinā,” twisting their tongues and attacking the religion. Had they said, “We hear and we obey,” and, “Hear us,” and “Look upon us,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has condemned them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few.
interpretation: This verse exposes the deliberate misuse of religious language as an expression of defiance: words are altered, ambiguous phrases are used to mock or insult, and outward speech conceals inner rejection. It teaches that true faith requires sincere obedience and respectful speech, not merely the appearance of listening. Their condemnation is attributed to persistent disbelief, while the few who believe remain an exception.

translation: O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what you already possess, before We obliterate faces and turn them backward, or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath. And the command of Allah is always fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse calls the People of the Scripture to accept the Qur’an because it confirms the truth originally revealed to them, warning that deliberate rejection after the truth has become clear brings severe divine punishment and disgrace, just as earlier transgressors were punished; Allah’s decree cannot be prevented or thwarted.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything less than that for whom He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse establishes that associating partners with Allah is the gravest form of wrongdoing because it attributes divine rights to something besides the One who alone deserves worship. If a person dies persisting in such association without repentance, it is not forgiven; whereas other sins remain subject to Allah’s will—He may forgive them or hold the sinner accountable. The verse therefore calls the believer to preserve pure monotheism and not treat any sin as insignificant.

translation: Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even by the thread of a date stone.
interpretation: The verse condemns self-righteousness and the assumption that one’s own claims, lineage, or deeds guarantee moral or spiritual purity. True purification is granted by Allah, who knows the reality of people better than they know themselves; nevertheless, He will judge them with perfect justice and deprive them of nothing, however insignificant.

translation: See how they invent lies against Allah; and sufficient is that as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This is a condemnation of those who attribute to Allah what He has not said or claim for themselves a purity and status He did not grant them. Such deliberate distortion is an unmistakable and grave sin before Him.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, yet believe in false deities and evil powers, and say to those who disbelieve, “These are more rightly guided than those who believe”?
interpretation: The verse censures people who possess knowledge from revelation but abandon its guidance, yielding to falsehood and oppressive powers. Their corruption reaches the point of endorsing disbelief and claiming that its followers are more rightly guided than the believers, showing how prejudice and pursuit of worldly interests can distort judgment even among those familiar with Scripture.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has condemned; and whoever Allah condemns, you will never find for him any helper.
interpretation: This warns that persistent rebellion against Allah’s guidance can lead to divine rejection, leaving a person without any protector or support capable of saving him from the consequences of that rejection.

translation: Or do they have a share in sovereignty? If so, they would not give people even the speck on a date stone.
interpretation: The verse exposes the envy and miserliness of those who resent God’s favor upon others: even if they possessed authority and control, they would withhold from people the tiniest possible share. It therefore reminds that true dominion belongs to God, who grants His فضل as He wills, while human beings have no justification for begrudging His generosity.

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has granted them of His bounty? Indeed, We gave the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.
interpretation: The verse condemns resentful envy of divinely granted favor: some people objected to the guidance and honor bestowed upon Muhammad and the believers, even though God had already granted the family of Abraham revelation, wisdom, and sovereignty. Such envy is irrational, because God’s gifts are bestowed according to His wisdom, and resenting them does not diminish them but exposes the envier’s rejection of God’s decree.

translation: Among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it. And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire.
interpretation: People respond differently to divine truth: some accept it with faith, while others deliberately reject it. The verse warns that turning away from revelation is not without consequence, for Hell is a fitting and devastating punishment for such rejection.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs—we will expose them to the Fire. Whenever their skins are fully consumed, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment. Surely, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the relentless punishment prepared for those who knowingly reject Allah’s signs: their suffering is repeatedly renewed, so it does not end through the destruction of their bodies. It also affirms that this judgment is carried out by Allah’s absolute power and perfect wisdom, establishing that the punishment is neither arbitrary nor beyond His authority.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. There they will have purified spouses, and We will admit them into deep, welcome shade.
interpretation: This verse promises enduring Paradise to those whose faith is expressed through righteous action. Its purified spouses and abundant shade signify a state completely free from impurity, discomfort, and hardship, in which God grants the believers lasting peace, honor, and comfort.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to whom they are due, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Excellent indeed is that with which Allah instructs you. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith requires fulfilling every trust—whether property, responsibility, promise, or entrusted authority—and returning it to its rightful holder without betrayal or favoritism. It also commands that every judgment among people be governed by justice, regardless of personal feelings, status, kinship, or enmity. Allah’s awareness of every word, decision, and hidden motive warns that these duties cannot be reduced to outward appearances; their true fulfillment is accountable before Him.

translation: O you who believe, obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and those entrusted with authority among you. If you differ over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger, if you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and best in outcome.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to obey Allah and His Messenger as the ultimate sources of guidance, and to obey legitimate authority within the community so long as that obedience does not conflict with divine instruction. When disagreement arises, it must be resolved by returning to the Qur’an and the authentic guidance of the Messenger, for doing so is a sign of genuine faith and leads to the soundest and most just outcome.

translation: Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they wish to seek judgment from false authorities, although they were commanded to reject them? Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of claiming faith while turning for ultimate judgment to authorities that oppose God’s revealed guidance. True faith requires rejecting every false source of ultimate authority and willingly submitting disputes to God’s revelation and the judgment that accords with it; choosing contrary judgments is a path of deception that carries a person far from the truth.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,” you see the hypocrites turning away from you in utter aversion.
interpretation: This portrays the hypocrites’ contradiction: although they profess faith, they reject the authority of Allah’s revelation and the Messenger’s judgment when it conflicts with their desires, deliberately avoiding the truth rather than submitting to it.

translation: So how will it be when a calamity befalls them because of what their own hands have sent ahead, then they come to you swearing by Allah, “We intended nothing but kindness and reconciliation”?
interpretation: The verse exposes the false justification of those who turn away from divine guidance: when the consequences of their own choices reach them, they disguise disobedience as good intention. Their oath does not change the reality that sincere goodness and reconciliation must be grounded in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, not used as excuses after wrongdoing.

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows. So turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them words that deeply reach their souls.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to deal with people whose inner hypocrisy and intentions are known to God by not becoming entangled in their outward excuses, while still offering sincere counsel. Their correction should be personal and profound—words that confront their conscience, awaken fear of God, and leave them no excuse to persist in wrongdoing.

translation: We did not send any messenger except that he be obeyed by Allah’s permission. If, when they had wronged themselves, they had come to you, sought Allah’s forgiveness, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Most Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that obedience to the Messenger is part of obedience to Allah, since his authority comes from Him. It also opens the way of return for those who have wronged themselves: sincere repentance requires turning to Allah, while seeking the Messenger’s prayer for forgiveness reflects humility and recognition of the authority Allah granted him. Whoever approaches Allah in this spirit will find Him welcoming repentance and extending mercy.

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not truly believe until they make you judge in whatever disputes arise among them, then find no resistance within themselves regarding what you decide, and submit with complete submission.
interpretation: True faith requires accepting the Messenger’s judgment as the decisive standard in disputes—not merely outwardly, but with the heart free from resentment or objection, and with wholehearted obedience to what he has commanded.

translation: And if We had prescribed for them, “Kill yourselves” or “Leave your homes,” they would not have done so except for a few of them. But if they had carried out what they were instructed to do, it would have been better for them and more strengthening.
interpretation: The verse exposes how reluctant many people are to obey divine commands when obedience demands great sacrifice. It teaches that genuine faith is shown through sincere compliance with God’s guidance, and that acting upon His instruction brings a person greater good, steadfastness, and strength in faith.

translation: Then We would surely have granted them from Us a great reward.
interpretation: Those who sincerely obey Allah and His Messenger are promised an immense reward that comes directly from Allah, emphasizing both its greatness and its special divine generosity.

translation: And We would surely have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: Had they obeyed Allah and His Messenger, Allah would have granted them clear, unwavering guidance leading to faith, righteous conduct, and salvation.

translation: Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has favored: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And how excellent are such companions!
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger elevates a person into the company of those who attained the highest ranks of faith and virtue. This companionship is not merely an honor in the Hereafter; it reflects a life shaped by truthfulness, sacrifice, and righteousness, leading to the finest spiritual fellowship and ultimate felicity.

translation: That is the bounty from Allah; and Allah is sufficient as All-Knowing.
interpretation: The honor and blessings granted to the faithful come entirely from Allah’s grace, and His perfect knowledge encompasses their deeds, sincerity, and spiritual rank.

translation: O you who believe, take your precautions, then march forth in groups, or march forth all together.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to remain vigilant and prepared when facing danger, organizing themselves wisely according to circumstances—whether by sending out smaller units or mobilizing collectively—rather than acting heedlessly or disorderly.

translation: And indeed among you is one who hangs back; then, if a calamity befalls you, he says, “Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the selfishness of the hypocrite who avoids sacrifice and responsibility, viewing the believers’ hardship only as something from which he has personally escaped rather than sharing their concern or standing with them.

translation: And if bounty from Allah befalls you, he will surely say—as though there had never been any affection between you and him—“If only I had been with them, I would have achieved a great triumph.”
interpretation: This describes the hypocrite whose loyalty is driven by personal gain: when believers receive success, he wishes he had joined them, not out of sincere faith or solidarity, but so that he could share in their worldly victory and spoils.

translation: So let those who trade the life of this world for the Hereafter fight in the cause of Allah. And whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or is victorious, We shall grant him a tremendous reward.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to place the everlasting reward of the Hereafter above worldly life and to strive sincerely in Allah’s cause. Their reward does not depend on the worldly outcome: whether they die or achieve victory, Allah promises them a great reward.

translation: And why do you not fight in the cause of Allah and for the sake of the oppressed men, women, and children who say, “Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper”?
interpretation: This verse calls believers to confront oppression and defend those who are unable to defend themselves. It presents the rescue of the oppressed as a righteous cause connected to devotion to Allah, while conveying their plea for liberation, protection, and help through means granted by Him.

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, while those who disbelieve fight in the cause of falsehood. So fight the allies of Satan; surely the plotting of Satan is weak.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between two opposing purposes: believers are to strive under God’s guidance and for justice, whereas the forces of disbelief are driven by false powers and corrupt aims. It therefore urges believers to resist those who serve such falsehood, reassuring them that Satan’s schemes—despite their apparent strength—cannot ultimately prevail against sincere faith and reliance on Allah.

translation: Have you not seen those who were told, “Withhold your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah”? Then, when fighting was prescribed for them, a group of them feared people as they should fear Allah—or even more—and said, “Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would delay it for us for a short while.” Say, “The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for whoever is mindful of Allah; and you will not be wronged, even by the thread of a date stone.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the weakness of faith that can appear when religious responsibility becomes difficult or costly. Those who had asked for permission to fight were first instructed to cultivate obedience through prayer and charity; when fighting was later commanded, some became more fearful of people than of Allah and preferred worldly safety. Allah reminds them that worldly life is fleeting, whereas the lasting good belongs to those who remain mindful of Him, and that obedience to His command will never cause them the slightest injustice or loss.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortified towers. When good befalls them, they say, “This is from Allah”; but when evil befalls them, they say, “This is from you.” Say, “All is from Allah.” What is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: The verse teaches that death reaches every person regardless of the strength of their defenses, so security cannot be found in worldly means alone. It also exposes the injustice of attributing blessings to Allah while blaming the Prophet for misfortunes: everything occurs by Allah’s decree, though human wrongdoing may be the cause of the harm people bring upon themselves. Their refusal to recognize this reveals a failure to understand faith and divine providence.

translation: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. We have sent you to humanity as a messenger, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: The verse teaches that every blessing should be recognized as a gift and favor from Allah, while a person must take responsibility for the wrong and harm that arise from their own choices and disobedience. It also affirms the Messenger’s mission to all people and establishes Allah’s testimony as sufficient proof of the truth of his message.

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has truly obeyed Allah. And whoever turns away—we have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: Obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah because the Messenger conveys and applies Allah’s guidance; faith therefore requires accepting his divinely guided commands. As for those who reject or turn away, the Prophet’s duty is to convey the truth, not to control people’s hearts or compel their obedience.

translation: They say, “Obedience.” But when they leave you, a group of them secretly plots at night contrary to what you have said. Allah records what they secretly devise. So turn away from them and place your trust in Allah; and Allah is sufficient as a Guardian.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who profess obedience outwardly while privately working against revealed guidance. Their hidden schemes are fully known and recorded by Allah, so the believer should not be overcome by their duplicity, but remain steadfast, disengage from their plotting, and entrust the matter to Allah, whose protection and support are sufficient.

translation: Do they not contemplate the Qur’an? Had it been from anyone other than Allah, they would have found in it much inconsistency.
interpretation: تدعو الآية إلى التأمل العميق في القرآن، لا إلى تلاوته دون فهم؛ فانسجام معانيه وتشريعاته، رغم نزوله متفرقًا وفي ظروف متعددة، يدل على أنه وحي من الله لا كلام بشر تحكمه حدود المعرفة والظروف.

translation: And when news of security or fear reaches them, they spread it publicly.
