Had they referred it to the Messenger and to those entrusted with authority among them, those capable of discerning its implications would have understood it from them. Were it not for Allah’s فضل and mercy upon you, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: The verse teaches that reports affecting public safety must not be circulated impulsively. They should be referred to the Messenger—and, after him, to qualified and trustworthy authorities—so that those with sound judgment can verify them, assess their consequences, and explain the proper response. It also reminds believers that their restraint and guidance are blessings from Allah, without which most people could be drawn into harmful confusion and obedience to Satan.

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are accountable only for yourself, and urge the believers. Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. Allah is stronger in might and more severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet must fulfill his own duty courageously, without allowing the hesitation or refusal of others to prevent him, while also inspiring the believers to stand firm. Victory and the restraint of hostile forces ultimately depend on Allah, whose power surpasses theirs and whose punishment is more severe.

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of its reward, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will bear a share of its burden. Allah is ever watchful and capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that advocating for others is morally significant: one shares in the consequences of whatever cause one supports, whether beneficial or harmful. Therefore, a believer should use influence to promote justice and good, knowing that Allah fully accounts for every deed.

translation: When you are greeted with a greeting, respond with one better than it, or return it equally. Indeed, Allah is ever حسابer of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes that Muslims should answer greetings graciously: they should ideally improve upon the greeting, or at least respond with an equivalent one. It also teaches that no interaction is insignificant before Allah, for He fully knows and holds people accountable for how they treat one another.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. He will surely gather you all on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And whose word is truer than Allah’s?
interpretation: Allah alone is worthy of worship, and His certain promise to resurrect and gather every person for judgment cannot be denied. Since Allah is the most truthful in speech, people should place complete trust in this promise and prepare to stand before Him.

translation: So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has turned them back because of what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has led astray? And whoever Allah leads astray, you will never find for him a way.
interpretation: The verse rebukes the believers for dividing over the hypocrites and judging them by conflicting standards. Their inward corruption and repeated wrongdoing have caused them to be turned away from guidance; therefore, human efforts cannot guide someone who deliberately persists in rejecting the truth. It also teaches that guidance is ultimately granted by Allah, while a person’s choice and accumulated deeds can lead him to become deserving of being left in misguidance.

translation: They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, so that you would be alike. Do not take any of them as allies until they emigrate in the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take any of them as an ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses a wartime situation involving people who outwardly associated with the believers while actively returning to hostility and seeking to make the believers abandon their faith. Their protection and alliance were contingent upon a clear commitment to the believing community, expressed through migration and loyalty to its cause. If they rejected that commitment and remained hostile, the verse permitted combat against them as enemies—not indiscriminate violence against all nonbelievers. The following verse makes this limitation explicit by exempting those who join a treaty or withdraw from fighting.

translation: Except those who join a people with whom you have a treaty, or those who come to you with hearts constrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. Had Allah willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you, do not fight you, and offer you peace, then Allah has not granted you any way against them.
interpretation: This verse establishes that those who neither engage in hostility against the believers nor support their enemies, and who instead seek peace or are bound by a treaty, must be left unharmed. It forbids aggression against people who refrain from fighting and shows that peaceful coexistence removes any justification for combat.

translation: You will find others who wish to be safe from you and safe from their own people. Whenever they are sent back to temptation and conflict, they relapse into it. So, if they do not withdraw from you, offer you peace, and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you encounter them. Against such people We have granted you clear authority.
interpretation: This verse addresses hostile groups in a state of conflict who sought safety from the Muslims while remaining aligned with their own people and repeatedly returning to aggression. The permission to fight is therefore tied to their refusal to withdraw, make peace, and cease hostilities; it is not a general authorization to harm those who are peaceful or uninvolved.

translation: It is not for a believer to kill another believer except by mistake. Whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay blood money to the victim’s family, unless they waive it as charity. If the victim was a believer from a people at war with you, then the killer must free a believing slave. But if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then the killer must pay blood money to his family and free a believing slave. Whoever cannot find the means must fast for two consecutive months, as repentance ordained by Allah. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the sanctity of a believer’s life is inviolable and that even an unintentional killing carries moral and legal responsibility. Its prescribed acts—emancipating a believing person, compensating the victim’s family, and allowing them to forgive the compensation—combine accountability, support for those harmed, and mercy. The differing rulings acknowledge the circumstances of the victim’s community and treaty status, while the two consecutive months of fasting provide a demanding form of repentance for one unable to emancipate a slave. Allah’s perfect knowledge encompasses every circumstance, and His wisdom governs these balanced obligations.

translation: Whoever deliberately kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, remaining therein; Allah is angry with him, has rejected him, and has prepared for him a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This verse presents the deliberate killing of a believer as an exceptionally grave crime: it incurs the severest divine threats because it violates the sanctity of human life and the bonds of faith. Its warning calls the perpetrator to fear Allah’s judgment and underscores that such bloodshed cannot be treated as an ordinary offense or erased through worldly excuses.

translation: O you who believe, when you travel in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who offers you peace, “You are not a believer,” seeking the fleeting gains of worldly life. With Allah are abundant spoils. Thus you were yourselves before, then Allah favored you, so investigate carefully. Indeed, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith cannot be denied on the basis of suspicion or the desire for material gain. Believers must verify a person’s circumstances and accept outward declarations of peace and faith rather than judging hidden intentions, remembering that they themselves once depended on Allah’s guidance and mercy. The repeated command to investigate emphasizes that God knows the motives behind every action.

translation: Those believers who remain behind—except those with a valid hardship—are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has granted those who strive with their wealth and lives a rank above those who remain behind. Yet Allah has promised the best reward to both. And Allah has favored those who strive over those who remain behind with a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse teaches that believers who make greater sacrifices in Allah’s cause—offering their wealth, effort, and lives—receive a higher rank and greater reward than those who stay behind without making that sacrifice. However, those prevented by genuine incapacity are not blameworthy, and those who remain behind while still faithful and obedient are not deprived of Allah’s promised goodness. It therefore combines recognition of differing levels of sacrifice with mercy and fairness toward those whose circumstances limit their ability to act.

translation: Ranks bestowed by Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah grants those who strive sincerely for His cause a higher spiritual standing, while also covering their shortcomings with forgiveness and surrounding them with mercy; this reward reflects His perfect forgiveness and enduring compassion.

translation: Indeed, when the angels take the souls of those who wronged themselves, they say, “What situation were you in?” They reply, “We were oppressed and weak in the land.” The angels say, “Was Allah’s earth not spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?” For such people, their refuge will be Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: This verse warns those who knowingly remain in an environment where they cannot uphold their faith, despite having the ability to leave for a place where they can worship Allah freely. It rejects helplessness as an excuse when a viable path to preserve one’s religion exists, while implying that genuine inability is judged differently.

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who are unable to devise a plan and cannot find a way.
interpretation: This exempts those genuinely powerless to escape oppression: lacking the means, ability, or guidance to change their circumstances. Their inability is recognized by God, so they are not held to account for what lies beyond their capacity.

translation: As for those, perhaps Allah will pardon them; and Allah is ever Pardoning, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: This expresses hope and reassurance that Allah may overlook the shortcomings of those who are unable to fulfill their obligations because of genuine circumstances, for His pardon is constant and His forgiveness encompasses their faults.

translation: Whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find in the earth many places of refuge and abundant provision. Whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward is assured with Allah. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere sacrifice for Allah is never wasted: whoever leaves behind familiar circumstances to uphold faith and obey Allah will find openings and relief, and even if death comes before the journey is completed, the intention and effort are fully rewarded by Allah, whose forgiveness and mercy encompass the servant.

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you. Indeed, the disbelievers are clearly your enemies.
interpretation: God grants travelers a concession to shorten the prayer when circumstances of travel involve danger or vulnerability, easing the burden of worship without excusing it. The warning about the disbelievers’ manifest hostility emphasizes the need for vigilance and reliance on God while preserving the obligation of prayer.

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them take up their arms. Then, when they have prostrated, let them move behind you, and let another group who have not yet prayed come forward and pray with you, taking their precautions and their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your arms and your equipment so that they could fall upon you all at once. There is no blame upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill and therefore lay down your arms, but remain on your guard. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that worship remains connected to responsibility even in danger: the believers organize the prayer in shifts so that they neither abandon their devotion nor expose themselves carelessly to attack. Their readiness is not a failure of trust in Allah, but part of the prudence required of them; only genuine hardship, such as illness or harmful rain, permits them to set down their weapons, while vigilance must remain. The verse thus teaches that reliance upon Allah is expressed through disciplined worship, mutual protection, and taking all reasonable precautions against those who seek to exploit heedlessness.

translation: فإذا أديتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قائمين وقاعدين وعلى جنوبكم، فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة؛ إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين فرضًا محددًا بأوقات.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن ذكر الله لا ينقطع في حال من الأحوال، ولا يسقط عن المؤمن حتى في ظروف الخوف أو العجز، لكنه إذا زال الخوف وجب أداء الصلاة على هيئتها التامة. كما تؤكد أن الصلاة فريضة مرتبطة بأوقات معلومة، فلا يجوز تعمد إخراجها عن وقتها.

translation: Do not falter in pursuing the enemy. If you are suffering, they too are suffering as you suffer; yet you hope from Allah what they do not hope. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse urges believers not to let hardship weaken their resolve in confronting injustice. Both sides may endure pain, but faith gives believers a higher hope in Allah’s reward, support, and ultimate justice; therefore their endurance is grounded in a purpose beyond worldly struggle.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for those who betray trust.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to judge among people according to the guidance He revealed, not according to personal inclination or pressure. Justice requires rejecting deception and refusing to defend the treacherous, even when they seek protection through claims, arguments, or outward appearances.

translation: And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This is a call to turn sincerely to Allah for forgiveness, trusting that He accepts repentance and responds with mercy rather than despairing over one’s mistakes.

translation: Do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love anyone who is persistently treacherous and sinful.
interpretation: The verse forbids taking the side of people who knowingly commit wrongdoing and then seek to conceal it or escape responsibility through false arguments. Such betrayal ultimately harms the wrongdoers themselves, and persistent treachery and sin place a person beyond Allah’s love.

translation: They hide themselves from people, but they cannot hide themselves from Allah, for He is with them when they secretly deliberate words that He does not approve. And Allah encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of concealing wrongdoing from people while disregarding Allah’s constant knowledge and presence. Private schemes and intentions are fully known to Him, so a person’s true accountability is determined not by what is successfully hidden from others, but by what Allah knows of the heart and deeds.

translation: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا، فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة، أم من يكون عليهم وكيلاً؟
interpretation: إن دفاعكم عن الخائنين وتبريركم أفعالهم قد ينفعهم ظاهريًا في الدنيا، لكنه لا يحميهم من عدل الله يوم القيامة؛ فلا أحد يستطيع أن يدفع عنهم حسابه أو يتولى أمرهم ويمنع عنهم جزاء ما اقترفوا.

translation: Whoever does wrong or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse opens the door of repentance to anyone who has committed a sin, whether its harm is directed toward others or toward oneself. Turning sincerely to Allah in remorse and seeking His forgiveness leads to His pardon and mercy.

translation: Whoever commits a sin only commits it against himself. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Wrongdoing ultimately harms the person who chooses it, because its moral and spiritual consequences return to the sinner rather than being transferred to anyone else. Allah knows every intention and action perfectly, and His judgment concerning each person is guided by complete wisdom.

translation: Whoever commits a sin or an offense and then blames it on an innocent person has surely burdened himself with slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: The verse warns that wrongdoing becomes even graver when a person shifts blame onto someone innocent: the guilty party not only commits the original offense but also bears the burden of false accusation and the injustice inflicted upon the blameless.

translation: Had it not been for Allah’s grace and mercy upon you, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you. Yet they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you in the least. Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom, and He has taught you what you did not know. Allah’s grace upon you is truly immense.
interpretation: Allah protected the Prophet ﷺ from the schemes of those who sought to lead him into error, showing that false accusations and deceptive counsel cannot ultimately harm the one whom He guides and supports. The verse also emphasizes that divine revelation and wisdom are gifts through which Allah grants understanding beyond ordinary human knowledge; therefore, His immense favor calls for trust in His guidance, gratitude, and steadfast adherence to the truth rather than reliance on the claims of those who distort it.

translation: There is no good in much of their private conversation, except in the words of one who encourages charity, kindness, or reconciliation between people. Whoever does this, seeking the pleasure of Allah, We shall grant him a tremendous reward.
interpretation: Private speech is only truly virtuous when it leads to beneficial action—helping others, promoting righteousness, or restoring peace—and its value is completed by sincere intention for Allah’s sake, for such efforts merit an immense reward from Him.

translation: Whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows a path other than that of the believers, We will turn him toward what he has chosen and admit him into Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: This verse warns that knowingly resisting the Messenger after the truth has been made clear, and deliberately abandoning the faithful community’s way, leads a person to be left with the path he has chosen and to face its destructive consequence in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives anything lesser than that for whom He wills. Whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly strayed far away.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly dying while attributing partners to Allah is the gravest form of spiritual deviation and is not forgiven, whereas sins lesser than associating partners remain subject to Allah’s judgment and mercy. It also leaves the door of repentance open before death, while emphasizing that shirk leads a person far from the truth and from the path of guidance.

translation: They invoke besides Him none but female deities, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: The verse exposes the emptiness of associating partners with Allah: those who abandon His worship are in reality appealing to powerless idols—often given feminine names—and following the influence of Satan, who persistently rebels against Allah and leads people away from the truth.

translation: Allah has cursed him, and he said, “I will surely take an ordained share of Your servants.”
interpretation: This portrays Satan’s defiance after being rejected by Allah: he vows to mislead a determined portion of humanity and claim them for his path. His declaration expresses his intent and relentless temptation, not power to compel anyone to disobey Allah.

translation: “I will surely lead them astray, fill them with vain desires, command them to slit the ears of cattle, and command them to alter Allah’s creation.” Whoever takes Satan as a patron instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse portrays Satan’s method of deception: he leads people away from guidance through false hopes and persuades them to corrupt the natural order and sacred practices established by Allah. Whoever willingly accepts Satan’s authority over Allah’s guidance ultimately loses both moral direction and true success.

translation: He makes them promises and fills them with hopes, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.
interpretation: Satan entices people by offering attractive promises and unrealistic hopes, yet his promises are deceptive and lead them away from truth and lasting good.

translation: Those—Hell is their abode, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persist in rejecting God and following the path of falsehood will face Hell as a permanent consequence, with no refuge or way of escape from its punishment.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining there forever. This is Allah’s true promise—and who is more truthful in speech than Allah?
interpretation: The verse assures believers that genuine faith, expressed through righteous action, leads by Allah’s promise to everlasting blessedness. Since Allah’s word is perfectly true and trustworthy, this promised reward is certain and cannot be compared with any claim or assurance from others.

translation: It is not according to your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be requited for it, and he will find for himself, apart from Allah, neither a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: Salvation is not secured by claims, affiliation, or wishful thinking; rather, every person is accountable before Allah for what they do. No one can rely on any other power to shield them from the consequences of wrongdoing or provide the ultimate help that belongs to Allah alone.

translation: ومن يعمل من الأعمال الصالحة، ذكراً كان أو أنثى، وهو مؤمن، فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يُنقصون شيئاً يسيراً من أجورهم.
interpretation: يبين الله أن النجاة والفضل لا يرتبطان بكون الإنسان ذكراً أو أنثى، بل بالإيمان والعمل الصالح؛ فمن جمع بينهما استحق دخول الجنة، والله عادل لا يضيع من أجره شيئاً، مهما كان قليلاً.

translation: And who is better in faith than one who submits himself to Allah, does good, and follows the way of Abraham, inclining exclusively toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as a close friend.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the finest form of devotion is sincere submission to Allah expressed through righteous action and wholehearted adherence to the pure monotheism exemplified by Abraham. Such faith is not merely a claim, but a life of humility, goodness, and turning away from every form of idolatry; the special closeness granted to Abraham shows the honor Allah gives to those who combine sincere faith with obedient conduct.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Allah encompasses all things.
interpretation: Everything in existence belongs entirely to Allah and remains under His authority; nothing is hidden from His knowledge or outside His power and care.

translation: They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and also concerning what is recited to you in the Book about orphan girls to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, while you desire to marry them; and concerning the vulnerable children; and that you uphold justice for orphans. Whatever good you do, surely Allah is All-Knowing of it.”
interpretation: Allah commands that orphan girls and vulnerable children be protected from exploitation and treated with complete justice. Those who have authority over them must not withhold their rightful dowries or possessions, nor use marriage as a means of taking advantage of them; every act of fairness and goodness toward them is fully known and accounted for by Allah.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or rejection, there is no blame upon them if they reconcile between themselves through a settlement; and reconciliation is best. Yet selfishness is ever present in human souls. And if you act with excellence and remain mindful of God, surely God is ever fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: When a marriage is threatened by a husband’s neglect, hostility, or withdrawal, Islam permits the spouses to reach a mutually agreed arrangement that preserves the marriage and prevents injustice. Such reconciliation is preferable to needless conflict or separation, but it must not be driven by coercion or exploitation. Because each person may cling selfishly to their perceived rights, both spouses are urged to show generosity, act with kindness, and maintain reverence for God, knowing that their treatment of one another is fully known and accountable to Him.

translation: You will never be able to be fully equal between wives, even if you strive earnestly. So do not incline entirely toward one, leaving another suspended. If you reconcile matters and remain mindful of God, then surely God is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse acknowledges that complete equality in inward affection is beyond human control, but it forbids allowing personal preference to become injustice in outward treatment, rights, time, and care. A believer must therefore restrain partiality, avoid neglecting any wife, and seek fairness and God-consciousness in what can be controlled.

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Wise.
interpretation: If reconciliation between the spouses is no longer possible and they part, neither should fear that separation will leave them without provision or care; Allah can grant each a new sufficiency from His limitless bounty, while His wisdom governs what is best for them.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you, and you as well, to be mindful of Allah. But if you disbelieve, then surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse teaches that reverence and obedience to Allah are a universal obligation entrusted to every revealed community, not a demand made for Allah’s benefit. Since all creation belongs to Him and depends entirely upon Him, disbelief cannot diminish His dominion in the slightest; rather, it deprives the disbeliever of the guidance and honor that come from recognizing Allah, the One who is completely independent and inherently worthy of praise.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs wholly to Allah, so all created things remain under His authority and care. Since He alone possesses complete knowledge, power, and control, He is sufficient for anyone who entrusts their affairs to Him.

translation: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others in your place. Allah is ever fully capable of doing that.
interpretation: This verse warns humanity that existence and authority are entirely subject to God’s will: no people are indispensable, and if they persist in disobedience, He can replace them with others who are more obedient. It therefore calls people to humility, gratitude, and faithful obedience rather than presuming upon God’s patience.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world—then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: Do not restrict your hopes to worldly gain, for all good in this life and the everlasting reward of the Hereafter are under Allah’s control. Seek His favor through sincere faith and obedience, knowing that He hears every request and sees every intention and deed.

translation: O you who believe, stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah, even if it is against yourselves, or your parents and close relatives. Whether the person is rich or poor, Allah has greater claim over both. So do not follow personal desire, lest you deviate from justice. And if you distort your testimony or turn away, surely Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to make justice an unwavering duty rooted in devotion to Allah, not in self-interest, family loyalty, sympathy for the poor, or deference to the rich. A person must be truthful even when the truth harms their own position or that of those closest to them, because human judgments of status and hardship do not override Allah’s right. It also warns that injustice may arise not only through false testimony but through twisting the truth or refusing to testify; therefore integrity requires both honest speech and the courage to uphold what is right.

translation: O you who believe, believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Book He has sent down upon His Messenger, and the Book He sent down before. Whoever denies Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: يأمر الله المؤمنين أن يثبتوا على إيمانهم ويحققوه في جميع أصوله، فلا يكون الإيمان انتقائيًّا يؤمن ببعض ما جاء به الوحي ويرفض بعضه؛ فالإيمان الحق يجمع التصديق بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر، ومن جحد أصلًا من هذه الأصول فقد ابتعد عن طريق الهداية ابتعادًا شديدًا.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, then disbelieve, then believe, then disbelieve, and then increase in disbelief—Allah will never forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This warns against repeatedly treating faith as something to be entered and abandoned at will, until disbelief becomes firmly rooted. Such persistent rejection, especially without sincere repentance before death, closes the path to divine forgiveness and guidance because the person has deliberately turned away from the truth after recognizing it.

translation: Give the hypocrites the news that they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a stern, ironic warning to those who display faith outwardly while concealing disbelief or treachery: their hypocrisy will not remain hidden from God and will lead to a painful punishment.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honor through them? Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah alone.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against seeking strength, status, or protection by giving ultimate loyalty to those who reject faith while turning away from the believers. True dignity and lasting power cannot be secured through such dependence; they belong entirely to Allah, so honor is found through obedience to Him rather than through compromised allegiance.

translation: He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s verses being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in Hell.
interpretation: This verse teaches that remaining in a gathering where Allah’s revelation is deliberately mocked, without objecting or leaving, amounts to approving of that conduct; believers must distance themselves until the mockery ends, because persistent passive acceptance can make them share in the wrongdoing and its consequence.

translation: Those who wait and watch you: if victory comes to you from Allah, they say, “Were we not with you?” But if the disbelievers gain a share, they say, “Did we not prevail over you and protect you from the believers?” Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the opportunism of hypocrites who attach themselves to whichever side serves their interests, claiming loyalty to the believers when they prosper while boasting of aiding the disbelievers when they gain advantage. Their double-dealing will not escape divine judgment, and although believers may sometimes appear politically or militarily overpowered, Allah will not grant disbelief a legitimate, enduring authority over them.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He will requite them for their deception. When they rise for prayer, they rise reluctantly, showing themselves to people, and they remember Allah only a little.
interpretation: The verse portrays hypocrisy as performing acts of worship without sincere faith: prayer becomes a burdensome display intended to gain people’s approval rather than draw near to Allah. Their scarce remembrance reveals the weakness of their connection with Him, while Allah’s requital means that their attempt to conceal their inner reality cannot deceive Him and will ultimately return upon them.

translation: Wavering between these and those, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah lets stray, you will never find for him a way.
interpretation: This describes the hypocrites who remain suspended between faith and disbelief, seeking neither sincere commitment to believers nor honest allegiance to disbelievers; because they reject clear guidance and persist in this duplicity, Allah leaves them without a path to truth.

translation: O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear proof against you?
interpretation: Believers are warned against giving their ultimate loyalty, trust, and support to those who reject faith while neglecting the believing community. Such allegiance can compromise their faith and place them in a position for which they have no valid excuse before Allah; therefore, their relationships and cooperation should be guided by loyalty to truth and justice, without betraying the believers.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will never find for them any helper.
interpretation: This warns that deliberate hypocrisy—outwardly professing faith while inwardly concealing rejection and working against the believers—is an especially grave form of betrayal, deserving the severest punishment. Their complete lack of a helper signifies that no worldly ally or excuse can rescue them from God’s judgment.

translation: Except those who repent, reform themselves, hold fast to Allah, and devote their religion sincerely to Allah—for they will be with the believers. And Allah will grant the believers a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse shows that sincere repentance is not merely expressing regret; it requires correcting one’s conduct, firmly relying on Allah, and purifying worship from hypocrisy and worldly motives. Whoever does so is restored to the fellowship of the believers and receives Allah’s immense reward.

translation: What would Allah gain by punishing you if you are grateful and believe? Allah is Appreciative, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah does not seek to punish people for its own sake; rather, punishment is connected to ingratitude and disbelief. Whoever responds to His blessings with gratitude and sincere faith has no reason to fear His punishment, for Allah recognizes and rewards every act of faith and gratitude, and fully knows the sincerity behind it.

translation: Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: God disapproves of exposing people’s faults, insulting them, or spreading harmful speech, but permits the wronged person to speak openly about the injustice done to them in order to seek help or establish their rights. This permission is not a license for excess or falsehood, for God hears every word and knows the truth and the intention behind it.

translation: Whether you reveal a good deed or conceal it, or pardon an evil, surely Allah is ever Pardoning, All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that goodness is honored whether it is done openly or privately, and that forgiving wrongdoing is a noble act reflecting Allah’s forgiveness and power. It encourages believers to choose pardon when they are able, while entrusting ultimate judgment and justice to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, seeking to distinguish between Allah and His messengers, saying, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” and seeking to adopt a path between that,
interpretation: This verse condemns the attempt to divide faith according to personal preference: accepting some messengers while rejecting others. True faith recognizes that all of Allah’s messengers convey one divine truth, so rejecting any of them is not a legitimate middle position but a denial of the unity and authority of revelation.

translation: Those are truly the disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse firmly declares that rejecting Allah and His messengers is genuine disbelief, and warns that such deliberate rejection leads to a punishment marked by humiliation and disgrace.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—it is they whom He will soon grant their rewards. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: True faith requires affirming all of Allah’s messengers without accepting some and rejecting others. Whoever holds this sincere, unified belief is promised a complete reward from Allah, whose forgiveness and mercy encompass those who remain faithful to His guidance.

translation: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down for them a scripture from heaven. Indeed, they asked Moses for something even greater than that, saying, “Show us Allah openly,” so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf, even after clear proofs had come to them, yet We pardoned them for that and gave Moses clear authority.
interpretation: The verse exposes a pattern of demanding extraordinary signs while persisting in defiance: the demand for direct vision of Allah was not a sincere search for guidance but an arrogant test, and their worship of the calf showed that the real obstacle was not lack of evidence but disobedience. Nevertheless, Allah’s pardon and His granting Moses clear authority demonstrate that divine judgment is joined with mercy, while revelation and legitimate prophetic authority provide sufficient guidance without catering to demands rooted in stubbornness.

translation: And We raised the mountain above them because of their covenant, and We said to them, “Enter the gate in humility,” and We said to them, “Do not transgress regarding the Sabbath.” And We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse portrays the seriousness of the covenant Allah took from the Children of Israel: divine commands were reinforced by unmistakable signs, and they were required to respond with humility, obedience, and restraint. Their covenant was not a verbal formality, but a solemn responsibility to honor sacred limits and refrain from violating them.

translation: So, for their breaking of their covenant, their rejection of Allah’s signs, their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, “Our hearts are wrapped”—rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they believe only a little.
interpretation: The verse explains that persistent rebellion—breaking solemn commitments, rejecting divine evidence, committing grave injustice, and arrogantly refusing guidance—causes the heart to become spiritually sealed. This sealing is a consequence of their chosen disbelief, leaving them with little genuine faith or receptivity to the truth.

translation: And for their disbelief and their uttering against Mary a monstrous slander.
interpretation: They were condemned for denying the truth and for falsely accusing Mary of a grave immorality, making a shocking and baseless claim against her honor.

translation: And for their saying, “Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.” Yet they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him—but it was made to appear so to them. Indeed, those who differ concerning him are truly in doubt about him. They have no knowledge of it, except the following of conjecture. And certainly, they did not kill him with certainty.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that Jesus was killed or crucified, clarifying that the matter was confused and made to appear otherwise to those involved. Their conflicting claims rested not on certain knowledge but on conjecture; therefore, the killing of Jesus was never established as a fact, and Allah preserved His messenger from their intended outcome.

translation: Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah protected and exalted Jesus by raising him from the reach of those who sought to kill him, demonstrating His absolute power and wise decree.

translation: وما من أحدٍ من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمننَّ به قبل موته، ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدًا.
interpretation: المعنى أن أهل الكتاب سيؤمنون بعيسى عليه السلام إيمانًا صحيحًا قبل وفاته، حين يتبيّن لهم أنه عبدُ الله ورسولُه وليس إلهًا ولا ابنَ إله؛ ثم يكون يوم القيامة شاهدًا على ما اعتقدوه وما قالوه فيه.

translation: So, for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them certain good things that had previously been lawful for them, and because they repeatedly turned many away from the way of Allah.
interpretation: The verse explains that certain lawful blessings were withheld from the Children of Israel as a consequence of their persistent injustice and deliberate obstruction of divine guidance; the restriction was a punishment for their wrongdoing, not an indication that those things were inherently impure.

translation: And for their taking usury, though they had been forbidden from it, and for their consuming people’s wealth unlawfully. We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns knowingly persisting in prohibited financial exploitation—especially usury—and acquiring others’ wealth through injustice. It shows that violating divine commands while benefiting from people’s vulnerability is a serious moral offense, and that those who reject the truth after it has been made clear face painful accountability.

translation: But those among them who are firmly grounded in knowledge, and the believers, believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you; and those who establish prayer, give zakāh, and believe in Allah and the Last Day—we shall grant them a great reward.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that true knowledge is shown by sincere faith in the revelation given to Muhammad and in the preceding revelations, accompanied by steadfast worship, charitable responsibility, and belief in the Hereafter. Such integrated faith and righteous conduct are the qualities for which Allah promises an immense reward.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon; and We gave David the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Muhammad’s revelation is part of the same divine tradition granted to the earlier prophets. Though their communities and circumstances differed, the source of their guidance was one: God. By naming many prophets and mentioning the Psalms given to David, it rejects the idea that revelation belongs exclusively to one people and establishes continuity between the Qur’an and the genuine revelations that preceded it.

translation: And messengers We have already told you about, and messengers We have not told you about. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: This verse teaches that God’s messengers were more numerous than those mentioned in revelation, so believers affirm all of them without limiting divine guidance to the stories they know. Moses is singled out as having received direct speech from God, signifying a distinctive honor and confirming the reality of divine communication to His prophets.

translation: Messengers bearing glad tidings and warnings, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah sent His messengers to make the truth clear, offering hope to those who respond and warning those who reject, so that no one could claim ignorance or injustice when held accountable. His sending of messengers reflects both His power and His perfect wisdom.

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has revealed to you; He revealed it with His knowledge, and the angels also bear witness. And Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This affirms that the revelation given to the Prophet is unquestionably from Allah, grounded in His perfect knowledge and attested by the angels; therefore, divine testimony is enough to establish its truth, regardless of those who reject it.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and hindered others from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far astray.
interpretation: يجمع هؤلاء بين إنكار الحق ومحاولة منع الناس من اتباعه، ولذلك كان ضلالهم عميقًا وبعيدًا عن سبيل الهداية؛ إذ لم يكتفوا بإضلال أنفسهم، بل سعوا إلى إضلال غيرهم وصدّهم عن طريق الله.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and acted unjustly—Allah would never forgive them, nor guide them to any path.
interpretation: This warns that deliberate disbelief joined with wrongdoing places a person beyond forgiveness and divine guidance so long as they persist in that state; it also implies that repentance and abandoning injustice are the way back to God’s mercy.

translation: Except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This warns that those who knowingly persist in rejection and wrongdoing may be led to Hell, where their punishment is everlasting, and that bringing about this judgment is entirely within Allah’s power and is not difficult for Him.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; that is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse calls all people to recognize the Messenger’s message as truth from God and to embrace faith for their own benefit. Their disbelief does not diminish God’s authority or possession of creation; rather, God knows their realities and judges them with perfect wisdom.

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, and say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of Allah, His word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, “Three.” Desist—it is better for you. Allah is only One God. Glory be to Him that He should have a child. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as a guardian.
interpretation: The verse calls the People of the Scripture to abandon exaggeration in religious belief and to speak of God only with revealed truth. It affirms Jesus’ honored status as Allah’s messenger, created by His command and brought into being through His word, while rejecting the claim that divinity is divided into three. The proper response is to believe in Allah’s absolute oneness and in all His messengers, recognizing that everything belongs to Him and that He needs neither a partner nor a child.

translation: The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels brought near. And whoever disdains His worship and acts arrogantly, He will gather them all to Him.
interpretation: True honor does not lie in refusing servitude to Allah; even the Messiah and the honored angels accept it. Whoever rejects worship out of pride will ultimately be brought before Allah, where arrogance will offer no escape or defense.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdain and act arrogantly, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will find for themselves, besides Allah, neither a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: The verse establishes that true faith expressed through righteous action leads to complete divine recompense and further generosity from Allah, while refusing submission out of arrogance leads to painful punishment and total helplessness. It contrasts humble obedience—which receives more than it has earned—with prideful rejection—which leaves a person without any power or ally capable of defending them before Allah.

translation: O humanity, there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light.
interpretation: The verse calls all people to recognize that God has provided decisive evidence of the truth and revealed guidance that illuminates the way from doubt and error; therefore, true clarity and right direction are found by turning sincerely to His revelation.

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold firmly to Him, He will admit them into mercy and grace from Him, and He will guide them to Himself along a straight path.
interpretation: Those who place true faith in Allah and depend steadfastly upon Him are promised His special mercy and abundant favor. Their reliance on Him is not merely a source of comfort; it becomes the means by which He directs them toward the straight path leading to His nearness and approval.

translation: They seek your ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah: if a man dies leaving no child, but he has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves; and he shall inherit from her if she leaves no child. If there are two sisters, they shall have two-thirds of what he leaves. If there are brothers and sisters, the male shall receive the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray. Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes the inheritance ruling for a person who dies without leaving a child or a parent who would otherwise inherit under the relevant legal framework. It assigns the deceased’s sister half of the estate when she is the sole qualifying sister, two-thirds collectively when there are two or more sisters, and gives each brother a share equal to that of two sisters when brothers and sisters inherit together. The ruling demonstrates that inheritance is determined by divinely defined kinship rights rather than personal preference, and the closing reminder calls believers to follow Allah’s clarification carefully, knowing that His law encompasses every circumstance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who believe, fulfill your contracts. Permitted for you are grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, while not making hunting lawful when you are in a state of ihrām. Indeed, Allah decrees whatever He wills.
interpretation: Faith requires believers to honor every genuine covenant and obligation, while accepting that Allah alone determines what is lawful and unlawful. The permission to benefit from livestock is therefore qualified by revealed exceptions, and the prohibition of hunting during ihrām teaches reverence for sacred limits even when ordinary actions would otherwise be permissible.

translation: O you who believe, do not violate the sacred rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial animals, nor the garlands marking them, nor those heading toward the Sacred House seeking bounty and approval from their Lord. When you have completed pilgrimage restrictions, you may hunt. And do not let the hatred you bear toward a people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque lead you to transgress. Cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression. Be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to honor the sanctities established by Allah and to respect those journeying to the Sacred House, while permitting ordinary hunting once the pilgrimage restrictions have ended. It also teaches that even hostility toward people who have committed an injustice must not cause believers to act unjustly themselves. Righteousness and reverence for Allah are to be pursued collectively, whereas support for sin, oppression, or aggression is forbidden, for accountability before Allah is certain.

translation: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which any name other than God’s has been invoked; also animals strangled, killed by a blow, killed by a fall, gored to death, or partly eaten by a wild animal—unless you slaughter them properly before they die—and what is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decisions through divining arrows. All this is disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired of overcoming your religion, so do not fear them; fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My blessing upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion. But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, without inclining toward sin, then surely God is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that lawful food is governed by reverence for God, humane and proper slaughter, and freedom from pagan practices. The prohibited foods and forms of death are not merely dietary restrictions; they mark a believer’s separation from impurity, idolatry, and arbitrary superstition. The declaration that the religion has been perfected signifies that God’s guidance has reached its complete and sufficient form, and that believers need not fear the loss of their faith before hostile opposition. Yet the law is not intended to destroy life: genuine necessity, such as extreme hunger, permits consuming what is normally forbidden when one seeks only to survive and does not deliberately pursue wrongdoing. God’s forgiveness and mercy accompany this principled concession.

translation: They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say, “The good things have been made lawful for you, and [lawful are] the animals of prey you have trained as hunters, teaching them from what Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it. And be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is swift in reckoning.”
interpretation: The verse establishes that lawful food is characterized by purity and goodness, and permits game caught by properly trained hunting animals when the hunter invokes Allah’s name. This permission is not unrestricted: it calls for disciplined training, conscious observance of Allah’s name, and reverence for His limits, reminding believers that even ordinary acts such as obtaining food remain subject to divine accountability.

translation: Today all good things have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And lawful for you are chaste believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, provided that you give them their bridal gifts, seeking marriage, not committing fornication or taking secret lovers. Whoever rejects faith—his deeds have surely become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a framework of lawful social relations with the People of the Scripture: their permitted food may be shared, and marriage is allowed with their chaste women when it is a genuine, responsible union founded on the payment of the bridal gift and protected from fornication and secret affairs. These permissions do not lessen the centrality of faith; rejecting faith nullifies the spiritual value of one’s deeds and leads to loss in the Hereafter.

translation: O you who believe, when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles. If you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill, traveling, or one of you has come from relieving himself, or you have had intimate contact with women and cannot find water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to burden you, but He intends to purify you and complete His blessing upon you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse establishes that worship requires both outward cleanliness and inward readiness. It prescribes ablution for ordinary prayer, full purification after major impurity, and dry ablution when water is unavailable or harmful to use, showing that the law preserves the purpose of purity without imposing hardship. These acts are not empty rituals: they prepare the believer to stand before Allah with humility and awareness of His blessing, while the concessions reveal that divine guidance is founded on mercy rather than needless burden.

translation: And remember Allah’s blessing upon you and the covenant He made with you when you said, “We hear and obey.” And be mindful of Allah; surely Allah knows what is within the hearts.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to remain faithful to their commitment of hearing and obeying Allah, remembering that faith is not merely a spoken declaration but a covenant reflected in sincere conduct. Awareness that Allah knows the innermost intentions of the heart should cultivate genuine obedience, reverence, and integrity.

translation: O believers, stand firm for Allah, bearing witness with justice. Do not let hatred of a people cause you to swerve from justice. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: True devotion to Allah requires impartial justice, even toward those whom one dislikes or opposes. Hatred must not distort judgment or lead to wrongdoing, because justice is among the clearest signs of God-consciousness, and Allah fully knows the intentions and actions behind every judgment.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a عظیم reward.
interpretation: This is a divine assurance that sincere faith, when expressed through righteous action, is met with the covering of sins and a reward beyond measure.

translation: As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse warns that knowingly rejecting faith and treating God’s revealed signs as false leads to the ultimate consequence of separation from divine mercy in the Hellfire.

translation: O you who believe, remember Allah’s blessing upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He restrained their hands from you. And be mindful of Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: Believers are called to remember that Allah protects them from harm, including dangers planned by others, so gratitude should lead to obedience and God-consciousness rather than complacency. The verse teaches that reliance on Allah is not passive: believers should remain vigilant and act responsibly, while trusting that ultimate protection and success are in His hands.

translation: And indeed, Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We appointed twelve leaders from among them. Allah said, “I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in My messengers, honor and support them, and lend Allah a good loan, I will surely erase your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever among you disbelieves after that has surely strayed from the right path.”
interpretation: This covenant teaches that divine support and forgiveness are tied to faithful action: sincere worship, care for the needy, belief in and support of God’s messengers, and generous spending for His sake. Allah’s promise of forgiveness and Paradise is an immense mercy, but knowingly abandoning the covenant after accepting it is a grave deviation from the path of guidance.

translation: So, for their breaking of their covenant, We condemned them and hardened their hearts. They distort words from their proper meanings and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. You will continue to discover treachery from them, except for a few. Yet pardon them and overlook their faults; surely Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: Because they repeatedly violated their covenant, they became deprived of divine mercy and spiritually hardened, leading them to manipulate revelation, neglect its guidance, and act deceptively. Nevertheless, the verse directs the believers to respond with forgiveness and graciousness when wisdom permits, showing that moral excellence and restraint remain beloved to Allah even in the face of wrongdoing.

translation: And from those who said, “We are Christians,” We took their covenant, but they neglected a portion of what they had been reminded of. So We stirred up among them hostility and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that claiming faith does not fulfill the covenant with God when people abandon part of the guidance entrusted to them. Their neglect produced division, hostility, and lasting estrangement among them as a consequence of their own conduct. The warning is that God will ultimately expose and judge the realities behind their actions, not merely their religious claims.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, clarifying for you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture with the coming of Muhammad, whose message exposes truths that had been concealed or obscured while refraining from dwelling on matters whose disclosure serves no benefit. The “light” and the “clear Book” signify divine guidance that illuminates the truth and makes the path of faith and obedience evident.

translation: Through it Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the ways of peace, brings them out of darknesses into the light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah guides those who sincerely pursue His approval through the revelation toward every path that leads to peace, righteousness, and soundness. By His enabling grace, He delivers them from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and sin into the light of faith and guidance, then keeps directing them along the upright way that leads to Him.

translation: Those who say, “God is the Messiah, son of Mary,” have certainly disbelieved. Say, “Who could possess any power against God if He intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, his mother, and everyone on earth?” To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them. He creates whatever He wills, and God is capable of all things.
interpretation: This verse rejects attributing divinity to Jesus by reminding that he and his mother are created beings entirely subject to God’s will. Absolute sovereignty belongs only to God: no one can prevent what He decrees, while Jesus, Mary, and all creation depend upon Him. God’s power to create as He wills confirms His uniqueness and independence from any partner or offspring.

translation: The Jews and the Christians say, “We are the children of Allah and His beloved.” Say, “Then why does He punish you for your sins?” Rather, you are human beings among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse rejects the notion that belonging to a religious community or claiming a special relationship with God grants automatic immunity from judgment. Divine favor is not established by lineage, titles, or mere claims; human beings remain accountable for their deeds, while forgiveness and punishment rest solely with Allah’s wisdom and justice. Since all creation belongs to Him and all return to Him, no one possesses an inherent privilege before His judgment.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, clarifying matters for you after an interval without messengers, lest you say, “No bearer of good news or warner came to us.” So a bearer of good news and a warner has indeed come to you. And Allah is over all things capable.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Scripture by reminding them that the coming of the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ removes any excuse of claiming that divine guidance had not reached them. He came after a long period without messengers to clarify the truth, convey the promise of reward, and warn against disbelief and wrongdoing. Allah’s complete power encompasses sending messengers, establishing proof, and holding people accountable according to the guidance that has reached them.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “O my people, remember Allah’s blessing upon you: when He appointed among you prophets, made you sovereign, and granted you what He had not granted anyone among all peoples.”
interpretation: Moses reminds the Children of Israel that their honor and prosperity were gifts from Allah, shown through the prophets raised among them, the dignity and independence granted to them, and the distinctive blessings they received. This remembrance calls them to gratitude, obedience, and faithfulness to Allah’s guidance rather than pride in their favored status.

translation: “O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has ordained for you, and do not turn back, lest you become losers.”
interpretation: Moses urges his people to obey Allah’s command with courage and trust. The Holy Land is presented as a divinely granted responsibility and opportunity, but abandoning the commanded path out of fear or hesitation would turn that opportunity into loss. The verse therefore teaches that faith requires steadfastness: one must not retreat from a rightful duty merely because it appears difficult.

translation: They said, “O Moses, indeed there are people of great strength in it, and we will never enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, then we will enter.”
interpretation: They responded to Moses with fear and hesitation, allowing their perception of the inhabitants’ power to override their trust in God’s promise. Their conditional willingness to act shows that they were prepared to enter only after the danger had disappeared, rather than relying on faith and courage in confronting the trial before them.

translation: Two men among those who feared Allah, upon whom He had bestowed His favor, said, “Enter upon them through the gate; when you enter it, you will surely prevail. And place your trust in Allah, if you are believers.”
interpretation: These two men urged the believers to confront their fear with courageous obedience: taking the required means by entering the gate, while recognizing that victory comes from Allah. Their words show that true faith combines decisive action with complete reliance upon Him.

translation: They said, “O Moses, we will never enter it so long as they remain in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will remain sitting here.”
interpretation: This expresses the Israelites’ fear, disobedience, and lack of trust in God: instead of relying on His promised help and obeying Moses, they refused to confront the people in the land and spoke to Moses with insolent defiance.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I have authority over none but myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: Moses acknowledges that he can govern only himself and Aaron, not a people who have chosen rebellion; therefore he asks God to distinguish the faithful from the disobedient and to judge between them with justice.

translation: He said, “Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered through the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: Because they refused to enter the Holy Land despite God’s command, they were deprived of it for forty years and left to wander as a consequence of their disobedience. The verse teaches that persistent defiance can forfeit divine blessings, while the faithful should not be consumed by grief over those who knowingly reject the truth.

translation: And recount to them, in truth, the account of the two sons of Adam: when they each offered a sacrifice, it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said, “I will surely kill you.” The other replied, “Allah accepts only from those who are mindful of Him.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that Allah’s acceptance depends not on the outward act alone, but on sincere devotion and mindful obedience. When rejection provokes envy and aggression, the truly God-conscious person responds with certainty that divine acceptance is governed by righteousness, not rivalry or worldly status.

translation: If you stretch out your hand to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The speaker refuses to answer aggression with aggression, not from weakness but from reverence for Allah and fear of committing injustice. His restraint reflects moral integrity: he will not become an aggressor even when threatened, entrusting judgment to the Lord of all creation.

translation: إني أريد أن تتحمل إثم قتلي وإثمك، فتكون من أهل النار؛ وذلك جزاء الظالمين.
interpretation: يقول المظلوم لأخيه إنه لن يقابله بالقتل، بل سيتركه يتحمل عاقبة عدوانه؛ فإن أقدم على قتله حمل وزر قتل النفس، إلى جانب آثامه، واستحق بذلك عذاب النار، لأن هذا هو جزاء من يعتدي ويظلم.

translation: Then his soul made the killing of his brother seem easy to him, so he killed him and became one of the losers.
interpretation: The verse portrays how envy and unchecked inner impulses can overcome a person’s conscience, leading to a grave sin whose consequences leave him spiritually and ultimately ruined.

translation: فأرسل الله غرابًا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري جسد أخيه، فقال: يا حسرتي، أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري جسد أخي؟ فأصبح من النادمين.
interpretation: يُظهر هذا أن الإنسان قد يتعلم أبسط صور الرحمة والمسؤولية من مشهد في الخلق، وأن الندم بعد ارتكاب الظلم لا يمحو الجريمة ولا يعيد ما فُقد؛ فالعبرة أن يُبادر المرء إلى تقوى الله وضبط غضبه قبل أن يقوده إلى فعل لا يستطيع إصلاح آثاره.

translation: For that reason We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a person—without that person having killed anyone or committed corruption in the land—it is as though he has killed all humanity; and whoever saves a life, it is as though he has saved all humanity. Our messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs, yet many of them thereafter continued to commit excesses in the land.
interpretation: The verse establishes the profound sanctity of human life: unjustly taking one life is morally equivalent to attacking humanity as a whole, while preserving or rescuing a life expresses a commitment to the value of all people. The allowance concerning just retribution and those who cause grave corruption affirms lawful justice, not personal vengeance. Despite receiving clear guidance, many still transgressed, showing that knowledge of truth does not by itself prevent wrongdoing without reverence for God and obedience to His limits.

translation: Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive throughout the land to spread corruption is that they be killed, crucified, have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be expelled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who, through organized violent aggression—such as armed banditry, murder, and terrorizing the public—create grave disorder and insecurity in society. The listed penalties are matters for legitimate judicial authority, applied according to the severity of the crime and with due process; they are not a license for individuals to punish others or for ordinary disagreement and sin to be treated as “waging war” against God and His Messenger.

translation: Except for those who repent before you gain power over them; then know that Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This establishes that sincere repentance made before a person is captured or brought under authority can remove the worldly punishment prescribed for the offense, while affirming Allah’s readiness to forgive those who genuinely turn back to Him.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah, seek the means of drawing near to Him, and strive in His cause so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to attain true success through reverent awareness of Allah, by pursuing every lawful act that brings them closer to Him—such as sincere worship, repentance, obedience, and good deeds—and by exerting themselves to uphold truth and goodness in His path. Prosperity is presented as the result of this wholehearted devotion and purposeful striving.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve—if they possessed everything on earth and the like of it besides, and offered it to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the absolute helplessness of disbelief before divine judgment: wealth, even if multiplied beyond all measure, cannot purchase escape once the Hereafter has begun. The refusal of the ransom reflects that salvation is not obtained through material possession, but through faith and righteous obedience before the opportunity for repentance ends.

translation: They will wish to escape from the Fire, but they will not be able to escape from it; and theirs will be a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This portrays the despair of those condemned to the Fire: although they long for release, their punishment will not end, because there is no escape or respite from the consequence of their rejection of the truth.

translation: As for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, as a deterrent ordained by Allah. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a serious legal penalty for theft, intended to protect people’s property and deter crime, while emphasizing that the ruling must be understood and applied within Allah’s justice and wisdom: it concerns legally proven theft meeting the required conditions, not every act of taking property, and its implementation belongs to legitimate judicial authority rather than individuals. The verse’s closing names—Almighty and All-Wise—indicate that justice, due process, proportionality, and the possibility of repentance and reform are integral to applying the ruling.

translation: So whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, Allah will accept his repentance. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: True repentance requires turning away from the wrongdoing and correcting its effects as far as possible. When a person sincerely does so, Allah erases the sin and restores him to His mercy, for His forgiveness is not limited by the gravity of the past when repentance is genuine.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. And Allah is over all things capable.
interpretation: This verse directs the heart to recognize Allah’s absolute sovereignty and power: judgment, punishment, and forgiveness belong solely to Him, governed by His perfect wisdom and justice. Therefore, no one may presume upon His mercy or despair of it; a person should remain humble, repent sincerely, and live with both reverent fear and hopeful trust in Allah.

translation: O Messenger, let not those who hasten toward disbelief grieve you—those who say with their mouths, “We believe,” while their hearts do not believe, and those who are Jewish. They eagerly listen to falsehood and listen for others who have not come to you. They distort words from their proper contexts, saying, “If you are given this judgment, accept it; but if you are not given it, then beware.” Whoever Allah wills to test through misguidance, you can do nothing for them against Allah. These are those whose hearts Allah has not willed to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Messenger that the hypocrisy and obstinate rejection of certain people cannot diminish the truth of his mission. It portrays people who outwardly claim faith while concealing denial, and others who seek rulings only when they serve their desires, manipulating revelation and concealing its intended meaning when it does not. Their corruption is not merely intellectual but rooted in hearts that refuse sincere submission; therefore, the Messenger is not responsible for forcing their purification or guidance. Their conduct brings humiliation in this life and grave punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: They are avid listeners to falsehood and devourers of unlawful gain. So if they come to you, judge between them or turn them away. If you turn them away, they cannot harm you in the least. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
