interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet ﷺ that people who willingly embrace lies and consume illicit wealth do not compel him to judge their disputes; he may either adjudicate or decline. Yet whenever he chooses to judge, he must do so with complete fairness, unaffected by their corruption or by any personal considerations. Their rejection or hostility cannot harm him, while justice is beloved to Allah.

translation: How is it that they ask you to judge when they have the Torah, in which is Allah’s judgment? Then they turn away after that; such people are not believers.
interpretation: The verse censures those who seek judgment only when they expect it to serve their interests, despite possessing revealed guidance that clearly establishes God’s ruling. Their refusal to accept the truth once it becomes evident exposes that their claim to faith is undermined by insincerity and selective obedience.

translation: Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which were guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted themselves to God judged for those who were Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars, because they were entrusted with the preservation of God’s Scripture and were witnesses to it. So do not fear people; fear Me. And do not exchange My revelations for a small price. Those who do not judge by what God has revealed—it is they who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Torah was a genuine divine revelation containing guidance and illumination, and that those entrusted with it were obligated to uphold its judgments faithfully. It warns religious authorities not to alter, conceal, or compromise God’s commands out of fear of people or desire for worldly benefit. The closing warning concerns those who reject or knowingly set aside God’s revealed authority, thereby placing themselves outside true submission to Him.

translation: And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds, equal retribution. But whoever relinquishes it as an act of charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes justice through proportionate accountability for bodily harm, preventing both vengeance and impunity, while elevating forgiveness as a charitable act that brings expiation to the one who waives retribution. It also warns that abandoning God’s revealed standard of justice and replacing it with oppression or favoritism is wrongdoing.

translation: And We sent Jesus, son of Mary, following in their footsteps, confirming the Torah that came before him. And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, confirming the Torah that came before it, and as guidance and an admonition for the mindful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Jesus’ mission was a continuation of the same divine guidance given to the earlier prophets: the Gospel affirmed the authentic truth of the Torah while providing guidance, spiritual illumination, and moral instruction for those who are conscious of God.

translation: Let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse commands the followers of the Gospel to uphold and judge according to the divine guidance Allah revealed in it, rather than abandoning or altering it for personal interests. It warns that knowingly refusing Allah’s revealed judgment is a form of grave disobedience and departure from obedience to Him.

translation: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming the Scriptures that came before it and standing as their guardian. So judge between them by what Allah has sent down, and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you. For each of you We have appointed a law and a way. Had Allah willed, He could have made you one community, but He tests you through what He has given you. So compete with one another in good deeds. To Allah you will all return, and He will then inform you about that over which you differed.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Qur’an is the truthful, final criterion entrusted to the Prophet, affirming the original revelation while serving as its authoritative guardian. Judgment must therefore be governed by Allah’s revealed guidance rather than by the desires or pressures of people. The differing laws and paths given to communities are part of a divine test, not a license for arrogance or neglect; believers are called to respond by striving to excel in righteousness. Since all people will return to Allah, He alone will ultimately settle the truth of their disagreements and judge how each community used the guidance it received.

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires. Beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. If they turn away, then know that Allah intends to afflict them for some of their sins. Indeed, many people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet—and, by extension, those entrusted with judgment—to uphold divine guidance impartially and without yielding to pressure, personal interests, or the preferences of those being judged. It warns that compromising even part of revealed guidance can become a means of abandoning it, while people’s rejection of truth exposes them to the consequences of their own wrongdoing; their disobedience does not diminish the authority or justice of Allah’s revelation.

translation: أفَيَبغونَ حكمَ الجاهليةِ؟ ومَن أحسنُ من اللهِ حكمًا لقومٍ يوقنونَ؟
interpretation: توبّخ الآية من يتركون حكم الله العادل إلى أهواء الجاهلية وأعرافها الباطلة، وتقرر أن من أيقن بحكمة الله وعدله لا يرى حكمًا أهدى ولا أحسن من حكمه.

translation: O you who believe, do not take the Jews and Christians as protectors or allies; they are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is truly one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against entrusting their loyalty and communal security to hostile groups in a way that compromises the faith and interests of the Muslim community. Its concern is disloyal alignment and political dependence, not a prohibition of fairness, kindness, or peaceful relations with Jews and Christians as individuals.

translation: You will see those whose hearts are afflicted with disease hastening toward them, saying, “We fear that a turn of fortune may befall us.” Yet perhaps Allah will bring victory or a command from Him, and then they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves.
interpretation: The verse exposes the fear-driven opportunism of hypocrites: instead of trusting Allah and remaining principled, they seek closeness to the opposing side in anticipation of changing circumstances. It warns that Allah may grant the believers victory or decisive judgment, leaving those who concealed their disloyal intentions to regret their calculated choice.

translation: And those who believe will say, “Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were surely with you?” Their deeds have come to nothing, and they have become losers.
interpretation: The believers will expose the contradiction of those who made solemn claims of loyalty while secretly aligning themselves against the truth. Their oaths and outward professions cannot benefit them, because deeds built upon hypocrisy and betrayal are rendered worthless, leaving them deprived of the reward they expected.

translation: O believers, whoever among you turns back from his faith—Allah will bring forth people whom He loves and who love Him: humble toward the believers, firm and dignified before the disbelievers, striving in Allah’s cause, and fearing no blame from anyone. That is Allah’s favor; He grants it to whom He wills. Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse warns that abandoning faith does not harm Allah’s religion, for He can replace those who turn away with sincere believers whose devotion is shown through love of Allah, humility and compassion toward fellow believers, strength and principled dignity before opposition, and readiness to strive for what is right without being deterred by people’s criticism. These qualities are a divine gift, granted according to Allah’s wisdom and encompassing knowledge.

translation: Your only guardian is Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe—those who establish prayer, give the zakat, and bow humbly.
interpretation: The verse directs believers to place their ultimate loyalty and reliance in Allah, His Messenger, and the faithful community, recognizing true faith through steadfast prayer, generosity toward those in need, and humble submission to Allah.

translation: Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies—indeed, the party of Allah are the victorious.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true allegiance belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers by supporting their truth, values, and righteous cause. Those who remain faithfully aligned with divine guidance will ultimately attain victory, even if they face hardship or opposition in this world.

translation: O you who believe, do not take as close allies those who have made your religion an object of ridicule and play—among those who were given the Scripture before you—and the disbelievers. And be mindful of Allah, if you are truly believers.
interpretation: Believers are instructed not to grant intimate loyalty, support, or authority to people who deliberately mock or trivialize their faith, whether from earlier scriptural communities or from those who reject faith. This is a call to preserve the dignity and commitments of Islam while maintaining justice and good conduct toward others; true faith is shown by reverence for Allah and by refusing to align oneself with contempt for what is sacred.

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it as a subject of mockery and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who respond to the call to worship with ridicule rather than reverence, identifying such contempt as a consequence of spiritual and intellectual blindness to the purpose and sanctity of prayer.

translation: Say, “O People of the Book, do you resent us for any reason other than that we believe in Allah, in what has been revealed to us, and in what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?”
interpretation: This is a reproach to those among the People of the Book who opposed the believers: the faith they condemned was belief in Allah and in all His revelations, both earlier and later. The verse exposes the real cause of their hostility—not any wrongdoing by the believers, but their own persistent disobedience and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Say, “Shall I inform you of those whose recompense with Allah is worse than that? They are those whom Allah has cursed, upon whom He has brought His wrath, and of whom He made apes and swine, and those who worshipped the false deity. They are worse in rank and farther astray from the right path.”
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberate rebellion against God’s guidance leads to divine curse, wrath, and degradation. It portrays those who abandon worship of Allah for false powers as having fallen into a state of spiritual corruption and profound misguidance, making their standing worse and their path farther from truth.

translation: When they come to you, they say, “We believe,” yet they entered with disbelief and departed with it. And Allah knows best what they used to conceal.
interpretation: This exposes the hypocrisy of those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly remaining committed to disbelief; their meeting with the believers does not transform their hearts, and Allah fully knows the hidden motives and rejection they conceal.

translation: You will see many of them hastening toward sin, aggression, and consuming what is unlawful. How evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who eagerly persist in wrongdoing, harming others, and benefiting from forbidden wealth, showing that repeated and deliberate pursuit of such acts is a grave moral failure.

translation: Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them from speaking sinful words and consuming unlawful gain? How evil is what they have been doing!
interpretation: The verse condemns religious leaders who remain silent before falsehood and illicit wealth, indicating that their failure to restrain wrongdoing makes them complicit in its spread and brings severe blame upon them.

translation: The Jews said, “God’s hand is tied up.” Their hands are tied, and they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills. What has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. We have cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it. They strive throughout the land to spread corruption, and Allah does not love those who spread corruption.
interpretation: This verse condemns attributing miserliness and limitation to Allah: His giving is unrestricted, abundant, and governed by His wisdom, while the phrase “His two hands are outstretched” affirms His generosity without likening Him to creation. It also reveals that revelation benefits those who respond sincerely but can intensify the arrogance and rejection of those who obstinately oppose it. Their recurring attempts to ignite conflict are ultimately frustrated by Allah, while their pursuit of corruption brings lasting hostility and divine displeasure.

translation: Had the People of the Book believed and been mindful of God, We would have erased their misdeeds and admitted them into gardens of bliss.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere faith and reverent obedience to God open the way to divine forgiveness and eternal reward. It also shows that belonging to a religious community alone does not suffice; salvation is connected to genuine belief, ethical responsibility, and turning away from wrongdoing.

translation: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أُنزِل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ۚ منهم أمة مقتصدة ۖ وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون
interpretation: المعنى أن أهل الكتاب لو التزموا حقًّا بما أنزله الله، فأقاموا أحكام التوراة والإنجيل وما جاءهم من ربهم، لفتح الله عليهم أبواب الرزق والبركة من كل جهة، كما يُفهم من قوله: «من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم». ومع ذلك فليسوا جميعًا على حال واحدة؛ فمنهم جماعة مستقيمة معتدلة، لكن كثيرًا منهم أصرّوا على الانحراف، فقبحت أعمالهم.

translation: O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. If you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: Allah commands the Messenger to deliver the revelation completely and without concealment, making clear that withholding any part of it would amount to failing in his entrusted mission. He assures him that protection from those who oppose the truth rests with Allah, while those who reject faith and resist divine guidance deprive themselves of its direction.

translation: Say, “O People of the Book, you have no firm ground until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.” Yet what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that religious affiliation or claims of faith have no value unless God’s revealed guidance is sincerely upheld and obeyed. It calls the People of the Book to honor the truth contained in their scriptures and to accept the further revelation sent by God. However, revelation benefits those who seek truth while causing others to become more obstinate when they reject it; therefore, the Prophet is told not to be consumed by sorrow over those who knowingly persist in disbelief.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians and the Christians—whoever truly believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds—no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse establishes that salvation is not granted by affiliation or mere claim, but by sincere faith in Allah and the Last Day expressed through righteous action. It assures such people that Allah’s justice and mercy remove the fear of what lies ahead and the grief over what has passed.

translation: Indeed, We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent messengers to them. Whenever a messenger brought them what their desires did not approve of, some they denied and some they killed.
interpretation: The verse condemns the rejection of divine guidance when it conflicts with personal desires, and shows that persistent resistance can lead people from denying God’s messengers to committing the grave injustice of killing them.

translation: They thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in mercy, but many of them again became blind and deaf. And Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: The verse warns that assuming one is beyond accountability can lead to spiritual blindness and deafness—an unwillingness to recognize truth or heed guidance. Even after Allah grants mercy and accepts repentance, returning to disobedience renews that blindness; yet no action escapes His knowledge.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, “Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.” Yet the Messiah said, “O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode will be the Fire. The wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing divinity to Jesus, affirming that he himself called people to worship the one God who is both his Lord and theirs. It teaches that associating any partner with Allah is a grave injustice that excludes a person from Paradise unless they turn back in repentance, and that no created power can rescue those who persist in such wrongdoing.

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, “Allah is the third of three,” while there is no god except One God. If they do not desist from what they say, those among them who disbelieve will surely be touched by a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse rejects the belief that God is one member of a plurality, affirming that divine reality is absolute and indivisible: God is uniquely One, without equals or partners. It warns that knowingly persisting in attributing partners to Him, rather than abandoning that claim, incurs severe consequences.

translation: أفلا يرجعون إلى الله بالتوبة ويطلبون مغفرته؟ والله كثير المغفرة، واسع الرحمة.
interpretation: في الآية دعوة إلى المبادرة بالتوبة والاستغفار، وبيان أن باب الرجوع إلى الله مفتوح؛ فمن أخلص في توبته وندم على ذنبه ورجع عنه وجد الله غفورًا لذنبه رحيمًا به.

translation: The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of God; messengers had indeed passed away before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both ate food. See how We make the signs clear to them, then see how they are turned away.
interpretation: تقرر الآية أن عيسى عليه السلام رسول مكرّم، وليس إلهاً ولا ابن إله؛ فقد سبقه رسل مضوا، وكانت أمه مريم عليها السلام صِدّيقة. وأكلهما الطعام يدل على حاجتهما البشرية وافتقارهما، كما أن وضوح هذه البراهين لا يمنع بعض الناس من الانحراف عن الحق ورفض دلالاته.

translation: Say, “Do you worship besides Allah that which has no power to harm or benefit you? And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the worship of anything incapable of controlling either harm or benefit, directing devotion instead to Allah alone, whose complete hearing and knowledge affirm His unique right to be worshipped.

translation: Say: O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who went astray before, led many others astray, and themselves deviated from the straight path.
interpretation: ينهى الله أهل الكتاب عن الغلو في الدين، أي تجاوز ما أنزله الله من الحق بإضافة ما ليس منه أو رفع الأشخاص والآراء فوق منزلتهم، كما ينهاهم عن اتباع أهواء من سبقهم ممن بنوا معتقداتهم على الانحراف والتقليد الأعمى؛ لأن ذلك يقود إلى إضلال الناس والابتعاد عن الطريق المستقيم.

translation: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed through the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and used to transgress.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent rebellion against God’s commands and continual violation of moral boundaries can bring about divine condemnation. The mention of David and Jesus indicates that righteous prophets openly denounced such wrongdoing, while the shared warning is that faith cannot be separated from obedience, justice, and restraint from transgression.

translation: They did not forbid one another from the wrongdoing they committed. How wretched was what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse condemns a community that becomes accustomed to evil and fails to restrain it, making each person morally responsible not only for committing wrongdoing but also for silently accepting it among others.

translation: You see many of them taking as allies those who disbelieve. Evil indeed is what they have sent ahead for themselves: that Allah is displeased with them, and in the punishment they will abide forever.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who, despite knowing the truth, give their loyalty and support to those who reject it, because such deliberate allegiance earns Allah’s displeasure and leads to enduring punishment.

translation: Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: True faith in Allah and His revelation should lead a person to loyalty toward the truth and distance from those who oppose it. Their choosing such allies reveals that many of them have abandoned obedience and persist in wrongdoing.

translation: You will surely find that the fiercest of people in hostility toward those who believe are the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe are those who say, “We are Christians.” That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse describes tendencies among religious communities in the context of the Prophet’s time, not an absolute judgment on every individual. It identifies hostility toward believers where religious or social opposition hardens into enmity, while praising those Christians whose learned and devoted servants cultivate humility, recognize truth, and do not reject it arrogantly. The measure of nearness is therefore moral and spiritual openness—not merely a community label—so individuals are judged by their response to faith, justice, and truth.

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because they recognize the truth. They say, “Our Lord, we believe, so record us among the witnesses.”
interpretation: This verse portrays sincere hearts that recognize divine truth when they encounter it and are moved to humble submission rather than resistance. Their tears arise from the harmony between revelation and the truth they inwardly perceive, and their prayer shows that genuine faith is expressed by openly affirming belief and seeking to stand among those who testify to and remain faithful to God’s truth.

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, while we hope that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people?
interpretation: This expresses a sincere response of faith: recognizing that belief in Allah and acceptance of the revealed truth are the natural consequence of understanding them, while humbly hoping for Allah’s mercy and inclusion among the righteous.

translation: So Allah rewarded them, for what they said, with gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: Allah honors sincere believers whose humble acknowledgment of the truth is demonstrated through righteous conduct, granting them lasting nearness, security, and bliss in Paradise as the fitting reward for their excellence.

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—they are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This warns that persistent disbelief and deliberate rejection of God’s revelations lead to the Hellfire, where such people will remain as its inhabitants.

translation: O you who believe, do not forbid yourselves the good things Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love those who transgress.
interpretation: Believers should not impose religious restrictions upon themselves by renouncing lawful blessings, nor should they exceed the limits set by Allah in pursuing or abstaining from them. The verse calls for a balanced obedience that respects what Allah has permitted and avoids both self-imposed prohibition and all forms of excess.

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you—lawful and wholesome—and be mindful of Allah, in whom you believe.
interpretation: Belief in Allah should be reflected in one’s choices: partake of the lawful and wholesome provisions He grants, while maintaining reverence for Him and avoiding what He has forbidden.

translation: Allah does not hold you accountable for unintentional expressions in your oaths, but He holds you accountable for the oaths you deliberately bind yourselves to. Their expiation is to feed ten needy people with the average of what you feed your own families, or to clothe them, or to free a slave. But whoever cannot afford this must fast for three days. This is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn them. Guard your oaths. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse establishes that accountability rests on deliberate commitments, not careless or habitual words, and that a broken intentional oath is repaired through a graduated act of expiation: feeding or clothing ten needy people, or freeing a slave; if none of these is possible, fasting three days. It also teaches believers to treat promises before Allah with restraint and seriousness, avoiding frequent or reckless swearing and honoring their commitments whenever they can.

translation: O believers, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so keep away from them that you may prosper.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to abandon intoxicants, gambling, idol-worship, and practices of seeking decisions through chance, because these corrupting influences belong to Satan’s work and undermine spiritual purity, sound judgment, and faithful obedience; true success lies in completely distancing oneself from them.

translation: Satan only seeks to stir up hostility and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling, and to hinder you from remembering Allah and from prayer. Will you then desist?
interpretation: This verse exposes the destructive aims behind intoxicants and gambling: they corrupt relationships, generate resentment, and distract the heart from the remembrance of Allah and the discipline of prayer. It is a decisive call to abandon them completely, leaving no room for treating their harm as insignificant or allowing them to weaken one’s faith and obligations.

translation: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger’s duty is only to deliver the clear message.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger, while warning that rejecting or neglecting this guidance carries responsibility upon the individual; the Messenger’s role is to convey the truth plainly, not to compel people to accept it.

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they consumed, provided that they remain mindful of God, believe, and do righteous deeds; then remain mindful and believe; then remain mindful and excel in goodness. And God loves those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that believers are not held accountable for what they consumed before a prohibition or obligation became applicable to them, so long as their lives thereafter are grounded in faith, reverent awareness of God, righteous action, and continual moral excellence. Repeated mention of mindfulness and faith emphasizes that true innocence is not a license for heedlessness, but a commitment to ongoing obedience and good conduct; God’s love belongs to those who embody this excellence.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، ليختبرنَّكم الله بشيء من الصيد تصل إليه أيديكم ورماحكم، ليُظهر من يخافه بالغيب؛ فمن تجاوز الحدَّ بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن التقوى تظهر حين يكون المحظور قريبًا وميسورًا، لا حين يتعذّر فعله؛ فإتاحة الصيد للمحرِمين كانت اختبارًا لصدق امتثالهم وخوفهم من الله في السر، ومن تعمّد تجاوز حكمه بعد بيانه فقد استحق الوعيد.

translation: O believers, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Whoever among you kills it deliberately must offer an equivalent sacrifice from livestock, as determined by two just men among you, to be brought as an offering to the Kaʿbah; or make atonement by feeding the needy; or observe fasting equivalent to that. This is so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what happened in the past, but whoever repeats it, Allah will punish him. Allah is Mighty, capable of retribution.
interpretation: The verse teaches that entering ihram places a person under a sacred restriction that protects wildlife and disciplines desire. Deliberately violating this prohibition requires a measured expiation determined fairly by trustworthy people: an equivalent livestock offering brought to the Kaʿbah, feeding those in need, or fasting corresponding to it. The purpose is not merely compensation, but to make the violator confront the seriousness and consequences of disobedience. Past violations are covered by Allah’s pardon, while knowingly returning to the offense exposes one to divine judgment.

translation: Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for travelers; but forbidden to you is the game of the land while you are in a state of ihram. And be mindful of Allah, to whom you will all be gathered.
interpretation: Allah grants pilgrims permission to benefit from what the sea provides, while forbidding them from hunting land animals during ihram. This distinction teaches that devotion requires respecting Allah’s limits even when ordinary lawful actions are temporarily restricted, with awareness that everyone will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: Allah has made the Kaʿbah—the Sacred House—a means of stability and welfare for humanity, and likewise the sacred month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands. This is so that you may know that Allah knows all that is in the heavens and the earth, and that Allah has knowledge of everything.
interpretation: By declaring these places, times, and offerings sacred, Allah establishes a divinely ordered framework that protects worship, restrains conflict, and secures people’s communal well-being. Their precise regulation reflects His complete knowledge of human needs and circumstances, teaching that true social and spiritual order rests upon His wisdom.

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse calls people to approach Allah with both awe and hope: His justice makes wrongdoing serious and deserving of accountability, while His forgiveness and mercy remain open to those who turn to Him sincerely and reform their ways.

translation: The Messenger’s duty is only to convey the message. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Messenger is responsible for delivering God’s revelation faithfully, not for compelling people to accept it or controlling their response. Every outward statement and hidden intention remains fully known to God, before whom each person is accountable.

translation: Say, “The impure and the pure are not equal, even if the abundance of the impure impresses you. So be mindful of Allah, O people of understanding, so that you may prosper.”
interpretation: Allah teaches that worth is determined by purity and righteousness, not by quantity, popularity, or outward appeal. Therefore, people of sound judgment must resist being impressed by the prevalence of wrongdoing and choose what pleases Allah, for true success lies in that choice.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، لا تسألوا عن أمورٍ إن تُكشف لكم تُحزنكم وتشقّ عليكم، وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تُبيَّن لكم؛ وقد عفا الله عنها، والله غفور حليم.
interpretation: ينهى الله المؤمنين عن التكلّف في السؤال عن أمورٍ لم يكلّفهم بها ولم يُظهر حكمها، ولا سيما ما قد يؤدي كشفه إلى زيادة المشقة أو الحرج عليهم. أما السؤال بقصد الفهم ومعرفة ما يحتاجون إليه فليس داخلًا في هذا النهي؛ وإنما المذموم هو السؤال المتعنت أو الذي يفتّش عن تفاصيل لو كُشفت لصارت قيدًا وتكليفًا. وما سكت الله عنه رحمةً وعفوًا، فعلى المؤمن أن يقبل هذا العفو ولا يتجاوز حدود الأدب مع الوحي، والله يغفر التقصير ويمهل عباده بحلمه.

translation: People before you asked about such matters, then became disbelievers because of them.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against pursuing needless or burdensome questions about religious matters in a way that leads to objection, rejection, or refusal to submit to God’s guidance, as happened to earlier peoples.

translation: Allah has not instituted any bahīrah, sā’ibah, wasīlah, or hām; rather, those who disbelieve fabricate lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason.
interpretation: The verse rejects the pre-Islamic custom of declaring certain livestock sacred or forbidden through invented labels and rituals, then falsely attributing those rules to God. It teaches that religious rulings must come from divine guidance, not from superstition, inherited custom, or unsupported claims made in God’s name.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,” they say, “Sufficient for us is what we found our forefathers following.” Even if their forefathers knew nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: The verse condemns treating inherited customs as sufficient proof when they conflict with divine guidance. Ancestral practice has no authority merely because it is old; truth must be accepted according to revelation and sound understanding, even when that requires abandoning the ways of those who came before.

translation: O you who believe, take responsibility for your own souls. Those who go astray cannot harm you when you are rightly guided. To Allah is the return of you all, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: الآية توجّه المؤمن إلى إصلاح نفسه والثبات على الهدى، فلا يضره ضلال الآخرين إذا أدّى ما عليه من الإيمان والطاعة والنصح بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر بالحكمة. فالمسؤولية الفردية لا تُسقط واجب الإصلاح، لكنها تعني أن الإنسان لا يحمل ذنب من اختار الضلال بعد قيام الحجة والنصيحة، وسيحاسب الجميع أمام الله على أعمالهم.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين يوصي، فليشهد على وصيته اثنان من ذوي العدالة منكم، أو شاهدان آخران من غيركم إن كنتم مسافرين فأدرك أحدكم الموت. احبسوا الشاهدين بعد الصلاة، فيقسمان بالله إن شككتم في صدقهما: لا نستبدل بيميننا أو شهادتنا عوضًا من مال، ولو كان المشهود له قريبًا، ولا نكتم شهادة الله؛ إن فعلنا ذلك لكنا من الآثمين.
interpretation: تقرر الآية إجراءً يحفظ حقوق المحتضر وورثته عند الوصية، ولا سيما في السفر حيث قد يتعذر وجود الشهود من المسلمين: فيُختار الشهود المعروفون بالعدل، ويُستوثق من صدقهم بالقَسَم، ويُحذَّرون من كتمان الحق أو تحريفه طمعًا في منفعة أو محاباةً لقريب. فالشهادة أمانة لله، وصيانتها مقدَّمة على المال والقرابة.

translation: But if it is discovered that the two were guilty of wrongdoing, then two others shall take their place from among those whose rights were violated—the two most entitled among them—and they shall swear by Allah: “Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; otherwise, we would indeed be among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: If the first witnesses are exposed as having lied, concealed facts, or betrayed the trust placed in them, the right of testimony passes to two people from the party whose inheritance or property was affected, especially those with the strongest legitimate claim. They must affirm under oath that their testimony is more truthful and that they have not exceeded the truth, showing that the law seeks to restore justice while holding every witness accountable before Allah.

translation: That is more likely to make them give testimony in its proper form, or to fear that oaths may be returned after their oaths. And be mindful of Allah and listen; Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The prescribed procedure of solemn testimony and the possibility that their oaths will be challenged and transferred to others is intended to restrain witnesses from distortion or concealment and compel them to speak the truth faithfully. Believers are therefore commanded to remain conscious of Allah and heed His guidance, for persistent defiance and disobedience deprive a person of divine guidance.

translation: On the Day Allah will gather the messengers and ask, “What response were you given?” They will say, “We have no knowledge; surely You alone are the Knower of all unseen.”
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a scene in which even the messengers, despite their honored status and witness to their peoples, submit entirely to Allah’s perfect knowledge. Their response expresses humility before Him and affirms that the full reality of people’s acceptance, rejection, sincerity, and deeds is known only to Allah, who will judge them with complete truth and justice.

translation: When Allah said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother: how I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit, so that you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity; and how I taught you the Scripture, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel; and how you fashioned from clay the form of a bird, by My permission, then breathed into it and it became a bird, by My permission; and you healed the congenitally blind and the leper, by My permission; and how you brought the dead to life, by My permission; and how I restrained the Children of Israel from harming you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those who disbelieved among them said, ‘This is nothing but clear sorcery.’”
interpretation: The verse establishes that every extraordinary sign granted to Jesus was a divine favor and occurred only by Allah’s permission, not through any independent power belonging to Jesus himself. His miraculous birth, teaching, speech, and healing therefore testify to his honored prophethood and to Allah’s absolute sovereignty, while the denial of these clear signs as sorcery reveals the obstinacy of those who rejected the truth. The mention of Allah’s protection of Jesus also shows that opposition cannot overcome the divine care given to His messengers.

translation: And when I inspired the disciples: “Believe in Me and in My messenger,” they said, “We believe, so bear witness that we are Muslims.”
interpretation: Allah reminds Jesus that He directed his devoted disciples toward faith in Allah and His messenger. Their response expresses sincere acceptance, submission, and readiness to affirm their commitment openly before Allah and others.

translation: When the disciples said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, is your Lord able to send down to us a table spread with food from heaven?” He said, “Fear Allah, if you are believers.”
interpretation: The disciples’ request reflects a desire for a tangible sign, while Jesus reminds them that genuine faith is founded on reverence and trust in Allah, not on demanding extraordinary proofs or testing His power.

translation: They said, “We wish to eat from it, to reassure our hearts, to know that you have told us the truth, and to be among its witnesses.”
interpretation: The disciples express a desire for a tangible sign that would deepen their inner certainty: sharing in the heavenly provision would calm their hearts, confirm the truth of Jesus’s message to them, and enable them to testify to the miracle with direct knowledge.

translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from heaven, to be a festival for us—for the first and the last of us—and a sign from You. Provide for us, for You are the best of providers.”
interpretation: Jesus appeals to Allah for a heavenly provision that will become a lasting sign of divine power and a shared occasion of worship and gratitude for his people, while acknowledging that all sustenance ultimately comes from Allah alone.

translation: Allah said, “Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever among you disbelieves thereafter, I will punish him with a punishment with which I have never punished anyone among all the worlds.”
interpretation: Allah warns that receiving such a manifest sign would establish an especially serious responsibility: whoever knowingly rejects faith after witnessing it will deserve an exceptionally severe punishment, because disbelief after clear divine evidence is a grave act of defiance.

translation: And when Allah said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah’?” He said, “Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. Had I said it, You would surely have known it. You know what is within my soul, while I do not know what is within Yours. Indeed, You alone are the Knower of all unseen things.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Jesus’ complete disavowal of any claim to divinity or partnership with Allah. He affirms that worship belongs solely to Allah, that he is only a servant and messenger, and that Allah’s perfect knowledge encompasses everything—while no created being can fully know the unseen or possess independent authority beside Him.

translation: I said to them only what You commanded me: “Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them; but when You took me, You were the Watcher over them. And You are Witness over all things.
interpretation: يبيّن عيسى عليه السلام أن دعوته لم تتجاوز توحيد الله وعبادته، وأنه لم يأمر قومه بعبادته أو بعبادة غير الله. وكانت رقابته على أتباعه مرتبطة بوجوده بينهم، أما بعد مفارقته لهم فالله وحده هو الرقيب على أعمالهم، العليم بما أحدثوه وما اعتقدوه، ولا يخفى عليه شيء.

translation: If You punish them, they are indeed Your servants; and if You forgive them, surely You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This is a humble submission to God’s judgment: all people belong to Him, so He may punish or forgive according to His perfect authority and wisdom. Forgiveness is not weakness or obligation, but an expression of mercy exercised by the One whose power and judgment are absolute.

translation: Allah will say, “This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. They will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining in them forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the supreme triumph.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, sincere faith and truthful conduct will be of lasting benefit, unlike worldly claims that are unsupported by deeds. Those who were truthful with Allah in belief, speech, and action will receive eternal nearness and contentment: Allah will be pleased with them through His acceptance and mercy, and they will be fully satisfied with His reward and decree. This mutual pleasure is the highest form of success.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens, the earth, and all that is within them; and He has power over all things.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth exists under Allah’s ownership and authority, so nothing lies beyond His control or ability. This calls people to recognize His absolute sovereignty, rely upon Him, and submit to His command.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. All praise belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Yet those who disbelieve set up equals with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse directs all praise and worship to Allah alone, since He is the sole Creator and the source of every form of light and guidance. In spite of this unmistakable evidence of His lordship, those who reject faith treat others as equal to Him, revealing the profound contradiction between acknowledging the created world and denying its One Creator.

translation: He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term; and a specified term is with Him—yet you still doubt.
interpretation: تذكّر الآية الإنسان بأصله الضعيف وبأن حياته الدنيوية محدودة بأجلٍ قضاه الله، بينما الأجل المسمّى عنده مرتبط بعلمه وتقديره للبعث والجزاء؛ فمع وضوح هذه الدلائل لا يليق بالإنسان أن يماري في قدرة الله ووحدانيته.

translation: And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows what you conceal and what you reveal, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: Allah alone is worthy of worship throughout the heavens and the earth; His authority and divinity encompass all creation, without implying that He is contained within any place. Nothing hidden or apparent escapes His knowledge, including every deed and consequence a person acquires, so human actions are always fully known and accountable before Him.

translation: Whenever a sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them, they turn away from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays a people whose persistent heedlessness prevents them from benefiting from divine guidance: every indication of God’s truth reaches them, yet they deliberately refuse to consider it or respond to it.

translation: Yet they denied the truth when it came to them; so soon there will come to them the tidings of what they used to mock.
interpretation: Those who reject the truth after it has reached them and ridicule its warnings will eventually confront the reality of what they dismissed, when its promised consequences become unmistakably clear.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them—generations whom We had firmly established on the earth as We have not established you? We sent the sky upon them with abundant rain, and We made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and raised up other generations after them.
interpretation: The verse warns that power, prosperity, fertile lands, and abundant resources are not signs of permanent security or divine approval. Earlier peoples possessed great strength and blessings, yet when they persisted in wrongdoing, those blessings could not protect them from destruction. Their fate teaches that societies are accountable for how they use what God grants them, and that the rise of later generations is itself a reminder of God’s power to replace those who reject His guidance.

translation: Had We sent down to you a scripture written on parchment, and they had touched it with their own hands, those who disbelieve would surely have said, “This is nothing but clear magic.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the obstinacy of those who reject revelation: their denial is not caused by a lack of tangible evidence, for even if the Qur’an had been physically delivered and directly touched, they would still dismiss it as magic. Their resistance arises from deliberate refusal to accept the truth, not from insufficient proof.

translation: And they say, “Why has an angel not been sent down to him?” Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been concluded, and they would not have been granted any respite.
interpretation: Their demand for an angel was not a sincere search for guidance, but a challenge to the Prophet. Had an angel appeared in a form they could directly perceive, the truth would have become an unmistakable decisive sign, leaving no room for continued testing or delay; those who persisted in denial would then have faced the final judgment without further respite.

translation: Had We made him an angel, We would have made him appear as a man, and We would have confused for them what they themselves confuse.
interpretation: Even if God had sent an angel as a messenger, people would have encountered him in human form so they could hear him, understand him, and relate to him. Thus their demand for an angel would not remove their excuses; they would still raise doubts and become confused in the same way because the real obstacle was their rejection, not the form of the messenger.

translation: Messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who ridiculed them were overtaken by the very punishment they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet and warns those who reject divine guidance: mockery does not weaken the truth or protect its mockers; rather, persistent ridicule and denial can lead to the very consequence they dismiss as impossible.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land and then observe what was the end of those who denied the truth.”
interpretation: This is a command to reflect on the remains and histories of past peoples: examining how denial and rejection of divine guidance led to their downfall should awaken people to heed the truth before suffering a similar end.

translation: Say, “To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?” Say, “To Allah.” He has prescribed mercy upon Himself. He will surely gather you all on the Day of Resurrection—there is no doubt about it. Those who have ruined their own souls will not believe.
interpretation: The verse establishes that all creation belongs entirely to Allah, whose dominion is joined with a mercy He has committed Himself to show. He will gather every person for certain judgment, yet those who reject faith ultimately harm only themselves, losing their own souls through their refusal to accept the truth.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Everything that exists—whether hidden in the darkness of night or active in the light of day—is wholly under Allah’s ownership and authority. Nothing is concealed from His hearing or knowledge, so all creation remains subject to His care, judgment, and command.

translation: Say, “Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed?” Say, “Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit, and never be among the polytheists.”
interpretation: The verse establishes that ultimate loyalty and reliance belong exclusively to Allah, because He alone created all existence and is entirely self-sufficient, whereas every other being depends on Him for sustenance. The Prophet is therefore commanded to embody complete submission to Allah and to reject every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I fear that if I disobey my Lord, I will suffer the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that even the Messenger ﷺ openly declares his complete submission to God, showing that no one is secure from the consequences of disobedience and that true safety lies in obedience and reverent fear of the Day of Judgment.

translation: Whoever is spared from it on that Day, He has surely received His mercy; and that is the clear triumph.
interpretation: The true success is to be protected from the punishment of the Day of Judgment, for such protection is an act of Allah’s mercy, not something attained through worldly status or achievement.

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is capable of all things.
interpretation: Whatever hardship or blessing reaches a person is under Allah’s control: no one can lift a hardship unless He permits it, and no one can prevent the good He wills. This calls the believer to turn to Him alone in adversity, trust His power in every circumstance, and recognize that all outcomes remain within His wisdom and ability.

translation: And He is the Supreme Overpowering Authority above His servants, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: God alone possesses absolute power and authority over all His servants; nothing can resist His decree or escape His knowledge. His rule is never arbitrary, for it is guided by perfect wisdom and complete awareness of every matter.

translation: Say, “What is greatest in testimony?” Say, “Allah is witness between me and you. This Qur’an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you through it and whoever it reaches. Do you truly testify that there are other gods alongside Allah?” Say, “I do not testify.” Say, “He is only One God, and indeed I am free of whatever you associate with Him.”
interpretation: The verse establishes Allah as the highest and decisive witness to the truth of revelation and the Prophet’s message. The Qur’an is a universal warning, extending to everyone whom it reaches. It rejects the claim that any being shares in Allah’s divinity, affirming that true faith requires exclusive devotion to the one God and complete disavowal of all forms of associating partners with Him.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their souls will not believe.
interpretation: Those who sincerely know the revealed Scripture can identify the truth of the Prophet’s message with the same certainty and familiarity with which a parent recognizes their own child. Yet some reject it despite this inner recognition, thereby choosing disbelief and bringing about their own spiritual loss.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah or denies His signs? Surely, the wrongdoers will never prosper.
interpretation: The verse declares that the gravest injustice is to attribute falsehood to Allah or reject the clear evidence of His revelation. Such distortion and denial corrupt a person’s relationship with truth, and therefore those who persist in them cannot attain true success.

translation: And on the Day We gather them all together, We will say to those who associated partners with Allah, “Where are your partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: This depicts the Day of Judgment, when those who attributed partners to Allah will be confronted with the false objects of worship they relied upon. Their inability to produce or receive help from them will expose the baselessness of their claims and the complete truth of Allah’s oneness.

translation: Then their only excuse will be to say, “By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.”
interpretation: When confronted with the consequences of associating partners with Allah, they will desperately deny what they had done, but their denial will not conceal the truth from Allah or save them from judgment.

translation: Look how they have lied against themselves, and how what they used to fabricate has failed them.
interpretation: They deceived themselves by denying the truth and attributing false claims to God; when confronted with reality, their invented excuses and alleged gods could neither support them nor save them.

translation: Among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed veils over their hearts so that they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. When they come to you, they argue with you, saying, “This is nothing but the legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: The verse portrays people whose persistent rejection has made them spiritually unreceptive: they hear the Qur’an outwardly but refuse to understand or accept its guidance. Their denial is not due to a lack of signs, but to an inward resistance that leads them to dismiss revelation as ancient tales and argue against it rather than respond sincerely.

translation: They prevent others from it and keep away from it themselves. They destroy none but their own souls, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: Those who reject the truth try both to stop others from accepting it and to distance themselves from it, but their opposition cannot harm the truth; it only deprives and ruins them spiritually, while their heedlessness prevents them from recognizing the consequence of their actions.

translation: If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire, they will say, “Would that we could be sent back! We would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers.”
interpretation: This portrays the remorse of those who rejected the truth when confronted with the reality of the Hereafter. Their plea to return is not evidence of genuine repentance but a desperate wish arising from witnessing punishment; having squandered their opportunity in this life, they can no longer undo their denial or gain the faith they once rejected.

translation: Rather, what they used to conceal before has become clear to them. Yet if they were sent back, they would return to what they had been forbidden from; indeed, they are truly liars.
interpretation: When confronted with the truth and the consequences of their deeds, they temporarily acknowledge what they had concealed or denied. But this recognition does not reflect sincere repentance or a changed character; if they were given another worldly opportunity, they would fall back into the same disobedience, showing that their promise to believe is merely a false claim born of fear.

translation: And they say, “There is nothing but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected.”
interpretation: They deny the life after death, claiming that human existence ends with this temporary worldly life and therefore rejecting resurrection and accountability before God.

translation: If only you could see when they are brought before their Lord. He will say, “Is this not the truth?” They will say, “Yes indeed, by our Lord!” He will say, “Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the undeniable moment when those who rejected resurrection and divine judgment stand before Allah and are forced to acknowledge the truth they had denied. Their acknowledgment then has no power to avert punishment, because it comes only after the reality has become manifest and their earthly opportunity to believe and repent has ended.

translation: Indeed, those who deny the meeting with Allah have lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, “Alas for us, for what we neglected concerning it!” They will carry their burdens upon their backs. Surely, evil is what they bear.
interpretation: Those who reject resurrection and accountability live in heedlessness until death and the Day of Judgment overtake them without warning. Then their regret will be useless, because the sins and neglected duties of their worldly lives will become a burden they must bear themselves; no one else can remove the consequences of what they chose to do.

translation: The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, while the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of God. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: Worldly life, with its fleeting pleasures and distractions, should not become the believer’s ultimate concern. Lasting success belongs to those who remain conscious of God and live by that awareness, because the reward of the Hereafter is enduring and far superior to anything this world can offer.

translation: We certainly know that what they say grieves you. Indeed, they do not call you a liar, but the wrongdoers reject the signs of Allah.
interpretation: Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ by clarifying that the rejection of his message does not arise from ignorance of his truthfulness; rather, it is the result of injustice and stubbornly denying the clear signs of Allah. Therefore, their denial should not cause him to doubt his mission or feel that he has failed.

translation: Messengers before you were indeed rejected, yet they patiently endured the rejection and harm inflicted upon them until Our help came to them. None can change the words of Allah. And there has already come to you some news of the messengers.
interpretation: Allah consoles the Prophet that rejection and persecution are part of the trial faced by those who convey His truth, while steadfastness is sustained by certainty that His promise of help cannot be altered and that the eventual outcome belongs to Him.

translation: وإن كان إعراضهم عنك شاقًّا عليك، فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقًا في الأرض أو سُلّمًا في السماء فتأتيهم بآية فافعل؛ ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى، فلا تكونن من الجاهلين.
interpretation: يواسي الله نبيَّه ﷺ ويعلّمه أن عناد المعرضين ليس دليلًا على نقص في الدعوة، وأن الهداية لا تُنتزع بالإكراه، بل هي بيد الله وحكمته؛ فعليه أن يثبت في تبليغ الحق وألا يستسلم للحزن أو يتمنى ما لا سبيل إليه، مع إدراك أن رفض المكذبين نابع من اختيارهم لا من قصور في الآيات.

translation: Only those who listen can respond; as for the dead, Allah will resurrect them, and then they will be returned to Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true response to divine guidance belongs to those who listen with receptive hearts and act upon what they hear. Those who reject it are likened to the dead in their inability to benefit, while the physically dead will be raised by Allah and brought back to Him for judgment.

translation: And they say, “Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.”
interpretation: Their demand for another miracle does not reflect a lack of divine power, but a failure to recognize that guidance depends on sincere understanding rather than on endlessly repeated signs. Allah can provide whatever sign He wills, yet many people remain unaware that their rejection stems from stubbornness and ignorance, not from insufficient evidence.

translation: There is no creature on earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, except that they are communities like you. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: Every living creature belongs to an ordered community under God’s care, with its own nature, needs, and way of life. Nothing in creation lies outside His encompassing knowledge and decree, and all creatures will ultimately return to Him for judgment according to His perfect wisdom.

translation: Those who deny Our signs are deaf and mute, enveloped in darknesses. Whomever Allah wills, He lets go astray; and whomever He wills, He places upon a straight path.
interpretation: The verse portrays persistent denial of divine truth as a spiritual deafness and muteness: such people cannot hear guidance or respond to it, and their confusion is like darkness layered upon darkness. Allah’s willing to guide or leave astray is understood in relation to a person’s response—those who turn sincerely toward truth are granted guidance, while those who persist in rejection are left to the misguidance they have chosen.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah’s punishment comes upon you or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon anyone other than Allah, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who turn to false deities: when faced with overwhelming punishment or the Final Hour, human beings recognize that only Allah has the power to help and remove distress. Their sincere appeal at such a moment exposes the falsehood of associating others with Him.

translation: Rather, it is Him alone you call upon; then He removes the hardship for which you call upon Him, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.
interpretation: When distress strips away false confidence, people instinctively turn to Allah alone, recognizing that only He has power to remove their affliction. Yet once relief comes, they often abandon that sincerity and neglect the partners they had invoked alongside Him, revealing the weakness and inconsistency of associating others with Allah.

translation: And We certainly sent messengers to nations before you, then We afflicted them with hardship and suffering so that they might humble themselves in supplication.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that earlier peoples were tested through poverty, illness, and distress after messengers came to them. These trials were meant to awaken their hearts, break their pride, and lead them to turn sincerely to Allah; when hardship does not produce humility and repentance, it reveals their persistent rejection rather than a failure of the divine warning.

translation: Why, then, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves? Rather, their hearts hardened, and Satan made attractive to them what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who encounter divine warning and hardship yet fail to respond with repentance and humility. Their continued defiance is attributed to hardened hearts, while Satan causes their sinful practices and misguided conduct to appear pleasing, preventing them from recognizing the need to return to God.

translation: Then, when they neglected the warning they had been given, We opened for them the gates of every blessing, until, as they rejoiced in what they had received, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were plunged into despair.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly ease and abundance are not necessarily signs of divine approval. When people persistently disregard admonition, prosperity may become a gradual test that deepens their heedlessness; then sudden punishment can overtake them, leaving them helpless and without hope.

translation: Thus the last remnant of the people who committed ظلم was cut off; and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This declares that wrongdoing ultimately leads to the complete downfall of its perpetrators, while Allah alone deserves praise for establishing justice and bringing the affairs of creation to their rightful end.

translation: قل: أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم، فأيُّ إلهٍ غير الله يأتيكم بها؟ انظر كيف نصرّف الآيات، ثم هم يصدفون.
interpretation: تُقيم الآية حُجّةً على عجز الإنسان وافتقاره الكامل إلى الله؛ فالسَّمع والبصر والقلب نعمٌ لا يملك أحدٌ سلبها أو إعادتها إلا الله. ومع ذلك، ينوّع الله البراهين ويعرضها بوجوهٍ متعددة ليتبيّن الحق، ثم يُعرض المكذّبون عنه إعراضًا متعمدًا.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah were to come upon you suddenly or openly, would any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?”
interpretation: This is a warning that divine punishment, whenever and however it comes, is not arbitrary; it overtakes those who persist in ظلم—rejecting truth and committing wrongdoing—while urging people to abandon injustice before they are seized unexpectedly.

translation: We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and acts righteously—there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: God’s messengers convey both hope in His mercy and warning of accountability. Those who respond with sincere faith and righteous conduct are granted security from the fearful consequences of the Hereafter and freedom from regret over what they have left behind.

translation: And those who deny Our signs—the punishment will afflict them because of their persistent defiance and disobedience.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s revealed signs and knowingly departing from His commands leads to punishment; the cause is not mere error, but a continuing pattern of rebellious conduct.

translation: Say, “I do not claim to possess the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel. I follow only what is revealed to me.” Say, “Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to declare that he is Allah’s servant and messenger, not the possessor of divine powers or independent knowledge of the unseen. His guidance comes solely through revelation. Those who reject revealed truth are like the blind, while those who accept it are like the seeing; the verse therefore calls people to use their reason and recognize the difference between unbelief and faith.

translation: And warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord; they will have no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may become mindful of Him.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a warning and a means of guidance for those whose awareness of standing before Allah makes them humble and receptive. On that Day, no one can independently protect or intercede for them apart from Allah, so this certainty should lead them to sincere faith, obedience, and careful avoidance of wrongdoing.

translation: Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable for anything of their account, nor are they accountable for anything of your account; if you were to drive them away, you would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere devotion, not wealth, rank, or social standing, is the measure of a person’s worth before God. Those who seek Him faithfully must not be excluded to satisfy the pride or preferences of others, for every person bears responsibility for their own deeds, and rejecting devoted believers because of their status is an injustice.

translation: Thus We have tested some of them through others, so that they may say, “Are these the ones whom Allah has favored among us?” Is Allah not best aware of those who are grateful?
interpretation: Allah tests people through the differences in status, wealth, and social standing among them, exposing whether they judge truth by worldly rank or recognize sincere faith. His favor is not determined by privilege or reputation; He alone knows those whose hearts are truly grateful and devoted.

translation: When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: “Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself: whoever among you does wrong in ignorance, then repents afterward and reforms, surely He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere believers should be welcomed with peace and that Allah’s mercy is assured for those who fall into wrongdoing through ignorance, then genuinely repent and correct their conduct; repentance is demonstrated not only by regret, but also by reform.

translation: Thus We explain the signs, so that the way of the criminals may become clear.
interpretation: God clarifies His signs and proofs with precision so that the path of those who reject and oppose the truth is unmistakably exposed, enabling people to recognize and avoid it.

translation: Say, “I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah.” Say, “I will not follow your desires; for then I would have gone astray and would not be among the rightly guided.”
interpretation: The verse commands unwavering devotion to Allah alone and rejects religious beliefs shaped by human desires or pressure. Following such desires would lead away from truth and deprive a person of divine guidance.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I stand upon clear proof from my Lord, yet you have denied it. I do not possess what you demand to be hastened. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He declares the truth, and He is the best of judges.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s duty is to follow and proclaim the clear evidence given by Allah, not to control the punishment or signs that people impatiently demand. Final judgment is solely Allah’s authority; He alone distinguishes truth from falsehood and decides between His servants with perfect justice.

translation: Say, “If I had what you are impatiently asking for, the matter between me and you would have been settled; and Allah knows best who the wrongdoers are.”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to clarify that the timing and power of divine judgment belong solely to Allah, not to him. The disbelievers’ demand to hasten punishment does not challenge Allah’s wisdom; He delays judgment according to His perfect knowledge and will, while fully knowing those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. No leaf falls without His knowledge, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, except that it is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: The verse affirms that complete knowledge of the unseen belongs exclusively to Allah, while His knowledge encompasses every detail of creation—whether apparent or hidden, great or insignificant, living or lifeless. Nothing occurs outside His awareness, and all things are preserved in a clear, comprehensive record, expressing His perfect knowledge and sovereignty over the universe.

translation: He is the One who takes your souls by night and knows what you have done by day; then He raises you again in it, so that an appointed term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse portrays sleep as a nightly form of death and awakening as a renewal granted by God. Human life therefore unfolds entirely under His knowledge and authority, until the appointed lifespan ends and every person returns to Him to be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: He is the Supreme over His servants, and He sends guardians over you. Then, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not fall short.
interpretation: The verse affirms Allah’s absolute authority over His creation and teaches that human beings remain under the care and watch of appointed angels throughout life. At the decreed moment of death, the angels entrusted with taking the soul carry out Allah’s command precisely, without delay, neglect, or error.

translation: Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Surely, judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.
interpretation: All creatures ultimately return to Allah, whose authority and ownership are absolute and whose judgment is perfectly just. Nothing is hidden from Him, and He settles every matter and reckons every deed with complete knowledge and without delay.

translation: Say, “Who saves you from the darknesses of the land and the sea, when you call upon Him humbly and secretly: ‘If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the grateful’?”
interpretation: Allah reminds people that in moments of danger—whether on land or at sea—they instinctively turn to Him with humility and sincerity, promising gratitude if rescued. The verse exposes the inconsistency of seeking Allah alone in distress and then failing to remain devoted and thankful once safety returns.

translation: Say, “Allah saves you from it and from every distress, yet you associate partners with Him.”
interpretation: Allah alone rescues people from dangers and severe hardships, but despite recognizing His power and turning to Him in moments of need, they return to attributing worship and divine partnership to others instead of remaining faithful to Him.

translation: Say, “He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to divide you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others.” See how We explain the signs in different ways, so that they may understand.
interpretation: The verse warns that divine punishment may come through overwhelming forces, disasters, or the destructive conflict that arises when people become divided into hostile factions. It calls people to recognize these warnings, abandon causes of division and aggression, and reflect on God’s signs before suffering becomes the consequence of their own corruption.

translation: Your people have denied it, though it is the truth. Say, “I am not appointed as your keeper.”
interpretation: The denial of people does not diminish the truth of revelation. The Messenger’s duty is to convey it clearly, not to control people’s hearts or force them to believe; each person remains responsible for his or her response.

translation: For every message there is an appointed time, and you will come to know.
interpretation: Every divine warning and promise will become evident at its destined time; those who reject it will ultimately discover its truth when the promised consequences arrive.

translation: When you see those who engage in vain discourse concerning Our revelations, turn away from them until they engage in some other conversation. And if Satan makes you forget, then, once you remember, do not remain seated with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse teaches that a believer must not remain in gatherings where Allah’s revelations are mocked, distorted, or treated frivolously, since continued presence can imply approval or weaken reverence for the truth. If one forgets and remains, one must leave as soon as one remembers; the command is to protect one’s faith and moral integrity, not to forbid sincere discussion or questioning.

translation: Those who are mindful of Allah are not accountable for them in the least; rather, their duty is only to remind them, so that they may become mindful.
interpretation: Those who possess taqwā are not held responsible for the sins of people who persist in wrongdoing, provided they do not approve of or participate in it. Their responsibility is to offer sincere counsel and remind others of the truth, in the hope that the reminder awakens their awareness of Allah and leads them to obedience.

translation: And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play, and whom worldly life has deceived. Remind them by it, lest a soul be delivered to ruin because of what it has earned; it will have no protector or intercessor besides Allah. Even if it offered every possible ransom, none would be accepted from it. Such are the ones delivered to destruction because of what they earned. For them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they persistently disbelieved.
interpretation: The verse commands believers not to compromise with people who treat faith as entertainment and allow worldly desires to deceive them, while still warning them sincerely through divine revelation.
