It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment each person will face the consequences of their own choices: no worldly authority, claimed intercession, or ransom can rescue someone who has rejected the truth. Their punishment is not arbitrary, but the fitting consequence of their persistent denial and heedlessness.

translation: Say, “Shall we invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us—like one whom the devils have lured into the earth, bewildered, while he has companions calling him to guidance, saying, ‘Come to us’?” Say, “Indeed, Allah’s guidance is the true guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse rejects abandoning revealed guidance for powerless objects, beliefs, or influences that cannot bring benefit or avert harm. Returning to misguidance after receiving truth is likened to a person lost and confused in the wilderness: false forces pull him away, while sincere companions call him back to the right path. True guidance is therefore not determined by desire, custom, or competing voices, but by Allah’s direction; accepting it requires humble submission to Him as the Lord and sustainer of all creation.

translation: And to establish prayer and be mindful of Him; and He is the One to whom you will all be gathered.
interpretation: This is a command to maintain prayer as a central expression of devotion and to live with reverent awareness of God, remembering that every person will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And on the Day He says, “Be,” and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He knows the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse establishes Allah’s absolute authority over creation, existence, and resurrection: everything comes into being by His command, and all worldly power will be shown to belong solely to Him when the Trumpet is blown. His perfect knowledge encompasses what is hidden and what is visible, while His wisdom and awareness ensure that His judgment and governance are entirely true and just.

translation: And when Abraham said to his father, Azar, “Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in clear error.”
interpretation: Abraham condemned the worship of idols because they are powerless creations and cannot deserve divine devotion. He perceived that treating them as gods was an unmistakable departure from true guidance, and he challenged both his father and his people to abandon inherited beliefs in favor of worshipping the one true God.

translation: Thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among those possessing certainty.
interpretation: Allah granted Abraham insight into the profound order and signs within the heavens and the earth, strengthening his recognition of divine oneness and elevating his faith from reflection to firm certainty.

translation: Then, when the night covered him, he saw a star and said, “This is my Lord.” But when it set, he said, “I do not love those that set.”
interpretation: Abraham was not genuinely worshipping the star; he was reasoning with his people in a way they could recognize. By showing that the star disappears and is subject to change, he demonstrated that it cannot be the eternal Lord worthy of worship.

translation: Then, when he saw the moon rising, he said, “This is my Lord.” But when it set, he said, “If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who have gone astray.”
interpretation: Abraham was demonstrating to his people that the moon cannot be divine, because it appears and disappears and is subject to change. By exposing its dependence and inability to remain, he showed that true lordship belongs only to the One who created and governs it, and he acknowledged that guidance away from false worship comes solely from God.

translation: Then, when he saw the sun rising, he said, “This is my Lord; this is greater.” But when it set, he said, “O my people, I am free of whatever you associate with God.”
interpretation: Abraham was demonstrating the falsehood of worshipping celestial bodies: even the sun, despite its immense appearance and power, rises and sets by a greater governing order and therefore cannot be God. He thus rejected all association of created things with God and affirmed His absolute transcendence.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, inclining exclusively to the truth, and I am not among those who associate partners with God.
interpretation: This is a declaration of sincere devotion: the speaker directs his worship and allegiance solely to the Creator of all existence, rejecting every form of idolatry, association, or deviation from pure monotheism.

translation: And his people argued with him. He said, “Do you argue with me about Allah, when He has guided me? I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then reflect?”
interpretation: Abraham responds that genuine guidance frees a person from being intimidated by false gods or the threats associated with them. Since everything lies within Allah’s knowledge and will, created beings possess no independent power to harm; therefore, disputing this truth is irrational, and people are urged to reflect on the weakness of what they worship besides Allah.

translation: And how should I fear what you associate with Allah, while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority to you? So which of the two groups is more entitled to security, if you truly know?
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of idolaters: they fear powerless objects while committing the far graver act of attributing partners to Allah without any divine proof. True security belongs to those who affirm Allah’s oneness and avoid associating anything with Him, because their faith is grounded in truth rather than baseless claims.

translation: Those who believe and do not taint their faith with wrongdoing—for them is security, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: True faith brings security and guidance when it is kept free from the greatest form of wrongdoing: associating partners with God. Those who affirm God’s oneness and remain sincere in their worship are granted reassurance in this life and the Hereafter, and are guided to what is right.

translation: And that was Our argument, which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise in ranks whom We will. Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah granted Abraham clear reasoning to overcome the objections of his people and establish the truth of monotheism. The raising of people in rank is according to His wisdom and knowledge, through faith, understanding, and righteous conduct—not by human preference or worldly status.

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob; each of them We guided. And We had guided Noah before him. And among his descendants were David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: This verse presents divine guidance as a blessing granted to Abraham and continued through a lineage of righteous prophets, showing that honor comes not merely through ancestry but through faith, guidance, and excellence in doing good; God rewards those who embody these qualities.

translation: And Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elijah—each was among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse affirms that these prophets, despite their different circumstances and missions, were united by sincere devotion to God and steadfast obedience, which made them exemplars of righteousness.

translation: And Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot—and We favored each of them above all peoples.
interpretation: Allah mentions these prophets among His honored servants, affirming that each was granted distinction, guidance, and a rank of excellence suited to his mission. Their different circumstances do not lessen their shared virtue; all were chosen to convey Allah’s guidance and serve as examples of faithfulness.

translation: And among their fathers, their descendants, and their brothers, We chose some and guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah bestowed His special favor upon certain members of these noble families, selecting them for faith and righteousness and guiding them firmly toward the way of truth and obedience.

translation: That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whoever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated partners with Him, whatever they used to do would have become worthless.
interpretation: Allah’s guidance is a gift that leads His servants to recognize and worship Him alone. Even those granted knowledge, prophethood, and righteous qualities would lose the value of their deeds if they turned to associating partners with Allah, because sincere monotheism is the foundation upon which every act of worship depends.

translation: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood. So if these people reject them, We have entrusted them to a people who will not reject them.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Scripture, sound judgment, and prophethood are divine gifts granted to chosen messengers. If the people addressed reject these truths, their rejection does not diminish their worth or invalidate the message; God will entrust it to others who recognize it, uphold it, and remain faithful to it.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance. Say, “I ask of you no reward for it; it is only a reminder for all worlds.”
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to follow the guidance of the prophets who came before him, especially their sincere devotion to Him and steadfastness upon truth. His message is not presented for worldly gain or personal benefit, but as a universal reminder that calls all people back to faith, righteousness, and awareness of their accountability before Allah.

translation: They have not esteemed Allah as He deserves to be esteemed when they said, “Allah has not revealed anything to any human being.” Say, “Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought, as a light and guidance for humanity, which you have made into separate sheets, displaying some of them while concealing much? And you were taught what neither you nor your forefathers knew.” Say, “Allah.” Then leave them to indulge in their vain discourse and amuse themselves.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny revelation by exposing the contradiction in their claim: they acknowledge the Torah given to Moses, yet reject the possibility that Allah could reveal guidance to humanity. Their selective presentation and concealment of Scripture show that the problem is not lack of evidence but deliberate distortion and denial. Allah’s revelation is a mercy and source of knowledge beyond what human beings could discover on their own; therefore, when they persist in disputing truth merely for diversion, they should be left to their futile argument while the truth remains clear.

translation: And this is a blessed Book We have sent down, confirming what came before it, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are constant in maintaining their prayer.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as a divinely revealed source of blessing and truth, affirming the genuine guidance preserved in earlier revelation. Its warning begins with Makkah and extends to all surrounding peoples, while sincere faith in the Hereafter leads a person to accept the Qur’an and demonstrate that faith through steadfast care for prayer.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah, or says, “It has been revealed to me,” when nothing has been revealed to him, or says, “I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed”? If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the throes of death, while the angels stretch out their hands, saying, “Give up your souls! Today you will be repaid with the punishment of humiliation because of what you used to say about Allah without truth, and because you were arrogant toward His signs.”
interpretation: The verse identifies the gravest form of wrongdoing as claiming divine authority without revelation—whether by inventing false statements about Allah, falsely claiming prophethood, or challenging His revelation with fabricated words. Such arrogance is exposed at death, when those who rejected or distorted Allah’s signs lose all power and are confronted by the angels with the humiliating consequence of their deliberate falsehood and defiance.

translation: And you have come to Us individually, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We granted you. We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in your affairs. The bond between you has been severed, and what you used to claim has vanished from you.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a complete exposure of reality: every person will stand before God alone, stripped of worldly possessions, status, and imagined sources of protection. The powers and false partners upon which people relied will neither accompany nor benefit them, and all claims that competed with God’s exclusive authority will collapse when the truth becomes unmistakable.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the One who splits open the grain and the date stone. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. That is Allah—so how can you be turned away?
interpretation: Allah’s bringing life from what appears lifeless, as when a seed bursts forth into a living plant, is a sign of His absolute power over creation and resurrection. Since only He governs these transformations, turning away from Him toward false objects of worship is irrational and without justification.

translation: He is the One who cleaves the dawn, and He has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the design of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The regular emergence of dawn, the repose of night, and the precisely measured courses of the sun and moon reveal that the universe operates by the deliberate decree of God, whose power establishes its order and whose knowledge encompasses every detail.

translation: And He is the One who made the stars for you, so that you may find your way by them through the darknesses of the land and the sea. We have certainly explained the signs for people who possess knowledge.
interpretation: The stars are presented as both a practical means of guidance and a sign of Allah’s purposeful ordering of creation. Their usefulness in navigating through darkness points the human heart toward recognizing divine wisdom and seeking guidance from the One who established such order.

translation: He is the One who brought you into being from a single soul, and there is a place of settlement and a place of safekeeping for you. We have surely explained the signs for people who understand.
interpretation: Humanity shares one origin, and every person exists under God’s knowledge and decree through successive stages and appointed places—whether in the womb, in this world, or in the grave. Recognizing this common origin and ordered journey should lead people to discern God’s wisdom and live with humility and accountability.

translation: And He is the One who sends down water from the sky, and by it We bring forth the growth of every kind of thing. Then We bring forth from it greenery, from which We produce clustered grains; and from the date palms, from their spathes, hanging low clusters; and gardens of grapes, olives, and pomegranates—similar yet distinct. Look at their fruit as it appears and as it ripens. Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The verse directs people to contemplate how one source—rainwater—gives rise to an astonishing variety of plants, fruits, forms, and flavors. This ordered transformation reveals the Creator’s power, wisdom, and sustaining mercy: He brings life from the earth, develops it through successive stages, and makes its blessings accessible to humanity. The similarity and diversity among these crops point to deliberate design rather than mere sameness or disorder, while the command to observe their growth and ripening teaches that attentive reflection on the natural world can lead the believer to recognize God’s signs and deepen faith.

translation: And they have attributed partners to Allah from among the jinn, although He created them; and they falsely ascribed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse condemns attributing divine status to the jinn and inventing offspring for Allah. Since Allah is the Creator of all beings, no created being can be His partner or child; such claims are baseless descriptions made without knowledge and are utterly beneath His transcendence.

translation: خالق السماوات والأرض على غير مثال سابق؛ كيف يكون له ولد ولم تكن له زوجة؟ وقد خلق كل شيء، وهو بكل شيء عليم.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية استحالة نسبة الولد إلى الله؛ فالولد إنما يكون من والدين، والله منزّه عن الحاجة والزوجة، وهو خالق كل موجود لا جزءٌ من موجود ولا شبيه له. وإحاطته التامة بكل شيء تؤكد كمال ربوبيته وتنزّهه عن صفات المخلوقين.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things. So worship Him, and He is the Trustee over all things.
interpretation: Since Allah alone created and sustains everything, He alone deserves worship. Entrusting all affairs to Him means relying on His wisdom and care while remaining devoted and obedient to Him.

translation: Eyes cannot encompass Him, while He encompasses all eyes; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: No created vision can fully perceive or encompass Allah, whereas His knowledge and power encompass every sight and every being. His subtle wisdom reaches all things, and He is perfectly aware of their realities and actions.

translation: There have come to you clear insights from your Lord. Whoever sees them, it is for his own benefit; and whoever is blind to them, it is against his own soul. I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: Allah has provided people with sufficient guidance and evidence, so accepting or rejecting it carries consequences that return to each person. The Messenger’s duty is to convey the truth clearly, not to compel people to believe or take responsibility for their refusal.

translation: Thus We explain the signs in various ways, so that they may say, “You have studied,” and so that We may make it clear to a people who have knowledge.
interpretation: Allah presents His signs in diverse and repeated forms so that sincere people may understand and be guided, while those who reject the truth may resort to accusing the Messenger of merely having learned them from others. The verse therefore shows that the same revelation can increase clarity for the knowledgeable but expose the stubbornness of those unwilling to believe.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god except Him, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: Remain firmly guided by the revelation from your Lord, grounding worship and obedience in the truth that none deserves worship but Him, and do not be drawn into accepting or endorsing the false beliefs of those who associate partners with Him.

translation: Had Allah willed, they would not have associated partners with Him. We have not appointed you as their guardian, nor are you responsible for managing their affairs.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the persistence of disbelief occurs within Allah’s sovereign permission, but the Prophet is not charged with forcing people to believe or controlling their choices. His duty is to convey the revelation clearly; guidance cannot be imposed, and each person remains accountable for the response they freely make.

translation: Do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in hostility without knowledge. Thus We have made the deeds of every community seem appealing to them. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that defending truth must be joined with wisdom and restraint: even when false beliefs are condemned, believers must not use needlessly provocative speech that causes people to respond with greater disrespect toward Allah. God has allowed each community to perceive its own practices as appealing, while ultimate judgment and the exposure of every deed belong to Him.

translation: They swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a sign comes to them, they will surely believe in it. Say, “The signs are only with Allah.” And what will make you realize that, when it comes, they will not believe?
interpretation: Their emphatic promises do not demonstrate genuine openness to guidance, for faith is not produced merely by witnessing a demanded miracle. Allah alone determines the signs, while their persistent rejection shows that the real obstacle is their unwillingness to submit, not a lack of evidence.

translation: We shall turn their hearts and eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We shall leave them wandering blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: Because they persistently reject the truth after it has become clear, their hearts and perceptions are deprived of receptivity to it; consequently, they are left confused and aimless in the excesses they have chosen.

translation: And even if We sent down the angels to them, and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered every sign before them, they would not believe unless Allah willed it—but most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: The verse teaches that persistent denial is not caused by a lack of evidence. Even extraordinary signs would not make people believe when they deliberately resist the truth; true faith occurs only by Allah’s permission and guidance. Their ignorance lies in failing to recognize that guidance is not attained merely through witnessing miracles, but through sincere openness to Allah’s truth.

translation: Thus We have made for every prophet enemies—devils from among humankind and the jinn—who inspire one another with embellished words in deception. Had your Lord willed, they would not have done so; so leave them and what they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse teaches that opposition to divine truth may arise from both human and unseen forces that cooperate by disguising falsehood in attractive language. Their ability to act exists only within God’s permission and does not diminish the truth of revelation; therefore, the prophet is instructed not to be consumed by their fabrications, but to remain steadfast and leave their accountability to God.

translation: And so the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, be pleased with it, and commit what they are committing.
interpretation: Allah allows the deceptive words of devils to reach those who reject the Hereafter as a test; because they are inclined to falsehood, they accept it and persist in their sins and wrongful deeds.

translation: أفغيرَ الله أطلبُ حكماً، وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتابَ مفصَّلاً؟ والذين آتيناهم الكتابَ يعلمون أنه منزَّلٌ من ربك بالحق، فلا تكوننَّ من الشاكّين.
interpretation: يقرر الله أن المرجع الحق في الحكم والتشريع هو وحده، لأن القرآن الذي أنزله بيّنٌ مفصّل، وتشهد الكتب السابقة وأهل العلم بها بأنه وحيٌ نازل من الله بالحق؛ لذلك ينبغي للنبي والمؤمنين أن يثبتوا على اليقين بحكم الله وألا يلتفتوا إلى شكوك المعارضين.

translation: And the word of your Lord has been perfected in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah’s declarations and judgments are complete, utterly true, and perfectly just; they contain neither error nor injustice. No created being can overturn or alter what He has decreed or revealed, for His perfect hearing encompasses every utterance and His complete knowledge encompasses every matter.

translation: And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you away from the path of Allah. They follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but speculate falsely.
interpretation: This verse warns that truth is not determined by the majority. Following widespread opinion without sound revelation and clear evidence can divert a person from Allah’s path, because many people rely on assumptions and speak without certain knowledge. સાચ

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows best who strays from His path, and He knows best those who are rightly guided.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses complete knowledge of people’s true spiritual condition: He knows who has turned away from the truth and who sincerely follows guidance. Therefore, judgment should be measured by His revealed guidance rather than by appearances or human opinion.

translation: So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you truly believe in His signs.
interpretation: Believers are instructed to consume only lawful food slaughtered or prepared with conscious mention of Allah’s name, because honoring this command is an expression of genuine faith in His revelations.

translation: Why should you not eat of that over which Allah’s name has been mentioned, when He has already explained to you what He has forbidden to you—except what you are compelled to eat? Indeed, many lead others astray through their desires without knowledge. Surely your Lord knows best those who transgress.
interpretation: The verse instructs believers to follow Allah’s clear rulings on lawful and unlawful food rather than adopting prohibitions based on custom, speculation, or personal desire. Necessity is treated with mercy, permitting what is otherwise forbidden only to the extent required to preserve life. It also warns that misleading judgments made without knowledge are forms of transgression, and that Allah fully knows those who exceed His limits.

translation: And abandon outward sin and inward sin. Indeed, those who commit sin will be repaid for what they used to perpetrate.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to avoid wrongdoing in every form—both the sins visible in their actions and those concealed within their hearts, such as insincerity, envy, and corrupt intentions. No sin is hidden from God, and every deliberate act of wrongdoing carries its just recompense.

translation: And do not eat from that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned; indeed, it is grave disobedience. Surely the devils inspire their allies to argue with you; and if you obey them, you will indeed be polytheists.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to honor Allah’s name in slaughter and to abstain from what is dedicated or slaughtered without it. It also warns that accepting the devils’ arguments against this command and obeying them in deliberate rejection of Allah’s guidance can become an act of associating partners with Him.

translation: Is one who was dead, then We gave him life and appointed for him a light by which he walks among people, like one who is in darknesses from which he cannot emerge? Thus the deeds of the disbelievers have been made appealing to them.
interpretation: The verse contrasts spiritual guidance with disbelief: faith revives the heart and gives a person divine insight by which to live rightly, whereas rejection of truth leaves the person trapped in confusion and wrongdoing. Because of their persistent denial, their evil actions become attractive to them, preventing them from recognizing the darkness in which they remain.

translation: And thus We have made the greatest criminals in every town its leaders, so that they may plot therein. Yet they plot only against themselves, though they do not realize it.
interpretation: Allah explains that powerful wrongdoers are allowed to take the lead in opposing truth and deceiving people, but their schemes ultimately bring harm upon themselves, because they incur sin and its consequences while mistakenly thinking they are benefiting.

translation: When a sign comes to them, they say, “We will never believe until we are given something like what Allah’s messengers were given.” Allah knows best where to place His message. The criminals will be struck by humiliation before Allah and a severe punishment because of their scheming.
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who reject revelation because they demand prophetic status or miracles on their own terms. Prophethood is not attained by insistence, social rank, or worldly ambition; Allah alone knows whom to choose for His message. Those who scheme against the truth and refuse it out of pride will ultimately face disgrace and severe punishment before Him.

translation: So whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to leave astray, He makes his heart constricted and distressed, as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse portrays guidance as an inner openness that enables a person to accept Islam with clarity and willingness, while rejection of faith produces spiritual constriction, distress, and resistance to truth. The comparison to ascending into the sky evokes an overwhelming sense of difficulty and suffocation, showing that persistent unbelief leaves the heart burdened by its own refusal to submit. Allah’s decree is not arbitrary: the passage describes the divine consequence of a person turning toward or away from faith, with spiritual impurity settling upon those who continually reject belief.

translation: And this is the straight path of your Lord. We have explained the signs for people who take heed.
interpretation: God’s way is perfectly upright and leads to Him without deviation; its signs have been made clear so that those who reflect may recognize the truth and follow it consciously.

translation: They will have the Abode of Peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector because of what they used to do.
interpretation: Those who live in obedience to Allah are promised a secure, peaceful home in His presence; their good deeds are a means through which Allah grants them His care, guidance, and protection.

translation: And on the Day He gathers them all together, He will say, “O company of jinn, you have led many of mankind astray.” Their allies among mankind will say, “Our Lord, some of us benefited from others, and we have reached the term You appointed for us.” He will say, “The Fire is your dwelling; you shall remain in it forever, except what Allah wills.” Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This depicts the final exposure of the corrupt alliance between rebellious jinn and the humans who followed them: each side found worldly advantage, influence, or gratification through the other, until death brought them before Allah. Their appeal does not excuse them, because they knowingly exchanged divine guidance for mutual benefit. The Fire is designated as their lasting abode, while the exception “except what Allah wills” affirms that Allah’s judgment remains governed entirely by His wisdom and knowledge, beyond any creature’s claim or control.

translation: Thus We cause some wrongdoers to become allies of others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This expresses a law of divine justice: people who persist in wrongdoing are joined to one another and given influence over one another as a consequence of their deeds, so their relationships become part of the punishment and perpetuation of their corruption.

translation: يا معشر الجن والإنس، ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا؟ قالوا: نشهد على أنفسنا. وقد غرّتهم الحياة الدنيا، وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين.
interpretation: يُصوِّر الله يوم القيامة حين يُواجَه الجن والإنس بالحجة التي أقامها عليهم بإرسال الرسل، فلا يجدون عذرًا ولا يستطيعون إنكار تقصيرهم، بل يقرّون بأنفسهم بكفرهم. وكان سبب هلاكهم أن زينة الحياة الدنيا خدعتهم فآثروا متاعها العاجل على الإيمان والاستعداد للقاء الله.

translation: That is because your Lord would never destroy towns unjustly while their people are unaware.
interpretation: Allah’s punishment is not arbitrary or unjust: He does not hold a people accountable until the truth has reached them and they have had the opportunity to understand and respond. Their destruction, when it occurs, follows deliberate wrongdoing after clear warning, not mere ignorance or lack of awareness.

translation: And for all are degrees according to what they have done; and your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: Every person’s standing and recompense are determined with perfect justice by their deeds, whether good or evil, and nothing they do escapes Allah’s knowledge or accountability.

translation: And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can remove you and bring after you whomever He wills, just as He brought you into being from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: Allah is independent of all creation, while His mercy encompasses them. Therefore, people should not feel secure from accountability or assume that their existence and authority are guaranteed: if they persist in disobedience, Allah can replace them with others, just as He brought them forth through earlier generations.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised will surely come to pass, and you cannot escape Allah’s power.
interpretation: Everything Allah has promised—whether reward, punishment, resurrection, or judgment—is certain to occur at its appointed time. No one can thwart His decree or evade His power, so people should respond with faith and obedience rather than denial or false security.

translation: Say, “O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. You will soon know who will have the ultimate outcome of the abode. Surely, the wrongdoers will not prosper.”
interpretation: The verse is a firm warning to those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing: they may continue according to their chosen way, while the Messenger remains steadfast in obedience to Allah. The true measure of success will become clear in the end, when Allah grants the righteous a good outcome and exposes the failure of the wrongdoers.

translation: They assigned to Allah a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock, saying, “This is for Allah”—as they claimed—“and this is for our partners.” Yet what was assigned to their partners did not reach Allah, while what was assigned to Allah reached their partners. Evil is the judgment they make.
interpretation: The verse condemns the pagan practice of dividing offerings between Allah and their alleged deities while treating Allah’s share as available for those deities, but refusing to give their share to Allah. It exposes the contradiction and injustice of assigning partners to Allah and judging according to self-serving desires rather than truth.

translation: And likewise, their partners made the killing of their children seem pleasing to many of the polytheists, in order to ruin them and confuse their religion. Had Allah willed, they would not have done so. So leave them with what they fabricate.
interpretation: The verse condemns how false religious authorities and superstitions can make grave wrongdoing—such as killing children—appear righteous. By attributing this practice to divine religion, the polytheists were led to destruction and had their faith deliberately confused. Allah’s allowing them to act does not mean He approves of their deeds; rather, they are accountable for choosing and inventing this falsehood.

translation: And they say, “These livestock and crops are forbidden; no one may eat them except those whom we permit”—as they claim. And there are livestock whose backs they have declared forbidden, and livestock over which they do not mention Allah’s name, fabricating lies against Him. He will repay them for what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: The verse condemns inventing religious rules without divine authority—declaring certain food or uses of animals lawful only for selected people, forbidding animals from being ridden, and omitting Allah’s name over them—then falsely attributing these customs to Him. It warns that manipulating sacred law for social privilege or superstition is a serious falsehood for which its perpetrators will be held accountable.

translation: They say, “What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. But if it is born dead, then they may all share in it.” He will recompense them for their claims. Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This exposes the baseless religious rules they invented concerning lawful and unlawful food, granting privileges to men while denying them to women and then applying inconsistent exceptions. Such claims cannot establish religious law; God will hold them accountable for attributing false judgments to Him, while His judgment is founded on perfect wisdom and complete knowledge.

translation: Indeed, those who killed their children foolishly, without knowledge, and declared unlawful what Allah had provided for them, fabricating lies against Allah, have truly suffered loss. They have gone astray and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns actions rooted in ignorance and superstition: destroying the lives of one’s children and forbidding God’s lawful provisions while falsely claiming divine authority. Such conduct is a grave loss because it violates God’s gifts and replaces His guidance with human invention.

translation: And He is the One who produced gardens, both trellised and untrellised, and palm trees, and crops of diverse produce, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest. And do not be wasteful; surely He does not love the wasteful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the diversity and abundance of agricultural blessings are gifts from God, not grounds for unrestricted consumption or hoarding. People may benefit from what the earth produces, but they must fulfill the rightful share owed from their harvest—especially to those entitled to support—and must avoid waste, excess, and misuse of resources. Gratitude therefore requires both generosity and moderation.

translation: And among the livestock are those used for carrying burdens and those kept close to the ground. Eat from what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan; indeed, he is your clear enemy.
interpretation: Allah has made livestock a lawful provision and means of benefit, so people should accept His guidance rather than inventing unjustified restrictions or practices concerning them. The warning against Satan’s footsteps teaches that deviation often begins with seemingly small acts of disobedience that gradually lead people away from gratitude and obedience to Allah.

translation: ثمانية أزواج: زوجان من الضأن، وزوجان من المعز. قل: أَهُمَا الذكران حرَّم أم الأنثيان، أم ما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين؟ أخبروني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين.
interpretation: يُبطل الله دعوى المشركين في تحريم بعض الأنعام بغير دليل، ويُلزمهم ببيان أساس هذا التحريم: أهو متعلق بالذكورة أم بالأنوثة أم بما في أرحام الإناث؟ فليس من حقهم أن ينسبوا إلى الله أحكامًا لم ينزل بها علمًا.

translation: And of the camels, two, and of the cattle, two. Say, “Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah instructed you concerning this?” Who, then, is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah in order to lead people astray without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who invented religious restrictions concerning livestock and attributed them to Allah without revelation. By asking whether the prohibition applies to males, females, or what the females carry, it exposes the inconsistency and groundlessness of their claims. True religious law must rest on divine knowledge and proof, not on conjecture or fabricated tradition; those who mislead others by falsely speaking for Allah thereby commit the greatest injustice and turn themselves away from His guidance.

translation: Say, “I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats, except that it be carrion, flowing blood, the flesh of swine—for it is impure—or sinful slaughter dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is compelled, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, then surely your Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that the foods explicitly prohibited in the revelation are carrion, spilled blood, pork, and animals slaughtered in dedication to other than Allah. It also shows that the prohibition is not meant to cause destruction or unbearable hardship: a person facing genuine necessity may eat only what is needed to preserve life, without seeking the forbidden food or exceeding the amount required. Allah’s forgiveness and mercy encompass the one compelled by necessity who observes these limits.

translation: And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry, or what is contained in the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. Thus We recompensed them for their wrongdoing; and surely We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse explains that certain dietary restrictions were imposed upon the Jews as a consequence of their transgression, not because such prohibitions reflected any falsehood or injustice from God. The exceptions clarify that the prohibition concerned particular forms of fat, while God affirms that His judgment and promise are entirely true and just.

translation: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين
interpretation: إذا كذّب المشركون النبيَّ، فعليه أن يذكّرهم بأن رحمة الله واسعة، لكنها ليست إذنًا بالإصرار على الجريمة؛ فمن تمادى في التكذيب والظلم استحقّ بأس الله، ولا يستطيع أحد أن يدفعه عنه.

translation: Those who associate partners with Allah will say, “If Allah had willed, we would not have associated partners with Him, nor would our forefathers, nor would we have forbidden anything.” In the same way, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, “Do you have any knowledge that you can bring forth for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.”
interpretation: The polytheists’ appeal to Allah’s will is a false excuse for their disbelief and self-imposed prohibitions: divine permission for something to occur does not make it morally right or remove human responsibility. If they truly possessed revealed knowledge supporting their claim, they should produce it; instead, their argument rests on speculation, and their persistence in it leads to the consequences that befell earlier deniers.

translation: Say: “To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He willed, He could have guided you all.”
interpretation: Allah possesses the decisive proof against all people, so no one can offer a valid excuse for rejecting the truth. Although He has the power to guide everyone by compulsion, He allows people to choose and holds them accountable for how they respond to His guidance.

translation: Say, “Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this.” If they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs, who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse rejects claims about religious prohibitions that have no genuine revelation as their basis. Even if those who invent such claims present testimony to support them, believers must not endorse it; instead, they must remain faithful to Allah’s revealed guidance and refuse to follow the desires of those who reject divine signs, deny the Hereafter, and attribute equals or partners to Him.

translation: Say, “Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him; and that you show kindness to parents; and that you do not kill your children out of poverty—we provide for you and for them; and that you do not approach immoralities, whether apparent or concealed; and that you do not kill the life that Allah has made sacred, except with due right. This is what He has instructed you, so that you may understand.”
interpretation: This verse establishes a foundational code of moral responsibility: worship must be devoted solely to Allah, parents must be treated with excellence, and the vulnerable—especially children—must not be harmed because of fear of poverty, for provision belongs to Allah. It also commands avoiding every path to sexual and moral corruption, whether public or hidden, and protects human life by forbidding unjust killing. These commands call people to exercise sound understanding by recognizing the sanctity of faith, family, dignity, and life.

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a close relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. This is what He has instructed you, so that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive standard of moral responsibility: protect the vulnerable, conduct transactions honestly, judge and speak impartially, and honor every commitment to Allah. Its command concerning the orphan’s wealth requires not merely avoiding theft, but managing it actively for the orphan’s genuine benefit until he is capable of safeguarding it himself. Justice must prevail even when personal affection or family ties could tempt one to favor someone, while Allah’s covenant gives all these duties their deepest accountability. The mention that no soul is burdened beyond its capacity affirms that these obligations are demanding yet attainable, calling people to practice integrity within the abilities and means Allah has granted them.

translation: And indeed, this is My straight path, so follow it; and do not follow other ways, lest they divert you from His way. This is what He has commanded you, so that you may be mindful of Him.
interpretation: God’s guidance is one clear path grounded in revelation and obedience to Him. A believer must resist competing paths shaped by desires, speculation, or division, because they lead away from divine guidance and weaken spiritual unity. Following the straight path with awareness of God is the means to develop taqwā and remain steadfast.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing Our favor upon the one who did good, and as an explanation of everything, and a guidance and mercy, so that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents the Torah as a complete divine gift to Moses and the Israelites: it affirmed and perfected the path of righteousness, clarified what they needed for faith and conduct, and served as guidance and mercy. Its ultimate purpose was to prepare them to believe with certainty in their return to and meeting with God.

translation: And this is a blessed Book We have sent down, so follow it and be mindful of Allah, so that you may be shown mercy.
interpretation: The verse calls people to treat the Qur’an as a source of divine blessing by following its guidance in belief and conduct, while maintaining reverence and obedience to Allah; such faithful adherence is a means of receiving His mercy.

translation: Lest you should say, “The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, and indeed we were unaware of their study.”
interpretation: This is a warning that no one should excuse their rejection of divine guidance by claiming that revelation was confined to earlier communities whose teachings they did not know. The Qur’an is given to remove that excuse and establish clear guidance accessible to those addressed by it.

translation: Or lest you should say, “Had the Book been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they.” So there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. Who, then, is more unjust than one who denies Allah’s signs and turns away from them? We shall repay those who turn away from Our signs with an evil punishment for their turning away.
interpretation: Allah removes the excuse of those who claim that they would have followed guidance if revelation had come to them. The Qur’an has now arrived as a manifest proof, guidance, and mercy, leaving no valid justification for rejecting it. Persistently turning away from Allah’s signs is a grave injustice, and the punishment promised corresponds to that deliberate rejection and avoidance.

translation: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? On the Day when some of your Lord’s signs come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, nor one that had not earned good through its faith. Say, “Wait, indeed we too are waiting.”
interpretation: This is a warning that faith is meaningful only when freely embraced before the arrival of overwhelming signs that make the unseen undeniable. Once the final manifestation of God’s signs occurs, neither a new profession of faith nor a claim of belief without righteous action will benefit those who previously rejected the truth; therefore, people must respond sincerely before judgment becomes evident.

translation: Indeed, those who divided their religion and became factions—you have nothing to do with them. Their affair rests only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns against turning religion into competing divisions through disputation, partisanship, or abandonment of revealed guidance. The Messenger is absolved of responsibility for such factions, while their judgment is left to Allah, who will hold them fully accountable for their deeds.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will be recompensed only with its equivalent; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: Allah’s justice and generosity are made clear: every good deed is rewarded abundantly, while wrongdoing is requited only in equal measure, with no one receiving less than they deserve or being burdened beyond their guilt.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path—a rightly upright religion, the way of Abraham, inclining wholly toward truth; and he was not among those who associated partners with God.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that true guidance is a clear and balanced way of life rooted in sincere devotion to God alone, following Abraham’s rejection of all forms of idolatry and false association.

translation: Say, “Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are devoted to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: This verse expresses complete devotion to Allah: every act of worship, every aspect of life, and even one’s death are to be directed sincerely toward Him, acknowledging that He alone is the Lord and sovereign over all creation.

translation: He has no partner. This is what I have been commanded, and I am the foremost among those who submit to Him.
interpretation: The speaker declares absolute devotion to God alone, rejecting every form of association with Him, and affirms wholehearted obedience as the defining path of submission.

translation: Say, “Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things? No soul earns anything except against itself, and no burdened soul shall bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that worship and ultimate reliance belong exclusively to Allah, since He alone governs all creation. It also establishes individual moral responsibility: each person bears the consequences of their own choices, not those of another. Final judgment belongs to Allah, who will clarify and judge the disputes in which people differed.

translation: He is the One who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in rank, so that He may test you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and He is certainly Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Human differences in power, wealth, knowledge, and status are not signs of inherent superiority but responsibilities by which people are tested. Those entrusted with greater blessings are accountable for how they use them, while everyone remains subject to God’s justice and may receive His forgiveness and mercy through repentance and righteous conduct.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm, Ṣād.
interpretation: The meanings of these separate letters are ultimately known only to Allah; their opening position signifies the mysterious, divine nature of the revelation that follows.

translation: This is a Book sent down to you, so let there be no distress in your heart because of it—that you may warn by it and remind the believers.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that revelation is a divine responsibility, not a cause for hesitation or inner constraint. He is to convey it courageously as a warning to those who reject truth and as guidance and renewed remembrance for those who believe.

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow protectors besides Him. Little do you take heed.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to make divine revelation their primary guide in faith and conduct, rather than submitting to other authorities, desires, or loyalties that compete with God’s guidance. It also reproaches human heedlessness: despite the clarity of this direction, people often reflect and remember its consequences only rarely.

translation: How many a town We have destroyed; Our punishment came upon it by night or while its people were resting at midday.
interpretation: The verse warns that communities may face divine judgment suddenly, whether in the darkness of night or during apparent security and repose, so worldly comfort must not lead people into heedlessness or persistent wrongdoing.

translation: Their only plea when Our punishment came upon them was: “Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: When divine punishment overtook them, all their arguments and excuses vanished, leaving only the acknowledgment that they had wronged themselves by rejecting the truth; this confession came after the opportunity to change had passed.

translation: We will surely question those to whom the messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will hold both communities and messengers accountable: the communities for how they responded to the divine message, and the messengers for faithfully conveying it. This establishes that no one will be judged without the truth having been made clear and that every responsibility will be examined.

translation: We will surely recount to them with full knowledge, for We were never absent.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will present the realities of people’s deeds and circumstances with perfect knowledge, leaving no matter hidden or misrepresented, because His awareness has never been absent from them at any moment.

translation: And the weighing on that Day is the truth. So those whose scales are heavy—it is they who will prosper.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every person’s deeds will be assessed with perfect justice, and true success will belong to those whose good deeds outweigh their wrongs through sincere faith and righteous conduct.

translation: And those whose scales are light—those are the ones who have lost themselves because they used to wrong Our signs.
interpretation: Those whose deeds lack the weight of sincere faith and righteousness on the Day of Judgment will suffer the greatest loss: they will have squandered their own souls by rejecting, denying, or disregarding the clear signs of God.

translation: Indeed, We have established you on the earth and provided for you therein means of livelihood; yet little are you grateful.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that their ability to live and prosper on earth, along with every means of sustenance, is granted by Him. The verse rebukes their limited gratitude, implying that they should recognize these blessings through sincere thankfulness, obedience, and the proper use of what they have been given.

translation: And We certainly created you, then shaped you, then We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam.” So they prostrated, except Iblīs; he was not among those who prostrated.
interpretation: The verse reminds humankind that its origin and form are entirely by God’s creative power, while the command to prostrate before Adam was a command of honor and obedience to God, not worship of Adam. All the angels submitted, but Iblīs was excluded because of his refusal, revealing that pride and disobedience can nullify one’s claim to superiority.

translation: He said, “What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?” He replied, “I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
interpretation: This exchange reveals that Iblīs’s disobedience arose from arrogant self-comparison: he treated the material of his creation as proof of superiority and rejected God’s command on that basis. The verse teaches that true honor is not determined by origin or physical substance, but by submission to God; pride can turn a perceived distinction into a cause of rebellion.

translation: He said, “Descend from it, for you have no right to be arrogant therein. So go out; indeed, you are among the humbled.”
interpretation: Allah rejects Iblīs because his pride made him refuse obedience. His exalted position could not justify arrogance, and his defiance resulted in expulsion and disgrace, showing that true honor lies in submission to Allah rather than in imagined superiority.

translation: He said, “Grant me respite until the day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: This is the defiant request of Iblīs for continued life until the Resurrection, reflecting his determination to persist in opposing God and misleading humanity.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you are among those granted respite.”
interpretation: Allah granted Iblis a delay until the appointed time, allowing him to persist in his rebellion and temptation as part of the divinely ordained test, not as an indication of approval or honor.

translation: He said, “Since You have led me astray, I will surely lie in wait for them along Your straight path.”
interpretation: Iblīs declares his determination to obstruct human beings from obeying God and following the path of truth, using temptation and deception to divert them from guidance.

translation: “Then I will surely come upon them from before them, from behind them, from their right, and from their left; and You will find most of them ungrateful.”
interpretation: Iblis declares that he will attack human beings from every direction by exploiting their desires, fears, doubts, and distractions, seeking to turn them away from obedience to God. Yet his claim is not that he can compel them, but that he will tempt and mislead them; those who remain mindful and grateful to God are not overcome by him.

translation: He said, “Get out of it, disgraced and banished. Whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with all of you.”
interpretation: Allah declares Satan expelled from His mercy and authority, humiliated and rejected. He also warns that whoever follows Satan in rebellion and misguidance will share his fate in Hell, demonstrating that allegiance to evil leads to accountability and punishment.

translation: And O Adam, dwell—you and your wife—in Paradise, and eat from wherever you both wish; but do not approach this tree, lest you become among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Allah granted Adam and his wife abundant freedom and provision in Paradise while setting one clear boundary as a test of obedience. The prohibition of even approaching the tree teaches that faithfulness includes avoiding the paths that lead toward disobedience, and that wrongdoing begins when a person transgresses the limits established by Allah.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them both, seeking to expose to them what had been concealed from them of their nakedness, and he said, “Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree lest you become angels or become immortal.”
interpretation: Satan approached Adam and Eve through deceptive persuasion, exploiting their desire for a higher state and lasting life. He presented disobedience as a path to elevation and immortality, concealing its true consequence: the loss of their protected state and the exposure of their vulnerability. The verse warns that temptation often disguises itself as sincere advice and promises benefits that are impossible to attain through defying God.

translation: And he swore to them, “Indeed, I am truly one of your sincere advisers.”
interpretation: Iblīs reinforced his deception by making a solemn oath, pretending to seek Adam and Eve’s welfare while concealing his intent to mislead them. The verse warns that false counsel may be presented with confidence and apparent sincerity, so trust must be guided by obedience to God rather than persuasive claims.

translation: So he led them both on by deception. Then, when they tasted of the tree, their nakedness became apparent to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves from the Garden. Their Lord called out to them: “Did I not forbid you both from that tree and tell you that Satan is indeed your manifest enemy?”
interpretation: The verse shows how Satan’s deception led Adam and his wife to disobedience, after which they became conscious of their vulnerability and sought to cover themselves. God’s questioning is a reminder that the command and the warning had already been made clear, teaching that human error often begins by trusting deceptive temptation and that awareness of wrongdoing should lead to recognition of one’s responsibility before God.

translation: They said, “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers.”
interpretation: Adam and his wife acknowledge their disobedience without excuse and turn sincerely to God in repentance. Their words teach that salvation depends on God’s forgiveness and mercy, and that admitting one’s fault with humility is the proper response after sin.

translation: He said, “Descend, some of you enemies to others. On earth you will have a dwelling place and provision for a time.”
interpretation: This decree marks humanity’s earthly life as a temporary arena in which conflict and rivalry may arise, while all people are granted a limited period of residence and provision before returning to God. The warning calls them not to mistake worldly security for permanence or allow enmity to lead them away from obedience.

translation: فيها تحيون، وفيها تموتون، ومنها تُخرجون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الأرض هي موطن الإنسان في حياته الدنيوية، ومحل موته ودفنه، ثم يُبعث منها يوم القيامة ليُحاسب على عمله.

translation: O children of Adam, We have sent down to you garments to cover your private parts and as adornment; but the garment of mindfulness of God is best. That is among the signs of God, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: God reminds humanity that clothing serves both modesty and dignified adornment, but true protection lies in taqwā—an inward awareness of God that restrains wrongdoing and beautifies a person’s character. External dress is valuable, yet it reaches its proper purpose only when accompanied by this spiritual garment.

translation: O children of Adam, do not let Satan deceive you as he caused your parents to leave Paradise, stripping them of their clothing so as to expose their nakedness. Indeed, he and his followers see you from where you do not see them. We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.
interpretation: يحذّر الله بني آدم من الاغترار بوساوس الشيطان، مذكّرًا بأن عداوته قديمة وأن غايته إفساد فطرة الإنسان وكشف عوراته المعنوية والحسية. ولأن الشيطان وأتباعه يراقبون الإنسان من جهة لا يراهم منها، فعليه أن يحتمي بالإيمان والتقوى وألا يمنحهم سلطانًا عليه؛ إذ إن موالاة الشياطين تنشأ من الإعراض عن الإيمان، فيصبح صاحبها مستجيبًا لوساوسهم ومعينًا لهم على نفسه.

translation: وعندما يرتكبون فاحشةً قالوا: وجدنا آباءنا يفعلونها، والله أمرنا بها. قل: إن الله لا يأمر بالفحشاء، أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون؟
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن اتباع عادات الآباء لا يجعلها حقًّا، ولا يجوز نسبة أي معصية إلى أمر الله بغير دليل؛ فالله لا يأمر بالقبيح، ومن ادّعى ذلك فقد تكلّم على الله بجهل.

translation: Say, “My Lord has commanded justice. Direct your faces toward every place of worship, and call upon Him, making the religion sincerely for Him. Just as He brought you into being, you will return.”
interpretation: God commands a life grounded in justice and a worship directed wholly toward Him, free from idolatry and hypocrisy. The reminder that people will return to Him as He first created them calls them to prepare for resurrection by maintaining sincere faith and righteous conduct.

translation: A group He guided, and a group was rightly destined for misguidance. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, while they think they are rightly guided.
interpretation: Guidance is granted to those who turn faithfully toward Allah, whereas those who knowingly follow satanic influences and reject divine truth become subject to misguidance. The verse warns that sincere conviction alone does not prove that one is guided; a person may be deeply mistaken while believing he is following the right path.

translation: O children of Adam, wear your adornment at every place of prayer, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not love those who are excessive.
interpretation: God calls people to approach worship with dignity and proper outward appearance, while also permitting them to enjoy lawful food and drink. This permission is governed by moderation: excess in consumption, extravagance, or heedlessness is blameworthy because it violates the balance and self-discipline that faith requires.

translation: Say, “Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the wholesome provisions?” Say, “They are for those who believe in this worldly life, and will be exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection.” Thus We explain the revelations for people who know.
interpretation: Allah rejects the idea that lawful beauty and wholesome blessings must be renounced in order to be pious. Such blessings may be enjoyed responsibly and gratefully, without extravagance or disobedience. In this world, believers and others may share in them, but in the Hereafter their complete and lasting enjoyment will belong exclusively to those who believed and lived by Allah’s guidance.

translation: Say, “My Lord has only forbidden immoralities—whether apparent or hidden—sin, transgression without right, associating with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and saying about Allah what you do not know.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that the true boundaries of prohibition are determined by Allah, not by human whims. It encompasses every shameful act, whether publicly committed or concealed, all forms of sin and unjust aggression, and especially the gravest wrongs: attributing partners to Allah without evidence and making claims about His religion without knowledge. It therefore calls believers to moral restraint, justice, sincere worship, and great caution when speaking in Allah’s name.

translation: For every nation there is an appointed term; when their term arrives, they can neither delay it for an hour nor bring it forward.
interpretation: Every community and people are subject to a divinely determined period of respite and existence. When that appointed time ends—whether because of persistent injustice, corruption, or the completion of their allotted course—nothing can postpone or hasten the decree of God. The verse calls people to use their time in obedience and reform rather than presume that worldly power can alter the limits set for them.

translation: O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves, recounting My revelations to you, then whoever is mindful of God and sets things right—there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This is a continuing divine summons to humanity: guidance is made accessible through messengers who convey God’s signs clearly, but its benefit depends on responding with reverent awareness of God and righteous reform. Whoever combines inward God-consciousness with outward rectitude is granted freedom from the fear of what lies ahead and the grief of what has passed.

translation: And those who deny Our signs and arrogantly turn away from them—they are the companions of the Fire; they will remain therein forever.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting God’s revealed signs and refusing to submit to their truth out of pride leads to the lasting consequence of Hell, because such arrogance is a deliberate rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their allotted share from the Book, until, when Our messengers come to take their souls, they say, “Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?” They reply, “They have abandoned us,” and they bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse portrays the ultimate consequence of inventing claims about Allah and rejecting His revealed signs: the deniers are allowed to continue until the share of life and provision decreed for them is completed, then death exposes the falsehood of the powers they invoked besides Allah. At that moment, their own admission confirms that their disbelief was a deliberate rejection, leaving them without any excuse or protector.

translation: He will say, “Enter among the nations that passed away before you, from among the jinn and humankind, into the Fire.” Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister-nation. Then, when they have all joined one another therein, the later ones will say to the earlier ones, “Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them twice the punishment of the Fire.” He will say, “For each of you is twice the punishment, but you do not know.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how those who followed misguidance will blame those who preceded and influenced them, while the leaders will not bear the followers’ punishment in their place. Each receives a doubled punishment because the earlier ones misled others and the later ones knowingly followed them; mutual condemnation will offer no escape from accountability.

translation: The first of them will say to the last of them, “You have no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.”
interpretation: Those who followed one another in disbelief will recognize that none can claim exemption or superiority before God; each group shares the consequence of its own chosen actions and cannot shift responsibility to others.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and arrogantly reject them—the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: The verse portrays the impossibility of Paradise for those who knowingly reject God’s signs out of arrogance: just as a camel cannot pass through a needle’s eye, they cannot enter Paradise while persisting in such denial and pride. Their exclusion is a just consequence of their chosen rebellion.

translation: They will have a bed of Hell, and above them coverings of it. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment of those who persist in wrongdoing: Hell surrounds them from below and above, leaving them no refuge or escape. This fitting recompense reflects the consequence of knowingly rejecting truth and violating justice.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—we do not burden any soul beyond its capacity—are the companions of Paradise; they will remain therein forever.
interpretation: Faith expressed through righteous action leads to eternal Paradise, while God’s justice ensures that no person is held responsible for what lies beyond their ability.

translation: And We will remove whatever rancor is in their hearts. Beneath them rivers will flow. They will say, “All praise belongs to Allah, who guided us to this; had Allah not guided us, we would never have found the way. Indeed, the messengers of our Lord brought the truth.” And it will be proclaimed to them, “This is Paradise, which you have inherited because of what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise receiving complete inner purification: every resentment and hostility has been removed, so their joy is undisturbed. They recognize that their arrival there was possible only through Allah’s guidance and the truth conveyed by His messengers, while their righteous deeds were the means by which they became worthy of inheriting Paradise through His mercy.

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire: “We have certainly found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?” They will say, “Yes.” Then a caller will proclaim between them: “The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: This scene reveals the absolute fulfillment of divine promise: the believers openly acknowledge the truth of Allah’s reward, while the people of the Fire are forced to admit the truth of the warning they rejected. The proclamation that follows declares that their deprivation of mercy is the just consequence of their persistent ظلم—wrongdoing expressed through disbelief, rejection of truth, and transgression against Allah’s guidance.

translation: Those who bar others from the way of Allah, seek to make it crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This describes people who do not merely reject divine guidance themselves, but actively hinder others from following it and distort its clear truth to suit their desires. Their rejection of the Hereafter reflects a denial of accountability, allowing them to persist in wrongdoing without fear of judgment.

translation: And between them is a barrier, and on the elevated places are men who recognize each by their marks. They will call out to the inhabitants of Paradise, “Peace be upon you!” They have not yet entered it, though they hope to.
interpretation: The verse portrays the barrier separating the people of Paradise from the people of Hell, with men positioned upon its heights and able to recognize both groups by the signs of their condition. Their greeting to the people of Paradise expresses their awareness of that blessed destiny, while their not yet entering it—despite their hope—conveys a state of awaiting Allah’s judgment and mercy.

translation: And when their eyes are turned toward the inhabitants of the Fire, they say, “Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of the Heights recoiling in fear when they behold the punishment of Hell. Their plea reflects their recognition that salvation depends on being kept apart from those whose injustice and rejection of God led them to ruin.

translation: And the people of the Heights will call out to men they recognize by their marks, saying, “What benefit did your gathering bring you, and what became of the arrogance you used to display?”
interpretation: The verse reveals that worldly power, numbers, and pride cannot protect a person before God; what seemed to be strength and superiority becomes utterly futile when the truth of the Hereafter is exposed.

translation: “Are these the ones whom you swore that Allah would not grant mercy? Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.”
interpretation: يُوبَّخ أهلُ الأعراف على حكمهم المتعجل على الضعفاء من أهل الإيمان، ثم يُظهر الله كرمَه وعدلَه بإدخال أولئك المستضعفين الجنة، ليبيّن أن النجاة والرحمة بيده وحده، وأن ازدراء الناس والحكم على مصائرهم بغير علم غرورٌ باطل.

translation: وسينادي أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة: «أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله». فيقولون: «إن الله حرّمهما على الكافرين».
interpretation: تصوّر الآية مشهدًا من شدة عذاب أهل النار وحاجتهم الملحّة، إذ يطلبون من أهل الجنة شيئًا من الماء أو الطعام، لكنهم يُحرمون منهما جزاءً على كفرهم وإصرارهم على رفض الحق؛ فالنعم التي يتمتع بها أهل الجنة ليست متاحة لمن استحقّ العذاب بكفره.

translation: Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the life of this world deceived—today We will leave them, just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs and used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: The verse warns that treating faith lightly and allowing worldly distractions to make one neglect accountability before God leads, in the Hereafter, to being deprived of His mercy and care. God’s “forgetting” them does not mean literal forgetfulness; it means leaving them to the consequences of their deliberate neglect and denial, just as they disregarded the certainty of meeting Him.

translation: Indeed, We have brought them a Book that We have explained in detail with perfect knowledge—guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s detailed explanations come from divine knowledge and are intended to guide and bring mercy to those who approach it with sincere faith; its benefit is realized by hearts willing to believe and follow its guidance.

translation: Are they waiting for its fulfillment? On the Day its fulfillment comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, “Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. Are there any intercessors for us who may intercede on our behalf, or may we be sent back so that we can do other than what we used to do?” They will have lost themselves, and what they used to invent will have forsaken them.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن حقيقة ما أخبر به القرآن ستنكشف يوم القيامة، وحينئذٍ يعترف المكذبون بأن الرسل جاءوا بالحق، لكن اعترافهم يأتي بعد فوات زمن العمل. فيطلبون شفعاء أو فرصة للرجوع إلى الدنيا لإصلاح أعمالهم، ولا يُجابون؛ لأنهم أضاعوا أنفسهم باتباع الباطل، وتلاشت عنهم الأوهام والأكاذيب التي كانوا يعتمدون عليها.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne.
