interpretation: The verse conveys that the punishment being faced is a just consequence of disbelief and defiance, warning that those who reject the truth will ultimately endure the severe punishment of Hellfire.

translation: O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing against you in battle, do not turn your backs on them.
interpretation: The verse commands believers to remain steadfast when directly confronting an advancing enemy, forbidding cowardly flight that abandons the struggle and weakens the community. It cultivates courage, discipline, and trust in God during the peril of battle.

translation: And whoever turns his back on them on that day—unless maneuvering for battle or joining another group—has certainly incurred the wrath of Allah, and his abode is Hell. What an evil destination!
interpretation: This verse condemns abandoning the battlefield out of fear when steadfastness is required, while recognizing that a strategic withdrawal or regrouping with fellow believers is not cowardice. It teaches that sincere courage includes discipline, loyalty, and purposeful action rather than reckless stubbornness.

translation: It was not you who killed them, but Allah killed them; and it was not you who threw when you threw, but Allah threw, so that He might test the believers with a gracious trial. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the believers’ actions were real, yet their effectiveness and victory came entirely through Allah’s power and support. By attributing the decisive outcome to Allah, it removes pride from the believers and directs their gratitude to Him, while the victory itself becomes a test through which He grants them favor and reveals their faith, obedience, and reliance upon Him.

translation: That is so, and Allah will weaken the schemes of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This affirms that the apparent success of those who oppose the truth is ultimately fragile: Allah can undermine their plans and render their efforts ineffective.

translation: If you seek a decisive judgment, then the judgment has come to you. If you desist, it will be better for you; but if you return, We will return, and your forces will not benefit you at all, even if they are numerous. Indeed, Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: The verse warns those opposing the truth that their demand for a decisive outcome has already been answered through the believers’ victory. They are urged to abandon hostility, because persistence will only bring renewed defeat; numerical strength cannot protect them when Allah supports the believers.

translation: O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you are listening.
interpretation: True faith requires sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger; merely hearing the guidance is not enough if one knowingly turns away from it in practice.

translation: Do not be like those who say, “We hear,” while they do not truly listen.
interpretation: Do not imitate those who claim to accept God’s guidance but refuse to understand it, heed it, or let it transform their actions; true hearing is shown through sincere obedience.

translation: إنَّ شرَّ الدوابِّ عند الله الصُّمُّ البُكمُ الذين لا يعقلون.
interpretation: المقصود بالذمّ ليس أصحابَ الصمم أو البكم الخِلقي، وإنما الذين أُوتوا القدرة على السماع والبيان والتفكّر ثم أعرضوا عن الحق، فكأنهم فقدوا هذه النعم ولم ينتفعوا بعقولهم في معرفة الله واتباع هداه.

translation: Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away, while they were averse.
interpretation: The verse shows that true benefit from revelation depends not merely on hearing words, but on a sincere readiness to accept and follow the truth. Those who persistently reject it would not be transformed by greater exposure; even if they heard clearly, their aversion would lead them to turn away.

translation: O you who believe, respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: True life is found in answering Allah’s guidance and the Messenger’s call with readiness, for faith and obedience awaken the heart and give it lasting purpose. Do not postpone this response, because Allah controls the heart and may place between a person and his intentions the barriers of heedlessness, doubt, or death; ultimately, every person will return to Him for judgment.

translation: وأتقوا فتنةً لا تصيبنَّ الذين ظلموا منكم خاصةً، واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب.
interpretation: يحذّر الله المؤمنين من فتنةٍ عامة تنشأ حين يُترك الظلم بلا إنكار أو إصلاح؛ فلا يقتصر أثرها على الظالمين، بل قد يعمّ المجتمع كله، ولذلك يجب مقاومة أسباب الفساد والقيام بالحق، مع استحضار شدة عقاب الله.

translation: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away; then He gave you shelter, strengthened you with His help, and provided you with good things, so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: God reminds the believers of their former weakness and vulnerability, when they lacked security and feared persecution, then contrasts this with the protection, victory, and provision He granted them. The verse teaches that safety and prosperity are divine favors, requiring grateful recognition of God rather than pride in one’s own strength.

translation: O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor knowingly betray the trusts entrusted to you.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that faith requires loyalty to Allah’s commands and the Messenger’s guidance, as well as honesty in every responsibility placed in their care. Betrayal is not limited to denying faith; it also includes deliberately neglecting obligations, violating covenants, and misusing trusts while knowing that they are duties before Allah.

translation: واعلموا أنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة، وأن الله عنده أجر عظيم.
interpretation: يُنَبِّه الله المؤمنين إلى أن المال والأولاد قد يكونان سببًا للاختبار؛ فقد يدفع حبّهما إلى التقصير في الطاعة أو الظلم أو التعلّق بالدنيا. لذلك ينبغي أن يُحسن الإنسان رعايتهما، وألا يجعلهما مقدَّمين على حق الله، عالمًا بأن الثواب الباقي والعظيم عند الله.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانًا، ويكفّر عنكم سيئاتكم، ويغفر لكم؛ والله ذو الفضل العظيم.
interpretation: يبين الله أن التقوى، وهي مراقبته وطاعته وترك معصيته، تمنح المؤمن بصيرةً يميّز بها بين الحق والباطل، وتكون سببًا لتكفير الذنوب ومغفرتها؛ وكل ذلك فضلٌ عظيم من الله لا يستحقه العبد بقوته، بل برحمة ربه.

translation: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you—to restrain you, kill you, or drive you out—they plotted, but Allah countered their plot; and Allah is the best of those who devise plans.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ by revealing that the conspirators’ schemes against him could never overcome Allah’s decree. Their plot sought to imprison, murder, or expel him, while Allah arranged matters in a way that protected His Messenger and advanced the truth. The verse teaches that human plans remain subject to divine wisdom and that ultimate success belongs to Allah, even when falsehood appears to possess power.

translation: When Our verses are recited to them, they say, “We have heard them. If we wished, we could certainly produce something like this. This is nothing but the tales of former peoples.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the arrogance of those who reject revelation: they acknowledge hearing the Qur’an but dismiss its divine authority, claiming that they could imitate it if they chose. Their statement reveals not a sincere evaluation of its message, but a defiant attempt to reduce divine guidance to invented stories and thereby justify their refusal to follow it.

translation: And when they said, “O Allah, if this is truly the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring upon us a painful punishment.”
interpretation: This expresses the defiant arrogance of those who rejected the truth: instead of sincerely seeking guidance, they challenged God to punish them, revealing their stubborn refusal to believe despite the evidence before them.

translation: Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would He punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse shows that God’s punishment is withheld from a people when they remain under the protection of His Messenger or sincerely turn to Him in repentance and seek His forgiveness; sincere istighfār is therefore a means of protection from divine retribution.

translation: And why should Allah not punish them while they hinder people from the Sacred Mosque and are not its guardians? Its guardians are only those who are mindful of Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that the polytheists were rightful custodians of the Sacred Mosque: by preventing people from worshipping there and opposing its true purpose, they forfeited any honor associated with it. True guardianship belongs not to those who possess authority over the sanctuary, but to those whose faith and obedience reflect reverence for Allah; their ignorance blinds them to this truth.

translation: Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for your disbelief.
interpretation: The verse condemns the worship practices of those who treated the Sacred House with mockery and empty ritual instead of sincere devotion to God; such deliberate rejection of truth makes them deserving of punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to hinder people from the way of Allah. They will spend it, then it will become a source of regret for them, and they will be overcome. Those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell.
interpretation: The verse warns that wealth used to obstruct truth and turn people away from Allah cannot ultimately succeed: it will be exhausted in vain, bring regret to its users, and end in defeat in this world and accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: So that Allah may distinguish the impure from the pure, place the impure together, pile it all up, and cast it into Hell. Those are the losers.
interpretation: Allah separates what is corrupt in belief, intention, and conduct from what is sound and righteous. The corrupt are gathered with those like them until their accumulated evil leads them to punishment, while true loss belongs to those who chose impurity over faith and obedience.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist, they will be forgiven for what has already passed; but if they return, then the precedent of the earlier peoples has already come to pass.
interpretation: God offers those who reject the truth a genuine opportunity to repent: abandoning disbelief and hostility wipes away their former wrongdoing. But returning to opposition after this warning exposes them to the same divine judgment that befell earlier nations who persisted in rejecting God.

translation: Fight them until there is no persecution and religion is wholly devoted to Allah. If they desist, then surely Allah sees all that they do.
interpretation: This verse permits fighting against those who actively persecute and obstruct people because of their faith, with the aim of ending religious oppression—not of forcing belief. If they cease their aggression and persecution, hostilities must end, leaving judgment of their sincerity and deeds to Allah.

translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector. How excellent is the Protector, and how excellent is the Helper.
interpretation: If those who oppose the truth abandon obedience or refuse to support it, the believers should not be shaken, because their ultimate reliance is upon Allah alone. He is the One who safeguards, manages, and supports them, and no ally or helper is better than Him.

translation: And know that whatever spoils you acquire, one fifth belongs to Allah, the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the stranded traveler—if you truly believe in Allah and what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two armies met. And Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the distribution of war gains is not left to personal desire: a designated portion is entrusted for the causes and people named by God, while the remainder is distributed according to the Messenger’s direction. True faith is shown through accepting this divinely ordained discipline and remembering that victory on the Day of Criterion came solely by Allah’s power.

translation: When you were on the nearer side of the valley, while they were on the farther side, and the caravan was below you. Had you made an appointment to meet, you would have disagreed over the appointed time. But Allah decreed a matter that was destined to be fulfilled, so that whoever was to perish would perish upon clear evidence, and whoever was to live would live upon clear evidence. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah arranged the circumstances of the encounter at Badr so that the believers and their opponents met without relying on a prearranged plan, making the truth unmistakably manifest. Thus, the outcome became a decisive proof: those who rejected faith did so knowingly, while those who embraced it did so on the basis of clear evidence; and Allah fully heard their words and knew their intentions.

translation: When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few, and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart and disputed over the matter. But Allah spared you from this. Indeed, He knows well what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: Before the encounter, Allah showed the Prophet ﷺ the opposing army as small in number so that the believers would remain resolute and united. This teaches that Allah may conceal the full scale of a trial from His servants to protect their courage and prevent fear and disagreement, for He knows the inner state of every heart.

translation: And when you met, He showed them to you as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes, so that Allah might bring about a matter already decreed. And to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: At the encounter, Allah caused each side to underestimate the other so that the confrontation would proceed and His decreed outcome would be fulfilled. The verse teaches that events unfold within His wisdom and determination, and that every affair ultimately returns to Him.

translation: O believers, when you confront a force, stand firm and remember Allah often, so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse teaches that believers facing danger or conflict should not be overcome by fear or confusion; they must remain steadfast, keep their hearts connected to Allah through frequent remembrance, and draw from that spiritual strength the courage and discipline needed to act rightly.

translation: And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose courage and your strength depart. Be steadfast; surely Allah is with the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse teaches that obedience to Allah and His Messenger must be accompanied by unity, for destructive quarrelling weakens a community, undermines its resolve, and causes it to lose its power and effectiveness. Patience means remaining disciplined and steadfast through hardship, trusting that Allah’s support is with those who endure faithfully.

translation: And do not be like those who came out of their homes exultantly and to be seen by people, turning others away from the way of Allah. And Allah encompasses all that they do.
interpretation: This warns believers not to act from pride, vanity, or the desire for public admiration, especially when such motives lead them to hinder truth and misguide others. God fully knows their outward actions and the intentions behind them, so no deed or motive escapes His judgment.

translation: And when Satan made their deeds appear attractive to them and said, “No one among humanity can overcome you today, and I am your protector.” But when the two forces came into sight of one another, he turned back on his heels and said, “I have nothing to do with you. I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah.” And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This portrays Satan’s deception: he gives people false confidence and encourages them to rely on apparent strength, then abandons them when the consequences become real. His claim to be their protector is exposed as a lie, while his sudden declaration of fear reflects his awareness of the divine punishment confronting him, not genuine repentance. The verse warns that reliance on Satan and self-assured wrongdoing ultimately ends in betrayal and ruin.

translation: When the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts said, “These people have been deluded by their religion.” But whoever places their trust in Allah—surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse exposes the mistaken judgment of those who regarded the believers’ faith and reliance on Allah as naïveté. True trust in Allah is not self-deception or weakness; it is confidence in the One whose might overcomes every threat and whose wisdom governs every outcome.

translation: If only you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, saying, “Taste the punishment of the blazing Fire.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment of death for those who rejected the truth as one of humiliation and torment: the angels seize their souls harshly and rebuke them for the consequences brought upon themselves by their disbelief and defiance.

translation: That is because of what your hands have sent ahead, and because Allah is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: The consequences people face arise from their own deeds and choices, not from any injustice by Allah; He judges His servants with perfect justice and does not wrong anyone, even in the smallest measure.

translation: Like the conduct of Pharaoh’s people and those before them: they disbelieved in Allah’s signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: Those who persist in rejecting God’s signs and opposing His truth follow the same destructive pattern as earlier nations, and their power cannot protect them from divine judgment; God’s punishment is grounded in perfect strength and justice.

translation: That is because Allah would never change a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah’s blessings are not withdrawn arbitrarily; when a people abandon gratitude, righteousness, and obedience and allow corruption to take root within themselves, they become responsible for the loss of those blessings. Their outward condition is tied to their inward choices, while Allah fully hears their words and knows their intentions and deeds.

translation: Like the practice of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh. All of them were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that persistent rejection of divine guidance, accompanied by wrongdoing, brings about destruction; the fate of Pharaoh’s people is presented as a warning that power and status cannot protect a society from the consequences of its injustice.

translation: Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, for they will not believe.
interpretation: This describes people who knowingly reject the truth and persist in disbelief despite clear evidence and opportunities for faith; by choosing obstinate denial, they forfeit the moral dignity and guidance that distinguish human beings.

translation: Those with whom you made a treaty, yet they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear God.
interpretation: This describes people who repeatedly violate their commitments without reverence for God or moral accountability, showing that their persistent betrayal reveals a settled lack of integrity rather than an isolated lapse.

translation: So if you encounter them in war, deal with them decisively so that those who follow them may take heed.
interpretation: This verse addresses a legitimate wartime situation involving hostile forces: when those who persist in aggression are encountered in battle, they should be decisively defeated in a manner that deters others from following the same path. It is not a general command against people outside the context of war, but a principle of deterrence against continued hostility and betrayal.

translation: And if you fear treachery from a people, then openly terminate the covenant with them on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous.
interpretation: If there are clear signs that a people intend to violate their agreement, do not betray them secretly or respond with concealed treachery. Instead, formally announce that the covenant is ended in a transparent and equal manner, so that both sides are aware of the changed relationship and justice is preserved. Allah condemns treachery, even when dealing with those suspected of it.

translation: Let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped; indeed, they cannot thwart Allah.
interpretation: Those who reject the truth must not imagine that their power, success, or temporary evasion places them beyond divine judgment. No matter how far they advance or avoid accountability, they remain within Allah’s power and cannot prevent His decree or escape its consequences.

translation: And prepare against them whatever strength you are able to muster, including trained warhorses, so that you may deter the enemy of Allah and your enemy, as well as others besides them whom you do not know, but Allah knows. Whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to maintain sufficient strength and readiness to protect the community and deter those who threaten it. The mention of horses refers to the military means of that time, while the broader command to prepare whatever strength is possible applies to every means of defense appropriate to one’s circumstances. Its purpose is deterrence and security, not injustice or aggression; and it reassures those who sacrifice their wealth for a righteous cause that Allah will preserve the full value of their effort and reward them without loss.

translation: And if they incline toward peace, then incline toward it, and place your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: When the opposing side genuinely seeks peace, Muslims should accept the opportunity and respond with a sincere willingness for reconciliation, while relying on Allah rather than fear or suspicion. Allah hears their words and knows the sincerity and intentions behind their actions.

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then surely Allah is sufficient for you. He is the One who strengthened you with His help and with the believers.
interpretation: Do not be distressed by the possibility of betrayal or deceit, for your security and success ultimately rest with Allah. He has already demonstrated His support through divine aid and through the faithful people whom He gathered around you.

translation: And He brought their hearts together. Had you spent all that is on earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that genuine unity and reconciliation among people are ultimately a gift from Allah: material wealth and human efforts alone cannot create lasting harmony when hearts are divided. Allah joins hearts through faith, sincerity, and wisdom, and His power and perfect judgment make such reconciliation possible.

translation: O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for whoever follows you among the believers.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that victory and protection come from Allah, while affirming that the believers who sincerely follow him are likewise under Allah’s sufficiency and support; their strength lies in reliance upon Him and steadfast obedience, not merely in their own numbers or means.

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are one hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: يأمر الله نبيَّه أن يقوّي عزائم المؤمنين عند مواجهة العدو، مبينًا أن الثبات والإيمان والبصيرة قد تمنح القلة قدرةً على غلبة أضعافها، بينما يضعف الكفرُ أصحابه بسبب جهلهم بحقيقة الحق وعواقب الباطل. والآية تحث على الصبر والشجاعة، ولا تبرر العدوان، بل تتعلق بموقف القتال المشروع في سياقه.

translation: Now Allah has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness among you. So if there are one hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are one thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand, by Allah’s permission. And Allah is with those who remain steadfast.
interpretation: This verse shows Allah’s mercy in easing a demanding obligation while preserving the believers’ responsibility to stand firm. Victory is not determined solely by numbers or physical strength, but is granted through steadfastness, reliance on Allah, and His permission; therefore believers should neither be reckless nor despair when facing a stronger opponent.

translation: It is not for a prophet to take captives until he has thoroughly subdued the enemy in the land. You desire the fleeting gains of this worldly life, while Allah desires the Hereafter for you. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse admonishes the believers for prioritizing immediate material benefit—such as ransom from prisoners—before decisively securing the community against its enemies. It teaches that divine guidance requires steadfastly establishing justice and protection first, rather than allowing worldly gain to determine decisions, for Allah’s wisdom aims at the believers’ lasting success in the Hereafter.

translation: Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone forth, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.
interpretation: Allah reminds the believers that taking ransom from the captives before fully overcoming the enemy was a serious matter; yet His prior decree of mercy and allowance concerning the spoils spared them from the punishment that their action could otherwise have brought.

translation: So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and wholesome, and be mindful of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah permits the believers to benefit from lawful spoils, but this permission must be accompanied by reverence for Him and obedience to His limits. Their lawful provision is a mercy, while their mistakes and excesses may be forgiven when they return sincerely to Allah.

translation: O Prophet, say to those captives in your possession: “If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will grant you better than what has been taken from you, and He will forgive you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse opens the door of hope for those who have been overcome or taken captive: sincere faith, repentance, and genuine goodness within the heart can transform their loss into a greater gift from Allah, both in this life and through forgiveness in the Hereafter. It teaches that a person’s future with Allah is not determined solely by past opposition or present weakness, but by the truthfulness of the goodness Allah knows within them.

translation: And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: If those who have entered into an agreement with the believers secretly plan treachery, their earlier rejection and violation of God’s commands have already exposed their disloyalty; therefore, God may cause their schemes to fail and place them under the believers’ authority. This should inspire vigilance without doubt that God’s knowledge and wisdom govern the outcome.

translation: Indeed, those who believed, emigrated, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave them shelter and support—they are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of alliance toward them until they emigrate. Yet if they seek your help in matters of faith, then you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse establishes that faith creates a bond of mutual loyalty and responsibility, especially among those who sacrificed and supported one another for its sake. It also distinguishes between spiritual solidarity and the practical obligations of the community: believers who remained behind were not included in the same protective alliance until they joined the believing society, but their right to religious assistance remained. Such assistance must, however, respect existing treaties, showing that defending faith does not permit betrayal or injustice toward those bound by covenant.

translation: Those who disbelieve are allies of one another. Unless you act likewise, there will be persecution in the land and great corruption.
interpretation: This verse teaches that believers must stand by and support one another in faith, loyalty, and mutual protection; otherwise hostile forces may dominate, causing oppression, confusion, and widespread moral and social فساد.

translation: And those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the way of Allah, and those who give refuge and support—those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: True faith is demonstrated through sincere belief joined with sacrifice, perseverance, and practical solidarity: some leave behind what is familiar and strive for Allah’s cause, while others welcome, protect, and support them. Such actions reveal the truthfulness of their faith, and Allah responds to that sincerity with forgiveness and an honored, abundant provision.

translation: And those who believed afterward, emigrated, and strove alongside you—they are among you. And blood relatives are closer to one another, according to the Book of Allah. Surely Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: The verse affirms that later believers who share in faith, migration, and striving belong fully to the believing community, while establishing that kinship also carries rights and precedence in matters such as inheritance and family responsibility, as determined by Allah’s revealed law. All such relationships and judgments fall within Allah’s complete knowledge.

translation: A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty.
interpretation: This verse publicly announces that Allah and His Messenger are withdrawing protection and treaty obligations from the polytheists concerned, signaling the end of the former covenant and a decisive change in relations with those who opposed or violated it.

translation: So travel freely through the land for four months, and know that you cannot frustrate Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a declaration granting those polytheists who had violated their agreements a limited period of security—four months—in which they could move through the land and reconsider their position. The respite was not evidence of weakness or escape from divine judgment; Allah’s decree would inevitably overtake them, and persistent disbelief and treachery would ultimately lead to their humiliation.

translation: And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to all people on the day of the Greatest Pilgrimage: Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation toward the polytheists. So if you repent, that is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you can never escape Allah. And give those who disbelieve the news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse publicly declares the end of the covenantal protection of those polytheists who had violated their commitments, making clear that their continued defiance would not weaken Allah’s authority or thwart His judgment. At the same time, it leaves the door of repentance open: abandoning polytheism and turning sincerely to Allah is the better path, while persistent rejection brings a certain and painful consequence.

translation: Except those among the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, who have not failed you in anything and have not supported anyone against you: so fulfill your treaty with them until its term. Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: This verse establishes that treaties must be honored faithfully when the other party has upheld its obligations and has not aided aggression. Justice and piety require Muslims to respect the agreed duration rather than betray or prematurely violate a covenant.

translation: When the sacred months have passed, then fight the polytheists wherever you encounter them; seize them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakāh, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hostile polytheists who had violated their covenants and waged war against the Muslims, after the period of protection granted to them had ended. Its command is therefore not a general license to attack all non-Muslims, but a directive concerning those in a state of active treaty-breaking aggression; if they cease hostility and enter the Muslim community through repentance, prayer, and zakāh, they are to be released and treated with mercy.

translation: And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah; then convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse commands that even an opponent who seeks refuge must be given security and allowed to hear the message without coercion; afterward, he must be escorted safely to a place where he is secure. It reflects justice, compassion, and the obligation to remove ignorance through clear communication rather than punishment or compulsion.

translation: كيف يكون للمشركين عهدٌ عند الله وعند رسوله، إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام؟ فما داموا مستقيمين على عهدهم لكم فاستقيموا لهم؛ إن الله يحب المتقين.
interpretation: لا يستحق المشركون عهدًا مع الله ورسوله إذا نقضوا المواثيق وأظهروا الخيانة، أما من حافظ منهم على عهده ولم يخلّ به، فعلى المسلمين أن يلتزموا تجاهه بالوفاء والعدل، لأن التقوى تقتضي مقابلة الأمانة بالأمانة وعدم تجاوز حدود الله.

translation: كيف يكون لهم عهدٌ، وهم إن يظفروا بكم لا يراعوا فيكم قرابةً ولا عهدًا؟ يرضونكم بكلامهم، وتأبى قلوبهم الوفاء، وأكثرهم خارجون عن الطاعة.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الثقة لا تُبنى على الكلام المعسول، بل على صدق العهد وثبات القلب عليه؛ فهؤلاء يُظهرون الودّ ما دام ذلك يوافق مصالحهم، لكنهم إذا قدروا على المؤمنين لم يراعوا بينهم قرابةً ولا ميثاقًا، ولذلك يُحذَّر من الاغترار بأقوال من عُرف بالغدر ونقض العهود.

translation: They have traded Allah’s revelations for a small price and turned people away from His path. Truly evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: They have knowingly abandoned and misused divine guidance for temporary worldly gain, thereby obstructing others from faith and obedience; such conduct is condemned because it sacrifices eternal truth for a worthless benefit.

translation: They observe neither kinship nor treaty with a believer; and they are the transgressors.
interpretation: Those who oppose faith are described as having no regard for the bonds of family, loyalty, or solemn covenant when dealing with believers; by violating these moral obligations and exceeding rightful limits, they reveal themselves to be aggressors.

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakāt, then they are your brothers in faith. We explain the verses in detail for people who know.
interpretation: This verse establishes that sincere repentance is demonstrated through a renewed commitment to worship and social responsibility. When people turn back to God, uphold prayer, and fulfill the duty of zakāt, they are to be recognized as full members of the believing community, with the rights and bonds of religious brotherhood; judgment of their faith should not remain fixed upon their past conduct.

translation: And if they break their oaths after their treaty and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no binding oaths, so that they may desist.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who, after entering a covenant, deliberately violate it and actively attack the Muslim community’s faith and security. It permits resistance against the leadership directing such aggression, not indiscriminate violence against all unbelievers, and presents fighting as a means of stopping treaty-breaking oppression and deterring further hostility.

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths, sought to expel the Messenger, and initiated hostilities against you the first time? Do you fear them, when God is more deserving of your fear, if you are believers?
interpretation: This verse rebukes the believers for hesitating before those who had violated their covenants and begun aggression. It calls them to place obedience to God and moral courage above fear of hostile opponents; the command is directed at this treacherous, attacking group in its specific context, not at people merely because they belong to another faith.

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, grant you victory over them, and heal the hearts of believing people.
interpretation: This is a command to confront those who persist in aggression and hostility toward the believers, assuring that victory and the weakening of oppression occur by Allah’s permission. The verse also acknowledges the believers’ pain and promises them relief, dignity, and renewed confidence through the defeat of their persecutors.

translation: And He will remove the anger from their hearts. Allah turns in mercy to whomever He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This assures believers that divine help will heal the pain and resentment caused by oppression, while repentance and forgiveness remain subject to Allah’s perfect knowledge and wisdom.

translation: أم حسبتم أن تُتركوا دون اختبار، ولما يُظهر الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين بطانةً أو أولياء؟ والله خبير بما تعملون.
interpretation: يُنبّه الله المؤمنين إلى أن الإيمان لا يثبت بمجرد الدعوى، بل يظهر عند الابتلاء والعمل والتضحية؛ فلابد أن تتكشف حقيقة من يجاهد في سبيل الحق، ويحفظ ولاءه لله ورسوله وجماعة المؤمنين، ولا يجعل لأهل العداء أو النفاق موضعَ ثقةٍ سرية في شؤونه. والله محيط بدقائق أعمالهم ونواياهم، فلا يخفى عليه صدقهم ولا تقصيرهم.

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while bearing witness against themselves to disbelief. Their deeds have come to nothing, and in the Fire they will remain forever.
interpretation: The verse declares that those who reject faith cannot claim the religious standing of guardians and true caretakers of Allah’s mosques, because the outward act of maintaining them has no spiritual value when it is joined with disbelief. Their deeds are rendered fruitless by that rejection, and their persistence in it leads to everlasting punishment.

translation: The mosques of Allah are maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakat, and fear none but Allah. It is those who may be among the rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the true honor of caring for Allah’s mosques is not measured merely by building or managing them, but by sincere faith and righteous conduct. Those who uphold prayer, fulfill their duty of zakat, and place their ultimate fear and reverence in Allah alone are the ones whose service to the mosque reflects genuine guidance.

translation: Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to faith in Allah and the Last Day and striving in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that outward religious services, however valuable, cannot be equated with sincere faith and wholehearted sacrifice for Allah’s cause. Acts such as serving pilgrims and caring for the Sacred Mosque attain their true worth when grounded in belief and obedience; status or public service alone does not establish spiritual excellence before Allah. Persisting in assigning equal merit to deeds while neglecting faith is a form of injustice that bars a person from divine guidance.

translation: Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank before Allah. It is they who are the successful.
interpretation: True success before Allah is attained through sincere faith demonstrated by sacrifice: leaving behind what obstructs obedience and dedicating one’s possessions, efforts, and life to His cause. Such commitment gives believers a higher spiritual rank and leads to lasting success.

translation: Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him, approval, and gardens in which they will have lasting bliss.
interpretation: This promise conveys that true faith and devoted striving lead to the greatest forms of divine reward: God’s mercy, His complete acceptance, and an everlasting life of joy that never fades.

translation: They will abide therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: The reward promised by Allah is everlasting, not temporary or subject to loss, and its true greatness comes from being granted by Him and enduring forever.

translation: O believers, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief to faith. Whoever among you takes them as allies—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith must take precedence over family loyalty when relatives openly choose disbelief and oppose the believers. It does not command abandoning kindness or just treatment toward them; rather, it forbids giving them allegiance, support, or precedence in a way that compromises one’s faith and commitment to God.

translation: Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose decline you fear, and the homes in which you take pleasure are dearer to you than Allah, His Messenger, and striving in His path, then wait until Allah brings about His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse establishes that love of Allah and commitment to His Messenger and His cause must take precedence over family ties, possessions, economic interests, and worldly comfort. It does not condemn these blessings themselves; rather, it warns against allowing attachment to them to override obedience, sacrifice, and devotion to God. Whoever knowingly places worldly concerns above this loyalty exposes himself to divine judgment and forfeits the guidance granted to those who remain faithful.

translation: Allah has certainly supported you in many places—and on the Day of Ḥunayn—when your numbers pleased you, but they availed you nothing, and the earth, vast as it is, became constricted for you; then you turned back, retreating.
interpretation: The verse teaches that victory does not come from numerical strength or worldly advantages, but from reliance upon Allah. At Ḥunayn, the believers’ confidence in their large number exposed the weakness of depending on means rather than on Allah, so their initial setback served as a correction of pride and a reminder that true security and success belong to Him alone.

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the believers, and sent down forces you could not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: When fear and confusion arose, Allah strengthened the Messenger and the believers with inner calm and unseen support, enabling truth to prevail despite the apparent weakness of its followers. Those who persisted in rejecting and opposing the truth were punished, showing that ultimate victory belongs to faith and that defiance of Allah has a fitting consequence.

translation: Then Allah will turn in mercy to whomever He wills after that. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Even after severe trials and consequences, the door of repentance remains open: Allah may restore those who sincerely return to Him, for His forgiveness and mercy are greater than their sins.

translation: O you who believe, indeed the polytheists are impure, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to prevent those who persist in associating partners with Allah from entering the Sacred Mosque, describing their impurity as a spiritual and religious condition arising from shirk rather than as physical dirt. It reassures the believers not to fear the economic effects of this restriction, for Allah can provide for them from His bounty according to His knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Fight those among the People of the Scripture who do not truly believe in God and the Last Day, who do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not follow the religion of truth, until they pay the jizyah directly and accept political submission.
interpretation: This verse is understood as addressing the Muslim polity’s armed conflict with hostile or defiant scriptural communities in its historical context, while establishing jizyah as the payment through which those communities could remain under Muslim rule rather than be compelled to convert. It is therefore a regulation of state-level warfare and political subordination, not a license for individuals to attack non-Muslims or an endorsement of indiscriminate violence.

translation: The Jews say, “Ezra is the son of Allah,” and the Christians say, “The Messiah is the son of Allah.” That is merely what they say with their mouths; they imitate the claim of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah condemn them—how are they turned away from the truth?
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing divine sonship to any human being, clarifying that such claims are unsupported assertions spoken without true knowledge and reflect the continuation of earlier forms of associating partners with Allah. Its closing expression condemns the distortion of pure monotheism and points to the baffling way people can be led away from the truth despite its clarity.

translation: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Glory be to Him above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse condemns treating religious authorities or the Messiah as possessing a share in divine authority—especially by obeying them when they alter what Allah has made lawful or unlawful—instead of submitting exclusively to Allah. True devotion requires recognizing that all ultimate authority and worship belong to Him alone, free from every form of association.

translation: They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: They seek to undermine the truth of divine guidance through denial, distortion, and hostile speech, but Allah guarantees its completion and triumph. Their opposition cannot diminish the truth or prevent its spread, regardless of how strongly they resent it.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may make it prevail over every religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: God sent the Messenger ﷺ with clear guidance and the true way of worship, promising that its truth and evidence would ultimately prevail over all competing systems, despite the opposition and hostility of those who reject monotheism.

translation: O believers, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume people’s wealth unjustly and turn them away from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah—give them news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns religious figures who exploit people’s wealth and obstruct them from divine guidance, and it warns all who treat wealth as something to hoard rather than a trust to be used responsibly for Allah’s cause and the welfare of others. Its warning concerns corrupt use of religious authority and the selfish accumulation of wealth, not the mere possession of lawful property; what is condemned is withholding wealth from its obligations and refusing to spend it rightly.

translation: On the Day when it is heated in the Fire of Hell and their foreheads, sides, and backs are branded with it: “This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.”
interpretation: The verse warns that wealth becomes a source of punishment when people selfishly accumulate it, withhold its obligatory rights, and neglect those in need. On the Day of Judgment, the very wealth they prized will be used to expose the consequences of their greed and refusal to spend it righteously.

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months, in the decree of Allah, from the day He created the heavens and the earth; four of them are sacred. That is the upright religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight the polytheists all together, just as they fight you all together, and know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the ordering and sanctity of time are matters determined by Allah, not by human alteration. The four sacred months are to be honored by restraining wrongdoing and aggression, while the command to fight concerns confronting those who collectively wage hostility, not initiating injustice. Thus, true religious integrity requires reverence for Allah’s limits, justice even in conflict, and steadfast awareness that divine support belongs to those who remain mindful of Him.

translation: Indeed, postponing the sacred months is an increase in disbelief. Through it, those who disbelieve are led astray: they permit it one year and prohibit it another, so that they may match the number of months Allah has made sacred, thereby making lawful what Allah has forbidden. Their evil deeds have been made appealing to them, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse condemns manipulating Allah’s sacred calendar to serve worldly interests while preserving only the outward count of sacred months. Such deliberate alteration turns obedience into a deceptive formality: what Allah has forbidden is treated as permissible, and divine commands are reshaped according to desire. The warning is that persistent justification of wrongdoing can make evil appear attractive and distance a person from guidance.

translation: O you who believe, what is the matter with you that, when you are told, “Go forth in the way of Allah,” you cling heavily to the earth? Are you content with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? Yet the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared with the Hereafter, is but little.
interpretation: The verse reproaches believers for allowing attachment to comfort, possessions, and worldly security to weaken their readiness to obey Allah and sacrifice for His cause. It reminds them that choosing temporary worldly ease over the lasting reward of the Hereafter is a profound misjudgment, since whatever this life offers is insignificant in comparison with the eternal life to come.

translation: إن لم تنفروا يغذّبكم عذابًا أليمًا، ويستبدل قومًا غيركم، ولن تضرّوه شيئًا؛ والله على كل شيء قدير.
interpretation: يحذّر الله المؤمنين من التخلّف عن نصرة الحق حين تتعيّن عليهم، فترك واجبهم يعرّضهم لعقوبة مؤلمة، وقد يرفع عنهم شرف القيام به ويستبدل بهم قومًا أصدق طاعة وأشد استعدادًا. أما تقصيرهم فلا ينقص من ملك الله ولا يضرّه، لأنه سبحانه مستغنٍ عن خلقه وقادر على كل شيء.

translation: If you do not support him, Allah has already supported him: when those who disbelieved expelled him as one of two, when the two were in the cave, and he said to his companion, “Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us.” Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him, strengthened him with forces you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is supreme. Allah is Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: The verse reminds believers that the success of the Messenger does not depend on their support, for Allah Himself protects and aids His chosen messenger even in the most vulnerable circumstances. During the migration, when the Prophet and his companion were hidden in the cave and pursued by those who sought to eliminate the message, the Prophet’s reassurance, “Allah is with us,” expressed complete trust in divine protection. Allah granted tranquility, provided unseen aid, and ultimately caused the disbelievers’ scheme and authority to fall beneath the truth. The verse therefore teaches that divine support may appear through both visible and unseen means, and that Allah’s wisdom and power ensure the ultimate elevation of His word over falsehood.

translation: Go forth, whether lightly equipped or heavily burdened, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: Believers are urged not to let comfort, hardship, age, possessions, or personal circumstances prevent them from fulfilling their duty to Allah. They should offer whatever resources and effort they are able to give in His cause, trusting that sincere obedience and sacrifice are ultimately better for them than holding back.

translation: Had it been an immediate gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you; but the distance seemed too far for them. They will swear by Allah, “If only we had been able, we would have gone out with you.” They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are surely liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who claimed inability to join the Messenger ﷺ only because the expedition was difficult and offered no obvious worldly benefit. Their false oath cannot conceal that they chose comfort over obedience; by persisting in deceit and evasion, they bring spiritual ruin upon themselves, while Allah fully knows the truth of their motives.

translation: May Allah pardon you! Why did you give them permission before it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?
interpretation: This is a gentle divine reproach of the Prophet ﷺ for allowing certain people to remain behind without first testing the sincerity of their excuses. It teaches that decisions affecting a shared moral responsibility should not be made hastily, but should allow truthfulness and hypocrisy to become evident.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask you for permission to remain behind from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah knows those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: Sincere faith produces readiness to sacrifice for what is right; therefore, the truly God-conscious do not seek excuses to avoid their duty when sacrifice is required. Allah knows the sincerity of those who step forward and the motives of those who hold back.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission, and whose hearts are filled with doubt; so they waver in their doubt.
interpretation: This verse exposes that their requests for exemption were not rooted in a genuine excuse but in the weakness of faith and uncertainty within their hearts. Because they lacked conviction in Allah and accountability in the Hereafter, they remained hesitant and unable to commit themselves to obedience.

translation: Had they intended to go forth, they would have made preparations for it. But Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said to them, “Remain with those who stay behind.”
interpretation: Their failure to prepare revealed that their claim of willingness was not sincere. Allah therefore allowed their reluctance to prevail, withholding from them the resolve to join the believers, because their departure would have brought harm through hypocrisy and discord. The verse warns that sincere intention is demonstrated by preparation and action, whereas persistent reluctance can become a condition in which a person is left behind by divine judgment.

translation: Had they gone forth with you, they would have added nothing to you but confusion, and they would have hastened among you, seeking to sow discord among you; and among you are those who listen to them. Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the harm of hypocritical companions: their presence in a righteous cause would not strengthen it but would spread disorder, exploit divisions, and undermine resolve. Their danger is increased by those within the community who are receptive to their words, yet Allah fully knows the motives and wrongdoing of all involved.

translation: They had already sought to spread discord before, and they turned matters against you until the truth came and Allah’s decree became manifest, though they disliked it.
interpretation: This verse exposes the persistent efforts of the hypocrites to undermine the believers and disrupt the Prophet’s mission. Their schemes and manipulation could not prevent the truth from prevailing, for Allah brings His decree to fulfillment despite the opposition of those who resent it.

translation: Among them are those who say, “Permit me to stay behind and do not expose me to temptation.” Surely, they have already fallen into temptation. Indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers.
interpretation: These hypocrites presented their fear of temptation as a reason to avoid the believers’ struggle, while their refusal itself revealed the deeper trial of hypocrisy, cowardice, and disobedience. Their supposed effort to protect themselves from wrongdoing had already led them into it, and their persistent rejection of faith leaves them surrounded by the consequence of Hell.

translation: If something good befalls you, it grieves them; but if a calamity befalls you, they say, “We took our precautions beforehand,” and they turn away, rejoicing.
interpretation: The verse portrays the hypocrisy of those whose hostility is exposed by their reaction to the believers’ circumstances: they are distressed by the believers’ success, pleased by their hardship, and use apparent prudence as an excuse to justify distancing themselves. It thus reveals that true loyalty is measured by sincere concern and steadfast support, not by claims of caution made after the event.

translation: Say, “Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.”
interpretation: This teaches believers to face every circumstance with confidence in Allah’s wisdom and care: whatever reaches them occurs within His decree, and true reliance on Him frees them from fear of people or events while still calling them to remain steadfast and responsible.

translation: Say, “Are you waiting for anything to befall us except one of the two best outcomes? Yet we are waiting for Allah to afflict you with a punishment from Him or through our hands. So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you.”
interpretation: The believers remain confident because whatever Allah decrees for them is ultimately good: either victory and success or martyrdom with its reward. In contrast, those who oppose the truth face the possibility of punishment from Allah directly or through the believers, so their apparent expectation of harm for the believers cannot undermine their certainty or resolve.

translation: Say, “Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people.”
interpretation: Their spending has no spiritual value because it is not offered with sincere faith and obedience to Allah; whether they give gladly or under compulsion, their persistent hypocrisy and disobedience prevent it from being accepted.

translation: Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger; they do not come to prayer except lazily, nor do they spend except reluctantly.
interpretation: Their outward acts of worship and charity have no spiritual worth because they are not founded on sincere faith. They approach prayer without eagerness and give only under inner resistance, revealing that their deeds are driven by compulsion or appearance rather than genuine devotion to Allah.

translation: So let neither their wealth nor their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through these in the life of this world, and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse warns against judging a person’s favor with God by outward prosperity. For those who persist in hypocrisy and disbelief, wealth and children become a means of punishment rather than blessing: they preoccupy the heart, expose them to anxiety and loss, and deepen their attachment to the worldly life until death comes while faith has not been embraced.

translation: They swear by Allah that they are truly among you, but they are not among you; rather, they are a people who are afraid.
interpretation: Their claim of belonging to the believers is merely a protective oath, not a reflection of sincere faith. Their fear of exposure and consequences drives them to conceal their true allegiance and pretend to share the community’s identity.

translation: Had they found a refuge, caves, or a passage, they would have turned toward it, rushing headlong.
interpretation: This portrays the hypocrites’ intense aversion to the believers: if any escape or hiding place were available, they would hasten toward it without hesitation, revealing that their presence among the believers is reluctant and insincere.

translation: Among them are those who criticize you concerning the charitable offerings: if they are given some of them, they are pleased; but if they are not given any of them, they are suddenly resentful.
interpretation: This condemns those who judge the Prophet’s fairness by whether they receive a personal share of charity, revealing that their concern is not justice or the welfare of the needy but their own worldly benefit. It teaches that resentment over not receiving what one desires exposes a lack of sincerity and trust in God’s wisdom and in the rightful distribution of resources.

translation: If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them, and said, “Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will grant us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger. Indeed, to Allah we turn with hope.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that true contentment lies in accepting what is allotted through Allah’s guidance and His Messenger’s distribution, while trusting that provision and generosity come from Allah. A believer should not be consumed by resentment over worldly shares, but should place hope in Allah, seek His favor, and remain confident in His wisdom and bounty.

translation: Indeed, charitable alms are only for the poor, the needy, those appointed to administer them, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, for freeing those in bondage, those burdened by debt, in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveler—an obligation prescribed by Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that obligatory alms are not to be distributed according to personal preference, but entrusted to the specific categories whose needs and circumstances Allah knows best: the poor and needy, those administering the alms, people whose reconciliation serves the good of faith and community, the liberation of those in bondage, debtors unable to repay, legitimate causes in Allah’s way, and travelers cut off from their resources. By ending with His knowledge and wisdom, Allah teaches that this allocation is a divinely ordered system of social mercy, justice, and responsible stewardship.

translation: Among them are those who offend the Prophet and say, “He is all ears.” Say, “He is an ear of goodness for you: he believes in Allah and trusts the believers, and is a mercy to those among you who believe.” Those who offend Allah’s Messenger will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who maliciously portray the Prophet’s attentive listening and compassionate acceptance of people’s words as gullibility. His readiness to listen is instead a virtue: he listens with faith, discernment, and concern for the believers. Thus, harming or disparaging Allah’s Messenger is a grave offense deserving painful punishment.

translation: They swear by Allah to you in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more deserving that they please Him, if they are believers.
interpretation: Their oaths are meant to win human approval, but true faith requires seeking Allah’s pleasure above the approval of people and aligning one’s conduct with the guidance brought by His Messenger.

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately resisting Allah and rejecting the authority of His Messenger leads to everlasting punishment; such defiance is the ultimate humiliation and loss, regardless of any worldly status or justification.

translation: The hypocrites fear that a surah may be revealed concerning them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, “Go on mocking; indeed, Allah will bring to light what you fear.”
interpretation: The verse warns that hypocrisy cannot remain concealed from Allah: revelation may expose the motives and inner corruption that people try to hide. Their mockery does not protect them; rather, it shows their defiance, while Allah is fully capable of uncovering the truth they fear.

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, “We were only engaging in idle talk and joking.” Say, “Was it Allah, His revelations, and His Messenger that you were mocking?”
interpretation: This verse makes clear that treating Allah, His revelations, or His Messenger with ridicule is not excused as mere humor or amusement. Such mockery reveals profound disrespect toward the sacred and requires sincere repentance rather than dismissal as harmless speech.

translation: لا تعتذروا، فقد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم. إن نعفُ عن طائفةٍ منكم نُعذِّب طائفةً لأنهم كانوا مجرمين.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الاعتذار لا يمحو جريمة الاستهزاء بالدين بعد الإيمان، لأن هذا القول يكشف عن كفرٍ يناقض حقيقة الإيمان. ومع ذلك، فالحكم ليس واحدًا على الجميع؛ فمن صدقت توبته واستحق العفو عُفي عنه، ومن أصرّ على سخريته وجرمه استحق العذاب، إذ يُحاسَب كل إنسان بحسب صدقه وتوبته وموقفه من الحق.

translation: The hypocritical men and hypocritical women are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong, forbid what is right, and withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse portrays hypocrisy as a shared moral character in which men and women support one another in rejecting truth: they promote wrongdoing, obstruct righteousness, and withhold their wealth and help from what is good. Their deliberate neglect of Allah results in being deprived of His mercy, guidance, and care; thus their hypocrisy is not merely a hidden attitude but a persistent rebellion that places them among the gravely disobedient.

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and women and the disbelievers the Fire of Hell, where they will remain forever. It is sufficient for them. Allah has cursed them, and they will have an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse declares that hypocrisy and disbelief, when maintained without repentance, lead to everlasting punishment because they represent a deliberate rejection of faith and moral truth. The Fire is described as their sufficient recompense, while Allah’s curse signifies their exclusion from His mercy; their enduring punishment reflects the permanence of their chosen state and its consequences.

translation: Like those before you, they were stronger than you in power and greater in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, and you have enjoyed your share, just as those before you enjoyed their share; and you have indulged in vain discourse as they indulged. Their deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter, and it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that material strength, wealth, and descendants are not signs of divine approval. Those who become absorbed in worldly pleasure, follow desires, and engage in false or futile pursuits—imitating earlier peoples—may cause their apparently good deeds to lose their spiritual value. True success depends not on worldly advantages, but on sincere obedience and accountability before God.

translation: Has the account not reached them of those who came before them: the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Abraham, the inhabitants of Midian, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, so Allah would never wrong them; rather, they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: The verse warns that the destruction of earlier peoples was not arbitrary or unjust: they were given clear guidance through messengers, but rejected it and brought the consequences upon themselves. Their history is therefore a lesson that divine punishment follows persistent wrongdoing, not oppression by Allah.

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another: they enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those—Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse teaches that faith creates a bond of mutual care and responsibility between believing men and women. Their loyalty is shown not merely by affection, but by helping one another uphold what is right, resist wrongdoing, maintain prayer, give zakat, and remain obedient to Allah and His Messenger. Because they actively support righteousness and fulfill their duties, they become deserving of Allah’s mercy, which is granted with perfect power and wisdom.

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever, and pure, pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of perpetual residence. Yet the pleasure of Allah is greater. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the reward of sincere faith is everlasting security, joy, and honor in Paradise, but the greatest gift is Allah’s acceptance and pleasure, which surpasses every created blessing. True success is therefore not merely attaining comfort or beautiful dwellings, but being received by Allah with His approval.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Their abode is Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: This is a command to the Prophet ﷺ to confront opposition to the faith with unwavering determination: confronting open hostility through the appropriate struggle, and confronting hypocrisy through truth, admonition, and firm accountability. The command to be firm does not permit injustice or transgression; it calls for resolute adherence to truth while warning that persistent rejection and hypocrisy lead to the punishment of Hell.

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say it, yet they certainly uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their submission, and they resolved to do what they could not accomplish. They resented nothing except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of people who deny their hostile words while their conduct reveals rejection and plans against the believers. Their resentment toward the Prophet and the community, despite the benefits and security they received through Allah’s grace, shows the corruption of ingratitude and hypocrisy. Yet the door of repentance remains open: sincere return to Allah would restore them, whereas persistent defiance leaves them without protection from the consequences of their choices in this life and the next.

translation: Among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: “If He grants us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and will surely be among the righteous.”
interpretation: This verse portrays people who condition their devotion and righteousness on receiving worldly blessings, revealing that a sincere covenant with Allah requires gratitude and obedience when His favor arrives, not merely promises made in hope of personal gain.

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, withdrawing.
interpretation: The verse censures those who, after receiving the blessing they had hoped for, abandon their promises and refuse to fulfill their obligations, revealing that their gratitude and devotion were not sincere.

translation: So He caused hypocrisy to take root in their hearts until the day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to Allah and because they used to lie.
interpretation: Their repeated breach of a solemn commitment and habitual falsehood corrupted their inner faith, leaving hypocrisy as a lasting consequence until the Day of Judgment.

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private conversations, and that Allah is the Knower of all unseen things?
interpretation: The verse warns that no concealed intention, whispered discussion, or hidden matter escapes Allah’s knowledge; therefore, a person must fear Him inwardly and outwardly, knowing that what is hidden will not remain hidden from His judgment.

translation: Those who criticize the believers who give generously in charity, and ridicule those who can find nothing but their utmost effort to give—Allah will turn their ridicule back upon them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the injustice of mocking people for their charity, whether their contribution is abundant or limited. Sincere generosity is measured by devotion and sacrifice, not by the amount given; those who belittle others’ efforts expose their own arrogance and will face the consequence of being disgraced for the very contempt they showed.

translation: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them—even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse declares that repeated prayer for forgiveness cannot benefit those who knowingly persist in disbelief and rebellion against Allah and His Messenger; the mention of seventy times emphasizes that no amount of intercession can overcome their deliberate rejection, while guidance and forgiveness remain connected to sincere faith and repentance.

translation: Those who stayed behind rejoiced at their remaining behind, contrary to the Messenger of Allah, and they disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. They said, “Do not march out in the heat.” Say, “The fire of Hell is far hotter,” if only they understood.
interpretation: The verse censures those who preferred comfort and worldly ease over sincere obedience, using the hardship of heat as an excuse to avoid supporting the Messenger and striving for God’s cause. It reveals that such excuses expose a failure to recognize the lasting consequences of one’s choices: temporary discomfort is insignificant compared with the punishment of Hell. True understanding would lead a person to endure righteous hardship rather than sacrifice eternal well-being for immediate comfort.

translation: So let them laugh a little and weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This is a warning that the fleeting amusement of those who disobey and evade their duty will lead to lasting regret and sorrow; their grief is the consequence of their own deliberate deeds.

translation: So if Allah brings you back to a group of them, and they ask your permission to go forth, say: “You shall never go forth with me, nor shall you ever fight an enemy alongside me. You were content to remain behind the first time, so remain behind with those who stay behind.”
interpretation: This verse declares that those who deliberately chose comfort and stayed behind when sacrifice was required cannot later claim the privilege of joining the believers in struggle. Their earlier contentment with abandoning duty exposed their insincerity, so they are told to remain apart with those who habitually hold back.

translation: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand by his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse forbids the Prophet ﷺ from performing the funeral prayer for, or seeking forgiveness at the burial of, those who knowingly persisted in hypocrisy and disbelief until death. Their outward association with the believers did not change their rejection of faith, so they were not to receive this particular form of communal honor and supplication.

translation: فلا تُعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم؛ إنما يريد الله أن يعذّبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا، وتزهق أرواحهم وهم كافرون.
interpretation: المقصود أن كثرة المال والولد ليست دليلًا على رضا الله ولا على سعادة أصحابها؛ فإذا خلت من الإيمان صارت سببًا للابتلاء والشقاء، بما تجرّه من هموم وتكاليف وتعلّق بالدنيا، ثم تكون خاتمتهم أن يموتوا على الكفر.

translation: And when a surah was revealed, saying, “Believe in Allah and strive alongside His Messenger,” those among them who possessed means asked your permission, saying, “Leave us to remain with those who stay behind.”
