interpretation: The verse exposes the reluctance of those who had the ability and resources to support the Messenger but preferred comfort and safety over obedience and sacrifice. Their request to remain behind reveals that true faith requires sincere willingness to act, not merely verbal belief when commitment becomes difficult.

translation: They were content to remain with those who stayed behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This describes people who preferred comfort and avoidance of responsibility over joining the believers in a necessary struggle. Their repeated refusal hardened their hearts, leaving them unable to recognize the truth or understand the consequences of their choice.

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. It is they who will have all that is good, and it is they who are successful.
interpretation: True faith is shown through sincere sacrifice: believers devote their wealth, strength, and lives to supporting the truth and serving God. Because they place obedience above comfort and personal gain, they are promised every form of good and the lasting success that comes from God’s pleasure.

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: This portrays the lasting reward Allah has prepared for those who are faithful and devoted to Him: an eternal life of peace and blessing, showing that true success lies not in temporary worldly gains but in attaining Allah’s everlasting approval.

translation: And those of the Bedouins who offered excuses came to seek permission, while those who denied Allah and His Messenger remained behind. A painful punishment will afflict those among them who disbelieved.
interpretation: The verse distinguishes between people who presented their excuses and sought permission to stay behind, and those who deliberately remained behind while rejecting Allah and His Messenger. It warns that mere outward excuses do not protect a person from accountability: those whose refusal is rooted in disbelief will face a painful punishment.

translation: There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find what they can spend, provided that they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause for reproach against those who do good; and Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse removes blame from those who are genuinely unable to participate or contribute because of weakness, illness, or poverty, as long as their hearts remain sincere and their intentions support Allah’s cause and His Messenger. It establishes that divine accountability is tied to a person’s capacity and sincerity, not to what lies beyond their means, while affirming that those who act with excellence and integrity have no valid basis for condemnation and may hope in Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Nor is there any blame upon those who came to you so that you could provide them with mounts, and you said, “I cannot find anything on which to carry you.” They turned away with their eyes overflowing with tears, grieving that they could not find anything to spend.
interpretation: This verse shows that God does not blame sincere believers who are prevented from striving by genuine lack of means. Their deep sorrow at being unable to participate and contribute reveals the sincerity of their faith, even though they possess no material resources.

translation: The reproach is only against those who ask your permission to stay behind while they are wealthy. They were content to remain with those who stayed behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not understand.
interpretation: Blame falls on those who had the means and ability to join the believers yet deliberately sought exemption, preferring ease and safety over duty. Their willing attachment to comfort hardened their hearts, leaving them unable to recognize the seriousness of their choice or the truth they were neglecting.

translation: They will offer you excuses when you return to them. Say, “Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs. Allah and His Messenger will see your deeds; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
interpretation: This verse exposes the futility of deceptive excuses after disobedience: claims are not accepted when conduct has already revealed the truth. Sincere repentance is demonstrated through changed deeds, while every action remains known to Allah and will be fully disclosed on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them so that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed, they are impure, and their refuge will be Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse exposes the insincere excuses of those who stayed behind and sought to avoid accountability through oaths. Believers are instructed not to be drawn into trusting or honoring such hypocrisy, but to distance themselves from it, because persistent deceit and disobedience corrupt a person and lead to punishment.

translation: They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. Yet if you are pleased with them, surely Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse warns that hypocrites may use solemn oaths to win the believers’ approval, but human satisfaction must not be granted at the expense of truth. Their outward pleas cannot conceal their persistent disobedience, and Allah’s displeasure with such conduct remains even if people are persuaded to accept their excuses.

translation: The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse identifies a spiritual vulnerability found among certain desert tribes: their isolation from the Prophet’s community and limited access to revelation made them more prone to disbelief, hypocrisy, and ignorance of Islam’s legal and moral boundaries. It is a warning that distance from sound knowledge and guidance can foster these qualities, not a condemnation of every individual Bedouin; Allah alone fully knows people’s inner states and judges with perfect wisdom.

translation: Among the desert Arabs are those who regard what they spend as a loss and await misfortunes to befall you. Upon them will be the evil turn of fortune. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This describes people whose outward support is driven by obligation rather than sincere faith: they see charitable spending as a burdensome loss and secretly hope that hardship will strike the believers. Their hostile intentions and resentment will return upon them as disgrace and misfortune, for God hears their words and knows the reality of their hearts.

translation: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and regard what they spend as means of drawing near to Allah and as the prayers of the Messenger. Surely, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that sincere faith is shown by treating one’s charitable spending as an act of devotion that brings one closer to Allah and by valuing the Messenger’s supplication for them. Such giving, when joined with genuine belief, becomes a cause of spiritual nearness and inclusion in Allah’s mercy, while His forgiveness and mercy remain the source of their acceptance.

translation: And the foremost among the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: The verse establishes the lasting virtue of the earliest sincere believers who migrated and supported the Messenger, as well as those who faithfully follow their example. Their mutual contentment with Allah reflects the highest fulfillment of faith, rewarded by eternal Paradise; true success is therefore found in sincere devotion and steadfastly following the path of righteousness.

translation: And among the Bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina are those who are entrenched in hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that hypocrisy may be deeply concealed within a community, even among those who outwardly belong to it, and that its hidden reality is fully known to God. The “two punishments” are understood as successive forms of punishment in this world—such as exposure, distress, or defeat—and in the grave, before the final punishment in the Hereafter; it emphasizes that persistent, deliberate hypocrisy brings consequences before the ultimate judgment.

translation: And others have acknowledged their sins: they have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in mercy. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse portrays sincere repentance as the path for those who have fallen into sin while still possessing faith and good deeds. Their acknowledgment of wrongdoing is itself a sign of sincerity, and they are called to hope in Allah’s forgiveness and mercy rather than persist in denial or despair. Their repentance must be genuine, expressed through abandoning the sin and returning to obedience, for Allah forgives those who turn to Him sincerely.

translation: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a source of reassurance for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that giving charity sincerely purifies the believer from the moral stains of wealth and selfishness, while the Prophet’s prayer for those who give brings them reassurance and acceptance. Allah hears their words and knows the sincerity behind their repentance and giving.

translation: Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and receives charitable offerings, and that Allah is the Ever-Relenting, Most Merciful?
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that sincere repentance and charity are accepted by Allah: repentance erases the servant’s return to disobedience, while charity is honored and received despite Allah being free of all need. His repeated acceptance of repentance and His mercy should inspire believers to return to Him without despair and to give generously with sincerity.

translation: And say, “Act, for Allah will see your deeds, as will His Messenger and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
interpretation: This verse commands people to act sincerely and righteously, knowing that their deeds are not hidden: Allah fully knows them, and their effects may become evident to His Messenger and the believers. Ultimately, everyone will return to Allah, who will reveal and judge the reality of all their actions.

translation: And others are deferred until Allah’s command: either He will punish them or turn to them in mercy. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This refers to people whose case is left pending by divine judgment: they are neither declared forgiven nor condemned, because their ultimate outcome rests entirely with Allah. He knows the sincerity, repentance, and deeds hidden within them, and He will decide their fate with perfect wisdom and justice.

translation: And those who took a mosque for harm, disbelief, division among the believers, and as a station for whoever had previously fought Allah and His Messenger—they will surely swear, “We intended nothing but good.” And Allah bears witness that they are truly liars.
interpretation: This verse warns that a religious institution or outwardly pious act is not righteous merely because it bears a sacred appearance; when it is established to cause harm, spread division, or support opposition to truth, its claimed good intention is exposed as deception. True worship must be founded on sincerity, unity, and loyalty to Allah’s guidance.

translation: Do not ever stand in it. A mosque founded upon reverence for God from the very first day is more worthy for you to stand in. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse teaches that a place of worship is honored not merely by its form, but by the sincerity and righteousness upon which it is founded. Worship should not support a setting established to cause harm, division, or opposition to truth; rather, believers should gather where devotion to God and inner and outward purification are upheld. Such sincere purity is beloved by God.

translation: Is one who founded his building upon mindfulness of Allah and His pleasure better, or one who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling cliff, which then collapsed with him into the Fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that deeds and institutions are judged by the foundations on which they are established: what is built upon sincere devotion to Allah and the pursuit of His approval is sound and worthy, while what is built upon hypocrisy, harm, or disobedience is unstable and ultimately destroys those who rely on it. True guidance is therefore withheld from those who persist in ظلم—placing things away from their rightful purpose and opposing the truth.

translation: The building they built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts, unless their hearts are torn apart. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: The hypocrites’ deceptive foundation will keep their hearts burdened with doubt and inner turmoil until their lives end or their hearts are completely broken; Allah fully knows their hidden intentions and judges with perfect wisdom.

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him, stated in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in the bargain you have made; that is the supreme success.
interpretation: Allah presents the believers’ wholehearted devotion as a covenant: they entrust their lives and possessions to Him, using them in obedience and in support of His cause, while He guarantees them Paradise. The promise is affirmed across the revealed scriptures, emphasizing its certainty and continuity. Their joy should arise not from worldly gain or conflict itself, but from knowing that sincere sacrifice for Allah is never lost and that His promise is more trustworthy than any agreement.

translation: Those who repent, worship, praise Allah, fast, bow, prostrate, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and guard the limits set by Allah—and give glad tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse portrays true faith as a life of continual return to Allah, devoted worship, gratitude, disciplined self-restraint, humble submission, moral responsibility, and respect for divine boundaries. Such qualities together mark sincere believers who are worthy of Allah’s promised glad tidings.

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they are close relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: Once the truth of a person’s persistent rejection of faith and their fate in the Hereafter has become clear, believers may not ask God to forgive that person’s disbelief, regardless of family ties. The verse teaches that loyalty to God’s truth takes precedence over kinship, while also indicating that seeking forgiveness is prohibited only after the person’s final rejection has been established—not while there remains hope that they may believe or repent.

translation: Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disavowed him. Indeed, Abraham was deeply compassionate and forbearing.
interpretation: Abraham initially sought forgiveness for his father in fulfillment of a personal promise, while hoping for his guidance. Once his persistent opposition to Allah became unmistakable, Abraham withdrew from him and ceased seeking forgiveness on his behalf. The verse shows that compassion and patience are noble qualities, but loyalty to Allah takes precedence when a person knowingly persists in hostility toward Him.

translation: Allah would never lead a people astray after guiding them until He has made clear to them what they must avoid. Surely Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: Allah’s justice means that He does not hold people accountable for abandoning guidance until the matters they must avoid have been clearly explained to them. Any deviation that follows such clarification arises from their own choice, while Allah’s complete knowledge encompasses their circumstances, intentions, and actions.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have, besides Allah, no protector and no helper.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute authority over all creation, including life and death. Therefore, no one can truly protect or support a person apart from Him, and reliance and obedience should be directed to Him alone.

translation: Allah has indeed turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Emigrants, and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of some of them had nearly wavered; then He turned to them in mercy. Surely, He is Most Kind and Most Merciful to them.
interpretation: This verse portrays divine mercy accompanying sincere believers through severe trial: although the hardship of the expedition brought some hearts close to hesitation, their commitment to follow the Prophet endured, and Allah accepted their repentance and strengthened them. It teaches that temporary weakness under overwhelming difficulty does not bar a person from Allah’s mercy when it is met with renewed sincerity, obedience, and perseverance.

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until the earth, vast as it is, became constricted for them, and their own souls became constricted, and they realized that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Surely Allah is the Ever-Relenting, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This describes the three believers who failed to join the expedition and were then separated from the community until their sincere remorse became overwhelming. Their distress shows that true repentance involves recognizing that no escape from guilt or its consequences is possible except by returning to Allah. When their repentance became genuine, Allah accepted them and restored them through His mercy, demonstrating that divine forgiveness is open to those who turn back sincerely.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and be among the truthful.
interpretation: This command calls believers to make awareness of Allah the foundation of their conduct and to remain in the company of people whose faith is reflected in sincere words, trustworthy actions, and steadfast obedience. Truthfulness here is not merely speaking accurately; it is integrity before Allah, consistency between one’s inner state and outward behavior, and loyalty to what is right even when it is difficult.

translation: It was not fitting for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind the Messenger of Allah, nor to prefer their own lives to his. That is because no thirst, hardship, or hunger afflicts them in the way of Allah, nor do they take a step that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any victory over an enemy, except that a righteous deed is recorded for them by it. Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere commitment to the Messenger requires believers to share in the sacrifices and hardships of the cause of truth rather than placing their own comfort and safety above it. Every difficulty endured, effort made, and benefit gained against opposition is known to Allah and recorded as a rewarded good deed, so no act of faithful service is wasted.

translation: Nor do they spend any amount, small or great, nor cross any valley, except that it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: Every sincere sacrifice made in obedience to Allah—even an apparently minor expense or effort—is known and preserved by Him. His reward is not limited to the outward size of the deed; by His grace, He rewards His servants in accordance with the finest of their righteous actions.

translation: The believers should not all go forth together. So why does not a group from each community go forth to gain a deeper understanding of the religion, and then warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?
interpretation: This verse establishes a balance between communal responsibilities: while some believers undertake necessary duties, others must devote themselves to acquiring sound religious understanding and then teach and warn their community. Religious knowledge is therefore a communal trust whose purpose is to guide people toward mindful obedience and protect them from error.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، قاتلوا من الكافرين الذين يجاورونكم ويهددونكم، وليجدوا فيكم حزمًا وقوة، واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين.
interpretation: توجّه الآية المؤمنين، في سياق الصراع والقتال، إلى مواجهة المعتدين الأقرب خطرًا عليهم بحزم وثبات، لا بظلم أو تجاوز. فالقوة المطلوبة هي قوة منضبطة بالتقوى والعدل، ولذلك تختم الآية بالتنبيه إلى أن معية الله تكون لمن يراقبه ويلتزم حدوده حتى في حال الحرب.

translation: وعندما تُنزَّل سورة، يقول بعضهم: «أيُّكم زادته هذه إيمانًا؟» فأما الذين آمنوا فتزيدهم إيمانًا، وهم يفرحون ويستبشرون.
interpretation: تكشف الآية أن أثر الوحي يختلف باختلاف حال القلب؛ فالمؤمنون يتلقّون السورة بالتصديق والتدبر، فيزداد يقينهم وثباتهم وفرحهم بطاعة الله، بينما يكشف سؤال المنافقين عن شكّهم واستخفافهم بما ينزل من الهدى.

translation: As for those whose hearts are diseased, it only increased them in impurity upon their impurity, and they died as disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine revelation does not benefit a person who approaches it with hypocrisy, denial, or persistent inner doubt; instead, such a person’s rejection causes further moral and spiritual corruption until they die in disbelief.

translation: Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year, yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed?
interpretation: The verse censures those who repeatedly encounter trials, warnings, and circumstances that should awaken their conscience, yet remain unchanged. Such recurring tests are opportunities to return to God and learn from what happens; refusing repentance and reflection reveals a heart becoming hardened through persistent heedlessness.

translation: And whenever a sūrah is revealed, they look at one another, asking, “Does anyone see you?” Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse portrays the hypocrites’ unease when revelation exposes their condition: they exchange furtive looks, hoping to leave unnoticed rather than listen and respond sincerely. Their turning away becomes a fitting consequence of their persistent refusal to understand and accept divine guidance; by choosing neglect, they are deprived of the receptiveness of heart that would lead them to faith.

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; your suffering is deeply distressing to him, he is deeply concerned for you, and toward the believers he is gentle and merciful.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that His Messenger ﷺ is one of them, understanding their condition and genuinely caring about their guidance and well-being. His distress over their hardship and his mercy toward believers express the sincerity of his mission: he does not seek their submission for personal gain, but desires that they be guided, protected from error, and granted success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: So if they turn away, say, “Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god but Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
interpretation: If people reject the truth or turn away from your message, remain steadfast and entrust your affair to Allah alone. He is fully sufficient as a protector and support, because He possesses absolute authority over creation; reliance upon Him gives the believer strength and peace despite others’ rejection.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Rā. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The opening letters draw attention to the miraculous nature of the Qur’an: although it is composed of the familiar letters of human speech, no one can produce anything comparable to it. Its verses are described as belonging to the Wise Book because they come from Allah and convey perfect wisdom, sound guidance, and truth.

translation: Is it astonishing to the people that We revealed to a man among them: “Warn the people and give good news to those who believe that they have a position of true honor with their Lord”? The disbelievers said, “Indeed, this is clearly a magician.”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who find revelation strange merely because it came through a human messenger. A prophet’s humanity does not diminish the divine origin of his message; rather, it makes his warning understandable and applicable to people. Those who respond with faith are promised an honored and firmly established reward with God, while those who reject the message dismiss it as sorcery instead of considering its truth.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. He directs every affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not take heed?
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s absolute authority over creation and all affairs. Since no one can intercede except by His permission, worship belongs to Him alone, and recognizing His sovereignty should awaken people to faith, obedience, and sincere devotion.

translation: To Him is your return, all together. Allah’s promise is true. Indeed, He originates creation and then brings it back, so that He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice. As for those who disbelieve, for them is a drink of boiling fluid and a painful punishment because they persisted in disbelief.
interpretation: The verse establishes resurrection as a certain and just return to Allah: the One who created humanity initially is fully able to recreate it. On that Day, faith expressed through righteous action will receive a fitting and equitable reward, while deliberate rejection of the truth will result in painful recompense, corresponding to the disbelief by which people turned away from Allah.

translation: He is the One who made the sun a radiant light and the moon a reflected light, and determined for it phases so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning of time. Allah did not create all this except with truth and purpose. He explains the signs for people who have knowledge.
interpretation: The ordered alternation of the sun’s radiance and the moon’s phases is a deliberate sign of Allah’s wisdom and power, providing humanity with a precise means of measuring time and organizing life. Its purposeful design calls those who understand to recognize that creation is neither random nor without meaning, and to respond with faith in its Creator.

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of night and day, and in all that Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for people who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: The continual succession of night and day and the order found throughout creation point to Allah’s wisdom, power, and sustaining authority. Those who are conscious of Him recognize these signs and respond with faith, gratitude, and obedience.

translation: Indeed, those who do not hope for Our meeting, are content with the life of this world and find reassurance in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs—
interpretation: This describes people whose hearts are confined to worldly life: they neither anticipate accountability before God nor seek the lasting life beyond it. Their contentment with the temporary world makes them neglect the signs that should awaken faith, reflection, and obedience.

translation: Those are the ones whose abode is the Fire because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: Their punishment is a just consequence of their persistent deeds and choices; the verse warns that a person’s actions can lead them away from mercy and make the Fire their final abode.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord will guide them through their faith. Rivers will flow beneath them in the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الإيمان الصادق، حين يظهر في العمل الصالح، يكون سببًا لهداية الله لعباده وتثبيتهم وإيصالهم إلى طريق النجاة؛ فبقدر ما يصدقون في إيمانهم ويستقيمون في أعمالهم ينالون نعيم الجنة وطمأنينتها.

translation: Their prayer therein will be, “Glory be to You, O Allah,” and their greeting therein will be, “Peace.” And the conclusion of their prayer will be, “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise as living in a state of continual purity, peace, and gratitude: they glorify Allah, exchange greetings of peace, and recognize that every blessing they enjoy ultimately comes from Him, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation.

translation: And if Allah were to hasten evil upon people as they hasten good, their term would surely be decreed for them. But We leave those who do not hope to meet Us wandering blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: Allah does not immediately bring about every harmful consequence people impulsively call for, just as He does not instantly grant every benefit they desire. His restraint is a mercy and a period of respite, allowing them to turn back; yet those who deny accountability and persist in wrongdoing are left to wander confused within their rebellion.

translation: And when affliction touches a person, he calls upon Us while lying on his side, sitting, or standing. But when We remove his affliction, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us concerning an affliction that touched him. Thus the deeds of the transgressors have been made appealing to them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the human tendency to turn urgently and sincerely to God in times of hardship, seeking Him in every condition, yet to become heedless once relief arrives and return to former ways as though no prayer had been made. It warns that persistent excess in wrongdoing can so distort a person’s judgment that such neglect and ingratitude appear acceptable to him.

translation: And We certainly destroyed the generations before you when they acted unjustly, even though their messengers came to them with clear proofs; yet they would not believe. Thus do We recompense the guilty people.
interpretation: This verse warns that persistent wrongdoing, especially the rejection of clear divine guidance after it has been presented, leads to ruin. The fate of earlier peoples demonstrates that God’s judgment is just: destruction came not from a lack of evidence, but from their deliberate refusal to believe and reform.

translation: Then We made you successors on the earth after them, so that We may see how you will act.
interpretation: Allah granted later generations authority and responsibility on earth after those who came before them, testing how they would use that trust—whether with obedience, justice, and gratitude, or with disobedience and corruption.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, “Bring us a Qur’an other than this, or change it.” Say, “It is not for me to change it on my own. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear—if I were to disobey my Lord—the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
interpretation: The verse shows that the Qur’an is not subject to human demands or alteration. The Messenger’s role is to convey revelation faithfully, not to reshape it to satisfy those who reject accountability before God. His refusal demonstrates that divine guidance is determined by God alone, and that even the Messenger is bound by obedience to Him and warned against changing or withholding what has been revealed.

translation: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به ۖ فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله ۚ أفلا تعقلون
interpretation: قل: لو أراد الله ألا أنزل هذا القرآن، لما تلوته عليكم ولما عرّفكم به. وقد عشت بينكم زمناً طويلاً قبل نزوله، تعرفون صدقي وأني لم أكن أقرأ كتاباً أو أتعلم هذا الكلام من أحد؛ أفلا تستدلون بذلك على أن القرآن وحي من الله لا افتراء مني؟

translation: Who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah or denies His signs? Surely, the criminals will never prosper.
interpretation: No one is more profoundly wrong than a person who knowingly attributes falsehood to Allah or rejects the clear evidence of His revelation. Such wrongdoing cuts a person off from true success, because persistence in falsehood and denial ultimately leads to failure and loss.

translation: They worship, besides Allah, what can neither harm them nor benefit them, and they say, “These are our intercessors with Allah.” Say, “Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on earth?” Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse condemns directing worship to beings that possess no power to cause harm or bring benefit, while inventing for them a role as mediators before Allah. Its question is a forceful denial: no intercessor has any authority unless Allah Himself grants it, so claiming otherwise is attributing to Allah a partner and a supposed divine arrangement that He has not revealed. Allah is far above such associations.

translation: Humanity was but one community, then they differed. Had it not been for a decree that had already gone forth from your Lord, judgment would have been made between them concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: People originally shared a common unity, but they later became divided in belief and conduct. God has allowed them time rather than bringing an immediate final judgment, in accordance with His prior decree; the ultimate resolution of their disagreements therefore belongs to Him.

translation: And they say, “Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The unseen belongs only to Allah, so wait; indeed, I am with you among those waiting.”
interpretation: Their demand for a particular miracle does not challenge the truth of revelation, because knowledge of the unseen and the timing of signs belong exclusively to Allah. The Prophet is therefore instructed to remain firm and let the truth become evident in its appointed time, while those who reject it await the consequences of their choice.

translation: And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they plot against Our signs. Say, “Allah is swifter in countering their plots.” Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme.
interpretation: The verse exposes the ingratitude of those who, after being relieved from hardship, respond not with gratitude but with opposition and attempts to undermine the truth of Allah’s signs. Their schemes are neither hidden nor beyond Allah’s power: His just response overtakes them swiftly, while the angels faithfully record every act and intention for which they will be held accountable.

translation: He is the One who enables you to travel through land and sea. Then, when you are aboard ships and they sail with them by a pleasant wind, and they rejoice in it, a storm wind strikes them, and the waves come upon them from every direction, and they realize that they are surrounded. They call upon Allah, sincerely devoting their worship to Him: “If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the human tendency to turn sincerely to Allah when all worldly means fail and danger becomes overwhelming, even if that sincerity is later abandoned when safety returns. It teaches that genuine devotion should not be limited to moments of crisis: the One who alone can rescue a person in hardship is also the One who grants security and blessings in ease, and therefore deserves constant worship and gratitude.

translation: But when He saves them, they immediately transgress throughout the land without right. O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves—a fleeting enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: When people are rescued from danger, they often forget the One who saved them and return to wrongdoing. Yet their injustice harms no one but themselves, yielding only temporary worldly benefit while leading to accountability before God, who will fully disclose and judge their deeds.

translation: The example of worldly life is like water We send down from the sky, with which the vegetation of the earth becomes luxuriant—some of it eaten by people and animals. Then, when the earth has taken on its adornment and become beautiful, and its people think they have full power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We reduce it to a stubble field, as though it had not flourished the day before. Thus We explain the signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: Worldly prosperity may appear complete, secure, and entirely under human control, yet it is fragile and can vanish suddenly by God’s decree. The verse calls people not to be deceived by temporary beauty and abundance, but to reflect on their transience and turn their hearts toward what endures with God.

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whoever He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah calls people toward Paradise, the realm of lasting security and well-being, and grants guidance to those who turn to Him, leading them along the upright way that reaches it.

translation: For those who do good is the finest reward—and more besides. Neither gloom nor humiliation will overcome their faces. They are the companions of Paradise; they will remain there forever.
interpretation: Those who sincerely believe and live righteously will receive Paradise and, beyond its blessings, an additional gift of nearness to and vision of Allah. Their joy and honor will be complete, untouched by the sorrow, darkness, or disgrace that afflicts those who reject the truth.

translation: And those who commit evil deeds—the recompense of an evil deed is one equivalent to it. Humiliation will overwhelm them; they will have no protector against Allah. It will be as though their faces were covered with pieces of a dark night. They are the companions of the Fire, remaining there forever.
interpretation: This verse portrays the just consequence of persistent wrongdoing: it is met with no more than its due measure, yet its disgrace becomes overwhelming because the sinners have rejected the protection and mercy of Allah. The darkness covering their faces symbolizes the exposure of their inner state—deprivation of light, honor, and hope—while their abiding in the Fire signifies the final fate of those who die in disbelief and remain opposed to Allah.

translation: And on the Day We gather them all, We will say to those who associated partners with Allah, “Stay where you are—you and your partners.” Then We will separate them from one another, and their partners will say, “You did not worship us.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the false bond between the idolaters and the beings or objects they worshipped will be completely broken. The alleged partners will disown their worshippers, revealing that the worshippers’ attachment was based on illusion and that those they invoked had neither accepted nor deserved their worship.

translation: So Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you: indeed, we were unaware of your worship.
interpretation: The objects of worship will disown those who worshipped them, declaring that they had no awareness of or consent to that worship. Allah alone will stand as the perfectly sufficient witness, exposing the falsehood of associating partners with Him.

translation: There, every soul will experience what it sent forth before, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master; and whatever they used to invent will have deserted them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each person will confront the real consequences of their deeds. They will return to Allah alone, the true Lord and disposer of their affairs, while the false beliefs, claims, and objects of devotion they had fabricated will prove powerless and disappear from them.

translation: Say, “Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Who controls hearing and sight? Who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who governs all affairs?” They will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: This verse confronts people with realities they themselves recognize: provision, the faculties of hearing and sight, the cycles of life and death, and the ordering of the universe all lie under Allah’s control. Their acknowledgment that Allah is the One behind these matters exposes the inconsistency of worshipping anything besides Him. True awareness of His absolute authority should lead them to reverent obedience, avoiding whatever displeases Him rather than merely admitting His existence.

translation: That, then, is Allah—your true Lord. So what is there after the truth except error? How, then, are you turned away?
interpretation: Allah alone is the true Lord, and once the truth has become clear, turning away from Him can only lead into misguidance; the verse therefore reproaches those who allow themselves to be diverted from what reason and revelation have established.

translation: Thus has the word of your Lord been fulfilled against those who defiantly disobey: they will not believe.
interpretation: This expresses God’s just judgment upon those who persist in rebellion and reject the truth: their continued defiance leads them to a state in which faith is no longer accepted by them, not because they were wronged, but because they knowingly chose obstinacy and turned away from guidance.

translation: Say, “Is there among your partners any who originates creation and then brings it back?” Say, “Allah originates creation and then brings it back. So how are you turned away?”
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that idols or other alleged partners of Allah possess divine power: none can create life in the first place or restore it after death. Since Allah alone has power over both origination and resurrection, turning toward anything else in worship is a departure from clear truth and sound reason.

translation: Say, “Are there among your partners any who guide to the truth?” Say, “Allah guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who cannot be guided unless he is guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in worshipping beings that possess no independent guidance or power, while Allah alone is the source of true guidance. Since the one who guides is more deserving of obedience than one who itself depends on guidance, sound judgment requires directing worship and following only Allah.

translation: Most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture is of no avail against the truth at all. Surely Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: Most people base their beliefs and judgments on unverified assumptions rather than sound knowledge. Such conjecture cannot replace the truth or establish it, while Allah fully knows their actions and the motives behind them.

translation: It is not possible for this Qur’an to have been fabricated apart from Allah; rather, it confirms what came before it and explains the Scripture in detail—there is no doubt that it is from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: تقرر الآية أن القرآن لا يمكن أن يكون افتراءً بشريًا، لأنه يوافق أصول الوحي السابق ويكشف معاني الهداية الإلهية ويوضحها، ولذلك فإن مصدره الرباني ثابت لا يعتريه شك.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whoever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who accuse the Prophet ﷺ of inventing the Qur’an: if their claim is true, they should produce even one chapter comparable to it and enlist every source of help they can find. Their inability to do so exposes the weakness of the accusation and points to the Qur’an’s divine origin.

translation: Rather, they rejected what they had not encompassed in knowledge, and whose fulfillment has not yet come to them. In the same way, those before them rejected the truth. So observe how the end of the wrongdoers was.
interpretation: The verse condemns rejecting revelation merely because its full meaning and promised realities have not yet become clear. It teaches that sincere judgment requires knowledge and patience, while denying the truth without understanding follows the destructive pattern of earlier peoples who opposed their messengers and ultimately suffered the consequences of their injustice.

translation: Among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord knows best who the corrupters are.
interpretation: People respond differently to divine revelation: some accept it sincerely, while others reject it. God alone fully knows the motives and inner condition of each person, and He distinguishes those whose rejection is rooted in corruption from those who are genuinely seeking the truth.

translation: And if they deny you, say: “My deeds are for me, and your deeds are for you. You are free of responsibility for what I do, and I am free of responsibility for what you do.”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to respond to rejection without compulsion or hostility: each person bears the consequences of their own choices and is accountable before God for their deeds. Faith cannot be imposed, and denial does not make the believer responsible for another person’s actions, nor does it excuse anyone from answering for their own.

translation: Among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?
interpretation: Some people may physically hear the Prophet’s words, yet their hearts are closed to understanding and accepting the truth. The question teaches that guidance cannot be forced upon those who deliberately refuse to reflect, just as the physically deaf cannot hear.

translation: Among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind, even though they cannot see?
interpretation: Their merely looking at the Messenger does not mean they perceive or accept the truth. The verse teaches that guidance cannot be forced upon those whose hearts are spiritually blind and unwilling to recognize what is clear.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong people in the least, but people wrong themselves.
interpretation: Allah’s justice is absolute: He never deprives anyone of a rightful due or punishes without cause. Human suffering and loss may arise from people’s own wrongdoing, rejection of guidance, and harmful choices, through which they bring injustice upon themselves.

translation: And on the Day He gathers them, it will seem to them as though they had remained only for an hour of the day, recognizing one another. Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, and they were not rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse portrays how insignificant worldly life will appear when people are resurrected: even a lifetime will seem like a brief passing moment. Their recognition of one another will not benefit those who rejected resurrection and accountability, for their denial led them away from the guidance that prepares a person for the meeting with Allah.

translation: Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or We cause you to die, to Us is their return; then Allah is witness over what they do.
interpretation: The fulfillment of God’s warning does not depend on the Prophet witnessing it during his lifetime. Whether its consequences appear before his eyes or afterward, all people will ultimately return to God, whose complete knowledge and testimony encompass every deed and ensure that none of their actions escapes judgment.

translation: And for every community there is a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment is made between them with justice, and they are not wronged.
interpretation: Every nation is given divine guidance through a messenger, and when the appointed time of accountability arrives, God judges that nation according to the truth and justice, rewarding or holding them accountable without diminishing anyone’s rights or burdening them unfairly.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They ask this question mockingly, challenging the warning of divine punishment or resurrection and demanding that it occur immediately, rather than responding with faith and humility.

translation: Say, “I have no power to bring myself harm or benefit except as Allah wills.” Every nation has an appointed term; when their term arrives, they can neither delay it for an hour nor bring it forward.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even the Messenger ﷺ is entirely dependent on Allah’s will and possesses no independent control over benefit, harm, or the course of events. It therefore directs people to place their trust in Allah rather than in created beings, while recognizing that every community and every person proceeds toward a divinely appointed time that cannot be postponed or hastened.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if His punishment were to come upon you by night or by day, what part of it would the criminals seek to hasten?”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who mockingly demand that punishment be brought sooner. Whether it arrives suddenly at night or openly during the day, they would have no reason to hasten it, because when divine judgment comes, escape and delay will no longer be possible.

translation: Is it then, when it has come to pass, that you will believe in it? Now—when you had been demanding that it come sooner?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who rejected the promised punishment and challenged its arrival: faith adopted only after divine judgment becomes undeniable is not the sincere faith of willing submission, but a forced acknowledgment after the opportunity to believe has passed.

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged themselves, “Taste the everlasting punishment. Are you being recompensed for anything other than what you used to earn?”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that divine punishment is neither arbitrary nor unjust: it is the consequence of the wrongdoing people deliberately committed and persisted in. The question is a rebuke, making clear that their fate corresponds to their own deeds and choices.

translation: They ask you, “Is it true?” Say, “Yes, by my Lord, it is certainly true, and you cannot escape [Allah].”
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to affirm with the strongest oath that Allah’s promised resurrection and judgment are unquestionably real, while reminding those who deny them that no power or refuge can prevent Allah from bringing His decree to pass.

translation: If every soul that had wronged possessed all that is on earth, it would offer it as ransom. They conceal their regret when they see the punishment. Judgment is passed among them with justice, and they are not wronged.
interpretation: The verse portrays the helplessness of those who persisted in wrongdoing when they finally confront punishment: even if they possessed the entire world, it could not save them. Their hidden regret comes too late, while God’s judgment is perfectly just, leaving no one deprived of what is due to them or punished without cause.

translation: Surely, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Surely, Allah’s promise is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs wholly to Allah and remains under His authority; therefore, His promise of resurrection, judgment, and recompense is certain. Yet most people fail to recognize this truth because they are unaware of Allah’s absolute ownership and power.

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Life and death are solely under Allah’s authority, and every person will ultimately return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you an exhortation from your Lord, a healing for what is in the hearts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse presents the Qur’an as a divine remedy for the inner ailments that corrupt faith and character—such as doubt, ignorance, arrogance, and despair. Its admonitions awaken people to truth, while its guidance leads those who accept it toward sound belief and righteous action; through that response, they receive Allah’s special mercy.

translation: Say, “In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that, let them rejoice; it is better than all that they accumulate.”
interpretation: True joy is found in Allah’s guidance and mercy, because they bring lasting spiritual benefit and salvation, whereas worldly possessions are temporary and ultimately inferior.

translation: Say, “Have you considered the provision Allah has sent down for you, and then you have made some of it unlawful and some lawful?” Say, “Has Allah given you permission, or do you fabricate lies against Allah?”
interpretation: This verse condemns declaring things lawful or unlawful in religion without divine authority. It teaches that judgments about what is permitted and forbidden belong to Allah, and that attributing such rulings to Him without revelation is a grave falsehood.

translation: And what do those who fabricate lies against Allah expect on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: Those who falsely attribute beliefs, rulings, or claims to Allah should not imagine that they will escape accountability; the Day of Resurrection will expose their deception and bring its consequences. Allah’s guidance, patience, forgiveness, and provision are immense favors bestowed upon humanity, yet most people respond with ingratitude by denying the truth and misusing His blessings.

translation: You are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite any part of the Qur’an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are immersed in it. Nothing escapes your Lord—not even the weight of a speck in the earth or in heaven, nor anything smaller or greater than that—but it is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse instills the awareness that God’s knowledge and witnessing encompass every human concern, recitation, and action at every moment. Nothing is hidden from Him or absent from His record, however small or insignificant it may seem; therefore, a believer should act with sincerity, vigilance, and accountability before God.

translation: Indeed, the close servants of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: Allah reassures those who sincerely believe in Him and live in faithful obedience that His care gives them security: they need not fear what lies ahead or grieve over what has passed, because their trust and nearness to Him remain greater than every worldly anxiety.

translation: Those who believe and are mindful of Allah.
interpretation: Allah’s close servants are distinguished by sincere faith in Him and by taqwa: remaining conscious of Him and guarding themselves from disobedience.

translation: For them are glad tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah. That is the great success.
interpretation: Those who remain mindful of Allah are promised reassurance, guidance, and good news in this life, as well as lasting reward in the Hereafter. Allah’s promise is certain and cannot be altered or revoked; attaining it is the true and greatest success.

translation: And let not their words grieve you. Indeed, all honor and might belong to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Do not be distressed by the denial, mockery, or hurtful claims of those who oppose you, for true authority, dignity, and victory belong entirely to Allah. He hears everything they say and knows the sincerity of your heart and the reality of every matter, so their words cannot ultimately diminish you or overcome the truth.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth. Those who invoke partners besides Allah follow nothing but conjecture; they do nothing but guess falsely.
interpretation: This verse affirms that all creation belongs exclusively to Allah and is subject to His authority. It rejects the claims of those who associate partners with Him, showing that their beliefs are not based on knowledge or proof, but on speculation and unsupported assumptions.

translation: He is the One who made the night for you so that you may rest in it, and the day bright and illuminating. Indeed, in that are signs for people who listen.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is a deliberate mercy and sign of God’s wisdom: night provides rest and renewal, while daylight enables life and activity. Those who truly listen with receptive hearts recognize through this ordered cycle God’s power, care, and oneness.

translation: They say, “Allah has taken a son.” Glory be to Him! He is Self-Sufficient; to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this claim. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?
interpretation: The verse declares Allah utterly beyond the need for offspring, since He possesses and sustains all creation and is dependent on none. Claiming that He has a child is therefore incompatible with His perfection and is not supported by any revealed proof or sound authority; it is an assertion made about Allah without knowledge.

translation: قل: إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون.
interpretation: أمر الله نبيَّه أن يعلن أن من ينسب إلى الله ما لم يقله، أو يشرّع بغير حق، فلن ينال فلاحًا حقيقيًّا؛ لأن الكذب على الله يفسد الاعتقاد والعمل ويحرم صاحبه التوفيق والعاقبة الحسنة.

translation: A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return, and then We will make them taste severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: Worldly pleasure is only a temporary respite; when people return to God, persistent disbelief will be met with the severe punishment it deserves.

translation: And recite to them the account of Noah, when he said to his people: “O my people, if my presence among you and my reminding you of Allah’s signs is burdensome to you, then I have placed my trust in Allah. So come to a firm decision, together with your partners, and let not your plan remain obscure to you; then carry it out against me and give me no respite.”
interpretation: Noah’s words express complete confidence in Allah and fearless steadfastness before opposition. He challenges his people to unite all their forces and false gods against him if they believe they can silence the truth, showing that a believer who relies upon Allah does not compromise his message out of fear, nor is he shaken by the threats of those who reject it.

translation: But if you turn away, I have not asked you for any reward; my reward is only with Allah. And I have been commanded to be among those who submit to Him.
interpretation: The messenger declares that his mission is not driven by worldly gain or personal benefit. Whether people accept or reject the truth does not change his duty, because he seeks his recompense from Allah alone and remains committed to sincere submission and obedience to Him.

translation: But they rejected him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark, and made them successors, while We drowned those who denied Our signs. So observe how terrible was the outcome of those who were warned.
interpretation: The verse shows that rejecting a messenger after the truth has been clearly conveyed leads to ruin, whereas faith and obedience become a means of deliverance. Noah’s rescue and the survival of his companions demonstrate that true authority and continuity belong ultimately to those who uphold God’s guidance, not to those who oppose it.

translation: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلًا إلى أقوامهم، فجاؤوهم بالبينات، فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذّبوا به من قبل؛ كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين.
interpretation: يبين الله أن إرسال الرسل وإقامة البراهين لا ينفع من أصرّ على التكذيب والعناد؛ فاستمرارهم في ردّ الحق بعد ظهوره يورث قلوبهم قسوة وانغلاقًا، حتى يصبح قبول الإيمان بعيدًا عنهم، وهذا جزاء تعدّيهم وإعراضهم المتكرر.

translation: Then We sent Moses and Aaron after them to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they acted arrogantly and were a criminal people.
interpretation: After the earlier messengers, God entrusted Moses and Aaron with confronting Pharaoh’s tyranny and calling him and his elite to the truth through clear signs. Yet their authority and status led them to reject the evidence arrogantly; their deliberate wrongdoing and oppression revealed them to be a people committed to sin and rebellion against God.

translation: When the truth came to them from Us, they said, “This is surely clear magic.”
interpretation: When confronted with the undeniable revelation from God, they rejected it by labeling it magic rather than responding to its truth, revealing their unwillingness to accept guidance.

translation: Moses said, “Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, ‘Is this magic?’ Yet magicians do not prosper.”
interpretation: Moses rebukes those who reject a clear divine truth by labeling it magic merely because it challenges their beliefs. He exposes the weakness of their claim: false sorcery cannot ultimately succeed, whereas God’s truth is not defeated or invalidated by their denial.

translation: They said, “Have you come to turn us away from what we found our forefathers following, and so that you may have greatness in the land? We will never believe in you both.”
interpretation: Their objection reveals that they were clinging to inherited tradition and worldly authority rather than considering the truth of the message. They portrayed Moses and Aaron’s call to faith as a political bid for power, using suspicion and arrogance to justify their refusal to believe.

translation: And Pharaoh said, “Bring me every skilled magician.”
interpretation: Pharaoh sought to gather the most accomplished practitioners of magic so that they could confront Moses and undermine his message, revealing his reliance on deception and spectacle to preserve his authority.

translation: When the magicians came, Moses said to them, “Cast whatever you are going to cast.”
interpretation: Moses gave the magicians permission to begin, confident that truth would expose the falsehood of their magic and that the outcome would not depend on intimidation or hesitation.

translation: Then, when they had cast, Moses said, “What you have brought is sorcery. Indeed, Allah will surely nullify it. Allah does not set right the work of those who spread corruption.”
interpretation: Moses exposes the magicians’ display as deception and declares that falsehood, however impressive, cannot endure against divine truth. Allah’s decree is that corrupt schemes ultimately fail and are deprived of lasting success.

translation: And Allah establishes the truth by His words, even though the criminals detest it.
interpretation: Allah makes the truth firm and victorious through His revelation and decree, regardless of how strongly wrongdoers oppose or resent it.

translation: فما آمن بموسى إلا جماعة قليلة من قومه، مع خوفهم من فرعون وأعيان قومه أن يفتنوهم ويصدّوهم عن دينهم؛ وإن فرعون كان متكبّرًا متجبّرًا في الأرض، وإنه كان من المتجاوزين للحدود.
interpretation: تُظهر الآية أن الإيمان بالحق قد يبدأ بأناس قليلين حين يواجهون سلطةً مستبدة تستخدم الترهيب والاضطهاد لردّ الناس عن عقيدتهم، وأن قلة أتباع موسى لم تكن دليلًا على ضعف حجته، بل نتيجةً لخوفهم من بطش فرعون، الذي جمع بين التسلّط والظلم والإفراط في الطغيان.

translation: And Moses said, “O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are truly submitting to Him.”
interpretation: Moses teaches that genuine faith is demonstrated through reliance on Allah: those who submit to Him should entrust their affairs and ultimate outcome to Him, even when facing fear, oppression, or uncertainty.

translation: So they said, “In Allah we place our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: They entrust themselves entirely to Allah and ask Him not to let the oppression of their enemies become a means of humiliating them, turning them away from faith, or causing others to think that falsehood has prevailed over the truth.

translation: And save us, by Your mercy, from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This is a supplication entrusting deliverance entirely to Allah’s mercy, asking Him to protect the believers from the oppression, persecution, and corrupt influence of those who reject faith.

translation: And We inspired Moses and his brother: “Settle your people in Egypt in houses, make your houses places of worship, establish prayer, and give glad tidings to the believers.”
interpretation: God instructed Moses and Aaron to establish the Israelite community in secure homes where they could gather in worship, orient themselves toward God, and maintain prayer despite oppression. Their steadfast devotion was to be accompanied by the assurance that God’s promise and relief belonged to the believers.

translation: And Moses said, “Our Lord, You have surely given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the worldly life. Our Lord, they use them to lead people away from Your path. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.”
interpretation: Moses’s supplication expresses his condemnation of Pharaoh’s deliberate use of worldly power and riches to mislead people and obstruct the truth. He asks that these means of corruption be removed and that Pharaoh’s heart be left to its chosen hardness until the punishment becomes undeniable, showing that persistent rejection after clear signs can bring a person to a state where faith is no longer accepted when compelled by the sight of impending punishment.

translation: He said, “Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”
interpretation: Allah assures Moses and Aaron that their prayer against Pharaoh’s tyranny has been accepted, while commanding them to remain firm in faith and obedience and not be swayed by the ignorance, false reasoning, or misguided ways of those who reject the truth.

translation: We carried the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his armies pursued them wrongfully and aggressively. Then, when drowning overtook him, he said, “I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among those who submit.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s declaration of faith came only when he was overwhelmed by certain death, after a lifetime of tyranny and rejection. It therefore reveals that genuine faith is not merely words uttered under compulsion, but sincere submission to God before the moment when punishment becomes unmistakable.

translation: Now? Yet you disobeyed before and were among those who spread corruption.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of Pharaoh’s repentance when destruction had already overtaken him: his declaration of faith was not accepted because it came only after a lifetime of defiance and corruption, when witnessing punishment had removed the possibility of sincere choice and reform.

translation: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية ۚ وإن كثيرًا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون
interpretation: المعنى أن الله أظهر جسد فرعون بعد هلاكه ونجّاه من أن يبتلعه البحر، ليبقى شاهدًا على عاقبة الطغيان وعبرةً لمن يأتي بعده، غير أن كثيرًا من الناس لا ينتفعون بآيات الله ولا يتفكرون فيها.

translation: Indeed, We settled the Children of Israel in a secure and blessed place and provided them with wholesome things. They did not differ until knowledge came to them. Surely, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Children of Israel that He granted them a stable homeland and abundant lawful blessings, yet their divisions arose not from lack of guidance but from disputes after knowledge had reached them. Their conflicting claims will ultimately be judged by Allah on the Day of Resurrection, whose judgment will distinguish truth from falsehood and justice from transgression.

translation: فإن كنتَ في شكٍّ مما أنزلنا إليك، فاسأل الذين يقرؤون الكتاب من قبلك. لقد جاءك الحق من ربك، فلا تكوننَّ من الشاكّين.
interpretation: الخطاب هنا للتثبيت وإقامة الحجة، لا لإثبات وقوع الشك من النبي ﷺ؛ فلو عُرض الشك على سبيل الفرض، فإن أهل الكتاب الذين عرفوا صفات الوحي والرسل في كتبهم يستطيعون الشهادة بصدق ما جاءه. ثم يؤكد الله أن القرآن حقٌّ نازل من عنده، ولذلك يجب الثبات عليه وترك التردد.

translation: And never be among those who deny the signs of Allah, lest you become one of the losers.
interpretation: This is a solemn warning to remain firmly committed to the truth revealed by Allah and never imitate those who reject or falsify His signs, for such denial leads to spiritual ruin and ultimate loss.

translation: إن الذين تحققت عليهم كلمة ربك لن يؤمنوا.
interpretation: المقصود أن من أصرّ على الكفر والعناد حتى استحقّ حكم الله عليه بالضلال والحرمان من الهداية، فلن ينتفع بآيات الله؛ لأن قلبه أغلقه الإعراض المتكرر عن الحق، لا لأن الله يظلمه أو يمنعه الهداية ابتداءً.

translation: Even if every sign were to come to them, they would not believe until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This describes the obstinacy of those who reject truth: no number of clear signs will benefit them while they persist in denial; only when punishment becomes visible will they acknowledge reality, but such recognition comes too late to count as sincere faith.

translation: Why was there not a single town that believed so that its faith would benefit it—except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and allowed them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse points out that earlier peoples generally believed only after witnessing the signs of impending punishment, when faith was no longer of benefit. The people of Jonah were the exception: they sincerely believed and repented before the punishment fully descended, so God removed from them their worldly humiliation and granted them respite and prosperity for the period He appointed.

translation: Had your Lord willed, everyone on earth would have believed, all of them together. So, would you compel people to become believers?
interpretation: Faith cannot be produced through coercion; God has allowed human beings the freedom to choose belief or disbelief. The Prophet’s duty is to convey the truth clearly, not to force people into faith, for genuine belief must arise from willing conviction.

translation: No soul can believe except by Allah’s permission; and He places spiritual defilement upon those who do not use their reason.
interpretation: Faith is granted through Allah’s enabling guidance, while those who refuse to reflect and understand the truth become subject to spiritual corruption as a consequence of their deliberate rejection.

translation: Say, “Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.” Yet the signs and warnings are of no avail to a people who do not believe.
interpretation: The verse calls people to contemplate the ordered realities of the heavens and the earth as evidence of God’s power and wisdom. Such evidence benefits those who approach it with openness and faith, but it cannot guide people who deliberately reject belief despite the signs and warnings before them.

translation: Do they await anything but the like of the days that befell those who passed away before them? Say, “Then wait; I too am waiting with you.”
interpretation: The verse warns those who reject the truth that persistent denial leaves them facing the same divine judgment that overtook earlier peoples. The command to “wait” is not approval of their stance, but a challenge exposing the certainty of God’s promise: the outcome will distinguish between the faithful and those who persist in rejection.

translation: Then We shall save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This is Allah’s assured promise that He will protect His messengers and sincere believers from ultimate ruin and punishment, granting them deliverance by His mercy after falsehood and its people are brought to destruction.

translation: Say, “O people, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah. Rather, I worship Allah, who causes you to die, and I have been commanded to be among the believers.”
interpretation: The verse declares that genuine faith is not shaped by doubt or conformity to the worship of others. The Prophet is commanded to reject every false object of worship and devote himself exclusively to Allah, whose power over life and death proves His sole right to be worshipped, while remaining firmly among those who believe.

translation: And set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be among those who associate partners with God.
interpretation: Direct yourself wholly and sincerely toward the true religion, turning away from every form of idolatry and false devotion. The verse calls for steadfast commitment to pure monotheism, with the heart and actions devoted to God alone.

translation: And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit nor harm you. If you do so, then you will surely be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse forbids directing prayer, reliance, or acts of worship to anything that has no independent power to bring benefit or avert harm. Such devotion belongs exclusively to Allah; turning it toward powerless beings is ظلم because it places worship where it does not belong and violates the truth of divine oneness.

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He intends good for you, none can withhold His فضل. He grants it to whom He wills among His servants, and He is the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that all harm and benefit ultimately lie under Allah’s authority: no created power can remove a hardship that He allows, nor prevent the good He decrees. This calls the believer to seek help from Him alone, rely on His wisdom, and remain humble and hopeful, knowing that His dealings with His servants are accompanied by forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Say: “O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord. So whoever follows guidance is only guided for his own benefit, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment. I am not appointed as a guardian over you.”
interpretation: The verse establishes that divine guidance is a clear truth from God, but accepting or rejecting it remains each person’s responsibility. Guidance brings its benefit to the one who follows it, while misguidance harms only the one who chooses it. The Messenger’s role is to convey the truth faithfully, not to compel people or control their choices.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges; and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This commands steadfast adherence to divine revelation and patience in the face of opposition or hardship, trusting that Allah’s final judgment is perfectly just and wiser than any human judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Rā. This is a Book whose verses have been perfected and then explained in detail, from One who is All-Wise, All-Aware.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Qur’an is divine revelation: its wording and guidance are precise, its meanings and rulings are clarified, and its entire message proceeds from Allah’s perfect wisdom and complete knowledge.

translation: Do not worship anything except Allah. Indeed, I am a warner and a bearer of good news from Him to you.
interpretation: The verse calls people to devote all worship to Allah alone, while recognizing the Messenger’s role: he warns of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and gives glad tidings of Allah’s mercy and reward to those who accept it.

translation: And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; He will grant you a good enjoyment until an appointed term, and He will give every possessor of excellence his due excellence. But if you turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true repentance is not merely verbal: it begins with seeking God’s forgiveness and is completed by turning away from sin and returning sincerely to Him. Such repentance brings a wholesome life by God’s grace for the time He has decreed, while every person’s sincere virtue will receive its fitting reward. Persisting in rejection, however, places one in danger of the severe reckoning of the Last Day.

translation: To Allah is your return, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: You will ultimately return to Allah for judgment, and nothing lies beyond His power, including bringing you back to life and holding you accountable for your deeds.

translation: Indeed, they fold up their chests in an attempt to hide themselves from Him. Yet when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Truly, He knows full well what lies within the hearts.
