interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of trying to conceal one’s rejection, intentions, or inner thoughts from God: even the most private feelings and hidden acts are completely known to Him, whether a person withdraws inwardly or outwardly seeks concealment.

translation: There is no creature on earth whose provision is not entrusted to Allah. He knows its dwelling place and its resting place; everything is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: Allah has taken responsibility for providing every living creature with what sustains it, while possessing complete knowledge of where each creature lives, travels, and ultimately comes to rest. Nothing in creation is overlooked or left outside His encompassing knowledge, all of it being recorded in a manifest record.

translation: And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, so that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. Yet if you say, “You will surely be resurrected after death,” those who disbelieve will surely say, “This is nothing but clear magic.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that creation is governed by divine wisdom and purpose, not chance: human life is a test of the quality of one’s deeds, especially sincerity and righteousness. It also warns that denial of resurrection often arises not from lack of evidence, but from rejecting accountability; therefore believers should remain certain that every deed will ultimately be judged by God.

translation: And if We delay the punishment for them until a predetermined period, they will surely say, “What is holding it back?” Indeed, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them, and what they used to ridicule will encompass them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the heedlessness of those who deny divine warning: when punishment is delayed by God’s wisdom, they mistake the delay for proof that it will never come and mock the warning. But when the appointed time arrives, no one will be able to avert it, and the very consequence they derided will surround and overtake them.

translation: And if We let a human being taste mercy from Us, then take it away from him, he is indeed despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse warns that a person may allow the loss of a blessing to overwhelm his awareness of God’s mercy, leading him to despair and deny gratitude; true faith requires remaining hopeful and thankful even when blessings are withdrawn.

translation: And if We let him taste prosperity after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, “The misfortunes have left me.” Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
interpretation: The verse exposes the instability of a person who lets circumstances define his faith: when hardship is removed, he quickly assumes that suffering will never return, becoming elated and arrogant instead of grateful and humble before Allah.

translation: Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds—for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: Those who remain steadfast through trials and consistently act righteously are promised that Allah will pardon their faults and grant them an immense, lasting reward.

translation: Perhaps you would leave aside some of what is revealed to you, and your chest feels constrained by their saying, “Why has no treasure been sent down to him, or why has no angel come with him?” You are only a warner, and Allah is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ, assuring him that he is not responsible for satisfying the unbelievers’ demands or altering the revelation because of their rejection. His duty is to convey the warning faithfully, while Allah oversees all matters and will judge those who accept or reject the truth.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “Then produce ten fabricated chapters like it, and call upon whoever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who claim that the Qur’an was invented by the Prophet to produce even ten chapters comparable to it, while seeking help from anyone besides Allah. This challenge exposes the weakness of their accusation: if the Qur’an were merely human composition, they should be able to imitate it. Their inability to meet the challenge confirms that it is revelation from Allah, not a fabrication.

translation: If they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed with Allah’s knowledge, and that there is no deity except Him. Will you then submit?
interpretation: Their inability to produce anything comparable to the revelation establishes that it comes from Allah, whose perfect knowledge is reflected in it. Recognizing its divine source should lead to affirming His exclusive oneness and willingly submitting to Him.

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.
interpretation: الآية تبيّن أن من جعل غايته الدنيا وزينتها، فقد يُعطى ثمرة سعيه فيها كاملة من مال أو جاه أو متاع، دون أن يُنقص من نصيبه الدنيوي، لكن ذلك لا يعني قبول عمله عند الله ولا نجاته في الآخرة؛ إذ إن الجزاء الدنيوي وحده لا يغني عن الإيمان وإرادة وجه الله.

translation: Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. All that they did therein will be rendered worthless, and all that they used to do will be in vain.
interpretation: This warns that deeds devoted to worldly aims alone, without faith and sincerity for Allah, may bring worldly results but have no lasting value before Him in the Hereafter.

translation: أفمن كان على بيّنةٍ من ربّه ويتلوه شاهدٌ منه، ومن قبله كتابُ موسى إمامًا ورحمةً؟ أولئك يؤمنون به، ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده؛ فلا تكن في شكٍّ منه، إنّه الحقّ من ربّك، ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن من قامت عنده حجة واضحة من الله، يؤيدها شاهد من الوحي، ويؤكدها كتاب موسى الذي كان هدايةً ورحمة، فهو جدير بالإيمان بالحق المنزل. أما من يرفضه بعد قيام الحجة عليه، مهما كان انتماؤه أو جماعته، فمصيره الوعيد الإلهي. وفي ذلك تثبيت للنبي ﷺ على يقينه، وبيان أن صدق الحق لا يتوقف على كثرة المصدقين به، إذ إن أكثر الناس قد يعرضون عن الإيمان رغم وضوح الدليل.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah? Such people will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, “These are the ones who lied about their Lord.” Indeed, Allah’s curse is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse portrays inventing claims about Allah as the gravest form of injustice, because it corrupts truth at its source and misleads others in matters of faith. On the Day of Judgment, such falsehood will be exposed before Allah, and the testimony of the witnesses will confirm their guilt; therefore, those who knowingly attribute to Allah what He has not revealed are deprived of His mercy.

translation: Those who hinder others from the way of Allah, seek to make it crooked, and deny the Hereafter.
interpretation: This describes people who deliberately obstruct others from following Allah’s guidance, distort its clear truth to suit their desires, and reject accountability after death; their denial of the Hereafter enables them to persist in wrongdoing without fearing its ultimate consequence.

translation: Those are not able to escape in the earth, nor do they have any protectors besides Allah. The punishment will be multiplied for them; they were unable to hear, and they could not see.
interpretation: They will have no refuge or power to evade Allah’s judgment, and no false protector can save them. Their punishment is multiplied because they persistently rejected the truth: they were not genuinely willing to listen to guidance or perceive its signs, despite having the faculties to do so.

translation: Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them.
interpretation: They have ruined their own souls by rejecting the truth, while the false gods and claims they invented will provide them no help and will completely fail them.

translation: Without a doubt, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: Those who prefer worldly gain while rejecting God’s guidance will ultimately lose the everlasting reward and face the consequences of their choices in the Hereafter.

translation: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الأعمال الصالحة وخضعوا لربهم وتواضعوا له، أولئك هم أهل الجنة، خالدون فيها أبداً.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الإيمان الحق لا يكتمل بمجرد الاعتقاد، بل يظهر في العمل الصالح وفي خشوع القلب لله وانقياده له؛ فهؤلاء يجمعون بين صحة الصلة بالله وصلاح السلوك، ولذلك يستحقون نعيم الجنة والخلود فيها.

translation: The example of the two groups is like that of the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: Allah contrasts those who reject the truth with those who accept it: the rejecters are like people deprived of sight and hearing, unable to perceive guidance, while the believers are like those who see and hear, recognizing and responding to it. These two ways of life cannot be equal, so people should use their understanding to distinguish truth from falsehood.

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, saying, “I am to you a clear warner.”
interpretation: God sent Noah to warn his people openly and unmistakably, calling them to recognize the truth and turn back before the consequences of rejecting it overtook them.

translation: Worship none but Allah; indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: This is a call to sincere monotheism: all worship must be directed to Allah alone, while the warning emphasizes that turning away from Him exposes a person to the severe consequences of the Day of Judgment.

translation: The chiefs of those who disbelieved among his people said, “We see you only as a human being like ourselves, and we see no one following you except the lowliest among us, at first glance. Nor do we see you possessing any superiority over us; rather, we think you are liars.”
interpretation: The disbelieving leaders rejected Noah’s message because they judged truth by social status, wealth, and worldly influence. They regarded the humble believers as insignificant and assumed that a true messenger would have to possess a visible advantage over them. Their response reveals arrogance and prejudice: instead of examining Noah’s call, they dismissed it because it came from someone they considered socially ordinary and attracted people they looked down upon.

translation: He said, “O my people, consider this: if I stand upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has granted me mercy from Himself, but it has been obscured from you, should we force it upon you while you are unwilling?”
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine truth may be evident to the messenger through revelation and grace, yet remain veiled from those who reject it; faith cannot be imposed by force, because genuine acceptance must come through willing recognition rather than compulsion.

translation: And, O my people, I ask no wealth from you for this; my reward is only with Allah. Nor will I drive away those who believe; indeed, they will meet their Lord. But I see that you are a people who act ignorantly.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a sincere caller to truth must seek no worldly payment and must not reject believers because of their low social standing or lack of wealth. Every believer is ultimately accountable before Allah, so judging people by worldly status rather than faith and truth is an expression of ignorance.

translation: And, O my people, who would help me against Allah if I were to drive them away? Will you not take heed?
interpretation: Nūḥ reminds his people that expelling the sincere believers merely to satisfy the powerful would be an act of injustice for which he could find no protection from Allah. He urges them to reflect before allowing status and prejudice to lead them into wrongdoing.

translation: And I do not say to you, ‘I possess the treasuries of Allah,’ nor do I claim to know the unseen, nor do I say, ‘Indeed, I am an angel.’ Nor do I say of those whom your eyes disdain, ‘Allah will never grant them any good.’ Allah knows best what is within their souls. If I did so, I would truly be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a messenger’s role is not to claim divine treasures, knowledge of the unseen, or angelic nature, but to convey the truth humbly and faithfully. Human status and outward appearance cannot determine a person’s worth before Allah; therefore, rejecting sincere believers because they seem poor or insignificant is unjust, since Allah alone knows their inner faith and true merit.

translation: They said, “O Noah, you have argued with us and prolonged your argument with us. So bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: They spoke out of stubborn defiance, having exhausted their willingness to consider Noah’s evidence. Instead of responding to his warning with reflection, they challenged him to bring the punishment he foretold, revealing their rejection and confidence that they would not be held accountable.

translation: He said, “Allah alone will bring it upon you if He wills, and you will not be able to thwart Him.”
interpretation: Hūd makes clear that the promised punishment is entirely under Allah’s command: He may bring it whenever He wills, and no one can escape it or prevent its decree.

translation: My counsel will not benefit you—even if I desire to advise you—if Allah wills to let you stray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: No advice can benefit those whom God leaves to the consequences of their persistent rejection and misguidance; guidance is ultimately under His authority. Since He is their Lord and they will return to Him, they cannot escape accountability for how they respond to the truth.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “If I have fabricated it, then my crime is upon me; and I am innocent of the crimes you commit.”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to answer the accusation calmly: if he had invented the revelation, he alone would bear the consequence of that falsehood, but the deniers cannot escape responsibility for rejecting the truth and committing their own wrongdoing. The verse exposes the injustice of blaming the messenger while refusing to examine their own actions.

translation: And it was revealed to Noah: “None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing.”
interpretation: Allah informed Noah that his people’s persistent rejection had reached its appointed limit and that no further faith was to be expected from them beyond those who had already believed. He was therefore consoled not to let their denial and wrongdoing consume him, since he had fulfilled his duty of conveying the truth and their accountability belonged to Allah.

translation: Build the Ark under Our watch and by Our revelation, and do not plead with Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they will be drowned.
interpretation: Allah commands Noah to construct the Ark under His constant care and guidance, assuring him that the believers will be protected while the persistent wrongdoers—who have rejected the truth and refused repentance—will face the decreed punishment. This also teaches that divine mercy does not cancel justice when wrongdoing is knowingly and persistently maintained.

translation: And he was building the Ark. Whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, “If you mock us, then we will surely mock you just as you mock us.”
interpretation: Noah continued obeying God and carrying out His command despite the ridicule of his people. His response was not mere retaliation, but a warning that the truth they mocked would soon be vindicated, while their arrogance would become a source of disgrace when God’s punishment came.

translation: Then you will know who will be visited by a punishment that humiliates him, and upon whom an enduring punishment will descend.
interpretation: في الآية تهديدٌ لمن أصرّ على التكذيب والعناد بأنهم سيعلمون عند وقوع العذاب أيُّهم استحقّ الخزي والمهانة، ومن نزل به عذابٌ دائم لا ينقطع.

translation: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, “Load onto it a pair of every kind, your family—except those against whom the decree has already been pronounced—and those who believe.” Yet none believed with him except a few.
interpretation: When God’s appointed judgment arrived and the sign of the overflowing oven appeared, Noah was commanded to board the Ark with pairs of living creatures, the believers, and the members of his household who were not destined for punishment. The verse emphasizes that truth is not measured by the number of its followers: despite Noah’s long call, only a small group accepted faith and was saved, while those who had persistently rejected it were excluded from deliverance.

translation: And he said, “Board it. In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: Noah instructed the believers to enter the Ark while entrusting its movement and safety entirely to Allah, invoking His name at departure and arrival. This teaches that believers rely on Allah’s protection while taking the means available to them, and that even amid judgment, His forgiveness and mercy remain open to those who turn to Him.

translation: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains. Noah called out to his son, who was apart: “O my son, board with us, and do not be among the disbelievers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Noah’s final, compassionate appeal to his estranged son amid the overwhelming flood. Physical closeness to Noah could not by itself save him; true safety required responding to faith and separating oneself from rejection of God. It also reflects a parent’s sincere concern, even when the child has chosen a path opposed to truth.

translation: He said, “I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water.” He said, “There is no protector today from Allah’s decree, except for those upon whom He has mercy.” And the waves came between them, so he was among the drowned.
interpretation: The verse reveals that no material shelter can protect a person when Allah’s judgment has arrived; true salvation lies only in Allah’s mercy and in responding to His guidance, not in relying on worldly means alone.

translation: And it was said, “O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, cease [your rain].” The water subsided, the decree was fulfilled, and the Ark came to rest upon al-Jūdī. And it was said, “Away with the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the flood ending instantly by the decisive command of God: nature obeys Him, the promised judgment is completed, and the Ark’s resting place marks the deliverance of the believers and the ruin of those who persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, “My Lord, surely my son is of my family, and surely Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges.”
interpretation: Noah appeals to God with the sincere assumption that His promise of saving his family includes his son, while affirming complete trust in God’s justice and wisdom. The verse portrays the tension between a prophet’s natural compassion for his child and his submission to God’s ultimate judgment.

translation: He said, “O Noah, he is not of your family; indeed, his conduct was unrighteous. So do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of. I admonish you, lest you become among the ignorant.”
interpretation: Allah clarifies that true belonging to Noah’s household is not secured by blood relation alone, but by faith and righteous conduct. Noah is therefore warned not to plead for a matter whose divine wisdom and justice he does not know, and to submit humbly to Allah’s judgment rather than let parental affection lead him into an uninformed request.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge. If You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers.”
interpretation: This is a confession of humility and repentance: the servant recognizes the limits of his knowledge, seeks protection from speaking or requesting anything without truth, and acknowledges that forgiveness and mercy from God are essential for salvation.

translation: It was said, “O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon communities descended from those with you. And there will be other communities whom We will grant enjoyment for a time; then a painful punishment from Us will afflict them.”
interpretation: After the flood, Noah and the believers with him are assured that their new beginning will be under God’s peace and blessing, while the mention of other communities makes clear that worldly prosperity is only temporary and does not exempt people from accountability or divine punishment.

translation: That is from the accounts of the unseen which We reveal to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this. So be patient; surely, the good outcome belongs to the mindful of God.
interpretation: God affirms that the account revealed to the Prophet is knowledge of the unseen, unknown to him and his people except through revelation. He therefore commands him to remain steadfast despite rejection and hardship, assuring him that ultimate success and a praiseworthy end are granted to those who remain conscious of God and obedient to Him.

translation: And to the people of ʿĀd We sent their brother Hūd. He said, “O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are only fabricating lies.”
interpretation: Hūd calls his people to abandon the false gods they invented and to devote worship exclusively to Allah, affirming that their claim to possess other deities is baseless fabrication.

translation: O my people, I ask no reward from you for it; my reward is only with Him who brought me into being. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: Hūd عليه السلام declares that his call is free from any worldly motive, since he seeks his recompense only from Allah, his Creator. He therefore urges his people to use their reason and recognize that a message offered without personal gain deserves sincere consideration.

translation: “O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him; He will send down abundant rain upon you and increase you in strength upon your strength. Do not turn away as criminals.”
interpretation: Hūd calls his people to sincere repentance: abandoning their wrongdoing, regretting it, and returning obediently to God. Such repentance becomes a cause of divine mercy, provision, and renewed strength, whereas persisting in rejection and sin is a form of criminal defiance that deprives them of these blessings.

translation: They said, “O Hūd, you have not brought us any clear proof, nor will we abandon our gods merely because of what you say, and we will not believe in you.”
interpretation: The people of Hūd rejected his call because they demanded a manifest proof and clung stubbornly to the worship of their idols; they treated inherited beliefs as more authoritative than his warning and therefore refused to accept him as a messenger.

translation: They said, “We can only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with harm.” He said, “Indeed, I call Allah to witness—and you too bear witness—that I am free of whatever you associate with Him.”
interpretation: When Hūd’s people attributed his message to a supposed punishment from their idols, he decisively rejected their superstition and declared his complete disassociation from every act of associating partners with Allah, calling both Allah and the people themselves to witness his unwavering faith.

translation: Other than Him. So scheme against me, all of you together, and do not give me any respite.
interpretation: The speaker declares that he rejects all supposed powers besides Allah and fearlessly challenges his opponents to unite and act against him, confident that their plots cannot harm him except by Allah’s permission.

translation: Indeed, I have placed my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature except that He holds it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.
interpretation: The speaker declares complete reliance on Allah, recognizing that every living creature is entirely under His authority and control. Since Allah governs all beings with perfect justice and wisdom, nothing can escape His decree, and those who trust in Him are assured that His judgment and guidance are never unjust or misguided.

translation: “But if you turn away, I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you. My Lord will replace you with another people, and you cannot harm Him in the least. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.”
interpretation: The prophet has fulfilled his duty by delivering God’s message, so the people’s rejection cannot diminish the truth or harm God in any way. Their refusal only exposes them to the consequences of abandoning guidance, while God remains fully in control: He can remove them and raise another people in their place, and nothing escapes His protection, knowledge, or governance.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hūd and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment.
interpretation: When God’s decreed punishment arrived, His mercy protected Hūd and the believers who followed him, while the people who rejected the truth were exposed to a terrible and overwhelming chastisement.

translation: And that was ʿĀd: they rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every defiant tyrant.
interpretation: The verse portrays the destruction of ʿĀd as the consequence of persistent arrogance: they rejected divine guidance, refused the call conveyed by their messengers, and surrendered their judgment to powerful leaders who opposed the truth. Their downfall resulted not merely from strength or worldly power, but from knowingly following rebellion and tyranny.

translation: They were pursued by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, ˹the people of˺ ’Aad disbelieved in their Lord. So away with ’Aad, the people of Hûd!
interpretation: The verse declares that the people of ’Aad earned lasting disgrace in this life and punishment in the Hereafter because they rejected their Lord despite the warning brought by Hûd. Their destruction is presented as a just consequence of persistent disbelief and rebellion, and as a warning that denying divine guidance leads to ruin.

translation: And to Thamūd We sent their brother Ṣāliḥ. He said, “O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He brought you forth from the earth and settled you in it, so seek His forgiveness and then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.”
interpretation: Ṣāliḥ calls his people to recognize Allah as the sole Creator and rightful object of worship, acknowledging that their existence and ability to prosper on earth are gifts entrusted to them. Their proper response is to seek forgiveness for disobedience and sincerely return to Allah, whose nearness means that He hears their repentance and responds to those who call upon Him.

translation: They said, “O Ṣāliḥ, we had placed our hopes in you before this. Do you forbid us from worshipping what our forefathers worshipped? Indeed, we are in unsettling doubt about that to which you call us.”
interpretation: Ṣāliḥ’s people remind him that they once regarded him as a promising and respected leader, implying that his call to abandon their inherited worship has disappointed them. Their objection reveals their attachment to ancestral tradition and their refusal to accept his message, while their claim of doubt reflects a troubled rejection rather than a sincere search for guidance.

translation: قال: يا قوم، أرأيتم إن كنتُ على بيّنةٍ من ربي، وآتاني منه رحمةً، فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته؟ فما تزيدونني غيرَ تخسيرٍ.
interpretation: يقول صالح عليه السلام لقومه: إنني على حجة واضحة من ربي، وقد خصّني برحمةٍ ووحي، فلا يمكنني أن أترك أمره أو أطيعكم في تكذيبه؛ إذ لا أحد يستطيع أن يحميني من عقابه إن عصيته. وإن إصراركم على دعوتي إلى مخالفة الوحي لا يجلب لي إلا الخسران والهلاك.

translation: “O my people, this is Allah’s she-camel, a sign for you. So leave her to graze in Allah’s land, and do not harm her, lest a near punishment seize you.”
interpretation: The verse conveys Ṣāliḥ’s warning that the she-camel was a divinely appointed sign and a test of the people’s obedience; respecting her meant submitting to Allah’s command, while harming her would reveal their defiance and bring swift punishment.

translation: So they hamstrung her, and he said, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that cannot be denied.”
interpretation: After defiantly violating God’s clear sign by killing the she-camel, the people of Thamūd were granted only a final three-day respite. The warning shows that divine judgment may be delayed as mercy, but once its appointed promise is given, no denial or escape can prevent it.

translation: So when Our command came, We saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Almighty.
interpretation: When divine judgment came upon the people who rejected Ṣāliḥ, Allah rescued him and the believers through His mercy, protecting them not only from destruction but also from the humiliation that accompanied it. The verse affirms that Allah’s power is absolute: He decisively supports those who believe and overcomes those who defy Him.

translation: And the mighty blast seized those who had wronged, and by morning they lay lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: The verse portrays the suddenness and finality of God’s punishment for those who rejected the truth and persisted in wrongdoing: the destructive cry struck them without escape, leaving them motionless and utterly powerless in the very homes where they had felt secure.

translation: As though they had never lived there. Indeed, Thamūd rejected their Lord. So away with Thamūd!
interpretation: The verse portrays the complete ruin and disappearance of Thamūd after their rebellion, as if they had never inhabited the land. Their destruction was the consequence of rejecting their Lord and refusing His guidance.

translation: And indeed Our messengers came to Abraham with good news. They said, “Peace.” He replied, “Peace.” Then he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf.
interpretation: The verse portrays Abraham’s immediate hospitality and graciousness: he welcomed the divine messengers with peace and promptly honored his guests with generous food, reflecting the virtue of sincere greeting and selfless generosity.

translation: But when he saw that their hands did not reach toward it, he found them strange and felt apprehensive of them. They said, “Do not fear; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lot.”
interpretation: When Abraham’s guests did not eat from the food offered to them, he sensed that they were not ordinary visitors and became afraid, since refusing hospitality could signal hostile intentions. They reassured him that he had nothing to fear: they were angels sent by God with a mission concerning the people of Lot.

translation: And his wife was standing by, and she laughed; so We gave her good news of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This expresses God’s gracious promise to Abraham and his wife of descendants despite their advanced age: first Isaac, and then Jacob through him. It also shows that God’s power brings about what seems impossible and that His blessings continue through righteous generations.

translation: She said, “Alas for me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this husband of mine is an old man? Indeed, this is truly astonishing!”
interpretation: She expressed amazement at the announcement of a child despite the natural circumstances that seemed to make childbirth impossible: her advanced age and her husband’s old age. Her response reflects human wonder at the extraordinary power of God, not denial of His ability; what appears impossible by ordinary causes is entirely possible by His command.

translation: They said, “Do you marvel at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings are upon you, O people of the household. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.”
interpretation: The angels reassure Abraham’s wife that Allah’s decree is not constrained by ordinary expectations: His mercy and blessings have chosen this household for an extraordinary gift. Her wonder is answered by affirming Allah’s perfect power, wisdom, and praiseworthiness.

translation: When the fear had left Abraham and the good news had come to him, he pleaded with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: After being reassured by the angels’ glad tidings, Abraham’s deep compassion moved him to plead with God on behalf of Lot’s people, seeking mercy for them despite their grave wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, tender-hearted, and ever turning to God.
interpretation: This portrays Abraham as possessing a gentle and patient character: he did not hasten to anger or punishment, his heart was deeply compassionate and moved by concern for others, and he continually returned to God in humility, prayer, and repentance.

translation: “O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and a punishment that cannot be turned back is surely coming upon them.”
interpretation: Allah instructs Abraham to stop pleading for Lot’s people, because the divine decree concerning their destruction has been issued and no intercession can prevent the punishment appointed for them.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt powerless to protect them, and said, “This is a difficult day.”
interpretation: Lot felt deep anguish because he feared that his people would harm his guests, while he was unable to prevent them; his words express the extreme hardship of facing a grave trial with limited human means.

translation: And his people came rushing toward him, and before that they had been committing evil deeds. He said, “O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So be mindful of Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a right-minded man?”
interpretation: Lot appeals to his people’s conscience and moral responsibility, offering a lawful alternative to their intended wrongdoing and urging them to fear Allah, respect the sanctity of guests, and let sound judgment restrain their corrupt desires.

translation: They said, “You already know that we have no desire for your daughters, and you surely know what we want.”
interpretation: They reject Lot’s offer of his daughters for marriage, declaring that their true intention is to pursue the male guests instead; their words reveal their deliberate persistence in their immoral demand despite knowing it is wrong.

translation: He said, “If only I had the strength to resist you, or could seek refuge in a mighty support.”
interpretation: Lot expressed his anguish at being unable to protect his guests or restrain his people’s wrongdoing, wishing he had powerful allies or a strong refuge to defend against them.

translation: They said, “O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night, and let none of you look back—except your wife; surely what strikes them will strike her. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is the morning not near?”
interpretation: The angels reassure Lot that his people cannot harm him, while commanding him to leave immediately and without hesitation. His wife is excluded because she will share the fate of the people through her alignment with them, showing that physical association with the righteous does not protect one who remains committed to wrongdoing. The nearness of morning emphasizes that God’s judgment is certain and imminent.

translation: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود
interpretation: حين صدر قضاء الله بعذاب قوم لوط، قلب قراهم رأسًا على عقب، وأنزل عليها حجارة من طين محرق متتابعة، جزاءً على إصرارهم على الفساد وتكذيبهم للحق.

translation: Marked by your Lord; and it is not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The punishment was specifically designated by God, and this serves as a warning that divine retribution remains near for those who persist in injustice and wrongdoing.

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuʿayb. He said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Do not give less than the full measure and weight. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb calls his people to recognize Allah’s exclusive right to worship and to let that faith govern their dealings with others. Their prosperity is a trust, not permission for fraud; deliberately reducing people’s due in trade is a form of corruption that can bring a punishment from which no one can escape.

translation: And, O my people, give full measure and weight with justice, do not deprive people of what is rightfully theirs, and do not spread corruption throughout the land.
interpretation: This is a command to uphold absolute fairness in trade and every dealing: no one may exploit others by concealing, reducing, or manipulating their rights. It also warns that dishonest transactions are not merely private wrongs; when injustice becomes widespread, it corrupts society and brings ruin.

translation: What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers; and I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: The lawful gain that Allah leaves for you after honest dealings is better and more blessed than wealth acquired through fraud or injustice. Faith requires trusting Allah’s provision and recognizing that the messenger can convey the truth, but cannot compel people to follow it or control their deeds.

translation: They said, “O Shuʿayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our forefathers worshipped, or that we should refrain from doing with our wealth whatever we wish? Indeed, you are surely the forbearing, rightly guided one!”
interpretation: They addressed Shuʿayb sarcastically, pretending to praise his patience and sound judgment while ridiculing his call. They rejected the idea that divine guidance should correct inherited beliefs and regulate how wealth is used, treating personal desire and economic freedom as matters beyond moral accountability.

translation: He said, “O my people, have you considered: if I stand upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with good provision? I do not intend to do what I forbid you from doing. I seek only to bring about reform as much as I am able. My success is granted only by Allah. In Him I place my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb explains that his call to justice and uprightness is not hypocrisy or a desire to control others, since he himself follows the guidance he teaches and does not practice what he forbids. His sole aim is sincere reform within the limits of his ability, while recognizing that true success depends entirely on Allah; therefore, he relies upon Him and continually returns to Him.

translation: And, O my people, let not your opposition to me bring upon you what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hūd, or the people of Ṣāliḥ; and the people of Lot are not far from you.
interpretation: Shuʿayb warns his people that their hostility toward him and rejection of his message must not lead them to repeat the fate of earlier nations destroyed for persistent disbelief and wrongdoing. The punishment of the people of Lot is presented as a recent and familiar lesson, showing that divine judgment is neither distant nor merely a story of the past.

translation: And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate.
interpretation: This calls people to combine seeking pardon for past sins with a sincere return to God through obedience and reform. His mercy forgives those who turn back, and His affection means that He receives the repentant with care and love.

translation: قالوا: يا شعيب، لا نفهم كثيرًا مما تقول، وإنّا لنراك فينا ضعيفًا، ولولا جماعتك وعشيرتك لرجمناك، وما أنت علينا بعزيز.
interpretation: يكشف قولهم عن عنادٍ لا عن عجزٍ في كلام شعيب؛ فقد استخدموا ادّعاء عدم الفهم ذريعةً لرفض دعوته، واحتقروا مكانته لضعف نفوذه المادي في نظرهم، ثم هدّدوه بالقتل مستندين إلى حماية قومه لا إلى حجة. وهذا يبيّن كيف قد يجعل التعصّب للقوة والجاه الإنسان يرفض الحق ويستبدل البرهان بالتهديد.

translation: He said, “O my people, is my clan more powerful in your eyes than Allah, while you have set Him aside behind your backs? Indeed, my Lord encompasses all that you do.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb reproaches his people for valuing tribal influence and fearing social consequences more than they revere Allah and obey His command. By treating divine authority as something placed behind them, they reveal their heedlessness; yet nothing they do is hidden from Allah, whose complete knowledge and power encompass them.

translation: And, O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. You will soon know who will be struck by a humiliating punishment and who is the liar. So wait; indeed, I am waiting with you.
interpretation: Shuʿayb warns his people that their defiance will not remain without consequence: they may persist in their opposition, while he remains steadfast in obedience and conveying the truth. The outcome will expose the liar and bring disgrace upon those who reject God’s guidance, so both sides are left to await God’s decisive judgment.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shuʿayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, while the blast seized those who did wrong, and they lay lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: When divine judgment arrived, God rescued Shuʿayb and the believers through His mercy, whereas the people who persisted in wrongdoing were overwhelmed by a devastating cry and left motionless in their dwellings. The verse shows that deliverance belongs to those who respond in faith, while stubborn injustice ultimately brings ruin.

translation: As though they had never prospered there. Surely, away with Midian, just as Thamūd was cast away.
interpretation: The people of Midian were destroyed so completely that it seemed they had never inhabited or flourished in their land; their fate is presented as a decisive consequence of rejecting the truth and persisting in wrongdoing, like the fate of Thamūd before them.

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
interpretation: God sent Moses supported by unmistakable miracles and compelling proof, so that his people would recognize the truth of his message and have no valid excuse for rejecting it.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed Pharaoh’s command, and Pharaoh’s command was not rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse condemns blind obedience to political authority: Pharaoh’s influential leaders followed his orders even though those orders led away from truth and sound judgment, showing that power and collective agreement do not make a command righteous.

translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them into the Fire. What an evil place to be led into!
interpretation: Pharaoh’s authority, which appeared powerful in this world, will become a cause of ruin for those who followed him: on the Day of Judgment he will precede them into Hell, and their destination will be the worst possible one.

translation: And they were pursued by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift that is bestowed.
interpretation: Those who persist in tyranny and reject the truth bring upon themselves disgrace in this life and lasting condemnation in the Hereafter; the punishment they receive is a miserable recompense, not an honor or benefit.

translation: That is from the accounts of the towns We relate to you: some of them remain standing, and some have been utterly destroyed.
interpretation: Allah relates the history of past communities to show that their worldly power did not protect them from divine judgment: some nations left enduring traces, while others were completely erased because of their wrongdoing.

translation: We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not benefit them at all when the command of your Lord came; they only increased them in ruin.
interpretation: Allah’s punishment came upon those peoples as a consequence of their own persistent injustice and rejection, not as an act of unfairness. When His decree arrived, the deities they relied upon were utterly powerless to protect them, and their attachment to them brought them nothing but greater destruction.

translation: وهكذا يكون أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة؛ إن أخذه أليم شديد.
interpretation: يبين الله أن إمهال الظالمين لا يعني إهمالهم أو عجزًا عنهم، فإذا جاء وقت المؤاخذة أخذهم أخذًا لا يفلتون منه، وكان عقابه مؤلمًا شديدًا بسبب استمرارهم في الظلم.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which all people will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed by all.
interpretation: The events of past peoples and the consequences of their rejection are a warning to those whose fear of the Hereafter makes them heed divine guidance. The Day of Judgment is uniquely certain and universal: every human being will be assembled for it, and its reality will become manifest to all.

translation: We delay it only for an appointed term.
interpretation: The coming of that moment is postponed only until a precisely determined time known to Allah; its delay is not cancellation, but part of His decree.

translation: On the Day when it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; among them will be the wretched and the blessed.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as one governed entirely by God’s authority: no one may speak or intercede without His permission, and every person’s final state will reveal whether they attained misery or true felicity.

translation: As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; therein they will have sighing and sobbing.
interpretation: Those destined for misery because of their rejection and wrongdoing will remain in Hell, overwhelmed by agonizing breaths and cries that express the severity of their torment.

translation: They will remain therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse affirms the enduring punishment of the people of Hell while emphasizing that its duration remains wholly subject to Allah’s will. Their remaining there is not something that limits or obligates Him; He alone determines what occurs, and nothing can restrain His decree.

translation: As for those who were blessed, they will remain in Paradise, abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure—except as your Lord wills. It is an unceasing gift.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a lasting, secure abode granted by God to those who attained blessedness. The phrase “except as your Lord wills” affirms that all existence remains subject to God’s absolute sovereignty, while “an unceasing gift” indicates that this divine favor will not be withdrawn or interrupted.

translation: So do not be in doubt about what these people worship. They worship only as their forefathers worshipped before them. Indeed, We will surely give them their share in full, without any reduction.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that the false worship of these people is not founded on truth or sound reasoning, but is merely the continuation of inherited tradition. Their persistence does not make their worship valid; rather, God will allow them their appointed portion of worldly consequence and ultimate recompense without withholding anything.

translation: We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but people differed concerning it. Had it not been for a decree that had already gone forth from your Lord, judgment would have been passed between them; indeed, they are in deeply unsettling doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse teaches that disagreement over divine revelation is not evidence of any defect in the revelation itself; rather, it arises from people’s refusal, distortion, or uncertainty. God has decreed to delay the final judgment, allowing them time to choose and act, but their persistent doubt will ultimately be resolved by His decisive judgment.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will surely repay all of them in full for their deeds. Surely, He is fully aware of what they do.
interpretation: God will hold every person accountable without exception, rewarding or requiting them precisely according to their deeds, because nothing they do escapes His complete knowledge.

translation: So remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and those who have turned back with you; and do not transgress. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet and the believers who follow him to maintain unwavering obedience to God, neither deviating from His guidance nor exceeding His limits. True steadfastness is shown through consistent action, while the reminder that God sees all deeds warns that faithfulness and transgression are both fully known to Him.

translation: Do not incline toward those who commit ظلم, lest the Fire touch you; and you will have no protectors besides Allah, then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to show approval, allegiance, or enabling support to oppressors, even if they do not commit the ظلم themselves. Such closeness can compromise one’s faith and expose one to punishment; true protection and help belong only to Allah.

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and during some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds erase misdeeds. This is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: Maintain prayer throughout the day and into the night, for its worship and the good deeds accompanying it cleanse the effects of sins and continually return a person to obedience. This promise should awaken hope and encourage sincere repentance and persistent righteousness, while reminding the mindful that no sincere good deed is without healing effect.

translation: And be patient, for Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in obedience and goodness even when results are delayed or difficulties arise, trusting that Allah preserves and will fully repay every sincere effort.

translation: Why, then, were there not among the generations before you people of virtue who would forbid corruption in the land—except for a few whom We saved? The wrongdoers pursued the luxuries in which they had indulged, and they were criminals.
interpretation: The verse reproaches communities for lacking principled people who resist corruption and restrain wrongdoing. Salvation is associated with those who uphold moral responsibility, while those who become absorbed in comfort and privilege are warned that indulgence can lead them to injustice and ruin.

translation: Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الهلاك العام لا ينزل بالناس لمجرد وجود التقصير، ما دام فيهم إصلاح حقيقي وردٌّ للفساد؛ فالله لا يعاقب جماعةً عقابًا شاملًا مع قيام الصلاح بينهم، وإنما يكون الهلاك عند استحكام الفساد والإصرار عليه.

translation: Had your Lord willed, He could have made all people one community; yet they will continue to differ.
interpretation: God’s leaving people with differing abilities, inclinations, and choices is part of His wisdom and decree. Their differences in belief and conduct are not evidence of any deficiency in divine power, but reflect the freedom and testing through which people are held accountable for the paths they choose.

translation: Except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for this He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: “I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together.”
interpretation: Human beings were created with the capacity to differ, yet divine mercy is granted to those who turn to truth and righteousness; those who persist in rebellion and division fulfill the warning of God and face the consequence He has decreed.

translation: And all that We relate to you of the accounts of the messengers is what We strengthen your heart with. In this has come to you the truth, an admonition, and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: Allah recounts the experiences of earlier messengers to reassure and strengthen the Prophet ﷺ amid opposition, showing that truth ultimately prevails despite hardship. These accounts are not merely historical narratives; they are a clear lesson and a continuing reminder for believers to remain steadfast, trust Allah, and follow the truth.

translation: And say to those who do not believe: “Act according to your position; indeed, we are acting.”
interpretation: This is a warning to the disbelievers that they may persist in their opposition, but the Prophet and the believers will remain steadfast in obedience to Allah; each side will ultimately face the consequences of its chosen path.

translation: And wait; indeed, we are waiting.
interpretation: Persist in your position if you will, for the outcome is awaited by both sides; God’s judgment will ultimately distinguish truth from falsehood and reveal who was upon the right path.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole affair will be returned. So worship Him and place your trust in Him. Your Lord is never unaware of what you do.
interpretation: Since all hidden realities belong to Allah and every matter ultimately returns to His judgment, worship must be directed to Him alone and reliance placed upon Him. This trust does not excuse action; rather, believers should act faithfully, knowing that Allah fully observes their deeds and will judge them with complete knowledge.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif Lām Rā. These are the verses of the Clear Book.
interpretation: The opening letters point to the Qur’an’s divine mystery and challenge, while the verse affirms that what follows is a clear revelation whose guidance and truth are made evident to those who heed it.

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an so that you may understand.
interpretation: Its revelation in clear Arabic makes its guidance accessible to its first audience, inviting them to reflect on its meanings and respond consciously rather than merely recite words they do not comprehend.

translation: We relate to you the finest of narratives through Our revelation of this Qur’an to you, although before it you were certainly among those unaware.
interpretation: Allah clarifies that the Qur’an’s accounts are the most excellent narratives because they are revealed with truth, wisdom, and guidance—not merely for storytelling. The Prophet had not known these realities before revelation, demonstrating that the knowledge he conveyed came from Allah and that people should receive the lessons of these accounts with attentive hearts and trust.

translation: When Joseph said to his father, “My father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating before me.”
interpretation: Joseph’s vision was a sign of the honored position God would later grant him, while the eleven stars represented his brothers and the sun and moon represented his parents. Their prostration signifies their humble acknowledgment of his elevated status, not worship, and the verse foreshadows the fulfillment of God’s promise through Joseph’s future trials and rise to authority.

translation: He said, “My son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you. Indeed, Satan is clearly an enemy to humankind.”
interpretation: Jacob’s counsel to Joseph reflects loving wisdom and prudent discretion: not every blessing or hopeful sign should be disclosed to those who may respond with jealousy. The verse also teaches that Satan exploits envy and hostility to create conflict, so a person should guard both their private gifts and their relationships with caution and trust in God.

translation: “And thus your Lord will choose you, teach you the interpretation of events, and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, just as He completed it before upon your forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Surely your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
interpretation: This verse conveys that Joseph’s coming trials and elevation are part of a deliberate divine choice and preparation. God will grant him the ability to understand the deeper meaning of dreams and events, honor him with guidance and blessing, and extend that favor through the family of Jacob, as He had done with Abraham and Isaac. The closing names of God affirm that this unfolding destiny rests on perfect knowledge and wisdom, even when its purpose is not yet apparent to Joseph.

translation: Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who inquire.
interpretation: The story of Joseph and his brothers contains clear lessons and proofs of God’s wisdom and power for those who sincerely seek understanding and reflect beyond the outward events.

translation: When they said, “Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, even though we are a strong group. Surely our father is clearly mistaken.”
interpretation: The brothers’ jealousy distorted their judgment: they measured their worth by their father’s affection and resented Joseph and his brother for receiving special love. Their confidence in their own numbers and strength led them to accuse their father unjustly, revealing how envy can make a person mistake sincere care for error and turn personal grievance into a conviction of right.

translation: “Kill Joseph or cast him away to some land, so that your father’s attention will be exclusively yours; then afterward you will become righteous people.”
interpretation: This reveals how jealousy distorted Joseph’s brothers’ judgment: they treated removing him as a way to regain their father’s affection, while reassuring themselves that they could repent and become righteous afterward. It exposes the danger of excusing a grave wrong by promising future repentance.

translation: One of them said, “Do not kill Joseph; instead, cast him into the depths of the well, so that some passing travelers may find him, if you are determined to do something.”
interpretation: Even amid their jealousy and hostility, one of Joseph’s brothers proposed a less extreme form of wrongdoing rather than murder. His words show an attempt to restrain their violence while still pursuing their unjust aim of removing Joseph, leaving his fate to travelers who might take him away.

translation: They said, “O our father, why do you not entrust Joseph to us, when we are truly sincere advisers to him?”
interpretation: Joseph’s brothers appeal to their father’s concern by presenting themselves as trustworthy protectors who genuinely seek Joseph’s welfare, while implicitly asking him to set aside his hesitation and allow them to take responsibility for him.

translation: أرسله معنا غدًا يرتع ويلعب، وإنّا له لحافظون.
interpretation: يطلب إخوة يوسف من أبيهم أن يسمح لهم بأخذه معهم بحجة الترفيه واللعب، ويطمئنونه بأنهم سيتولّون حمايته، مع أن هذا الوعد سيُستعمل لاحقًا لخداعه والتدبير لإبعاده.

translation: He said, “It grieves me that you should take him away, and I fear that a wolf may devour him while you are heedless of him.”
interpretation: Jacob expresses his deep attachment to Joseph and his anxiety about entrusting him to his brothers, fearing that their distraction could leave him vulnerable to danger.

translation: They said, “If a wolf were to devour him while we are a strong group, then surely we would be losers.”
interpretation: They tried to reassure their father that, because they were numerous and capable of protecting Joseph, it was inconceivable that a wolf could harm him in their presence; their statement also reveals their awareness that failing to protect him would expose them as negligent and defeated.

translation: So when they took him away and agreed to cast him into the depths of the well, We inspired him: “You will surely inform them of this deed of theirs while they are unaware.”
interpretation: Even in the moment of greatest danger and apparent abandonment, Allah comforted Joseph with the assurance that his suffering would not be the end of his story: he would one day confront his brothers and expose what they had done, while they would not recognize him or realize that the one speaking to them was Joseph.

translation: And they came to their father in the evening, weeping.
interpretation: Their arrival at night, accompanied by exaggerated weeping, portrays an outward display of grief intended to make their father accept their account, even though their actions had concealed the truth.

translation: They said, “Our father, we went off racing one another and left Joseph with our belongings, then the wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us, even if we are telling the truth.”
interpretation: Joseph’s brothers present a fabricated account to conceal what they have done, anticipating that their father will doubt them; their insistence that he would not believe them even if truthful reveals their awareness that their story lacks credibility.

translation: And they came with false blood upon his shirt. He said, “Rather, your own souls have prompted you to do something. So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.”
interpretation: When faced with a painful claim that he knows is untrue, Jacob does not respond with despair or retaliation. He entrusts the matter to Allah, recognizing that enduring the trial with dignified patience and seeking Allah’s help is better than being overcome by grief or responding to falsehood in kind.

translation: And a caravan came, so they sent their water-drawer, and he lowered his bucket. He said, “Good news! Here is a boy.” And they concealed him as merchandise, while Allah was fully aware of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse portrays how Yusuf’s rescue from the well came through an ordinary human event that was nevertheless within Allah’s providence. The travelers’ decision to treat him as merchandise reveals their greed and moral wrongdoing, but their concealment could not escape Allah’s knowledge or alter His unfolding decree for Yusuf.

translation: And they sold him for a meager price—just a few silver coins—and they had little regard for him.
interpretation: The verse portrays how Joseph, despite his true worth and the great destiny Allah had prepared for him, was treated by those who sold him as something insignificant and cheaply disposable. Human judgment may undervalue a person, but it cannot diminish the worth or outcome Allah has ordained for them.

translation: And the man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, “Treat his stay honorably; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.” Thus We established Joseph in the land, so that We might teach him the interpretation of events. Allah prevails in carrying out His command, but most people do not know.
interpretation: Although Joseph appeared to be merely a purchased servant, Allah was directing his circumstances toward honor, authority, and knowledge. The kindness of the Egyptian household became a means within this divine plan, showing that Allah’s decree unfolds beyond what people can perceive, and that apparent hardship may lead to a greater purpose known only to Him.

translation: And when he reached full maturity, We granted him sound judgment and knowledge. Thus do We reward those who do good.
interpretation: When a person reaches intellectual and moral maturity, sincere excellence in conduct becomes a means by which God grants deeper wisdom and understanding. The verse portrays Joseph’s development as both a divine gift and a reward for his steadfast goodness, teaching that true knowledge and sound judgment are blessings bestowed upon those who live righteously.

translation: The woman in whose house he was tried to seduce him. She bolted the doors and said, “Come to me.” He said, “God forbid! He is my master, who has given me a good home. Surely the wrongdoers will never prosper.”
interpretation: Joseph refuses the seduction because he recognizes both the sacred prohibition of betrayal and the trust placed in him by the man who sheltered him. His appeal to God shows that moral steadfastness comes from reverence for Him, while his final statement affirms that wrongdoing may appear attractive or advantageous for a moment, but cannot lead to true success.

translation: She certainly desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus We turned away from him evil and indecency; indeed, he was among Our chosen servants.
interpretation: Joseph was exposed to a severe temptation, yet God granted him clear spiritual insight that restrained him before he committed any wrongdoing. His refusal was not merely personal strength but divine protection, demonstrating that sincere devotion preserves a servant from evil and immoral conduct.

translation: And they both raced toward the door, and she tore his shirt from the back. They found her master at the door. She said, “What should be the punishment of one who intended evil toward your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”
interpretation: In her attempt to conceal her own wrongdoing, the woman falsely accused Joseph and sought to have him punished. Yet the torn shirt from the back was a clear sign that he had been fleeing from her, exposing the truth of his innocence and the danger of judging without examining the evidence.

translation: He said, “She tried to seduce me.” And a witness from her household testified: “If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is among the liars.”
interpretation: Joseph defended himself by declaring that the woman had sought to seduce him. A witness from her family proposed an impartial physical test: a tear in the front of his shirt would indicate that he had been resisting her approach, supporting her claim; its absence—or a tear elsewhere—would expose her accusation as false. The verse illustrates how truth may be established through clear evidence rather than mere competing assertions.

translation: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is among the truthful.
interpretation: The direction of the tear serves as clear evidence: a garment ripped from behind indicates that he was fleeing while she pursued him, exposing her accusation as false and confirming his innocence.

translation: So when he saw that his shirt had been torn from the back, he said, “Indeed, this is part of your scheming; truly, your scheming is formidable.”
interpretation: The torn back of Joseph’s shirt revealed that he had been fleeing while she pursued him, exposing her accusation as false. The statement condemns the deceptive plot being employed to conceal wrongdoing, while highlighting how powerful and dangerous such manipulation can be when driven by desire and deceit.

translation: Joseph, turn away from this; and you, seek forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you have been among those who were at fault.
interpretation: The husband recognized Joseph’s innocence and sought to contain the matter discreetly: Joseph was told not to pursue or publicize what had occurred, while his wife was urged to repent and ask God’s forgiveness for attempting to seduce him.

translation: And women in the city said, “The wife of the governor is seeking to seduce her young servant; she has been overcome with love for him. Indeed, we see her in clear error.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how the women of the city spread the news of the governor’s wife and judged her conduct as morally misguided. Their words reveal that her passion had deeply overtaken her heart, while also introducing the social pressure and scrutiny surrounding Joseph’s situation.

translation: So when she heard of their plotting, she invited them, prepared for them a banquet, gave each of them a knife, and said to Joseph, “Come out before them.” When they saw him, they were utterly captivated by him and cut their hands, saying, “Allah is far above this! This is no human being; he is nothing but a noble angel.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how overwhelming beauty can distract people from awareness and self-control: the women were so astonished by Joseph’s appearance that they injured themselves without noticing. Their exclamation does not make Joseph divine; it expresses their extreme admiration by comparing his extraordinary beauty to that of a noble angel.

translation: She said, “This is the one concerning whom you blamed me. Indeed, I tried to seduce him, but he firmly resisted. Yet if he does not do what I command him, he will certainly be imprisoned and will surely be among the humiliated.”
interpretation: The woman openly admits her attempt to seduce Joseph and acknowledges his moral steadfastness, but her pride and desire for control lead her to threaten him with imprisonment when he refuses her. The verse contrasts Joseph’s chosen purity with the abuse of power and coercion used against him.

translation: He said, “My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to. If You do not turn their scheming away from me, I may incline toward them and become one of the ignorant.”
interpretation: Joseph prefers the hardship of imprisonment to disobedience and openly acknowledges that steadfastness depends on God’s protection. His prayer shows humility: he does not trust only in his own strength, but seeks God’s help to resist temptation and remain guided.

translation: So his Lord answered him and turned away from him their scheme. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse shows that God responded to Joseph’s sincere supplication by protecting him from temptation and its consequences. God hears the believer’s prayer and knows the truth of his intentions, his weakness, and the dangers surrounding him; therefore, relying on Him is a means of steadfastness and deliverance.

translation: Then it seemed best to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time.
interpretation: Despite recognizing Joseph’s innocence through the clear signs, they chose to imprison him to protect their reputation and conceal the scandal, showing how social pressure and fear of disgrace can lead people to ignore the truth.

translation: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, “I see myself pressing wine,” and the other said, “I see myself carrying bread on my head, from which the birds are eating. Tell us its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of those who do good.”
interpretation: The two prisoners recognized Joseph’s wisdom and righteousness and turned to him for guidance, revealing that true goodness and trustworthiness can make a person a source of hope even in the darkest circumstances.

translation: He said, “No food that you are provided with will come to you without my informing you of its interpretation before it comes to you. This is part of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have forsaken the way of a people who do not believe in Allah, and who are deniers of the Hereafter.”
interpretation: Joseph explains that his insight is not personal power or occult knowledge, but a gift taught to him by Allah. By mentioning this before interpreting the prisoners’ dreams, he directs their attention from curiosity about the unseen to the faith that grants true understanding, while declaring his rejection of disbelief in Allah and the Hereafter.

translation: And I have followed the way of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from Allah’s فضل upon us and upon people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: Joseph affirms that true faith is the inherited path of the prophets: exclusive devotion to Allah and rejection of every form of شرك. He regards this monotheism not as a personal achievement, but as a فضل granted by Allah to him, his forefathers, and humanity at large. Yet people often fail to recognize this gift through gratitude—by acknowledging Allah’s oneness and living in obedience to Him.

translation: O my two companions in prison, are separate and diverse lords better, or Allah—the One, the Supreme Overpowering?
interpretation: Joseph calls them to recognize that worshipping many supposed gods is irrational and degrading, because true authority and power belong solely to Allah, whose oneness and absolute dominion leave no room for rivals.

translation: You worship nothing besides Him except names that you and your forefathers have invented; Allah has sent down no authority for them. Judgment belongs only to Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse teaches that false gods possess no real authority or divine reality; they are merely labels inherited from human tradition. Since ultimate authority and the right to be worshipped belong solely to Allah, true religion is founded on sincere devotion to Him alone and on rejecting beliefs unsupported by revelation, even when they are widely accepted.

translation: يا صاحبي السجن، أما أحدكما فيسقي ربَّه خمراً، وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه؛ قُضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان.
interpretation: يُخبر يوسف صاحبيه بأن تأويل رؤياهما قد حُسم بقدر الله: سينجو أحدهما فيعود إلى خدمة سيده وسقايته الخمر، أما الآخر فسيُقتل صلباً، فلا مجال لتغيير ما قُدِّر بعد صدور الحكم الإلهي.

translation: And he said to the one of the two whom he thought would be saved, “Mention me to your master.” But Satan caused him to forget mentioning him to his master, so he remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: Joseph asked the cupbearer to tell the king about his innocence and situation, but the cupbearer forgot him after being released. Thus, by God’s decree, Joseph’s imprisonment continued for several years, teaching that deliverance may be delayed even when one takes the available means, until the appointed time arrives.

translation: And the king said, “Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of grain and others dry. O assembly, explain my dream to me, if you are able to interpret dreams.”
interpretation: This vision signifies that a period of seven years of prosperity will be followed by seven years of severe famine. It is a divine warning that abundance should be managed wisely and preserved in preparation for future hardship.

translation: They said, “They are confused dreams, and we are not knowledgeable in interpreting dreams.”
interpretation: The king’s officials regarded his troubling vision as a jumble of meaningless dream-images and, lacking the insight to understand it, acknowledged their inability to interpret it.

translation: وقال الذي نجا من الرجلين وتذكّر بعد مدة: أنا أخبركم بتأويل هذه الرؤيا، فأرسلوني.
interpretation: يفيد ذلك أن تذكّر الساقي لتعبير يوسف عليه السلام جاء في الوقت الذي احتاج فيه الملك إلى تفسير رؤياه، فكان تمهيدًا لإظهار علم يوسف وبراءته وإخراجه من السجن بإذن الله.

translation: “Joseph, O truthful one, tell us the meaning of seven fat cows devoured by seven lean cows, and seven green ears of grain and others dry, so that I may return to the people and perhaps they may come to know.”
interpretation: The king’s cupbearer turns to Joseph, acknowledging his truthfulness and insight, to seek a clear explanation of the troubling dream. His request reflects the need for sound knowledge to guide people through an uncertain future and prepare them wisely for what lies ahead.

translation: He said, “You will cultivate for seven consecutive years. Whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except for a little of what you eat.”
interpretation: Joseph instructs them to manage the years of abundance with disciplined foresight: preserve most of the grain in its husks so it remains protected and available for the coming hardship, while taking only what is necessary for immediate consumption.

translation: Then after that will come seven difficult years, which will consume what you have stored for them, except a little of what you preserve.
interpretation: This foretells seven years of severe famine that will exhaust the grain gathered during the preceding years of abundance, while urging people to preserve a carefully managed reserve rather than consume all their supplies.

translation: Then, after that, there will come a year in which people will receive abundant rain and relief, and in which they will press their produce.
interpretation: After the seven years of hardship, God will restore prosperity to the people through rain and abundant provision, enabling them to resume agriculture and extract the fruits of their harvests.

translation: And the king said, “Bring him to me.” Then when the messenger came to him, Joseph said, “Return to your master and ask him what happened to the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is fully aware of their scheme.”
interpretation: Joseph does not leave prison merely because the king has summoned him; he insists that the truth about the women’s accusation be made public first. This shows his dignity, patience, and commitment to clearing his name, while affirming that God was fully aware of the deception directed against him.

translation: قال: «ما شأنكنّ حين راودتنَّ يوسفَ عن نفسه؟» قلن: «حاشَ لله، ما علمنا عليه من سوء». قالت امرأة العزيز: «الآن ظهر الحقُّ جليًّا؛ أنا راودتُه عن نفسه، وإنه لمن الصادقين».
interpretation: يُظهر هذا الموقف انكشاف الحقيقة وبراءة يوسف عليه السلام بعد اعتراف امرأة العزيز، كما يبيّن أن الصدق والثبات أمام الفتنة يرفعان عن الإنسان التهمة، وأن الحق قد يتأخر ظهوره لكنه لا يضيع.

translation: “That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the schemes of the treacherous.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that truth and integrity ultimately prevail: a person who remains faithful even when unseen is protected by Allah, while deceitful schemes are deprived of His guidance and cannot achieve lasting success.

translation: “And I do not claim my soul to be free of fault; surely the soul is ever inclined toward evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that human beings should not trust their own inner impulses or assume themselves immune to wrongdoing, because the soul can strongly incline toward desire and sin.
