Protection from this tendency comes only through Allah’s mercy, while sincere repentance and reliance on His forgiveness keep a person from despair and self-righteousness.

translation: And the king said, “Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively to my service.” Then, when he spoke with him, he said, “Today you are firmly established with us and fully trusted.”
interpretation: The verse shows that Joseph’s innocence, wisdom, and dignified speech became evident when he met the king. Recognizing his exceptional character and ability, the king chose to draw him close, granting him authority and security. It also indicates that genuine merit can restore a person’s honor and elevate them to a position of trust after a period of unjust hardship.

translation: He said, “Appoint me over the storehouses of the land; indeed, I am a trustworthy guardian and knowledgeable.”
interpretation: Joseph’s request was not driven by ambition, but by his awareness of the responsibility required to protect the nation’s provisions and manage them wisely during the coming years of famine. He openly stated his qualifications because assuming public responsibility is justified when it serves the people and the capable person is uniquely suited to it.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land, settling wherever he wished. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.
interpretation: Allah enabled Joseph, after his trials, to attain authority and stability in the land, granting him freedom and means to act according to his wisdom. This establishment was not merely the result of worldly causes, but a manifestation of divine mercy. The verse teaches that sincere goodness is never lost: even when its reward is delayed and a person passes through hardship, Allah preserves its value and grants honor and relief in the way He wills.

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and remain mindful of Allah.
interpretation: True faith and reverence for Allah lead a person to prioritize the lasting reward of the Hereafter over the temporary gains of this world; that eternal reward is superior in value and permanence.

translation: And Joseph’s brothers came and entered before him, and he recognized them, while they did not recognize him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reversal brought about by God’s providence: Joseph, once cast away and separated from his family, now stands in a position of authority before the very brothers who wronged him, while they remain unaware of his identity.

translation: When he had provided them with their supplies, he said, “Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?”
interpretation: After treating his brothers generously and ensuring they received their full due, Joseph asked them to bring their paternal brother so that he could verify their claim and extend the same hospitality and provision to him. His words combine a request with a reminder of his fairness, generosity, and trustworthy administration.

translation: “But if you do not bring him to me, then you shall have no measure from me, nor shall you come near me.”
interpretation: Joseph makes bringing his brother a firm condition for receiving further provisions: without fulfilling this trust, they will receive no additional allotment and will lose access to him altogether.

translation: They said, “We will try to persuade his father to let him go, and we will surely do so.”
interpretation: The brothers assured Joseph that they would make every effort to convince their father to allow Benjamin to accompany them, expressing confidence in their ability to fulfill this promise.

translation: And he said to his servants, “Put their merchandise back in their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their family, so that they may come back.”
interpretation: Joseph instructed that their payment be secretly returned as an act of generosity and as a means of encouraging them to come back for another provision, trusting that when they discovered it upon returning home, they would be moved to return.

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, “Our father, the measure of grain has been denied to us, so send our brother with us that we may receive our measure. Indeed, we will surely protect him.”
interpretation: They sought to persuade their father to let Benjamin accompany them by presenting the practical consequence of the governor’s condition: without their brother, they would receive no further provisions. Their promise to protect him was meant to reassure Jacob, though the verse also exposes the tension between their confident pledge and the painful history surrounding Joseph, reminding us that assurances must be proven through faithful action.

translation: He said, “Should I entrust him to you as I entrusted his brother to you before? Yet Allah is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Jacob’s words express both understandable caution—shaped by the loss of Joseph—and his ultimate reliance on Allah. Human assurances are limited, whereas Allah alone provides perfect protection and mercy, so trust in Him must remain greater than trust in people.

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found that their goods had been returned to them. They said, “Our father, what more can we ask for? Here are our goods, returned to us. We can obtain provisions for our family, protect our brother, and receive an additional camel-load. That is an easy measure.”
interpretation: The brothers use the returned payment as evidence that they can obtain provisions without loss: by taking their brother with them, they will secure food for their household, safeguard him during the journey, and receive an extra measure. Their words appeal to their father’s practical concerns while revealing their eagerness to fulfill the governor’s condition.

translation: He said, “I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn covenant in Allah’s name that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are completely overwhelmed.” When they gave him their covenant, he said, “Allah is Guardian over what we say.”
interpretation: Jacob would not entrust Benjamin to his sons without a binding oath before Allah, reflecting his rightful caution after their earlier betrayal. He acknowledged that the promise applied as far as human ability extended, while any circumstance beyond their control lay with Allah. By declaring Allah their Guardian, he reminded them that their pledge was not merely to him but was fully known and answerable to Allah.

translation: And he said, “My sons, do not enter through one gate; enter through different gates. I cannot avail you against Allah in any way. Judgment belongs only to Allah. Upon Him I rely, and upon Him let those who rely place their reliance.”
interpretation: Jacob advises his sons to take prudent measures to protect themselves, while affirming that such measures have no power independent of Allah’s decree. True reliance means using lawful means without depending on them, entrusting the outcome entirely to Allah, whose judgment alone governs what occurs.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had instructed them, it could not avail them against Allah in the least; it was only a need within Jacob’s heart that he fulfilled. Indeed, he possessed knowledge because We had taught him, but most people do not know.
interpretation: Jacob’s advice to enter through separate gates was a prudent measure born of his concern for his sons, but it could not alter Allah’s decree. The verse teaches that taking reasonable precautions is part of human responsibility, while protection and outcomes ultimately remain in Allah’s hands; true understanding recognizes both realities.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother into his arms and said, “Indeed, I am your brother, so do not grieve over what they used to do.”
interpretation: Joseph revealed his true identity to his brother privately and comforted him, assuring him that the harm inflicted by their brothers in the past should no longer cause him distress, for their family bond and God’s providential plan had brought them together again.

translation: So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he placed the drinking cup in his brother’s saddlebag. Then a caller announced: “O caravan, you are surely thieves!”
interpretation: After providing the brothers with what they needed, Joseph secretly placed the king’s cup among Benjamin’s belongings. The announcement of theft was then made to set in motion the plan by which Benjamin would remain with him, while the brothers were confronted with the consequences of their suspected crime.

translation: They said, turning toward them, “What is it that you are missing?”
interpretation: The travelers confronted the heralds with a question meant to clarify the accusation, asking them to identify the lost object before any blame was placed upon them.

translation: قالوا: نفتقد مكيالَ الملك، ولمن يأتي به حِملُ بعير، وأنا ضامنٌ لذلك.
interpretation: يعلن المنادون أن مكيال الملك قد فُقد، ويحفّزون على إعادته بجعل مكافأةٍ قدرها حمل بعير لمن يعثر عليه، مع تأكيد المتحدث التزامه بضمان هذه المكافأة والوفاء بها.

translation: They said, “By Allah, you surely know that we did not come to spread corruption in the land, nor are we thieves.”
interpretation: They swear to affirm their innocence, reminding those questioning them that their conduct and purpose have never been that of people who cause harm or steal; thus they reject the accusation with a solemn appeal to what is already known about them.

translation: They said, “What shall be the punishment for it, if you are lying?”
interpretation: يطلبون تحديد العقوبة التي يستحقها من وُجد المتاع في رحله إن ثبت كذبهم، فيُلزمون أنفسهم بالحكم الذي سيُطبَّق عند ظهور الحقيقة.

translation: They said, “Its recompense is that whoever is found in whose saddlebag it is shall himself be its recompense. Thus do We requite the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: They acknowledged that, according to the law they had accepted, the person in whose baggage the lost vessel was discovered would be held as the penalty for the theft. This statement established the basis for retaining Joseph’s brother, while affirming that wrongdoing deserves a fitting consequence.

translation: So he began searching their bags before searching his brother’s bag, then he brought it out from his brother’s bag. Thus We devised a plan for Joseph. He could not have detained his brother under the king’s law unless Allah willed. We raise in rank whom We will, and above everyone possessed of knowledge is One who is more knowing.
interpretation: Allah enabled Joseph to arrange matters wisely so that his brother could remain with him without injustice or deception for its own sake. The event shows that divine wisdom may work through lawful means and careful planning beyond what people perceive, while every degree of knowledge and authority remains limited beneath Allah’s perfect knowledge.

translation: They said, “If he has stolen, then a brother of his stole before.” But Joseph kept it within himself and did not disclose it to them. He said, “You are worse in situation, and Allah knows best what you allege.”
interpretation: When Joseph’s brothers sought to justify their suspicion by recalling the supposed theft of his brother, Joseph restrained himself from exposing their past wrongdoing or answering them harshly. His inward response—that they were in a worse position—reflects the moral truth that their accusation and false characterization were more blameworthy than the act they alleged, while the closing statement entrusts the full judgment of their claims to Allah, who knows what is true and what is fabricated.

translation: They said, “O noble minister, he has an aged father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of those who do good.”
interpretation: They appealed to the minister’s compassion, emphasizing the deep hardship that their elderly father would suffer if his son were detained. Their offer to substitute one of themselves reflects their willingness to bear the consequence in his place, while their reference to his goodness respectfully urges him to respond with mercy.

translation: He said, “God forbid that we take anyone except the one with whom we found our property. Indeed, if we did so, we would be wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The speaker refuses to detain an innocent person in place of the one whose possession contains the property, recognizing that such an act would violate justice and make them wrongdoers.

translation: When they despaired of him, they withdrew to confer privately. Their eldest said, “Do you not know that your father has taken a solemn pledge from you before Allah? And before this, you failed concerning Joseph. So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me; and He is the best of judges.”
interpretation: Having exhausted every effort to secure Benjamin’s release, the brothers retreat in grief and private counsel. Their eldest brother recognizes that they are bound by a covenant with their father and that their earlier betrayal of Joseph has already brought them lasting shame. Unlike before, he refuses to escape or conceal what happened; he accepts responsibility, remains where the crisis occurred, and entrusts the outcome to his father’s decision and Allah’s judgment, demonstrating repentance, accountability, and patience in adversity.

translation: Return to your father and say, “Our father, indeed your son has stolen. We testify only to what we know, and we were not guardians of the unseen.”
interpretation: They instructed one another to report the incident honestly while limiting their testimony to what they had directly witnessed. Their words acknowledge that human knowledge is restricted and that they cannot affirm what lies beyond their observation; ultimate knowledge of hidden matters belongs to God alone.

translation: “And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan with which we came; indeed, we are truthful.”
interpretation: Joseph’s brothers urge their father to verify their account through the people of the town and the members of the caravan who witnessed what happened, presenting external testimony to assure him that they are truthful about Benjamin’s detention.

translation: He said, “Rather, your souls have prompted you to do something. So patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them all back to me. Indeed, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: Jacob recognizes that his sons’ account is shaped by their own actions and does not allow grief to turn him toward despair or accusation. He responds with steadfast, dignified patience, preserving hope that Allah will reunite him with Joseph, Benjamin, and their brother, because Allah’s complete knowledge and perfect wisdom govern what remains hidden from him.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, “Alas, my sorrow over Joseph!” His eyes became white from grief, while he was filled with suppressed anguish.
interpretation: This portrays Jacob’s profound love and sorrow over Joseph’s absence. His grief affected him physically, yet he endured it with restraint, keeping his anguish within rather than responding with despair or rebellion against Allah.

translation: They said, “By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you waste away or become one of those who perish.”
interpretation: His family reproached him for allowing grief over Joseph to consume him, believing that his relentless sorrow would lead to severe weakness or even death.

translation: He said, “I only complain of my anguish and sorrow to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.”
interpretation: This expresses that profound grief should be entrusted to God rather than turned into despair or resentment toward people. The believer may feel sorrow deeply while remaining certain that God knows the hidden reality of events, possesses wisdom beyond human perception, and can bring relief and reunion from circumstances that appear hopeless.

translation: O my sons, go and search for Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, none despairs of Allah’s mercy except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: Jacob urges his sons to continue seeking Joseph and his brother while maintaining hope in Allah’s mercy and relief. Despair reflects a refusal to trust in Allah’s power and wisdom, whereas faith requires persevering through hardship with hope, even when circumstances seem impossible.

translation: So when they entered upon him, they said, “O exalted one, hardship has afflicted us and our family, and we have brought only meager merchandise. So give us the full measure and be charitable to us. Surely Allah rewards those who give charity.”
interpretation: The brothers appeal to Joseph’s compassion after their severe distress has humbled them. They acknowledge that what they offer is of little value, yet ask him not to withhold provision because of it, invoking generosity and the divine reward promised to those who show mercy. The verse highlights how genuine need calls for kindness beyond strict commercial exchange.

translation: He said, “Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?”
interpretation: Joseph gently confronted his brothers with the harm they had caused him and Benjamin, attributing their wrongdoing to the blindness and immaturity of ignorance, while inviting them to recognize their guilt and repent.

translation: They said, “Are you indeed Joseph?” He said, “I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly bestowed His favor upon us. Indeed, whoever is mindful of Allah and patient, surely Allah does not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.”
interpretation: Joseph reveals his identity without arrogance, attributing his deliverance and reunion with his brother to Allah’s favor. His words teach that steadfast obedience and patience through hardship ultimately lead to Allah’s just reward and vindication.

translation: They said, “By Allah, Allah has certainly favored you over us, and indeed we were sinners.”
interpretation: Joseph’s brothers openly acknowledge that God granted him a higher rank and honor, while confessing that their past actions against him were wrongful and sinful.

translation: He said, “There is no blame upon you today. May Allah forgive you; He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Joseph عليه السلام responds to his brothers’ wrongdoing with complete forgiveness, removing both reproach and humiliation from them. His words reflect noble character: he does not deny that harm occurred, but chooses reconciliation over retaliation and entrusts their ultimate forgiveness to Allah, whose mercy surpasses all mercy.

translation: “Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father’s face; he will regain his sight. Then bring me all your family.”
interpretation: Joseph’s instruction expresses his confidence in God’s power to restore his father’s sight and reveals his longing for a complete family reunion after years of separation; the shirt becomes a means through which God brings healing and hope.

translation: ولما انطلقت القافلة قال أبوهم: «إني لأجد رائحة يوسف، لولا أن تنسبوني إلى الخَرَف أو تظنوني واهمًا».
interpretation: يُظهر يعقوب عليه السلام يقينًا عميقًا بقرب الفرج وعودة يوسف، حتى أحسّ بأثره رغم بُعد المسافة، بينما خشي أن يفسّر أهله كلامه على أنه ناشئ عن شدة الحزن أو اختلال الرأي.

translation: They said, “By Allah, you are surely still in your old error.”
interpretation: They regarded Jacob’s persistent grief for Joseph and his continued hope of finding him as misguided and excessive, unaware that his conviction was grounded in faith and insight rather than mere emotion.

translation: Then, when the bearer of good news came, he cast it over his face, and he regained his sight. He said, “Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?”
interpretation: The return of Jacob’s sight through Joseph’s garment manifests the fulfillment of divine promise and the truth of Jacob’s unwavering hope. His words rebuke his sons’ limited judgment: his certainty was grounded in knowledge and trust granted by Allah, even when the circumstances appeared to contradict it.

translation: They said, “O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed, we were sinners.”
interpretation: After recognizing the harm they had caused, Joseph’s brothers humbly turned to their father, acknowledging their wrongdoing and asking him to seek God’s forgiveness for them. Their words express sincere remorse and the need to confront one’s guilt rather than conceal it.

translation: He said, “I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
interpretation: Jacob responds to his sons with compassion, promising to seek God’s forgiveness for them and directing their hope toward God’s boundless mercy rather than allowing their past wrongdoing to define their relationship with Him.

translation: Then, when they entered upon Joseph, he embraced his parents and said, “Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security.”
interpretation: Joseph’s welcoming embrace expresses the fulfillment of God’s promise after years of separation and hardship. By linking their safety to Allah’s will, he acknowledges that true security and the realization of blessings come only through divine protection.

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they all fell before him in prostration. He said, “O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream from before. My Lord has made it come true. He has certainly been gracious to me: He brought me out of prison and brought you here from the desert after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is subtle in bringing about whatever He wills. Surely He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: Joseph recognizes that the fulfillment of his childhood dream was brought about by God’s wise and gentle plan through every stage of his hardship. Rather than dwelling on the wrong his brothers committed, he attributes their estrangement to Satan’s incitement, showing forgiveness and restraint. His words teach that divine care may work quietly through trials, delay, and unexpected turns until God’s purpose is realized.

translation: My Lord, You have indeed granted me sovereignty and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die in submission to You and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This is Joseph’s prayer of humble gratitude: despite receiving authority and special knowledge, he recognizes that every blessing comes from God and that true security lies only in God’s guardianship. He therefore asks not for worldly increase, but for steadfast submission until death and for companionship with the righteous in the Hereafter.

translation: That is from the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they resolved their affair and were plotting.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the account of Joseph and his brothers was revealed knowledge, not something the Prophet learned by witnessing it or from human sources. The verse also exposes the brothers’ concealed plotting and shows that divine revelation discloses realities hidden from people, while reminding that God fully knows every secret plan.

translation: Yet most people, however eagerly you may desire it, will not be believers.
interpretation: Even the sincere efforts and deep concern of a messenger cannot compel people to believe; faith comes only when people respond sincerely to the truth and accept God’s guidance.

translation: You do not ask them for any reward for it; it is only a reminder for all worlds.
interpretation: The message is presented with no demand for worldly compensation, demonstrating that its purpose is sincere guidance and remembrance of God for all people, not personal gain.

translation: How many a sign there is in the heavens and the earth that they pass by while turning away from it.
interpretation: Countless signs of Allah’s power, wisdom, and oneness are present throughout creation, yet many people encounter them without reflection or humility; their physical seeing does not benefit them because they deliberately turn their hearts away from the truth.

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating partners with Him.
interpretation: Many people acknowledge Allah as their Creator and Lord, yet their faith is corrupted by associating others with Him in worship, reliance, obedience, or attribution of divine power. True faith requires affirming Allah’s oneness and directing worship exclusively to Him.

translation: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتةً وهم لا يشعرون؟
interpretation: في الآية إنكارٌ على من اغترّ بإمهاله وظنّ أنه بمنأى عن العقوبة؛ فالله يحذّر من أن ينزل به عذابٌ شامل، أو تقوم الساعة فجأة قبل أن يتنبه أو يستعد، ولذلك لا ينبغي للإنسان أن يؤخر التوبة والعمل الصالح اعتمادًا على طول الأمل.

translation: Say, “This is my way: I call to Allah with clear insight—I and those who follow me. Glory be to Allah, and I am not one of the polytheists.”
interpretation: The verse directs the Messenger and all who follow him to make calling people to Allah their path, grounded in knowledge, certainty, and sound understanding rather than speculation or blind imitation. It also teaches that this mission belongs to Allah alone, while declaring Him free of all imperfection and affirming complete rejection of associating partners with Him.

translation: And We sent before you only men to whom We revealed, from among the inhabitants of the towns. Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who came before them? The abode of the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of God. Will you not then reason?
interpretation: The verse affirms that God’s messengers were human beings chosen from settled communities, so their humanity is not a reason to reject their revelation. It urges people to learn from the ruins and history of earlier nations who denied the truth, recognizing that worldly power and prosperity do not determine ultimate success. True success belongs to those who remain mindful of God, because the reward of the Hereafter is lasting and superior to every temporary worldly gain.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and We saved whom We willed. And Our punishment cannot be averted from the guilty people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine relief may come at the very point when the trial reaches its utmost intensity and the messengers seem to have no remaining worldly means of support. Their eventual deliverance demonstrates that victory belongs solely to God: He saves those who remain worthy of salvation, while no power can repel His judgment from those who persist in guilt.

translation: Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for people of understanding. This is not a fabricated account, but a confirmation of what came before it, an explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The accounts of the prophets are presented as truthful revelation whose events carry enduring lessons for those who reflect. They confirm the essential truths of earlier divine scriptures, clarify what people need for faith and right conduct, and become a source of guidance and mercy for those who receive them with sincere belief.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rā. These are the verses of the Book. What has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an revealed to the Prophet ﷺ is the certain truth from Allah. The disjointed letters draw attention to the miraculous nature of the revelation, composed of the very letters familiar to people, while their widespread refusal to believe does not diminish its truth.

translation: Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then established Himself above the Throne. He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for an appointed term. He governs every affair and makes the signs clear, so that you may be certain of meeting your Lord.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to recognize Allah’s absolute power, wisdom, and authority through the ordered structure of creation. The heavens, the sun, and the moon do not operate independently; they remain subject to His command and continue according to limits He has appointed. By managing the universe and clarifying His signs, Allah calls people to move beyond observing creation to certainty that life has a purpose and that they will ultimately return to their Lord.

translation: And He is the One who spread out the earth, placed upon it firm mountains and rivers, and made in it two kinds of every fruit. He causes the night to cover the day. Surely in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: Allah’s ordering of the earth, its mountains, flowing waters, diverse fruits, and the continual alternation of night and day reveals deliberate wisdom and sustaining power. These signs invite thoughtful people to recognize that creation is governed by one purposeful Creator, not by chance or competing powers.

translation: And on the earth are adjacent tracts, gardens of grapevines, crops, and date palms—some growing from a single root and others from separate roots—watered by the same water. Yet We make some of them more excellent than others in taste. Surely in that are signs for people who understand.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection on how one earth, one water, and similar conditions produce remarkably different plants and fruits in form, quality, and taste. This ordered diversity points to the Creator’s wisdom and power, and teaches that outwardly similar causes do not act independently but produce their effects by God’s will; those who use reason recognize this as evidence of His oneness and purposeful creation.

translation: And if you are amazed, then amazing indeed is their saying: “When we have become dust, will we truly be in a new creation?” Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord. And those are the ones with shackles around their necks; they are the companions of the Fire, remaining there forever.
interpretation: The verse presents the denial of resurrection as the real cause for astonishment: people accept the wonder of their first creation yet reject the possibility of being recreated after death. Their refusal is not merely an intellectual mistake but a rejection of their Lord, which spiritually binds them through stubbornness and leaves them subject to the lasting consequence of the Fire.

translation: They urge you to bring about evil before good, though exemplary punishments have already occurred before them. Surely your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing, and surely your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who mockingly demand the punishment they have been warned about instead of seeking the mercy and guidance represented by the promised good. God nevertheless gives wrongdoers time and forgiveness rather than hastening their punishment, yet this forbearance must not be mistaken for approval or safety, because persistent injustice ultimately meets His severe and just retribution.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” You are only a warner, and every people has a guide.
interpretation: The deniers demand a miracle as though faith depended on spectacle, but the Prophet’s essential mission is to warn and convey God’s message; guidance is provided to every community through the means God appoints, so rejection cannot be justified by claiming that they were left without guidance.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase; and everything with Him is determined according to a precise measure.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge encompasses every hidden detail of creation, including the stages and variations of pregnancy, and that nothing occurs randomly or beyond His wisdom and precise decree.

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the manifest, the Most Great, the Most Exalted.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything hidden from creation and everything openly perceived, while His greatness and exaltedness are absolute; nothing is beyond His knowledge or above His authority.

translation: Whether any of you conceals his speech or voices it, and whether he hides himself by night or goes openly forth by day.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses every person completely: what they conceal in their hearts and speech, what they make known, and all their actions whether hidden in the darkness of night or visible in the daylight. Nothing about them escapes His awareness.

translation: For each person are angels in succession, before him and behind him, guarding him by Allah’s command. Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. And when Allah wills harm for a people, none can avert it, nor do they have any protector besides Him.
interpretation: Allah has appointed angels to watch over people by His command, yet people remain responsible for the direction of their lives. Divine change in a community is connected to the change of its inner beliefs, intentions, and conduct: when they reform themselves through faith and obedience, Allah can transform their condition; when they turn toward corruption, they expose themselves to its consequences. Once Allah decrees harm for a people because of their persistent wrongdoing, no power can repel it, and no one besides Him can truly protect them.

translation: He is the One who shows you lightning, causing fear and hope, and brings forth heavy clouds.
interpretation: Allah displays lightning as a sign of His power: it awakens fear of His might and of the storm, while also inspiring hope for the rain and benefit carried by the heavy clouds.

translation: The thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and the angels do so out of awe of Him. He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, yet they dispute concerning Allah, while He is mighty in power.
interpretation: The verse portrays the forces of nature and the angels as submitting to and magnifying Allah, while human beings may still argue against Him despite the unmistakable signs of His power. The thunderbolts demonstrate that His will is absolute and that no one can resist or escape His overwhelming authority.

translation: To Him belongs the true supplication. Those whom they invoke besides Him do not answer them in anything—except as one who stretches out his hands toward water, hoping it will reach his mouth, though it will never reach it. The supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.
interpretation: Only Allah possesses the power to answer prayer and bring about what is truly sought. Calling upon beings besides Him is futile: it resembles a thirsty person reaching toward water without bringing it to his mouth. Such reliance is misdirected and leads the one who practices it away from the truth.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. ۩
interpretation: All creatures are subject to Allah’s authority: some submit to Him knowingly and willingly, while none can escape His decree and created order. Even their shadows testify to this universal submission as they lengthen and contract with the movement of the sun.

translation: Say, “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” Say, “Allah.” Say, “Have you then taken protectors besides Him who possess no power to benefit or harm even themselves?” Say, “Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are darknesses and light equal? Or have they attributed partners to Allah who created as He creates, so that creation became confused for them?” Say, “Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Overpowering.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the irrationality of associating partners with Allah: beings that cannot even control benefit or harm for themselves cannot rightly be treated as divine protectors. Just as blindness cannot be equated with sight and darkness with light, ignorance and false worship cannot be equated with faith and recognition of truth. The question about partners who create like Allah challenges whether any created being truly shares His creative power; since all creation belongs to Him and depends upon Him, He alone is the One without equal and the irresistible Sovereign over everything.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity; then the torrent carries rising foam. And from what they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments or articles of use, there is foam like it. Thus Allah sets forth the example of truth and falsehood: as for the foam, it passes away as scum; but what benefits people remains in the earth. Thus Allah sets forth the examples.
interpretation: Allah illustrates that truth, though it may be accompanied by confusion, exaggeration, or falsehood, is like life-giving water or useful metal: it settles, endures, and benefits people. Falsehood is like foam—visible and swelling for a time, but empty and destined to disappear. The verse therefore teaches that lasting value is measured not by outward display or temporary dominance, but by the enduring benefit produced by what is true.

translation: For those who respond to their Lord is the finest reward. But those who do not respond to Him—even if they possessed everything on earth and the like of it besides, they would offer it all as ransom. For them is the evil reckoning, and their abode is Hell—how wretched a resting place.
interpretation: Responding to God means accepting His guidance with faith, obedience, and sincere submission, which leads to the best recompense. Rejecting Him leaves a person accountable for what they have done; on the Day of Judgment, no amount of worldly wealth or sacrifice can avert the consequences, and material possessions that once seemed valuable will provide no escape from divine judgment.

translation: So, can one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth be like one who is blind? Only those endowed with understanding take heed.
interpretation: Those who recognize the revelation as truth and submit to its guidance are not equal to those whose hearts are spiritually blind and unable to perceive it. True understanding is shown by reflecting on God’s message and allowing it to shape one’s life.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the covenant.
interpretation: They remain faithful to every binding commitment made before Allah, honoring its obligations consistently rather than violating or abandoning them when it becomes difficult or inconvenient.

translation: And those who uphold what Allah has commanded to be upheld, fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.
interpretation: These are people who preserve the bonds and responsibilities Allah has made sacred—foremost their relationship with Him, and also their ties with others—out of reverence for Him. Their fear of the Day of Judgment makes them careful in their conduct, knowing that no injustice, neglected duty, or hidden wrongdoing will escape accountability.

translation: And those who patiently persevere, seeking the pleasure of their Lord, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good—for them is the ultimate abode.
interpretation: This describes sincere believers whose patience is devoted to seeking God, whose worship is shown through prayer and generosity, and whose response to wrongdoing is to overcome it with kindness and righteousness. Their reward is the lasting, honored home in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence, which they will enter, together with those among their fathers, spouses, and descendants who were righteous; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This portrays the believers’ complete and lasting felicity: they are admitted to Paradise, reunited with righteous members of their families, and surrounded by the welcoming presence of angels. The mention of righteousness indicates that this reunion is a divine honor for those united in faith and uprightness, not merely a consequence of worldly kinship.

translation: “Peace be upon you for your patience. How excellent is the final abode!”
interpretation: This is the greeting of the angels to those who remained steadfast in faith, obedience, and endurance through hardship. Their patience has led them to lasting peace and the best eternal home with God.

translation: And those who break Allah’s covenant after affirming it, sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption throughout the earth—for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.
interpretation: This describes people who knowingly abandon their obligations to Allah, break the bonds and responsibilities He has commanded them to uphold, and cause harm and disorder in society. Their persistent betrayal leads to being deprived of Allah’s mercy and ending in the punishment of the Hereafter.

translation: Allah enlarges provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Yet they rejoice in the life of this world, while the life of this world, compared with the Hereafter, is only a fleeting enjoyment.
interpretation: The abundance or scarcity of worldly provision is determined by Allah’s wisdom and is not, by itself, a sign of honor or disgrace. Those who measure success by worldly pleasures rejoice in something temporary, whereas the Hereafter is lasting and therefore deserves their greater concern.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him.”
interpretation: The demand for a miraculous sign does not by itself indicate a sincere search for truth, for guidance depends on a person’s willingness to turn humbly toward Allah. Whoever sincerely seeks Him is guided, while one who stubbornly rejects the truth is left to the consequences of that rejection.

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah—surely, in the remembrance of Allah hearts find comfort.
interpretation: True faith gives the heart its deepest stability through remembering Allah: turning to Him in prayer, awareness, and trust quiets inner unrest and provides a lasting peace that worldly distractions cannot secure.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds—blessedness is theirs and an excellent destination.
interpretation: True faith, when expressed through righteous action, leads to lasting happiness, divine favor, and a beautiful final return to God in Paradise.

translation: Thus We have sent you to a nation before which other nations have passed away, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, “He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s mission continues the pattern of divine guidance sent to earlier peoples, even when those addressed reject one of Allah’s most encompassing names, the Most Merciful. In response to their denial, he is instructed to affirm that Allah alone is his Lord and source of support, placing his trust entirely in Him and directing his repentance and ultimate return to Him.

translation: Had there been a Qur’an by which the mountains could be moved, the earth split apart, or the dead made to speak, it would have been this one. Yet all authority belongs to Allah. Have the believers not realized that if Allah willed, He could guide all people? The disbelievers will continue to be afflicted by calamities because of what they have done, or calamity will strike near their homes, until Allah’s promise comes. Indeed, Allah never breaks His promise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that even the most extraordinary signs would not necessarily make obstinate hearts believe, because guidance ultimately depends on Allah’s will and a person’s response to truth. Those who reject it should not mistake their temporary security for escape: the consequences of their wrongdoing will continue to reach them, while Allah’s promised judgment is certain and cannot be delayed or annulled.

translation: Messengers before you were certainly mocked, so I granted the disbelievers respite; then I seized them. How terrible, then, was My punishment!
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that mockery by his opponents is not a sign of truth being defeated, for earlier messengers endured the same rejection. God may delay punishment, giving those who deny the truth time to reconsider, but this delay is not approval or escape; when accountability comes, His justice is decisive and severe.

translation: Is He who watches over every soul and all that it earns—[worthy of partners]? Yet they have attributed partners to Allah. Say, “Name them.” Or are you informing Him of something He does not know on earth? Or is it merely an outward expression of words? Rather, the schemes of those who disbelieve have been made appealing to them, and they have been turned away from the way. Whoever Allah allows to stray will have no guide.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in associating partners with Allah: He alone fully oversees every soul, knows all its deeds, and governs the universe, whereas the alleged partners have no real authority or independently established existence. The command to “name them” challenges the idolaters to provide genuine proof rather than rely on inherited claims and empty words. Their false beliefs appear attractive to them because of their own deception, and their rejection of truth ultimately leaves them without guidance.

translation: For them is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe; and they will have no protector against Allah.
interpretation: Those who persist in rejecting God and opposing the truth may face consequences even in this life, but the suffering awaiting them in the Hereafter is far more grievous and lasting. No ally or defender will be able to shield them from God’s judgment.

translation: The likeness of the Garden promised to the mindful of Allah is this: beneath it rivers flow; its provision is everlasting, and so is its shade. That is the ultimate end of those who are mindful of Allah, while the ultimate end of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as the enduring and secure reward of those who remain conscious of Allah and live by that consciousness. Its flowing rivers, unfailing sustenance, and constant shade signify a perfected existence untouched by deprivation or decline. In contrast, the Fire is the final consequence awaiting those who reject faith and persist in turning away from Allah.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, while among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, “I have only been commanded to worship Allah and associate no partner with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that sincere possessors of earlier revelation recognize the truth in the Qur’an, while rejection by some groups does not diminish its validity. The Prophet is instructed to remain firm in pure monotheism: his mission is to call people to Allah alone, free from all association, and to remember that his ultimate return—and the return of everyone—is to Him.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. Yet if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or defender against Allah.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the Qur’an is a clear, Arabic revelation containing decisive guidance and judgment. The warning teaches that revealed truth must not be altered to satisfy people’s preferences; whoever knowingly abandons it for their desires forfeits any true refuge or protection from Allah.

translation: And We certainly sent messengers before you and appointed for them wives and offspring. It was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by Allah’s permission. For every appointed term there is a decree.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that earlier messengers were human beings who married and had children, so having family responsibilities does not diminish a messenger’s rank or mission. Miracles are not performed at a messenger’s personal choice; they occur only when Allah permits them and for the purpose He wills. Every matter and every period has a divinely determined decree, so revelation, signs, and the fulfillment of Allah’s promises occur according to His wisdom and appointed time.

translation: Allah effaces whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills; and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: Allah has complete authority over the unfolding of events: He may remove or establish matters according to His wisdom, while the ultimate, unchanging record of His knowledge and decree remains with Him.

translation: Whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning.
interpretation: The verse reassures the Prophet that he is responsible for delivering God’s message faithfully, not for witnessing the full worldly consequences promised to its rejecters. Whether those consequences appear during his lifetime or afterward, God Himself will bring people to account and judge them with complete justice.

translation: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? Allah decrees, and none can overturn His decree; and He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: The verse warns the deniers that Allah’s power is visibly diminishing the strength and territory of those who oppose the truth, while His decree steadily prevails. No authority can resist what He has ordained, and His judgment will come swiftly and decisively.

translation: Those before them plotted, but all plotting belongs to Allah. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will soon know for whom the final abode is.
interpretation: The schemes of those who oppose the truth cannot escape Allah’s knowledge or overturn His decree; He allows events to unfold while fully knowing every person’s deeds, and in the end the disbelievers will recognize that lasting success and the final home belong to those who remained faithful to Him.

translation: Those who disbelieve say, “You are not a messenger.” Say, “Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever possesses knowledge of the Scripture.”
interpretation: When people reject the Prophet’s message, their denial does not invalidate it: Allah Himself is the decisive witness, and those who truly understand the revealed Scripture can recognize that his message accords with the truth and signs of earlier revelation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Rā. This is a Book We have sent down to you so that you may bring people out of darknesses into the light, by their Lord’s permission, onto the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The Qur’an is revealed as divine guidance through the Prophet, intended to free humanity from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and wrongdoing and lead it into the light of faith, truth, and righteous conduct. This transformation occurs by Allah’s permission and directs people to the straight path of the One whose power is absolute and whose praise is deserved.

translation: Allah is He to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth is under Allah’s complete ownership and authority, so rejecting Him is not merely disbelief in an idea but defiance of the One who sustains and governs all existence. The verse therefore warns that persistent denial carries a grave consequence: severe punishment.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, hinder others from the path of Allah, and seek to make it appear crooked—they are in far-reaching error.
interpretation: The verse portrays a deep moral deviation: valuing temporary worldly life above eternal accountability leads a person not only to reject divine guidance personally, but also to obstruct others and distort the truth so that it seems unclear or unacceptable. Such deliberate resistance places them far from the straight path and from salvation.

translation: We have not sent any messenger except in the language of his people, so that he might make the message clear to them. Then Allah lets go astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Every messenger was sent with a message expressed in the language and terms his people could understand, removing the excuse of ignorance and making the truth clear. Guidance, however, is granted according to Allah’s wisdom: those who turn sincerely toward the truth are guided, while those who reject it after it has become clear are left to their misguidance. His power is absolute, and His guidance and judgment are never without wisdom.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs, saying: “Bring your people out of the darknesses into the light, and remind them of the Days of Allah.” Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful.
interpretation: Allah sent Moses with clear miracles and guidance to lead his people from disbelief, ignorance, and oppression into faith and truth. “The Days of Allah” refers to the moments when Allah’s mercy, victory, blessings, or punishment became manifest, so that people would learn from His dealings with earlier nations. These lessons benefit those who remain steadfast through hardship and grateful for Allah’s favors.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “Remember Allah’s blessing upon you when He rescued you from Pharaoh’s people, who subjected you to terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women; and in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.”
interpretation: Moses reminds the Israelites that their deliverance from Pharaoh’s oppression was a profound manifestation of Allah’s mercy, while the suffering they endured was a severe test that called them to recognize His power, remain grateful, and live in obedience after being freed.

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed: “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, surely My punishment is severe.”
interpretation: Allah declares that recognizing His blessings, praising Him, and using those blessings in obedience will bring further increase and blessing. But denying or misusing His favors is an act of ingratitude that exposes a person to His severe punishment.

translation: And Moses said, “If you and everyone on earth were to disbelieve, indeed Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.”
interpretation: Moses makes clear that faith and gratitude do not benefit Allah, nor does disbelief harm Him; He is entirely independent of His creation, while all creatures remain dependent on Him. He is inherently worthy of praise regardless of whether people acknowledge Him.

translation: Has the news not reached you of those who came before you—the people of Noah, ʿĀd, and Thamūd—and those who came after them, whom none knows except Allah? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, “Indeed, we reject what you have been sent with, and we are truly in perplexing doubt about that to which you invite us.”
interpretation: The verse warns that the rejection of revealed truth is not a new phenomenon: earlier nations received clear evidence through their messengers, yet responded with denial and doubt rather than submission. Their putting their hands to their mouths expresses their hostile refusal to hear and accept the message, while the mention that Allah alone knows all the later nations emphasizes the vastness of human history and the completeness of His knowledge of those who opposed His guidance.

translation: Their messengers said, “Can there be any doubt about Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you so that He may forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed term.” They said, “You are only human beings like us. You want to turn us away from what our forefathers worshipped, so bring us clear authority.”
interpretation: The messengers answer that recognizing Allah should be the most evident truth, since He created and sustains the entire universe. His call is an opportunity for repentance and mercy, with life prolonged until the time He has decreed. Yet the people reject the message not because of a valid argument, but because they cling to ancestral tradition and question the messengers’ humanity; they demand a manifest miracle as a condition for belief.

translation: قالت لهم رسلهم: ما نحن إلا بشر مثلكم، ولكن الله يتفضل على من يشاء من عباده، وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بحجة أو آية إلا بإذن الله، وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون.
interpretation: يبين هذا أن الرسل يشتركون مع الناس في البشرية، لكن الله اختارهم لحمل رسالته ومنحهم ما يؤيد صدقهم من الآيات بإذنه، فلا يملكون شيئًا من عند أنفسهم. ولذلك يكون اعتماد المؤمنين على الله وحده، مع الإيمان بأن النصر والحق لا يتحققان إلا بتوفيقه.

translation: “Why should we not rely upon Allah when He has guided us to our ways? We will surely endure whatever harm you inflict upon us. And upon Allah let those who rely place their trust.”
interpretation: The believers affirm that Allah’s guidance gives them every reason to depend on Him, while their faith enables them to remain steadfast in the face of persecution and harm. True reliance on Allah involves both patient endurance and complete trust in His support and judgment.

translation: Those who disbelieved said to their messengers, “We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion.” Then their Lord revealed to them, “We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the arrogant rejection of truth by those who threatened the messengers with exile unless they abandoned their faith. God reassures His messengers that worldly power cannot protect such oppression from His judgment, and that the fate of those who persecute and reject the truth is destruction.

translation: And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears standing before Me and fears My warning.
interpretation: Allah promises that those who remain mindful of being answerable before Him and take His warning seriously will ultimately be granted security, stability, and rightful establishment after the downfall of wrongdoing people.

translation: They sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed.
interpretation: When the conflict between truth and falsehood reached its decisive point, God granted judgment in favor of His messengers and believers, while every arrogant and stubborn oppressor was utterly defeated and deprived of the success he pursued.

translation: Ahead of him is Hell, and he will be given water of festering fluid to drink.
interpretation: This portrays the fate awaiting the obstinate wrongdoer: instead of relief or nourishment, he will face Hell and be forced to drink a repulsive, painful fluid, signifying severe punishment and utter humiliation.

translation: He will gulp it down, but he will scarcely be able to swallow it. Death will come to him from every direction, yet he will not die; and beyond him is a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This portrays the torment of one who is confronted with an unbearable drink and surrounded by every cause of death, yet is denied the release of dying. The unending suffering, followed by an even more severe punishment, expresses the utter hopelessness and severity of the fate awaiting those who reject the truth.

translation: The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes blown forcefully by the wind on a stormy day. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the farthest straying.
interpretation: Their good deeds, lacking faith in God, have no lasting foundation or acceptance before Him; like scattered ashes, they cannot benefit them when they most need the reward of what they did. This illustrates the profound loss of directing one’s efforts without recognizing and submitting to the One who gives those efforts their true purpose.

translation: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and with purpose? If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: The verse reminds human beings that they are wholly dependent on Allah, whose purposeful creation demonstrates His absolute power. He is not dependent on them; if they persist in rejection and disobedience, He can remove them and replace them with another people who submit to Him.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: Nothing that Allah wills is beyond His power, no matter how impossible or immense it may appear to human beings.

translation: They will all appear before Allah, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, “Indeed, we followed you; can you spare us anything of Allah’s punishment?” They will reply, “Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we despair or endure; there is no escape for us.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who blindly followed influential and arrogant people will discover that their leaders cannot bear any part of their punishment. Both followers and leaders will recognize that guidance was neglected in worldly life and that, once judgment has come, regret, despair, or patience cannot provide a way out.

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, “Indeed, Allah made you a true promise, and I made you a promise, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot answer your cry for help, nor can you answer mine. Indeed, I reject your having associated me with Allah before.” Surely, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: Satan’s admission reveals that his influence was only deception and invitation, not compulsion. Those who followed him remain responsible because they willingly answered his call, and on the Day of Judgment neither he nor they will be able to help one another. His disavowal of their association of him with Allah exposes the futility of obeying any created being in disobedience to God; ultimate blame and accountability belong to those who chose that path.

translation: And He will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein by the permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, “Peace.”
interpretation: Those who combine sincere faith with righteous action will enter Paradise and remain there forever through God’s grace and permission, finding their abiding condition marked by complete peace and security.

translation: Have you not seen how Allah sets forth a parable: a good word is like a good tree—its root is firmly grounded and its branches reach into the sky.
interpretation: The good word represents sincere faith and speech that brings truth, goodness, and benefit. Like a healthy tree anchored by deep roots yet spreading its branches high, genuine faith is firmly established in the heart and produces enduring, elevated effects through righteous deeds and beneficial words.

translation: It yields its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord. And Allah sets forth parables for people so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The good word, firmly rooted in faith, continually produces beneficial effects in a believer’s life by Allah’s grace, just as a healthy tree bears fruit in every season. This parable teaches that sincere faith should manifest in enduring righteous deeds and benefit to others, while inviting people to reflect and learn from Allah’s signs.

translation: And the likeness of a corrupt word is that of a corrupt tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: A false or wicked belief and speech may appear for a time, but because they lack truth and sound foundations, they cannot endure or produce lasting good; like a tree torn from its roots, they have no firm existence or stability.

translation: Allah makes those who believe firm through the steadfast word in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah leads the wrongdoers astray; Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: Allah strengthens sincere believers to remain anchored in faith and to speak the truth when tested in this life, and He grants them firmness when they are questioned in the Hereafter. As for those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth, they are deprived of this guidance and left to go further astray. All of this occurs according to Allah’s wisdom and sovereign will.

translation: Have you not seen those who exchanged Allah’s blessing for disbelief and brought their people to the abode of ruin?
interpretation: The verse condemns those who respond to Allah’s gifts—especially guidance and faith—with rejection, then lead their communities into spiritual destruction by making disbelief and disobedience their way of life.

translation: They will enter Hell and burn in it—what a wretched abode!
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as the dreadful and irreversible consequence awaiting those who reject the truth, emphasizing the misery of their final dwelling.

translation: And they set up equals to Allah in order to mislead others from His way. Say, “Enjoy yourselves for a while; indeed, your destination is the Fire.”
interpretation: Those who associate partners with Allah and use that falsehood to divert people from the truth may enjoy worldly life temporarily, but such enjoyment cannot avert the inevitable consequence of disbelief and misguidance: return to the punishment of Hell.

translation: Tell My believing servants to establish prayer and spend, privately and publicly, from what We have provided for them, before a Day comes when there will be neither bargaining nor friendly bonds.
interpretation: Believers are urged to respond to God’s provision through sincere worship and generous giving, whether their charity is hidden or openly practiced for a sound purpose. These deeds must be done before the Day of Judgment, when worldly exchanges and relationships will no longer offer any means of obtaining salvation or easing accountability.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, sent down water from the sky, and brought forth through it fruits as provision for you. He subjected the ships to you so that they may sail through the sea by His command, and He subjected the rivers to you.
interpretation: This verse directs people to recognize Allah’s complete sovereignty and mercy through the ordered provisions and forces of creation: rain produces sustenance, ships traverse the seas, and rivers serve life and human needs. Such blessings are not independent or accidental; they operate only by Allah’s command, calling people to gratitude, humility, and faithful reliance upon Him.

translation: And He has subjected the sun and the moon to you, both persistently pursuing their courses; and He has subjected the night and the day for you.
interpretation: God has made the sun, moon, night, and day operate in an ordered, continuous pattern that serves human life, providing light, time, and the conditions necessary for existence. Their regularity is a sign of His sustaining power and calls people to recognize His favor and live in gratitude rather than treating these blessings as self-sustaining or without purpose.

translation: And He has given you some of all that you have asked of Him. If you were to count the blessings of Allah, you could never enumerate them. Indeed, the human being is truly unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: Allah has surrounded humanity with countless blessings, granting what is needed and what is sought in ways known to Him, yet people are unable to fully recognize or account for them. The verse warns that human beings often wrong themselves by overlooking these gifts and respond with persistent ingratitude instead of acknowledging Allah’s favor and using it rightly.

translation: And when Abraham said, “My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my children away from worshipping idols.”
interpretation: Abraham’s prayer teaches that true security is joined with pure worship: even a prophet seeks Allah’s protection from idolatry for himself and his descendants, showing that faith must be guarded through continual dependence on Allah.

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray. So whoever follows me is truly of me; and whoever disobeys me—surely You are Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Abraham declares that idols have diverted many from the truth, while defining true belonging by following divine guidance rather than by lineage or claim. Yet he entrusts those who disobey to God’s mercy, leaving the door of repentance and forgiveness open.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of some people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful.
interpretation: Ibrahim عليه السلام entrusts his family to Allah in a barren place because the greater purpose is to establish worship at the Sacred House. He asks Allah to place love and longing for them in people’s hearts and to sustain them with provision, so that their security, community, and blessings lead them to recognize Allah’s favor and respond with gratitude.

translation: Our Lord, surely You know what we conceal and what we disclose; nothing at all is hidden from Allah, whether on earth or in heaven.
interpretation: This is a confession of God’s perfect and encompassing knowledge: He is aware of every hidden intention and every outward action, and nothing in the entire universe escapes His knowledge. It therefore calls the servant to sincerity, humility, and constant awareness that Allah knows the reality of what lies within the heart as well as what appears before people.

translation: Praise belongs to Allah, who granted me Ishmael and Isaac despite my old age. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses Abraham’s profound gratitude that Allah answered his prayer and blessed him with children in his old age. It teaches that no circumstance is beyond Allah’s power, and that sincere supplication is never unheard by the Lord who listens and responds with wisdom.

translation: My Lord, make me one who steadfastly establishes prayer, and [make] some of my descendants so as well. Our Lord, accept my supplication.
interpretation: This is a prayer for steadfast devotion: the speaker asks God to make prayer a firmly established part of his life and to grant the same faithfulness to some of his descendants, while humbly entrusting the acceptance of his supplication to God.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the account is established.
interpretation: This is a humble supplication that seeks God’s forgiveness for oneself first, then for one’s parents and all believers, while recognizing that complete justice and final judgment belong to the Day of Resurrection. It teaches that sincere faith combines personal repentance, gratitude toward one’s parents, and compassion for the believing community.

translation: And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only grants them respite until a Day when eyes will stare in horror.
interpretation: The verse warns against mistaking the delay of divine punishment for neglect or approval. Allah fully knows the ظلم of the wrongdoers, but postpones their reckoning until the Day of Judgment, when terror and accountability will become unmistakable.

translation: They will hasten forward, their heads raised, their gaze unable to turn back to them, and their hearts utterly empty.
interpretation: This portrays the people of wrongdoing on the Day of Judgment, rushing in terror with their eyes fixed and unmoving, while fear has stripped their hearts of calm, strength, and understanding.

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come upon them. Then those who did wrong will say, “Our Lord, delay us for a little while; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.” It will be said, “Did you not previously swear that you would never perish?”
interpretation: The verse warns that repentance and obedience cannot be postponed indefinitely. When the consequences of wrongdoing become manifest, the unjust will ask for another opportunity, but their former confidence that they would escape accountability will expose the falseness of their excuses. The time for responding to divine guidance is before punishment arrives, not after its reality has become undeniable.

translation: And you lived in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it had become clear to you how We dealt with them; and We set forth examples for you.
interpretation: The verse warns those who witness the ruins and fate of earlier transgressors that such knowledge carries responsibility: seeing the consequences of injustice should lead to repentance and obedience, not complacency. The examples Allah presents are clear evidence that wrongdoing ultimately brings punishment, leaving no valid excuse for ignoring the warning.

translation: They devised their scheme, but their scheme is within Allah’s knowledge and power, even though it was enough to move the mountains.
interpretation: The verse warns that no matter how immense, deceptive, or seemingly powerful the schemes of the rejecters may be, they remain fully encompassed by Allah’s knowledge and subject to His will; their apparent strength cannot overcome the truth or escape divine judgment.

translation: So never think that Allah will fail to keep His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, capable of retribution.
interpretation: This verse assures that Allah’s promised support and final victory for His messengers will certainly come, even if its fulfillment appears delayed; His absolute power ensures that wrongdoing will ultimately be answered with justice.

translation: On the Day when the earth will be changed into another earth, and the heavens as well, and they will all appear before Allah, the One, the All-Compelling.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Resurrection as a complete transformation of the created order: the familiar world will give way to a new one, and every creature will stand openly before Allah without concealment or escape. His oneness and irresistible authority will then be unmistakably manifest, leaving all beings subject to His final judgment.

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in fetters.
interpretation: This portrays the criminals’ complete helplessness and humiliation on the Day of Judgment: they will be restrained in chains, unable to escape or resist the consequences of their wrongdoing.

translation: Their garments will be made of tar, and the Fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This portrays the utter humiliation and torment of those who rejected the truth: even what clothes and protects them becomes a source of punishment, while the Fire overwhelms their faces, the most visible part of their being.

translation: So that Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: Allah will judge every person with complete justice, rewarding or holding them accountable according to their deeds; His perfect knowledge and power make the reckoning certain and require no delay.

translation: This is a proclamation for humanity, so that they may be warned by it, know that He is only One God, and that those endowed with understanding may take heed.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as a clear, universal admonition whose warning awakens people to accountability before God. Sound reflection should lead them to recognize His absolute oneness and to remember the guidance conveyed by His signs.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur’an.
interpretation: The revelation is identified as a divinely given Book whose message is clear and illuminating, while the opening letters remind the listener that its ultimate nature lies beyond ordinary human explanation.

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: حين ينكشف لهم يوم الحساب صدق الإيمان وبطلان الكفر، يدركون ما فاتهم من النجاة، فيتمنون الرجوع إلى الإسلام، لكن ذلك التمني يأتي بعد فوات زمن الاختيار والعمل.

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let false hope distract them; they will soon know.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who make worldly pleasure and unending hopes their primary concern may continue heedlessly for a time, but death and judgment will ultimately expose the consequences of their neglect.

translation: We never destroyed any town except that it had a prescribed, known decree.
interpretation: Destruction does not occur arbitrarily; every community is given an appointed term known to God, and its end comes only according to His determined wisdom.

translation: No nation can advance its appointed term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: Every community has a divinely determined period of existence that cannot be brought forward or postponed; its rise, decline, and final end occur only at the time God has decreed.

translation: And they said, “O you upon whom the Reminder has been sent down, surely you are mad.”
interpretation: The unbelievers mockingly addressed the Prophet Muhammad, dismissing the revelation and labeling him insane because his message challenged their beliefs; their accusation reflects rejection and ridicule, not any truth about him.

translation: Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?
interpretation: هذا قولٌ صدر عن المكذّبين على سبيل التحدّي والاستهزاء، إذ طلبوا رؤية الملائكة دليلاً حسّيًا مع أن طلبهم لم يكن بحثًا صادقًا عن الحق، بل عنادًا وإنكارًا لرسالة النبي.
