translation: We do not send down the angels except with the truth, and then they would not be granted respite.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that angels are not sent down in response to demands for amusement or as a spectacle; their descent occurs only by God’s wisdom and for a decisive, truthful purpose. When they come with judgment or punishment, the guilty will receive no further delay.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will surely preserve it.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the Qur’an is revealed by Him and that He Himself guarantees its protection from loss, distortion, and corruption, preserving its truth and guidance for humanity.

translation: And We certainly sent messengers before you among the communities of earlier peoples.
interpretation: God reassures the Prophet that his mission follows the established pattern of divine guidance: messengers were sent to many previous nations, so the rejection he faced was not unprecedented but part of the recurring test of human response to revelation.

translation: No messenger came to them without their mocking him.
interpretation: The verse portrays mockery of God’s messengers as a recurring response of arrogant peoples who reject guidance; such ridicule does not diminish the truth of the message, but reveals the rejecters’ refusal to submit to it.

translation: Thus We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: God describes the entrenched denial of the guilty: the same rejection and mockery of revelation becomes fixed within their hearts, so they persist in refusing the truth even when it is made clear to them.

translation: They will not believe in it, though the way of the earlier peoples has already passed.
interpretation: Those who stubbornly reject the truth will not accept it even when confronted with clear signs, following the same pattern of denial that characterized earlier peoples and led to their ruin.

translation: And even if We opened for them a gate in heaven and they continued ascending through it,
interpretation: Even if those who deny the truth were given direct access to the heavens and allowed to witness extraordinary signs with their own eyes, their stubbornness would lead them to dismiss what they saw as illusion rather than submit to the truth.

translation: They would say, “Our eyes have merely been dazzled; rather, we are a bewitched people.”
interpretation: Even if they were shown a clear sign from heaven, they would reject it by claiming that their perception had been deceived and that they were under magic, revealing their deliberate refusal to accept the truth.

translation: And We have surely placed constellations in the sky and adorned it for those who behold it.
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the ordered beauty of the heavens as a sign of His wisdom and power, inviting people to contemplate creation rather than treat the stars as objects of superstition or worship.

translation: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: Allah safeguarded the heaven from every expelled devil, preventing them from trespassing into it or approaching the divine realm in defiance.

translation: Except for whoever stealthily eavesdrops, then a clear, blazing flame pursues him.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the devils are barred from accessing the heavenly realm and attempting to intercept divine knowledge; any one of them who tries to snatch a hearing is immediately pursued by a manifest, piercing flame, affirming that revelation is protected from their interference.

translation: And the earth We spread out, and We placed upon it firm mountains, and caused to grow therein every thing in due measure.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to Allah’s wisdom in preparing the earth for life: He extended it as a habitable expanse, anchored it with mountains, and brought forth its diverse provisions in precise proportion and balance. This order and measured abundance point to His power, knowledge, and deliberate design.

translation: وجعلنا لكم فيها أسبابَ المعيشة، وجعلنا فيها أيضًا من لستم رازقين له.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الله سخّر في الأرض مواردَ الحياة وأسبابَ الرزق للإنسان ولمن يعولهم أو ينتفعون بما فيها، مع التأكيد على أن الرزق في حقيقته من الله، لا من قدرة الإنسان وحدها.

translation: There is nothing except that its treasures are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This signifies that every form of provision, blessing, and created resource belongs to Allah in its ultimate source, and that whatever He brings into the world is apportioned with precise knowledge and wisdom, not by chance or without measure.

translation: And We sent the winds to fertilize, then We sent down water from the sky and gave it to you to drink; and you are not able to store and preserve it.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to Allah’s precise ordering of creation: He makes the winds carry what brings about fertilization, sends down the rain, and makes it available for human life. Though people benefit from water and may store some of it, they cannot control its ultimate provision or secure it independently; it remains a divine gift and a reminder of human dependence on Allah.

translation: And indeed, We alone give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute power over life and death, and when all created beings pass away, He remains as the everlasting Owner and Sovereign over all existence.

translation: And We certainly know those among you who have gone ahead, and We certainly know those who have lagged behind.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses every person’s position and course: He knows those who hasten toward obedience and those who delay, so none can conceal their deeds or their standing before Him.

translation: Indeed, your Lord—He will gather them all. Surely He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah will bring all people together for the appointed reckoning, and His judgment will be perfectly wise and fully informed of every person’s deeds and circumstances.

translation: And indeed We created humankind from sounding clay, formed from dark, altered mud.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to the humble material origin of human beings and to the deliberate act of God in shaping them, reminding humanity that its dignity comes from its Creator rather than from the substance from which it was made.

translation: And the jinn We created before that from a scorching, smokeless fire.
interpretation: This indicates that the jinn were created before humankind and that their origin is a subtle, intensely penetrating fire, unlike the earthly clay from which Adam was created.

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, “Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay formed from dark, altered mud.”
interpretation: This verse presents human creation as a deliberate act of divine will and emphasizes humanity’s humble material origin, calling people to recognize their dependence on their Creator rather than take pride in themselves.

translation: So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him in prostration.
interpretation: After Allah completed Adam’s creation and granted him life by the spirit He created and attributed to Himself as an honor, He commanded the angels to prostrate before him as a sign of respect and recognition of Adam’s honored status—not as worship of Adam.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together.
interpretation: This emphasizes the complete and unanimous obedience of the angels to Allah’s command: none held back or resisted, and their prostration honored the command given concerning Adam.

translation: Except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrated.
interpretation: Iblis deliberately rejected God’s command out of arrogance, revealing that pride can lead a creature to defy divine guidance even when the command is clear.

translation: He said, “O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not among those who prostrate?”
interpretation: Allah confronts Iblis over his refusal to obey the command to prostrate, exposing that his exclusion from the obedient servants is the result of his deliberate defiance and pride.

translation: He said, “I would never prostrate before a human being whom You have created from dried clay, from black mud molded into shape.”
interpretation: This expresses Iblīs’s arrogant rejection of God’s command: he judged Adam by his material origin and considered himself superior, placing his own reasoning above divine obedience.

translation: He said, “Then leave it, for you are indeed accursed.”
interpretation: Allah commanded Iblīs to depart from the honored presence and cast him away because of his arrogant disobedience; being accursed means being expelled from divine mercy.

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This is Allah’s declaration that Satan is permanently cast away from His mercy and favor until the Day of Judgment, because of his defiance and refusal to obey Allah’s command.

translation: He said, “My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: This is the plea of Iblīs, who asks to be spared until the Resurrection so that he may continue pursuing and misleading humankind; his request reflects defiance and persistence in evil, not repentance.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you are among those granted respite.”
interpretation: God granted Iblīs a delay until the appointed time, allowing him to remain for a period rather than destroying him immediately.

translation: Until the day of the appointed time.
interpretation: This refers to the fixed time decreed by Allah when the final reckoning will occur, a time whose exact knowledge belongs to Him alone.

translation: He said, “My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make the things of the earth seem attractive to them, and I will surely mislead them all.”
interpretation: Iblīs declares that he will exploit worldly desires and adorn disobedience until falsehood appears appealing, seeking to divert all people from obedience to God. His claim that God led him astray is an excuse that shifts blame, whereas his rebellion and deliberate choice to mislead are his own responsibility.

translation: Except Your servants among them who are sincerely devoted to You.
interpretation: Satan acknowledges that he will have no power over those whom Allah has purified through sincere faith and devotion, keeping them steadfast against his deception.

translation: He said, “This is a straight path leading directly to Me.”
interpretation: Allah declares that sincere devotion to Him is the direct, protected path from which Satan cannot divert those who truly belong to Him.

translation: Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them, except those among the misguided who follow you.
interpretation: God assures that Satan cannot compel or control His sincere servants; his influence reaches only those who willingly turn away from guidance and choose to follow his path.

translation: Indeed, Hell is the promised destination for them all.
interpretation: All those who follow Satan’s path will ultimately face Hell as the just and appointed consequence of their rebellion against Allah.

translation: It has seven gates, and for each gate there is an allotted portion of them.
interpretation: Hell is described as having seven entrances, with its inhabitants divided among them according to their distinct degrees of disbelief, corruption, and punishment; this allocation reflects the justice and order of divine judgment.

translation: Indeed, the mindful of Allah will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: Those who remain conscious of Allah, obeying Him and avoiding disobedience, will be granted lasting bliss in Paradise, symbolized by its beautiful gardens and abundant springs.

translation: Enter it in peace, safe and secure.
interpretation: This is a divine welcome to the righteous into Paradise, assuring them that they will enter it under God’s protection, free from fear, harm, and every form of distress.

translation: And We shall remove whatever resentment is in their hearts; they will be brothers, reclining on couches facing one another.
interpretation: Allah describes the people of Paradise as being inwardly purified from envy, bitterness, and hostility, so that their relationships are marked by sincere brotherhood and mutual affection, with no alienation or conflict between them.

translation: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they ever be expelled from it.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of complete and everlasting security: its inhabitants will experience neither weariness nor hardship, and their bliss will never be interrupted by expulsion or loss.

translation: Inform My servants that I am truly the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet ﷺ to reassure His servants that His forgiveness and mercy are vast, inviting them to turn to Him with sincere repentance and hope, rather than despairing of His compassion.

translation: And that My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This warns that although Allah’s mercy and forgiveness are vast, those who persist in rebellion and reject His guidance will face a severe and painful punishment.

translation: And tell them about Abraham’s guests.
interpretation: This is a command to recount the account of Abraham’s honored visitors, drawing attention to the divine purpose and lessons contained in their arrival.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, “Peace,” he said, “Indeed, we are fearful of you.”
interpretation: Abraham’s fear arose because these unfamiliar guests had entered without eating or revealing their purpose; their unusual presence made him apprehensive, despite their peaceful greeting.

translation: They said, “Do not be afraid; indeed, we give you good news of a knowledgeable boy.”
interpretation: The angels reassure Abraham that they have come with mercy, not harm, and announce the birth of a son distinguished by knowledge and wisdom—a divine gift beyond what Abraham and his wife expected in their old age.

translation: He said, “Do you give me this good news even though old age has afflicted me? What, then, is the nature of this good news?”
interpretation: Abraham expresses astonishment at being promised a child despite his advanced age, not disbelief in God’s power. His question highlights that the promised birth is an extraordinary act of divine grace beyond ordinary human expectation.

translation: They said, “We have given you good news in truth, so do not be among those who despair.”
interpretation: The angels reassure Abraham that their promise is certain and divinely true; therefore, a believer should not let an apparently impossible situation lead to despair of Allah’s mercy and power.

translation: He said, “Who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?”
interpretation: Despairing of Allah’s mercy is a form of misguidance, because no matter how grave a person’s sins or difficult their circumstances, Allah’s mercy remains open to those who turn to Him in faith and repentance.

translation: He said, “What is your mission, O messengers?”
interpretation: Abraham asked the angels to explain the serious matter for which they had been sent, seeking to understand the purpose of their visit beyond the glad tidings they had delivered.

translation: They said, “Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals.”
interpretation: The angels explain that God has sent them to a people who persist in grave wrongdoing and rebellion, indicating that their mission is to carry out divine judgment upon them.

translation: “Except the family of Lot; indeed, We will save them all.”
interpretation: Allah declares that Lot’s household will be spared from the impending punishment and rescued in its entirety, distinguishing those who remain faithful from the people who incurred the judgment.

translation: Except his wife; We had decreed that she would be among those who remained behind.
interpretation: Her exclusion from salvation was decreed because she shared in the rejection and wrongdoing of the condemned people; she would remain behind with them when the believers were delivered.

translation: Then, when the messengers came to the family of Lot,
interpretation: The verse marks the arrival of the angels sent by Allah to Lot’s household, initiating the divine warning and the events that would reveal the fate of his people.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you are an unfamiliar people.”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm expressed his concern because the visitors were unknown to him and had arrived without the customary signs of guests; his words were a request for clarification rather than an accusation.

translation: They said, “Rather, we have brought you what they used to doubt.”
interpretation: The angels clarify to Lot that they have come with the inevitable punishment his people repeatedly doubted and denied, showing that divine judgment is certain even when people dismiss its warning.

translation: And we have brought you the truth, and indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: The messengers affirm that their message comes from God as undeniable truth, and that their testimony and promise are completely reliable, leaving no basis for doubt or suspicion.

translation: So set out with your family during a part of the night, follow behind them, and let none of you look back. Proceed wherever you are commanded.
interpretation: This command to Lūṭ عليه السلام emphasizes complete obedience and decisive departure from a doomed, corrupt society: his family must leave quietly, avoid looking back in attachment or hesitation, and trustfully follow the direction given by God.

translation: And We revealed to him this decree: “Indeed, the last remnant of these people will be cut off by morning.”
interpretation: This is Allah’s decisive announcement to Lot that the people persisting in corruption would be completely destroyed before dawn, leaving no continuation of their wrongdoing or survivors among them.

translation: And the people of the city came, rejoicing.
interpretation: The people hurried toward Lot’s guests in excited anticipation, revealing that their apparent joy was rooted in the corrupt desires and wrongdoing that had become characteristic of their society.

translation: He said, “These are my guests, so do not disgrace me.”
interpretation: Lot appealed to his people to honor the sanctity of his guests and not subject them to humiliation or abuse, reminding them that violating the protection owed to guests would bring shame upon him.

translation: And fear Allah, and do not disgrace me.
interpretation: Prophet Lot appeals to his people to remain conscious of God and to refrain from violating his honor by abusing and humiliating his guests under his protection.

translation: They said, “Did we not forbid you from receiving anyone from all people?”
interpretation: Lūṭ’s people rebuked him for protecting and hosting his guests, reminding him that they had already imposed their corrupt prohibition against offering refuge to outsiders. Their words reveal their defiance of moral and social responsibility and their determination to violate the guests’ dignity.

translation: He said, “These are my daughters, if you are going to act.”
interpretation: Lot offered the women of his community as lawful wives rather than allowing his guests to be violated, appealing to them to pursue a legitimate and morally pure course instead of their depraved desire.

translation: By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Prophet’s life to emphasize that those people were so overcome by heedlessness and desire that they moved blindly within their moral corruption, unable to recognize the truth or respond to warning.

translation: فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين
interpretation: فأهلكتهم الصيحة المهلكة حين أشرق الصباح، جزاءَ إصرارهم على التكذيب والتمادي في الفساد.

translation: So We turned its upper part upside down and rained upon them stones of baked clay.
interpretation: This describes the destruction of the people of Lot: their dwellings were overturned and they were struck by stones decreed as a punishment for their persistent rejection and grave wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: Allah’s signs are evident to those who possess insight and carefully reflect on what lies beneath outward events, recognizing the lessons and warnings they contain.

translation: And indeed, it lies on a well-traveled road.
interpretation: The destroyed towns of Lot remained along a known, established route, so their fate was not hidden from travelers; their ruins served as a continuing warning to those who passed by.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The matter referred to contains clear evidence of Allah’s power and wisdom, which believers recognize as guidance that strengthens their faith.

translation: And indeed, the people of the thicket were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The people of the thicket were condemned because they persisted in injustice and disobedience, rejecting the truth brought by their messenger and wronging themselves through their corrupt conduct.

translation: So We took retribution from them, and both of them lie along a clearly visible path.
interpretation: God’s punishment of these two rejecting peoples was not hidden or arbitrary; the remains and locations of their settlements stood on a known route as an enduring, visible warning to those who passed by and reflected on the consequences of defying God.

translation: And indeed, the people of al-Ḥijr denied the messengers.
interpretation: The people of al-Ḥijr rejected Ṣāliḥ and, by denying him, denied the unified message of all the messengers: worship God alone and obey His guidance. Their prosperous settlement and material strength did not protect them from the consequences of persistent disbelief.

translation: And We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them.
interpretation: God made His guidance and signs clear to them, yet they deliberately refused to heed them or reflect upon their truth, choosing instead to turn away.

translation: They used to carve homes into the mountains, feeling secure.
interpretation: Their strong dwellings and sense of safety did not protect them from Allah’s punishment; the verse warns that material security and power cannot shield a people from accountability when they reject the truth.

translation: So the mighty blast seized them at daybreak.
interpretation: The verse portrays the suddenness and inevitability of divine punishment: when morning came, the people were overtaken by a devastating cry before they could escape or defend themselves.

translation: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون.
interpretation: لم تنفعهم أموالهم وأعمالهم ومكاسبهم حين نزل بهم العذاب؛ إذ لا يغني الإنسانَ عن عاقبة كفره ما جمعه في الدنيا إذا لم يكن قائمًا على الإيمان والعمل الصالح.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them except with truth and purpose. Indeed, the Hour is surely coming, so pardon with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: Allah created the universe with wisdom, justice, and a definite purpose, not in vain. Since the Day of Judgment is certain, respond to those who oppose you with dignified patience and sincere forgiveness, without bitterness or retaliation, while leaving ultimate judgment to Allah.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the Supreme Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah alone creates all things with perfect power and wisdom, and His complete knowledge encompasses every creature, matter, and outcome.

translation: And We have certainly given you the seven oft-repeated verses and the عظیم Qur’an.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ of the immense gift bestowed upon him: the seven repeatedly recited verses of Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, together with the Qur’an in its full greatness. This emphasizes that divine revelation is both a source of continual worship and the supreme guidance and honor granted by Allah.

translation: Do not stretch your eyes toward the enjoyment We have granted to some groups among them, nor grieve over them; and lower your wing in gentleness toward the believers.
interpretation: Do not let the worldly wealth and pleasures granted to others captivate your heart or cause you sorrow over what they possess. Instead, remain content with what Allah has given you and treat the believers with humility, compassion, and kindness.

translation: And say, “Indeed, I am the clear warner.”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to proclaim openly that his role is to warn people plainly about the consequences of rejecting God and disobeying Him, leaving the message clear and unmistakable.

translation: Just as We sent down upon those who divided,
interpretation: This is a warning that God’s punishment befell those who fragmented the revealed message, accepting some of it while rejecting or distorting the rest, and thereby treating divine revelation with division and contempt.

translation: Those who have divided the Qur’an into parts,
interpretation: It refers to those who fragmented their approach to the Qur’an—accepting what suited them while rejecting or disregarding the rest, rather than submitting to it as a unified revelation.

translation: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين: «فوربك، لنسألنهم جميعًا.»
interpretation: يقسم الله تعالى بربوبيته لنبيّه أن يسأل جميع المكذّبين يوم القيامة عن أعمالهم ومواقفهم، فلا يفلت أحد من الحساب ولا يُستثنى أحد من المسؤولية.

translation: About what they used to do.
interpretation: It indicates that they will be questioned and held accountable for their deeds and conduct.

translation: So proclaim openly what you have been commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: God commands the Prophet to deliver the revelation clearly and courageously, without allowing the hostility of those who reject monotheism to intimidate him or divert him into futile disputes.

translation: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet that He Himself will protect and support him against those who ridicule his message, rendering their hostility powerless before His care and judgment.

translation: Those who set up another deity alongside Allah will soon come to know.
interpretation: This is a warning that associating partners with Allah is a grave falsehood whose consequences will become unmistakably clear to those who commit it, especially when they face the truth and the judgment of Allah.

translation: And We certainly know that your heart is distressed by what they say.
interpretation: God consoles the Prophet by affirming that He fully knows the pain caused by the denials and hurtful words of his opponents; this recognition assures him that his distress is neither hidden nor disregarded by God.

translation: So glorify your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate.
interpretation: When confronted with distress or opposition, turn to Allah by declaring His perfection, praising Him, and joining the humble worshippers whose prostration expresses complete submission to Him.

translation: And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.
interpretation: Remain devoted to worshipping your Lord throughout your life, until death—the certain end that comes to every person.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: Allah’s promised decree—especially His judgment and the consequences of rejecting Him—is certain and so near in its inevitability that it is described as having already come. People must not demand that it be hastened or treat divine patience as weakness; instead, they should affirm Allah’s absolute transcendence and reject every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: He sends down the angels with the Spirit, by His command, upon whomever He wills of His servants, saying: “Warn that there is no deity except Me, so be mindful of Me.”
interpretation: Allah conveys revelation through the angels to those He chooses as messengers, making clear that the essence of their warning is to affirm His absolute oneness and to live in reverent obedience and awareness of Him.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and purpose. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The ordered creation of the heavens and the earth is founded upon divine wisdom and truth, bearing witness that worship belongs solely to their Creator; therefore, Allah is far above every partner or false deity attributed to Him.

translation: He created الإنسان from a sperm-drop, yet suddenly he is a clear, outspoken opponent.
interpretation: The verse highlights the astonishing contrast between the human being’s humble origin and his later arrogance: although created from an insignificant drop, he becomes capable of disputing, arguing, and opposing the truth openly. It is a reminder of human dependence and a warning against pride before the Creator.

translation: And the livestock—He created them for you. In them is warmth and other benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: God presents livestock as a manifestation of His care and provision: they provide protection from the cold, many practical benefits, and nourishment. Their creation and usefulness should lead people to recognize His mercy and respond with gratitude rather than treating these blessings as mere possessions.

translation: And for you there is beauty in them when you bring them home in the evening and when you take them out to pasture.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the wholesome pleasure and dignity people find in witnessing their livestock return home and go out to graze, highlighting how God has placed both practical benefit and beauty in His provision.

translation: And they carry your burdens to a land you could not reach except with great hardship. Surely your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to how God has made animals a means of transport, enabling people to bear their goods and travel distances that would otherwise be beyond their strength. This provision reflects His gentleness and mercy in easing human burdens through the resources He has created.

translation: And He created horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that the animals placed at their service are both practical means of transport and sources of beauty, while His words “He creates what you do not know” affirm that His creative power and the forms of provision He brings forth extend beyond human knowledge and expectation.

translation: And upon Allah is the direction of the right path, while some paths deviate. Had He willed, He could have guided you all.
interpretation: Allah has made the straight path clear and its guidance rests with Him, but people may turn away from it and follow deviant ways. His ability to guide everyone does not mean that He compels faith; rather, He allows people to choose, while guidance is granted according to His wisdom.

translation: He is the One who sends down water from the sky. From it is drink for you, and from it grow plants among which you pasture your livestock.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to Allah’s care and power: He provides the essential water that sustains human life and produces vegetation upon which animals depend, reminding people that these blessings are granted by Him and deserve their gratitude.

translation: By it He causes crops, olives, date palms, grapevines, and all kinds of fruits to grow for you. Surely in that is a sign for people who reflect.
interpretation: The diverse and purposeful growth of the earth’s produce, brought forth through the same life-giving rain, reveals God’s power, wisdom, and gracious provision; recognizing this sign requires thoughtful reflection rather than mere observation.

translation: And He has subjected for you the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; and the stars are subjected by His command. Surely in that are signs for people who use reason.
interpretation: Allah has made the alternation of night and day and the orderly movement of the sun, moon, and stars serve human life according to a precise and governed system. Their dependence on His command demonstrates His absolute power, wisdom, and oneness, which become evident to those who reflect thoughtfully.

translation: And whatever He has created for you on the earth, differing in its colors—surely in that is a sign for people who take heed.
interpretation: The countless forms, qualities, and colors found in the earth are deliberate signs of Allah’s wisdom and creative power; those who reflect upon them recognize His unity, mercy, and sovereignty.

translation: And He is the One who subjected the sea for you, so that you may eat from it fresh meat, extract from it ornaments that you wear, and see the ships plowing through it, so that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps be grateful.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that the sea, with its nourishment, beauty, navigable waters, and means of livelihood, is made accessible by His power and wisdom. These blessings are not merely for enjoyment but should lead people to recognize His generosity, pursue lawful provision, and respond with sincere gratitude rather than heedlessness.

translation: And He placed firm mountains in the earth lest it should shake with you, and rivers and paths, so that you may be guided.
interpretation: Allah points to the ordered features of the earth as signs of His wisdom and mercy: the mountains provide stability, while rivers and pathways make life, travel, and settlement possible. These blessings should lead people to recognize their Creator and follow the guidance He has given.

translation: وخلق علاماتٍ يهتدون بها، وبالنجم هم يهتدون.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الله جعل في الأرض معالمَ ظاهرة، وجعل النجوم وسائلَ للاهتداء، ولا سيما للمسافرين في البر والبحر؛ وفي ذلك تذكير بنعمه وتدبيره الدقيق للخلق.

translation: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق؟ أفلا تتذكرون؟
interpretation: لا يستوي الخالق القادر على الإيجاد والتدبير مع ما لا يخلق شيئًا ولا يملك نفعًا ولا ضرًّا؛ فالعقل يقتضي إفراد الله بالعبادة وترك ما سواه.

translation: And if you were to count Allah’s blessings, you could never enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that Allah’s favors are so abundant and continuous that human beings can neither fully recognize nor count them. Their inability to repay these blessings highlights their dependence on Him, while His forgiveness and mercy assure them that their shortcomings in gratitude do not place them beyond His compassion.

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal.
interpretation: Nothing within you is hidden from Allah—neither the thoughts and intentions you keep private nor the words and actions you make known—so live with sincerity and awareness that all you do is fully known to Him.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Allah create nothing, while they themselves are created.
interpretation: This verse establishes that worship belongs solely to Allah, because all supposed deities are created beings incapable of creating anything; therefore, invoking them as gods is a fundamental error.

translation: They are dead, not alive, and they do not know when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: The idols and false objects of worship are utterly lifeless and possess no awareness or power to respond; they cannot perceive the time when God will raise creation for judgment.

translation: Your God is One God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts deny the truth, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: The verse explains that rejection of God’s oneness is rooted not in a lack of evidence, but in an inward refusal to submit to the truth. Denial of the Hereafter exposes a hardened heart, while arrogance prevents a person from accepting divine guidance and accountability.

translation: Certainly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.
interpretation: Nothing hidden or openly expressed escapes Allah’s knowledge, and this awareness exposes the arrogance of those who reject truth and exalt themselves; such pride places them far from Allah’s love.

translation: And when it is said to them, “What has your Lord sent down?” they say, “Legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: This portrays the stubborn rejection of revelation by those who dismiss the Qur’an as mere ancient tales, revealing their unwillingness to recognize its divine origin and guidance.

translation: So that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, along with some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Truly evil is what they bear.
interpretation: Those who deliberately lead others astray will not escape responsibility for their own wrongdoing; they will also bear the burden of the misguidance they caused, without diminishing the responsibility of those who followed them. This is a warning against speaking or acting without knowledge, since misleading others compounds one’s guilt.

translation: Those before them plotted, so Allah struck at the foundations of their building; then the roof fell upon them from above, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse portrays how schemes built against God’s truth are destroyed from their very foundations: what the plotters constructed for protection and power becomes the cause of their ruin, and divine punishment reaches them unexpectedly.

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them and say, “Where are My partners for whose sake you used to oppose others?” Those who were granted knowledge will say, “Indeed, disgrace and misery today are upon the disbelievers.”
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the false gods whom the disbelievers defended and set beside Allah will prove powerless, and their worshippers will be exposed and humiliated. The people of true knowledge will affirm that disgrace and every form of evil belong to those who rejected Allah and persisted in associating partners with Him.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves will offer submission, saying, “We were not doing any evil.” Indeed, Allah knows best what you used to do.
interpretation: When people persist in wrongdoing until death overtakes them, they can no longer conceal or deny their deeds before the angels. Their claim of innocence is rejected because Allah’s complete knowledge exposes the reality of what they practiced, showing that repentance cannot be replaced by a last-moment denial.

translation: So enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. Indeed, how wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: Those who rejected the truth out of arrogance will be cast into Hell and remain there, receiving a punishment that is the fittingly miserable consequence of their pride and refusal to submit to God.

translation: And it was said to those who were mindful of God, “What has your Lord revealed?” They replied, “Good.” For those who do good in this world is a good reward, and the home of the Hereafter is even better. How excellent is the home of the God-fearing!
interpretation: The verse portrays the God-fearing as recognizing divine revelation as wholly good and responding to it with faith and righteous action. God promises them goodness in this life, while assuring them that the lasting reward of the Hereafter is superior; their true success lies in the excellent eternal home prepared for their piety.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow. There they will have whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the mindful of Him.
interpretation: Allah promises those who remain conscious of Him and obey Him an eternal dwelling of complete peace and abundance. Their reward is not limited to what they can imagine or earn in this world; in Paradise, every wholesome desire is fulfilled as an expression of Allah’s perfect generosity and justice.

translation: Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure and righteous, saying, “Peace be upon you; enter Paradise because of what you used to do.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the believers’ blessed end: because they remained pure in faith and conduct, the angels greet them with peace and announce their admission to Paradise. Their righteous deeds are the manifested cause of this reward, granted ultimately by Allah’s mercy.

translation: هل ينتظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي أمر ربك؟ كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم، وما ظلمهم الله، ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون.
interpretation: المعنى أن المكذبين لا يطلبون برهانًا جديدًا، بل يؤخرون الإيمان حتى تحضرهم الملائكة أو ينزل بهم قضاء الله، وعندئذ لا ينفعهم الإيمان الاضطراري. وهذه سنة تكررت في الأمم السابقة؛ فلم يكن هلاكهم ظلمًا من الله، وإنما كان نتيجة ظلمهم لأنفسهم بإصرارهم على الكفر ورفضهم الحق حتى استحقوا عاقبته.

translation: Then the evil consequences of what they had done befell them, and what they used to mock encompassed them.
interpretation: Their rejection and ridicule did not avert the truth; instead, the consequences of their own deeds came upon them, and the punishment they had treated mockingly surrounded them from every side.

translation: Those who associate partners with Allah say, “Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything without Him.” In the same way acted those before them. So is anything required of the messengers except clear conveyance?
interpretation: The verse exposes the false use of divine decree as an excuse for disbelief and forbidden practices. Allah’s allowing people to choose does not mean that He approves of their choices or removes their responsibility for them. The messengers’ duty is to deliver the truth clearly, while people remain accountable for whether they accept or reject it.

translation: And We certainly sent a messenger to every community, saying, “Worship Allah and keep away from false gods.” Among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom misguidance became justified. So travel through the land and observe how the end of those who denied was.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the central call of every messenger was to worship Allah alone and reject every form of false authority or devotion that competes with Him. Guidance was made available through the messengers, yet people differed in how they responded: some accepted the truth and were guided, while others persisted in rejection until misguidance became their deserved consequence. The command to travel and reflect on the fate of earlier deniers is an invitation to learn from history, recognizing that arrogant denial ultimately leads to ruin.

translation: If you are deeply concerned that they be guided, then surely Allah does not guide those whom He allows to go astray, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ that even his earnest desire for people’s guidance cannot compel those who knowingly persist in rejection; when they choose misguidance and turn away from truth, Allah does not grant them guidance by force, nor will they find anyone able to rescue or support them.

translation: They swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die. Indeed, He will—this is a binding promise upon Him, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the certainty with which the deniers rejected resurrection, despite having no sound knowledge for their claim. Allah affirms that bringing the dead back to life is a true and unavoidable promise, demonstrating His power and establishing the reality of accountability after death; the denial arises from ignorance rather than evidence.

translation: So that He may make clear to them that over which they differ, and so that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.
interpretation: Allah will resurrect the dead to establish the truth concerning the matters over which people disputed—especially the reality of resurrection—and to expose the falsehood of those who denied it.

translation: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: Allah’s will is absolute and needs no effort, means, or delay: when He decrees the existence of something, His command alone brings it into being. This affirms His complete power and that creation depends entirely on His command.

translation: And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after having been wronged, We will surely settle them in a good dwelling in this world; and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse promises that those who leave behind persecution and injustice for Allah’s sake will be granted a dignified and благоприятный life in this world, while their reward with Allah in the Hereafter will be far greater. It encourages steadfastness and sacrifice, assuring the oppressed believer that abandoning wrongdoing for faith is never a loss, even when the full value of the reward is not yet understood.

translation: Those who remain steadfast and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: They endure hardship with faith and entrust their affairs to Allah, relying on Him while continuing to act with righteousness and perseverance.

translation: We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.
interpretation: This affirms that God’s messengers were human beings chosen to receive revelation, not angels or divine beings. It also establishes that those who lack knowledge should seek clarification from trustworthy people who possess sound understanding.

translation: [We sent them] with clear proofs and scriptures. And We revealed to you the Reminder so that you may explain to people what has been sent down to them, so that they may reflect.
interpretation: God supported His messengers with evident signs and revealed writings, and entrusted the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with the Qur’an not only to convey its words but also to clarify their meanings and guidance. This clarification is meant to awaken thoughtful reflection, leading people to understand the revelation and live by it.

translation: Do those who plot evil feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in plotting evil must not assume they are safe from Allah’s judgment; His punishment may reach them suddenly and in a manner they neither expect nor can prevent.

translation: Or He may seize them during their movements, and they cannot thwart Him.
interpretation: God can overtake people even while they are actively going about their affairs, and no power or escape can render them beyond His authority.

translation: Or that He may seize them gradually through fear—for indeed, your Lord is Most Kind, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse warns that God may bring people to account through a gradual decline in their security, strength, or blessings, giving them opportunities to recognize their wrongdoing and return to Him; this measured forbearance reflects His kindness and mercy rather than indifference.

translation: Do they not see the things Allah has created, whose shadows turn to the right and the left, prostrating themselves before Allah in humility?
interpretation: The verse directs people to contemplate the created world: even the changing shadows, through their movement, testify to the order and authority of Allah and are described as prostrating before Him. This indicates that every creature is subject to His command, whether its submission is understood by humans or not; therefore, people should abandon arrogance and willingly humble themselves before their Creator.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever creature is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, as do the angels; they are not arrogant.
interpretation: All living beings, each in the manner Allah has ordained for them, are subject to His authority and submit to His will. The angels exemplify complete obedience, never refusing or considering themselves above worship, reminding human beings that true honor lies in humble submission to Allah.

translation: They fear their Lord above them and do whatever they are commanded.
interpretation: The verse portrays the angels as profoundly reverent and obedient servants of God: they recognize His absolute authority and carry out His commands without resistance or disobedience.

translation: And Allah has said, “Do not take two gods; He is only One God. So fear Me alone.”
interpretation: Allah commands that no partner or rival be associated with Him, affirming His absolute oneness and exclusive right to worship. Since all power and authority belong to Him alone, reverence and obedience must be directed solely to Him.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs the enduring devotion. Will you then fear someone other than Allah?
interpretation: Since Allah alone owns and governs all creation, worship, obedience, and reverent fear must be directed exclusively to Him; fearing any other as though it possessed independent power is unfounded.

translation: Whatever blessing you have is from Allah; then, when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help.
interpretation: Every good and benefit a person possesses ultimately comes from Allah, even when received through created means. Yet when hardship strikes, human beings instinctively turn to Him and plead for relief, revealing their innate dependence on their Creator and calling them to acknowledge Him with the same sincerity in times of ease.

translation: ثم إذا كشف الله عنكم الضر، إذا فريق منكم بربهم يشركون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن بعض الناس يلجؤون إليه وحده عند الشدة، فإذا زال عنهم البلاء عادوا إلى الغفلة والشرك، فنقضوا مقتضى اعترافهم بقدرة الله وفضله.

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them. Enjoy yourselves, then; soon you will know.
interpretation: This is a stern warning to those who respond to God’s blessings with ingratitude and associating partners with Him: their worldly enjoyment is temporary, and they will soon face the consequences of their denial.

translation: And they assign to those of whom they have no knowledge a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.
interpretation: They arrogantly devote part of God’s blessings to invented deities whose reality and authority they do not know, treating these false objects of worship as partners in what belongs solely to God. This fabricated attribution will not go unanswered; they will be held accountable for the false claims and acts of worship they ascribed to God.

translation: They attribute daughters to Allah—glory be to Him—while assigning to themselves whatever they desire.
interpretation: The verse condemns the pagan claim that angels or divine beings are Allah’s daughters, while they themselves preferred sons. It exposes this as a false, self-serving judgment and declares Allah far above such humanly invented descriptions.

translation: And when one of them is given the news of a female child, his face darkens, and he is inwardly consumed with grief.
interpretation: This portrays the shame and anguish that pre-Islamic people felt upon the birth of a daughter, exposing their unjust contempt for females and their inability to accept what God had decreed for them with contentment.

translation: He withdraws from the people because of the shame of the news he has been given. Should he keep the child in humiliation, or bury it in the earth? Surely evil is the judgment they make.
interpretation: The verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of treating the birth of a daughter as disgrace and contemplating her burial, exposing the injustice of valuing children according to gender and showing that such shameful judgments are utterly corrupt before God.

translation: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter possess the worst description, while Allah has the highest description. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Those who deny the Hereafter are characterized by the most deficient beliefs and qualities, whereas Allah alone possesses every attribute of perfection and majesty. His power is absolute, and His wisdom governs all things.

translation: If Allah were to hold people accountable for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature. But He grants them respite until an appointed time. Then, when their appointed time arrives, they can neither delay it for an hour nor bring it forward.
interpretation: Allah’s continued preservation of the world is an expression of His forbearance, not approval of wrongdoing. He gives people time to repent and reform, while judgment remains certain and fixed; once the appointed term comes, no one can postpone it or make it occur sooner.

translation: They attribute to Allah what they themselves dislike, and their tongues utter lies, claiming that theirs will be the best outcome. Without doubt, the Fire is theirs, and they will be sent ahead into it.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of those who attribute to Allah what they consider shameful for themselves, while falsely assuring themselves of honor and salvation. Their invented claims cannot protect them; because of their disbelief and lies, their final destination will be Hell.

translation: By Allah, We certainly sent messengers to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them. So he is their ally today, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: Allah consoles the Prophet by showing that rejection and Satan’s deception are not new: earlier peoples were led to regard their false beliefs and wrongdoing as good. By choosing that deception, they made Satan their protector instead of Allah, but this apparent alliance will end in the Hereafter with painful punishment.

translation: We have not sent down the Book to you except so that you may clarify for them that over which they differ, and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an was revealed to resolve humanity’s disputes about truth, belief, and right conduct by making God’s guidance clear through the Prophet. Those who sincerely believe receive from it direction toward what is right and mercy that leads them away from error and confusion.

translation: And Allah sends down water from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. Indeed, in that is a sign for people who listen.
interpretation: The revival of barren earth through rain is a clear indication of Allah’s power to bring life where there was lifelessness, and it calls attentive hearts to recognize His creative authority and the certainty of resurrection.

translation: And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you drink from what is within their bellies—between digested matter and blood—pure milk, pleasant and easy for those who drink it.
interpretation: This verse directs attention to God’s power and wisdom in bringing forth pure, nourishing milk from within livestock, despite its emergence amid digested contents and blood. It is a sign of His creative precision and a reminder that His blessings may arise through processes whose hidden workings surpass human perception.

translation: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سَكَرًا ورزقًا حسنًا؛ إن في ذلك لآيةً لقومٍ يعقلون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن من ثمار النخيل والأعناب ما يصنعه الناس من شرابٍ مُسكِر، ومنها ما ينتفعون به رزقًا طيبًا نافعًا. وفي هذا التنوع، وما أودعه الله في الثمار من منافع، دليلٌ على قدرته وتدبيره، وعبرةٌ لمن يتفكر بعقله فيحسن التمييز بين النافع والضار.

translation: And your Lord inspired the bees: “Take dwellings in the mountains, in the trees, and in what people construct.”
interpretation: Allah guides the bees by His innate instruction to choose secure places for their homes, whether in mountains, trees, or human-made structures. This divine guidance reveals His wisdom and care in ordering even the smallest creatures, directing them toward a life suited to their nature and benefit.

translation: “Then eat from every kind of fruit and follow the ways of your Lord, made easy for you.” From their bellies comes a drink of varying colors, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect.
interpretation: Allah directs attention to the bee’s instinctive obedience and the remarkable order through which it produces honey of different colors and beneficial qualities. This points to His wisdom, power, and care in making creation serve human well-being, while inviting people to recognize these signs through thoughtful reflection.

translation: And Allah created you, then He causes you to die. Among you are those who are brought back to the feeblest stage of life, so that after having knowledge they know nothing. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize their complete dependence on Allah throughout every stage of life: He brings them into existence, determines their lifespan, and may return some to a state of extreme weakness in which their acquired knowledge and abilities fade. This change reveals that human strength and understanding are temporary, while Allah’s knowledge and power remain perfect and unrestricted.

translation: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. Yet those who have been favored would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess so that they would become equal in it. Do they then deny Allah’s favor?
interpretation: تُقيم الآية حُجّة على من يجعل لله شركاء: فالإنسان لا يرضى عادةً أن يساوي مَن تحت يده في ماله وملكه، فكيف ينسب إلى الله شركاء من خلقه، أو يجحد أن ما عنده من النعم إنما هو فضل من الله؟

translation: And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and from your spouses He has given you children and grandchildren, and He has provided you with wholesome things. Will they then believe in falsehood and deny Allah’s blessing?
interpretation: Allah reminds people that the intimate bonds of marriage, the continuation of family through children and descendants, and the provision of good things are all gifts from Him. The verse therefore condemns the contradiction of benefiting from Allah’s blessings while directing belief toward falsehood or denying that those blessings come from Him.

translation: And they worship besides Allah those who have no power to provide them with anything from the sustenance of the heavens and the earth, nor are they able.
interpretation: The verse exposes the futility of worshipping anything besides Allah: such beings neither control any provision in the universe nor possess the ability to grant it. Since all sustenance ultimately comes by Allah’s power, devotion and reliance belong to Him alone.

translation: So do not draw comparisons for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: Do not liken Allah to His creation or attribute to Him qualities based on human assumptions; His reality and perfection surpass human understanding, so belief about Him must rest on what He has revealed rather than on speculative comparisons.

translation: Allah sets forth the example of a slave owned by another, who has power over nothing, and one whom We have provided with good sustenance from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise belongs to Allah; yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: Allah exposes the falsehood of equating powerless idols with Him: just as a helpless owned servant cannot be compared with a person whom Allah has enriched and who gives from that provision, nothing can be compared with Allah, the true Provider and Sovereign worthy of worship. Their failure to recognize this is due to ignorance of the vast difference between the Creator and those who possess no independent power.

translation: Allah presents the example of two men: one of them is mute, incapable of anything, and is a burden on his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is himself on a straight path?
interpretation: This parable exposes the emptiness of worshipping powerless beings: they can neither act nor benefit those who rely on them. Such beings cannot be compared with Allah, whose command establishes justice and whose guidance is perfectly straight.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. The coming of the Hour is only like the blink of an eye—or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.
interpretation: All realities hidden from creation are fully known and governed by Allah, so the exact time of the Resurrection lies solely within His knowledge. Its occurrence, whenever He decrees it, requires no gradual process or effort: His command brings it about instantly, demonstrating that nothing is beyond His power.

translation: And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing, and He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الإنسان يبدأ حياته عاجزًا عن العلم، ثم يهبُه وسائل الإدراك والتفكير ليتعلم ويميز الحق من الباطل. فهذه النعم ليست مجرد قدرات جسدية، بل أمانة تقود إلى معرفة الله وشكره باستعمال السمع والبصر والعقل فيما يرضيه.

translation: Have they not seen the birds, subjected to God’s command, soaring in the expanse of the sky? None holds them aloft except God. Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The birds’ ability to remain in flight, governed by laws and capacities that God has established, is a sign of His sustaining power and wise order. Those who believe perceive in this ordinary spectacle evidence that creation is neither self-sufficient nor without purpose, but continually upheld by God.

translation: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of tranquility, and He has made for you from the hides of livestock homes that you find light to carry on the day of your travel and the day of your stay. And from their wool, fur, and hair He has provided furnishings and goods for you to enjoy for a time.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that He has placed comfort, security, and stability in their homes, and has also made the animals He created a source of practical benefit. Their hides can provide portable shelter, while their wool, fur, and hair can be made into furnishings and useful possessions. These blessings show divine care through both permanent and movable forms of livelihood, while the phrase “for a time” points to the temporary nature of worldly provisions and comforts.

translation: And Allah has made for you, from what He created, shades for shelter; He has made for you retreats in the mountains; and He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your own violence. In this way He completes His blessing upon you, so that you may submit.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize Allah’s encompassing care in the ordinary means of protection He has provided—shade, natural shelters, clothing, and protective equipment. These blessings are not merely material conveniences; they are signs of His mercy and a reminder that true gratitude is shown by submitting to Him and using what He provides in ways that preserve life, restrain violence, and obey His guidance.

translation: But if they turn away, your only duty is to deliver the message clearly.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the messenger’s responsibility is to convey God’s revelation openly and unmistakably; whether people accept or reject it remains their own choice and accountability.

translation: They recognize Allah’s blessing, then deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: They perceive the blessings Allah has granted them, yet refuse to acknowledge that He alone is their source or to respond with gratitude and submission; this denial is a form of disbelief.

translation: And on the Day We raise from every nation a witness, those who disbelieved will not be permitted to speak, nor will they be allowed to seek reconciliation.
interpretation: This portrays the final judgment as a moment when each community’s truth is established through its witness, leaving those who rejected faith without a valid excuse or any opportunity to return, make amends, or have their punishment deferred.

translation: And when those who wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: The verse portrays the final consequence of persistent wrongdoing: once the punishment becomes manifest, it cannot be reduced or postponed, leaving the wrongdoers with no opportunity to escape or delay its due recompense.

translation: And when those who associated others with Allah see their partners, they will say, “Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke instead of You.” But they will throw their claim back at them, saying, “Indeed, you are liars.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the idolaters will point to the beings they worshipped besides Allah and try to justify their devotion before Him. Those supposed partners will reject that claim and disown them, exposing the falsehood of their worship and leaving them without any defense.

translation: On that Day they will offer submission to Allah, and what they used to invent will vanish from them.
interpretation: When confronted with the truth and Allah’s judgment, those who denied Him will have no choice but to surrender completely; the false claims and fabricated partners they relied upon in worldly life will prove powerless and disappear.

translation: Those who disbelieved and hindered others from the path of Allah—We will increase them in punishment upon punishment because of the corruption they used to spread.
interpretation: The verse warns that responsibility is intensified when a person not only rejects truth personally but also actively prevents others from following it and spreads corruption. Their additional punishment reflects the broader harm they deliberately caused beyond their own wrongdoing.

translation: And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these people. We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, and as guidance, mercy, and good news for those who submit to Allah.
interpretation: The verse depicts the Day of Judgment, when every community will be confronted by a witness from within its own history, while the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will testify concerning his people and their response to the revelation. The Qur’an is described as explaining everything essential for faith, worship, moral conduct, and salvation—not by detailing every worldly fact, but by providing the principles and guidance necessary for living rightly. Its guidance brings mercy through reform and forgiveness, and its promise of success is glad tidings for those who sincerely submit to Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence, and giving to relatives, and He forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may take heed.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive moral principle: believers must uphold fairness, go beyond bare obligation through kindness and generosity—especially toward family—and actively avoid every form of indecency, harmful wrongdoing, and oppressive excess. Its reminder calls people to reflect and let these commands shape their conduct toward others.

translation: وفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم، ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها، وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلًا؛ إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون.
interpretation: يأمر الله بالالتزام بالعهود والمواثيق والصدق في الأيمان، ويحذر من نقضها بعد توثيقها، لأن من أقسم فقد أشهد الله على نفسه وجعله ضامنًا لما التزم به. ولا يخفى على الله شيء من الوفاء أو الخيانة، ولذلك سيحاسب الإنسان على حقيقة أفعاله لا على مجرد أقواله.

translation: ولا تكونوا كالمرأة التي نقضت غزلها من بعد إحكامه خيوطًا متفرقة، تجعلون أيمانكم وسيلةً للخداع والغدر بينكم، بحجة أن جماعةً أكثر عددًا وقوةً من جماعة. إنما يختبركم الله بذلك، وليبيّنن لكم يوم القيامة حقيقة ما كنتم تختلفون فيه.
interpretation: ينهى الله عن نقض العهود بعد توكيدها، وعن استعمال الأيمان ستارًا للمصلحة والخداع حين يُترك الالتزام لأن طرفًا آخر أقوى أو أكثر عددًا. فالوفاء بالعهد مبدأ ثابت لا يتغير بتغير موازين القوة، وسيكشف الله يوم القيامة صدق المواقف وحقيقة الخلافات.

translation: Had Allah willed, He could have made you one single community; but He lets stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: Human differences in faith and conduct occur within Allah’s wisdom and sovereign will, yet this does not remove human responsibility: people are accountable for the choices and actions through which they accept guidance or turn away from it.

translation: Do not use your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves, lest a foot slip after it has been firmly planted, and lest you taste evil because you have hindered others from the way of Allah; and for you is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against making promises under oath and then using them deceitfully or breaking them for worldly gain. Such betrayal undermines trust after it has been established, leads to moral downfall, and becomes especially grave when it causes people to turn away from Allah’s path; its consequence is both humiliation in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Do not exchange Allah’s covenant for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: Do not break or compromise your commitment to Allah in pursuit of temporary worldly gain. Whatever reward and lasting good Allah has prepared is far superior to anything acquired by sacrificing faithfulness to His covenant.

translation: Whatever you have will perish, but whatever is with Allah will remain. And We will surely reward those who are patient with a reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart away from reliance on temporary worldly possessions and toward what endures with Allah: faith, obedience, and the reward preserved for them. It also teaches that steadfastness in hardship and in doing what is right is never wasted, for Allah rewards the patient with a generous recompense measured by the finest of their deeds.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely grant them a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: True faith joined with righteous action brings a person a wholesome life grounded in inner contentment, trust in God, and a sense of purpose, even amid worldly hardship. In the Hereafter, God will honor such people with a reward surpassing the value of their deeds through His generosity.

translation: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
interpretation: Before reciting the Qur’an, the believer is instructed to turn to Allah for protection from Satan, so that distracting thoughts and misleading influences do not obstruct sincere attention, understanding, and obedience to His words.

translation: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: Satan cannot compel or govern those whose faith is sincere and whose hearts depend upon Allah; his influence over them is limited to temptation, which they can resist by turning back to their Lord.

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate partners with Him.
interpretation: Satan’s influence is not an independent power over everyone; it prevails over those who willingly follow and rely on him, and over those whose shirk places them outside sincere submission to Allah.

translation: And when We replace one verse with another—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, “You are only fabricating.” Rather, most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that divine revelation may be replaced or superseded according to Allah’s wisdom and knowledge of what best serves each stage of guidance. The accusation of fabrication arose from ignorance of this wisdom; revelation is determined by Allah, not invented by the Prophet.

translation: Say, “The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to strengthen those who believe, and as guidance and good news for those who submit.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Qur’an is a truthful revelation from God, conveyed by the Holy Spirit—understood as Gabriel. Its purpose is to steady believers in faith, guide them toward what is right, and give glad tidings to those who sincerely submit to God.

translation: And We certainly know that they say, “It is only a human being who teaches him.” The language of the one to whom they allude is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: The verse rejects the claim that the Qur’an was taught to the Prophet by a human being: the person they alleged was not an eloquent Arabic speaker, whereas the Qur’an was revealed in exceptionally clear and powerful Arabic. Its linguistic form therefore exposes their accusation as implausible and confirms that its source is divine revelation, not human instruction.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in Allah’s signs—Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Because they knowingly reject Allah’s clear signs and persist in disbelief, they deprive themselves of divine guidance; consequently, they face a painful punishment for their deliberate refusal of the truth.

translation: It is only those who do not believe in Allah’s signs who fabricate lies; it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: The verse declares that deliberate falsehood against divine truth arises from rejecting Allah’s signs. Those who deny revelation and invent claims against it are not merely mistaken; their persistent rejection exposes them as the true liars.

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after having believed—except one who is compelled while his heart remains steadfast in faith—but those who willingly open their hearts to disbelief shall incur the wrath of Allah, and theirs will be a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This verse teaches that accountability rests primarily on the heart’s willing choice: a person forced to utter words of disbelief while inwardly holding firmly to faith is not condemned, whereas one who embraces disbelief deliberately and accepts it inwardly turns away from Allah and faces His wrath and severe punishment.

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: Their rejection of faith arises from choosing immediate worldly desires and benefits over the lasting consequences of the Hereafter; by persistently preferring disbelief and turning away from truth, they deprive themselves of divine guidance.

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed; and those are the heedless.
interpretation: Because they persistently reject the truth, their inner faculties become closed to guidance: their hearts no longer understand it, their hearing no longer receives it, and their sight no longer perceives its signs. Their heedlessness is therefore not a lack of ability, but the consequence of turning away until rejection becomes firmly established in them.

translation: Without a doubt, in the Hereafter they will be the losers.
interpretation: Their denial and rejection of truth may bring them temporary worldly advantages, but it will ultimately deprive them of God’s reward and leave them facing the loss of the Hereafter.

translation: Then indeed your Lord—for those who emigrated after having been persecuted, then struggled and remained steadfast—indeed your Lord, after that, is surely All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse assures believers who were pressured or persecuted for their faith that sincere repentance, sacrifice, perseverance, and striving in obedience to God erase what preceded them and place them under His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: On the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be fully repaid for what it did, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment of complete personal accountability: each person will be concerned with defending their own deeds, while God will render a perfectly just judgment, withholding neither reward nor punishment deserved by anyone.

translation: And Allah presents the example of a town that was secure and peaceful, with its provision coming to it abundantly from every place. Yet it denied the blessings of Allah, so Allah made it taste the clothing of hunger and fear because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse teaches that security, prosperity, and abundant provision are divine blessings, not guarantees of permanence. When a people respond to these blessings with denial, ingratitude, and persistent wrongdoing, they may lose their wellbeing and experience hardship and insecurity as a consequence of their own actions.

translation: Indeed, a messenger from among them came to them, but they rejected him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse shows that their punishment was not unjust or unexpected: they were given guidance through a messenger from their own people, yet they deliberately denied him and persisted in wrongdoing, making them deserving of the consequences that befell them.

translation: So eat of the lawful and wholesome things that Allah has provided for you, and give thanks for Allah’s blessing, if it is Him that you worship.
interpretation: True worship of Allah requires receiving His provision within what He has made lawful and wholesome, while acknowledging His generosity with sincere gratitude rather than treating His blessings as one’s own entitlement.

translation: He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which a name other than Allah’s has been invoked. But whoever is compelled by necessity—neither desiring it nor exceeding the limits—then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
