interpretation: The verse establishes that these foods are prohibited, while affirming that genuine necessity is an exception: a person facing serious need may consume only what is required to preserve life, without seeking the forbidden food or going beyond the amount needed. This concession reflects Allah’s mercy and forgiveness, while preserving the seriousness of the prohibition.

translation: Do not say, falsely claiming with your tongues, “This is lawful and this is unlawful,” thereby fabricating lies against Allah. Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never prosper.
interpretation: The verse forbids declaring something lawful or unlawful in Allah’s name without clear revelation or sound knowledge. Such claims are not mere personal errors; they are a serious form of attributing falsehood to Allah, and those who persist in this have no true success or blessing.

translation: A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Whatever worldly benefit they gain through falsehood or disobedience is temporary and insignificant; it cannot protect them from the painful punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter.

translation: And for those who were Jews, We prohibited what We have previously related to you. We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The prohibitions imposed upon the Jews were a just consequence of their own wrongdoing and transgression, not an injustice from God. Their suffering arose from their choices, while God’s judgment remained fair and purposeful.

translation: Then indeed, your Lord is—for those who commit evil out of ignorance, then repent afterward and reform—indeed, your Lord after that is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Even when a person falls into wrongdoing through ignorance, heedlessness, or weakness, the door of mercy remains open: sincere repentance must be followed by correcting one’s conduct and making amends where possible. Whoever turns back to God in this way may hope for His complete forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a model community, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not among the polytheists.
interpretation: Abraham embodied the virtues of an entire community: steadfast faith, sincere submission, and unwavering devotion to Allah alone. He turned away from every form of idolatry and false belief, remaining upright in his worship and setting an enduring example of pure monotheism.

translation: Grateful for His blessings; He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This describes Abraham as one who recognized Allah’s blessings with sincere gratitude expressed through faith and obedience. Because of his devotion, Allah selected him for a special mission and guided him firmly along the path of truth.

translation: And We granted him goodness in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: Allah honored him with blessings, a good reputation, and steadfast guidance in this life, and promised him the elevated rank of the righteous in the Hereafter because of his sincere faith and obedience.

translation: Then We revealed to you: “Follow the way of Abraham, inclining exclusively toward truth; he was not of the polytheists.”
interpretation: God commands the Prophet to uphold Abraham’s pure, sincere devotion to Him alone, free from every form of associating partners with God. This establishes that true guidance is steadfast monotheism and rejection of all idolatry.

translation: The Sabbath was imposed only upon those who differed concerning it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: The Sabbath was not an obligation imposed universally, but a distinctive command given to a particular people after they disputed about it. Their disagreement and conduct concerning this command will ultimately be resolved by God, whose judgment on the Day of Resurrection will expose the truth and distinguish right from wrong.

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and gracious instruction, and debate with them in the best manner. Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are rightly guided.
interpretation: Call people to faith through sound judgment, compassionate counsel, and respectful dialogue—not through coercion, harshness, or humiliation. God alone fully knows the inner state of those who have gone astray and those who are guided, so the caller’s duty is to communicate truth with wisdom and leave ultimate judgment to Him.

translation: And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the equivalent of what was inflicted upon you. But if you are patient, it is surely better for those who are patient.
interpretation: This verse establishes justice as a limit in responding to harm: retaliation may not exceed the original wrong. Yet it directs believers toward the higher path of restraint, teaching that patience and forgiveness are spiritually better because they prevent revenge from becoming another form of injustice.

translation: And be patient, for your patience is only through Allah. Do not grieve over them, nor be distressed by the plots they devise.
interpretation: The verse teaches that steadfastness is not achieved by human strength alone, but by seeking Allah’s help and placing one’s trust in Him. The believer should not let the rejection or hostility of others cause despair, nor allow their schemes to disturb the heart, knowing that Allah sustains those who remain patient and faithful.

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who are mindful of Him and those who excel in doing good.
interpretation: Allah grants His special support, guidance, protection, and nearness to those who guard themselves from disobedience and sincerely practice excellence in their conduct and worship.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, so that We might show him some of Our signs. Indeed, He alone is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse proclaims Allah’s absolute transcendence and power through the miraculous Night Journey of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Makkah to Jerusalem. By describing Muhammad as “His servant,” it honors him through complete devotion and servitude to Allah, while showing that the journey was a divine sign intended to reveal realities beyond ordinary human experience. The blessing around the Farthest Mosque points to the sacredness and spiritual significance of Jerusalem, and Allah’s being All-Hearing and All-Seeing affirms that the journey occurred by His perfect knowledge, witnessing, and authority.

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: “Do not take anyone besides Me as a trustee.”
interpretation: The revelation given to Moses was meant to guide the Children of Israel toward exclusive devotion to God. They are commanded not to entrust their ultimate dependence, protection, or worship to anyone besides Him.

translation: يا ذريةَ من حملنا مع نوح، إنه كان عبدًا شكورًا.
interpretation: يذكّر الله بني إسرائيل وذرية المؤمنين بنعمة إنجاء آبائهم مع نوح، ويدعوهم إلى الاقتداء بنوح في إخلاص العبودية وكثرة شكر النعم، إذ كان يشكر الله في جميع أحواله.

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: “You will surely spread corruption in the land twice, and you will surely rise to great arrogance.”
interpretation: This verse is a divine foretelling that the Children of Israel would, at two distinct times, transgress God’s commands, spread injustice and corruption, and become excessively proud and oppressive. It warns that power and privilege, when severed from obedience and righteousness, lead to ruin and divine accountability.

translation: Then, when the promise of the first of the two came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they penetrated throughout the homes; and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This means that after the Children of Israel committed the first great corruption, God brought upon them a powerful people as an instrument of judgment. They entered their cities and homes, demonstrating that the foretold punishment was certain and could not be averted.

translation: Then We gave you back the upper hand over them, and We reinforced you with wealth and children, and made you greater in number and strength.
interpretation: After the Israelites’ repentance and return to obedience, God restored their power over their enemies, increased their prosperity and offspring, and strengthened them through greater numbers and support.

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. Then, when the promise of the latter occasion comes, they will bring sorrow to your faces, enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy whatever they overcome.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the consequences of human conduct ultimately return to the people themselves: righteousness brings benefit, while wrongdoing brings harm. It also warns that persistent corruption and transgression can lead to severe humiliation and destruction when divine judgment is fulfilled.

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you. But if you return to wrongdoing, We will return to punishment. And We have made Hell a confinement for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse leaves the door of repentance open while warning that repeated rebellion brings renewed divine punishment; Hell is the final confinement prepared for those who persist in disbelief.

translation: Indeed, this Qur’an guides to what is most upright and gives glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a guide to the soundest way of belief, character, and conduct. Those who respond to its guidance through faith and righteous action are promised an immense reward from Allah.

translation: And indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This warns that rejecting the resurrection and accountability before God leads to severe punishment, because denial of the Hereafter removes the awareness that gives human actions their ultimate moral consequence.

translation: Man prays for evil as he prays for good; and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: الإنسان، من شدة عجلته وقلة بصيرته بعواقب الأمور، قد يدعو على نفسه أو غيره بالشر كما يدعو بالخير، أو يطلب ما يظنه نافعًا وهو في الحقيقة ضارّ به؛ لذلك يوجّهه الله إلى التأنّي والتثبت قبل الدعاء والطلب.

translation: And We made the night and the day two signs. Then We blotted out the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, so that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. And We have explained everything in detail.
interpretation: The alternation of darkness and light is a deliberate sign of God’s ordering and wisdom: the night’s concealment and the day’s illumination establish the conditions for rest, activity, seeking provision, and measuring the passage of time. By observing this ordered pattern, people are directed to recognize that creation is neither random nor without purpose, and that its details point to the precision of its Creator.

translation: And We have attached every person’s record to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection We will bring forth for him a book that he will find laid open.
interpretation: Every person carries the consequences of their own deeds inseparably, and on the Day of Resurrection their complete record will be made openly visible, leaving no room to deny or conceal what they did.

translation: “Read your record. Today your own soul is sufficient as an account-setter against you.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, each person will be confronted with the complete record of their deeds, leaving no need for another witness or judge to establish the truth. Their own awareness and recognition of what they did will be enough to hold them accountable.

translation: Whoever is guided is guided only for his own benefit, and whoever goes astray goes astray only to his own detriment. No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. We would never punish until We have sent a messenger.
interpretation: Guidance and misguidance ultimately affect each person’s own moral and spiritual outcome. No one will be held accountable for another’s wrongdoing, and God’s justice is such that punishment does not come before clear communication of His message through a messenger.

translation: And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent people, but they act wickedly within it; thus the decree becomes binding upon it, and We utterly destroy it.
interpretation: المقصود أن الله إذا أراد إهلاك قرية أقام على أهلها الحجة، فبلّغ أهلَ النعمة والقدرة فيها أمرَه ونهاه، لكنهم استكبروا وفسقوا، واتبعهم غيرهم، فاستحقّت القرية العذاب. وليس المعنى أن الله يأمرهم بالفسق، بل إن عصيانهم بعد قيام الحجة هو سبب استحقاق الهلاك.

translation: And how many generations We destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord as All-Aware and All-Seeing of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: The verse warns that the destruction of past nations was a consequence of their wrongdoing, while affirming that God knows every sin and perceives every deed completely; therefore, no injustice or hidden transgression escapes His judgment.

translation: Whoever desires the immediate world, We hasten for him therein whatever We will, for whomever We intend. Then We appoint Hell for him; he will enter it condemned and banished.
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly desire alone does not secure a person’s aims: God grants from it only what He wills and to whom He wills. Whoever makes the fleeting world his ultimate pursuit, neglecting accountability and obedience to God, will ultimately face humiliation and exclusion in the Hereafter.

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as it ought to be, while being a believer—then their striving will be appreciated.
interpretation: True pursuit of the Hereafter requires sincere faith accompanied by righteous effort directed according to God’s guidance. Such effort is not lost; God accepts it and rewards it, even if its results are not fully seen in this world.

translation: No indeed, We provide for these and for those from the gift of your Lord; and the gift of your Lord has never been restricted.
interpretation: God grants worldly provision to both those who seek the Hereafter and those who pursue only this life, according to His wisdom. Such provision is not itself proof of divine approval or spiritual success, for God’s gifts are vast and unrestricted, while true distinction lies in how people respond to Him and what they ultimately receive in the Hereafter.

translation: See how We have favored some of them over others; yet the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in excellence.
interpretation: Worldly differences in wealth, status, ability, and circumstance are limited and temporary signs of God’s wisdom, not measures of ultimate worth. The true and far greater distinctions will appear in the Hereafter, where people will be rewarded according to faith, righteousness, and their deeds.

translation: Do not set up another deity alongside Allah, lest you sit disgraced and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse commands exclusive devotion to Allah and warns that directing worship or ultimate reliance to anyone besides Him leads to humiliation, blame, and spiritual abandonment.

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you show kindness to parents. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, do not say to them even “uff,” nor rebuke them, but speak to them graciously.
interpretation: This verse establishes devotion to God as the foundation of life and places dutiful kindness to parents immediately after it, especially when age makes them dependent and vulnerable. It forbids even the slightest expression of annoyance, whether in words or attitude, and commands respectful, gentle, and dignified speech. True righteousness therefore appears not only in serving parents, but in preserving their honor and responding to their weakness with patience and mercy.

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility, out of mercy, and say, “My Lord, have mercy on them, as they raised me when I was small.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that gratitude to one’s parents should be expressed through gentle humility, compassionate care, and sincere prayer for them, remembering the mercy and devoted nurturing they showed during one’s helpless childhood.

translation: Your Lord knows best what is within yourselves. If you are righteous, then surely He is ever Forgiving to those who constantly turn back to Him.
interpretation: God knows the sincerity and hidden intentions of people, so outward appearances cannot conceal their true condition. Whoever strives for righteousness and, when falling short, repeatedly returns to God in repentance may rely on His continual forgiveness.

translation: And give the relative his due, as well as the needy and the traveler, and do not squander wastefully.
interpretation: This verse commands honoring the rights of relatives and providing support to those in need, including travelers who lack resources. It also forbids wastefulness, teaching that wealth should be spent responsibly and with balance rather than extravagantly or without purpose.

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and Satan has always been ungrateful to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse condemns extravagant and irresponsible spending because it reflects the rebellious, ungrateful disposition of Satan: using blessings without restraint or gratitude instead of honoring the One who granted them.

translation: And if you turn away from them, seeking a mercy from your Lord that you hope for, then speak to them gentle words.
interpretation: When you cannot fulfill someone’s request because you yourself are awaiting provision from God, do not respond with harshness or humiliation. Address them with kindness, reassurance, and words that preserve their dignity and keep hope alive.

translation: Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully, lest you sit blameworthy and exhausted.
interpretation: This teaches moderation in spending: do not be miserly by withholding what is due, nor wasteful by giving beyond your means, for either extreme brings blame and leaves a person unable to meet their responsibilities.

translation: Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whoever He wills and restricts it. Surely, He is All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: Provision is distributed according to God’s perfect wisdom and knowledge of each person’s circumstances, not merely according to worldly merit or status. Therefore, abundance should inspire gratitude rather than pride, while scarcity should be met with patience and trust, knowing that neither reflects God’s ignorance or neglect of His servants.

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you. Indeed, killing them is a grave sin.
interpretation: God forbids taking the lives of children because of fear that poverty will result from supporting them. Provision belongs to God, who sustains both children and parents; therefore, anxiety about material hardship cannot justify such a grave violation of innocent life.

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is an obscenity and an evil way.
interpretation: The verse forbids not only the act itself but also the paths that lead toward it, such as improper intimacy, desire-driven conduct, and circumstances that weaken moral restraint. It describes this sin as profoundly indecent because it violates human dignity and sacred boundaries, and as an evil way because it harms individuals, families, and society and leads away from righteousness.

translation: Do not kill the soul whom Allah has made sacred, except with due right. And whoever is killed unjustly, We have granted his heir authority; so let him not exceed the limits in killing. Indeed, he has been supported.
interpretation: Allah forbids unlawful killing and grants the victim’s rightful heir the authority to pursue justice, but prohibits vengeance that exceeds the bounds of a just penalty. Divine support is promised through the protection of this right, not through unchecked retaliation.

translation: And do not approach the orphan’s property except in the best manner, until they reach maturity. And fulfill the covenant; surely, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse commands that an orphan’s wealth be protected and managed only in a way that serves the orphan’s welfare, with no exploitation or improper use, until the orphan becomes mature and capable of managing it. It also establishes that commitments are a serious trust: every covenant must be honored, because those who make promises are accountable for them before God.

translation: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم، وزنوا بالميزان المستقيم العادل؛ ذلك خيرٌ لكم وأحسنُ عاقبةً ومآلًا.
interpretation: يأمر الله بإقامة العدل في معاملات الناس، فلا ينقص المرء حقوقهم حين يكيل أو يزن، لأن الأمانة والإنصاف يحققان البركة والثقة، ويقودان إلى العاقبة الحسنة في الدنيا والآخرة.

translation: Do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, hearing, sight, and heart—all of these will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse forbids people from adopting, repeating, or acting upon claims without reliable knowledge. It reminds us that our faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding are trusts for which we will be held accountable, so they must be used truthfully and responsibly.

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will never tear through the earth, nor will you reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse teaches that arrogance is contrary to a person’s true nature and limits. However powerful or elevated one may feel, one remains a dependent creature, unable to overcome the earth beneath them or equal the mountains above them. It therefore calls for humility in conduct, reminding us that pride has no basis in the face of human weakness and the greatness of God’s creation.

translation: All of that—its evil—is detestable in the sight of your Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the prohibited behaviors previously mentioned are not merely socially harmful but morally repugnant to God; therefore, a believer should avoid them out of reverence for Him, knowing that He condemns both their outward harm and the corruption they cause within human character and society.

translation: That is among the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you. Do not set up another deity alongside Allah, lest you be cast into Hell, condemned and cast away.
interpretation: The guidance and moral commands just given are divine wisdom, intended to shape a life of justice, humility, and responsibility. At their foundation is pure devotion to Allah: associating any partner with Him rejects the source of this guidance and leads a person to ultimate disgrace and exclusion from His mercy.

translation: Has your Lord then chosen sons for you, while taking females from among the angels? Indeed, you are saying something monstrous.
interpretation: The verse rebukes the claim that God has children while people reserve sons for themselves and attribute daughters to Him, especially by calling the angels female. It exposes this belief as a grave contradiction and an outrageous falsehood, since God is exalted above having offspring or being described through human distinctions and preferences.

translation: Indeed, We have presented in this Qur’an every kind of reminder so that they may take heed, but it only increases them in aversion.
interpretation: Allah has varied the Qur’an’s signs, teachings, warnings, and examples to awaken people’s reflection and guide them to truth. Yet those who stubbornly reject it respond with greater estrangement, because their refusal prevents them from benefiting from its guidance.

translation: Say, “If there had been gods alongside Him, as they claim, they would surely have sought a way to challenge the Lord of the Throne.”
interpretation: The verse refutes the claim that God has partners: true gods would possess independent power and would therefore contend for authority or seek to overcome the Possessor of the Throne. The absence of any such rivalry demonstrates that sovereignty belongs exclusively to God.

translation: Glory be to Him, and exalted is He far above what they say.
interpretation: This declares that Allah is utterly transcendent and free from every false claim or imperfection attributed to Him; nothing people say can diminish His absolute perfection and majesty.

translation: The seven heavens, the earth, and all who are in them glorify Him. There is nothing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Ever-Forbearing, Most Forgiving.
interpretation: Everything in creation continually bears witness to Allah’s perfection and submits to His order, even though human beings generally cannot perceive the manner of that glorification. The verse calls people to humility before the universal worship surrounding them: despite their failure to recognize it, Allah does not hasten to punish them, but gives them respite and forgives those who turn back to Him.

translation: And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed barrier.
interpretation: When the Qur’an is recited with truth, those who deny the Hereafter may be present and hear its words, yet their rejection creates an unseen barrier that prevents them from recognizing its guidance and responding to it. This barrier is not a physical separation, but a spiritual veil resulting from their disbelief and resistance to the truth.

translation: And We have placed veils over their hearts so that they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn their backs in aversion.
interpretation: The verse portrays how persistent rejection of truth can harden a person’s inner perception: although the Qur’an is recited to them, their hearts become unreceptive and their ears unwilling to listen. Their turning away when God alone is mentioned reveals their attachment to false beliefs and their refusal to acknowledge sincere monotheism.

translation: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك، وإذ هم يتناجون سرًّا، إذ يقول الظالمون: ما تتبعون إلا رجلًا مسحورًا.
interpretation: يبين الله تعالى أنه محيط بعلم حال المشركين حين يستمعون إلى النبي ﷺ، وبما يتناجى به بعضهم خفية؛ فقد كانوا لا ينصتون طلبًا للحق، بل يتآمرون على رد دعوته، ويتهمونه ظلمًا بالسحر ليصرفوا الناس عن تصديقه، مع أن عجزهم عن مواجهة حجته لا يبرر هذا الاتهام.

translation: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلّوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلاً
interpretation: يأمر الله نبيَّه أن يتأمل في حجج المكذبين وتشبيهاتهم الباطلة؛ فقد انحرفوا عن الحق بسببها، ولذلك عجزوا عن الوصول إلى طريق يهديهم إليه.

translation: And they say, “When we have become bones and disintegrated remains, will we truly be raised as a new creation?”
interpretation: This expresses the disbelievers’ rejection of resurrection: they consider the body’s decay proof that returning to life is impossible, overlooking that the One who created them originally is fully capable of recreating them after death.

translation: Say, “Become stones or iron,”
interpretation: Even if you imagine yourselves transformed into something as hard and lifeless as stone or iron, you cannot escape Allah’s power to resurrect you.

translation: “Or [be] a creation that is even greater in your hearts.” They will then say, “Who will bring us back?” Say, “The One who created you the first time.” Then they will shake their heads at you and say, “When will it be?” Say, “Perhaps it is near.”
interpretation: The verse answers those who regard resurrection as impossible: no matter how extraordinary or immense they imagine their transformation to be, the One who originated them from nothing has full power to restore them. Their shaking of their heads reflects mockery and denial, while the command to say that it may be near warns that the promised resurrection and reckoning could arrive sooner than they expect.

translation: On the Day He will call you, and you will respond with praise of Him, and you will think that you remained only a little while.
interpretation: When God summons people for resurrection, they will answer His call and acknowledge His perfection, while the long span of worldly life will seem insignificant—like only a brief moment—compared with the eternal reality now before them.

translation: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن ۚ إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم ۚ إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا
interpretation: أمر الله نبيَّه أن يوجّه عباده إلى اختيار أطيب الكلام وأرفقه، لأن الكلمة الجارحة أو الأسلوب السيئ قد يستغله الشيطان لإثارة العداوة والخصومة بينهم؛ فالشيطان عدوّ ظاهر للإنسان، ومن دفع نزغِه التزم الحكمة واللين وحسن الخطاب.

translation: Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He may have mercy on you, and if He wills, He may punish you. We have not sent you, O Muhammad, as a guardian over them.
interpretation: Allah alone fully knows people’s inner states and deeds, so mercy and punishment belong to His perfect wisdom and judgment. The Messenger’s duty is to convey the truth, not to control people, compel their faith, or determine their ultimate fate.

translation: And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, We have favored some prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses complete knowledge of all creation and its true worth. The differing ranks He grants to His prophets reflect His wisdom and authority, not any human standard of status; David’s receiving the Psalms is one example of the special revelation and favor bestowed upon certain prophets.

translation: Say, “Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove harm from you or transfer it elsewhere.”
interpretation: This verse challenges the false objects of worship by declaring that none besides Allah possesses independent authority to relieve hardship or change a person’s condition. Therefore, supplication and reliance should be directed to Allah alone.

translation: Those whom they invoke are themselves seeking the means of access to their Lord—whichever of them is nearest—and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, your Lord’s punishment is something to be feared.
interpretation: The verse corrects the assumption that created beings invoked besides Allah possess independent power or deserve worship: even the righteous servants whom people call upon are themselves dependent on Allah, striving to draw nearer to Him through obedience, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment. Thus worship and ultimate reliance belong to Allah alone, and His punishment must never be treated lightly.

translation: ولا توجد قرية إلا سنُهلكها قبل يوم القيامة أو نعذّبها عذابًا شديدًا؛ كان ذلك مثبتًا في الكتاب.
interpretation: يبين الله أن مصير كل مجتمع واقع ضمن قضائه المحتوم؛ فقبل قيام الساعة لا بد أن ينال كل بلدٍ هلاكه أو عذابًا شديدًا وفق ما استحقه، وقد سُجّل ذلك في الكتاب تقديرًا محكمًا لا يتخلف.

translation: Nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the earlier peoples rejected them. We gave Thamūd the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her; and We send signs only as a warning.
interpretation: Allah explains that extraordinary signs are not withheld out of inability, but because those who demanded them had repeatedly denied them, exposing themselves to judgment. The she-camel given to Thamūd was an unmistakable proof, yet their transgression showed that a sign benefits only those willing to submit to the truth. Thus divine signs are warnings meant to awaken people before accountability and punishment.

translation: And when We said to you, “Indeed, your Lord encompasses all people.” We made the vision We showed you only as a trial for the people, as well as the accursed tree mentioned in the Qur’an. We warn them, but it only increases them in great rebelliousness.
interpretation: God’s knowledge, power, and control encompass all people, and the signs He gives— including the vision shown to the Prophet and the warning of the accursed tree of Hell—test whether people respond with faith and humility. Those who reject the warning do not become excused by it; rather, their persistent denial exposes and deepens their arrogance and rebellion.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they all prostrated except Iblīs. He said, “Should I prostrate before one whom You created from clay?”
interpretation: The verse portrays Iblīs’s defiance as rooted in arrogance: he judged Adam by his material origin rather than submitting to God’s command and honoring the rank God had granted him. It warns that pride can cause a person to reject divine guidance even when its truth is clear.

translation: He said, “Tell me—this one whom You have honored above me? If You grant me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely bring all his descendants under my sway, except for a few.”
interpretation: This is Satan’s defiant arrogance: he views Adam’s honor as unjustified and vows to exploit human weakness to mislead Adam’s descendants. His claim that only a few will escape highlights that steadfast faith and obedience protect a person from his influence.

translation: He said, “Go! Whoever among them follows you—surely Hell is the recompense for you all, an abundant recompense.”
interpretation: God allows Satan to pursue his misguidance, but declares that Satan and all who knowingly follow him will ultimately receive the full and fitting consequence of their rebellion: Hell.

translation: “And incite whoever among them you can with your voice, rally against them your cavalry and infantry, share with them in their wealth and children, and make them promises.” But Satan promises them nothing except delusion.
interpretation: This is a warning that Satan is permitted to tempt people through every means available—seductive calls, human agents, misuse of wealth, and corruption in family and offspring—but he possesses no power to compel them. His promises of success, pleasure, or security apart from obedience to God are ultimately deceptive, so people must resist him through faith, discernment, and righteous action.

translation: Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian and Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: Those who sincerely belong to God and rely upon Him are not subject to Satan’s compelling control; his influence is limited to temptation and invitation. God’s protection and care are sufficient for them, so they should place their trust in Him and resist Satan through obedience and faith.

translation: Your Lord is the One who propels the ships for you across the sea so that you may seek of His bounty. Surely, He has always been Merciful to you.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that their ability to travel by sea and pursue lawful provision is made possible by His power and care. The smooth movement of ships, despite the vastness and danger of the ocean, is a sign of His mercy and an invitation to rely on Him with gratitude while seeking His blessings.

translation: And when hardship touches you at sea, those you call upon disappear from you except Him. But when He saves you to land, you turn away; and the human being is ever ungrateful.
interpretation: When people face mortal danger and all created means fail them, the illusion of relying on other powers falls away and they instinctively turn to God alone. Yet after He rescues them, many abandon that sincere dependence and return to heedlessness, revealing humanity’s tendency to forget divine mercy and respond with ingratitude.

translation: Do you feel secure that He will not cause the land to swallow you on one side, or send against you a shower of stones, and then you will find no protector for yourselves?
interpretation: The verse warns people not to become complacent about divine power and protection: the One who saves them from danger can also expose them to sudden punishment, and no created being can shield them if they turn away from Him.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will return you to the sea once again and send against you a tempestuous wind, drowning you because of your disbelief? Then you would find no one to avenge you against Us.
interpretation: The verse warns people not to become complacent after being rescued from danger. The One who saves them possesses complete power to return them to the same peril and punish their ingratitude and denial, while no protector could hold Him accountable or secure them from His judgment.

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, provided them with good things, and favored them greatly over many of Our creations.
interpretation: God has granted human beings inherent dignity and distinctive blessings, enabling them to travel, benefit from wholesome provision, and exercise knowledge and responsibility. This honor is a gift and a trust: it calls people to recognize God’s generosity, preserve their dignity and the dignity of others, and use their abilities responsibly rather than with pride or injustice.

translation: On the Day We will call every people with their leader. So whoever is given their record in their right hand will read their record, and they will not be wronged even by the thread of a date stone.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, each community will be summoned in association with the guide, leader, or way it followed in the world, and every person will face a complete record of their deeds. Those who receive it in their right hand will read it with joy and certainty, because God’s judgment will be perfectly just: no good deed will be diminished and no person will suffer the slightest injustice.

translation: Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter, and even farther astray from the way.
interpretation: The verse refers to spiritual blindness: whoever refuses to recognize God’s signs and follow the truth in this life will enter the Hereafter deprived of guidance and insight, and will be even farther from the path of salvation.

translation: And indeed, they nearly tempted you away from what We have revealed to you, so that you might invent something else in Our name. And then they would surely have taken you as a close friend.
interpretation: The verse portrays the severity of the pressure placed upon the Prophet ﷺ to compromise or alter the revelation. It affirms that even the slightest deviation from what Allah revealed—were it possible—would have been treated by those people as a basis for intimate alliance, revealing that their desired friendship depended on religious concession rather than sincere acceptance of the truth.

translation: Had We not strengthened you, you would almost have inclined toward them a little.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that His steadfasting support protected him from yielding even slightly to the pressure of those who sought compromise; the verse emphasizes that his firmness in upholding revelation was granted by divine preservation.

translation: Then We would have made you taste a double punishment in this life and a double punishment in the Hereafter, and you would have found no one to help you against Us.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that compromising divine revelation, even under pressure, would bring an intensified punishment both in this world and in the Hereafter; no person or power could then protect the offender from Allah’s judgment.

translation: And they nearly drove you from the land in order to expel you from it; and then they would have remained there after you only a little while.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who sought to force the Messenger ﷺ from his homeland would not gain lasting security or authority through that wrongdoing. Their opposition could bring about his departure, but their own presence and power afterward would endure only briefly, in accordance with Allah’s decree and judgment.

translation: This was Our way with the messengers We sent before you, and you will find no alteration in Our way.
interpretation: God’s treatment of those who oppose and drive out His messengers follows a firm, unchanging pattern: falsehood may resist for a time, but it cannot escape the consequences God has decreed.

translation: Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of night, and the recitation at dawn. Indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.
interpretation: Maintain the prescribed prayers throughout their appointed times, beginning after the sun’s decline and continuing into the night, with special emphasis on the dawn prayer. The dawn recitation is “witnessed” because it is attended by the angels of the night and day, highlighting its spiritual significance and the importance of beginning the day in worship.

translation: And during part of the night, keep vigil with it as an additional prayer for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.
interpretation: Rise for voluntary prayer during the night, reciting the Qur’an with devotion beyond the obligatory prayers. This worship is a special means of drawing nearer to Allah, and Allah may honor the one who perseveres in it with the Praised Station—the مقام of intercession and distinction granted to the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And say, “My Lord, admit me by an entrance of truth and bring me out by an exit of truth, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.”
interpretation: This is a supplication for Allah to make every beginning and ending sincere, righteous, and blessed: to enter into circumstances through truth and obedience, and to leave them with integrity and divine approval. The request for “supporting authority” means asking Allah for decisive strength, proof, and assistance that enable one to uphold the truth and overcome opposition—not power pursued for personal pride, but strength placed in the service of what is right.

translation: And say, “Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.”
interpretation: يأمر الله نبيَّه بإعلان انتصار الحق بظهوره وقيام حجته، وأن الباطل مهما بدا قوياً فهو زائل بطبيعته، إذ لا يملك أساساً ثابتاً يدوم أمام نور الحق.

translation: ونُنَزِّل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين، ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارًا.
interpretation: يبين الله أن القرآن يعالج أمراض القلوب من الشك والجهل والضلال، ويمنح المؤمنين رحمةً وهدايةً وثباتًا. أما من يظلم نفسه بالإعراض عنه ورفض هدايته، فلا ينتفع به، بل يزداد بُعدًا عن الحق وخسرانًا بسبب إصراره على ظلمه.

translation: And when We bestow blessings upon the human being, he turns away and distances himself; but when misfortune touches him, he becomes despairing.
interpretation: Human beings often respond to ease with heedlessness, withdrawing from gratitude and remembrance of God, yet respond to hardship with hopelessness. The verse reproves both attitudes, teaching that prosperity should lead to humility and thankfulness, while adversity should be met with patience and trust in God’s mercy rather than despair.

translation: Say, “Each acts according to their own disposition and way; and your Lord knows best who is guided to the soundest path.”
interpretation: Human beings act in accordance with the inclinations, character, and principles that shape them, but outward actions alone do not escape God’s knowledge. He fully knows whose way is rightly guided, so people should examine the direction of their lives rather than judge guidance merely by appearances.

translation: They ask you about the soul. Say, “The soul is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the soul belongs to the realm of God’s command and that its true nature lies beyond the limits of human investigation. Whatever knowledge people possess is finite, so they should approach this mystery with humility and recognize that complete understanding belongs to God alone.

translation: And if We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you; then you would find no guardian for you against Us concerning it.
interpretation: The revelation is entirely a gift and trust from God, under His absolute control. No created being—including the Prophet—can preserve it or secure it against God’s will, which teaches complete dependence upon Him and humility before His authority.

translation: Except by a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His فضل upon you has always been great.
interpretation: Whatever knowledge or guidance reaches you is granted through your Lord’s mercy, not through human power alone; His continual favor sustains and elevates you beyond what you could attain by yourself.

translation: Say, “If humankind and the jinn were to unite to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce its like, even if they supported one another.”
interpretation: The verse declares the Qur’an’s unique divine nature: no combined effort of humans and jinn, however extensive their knowledge, skill, or cooperation, can reproduce its guidance, truth, eloquence, and profound effect. Their inability demonstrates that it is revelation from Allah, not the work of the Prophet or of human beings.

translation: We have certainly set forth for people in this Qur’an every kind of example, but most people refuse anything except disbelief.
interpretation: Allah has presented the truth through varied examples and explanations so that people may understand, yet most reject it out of stubbornness and respond with denial rather than faith and gratitude.

translation: And they said, “We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.”
interpretation: This expresses the rejection of those who imposed arbitrary demands on the Prophet as a condition for faith, revealing that their resistance was rooted not in a sincere search for truth but in stubbornness and a desire to control the signs they would accept.

translation: Or you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, through which you cause rivers to gush forth abundantly.
interpretation: This expresses the skeptics’ demand for an extraordinary worldly proof of prophethood: they would not be satisfied with the message itself, but wanted the Prophet to possess a magnificent garden whose rivers flowed visibly through it. The verse exposes their materialistic standard for truth and implies that divine guidance is not validated by displays of wealth or miraculous luxury demanded by people.

translation: “Or cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you claim, or bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the defiant demands of those who reject the Prophet’s message: they insist on extraordinary, visible signs—such as the sky collapsing or God and the angels appearing directly—as a pretext for disbelief. It exposes their demand as obstinacy, since faith is not founded on forcing miraculous spectacles according to human conditions.

translation: أو يكون لك بيتٌ من زخرف، أو ترقى في السماء، ولن نؤمن لرُقيِّك حتى تُنزِّل علينا كتابًا نقرؤه. قل: سبحان ربي، هل كنتُ إلا بشرًا رسولًا؟
interpretation: يبيّن الآية تعنّت المكذّبين؛ فلم يطلبوا الدليل طلبَ الباحث عن الحق، بل اشترطوا خوارق مادية متتابعة ليبرّروا رفضهم للرسالة. ويأمر الله نبيَّه أن يعلن تنزّه ربّه عن أن يُستجاب لمثل هذه المطالب، وأن وظيفته ليست أن يكون مَلَكًا أو يملك الآيات كيف يشاء، وإنما هو بشر اصطفاه الله رسولًا، يؤيّده بما شاء من البينات.

translation: Nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, “Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?”
interpretation: Their refusal to believe was rooted in rejecting the possibility that God would choose an ordinary human being to convey His revelation; this objection reflects arrogance and a failure to recognize that humanity does not prevent someone from being entrusted with divine guidance.

translation: Say: “Had there been angels walking about on earth, dwelling in security, We would have sent down to them from heaven an angel as a messenger.”
interpretation: Allah explains that messengers are sent in a form suited to the people addressed, so that they can understand, communicate with, and follow them. Since human beings inhabit the earth, the messenger sent to them is human rather than an angel; the demand for an angel therefore does not invalidate the truth of the message.

translation: Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants.”
interpretation: The Prophet is directed to entrust the dispute between himself and his deniers to Allah, whose complete knowledge and vision encompass their intentions, words, and deeds. Thus, Allah’s testimony is sufficient to establish the truth, regardless of whether people accept it.

translation: Whomever Allah guides is truly guided; and whomever He leaves astray, you will never find for them protectors besides Him. We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, fallen upon their faces—blind, mute, and deaf. Their abode will be Hell; whenever its flames subside, We will increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true guidance is granted by Allah and that those who knowingly turn away from it will find no protector or source of salvation apart from Him. Their resurrection in a state of blindness, muteness, and deafness reflects the spiritual condition they embraced in the world: they refused to see the truth, hear its call, or respond to it; and their punishment in Hell will continue without relief.

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, “When we have become bones and dust, will we truly be raised again as a new creation?”
interpretation: Their punishment is the consequence of rejecting God’s signs and denying resurrection. Their question expresses the mistaken belief that decay and dispersal make restoration impossible, whereas God’s power to create them initially also encompasses bringing them back to life anew.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is capable of creating the like of them? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt; yet the wrongdoers insist on nothing but disbelief.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny resurrection: the One who originated the immense heavens and earth is certainly able to recreate human beings. Their appointed end and resurrection are definite, but persistent wrongdoing causes them to reject this truth despite the clear evidence of Allah’s power.

translation: Say, “If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord’s mercy, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending; and mankind is ever miserly.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the human tendency to cling to blessings out of fear that giving will diminish them. Unlike Allah’s limitless mercy, people are limited, anxious, and often miserly; recognizing this weakness should lead them to trust Allah’s provision and become more generous toward others.

translation: We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel about when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, “Indeed, O Moses, I think you are bewitched.”
interpretation: Allah reminds that Moses was supported with nine unmistakable miracles, making the truth clear to Pharaoh and his people. Yet Pharaoh rejected them and tried to discredit Moses by claiming that he was bewitched, revealing his arrogance and refusal to submit despite evident proof.

translation: He said, “You certainly know that none has sent these signs down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, as enlightening proofs. And indeed, I think you, Pharaoh, are doomed to ruin.”
interpretation: Moses confronts Pharaoh by asserting that the miracles are not magic or deception but unmistakable signs from the Creator of the universe. He indicates that Pharaoh inwardly recognizes their truth, yet persists in denial and oppression; therefore, Moses warns that such arrogant rejection will lead to his destruction and loss.

translation: So he intended to drive them out of the land, but We drowned him and all those with him.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s attempt to eradicate Moses and his followers was ultimately turned against him: his tyranny ended in destruction, while God protected those he sought to expel.

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, “Dwell in the land; then, when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together as one assembled multitude.”
interpretation: Allah granted the Children of Israel a period of settlement in the land after Pharaoh’s destruction, but their worldly dwelling was not the end of the matter. When the appointed promise of the Hereafter arrives, He will gather them—and all people—together for judgment, leaving no one outside His reckoning.

translation: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل ۗ وما أرسلناك إلا مبشّرًا ونذيرًا
interpretation: أنزل الله القرآن مشتملًا على الحق ومؤيدًا به، فنزل محفوظًا من الباطل والتحريف، وأرسل النبي ﷺ ليبشّر من آمن وعمل صالحًا برحمة الله وثوابه، وينذر من أعرض وعصى بعقابه؛ فمهمته البلاغ الواضح، لا إكراه الناس على الإيمان.

translation: And it is a Qur’an We have revealed in portions, so that you may recite it to the people gradually and with deliberation; and We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine guidance was given in stages, allowing the Prophet to convey it thoughtfully and enabling people to understand, reflect upon, and live by its teachings over time.

translation: Say, “Believe in it or do not believe.” Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration.
interpretation: This is a warning that the Qur’an’s truth does not depend on people’s acceptance of it. Those granted sincere knowledge recognize its divine signs, and their recognition produces humility, worship, and submission before Allah.

translation: And they say, “Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord is sure to be fulfilled.”
interpretation: They acknowledge that God is exalted above all imperfection and affirm with certainty that His promise—especially His promise of truth and judgment—cannot fail to come to pass.

translation: And they fall upon their faces, weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: Those who recognize the truth of Allah’s revelation respond with sincere tears and prostration; their awareness of His greatness deepens their humility and submission to Him.

translation: Say, “Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Compassionate—whichever name you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. And do not recite your prayer too loudly, nor make it too quiet, but seek a way between the two.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s many names refer to one Lord, so calling upon Him by any of His beautiful names is valid. It also teaches balance and sincerity in prayer: worship should neither be performed with excessive loudness that causes disturbance or display, nor with such quietness that its recitation is lost, but with measured composure and attentiveness.

translation: And say, “Praise belongs to Allah, who has not taken a son, nor has He any partner in sovereignty, nor does He need a protector because of weakness. And glorify Him with immense glorification.”
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute perfection, authority, and independence: He is not dependent on offspring, shares His dominion with no one, and requires no guardian or ally to protect Him. Therefore, He deserves exclusive praise and exaltation, with the heart and tongue recognizing His incomparable greatness.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant and placed no crookedness in it.
interpretation: Allah is praised for revealing the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a perfectly straight and sound guidance, free from contradiction, distortion, or deviation, so that it may lead people toward truth and righteousness.

translation: An upright Book, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have an excellent reward.
interpretation: The Qur’an is perfectly straight and free from contradiction; it warns those who reject God’s guidance of grave consequences, while assuring believers whose faith is expressed through righteous action of a lasting and beautiful reward from Him.

translation: Remaining therein forever.
interpretation: It signifies an everlasting dwelling in that place, with no departure or end.

translation: ويُنذِرَ الذين قالوا: اتخذَ اللهُ ولدًا.
interpretation: في الآية تحذيرٌ شديد من نسبة الولد إلى الله تعالى؛ لأن ذلك ينافي كمال توحيده وتنزّهه عن صفات المخلوقين، ويترتب عليه استحقاق الوعيد ما لم يُرجع القائل عنه إلى الحق.

translation: They have no knowledge of this, nor did their forefathers. Grave is the word that comes from their mouths; they say nothing but lies.
interpretation: Those who attribute a child or offspring to Allah make a claim without any knowledge or proof, merely repeating the error of earlier generations. Such a statement is profoundly false and grievous, because it assigns to Allah what is incompatible with His absolute uniqueness and perfection.

translation: Perhaps you would consume yourself with grief in their wake if they do not believe in this message.
interpretation: This is a compassionate consolation to the Prophet: his duty is to convey the truth faithfully, not to destroy himself with sorrow when people reject it, for guidance cannot be forced upon them.

translation: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينةً لها لنختبرهم أيُّهم أحسن عملاً.
interpretation: جعل الله ما في الأرض من متاعٍ وجمالٍ وسيلةً للابتلاء، ليظهر من يتعامل معه بطاعةٍ وشكرٍ واستقامة، لا من ينشغل به عن الله؛ فالمعيار هو إحسان العمل، لا كثرة ما يملكه الإنسان أو تمتّعه بزينة الدنيا.

translation: And indeed, We will turn all that is upon it into barren dust.
interpretation: Everything on the earth—its beauty, wealth, and adornments—is temporary, and Allah can reduce it all to a lifeless, barren land; therefore, worldly splendor should not be treated as permanent.

translation: أم حسبتَ أن أصحابَ الكهفِ والرَّقيمِ كانوا من آياتِنا عجبًا؟
interpretation: المعنى: لا تظنّن أن قصة أصحاب الكهف هي أعجب آيات الله وأعظمها؛ فهي، مع ما فيها من خرقٍ للعادة، دليلٌ من دلائل قدرته التي لا يحدّها شيء، وليست أمرًا يعجزه أو يستنفد عجائب صنعه.

translation: When the young men took refuge in the cave, they said, “Our Lord, grant us mercy from You and guide our affair to what is right.”
interpretation: This supplication portrays the believers’ turning to Allah when they could no longer safely uphold their faith among their people. By asking for mercy and right guidance, they acknowledge that protection, steadfastness, and a sound outcome come only from Him, and they entrust their uncertain situation entirely to His wisdom.

translation: So We cast a veil over their ears in the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: Allah caused the companions of the cave to fall into a deep sleep, preventing them from hearing and awakening, while preserving them there for the appointed period.

translation: Then We awakened them so that We might make clear which of the two groups had more accurately calculated the length of time they had remained.
interpretation: Their awakening was part of God’s unfolding of the sign of the Companions of the Cave: the differing estimates of their stay would expose the limits of human knowledge and demonstrate that God alone fully encompasses the unseen and the exact measure of time.

translation: We relate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere faith, when embraced with courage and steadfastness—especially by the young—becomes a cause for greater guidance from God. Their initial belief was met with divine support, strengthening their insight, resolve, and commitment to the truth.

translation: And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any deity besides Him; if we did, we would surely have uttered an outrageous falsehood.”
interpretation: Allah granted the young believers courage and steadfastness to declare pure monotheism openly. Their confession affirms that sovereignty belongs solely to the Lord of all creation, while associating any partner with Him is a grave deviation from truth.

translation: These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring clear proof for them? So who is more wrong than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?
interpretation: The verse condemns associating partners with Allah without any valid evidence, affirming that worship must be founded on clear truth rather than conjecture, tradition, or invented claims. It declares that attributing such false beliefs to Allah is among the greatest forms of injustice.

translation: And when you have withdrawn from them and from what they worship besides Allah, then take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread His mercy over you and prepare for you a means of ease in your affair.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when preserving faith requires distancing oneself from false beliefs and those who insist upon them, seeking refuge in Allah is the proper course. Whoever sacrifices worldly security for sincere devotion can trust that Allah will surround them with mercy and provide relief and a way forward beyond what they can see.

translation: And you would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave toward the right, and when it set, passing away from them toward the left, while they lay in an open space within it. That was one of Allah’s signs. Whoever Allah guides is truly guided; and whoever He lets go astray, you will never find for him a protecting guide.
interpretation: The arrangement of the cave protected the Companions from the sun’s harmful exposure while they remained in a spacious part of it, demonstrating Allah’s providential care over them. Their physical preservation points to a greater truth: true guidance and protection ultimately come only from Allah, and without His guidance no one can find a path leading to what is right.

translation: You would have thought them awake, though they were asleep. We turned them from side to side, and their dog lay with its forelegs stretched out at the entrance. Had you looked upon them, you would have turned away from them in flight and been filled with terror.
interpretation: The verse portrays the People of the Cave as being preserved by Allah in a state that concealed them from ordinary human intrusion. Their apparent wakefulness, continual turning, and the guarding presence of the dog created an awe-inspiring sight, so that anyone who discovered them would instinctively flee. This demonstrates Allah’s complete protection of them and the extraordinary manner in which He safeguarded them while they remained in their prolonged sleep.

translation: And so We awakened them, that they might question one another. One of them said, “How long have you remained?” They replied, “We have remained for a day, or part of a day.” They said, “Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you to the city with this silver coin of yours; let him see which food is purest and bring you provisions from it. Let him be discreet, and let him not make anyone aware of you.”
interpretation: Their awakening reveals that God preserved them through an extraordinary passage of time while leaving them unaware of its length. Their uncertainty teaches that human perception is limited and that ultimate knowledge belongs to God. Their careful decision to send one person discreetly for wholesome food also shows their prudence: believers should seek what is pure, act wisely, and protect themselves from unnecessary danger when circumstances require concealment.

translation: Indeed, if they gain power over you, they will stone you or force you back into their religion, and then you will never succeed.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who are hostile to faith may resort to persecution and coercion, so believers must not surrender their convictions under pressure, for abandoning the truth in order to appease its opponents leads to ultimate loss.

translation: And thus We caused them to be discovered, so that people might know that Allah’s promise is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour. As they disputed among themselves about their affair, they said, “Build a structure over them; their Lord knows best about them.” Those who prevailed in the matter said, “We will surely build a mosque over them.”
interpretation: Allah made the People of the Cave known to their society as a sign confirming the truth of resurrection and the certainty of the Day of Judgment. The verse also portrays how people differed in responding to the sign: some stopped at acknowledging their ignorance, while those who held authority proposed commemorating the site with a mosque, revealing how communities may turn a divine sign into a matter of public dispute and religious practice.

translation: سيقولون: «ثلاثة، رابعهم كلبهم»، ويقولون: «خمسة، سادسهم كلبهم»، ظنًّا وتخمينًا في الغيب، ويقولون: «سبعة، وثامنهم كلبهم». قل: «ربي أعلم بعدّتهم، وما يعلمهم إلا قليل». فلا تجادل في شأنهم إلا جدالًا ظاهرًا موجزًا، ولا تستفتِ فيهم أحدًا منهم.
interpretation: يعلّم الله نبيَّه أن يتعامل مع الأخبار التي لا يترتب عليها عمل ولا دليل قاطع فيها بالتواضع والتوقف عند حدود العلم، وألا ينشغل بالجدال والتخمين أو يطلب تصديقًا ممن لا يملك علمًا موثوقًا؛ فالعبرة من قصتهم ليست في تحديد عددهم، بل في ردّ العلم إلى الله وترك المراء فيما لا ينفع.

translation: And never say of anything, “Indeed, I will do that tomorrow.”
interpretation: This teaches that a person should not speak with absolute certainty about future actions, because the future and one’s ability to act remain subject to Allah’s will; plans should therefore be expressed with humility and reliance upon Him.

translation: Unless Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget, and say, “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a person should not speak with certainty about future actions apart from Allah’s will. If he forgets to acknowledge this, he should remember Allah as soon as he recalls, and ask Him to guide him toward what is more correct and beneficial, recognizing that true guidance comes from Him.

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and added nine.
interpretation: This states the exact duration of the Companions of the Cave’s stay: three hundred solar years, corresponding to three hundred and nine lunar years, thereby affirming Allah’s precise knowledge and power over time and resurrection.

translation: Say: “Allah knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How perfectly He sees and hears! They have no protector besides Him, and He does not share His judgment with anyone.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that the complete knowledge of hidden realities, including the true duration of the sleepers’ stay, belongs exclusively to Allah. His sight and hearing encompass everything without limitation, so ultimate protection, authority, and judgment are His alone; no created being can share in His rule or independently determine what is true.

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. None can change His words, and you will never find any refuge apart from Him.
interpretation: This commands the Prophet—and, through him, believers—to remain faithful to the revelation, trusting that God’s words, promises, and judgments cannot be altered or overridden. Since no created power can replace or protect a person from God, true refuge is found only in turning to Him.

translation: And keep yourself patiently with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Do not let your eyes turn away from them, desiring the adornment of the life of this world. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his own desire and whose affair is excess.
interpretation: Remain devoted to sincere believers whose worship is directed solely toward Allah, regardless of their poverty or lack of worldly status. Do not abandon their company in pursuit of worldly prestige, nor allow the demands of influential people to draw you away from them. The verse also warns against following those who neglect remembrance of Allah and let desire govern their lives, for such heedlessness causes a person to lose balance and squander his ultimate purpose.

translation: وقل: الحق من ربكم، فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر. إنا أعددنا للظالمين نارًا أحاط بهم سُرادقها، وإن يستغيثوا يُغاثوا بماء كالمُهل يشوي الوجوه. بئس الشراب وساءت مُرتفقًا.
interpretation: يقرر الله أن الحق ثابت صادر من عنده، وأن للإنسان أن يختار الإيمان أو الكفر، لكن هذا الاختيار لا يلغي المسؤولية ولا يساوي بين الطريقين؛ فمن اختار الظلم والكفر فقد عرّض نفسه لعذاب محيط لا يجد فيه إلا إغاثة تزيده ألمًا، وفي ذلك تهديد شديد وتحذير من الإعراض عن الحق.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—surely We will not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that sincere faith joined with righteous action is never overlooked by God; He preserves and fully rewards every act done with excellence and sincerity, even when its value is unseen by people.

translation: Those are the ones for whom are the Gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein upon couches. Excellent is the reward, and beautiful is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse portrays the lasting honor and complete comfort prepared for the believers: an eternal dwelling filled with flowing life, beauty, noble adornment, luxurious clothing, and peaceful repose. Its description teaches that the reward of faith is not merely survival after death, but a dignified and serene existence in which every form of distress is replaced by security, beauty, and contentment.

translation: And set forth for them the example of two men: We granted one of them two gardens of grapevines, surrounded them with palm trees, and placed cultivated fields between them.
interpretation: This example portrays worldly prosperity as a divine gift, not a sign of personal superiority or permanent security. The gardens’ abundance—grapes, palms, and crops—shows how blessings may be arranged in perfect harmony, while the mention of two men prepares a contrast between one who recognizes that dependence and one who may be deceived by his wealth.

translation: كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ أَتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِمْ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا ۚ وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا
interpretation: أي إن كلتا الجنتين أخرجت ثمرها كاملًا ووفيرًا دون نقص، وأجرى الله بينهما نهرًا يمدّهما بالحياة والري؛ وفي ذلك بيان أن تمام النعمة ودوام أسبابها إنما هو بقدرة الله وتقديره.

translation: He had abundant produce, so he said to his companion while conversing with him, “I have more wealth than you and greater support.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how material abundance can lead a person to arrogance and contempt for others, causing him to measure his worth by wealth and social standing rather than by gratitude and righteousness.

translation: And he entered his garden, wronging himself, and said, “I do not think that this will ever perish.”
interpretation: His wealth and prosperity led him to arrogance and heedlessness, so he trusted in the permanence of his worldly possessions and forgot that all created things are temporary and subject to Allah’s will.

translation: I do not think that the Hour will ever come; and if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find something better than this as a place of return.
interpretation: The speaker’s denial of resurrection and his confidence that he would receive something even better in the Hereafter reveal his arrogance and delusion: he treats worldly prosperity as proof of divine favor, though wealth in this life does not guarantee salvation or reward with God.

translation: His companion said to him, while conversing with him, “Have you disbelieved in Him who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, and then fashioned you into a man?”
interpretation: The believing companion rebukes the man for denying God despite the clear evidence of his own origin: God brought him from humble beginnings into a fully formed human being. This should lead to recognition of God’s power and gratitude, not arrogance or disbelief.

translation: But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: The believer affirms that Allah alone is his Lord and rejects every form of associating partners with Him, attributing all ultimate authority, dependence, and worship exclusively to Allah.

translation: Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, “What Allah has willed; there is no power except through Allah”? Though you see me as having less wealth and children than you.
interpretation: The verse teaches that when a person sees prosperity in himself or others, he should acknowledge that it exists only by Allah’s will and power. This recognition protects the heart from pride and from despising those who possess less of the temporary blessings of worldly life.

translation: “Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and send upon it a calamity from heaven, so that it becomes barren, slippery ground.”
interpretation: This expresses the believer’s recognition that worldly prosperity is entirely subject to God’s will: He can replace apparent abundance with something better for the faithful, while allowing arrogance and ingratitude to be stripped of the blessings they take for granted.

translation: Or its water may sink deep into the earth, and you will never be able to recover it.
interpretation: This is a warning that every worldly blessing depends entirely on Allah’s preservation; if He withdraws it, human power and effort cannot restore it.

translation: And his fruits were utterly destroyed, so he began wringing his hands over all that he had spent on it, while it lay fallen upon its trellises, and he said, “Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret of a person whose worldly wealth is suddenly ruined after he had relied on it with arrogance and denied God’s power. His remorse comes only after loss, revealing that associating partners with Allah and placing ultimate trust in worldly possessions leads to ruin and belated regret.

translation: And he had no group to help him besides Allah, nor was he able to defend himself.
interpretation: When Allah’s judgment came upon him, the worldly power and wealth he relied upon could neither protect him nor rescue him; no created force can prevail against Allah’s decree.

translation: There, all authority belongs to Allah, the True. He is best in reward and best in outcome.
interpretation: When worldly power and means fail, it becomes clear that true protection, judgment, and authority belong solely to Allah. Whoever relies on Him receives the finest reward, and his final end is better than any outcome secured by worldly wealth or status.

translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world: it is like water We send down from the sky, which mingles with the plants of the earth, then they become dry fragments scattered by the winds. And Allah is fully capable of all things.
interpretation: Worldly life may appear flourishing and attractive for a time, like vegetation nourished by rain, but its beauty and strength soon fade and disperse. This likeness calls people not to be deceived by temporary worldly prosperity, while affirming that Allah has complete power to bring about change, decay, and renewal.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world, but the enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope.
interpretation: Worldly possessions and family may beautify a person’s life, but their value is temporary. What truly endures and brings lasting benefit before God is sincere, righteous action; therefore, a believer should not let worldly adornments become more important than deeds that earn God’s lasting reward and inspire hope in His mercy.

translation: ويوم نُسيِّر الجبالَ وترى الأرضَ بارزةً، وحشرناهم فلم نُغادر منهم أحدًا.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية مشهد القيامة حين تزول معالم الدنيا، وتنكشف الأرض بلا ساتر، ويُجمع جميع الخلق للحساب دون أن يُستثنى منهم أحد؛ وفي ذلك تأكيد على شمول البعث ودقة الجزاء الإلهي.

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: “You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time.” Rather, you claimed that We would never appoint a time for you.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, all people will stand openly and orderly before God, stripped of the worldly excuses and distinctions they relied upon. Their return in the same created state exposes the certainty of resurrection and rebukes their former denial that God had appointed a time to hold them accountable.

translation: And the record will be set down, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it. They will say, “Woe to us! What is this record that leaves nothing, small or great, without recording it?” They will find all that they did present before them; and your Lord wrongs no one.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Day of Judgment, when every person’s deeds will be disclosed with complete precision. The wrongdoers’ fear arises from realizing that even actions they considered insignificant have been preserved, while Allah’s perfect justice ensures that no one is punished beyond what they truly earned and no deed is overlooked.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he rebelled against the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, even though they are your enemies? How evil a substitute the wrongdoers have chosen!
interpretation: The verse warns that allegiance to Satan and his descendants is a deliberate exchange of the protection and guidance of God for the companionship of an enemy.
