Iblis’s refusal reveals that rebellion against God begins with pride, while following him makes a person abandon the true source of loyalty and security.

translation: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor even their own creation; nor would I take those who mislead as helpers.
interpretation: Allah rejects the authority of Satan and his followers: they neither participated in nor witnessed the origins of creation, so they possess no knowledge that qualifies them to be followed. Their being taken as allies or advisers is therefore baseless, for Allah does not rely on those who lead others astray.

translation: And on the Day He will say, “Call upon My partners whom you claimed.” So they will call upon them, but they will not answer them; and We will place between them a gulf of destruction.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who attributed partners to Allah will be exposed in their helplessness: the beings they worshipped will neither hear nor rescue them. Allah will separate the worshippers from their false objects of devotion by a deadly barrier, signifying their complete disavowal and the ruin brought about by associating partners with Him.

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and realize that they are about to fall into it, and they will find no way to turn away from it.
interpretation: When the guilty finally behold Hell, their denial will vanish and they will become certain that it is their unavoidable destination. They will have no escape, protection, or means of diverting its punishment.

translation: Indeed, We have presented in this Qur’an for people every kind of example, but humankind is the most argumentative of all beings.
interpretation: Allah has explained guidance through varied examples so that people may understand and take heed, yet human beings often respond with excessive disputation, resisting the truth rather than humbly accepting and acting upon it.

translation: Nothing prevented people from believing when guidance came to them and from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness except that they awaited the fate of earlier peoples or that the punishment would come upon them directly.
interpretation: The verse censures those who reject faith despite clear guidance, showing that their refusal is not due to a lack of evidence but to their insistence on postponing repentance until they witness the destructive consequences that befell earlier nations or encounter punishment themselves. It therefore calls people to believe and seek forgiveness before such irreversible signs arrive.

translation: We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. Yet those who disbelieve argue with falsehood in order to refute the truth by it, and they take My signs and the warnings they have received as a mockery.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the messengers’ role is to offer hope to those who respond to God and to warn those who reject Him. It condemns the attitude of unbelievers who use deceptive arguments—not to seek truth, but to undermine it—and who treat divine revelations and warnings with ridicule, revealing their deliberate refusal to take God’s guidance seriously.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, yet turns away from them and forgets what his hands have sent forth? Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts so that they do not understand it, and deafness in their ears. And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.
interpretation: The verse portrays the deepest injustice as knowingly rejecting divine reminders while neglecting accountability for one’s deeds. The coverings over the heart and deafness of the ears signify a state of spiritual hardening brought about by persistent refusal: the person is no longer receptive to truth, so even an invitation to guidance fails to benefit him. This is not an arbitrary deprivation, but the consequence and divine confirmation of his deliberate turning away.

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to take them to account for what they have earned, He would hasten the punishment for them. Rather, they have an appointed time from which they will find no refuge.
interpretation: Allah’s delay in punishing wrongdoing is an expression of His mercy and forbearance, not approval of sin or abandonment of justice. He grants people time to repent and reform, but when the appointed reckoning arrives, no escape or refuge will remain for those who persisted in wrongdoing.

translation: And those towns—We destroyed them when they committed ظلم, and We appointed a time for their destruction.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the destruction of unjust peoples occurs because of their wrongdoing and by a time decreed by God; punishment is neither arbitrary nor outside His determined wisdom.

translation: And when Moses said to his young companion, “I will not stop until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I must travel for ages.”
interpretation: This expresses Moses’s determination to pursue knowledge and fulfill his purpose, showing that a sincere seeker remains patient and persistent despite the length or difficulty of the journey.

translation: Then, when they reached the meeting point between the two seas, they forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea, slipping away.
interpretation: The fish’s escape was the sign Allah had appointed to guide Moses and his companion to the place where Moses would encounter the righteous servant. Their forgetting it was not meaningless negligence, but part of the divinely directed course of events.

translation: Then, when they had gone beyond it, he said to his young companion, “Bring us our meal; surely we have been exhausted by this journey of ours.”
interpretation: This shows that even a determined seeker of knowledge experiences human weakness and fatigue; acknowledging one’s need for rest and nourishment is not a failure, but part of continuing a demanding journey with awareness and humility.

translation: He said, “Did you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan. And it took its way into the sea in a wondrous manner.”
interpretation: The young companion explains that the fish—whose escape was the appointed sign—had slipped into the sea at the rock, but Satan caused him to forget to report it. Its extraordinary departure was a clear indication that they had reached the place where Moses was to meet the servant granted special knowledge by God.

translation: He said, “That is what we were seeking.” So they turned back, retracing their steps.
interpretation: Moses recognized that the place where the fish had disappeared was the sign they had been searching for, so he and his companion returned along their path to find it.

translation: Then they found a servant from among Our servants, to whom We had granted mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence.
interpretation: This describes a chosen servant honored by Allah with two gifts: special mercy that guides and protects him, and divinely granted knowledge beyond what ordinary human learning can attain. It teaches that true spiritual insight is a gift from Allah and that human understanding remains limited before His wisdom.

translation: Moses said to him, “May I follow you so that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?”
interpretation: This verse teaches that a sincere seeker of knowledge approaches the knowledgeable with humility and respect, openly acknowledging their expertise and seeking guidance with the aim of attaining what is right and beneficial.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you will never be able to remain patient with me.”
interpretation: Al-Khidr warns Moses that he will struggle to remain patient because he does not yet understand the hidden wisdom behind what Al-Khidr does; true patience here requires trusting divine wisdom beyond one’s immediate perception.

translation: And how can you be patient with what you have not fully understood?
interpretation: True patience is difficult when the wisdom behind events remains hidden; this verse teaches that limited human understanding can make a person hasten to judge what may contain a wisdom he has not yet grasped.

translation: He said, “You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey any command of yours.”
interpretation: This is a pledge of humility and sincere commitment to learning: the speaker entrusts his ability to remain patient to Allah’s will and promises to follow his teacher’s guidance faithfully.

translation: He said, “If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention its explanation to you.”
interpretation: Al-Khidr instructs Moses to remain patient and refrain from questioning what he witnesses until the proper time for its hidden wisdom to be revealed; this teaches that seeking understanding requires disciplined patience when one does not yet possess the full context.

translation: So they proceeded until, when they boarded a ship, he damaged it. He said, “Have you damaged it so as to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave and astonishing thing.”
interpretation: Moses objected because the act appeared to endanger innocent people, revealing that outward appearances may conceal a deeper wisdom known only to God and those whom He grants special knowledge. The verse also highlights the seriousness of judging an action before understanding its full circumstances.

translation: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to remain patient with me?”
interpretation: This is a gentle but firm reminder that the difficulty of understanding events whose wisdom is hidden can exceed a person’s patience; true understanding requires humility, restraint, and trust in what has not yet been explained.

translation: He said, “Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with hardship in my affair.”
interpretation: Moses asked al-Khidr to excuse his forgetfulness and not make his companionship difficult for him, acknowledging his mistake with humility and seeking leniency.

translation: So they went on until they met a boy, and he killed him. Moses said, “Have you killed an innocent soul without its having killed anyone? You have certainly done a dreadful thing.”
interpretation: Moses condemned the killing because it appeared to be the taking of an innocent life without legal cause. The verse highlights the limits of human judgment: an act may seem utterly wrong when viewed only from its outward appearance, while its deeper wisdom is known only through God’s revelation and decree.

translation: He said, “Did I not tell you that you would never be able to remain patient with me?”
interpretation: Moses’ second objection confirms that his companion’s warning was justified: without understanding the hidden wisdom behind these events, Moses would find it difficult to endure them patiently.

translation: He said, “If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as your companion. You have received from me a sufficient excuse.”
interpretation: Moses acknowledged that his repeated questioning had reached the limit he had set with al-Khidr. He therefore accepted that, if he questioned again, their companionship would justly come to an end, while recognizing that al-Khidr had already given him a valid reason for parting.

translation: So they set out, until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. Then they found there a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright. He said, “If you wished, you could have taken payment for it.”
interpretation: After being denied hospitality, Moses questioned why the wall was repaired without compensation. This reveals the contrast between ordinary human expectations of fairness and the deeper wisdom guiding the righteous servant’s actions: he was preserving something beneficial for the town’s vulnerable people, even though its inhabitants had shown no kindness and no immediate reward was received. The verse teaches that a good deed may be done for a higher purpose, not merely in response to gratitude or material gain, while also showing Moses’ natural concern for practical justice and appropriate recompense.

translation: He said, “This is the parting between me and you. I will now inform you of the meaning of that over which you could not remain patient.”
interpretation: Al-Khidr declares that their companionship has reached its end because Moses could not yet endure witnessing actions whose wisdom was hidden from him. Before they separate, he promises to explain the divine wisdom behind those events, teaching that limited human knowledge cannot always grasp the purposes of God’s decree immediately.

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked at sea. So I intended to damage it, for behind them was a king who seized every sound ship by force.
interpretation: The apparent harm done to the ship was in fact a means of protecting its owners from a greater loss: by making it defective, it would be overlooked by the tyrannical king, allowing the poor sailors to keep their livelihood. This teaches that an event which appears harmful may conceal divine mercy and protection from a greater evil.

translation: “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overwhelm them with rebellion and disbelief.”
interpretation: بيّن الخَضِر أن قتل الغلام كان بأمرٍ من الله وبعلمه بحاله ومآله، إذ كان سيصبح سببًا لفتنة أبويه المؤمنين وإضلالهما بشدة التعلّق به؛ فكان في إبدالهما خيرًا منه رحمةٌ وحفظٌ لدينهما، وليس في الآية تبريرٌ لأحد أن يتصرف في الأرواح بغير وحيٍ أو حقٍّ شرعي.

translation: So we intended that their Lord replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in affection.
interpretation: The child who was taken away would have caused his believing parents distress and hardship, so Allah decreed that they receive another child who would be more righteous, pure in character, and more loving and beneficial to them.

translation: “As for the wall, it belonged to two orphaned boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been righteous, so your Lord intended that they reach maturity and then retrieve their treasure—as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do any of this on my own. That is the explanation of what you could not bear patiently.”
interpretation: The events that seemed unjust or incomprehensible were governed by divine wisdom: the wall was preserved to protect the orphans’ inheritance until they became capable of recovering it, and their father’s righteousness was a cause of mercy extended to them. This teaches that Allah may arrange hidden protection and delayed benefit in ways people cannot perceive, and that the apparent actions of the servant were ultimately carried out only by Allah’s command.

translation: And they ask you about Dhū al-Qarnayn. Say, “I will recite to you an account of him.”
interpretation: God instructs the Prophet to present Dhū al-Qarnayn’s story as a meaningful account from which people may learn, rather than as mere curiosity about his identity. The wording directs attention to the lessons revealed through his conduct, power, and responsibility, while affirming that the Prophet conveys only what God has made known.

translation: Indeed, We established him firmly in the land and granted him the means to accomplish everything.
interpretation: Allah granted Dhul-Qarnayn authority, stability, and the resources needed to pursue his purposes, showing that power and success come through means provided by God.

translation: So he followed a means.
interpretation: He pursued the route or practical means Allah had made available to him, demonstrating that achieving a purpose requires deliberate effort and taking the proper steps.

translation: Until, when he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and he found a people near it. We said, “O Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them with kindness.”
interpretation: The verse depicts Dhul-Qarnayn reaching the western limit of his journey, where the sun appeared to set into a murky spring from his vantage point, and encountering a community there. God then entrusted him with authority to choose between punishing wrongdoing and dealing mercifully, indicating that just leadership requires both accountability and benevolent treatment.

translation: He said, “As for whoever does wrong, we shall punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.”
interpretation: Dhul-Qarnayn declares that wrongdoing warrants immediate worldly justice under his authority, but ultimate judgment belongs to Allah: the wrongdoer will return to Him and face a severe and detestable punishment for his deeds.

translation: As for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, he will have the best reward, and We will speak to him of Our command with ease.
interpretation: Whoever combines sincere faith with righteous action will receive a generous reward from God, and will be treated with gentleness, mercy, and words that are easy and considerate rather than hardship or severity.

translation: Then he followed a course.
interpretation: After being granted power and the means to act, Dhul-Qarnayn proceeded along the route Allah had made accessible to him, seeking to fulfill his mission with purposeful action.

translation: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قومٍ لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترًا
interpretation: بلغ ذو القرنين أقصى جهة المشرق، فوجد قومًا يعيشون في أرض مكشوفة لا يقيهم فيها شيء من الشمس، فكان ذلك وصفًا لحالهم من شدة التعرّض لحرارتها وانعدام المأوى أو الحاجز الذي يسترهم عنها.

translation: Thus it was; and We had full knowledge of all that he possessed.
interpretation: Allah’s statement emphasizes His complete awareness of the circumstances, actions, and possessions of Dhū al-Qarnayn; nothing connected with his rule or journey was hidden from Him.

translation: Then he followed a means.
interpretation: He proceeded along the path and means Allah had granted him, using them to pursue his purpose and fulfill his mission.

translation: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوماً لا يكادون يفقهون قولاً
interpretation: فلما وصل ذو القرنين إلى موضعٍ بين حاجزين عظيمين، وجد وراءهما قوماً ضعاف الفهم أو مختلفي اللغة، حتى كاد يعسر عليهم فهم كلام الآخرين والتفاهم معهم.

translation: They said, “O Dhū al-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are spreading corruption throughout the land. So may we offer you a payment in return for building a barrier between us and them?”
interpretation: The people sought protection from a powerful source of disorder and offered material compensation, while Dhū al-Qarnayn’s response in the following passage demonstrates that righteous leadership is based not on exploiting people’s fear for profit, but on using strength and resources to secure justice and protection.

translation: He said, “What my Lord has granted me is better, so assist me with strength; I will make between you and them a barrier.”
interpretation: Dhul-Qarnayn declines their offer of payment, seeing the authority and means Allah has granted him as sufficient. He asks instead for their practical cooperation and labor to build a strong barrier protecting them from the corruption and attacks of Gog and Magog, showing that righteous power is used for public protection rather than personal gain.

translation: “Bring me blocks of iron.” Then, when he had filled the gap between the two mountain sides, he said, “Blow”—until he had made it glow like fire. He said, “Bring me molten copper so that I may pour it over the iron.”
interpretation: This describes Dhū al-Qarnayn’s construction of a formidable barrier: he used iron to fill the passage between the mountains, heated it intensely through controlled blowing, and strengthened and sealed it by pouring molten copper over it. The verse highlights his reliance on practical skill, organized labor, and material means while carrying out justice and protecting the vulnerable.

translation: So they were unable to climb over it, nor were they able to penetrate it.
interpretation: The barrier was constructed with such strength and precision that the hostile peoples could neither surmount it from above nor break through it from within, demonstrating that human power is limited before what Allah enables to be established.

translation: قال: «هذا رحمةٌ من ربي، فإذا جاء وعدُ ربي جعله دكّاء، وكان وعدُ ربي حقًّا».
interpretation: يبيّن ذو القرنين أن ما مكّنه الله منه من إقامة السدّ رحمةٌ إلهية، لكنه ليس باقياً إلى الأبد؛ فعندما يحين وعد الله المعلوم لزواله، يهدمه ويجعله مستوياً بالأرض، لأن وعد الله واقع لا محالة ولا يتخلّف.

translation: And on that Day We will leave some of them surging over others; then the Trumpet will be blown, and We will gather them all together.
interpretation: This portrays the upheaval of the Last Day: people will be overwhelmed and intermixed in confusion, then the blowing of the Trumpet will bring every one of them before God for judgment, with none left beyond His summons.

translation: And We will display Hell on that Day openly before the disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who rejected faith will be made to confront Hell plainly and unmistakably, with no veil or escape from recognizing the consequence of their denial.

translation: Those whose eyes were veiled from My reminder and who were unable to hear.
interpretation: This describes people whose hearts are so closed to God’s guidance that they cannot perceive His signs or benefit from His reminder; their inability to hear is a spiritual refusal to accept and respond to the truth, not merely a physical impairment.

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: الآية تنكر على الكافرين ظنَّهم أن اتخاذهم عبادَ الله أولياء من دونه يمنحهم نفعًا أو حماية؛ فالمخلوق لا يملك شيئًا أمام الله ولا يستحق العبادة، ومن جعلهم وسائطَ استقلالٍ أو صرف لهم شيئًا من العبادة فقد اختار طريق الكفر، وكانت عاقبته جهنم التي أُعدّت له إعدادَ المنزل لنزيله، على سبيل التهديد والإهانة.

translation: Say, “Shall We inform you of those who are the greatest losers in their deeds?”
interpretation: This is a warning that the greatest loss is not merely failing to achieve worldly aims, but exhausting one’s efforts in actions that are misguided or devoid of sincere faith while believing they are doing good.

translation: Those whose efforts are lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good.
interpretation: This describes people whose actions appear purposeful to them but are rendered worthless because they are founded on false belief, misguided intentions, or disobedience to God; their sincere confidence does not turn error into righteousness.

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have come to nothing; therefore, We will assign them no weight on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This warns that deeds are not accepted merely because they appear abundant or good; rejecting God’s signs and denying accountability before Him deprives them of the faith and sincerity that give deeds lasting value, leaving them without any standing or worth before Him on the Day of Judgment.

translation: That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery.
interpretation: Their punishment is Hell because their disbelief was joined with deliberate contempt for God’s revelations and ridicule of His messengers, reflecting a willful rejection rather than mere ignorance.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of al-Firdaws as their lodging.
interpretation: Allah promises sincere believers who embody their faith through righteous deeds a permanent, honored dwelling in the highest and most excellent gardens of Paradise, where they will be welcomed and settled in comfort.

translation: Abiding therein forever, they will never wish to leave it.
interpretation: The righteous will remain permanently in Paradise, completely content with it and having no desire for any replacement or departure.

translation: Say, “If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely run out before the words of my Lord ran out, even if We brought another sea like it to replenish it.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that Allah’s knowledge, wisdom, decrees, and signs are limitless. All created means, no matter how vast, would be exhausted before they could encompass what belongs to Him; therefore, human beings must recognize the boundlessness of His perfection and the limits of their own understanding.

translation: Say, “I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is One God. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Prophet’s human nature does not diminish his mission, because revelation establishes the truth he conveys: God is uniquely worthy of worship. Whoever sincerely hopes for acceptance and reward when returning to Him must combine righteous action with undivided devotion, keeping worship free from shirk, hypocrisy, and the pursuit of anything besides God’s pleasure.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’an’s mysterious disjointed letters; their precise meaning is known only to Allah, while their placement draws attention to the revelation and its miraculous composition from the very letters known to its hearers.

translation: This is a mention of your Lord’s mercy upon His servant Zechariah.
interpretation: The verse introduces the account of Zechariah as a manifestation of Allah’s special mercy toward a devoted servant, inviting reflection on how divine care reaches the faithful even through their most personal hopes and trials.

translation: When he called upon his Lord in a quiet, private prayer.
interpretation: This portrays Zakariyya’s sincere humility and intimate trust in God: he turned to Him discreetly, with a heart free from display, confident that God hears even the softest supplication.

translation: He said, “My Lord, indeed my bones have grown weak, and my head has flared with gray, yet never, my Lord, have I been disappointed in supplicating You.”
interpretation: Zakariyya presents his physical weakness and advanced age with humility, while affirming his enduring confidence in Allah’s mercy: his previous prayers were never rejected, so he continues to ask with sincere hope rather than despair.

translation: “Indeed, I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir.”
interpretation: Zakariyya turns to God with humility, expressing concern that after his death no suitable successor may continue the religious responsibility entrusted to him. Although his wife is barren and the natural means seem impossible, he asks God for a righteous heir, showing his trust that divine mercy is not limited by human circumstances.

translation: He will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Jacob; and make him, my Lord, pleasing to You.
interpretation: Zakariyya is asking Allah for a righteous successor who will preserve the spiritual and prophetic legacy of his family, and whose faith, character, and deeds will be pleasing to Allah.

translation: “O Zechariah, We give you the good news of a boy whose name will be John. We have not given that name to anyone before him.”
interpretation: God responds to Zechariah’s sincere prayer with a child whose very name and distinguished mission are appointed by Him, demonstrating His power to bring about what seems impossible and granting the child a unique honor from the beginning.

translation: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached an extreme old age?”
interpretation: Zakariya expresses astonishment at how this promise will be fulfilled, since the ordinary means of having a child appear impossible; his question reflects wonder at God’s power rather than rejection of His promise.

translation: He said, “So it shall be. Your Lord says: ‘That is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing.’”
interpretation: Allah reassures Zakariyya that granting him a child despite his old age and his wife’s barrenness is effortless for Him, since bringing a person into existence from nothing demonstrates that no human circumstance can limit His creative power.

translation: He said, “My Lord, appoint for me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, while you are sound and well.”
interpretation: Zakariyya’s requested sign was answered through a temporary, extraordinary inability to speak—not because of illness or harm, but as a divine confirmation that God had granted his prayer. His bodily well-being made clear that this silence was a miraculous sign rather than a natural condition.

translation: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them, “Glorify Allah morning and evening.”
interpretation: Zakariyya’s inability to speak was a sign from Allah, yet he continued guiding his people: they were to devote themselves to praising and remembering Allah regularly at the beginning and end of each day.

translation: “O John, hold firmly to the Scripture.” And We granted him wisdom while he was still a child.
interpretation: God commands John to embrace the revealed Scripture with steadfastness, seriousness, and wholehearted commitment. He endowed him with sound judgment and understanding from an early age, showing that spiritual wisdom is a divine gift not restricted by youth.

translation: And [We gave him] tenderness from Us and purity, and he was mindful of God.
interpretation: God endowed Yahya with compassionate mercy toward others and spiritual purity, enabling him to live in sincere obedience and constant awareness of Him.

translation: And he was dutiful to his parents, and he was not arrogant or disobedient.
interpretation: True righteousness is shown through humble, compassionate obedience to one’s parents, while avoiding the pride and defiance that lead a person to reject rightful guidance.

translation: And peace be upon him on the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This declares God’s special peace, protection, and honor for John throughout the three most vulnerable and momentous transitions of human existence: entering this world, departing from it, and being resurrected for judgment.

translation: And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place.
interpretation: This verse portrays Mary’s devoted retreat from her family into solitude, preparing her for a profound divine encounter. Her withdrawal reflects modesty, spiritual dedication, and complete turning toward God away from worldly distraction.

translation: Then she withdrew from her people to an eastern place and veiled herself from them. We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared before her as a well-formed man.
interpretation: Maryam withdrew in privacy and placed a barrier between herself and her people; then Allah sent Jibrīl to her in human form, so that the divine message could be conveyed to her in a manner she could directly perceive, while his appearance remained that of a complete and dignified human being.

translation: She said, “Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing.”
interpretation: Maryam turns to Allah for protection and appeals to the man before her to fear Him and refrain from any improper approach, making piety the reason he should respect her sanctity.

translation: He said, “I am only a messenger of your Lord, sent to grant you a pure son.”
interpretation: The speaker clarifies that he is merely conveying God’s command and acting by His permission, announcing to Mary the miraculous birth of a son distinguished by purity, righteousness, and spiritual excellence.

translation: She said, “How can I have a boy when no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?”
interpretation: Maryam expresses astonishment at the announcement of a child, affirming that she has had no marital or illicit contact and is entirely chaste; her question highlights that the birth will occur by God’s miraculous power, beyond ordinary human means.

translation: He said, “So it will be. Your Lord says: ‘That is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us. It is a matter already decreed.’”
interpretation: The miraculous birth of Jesus is not beyond God’s power; it occurs by His command and wisdom. Through it, God manifests His authority, makes Jesus a sign of His creative power, and grants humanity mercy and guidance, for this event was established by His irrevocable decree.

translation: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a distant place.
interpretation: After receiving the divine decree, Mary conceived Jesus and isolated herself from her people in a remote place, seeking privacy as she faced the immense trial and responsibility entrusted to her.

translation: Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, “Oh, I wish I had died before this and become something forgotten and completely disregarded.”
interpretation: The intensity of Mary’s labor, together with her fear of facing people’s accusations and shame, overwhelmed her so deeply that she wished she had died before experiencing this trial and become entirely forgotten.

translation: Then he called to her from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a flowing stream.”
interpretation: In the midst of Mary’s isolation, pain, and fear, Allah reassures her that she is not abandoned. He provides immediate comfort and sustenance, teaching that divine care can emerge precisely at the moment of greatest distress.

translation: And shake the trunk of the palm tree toward you; it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you.
interpretation: Mary was instructed to take the available means despite her weakness, while trusting that God would provide for her; the falling dates were both nourishment and a sign of His care and mercy.

translation: So eat, drink, and be comforted. And if you see any human being, say: “Indeed, I have vowed a fast for the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any person.”
interpretation: God reassures Mary that, after her hardship, she may partake of His provision and find peace. Her vow of silence directs her away from futile confrontation and leaves the truth of her situation to be made clear by God Himself, teaching that trust in Him can bring composure when human explanations would only intensify distress.

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, “O Mary, you have certainly done an outrageous thing.”
interpretation: Mary returned to her community carrying the child, and they immediately condemned her, assuming that his birth resulted from a grave violation of chastity and reproaching her for what they regarded as an utterly shocking act.

translation: يا أخت هارون، ما كان أبوكِ رجلَ سوء، وما كانت أمكِ بَغِيًّا.
interpretation: يخاطب قومُ مريمَ عليها السلام بهذا الكلام مستنكرين ما ظنّوه من حالها، مستحضرين صلاح أبيها وعفّة أمها؛ فعبارة «أخت هارون» تشير إلى انتسابها إلى بيتٍ معروف بالصلاح، لا يلزم منها أنها أخته الشقيقة لنبيّ الله هارون.

translation: فأشارت إليه ۖ قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيًا
interpretation: أشارت مريم إلى عيسى عليه السلام ليكون جوابه بنفسه آيةً على براءتها، فاستنكر قومها أن يُخاطَب رضيعٌ لا يزال في المهد، إذ لم يدركوا بعدُ أن الله سيُجري على لسانه كلامًا خارقًا للعادة.

translation: He said, “Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has granted me the Scripture and made me a prophet.”
interpretation: Jesus declares that he is Allah’s servant, not divine or independent of Him. His scripture and prophethood are gifts bestowed by Allah, affirming that his authority comes entirely from his Lord.

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh as long as I remain alive.
interpretation: True blessing is reflected in bringing benefit wherever one is, while remaining devoted to worship and responsible care for others throughout life.

translation: And He has made me dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me arrogant or miserable.
interpretation: This expresses that true righteousness is shown through humble, compassionate devotion to one’s parent, while arrogance and rebelliousness lead to spiritual misery; God’s favor is seen in cultivating a character marked by obedience, gentleness, and humility.

translation: And peace be upon me on the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: Jesus عليه السلام declares that Allah’s protection, mercy, and safety accompany him through the three greatest transitions of human existence: his birth, his death, and his resurrection. This conveys his complete dependence on Allah and his honored status under divine care in this world and the Hereafter.

translation: That is Jesus, son of Mary—the word of truth concerning which they dispute.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Jesus is truly the son of Mary and that the divine account of him is the ultimate truth, exposing as mistaken the conflicting claims and doubts people hold about his identity.

translation: It is not for Allah to take a child. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: Allah is far above needing or possessing offspring, for He is utterly independent and unlike His creation. His will alone brings every matter into existence: when He decrees something, it comes to be without difficulty, means, or opposition.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: True guidance rests on recognizing that Allah alone is the Lord of all people and directing worship exclusively to Him; this sincere devotion is the clear and upright way to Him.

translation: Then the factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who disbelieve at the witnessing of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: The verse condemns the conflicting claims made about Jesus and warns that those who reject the truth will face severe ruin when all people are gathered before God for the decisive judgment.

translation: How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us! Yet today the wrongdoers are in manifest error.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject truth in this life will perceive reality with perfect clarity when they stand before God, but that recognition will come too late to benefit them. Their present refusal to heed revelation is therefore a clear and self-inflicted deviation from the truth.

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are heedless and do not believe.
interpretation: They are being warned that the final judgment will come when repentance and return are no longer possible; then those who lived heedlessly without faith will deeply regret having rejected the truth, but their regret will not benefit them.

translation: Indeed, We shall inherit the earth and all who are upon it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: Allah alone is the everlasting owner and sovereign of creation; when all worldly possessions and people pass away, every person will return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to recall Abraham as an exemplary model of unwavering truthfulness and divinely guided leadership: his sincerity in belief and speech was joined with the responsibility of conveying God’s revelation, showing that genuine prophethood is grounded in complete integrity before God.

translation: When he said to his father, “My dear father, why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you in any way?”
interpretation: Abraham respectfully challenged his father’s idolatry by pointing out that worship is due only to the One who hears, sees, and possesses the power to benefit and protect. Anything incapable of perception or action cannot truly be worthy of devotion, regardless of its status or the customs surrounding it.

translation: “O my father, knowledge has come to me that has not come to you, so follow me and I will guide you to a straight and upright path.”
interpretation: Abraham addresses his father with gentleness and respect, explaining that the divine knowledge granted to him gives him insight into the truth that his father lacks. He invites him to follow revelation—not out of arrogance, but so that he may be guided away from error to the balanced and righteous way pleasing to God.

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has always been disobedient to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Abraham gently warns his father that turning to idols is, in reality, obedience to Satan, who calls people away from worshipping Allah. Satan’s persistent rebellion against the Most Merciful shows that following him leads a person away from divine guidance and mercy.

translation: “O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful may touch you, and you would then become an ally of Satan.”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm gently warns his father that persisting in worshipping idols and rejecting the truth could expose him to divine punishment, causing him to follow Satan’s path and become subject to his influence. The verse reflects sincere concern expressed with respect and compassion, even when confronting serious disbelief.

translation: He said, “Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long while.”
interpretation: Abraham’s father responds to his call to abandon idolatry with anger, threatening violence and demanding separation. The verse illustrates how attachment to inherited beliefs can lead a person to reject sincere counsel and answer truth with hostility.

translation: He said, “Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; surely He has always been gracious to me.”
interpretation: Abraham responds to his father’s rejection with courtesy and restraint, showing that faithfulness to God does not permit abandoning kindness toward one’s family. His promise to seek forgiveness reflects hope in God’s mercy and his awareness of God’s continual care for him.

translation: And I will withdraw from you and from what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps, by calling upon my Lord, I will not be wretched.
interpretation: Abraham declares his spiritual separation from his people’s idolatry, choosing sincere devotion to Allah alone. His words also express humble hope: turning to Allah in prayer is the path to divine care, and whoever relies upon Him will not ultimately be abandoned or deprived.

translation: So when he withdrew from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and We made each of them a prophet.
interpretation: When Abraham renounced the idolatry of his people and devoted himself wholly to Allah, Allah compensated him with a blessed family and continued guidance through descendants chosen for prophethood. This shows that sincere sacrifice for faith is met by divine generosity, and that leaving falsehood for Allah can become the beginning of enduring spiritual blessing.

translation: And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy, and granted them a lofty tongue of truth.
interpretation: Allah favored Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob with special mercy and blessed them with enduring, honorable mention among later generations, so that their truthfulness and righteousness would remain exalted and praised.

translation: And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was devoted [to Allah], and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: Moses is presented as a servant whose worship and intention were sincerely devoted to Allah, free from associating partners with Him or seeking worldly recognition. His distinction as both a messenger and a prophet signifies that Allah chose him to receive revelation and entrusted him with conveying divine guidance to his people.

translation: And We called him from the right side of the Mount, and brought him near in intimate communion.
interpretation: Allah honored Moses by calling him from the blessed side of Mount Sinai and granting him the special nearness of direct, private conversation, showing his elevated rank and the intimacy of his relationship with his Lord.

translation: And We granted him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: Allah answered Moses’ need for support by granting him his brother Aaron as a prophet, showing that divine mercy may come through a righteous companion who strengthens the mission of conveying God’s guidance.

translation: And mention in the Book Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: Allah commands that Ishmael be remembered as an example of unwavering faithfulness: he honored his commitments, fulfilled what he promised, and combined this integrity with the honor of prophethood and the duty of conveying Allah’s message.

translation: And he used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakat, and he was pleasing to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse portrays true righteousness as beginning with faithful personal devotion and extending to the care and guidance of one’s household. By consistently directing them toward prayer and charitable responsibility, he earned the pleasure of Allah, showing that sincere obedience is reflected both in worship and in concern for others.

translation: And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to recall Idris as an exemplar of complete sincerity: he affirmed the truth, lived by it, and was honored with prophethood. His mention teaches that truthfulness joined with faithful obedience raises a person in God’s sight.

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This indicates that God granted Idrīs an exalted rank, honoring him with closeness, dignity, and elevated status in both spiritual standing and divine favor.

translation: Those are the prophets whom Allah has blessed: from the descendants of Adam, from those We carried with Noah, and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration, weeping.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true honor lies not merely in noble lineage or being chosen, but in responding to Allah’s revelation with profound humility, submission, and a heart moved to tears. The prophets’ immediate prostration shows that sincere guidance produces reverence and grateful worship.

translation: Then there came after them successors who neglected the prayer and followed their desires; so they will meet ruin.
interpretation: The verse warns that when people abandon the discipline and devotion embodied in prayer and instead submit themselves to their appetites, they move toward spiritual ruin and the consequences of that ruin in the Hereafter.

translation: Except those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; such people will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: Allah excludes from punishment those who sincerely turn away from sin, affirm true faith, and demonstrate it through righteous actions. He promises them entry into Paradise, where their reward will be granted in full, without any decrease or injustice.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Surely, His promise will certainly be fulfilled.
interpretation: These gardens are a divinely guaranteed reward for those who believe and remain faithful, even though they cannot see them in this world. The promise reflects Allah’s mercy and absolute faithfulness: what He has promised will inevitably come to pass.

translation: There they will hear no vain speech, only words of peace; and there they will have their provision morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place free from every harmful, empty, or disturbing utterance, where speech is marked by peace and honor. Its provision is continuous and assured—expressed by “morning and evening” according to familiar human time, though Paradise is beyond worldly limitation.

translation: That is the Paradise We will grant as an inheritance to whichever of Our servants is mindful of God.
interpretation: Paradise is a divine inheritance reserved for those who live in reverent obedience to God, guarding themselves from wrongdoing and remaining faithful to His guidance.

translation: “We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs whatever is before us, whatever is behind us, and whatever lies between them. And your Lord is never forgetful.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that the angels act and descend only according to God’s command, not by their own choice or timing. Everything in existence—past, present, and future—is under His ownership and knowledge, so His delay or withholding is never due to forgetfulness or neglect, but occurs according to His perfect wisdom.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—so worship Him and remain steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone comparable to Him?
interpretation: Since God alone sustains and governs all existence, worship belongs exclusively to Him. The command to persevere in worship calls for patient, steadfast devotion, while the closing question affirms that no one shares His unique lordship or is comparable to Him.

translation: And man says, “When I have died, will I truly be brought forth alive?”
interpretation: The verse portrays the denier of resurrection questioning how life could return after death, overlooking that the One who created him initially has full power to recreate him.

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
interpretation: The verse rebukes the person who doubts resurrection: the One who brought human beings into existence from absolute nonexistence is fully able to recreate them after death.

translation: So, by your Lord, We will surely gather them together with the devils, then We will surely bring them around Hell, kneeling.
interpretation: This is a solemn divine oath affirming that those who persist in rebellion will be resurrected alongside the forces that led them astray and brought before Hell in a state of humiliation and helpless submission.

translation: Then We will surely draw out from every faction whoever was most insolent toward the Most Merciful.
interpretation: يبين الله أنه يوم القيامة سيُميّز من كل جماعة أشدَّ أهلها تمردًا واستكبارًا على الحق والرحمن، فيُقدَّمون للعقوبة؛ لأن بلوغهم غاية العتو يجعلهم أحقَّ بالمؤاخذة وأبرزَ في انكشاف جرمهم.

translation: Then We certainly know best who is most deserving of entering and suffering in it.
interpretation: Allah knows precisely which people are most deserving of Hell because of their disbelief and wrongdoing, and His judgment concerning their punishment is founded on perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: وما منكم أحدٌ إلا سيمرّ بها أو يَرِدُ عليها؛ كان ذلك على ربك قضاءً محتومًا.
interpretation: المعنى أن جميع الخلق سيُحضَرون إلى جهنم أو يمرّون عليها يوم القيامة امتحانًا وإظهارًا لتمام عدل الله، ثم يُنجي الله أهل التقوى منها ويترك الظالمين فيها؛ فهذا أمر قضاه الله قضاءً لا مفرّ منه.

translation: Then We will save those who were mindful of Allah, and leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling.
interpretation: This portrays God’s judgment as a decisive distinction between the righteous and the unjust: those who lived with reverent obedience will be delivered from punishment, while those who persisted in wrongdoing will remain humbled and helpless within it.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, “Which of the two groups is better in position and superior in assembly?”
interpretation: The disbelievers reject the truth by appealing to their worldly status, wealth, and influence, assuming that these prove their way is superior to that of the believers. Their question is meant as mockery and self-congratulation, whereas worldly prominence is not a measure of truth or of a person’s standing before God.

translation: وكم من أممٍ كثيرة أهلكنا قبلهم، وكانت أحسن منهم متاعًا ومظهرًا.
interpretation: يبين الله أن كثرة المال وحسن الهيئة لا يدلان على رضا الله ولا يضمنان النجاة؛ فقد أهلك أممًا كانت أوفر متاعًا وأبهى منظرًا حين كذبت واستكبرت، فالعبرة بالإيمان والعمل الصالح لا بزينة الدنيا.

translation: قل: من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدًّا، حتى إذا رأوا ما يُوعدون، إما العذاب وإما الساعة، فسيعلمون من هو شرٌّ مكانًا وأضعفُ جندًا.
interpretation: المعنى أن الله يمهل الضال ويترك له فسحة من الزمن، لا رضًا بضلاله ولا إقرارًا له، حتى يبلغ الأجل الذي يظهر فيه الحق ظهورًا لا مجال لإنكاره؛ فعند نزول العذاب أو قيام الساعة يتبين أن أهل الباطل هم الأسوأ حالًا والأعجز نصرًا، مهما بدا لهم في الدنيا من قوة أو تفوق.

translation: And Allah increases those who are rightly guided in guidance. The enduring righteous deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in outcome.
interpretation: Allah grants those who sincerely follow guidance an increase in insight, faith, and steadfastness. Unlike temporary worldly pleasures, righteous deeds endure through their lasting benefit and will bring a better reward and final outcome before Him.

translation: Have you considered the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, “I will surely be given wealth and children”?
interpretation: The verse exposes the delusion of a person who rejects God’s signs yet confidently assumes that worldly prosperity and descendants will guarantee him favor and security, treating his hopes as though they were a promise from God.

translation: Has he looked into the unseen, or taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question rejecting the claim that a person is assured of blessings in the Hereafter: does he possess knowledge of the unseen, or has Allah given him a promise guaranteeing it? He has neither, so such certainty is unfounded.

translation: No indeed! We shall record what he says, and We shall prolong for him the punishment extensively.
interpretation: Allah rejects the person’s false claim and warns that every word is preserved as evidence against him; because of his deliberate persistence in falsehood, his punishment will be prolonged and intensified.

translation: And We shall inherit from him what he speaks of, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: Allah will strip him of everything he relied upon in this world, while his claims and possessions remain behind, and he will face God individually, without wealth, status, or supporters.

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping that they would be a source of honor and strength for them.
interpretation: They turned to idols and other false objects of worship, believing these could grant them power, protection, and status; yet true honor and strength belong only to Allah, and no created thing can provide them independently of Him.

translation: No indeed! They will deny their worship and become adversaries against them.
interpretation: The false gods whom the disbelievers worship will disown that worship on the Day of Judgment and turn against their worshippers, testifying against them rather than benefiting them.

translation: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, urging them on relentlessly?
interpretation: The verse means that those who reject truth become subject to the influence of devils, who continually provoke and drive them toward wrongdoing, rebellion, and hostility. This influence does not compel them against their will; rather, it intensifies the evil they willingly choose, as part of their being left to the consequences of their rejection.

translation: So do not hasten against them; We are only counting out for them a precise count.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet not to seek the immediate punishment or destruction of those who reject the truth, because their respite is deliberate and measured by God; every passing moment brings them closer to the appointed reckoning.

translation: On the Day We will gather the mindful of God before the Most Merciful as an honored delegation.
interpretation: The verse depicts the God-conscious being brought to Allah with dignity and honor, like honored guests welcomed into the presence of the Most Merciful, signifying their nearness to Him and the gracious reward prepared for their faith and obedience.

translation: And We will drive the guilty ones to Hell, thirsty.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing will be brought to Hell in a state of utter need and humiliation, deprived of the comfort and relief they once sought.

translation: They have no power of intercession, except those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Intercession is not an independent power possessed by anyone; it belongs entirely to God’s permission. Only those who have established a covenant with Him through true faith and obedience may be granted the privilege of interceding or benefiting from intercession.

translation: And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken a son.”
interpretation: This is a grave false claim that attributes offspring to Allah, whereas He is utterly free of dependence, lineage, and any likeness to His creation.

translation: لقد أتيتم أمرًا عظيمًا منكرًا.
interpretation: هذا توبيخ شديد لمن نسب إلى الله ولدًا؛ فهذه دعوى باطلة شنيعة تتجاوز حدود الحق وتعظّم الجرم في حق الله تعالى.

translation: The heavens almost rupture because of it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse completely.
interpretation: This portrays, through immense cosmic imagery, the gravity and enormity of attributing to God what is incompatible with His absolute uniqueness and majesty.

translation: That they have attributed a child to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This condemns the belief that Allah has offspring, affirming that His absolute divinity and perfection are incompatible with having a child or any created relation of lineage.

translation: It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: Allah’s perfect nature and absolute independence mean that He has no need for offspring, nor can any created being be His child; attributing a son to Him contradicts His oneness and majesty.

translation: There is none in the heavens and the earth except that they will come to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: Every created being is wholly dependent on God and subject to His authority; no one possesses true independence before Him, and all will ultimately stand before Him in the position of a servant.

translation: He has encompassed them and counted them precisely.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses every person completely; none is hidden from Him or beyond His reckoning.

translation: And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: Every person will stand before Allah individually, without relying on family, wealth, or status, and will be answerable for their own faith and deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: Allah promises that sincere faith and righteous conduct will bring about a special love and acceptance for the believer, placing affection for them in the hearts of people and granting them honor and closeness through His mercy.

translation: We have made it easy in your tongue only so that you may give glad tidings through it to the mindful and warn through it a stubbornly disputatious people.
interpretation: The Qur’an was revealed in a clear, accessible language so that its guidance could reach people plainly: those who are conscious of God may receive hope and encouragement, while those hardened in opposition and argument may be warned of the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: And how many generations before them We have destroyed! Can you perceive any one of them, or hear from them the faintest sound?
interpretation: This is a warning that the powerful peoples who rejected God were ultimately erased without leaving any ability to answer or defend themselves. Their silence demonstrates that worldly strength and permanence are illusions, while those who deny the truth should fear a similar end and heed the warning before it is too late.

translation: طه (طه)
interpretation: هذان حرفان من الحروف المقطَّعة التي افتُتحت بها بعض السور، وحقيقتهما التفصيلية مما استأثر الله بعلمه، وفي افتتاح السورة بهما تنبيه إلى إعجاز القرآن المؤلَّف من الحروف التي يعرفها العرب.

translation: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you so that you would suffer.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet ﷺ that the Qur’an is not meant to impose unbearable hardship upon him; rather, its revelation is an act of mercy and guidance, and his duty is to convey it faithfully without being consumed by grief over those who refuse to believe.

translation: But only as a reminder for whoever fears Allah.
interpretation: The Qur’an is not meant to impose hardship; it serves to awaken the heart of one who has reverence for Allah, guiding such a person to reflect, remember, and respond obediently.

translation: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This Qur’an is revealed by Allah, the Creator of the earth and the lofty heavens; its source is therefore divine, perfect in authority, and beyond human invention.

translation: The Most Merciful established Himself over the Throne.
interpretation: This affirms Allah’s supreme dominion and exalted authority over all creation, without comparing Him to created beings or defining the manner of His establishment.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between them, and whatever lies beneath the soil.
interpretation: Everything in existence belongs exclusively to Allah—whether seen or unseen, above or below—and is completely subject to His ownership, knowledge, and authority.

translation: And whether you speak aloud, He surely knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses every reality: what people conceal in their hearts and even the innermost thoughts and intentions that remain hidden from themselves or never become words.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names.
interpretation: Allah alone is worthy of worship, for He possesses every perfection, and His names express His sublime attributes and absolute perfection. Knowing these names should lead the believer to worship Him sincerely and call upon Him through them.

translation: And has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: يستفتح الله تعالى ذكر قصة موسى بهذا الاستفهام ليلفت انتباه المخاطَب إلى قصة عظيمة تحمل من العبر والهداية ما يستحق التأمل والإنصات.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, “Stay here. I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a burning brand from it, or find some guidance at the fire.”
interpretation: Moses, traveling with his family, noticed a fire and asked them to remain where they were while he went toward it. He hoped either to obtain warmth or light from it, or to find someone who could guide them, showing his practical concern for his family and his uncertainty about the extraordinary encounter that awaited him.

translation: Then when he came to it, he was called: “O Moses!”
interpretation: When Moses reached the fire, Allah addressed him directly, marking the beginning of his prophetic mission and drawing his attention to the divine revelation about to be given to him.

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā.
interpretation: Allah commands Moses to approach the sacred place with humility and reverence, recognizing that he is standing in a divinely sanctified setting before his Lord.

translation: Indeed, I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: God informs Moses that He has specially selected him for the honor of prophethood and commands him to attend with complete readiness and obedience to the revelation that will guide his mission.

translation: إنني أنا الله، لا إله إلا أنا، فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري.
interpretation: يُعلن الله تعالى وحدانيته المطلقة واستحقاقه وحده للعبادة، ويوجّه عباده إلى إخلاص العبادة له، وإقامة الصلاة بوصفها أعظم وسائل دوام ذكره وحضور القلب معه.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is surely coming. I keep it hidden so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives.
interpretation: The exact time of the Day of Judgment is concealed by God, yet its coming is certain. This hiddenness calls people to remain vigilant and sincere, knowing that every effort and deed will ultimately receive its fitting recompense.

translation: So let not one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn you away from it, lest you perish.
interpretation: Do not allow the denial and misguided desires of those who reject the Resurrection to divert you from faith in it and from living according to its truth, for yielding to their path leads to ruin.

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: Allah asks Moses about the object in his hand—not out of ignorance, but to draw his attention to it and prepare him for the miracle by which his staff will become a sign of divine power.

translation: He said, “It is my staff; I lean on it, use it to shake leaves down for my sheep, and have other uses for it.”
interpretation: Moses speaks to Allah with humility and familiarity, explaining the ordinary practical purposes of his staff. His answer also reflects his care for his flock and his complete dependence on Allah, who is about to transform this simple staff into a manifest sign.

translation: He said, “Cast it down, O Moses.”
interpretation: God commands Moses to throw down the staff he is holding, preparing him to witness the sign by which God will affirm His support and strengthen his mission.

translation: فألقاها، فإذا هي حيّةٌ تسعى.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية تحوّل عصا موسى عليه السلام إلى حيّةٍ تتحرّك بأمر الله، في ظهورٍ لمعجزةٍ خارقة تدلّ على قدرة الله وتأييده لنبيّه.

translation: He said, “Take it and do not fear; We will return it to its former state.”
interpretation: Allah reassures Moses that the staff, despite its frightening transformation, remains under His power and will be restored to its original form, teaching him to trust divine protection while confronting the sign before him.

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will emerge white, without affliction—another sign.
interpretation: Allah gives Moses a further miraculous sign: when he places his hand against his side and then withdraws it, it shines with a striking whiteness, yet remains free from illness or harm. This confirms that the change is a divine sign and strengthens Moses for his mission.

translation: So that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: God is assuring Moses that the miracles granted to him are meant to reveal the truth of his mission and demonstrate the greatness of God’s power.

translation: اذهب إلى فرعون، إنه طغى.
interpretation: في هذه الآية تكليفٌ لموسى عليه السلام بمواجهة فرعون ودعوته إلى الحق، لأن استكباره وتجاوزه لحدود الله جعلا إصلاحه ومساءلته أمراً واجباً.

translation: He said, “My Lord, expand my chest for me.”
interpretation: Moses appeals to God to grant him inner openness, calm, courage, and the ability to bear the responsibility of his mission and speak with clarity.

translation: And make my task easy for me.
interpretation: This is a supplication for Allah to remove difficulty, grant clarity and capability, and make the responsibility one faces manageable and successful.

translation: And loosen the knot from my tongue,
interpretation: Moses asks God to remove the impediment affecting his speech so that he may express himself clearly and communicate His message effectively.

translation: So that they may understand my speech.
interpretation: Moses asks Allah to remove any impediment from his expression so that his people can clearly comprehend the message he conveys.

translation: And appoint for me an aide from my family.
interpretation: Moses asks God to grant him a trusted member of his own family to support and assist him in carrying out his mission.

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: Moses identifies Aaron as his brother and presents him as the trusted person who can support him in carrying out his mission.

translation: Strengthen my back through him.
interpretation: Moses asks Allah to support and fortify him through his brother Aaron, so that he may face the burden of his mission with greater strength and steadfastness.

translation: And let him share in my mission.
interpretation: Moses asks Allah to appoint Aaron as a helper and partner in carrying out the prophetic responsibility, so that he may support him in conveying the message and fulfilling its demands.

translation: So that we may glorify You abundantly.
interpretation: Moses asks Allah for support through his brother so that they may worship Him sincerely, repeatedly proclaiming His perfection and exalting Him in all circumstances.

translation: and remember You often
interpretation: Moses expresses his desire, together with Aaron, to remain constantly mindful of Allah and to praise and obey Him abundantly while carrying out their mission.

translation: Indeed, You have always been All-Seeing of us.
interpretation: Moses acknowledges that Allah has complete and constant awareness of their condition, weakness, and need, and therefore trusts that He will guide and support them.

translation: He said, “Your request has indeed been granted, O Moses.”
interpretation: Allah reassures Moses that his supplication has been accepted and that the help and support he asked for in carrying out his mission will be given to him.

translation: And We had certainly shown you favor another time.
interpretation: Allah reminds Moses that His care and grace had already reached him before this new commission, assuring him that the One who had protected and guided him previously would continue to support him.

translation: When We revealed to your mother what was to be revealed,
interpretation: Allah reminds Moses of the special divine inspiration given to his mother, guiding her through the extraordinary circumstances surrounding his infancy and showing that His care and plan had been with Moses from the very beginning.

translation: “Place him in the chest, then cast it into the river; let the river cast it onto the shore, where an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him. And I bestowed upon you love from Me, so that you would be raised under My watchful care.”
interpretation: Allah recounts how He protected Moses from infancy through a plan whose outward means appeared perilous but was governed entirely by divine care. The river carried him safely to Pharaoh’s household, even though Pharaoh was an enemy of Allah and of Moses, while Allah placed an irresistible affection for Moses in those who encountered him. Thus Moses was preserved and nurtured under Allah’s direct protection until he was prepared for his mission.

translation: حين كانت أختك تمشي فتقول: «هل أدلّكم على من يتكفّله؟» فرددناك إلى أمك كي تقرّ عينها ولا تحزن، وقتلتَ نفسًا فنجّيناك من الغم، وابتليناك ابتلاءاتٍ متعاقبة، فلبثتَ سنين في أهل مدين، ثم جئتَ في الوقت المقدّر يا موسى.
interpretation: يبيّن الله لموسى أن عنايته به أحاطت به منذ طفولته؛ فدبّر رجوعه إلى أمه، وأنقذه من آثار خطئه، وهيّأه عبر الابتلاء والغربة في مدين حتى بلغ الموعد الذي قدّره له للرسالة. وفي ذلك تسلية له بأن مراحل حياته، بما فيها من محن وتأخير، كانت إعدادًا إلهيًا لمهمته وليست ضياعًا أو مصادفة.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: Allah is telling Moses that He personally selected him, cared for him, and prepared him for the role of conveying His message and serving His purpose.

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me.
interpretation: God commands Moses and Aaron to undertake their mission relying on His revealed signs, while remaining constant and unwavering in remembrance of Him, so that their efforts are guided by continual awareness of God rather than weakness or neglect.

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed all bounds.
interpretation: Moses and Aaron are commanded to confront Pharaoh because his tyranny and rebellion have exceeded the limits of justice and obedience to God.

translation: “Then speak to him with gentle speech, so that he may perhaps take heed or become mindful.”
interpretation: Allah instructs Moses and Aaron to address Pharaoh with kindness and restraint, even despite his tyranny, because gentle words may awaken reflection in a hardened heart or lead it to fear accountability before Allah.

translation: They said, “Our Lord, we fear that he may hasten to punish us or transgress against us.”
interpretation: Moses and Aaron express their fear that Pharaoh may react immediately with violence or exceed all bounds in oppression, asking God for reassurance and protection as they confront him.

translation: He said, “Do not fear. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.”
interpretation: Allah reassures Moses and Aaron that they need not fear confronting Pharaoh, because His complete knowledge and watchful care accompany them: He hears everything that is said and sees every circumstance, so their mission is under His protection and guidance.

translation: فاذهبا إليه فقولا: إننا رسولا ربك، فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم. لقد جئناك بآية من ربك، والسلام على من اتبع الهدى.
interpretation: يأمر الله موسى وهارون أن يواجها فرعون برسالة واضحة تجمع بين المطالبة برفع الظلم عن بني إسرائيل، وإظهار الدليل الإلهي على صدقهما، والدعوة إلى اتباع الهدى؛ فالأمان والسلام الحقيقيان إنما يكونان لمن يقبل هداية الله ويستجيب لها.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that punishment will be upon whoever denies the truth and turns away.
interpretation: The verse conveys that divine punishment is directed toward those who reject the truth after it has been made clear to them and deliberately turn away from obedience and guidance.

translation: He said, “Who then is your Lord, O Moses?”
interpretation: Pharaoh asks Moses to identify his Lord, challenging the claim that he and Aaron have been sent by God and implicitly demanding an authority beyond Pharaoh’s own claimed rule.

translation: He said, “Our Lord is the One who gave everything its form, then guided it.”
interpretation: Moses declared that Allah created every being with the qualities and capacities suited to it, and then guided it toward the purposes and functions for which it was created.

translation: He said, “What then became of the former generations?”
interpretation: Pharaoh asks about the fate of earlier peoples, seemingly seeking to challenge Moses and divert the discussion toward matters beyond his claimed authority; the question also raises the issue of how past nations are judged by God.

translation: He said, “Knowledge of them is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.”
interpretation: Moses affirms that God’s knowledge encompasses every detail of creation and is preserved in a complete record. Unlike human knowledge, God’s knowledge is free from error, omission, and forgetfulness; therefore, His judgment and care over all things are perfectly certain.

translation: He is the One who made the earth a cradle for you, laid out pathways for you upon it, and sent down water from the sky, by which We brought forth various kinds of plants.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to God’s ordered provision: He made the earth habitable and accessible, opened routes across it, and made rain the means by which diverse plant life emerges. This harmony between the earth, water, and vegetation reveals His sustaining power and calls people to recognize His wisdom and care.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for people of sound understanding.
interpretation: The varied nourishment and orderly provision made available for human beings and their livestock point to the wisdom, power, and mercy of their Creator; those endowed with sound reason recognize these signs and respond with gratitude and faith.

translation: From it We created you, into it We shall return you, and from it We shall bring you forth once again.
interpretation: Human beings originate from the earth, return to it through burial after death, and will be resurrected from it by God for the final judgment.

translation: And We certainly showed him all Our signs, but he denied them and refused.
interpretation: The verse portrays Pharaoh’s rejection as deliberate: despite being confronted with clear divine signs, his arrogance led him to deny the truth and refuse submission.

translation: He said, “Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?”
interpretation: Pharaoh rejected Moses’ message by portraying it as sorcery and accusing him of seeking to expel the established people from their homeland. This accusation reflects Pharaoh’s fear that Moses’ call to truth would undermine his authority and the political order he controlled.

translation: “We will surely bring you magic like it, so set between us and you an appointment that neither we nor you will fail to keep—a place of equal openness.”
interpretation: The magicians’ challenge reflects their confidence that Moses’s sign was merely sorcery and that they could match it. They demand a public, neutral meeting place and a fixed time so the contest will be witnessed by everyone, revealing their desire to turn the matter into a spectacle before the people.

translation: He said, “Your appointment is on the day of the festival, and let the people be assembled in the forenoon.”
interpretation: The speaker set a public time and place for the confrontation, choosing a festival day and the morning when people would gather, so the matter would be witnessed openly and the truth could become clear to everyone.

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, gathered his scheme, and then came.
interpretation: Pharaoh withdrew to devise his response, mobilized all his resources and sorcery against Moses, and returned prepared for the confrontation.

translation: Moses said to them, “Woe to you! Do not fabricate lies against Allah, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, whoever fabricates lies has truly failed.”
