interpretation: Moses warned the sorcerers that attributing falsehood to Allah and presenting deception as divine truth would bring about their ruin. Their apparent success through falsehood could not save them, for the ultimate outcome of inventing lies against Allah is loss and failure.

translation: Then they disputed among themselves over their affair and kept their secret counsel hidden.
interpretation: The opponents of Moses privately debated how to confront him, concealing their deliberations from the public as they tried to agree on a strategy against the truth he had brought.

translation: They said, “These two are certainly magicians who intend to drive you out of your land by their magic and to do away with your exemplary way of life.”
interpretation: The leaders warned Pharaoh’s people against Moses and Aaron by portraying their call to truth as a magical threat to their homeland and inherited social order, thereby stirring fear and urging resistance to the message.

translation: So gather your schemes, then come in ranks; whoever prevails today will surely succeed.
interpretation: The magicians are urged to unite their efforts, arrange themselves confidently, and confront Moses together, believing that victory and superiority in this contest will bring them success.

translation: They said, “O Moses, either you cast first, or we will be the first to cast.”
interpretation: The magicians confidently offered Moses the choice of beginning, displaying their composure and trust in their apparent power; yet their willingness to let him proceed first also set the stage for the truth to expose the deception of their magic.

translation: He said, “No, you throw first.” Then suddenly, their ropes and staffs appeared to him, through their magic, as though they were moving swiftly.
interpretation: The magicians’ sorcery created a powerful visual illusion, making their inanimate ropes and staffs seem to move, though they had not truly come to life. આ

translation: Then Moses felt a fear within himself.
interpretation: Moses experienced a natural moment of apprehension when confronted by the magicians’ display, but this fear did not signify doubt in God; it reflected the gravity of the situation before divine reassurance and support came to him.

translation: We said, “Do not fear; indeed, you will be superior.”
interpretation: Allah reassured Moses that he should not be intimidated by the magicians or their display, for divine truth would prevail through him and his sign would overcome their deception.

translation: “Throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a magician, and the magician will never succeed, wherever he may go.”
interpretation: God commands Moses to expose the falsehood of the magicians’ work: their display is merely deceptive craft, while divine truth overcomes it completely. The verse affirms that sorcery and deception cannot ultimately prosper, regardless of the power or place of those who practice them.

translation: Then the magicians fell down in prostration, saying, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
interpretation: The magicians recognized that Moses’ sign was divine truth, not sorcery, and they immediately submitted to Allah, openly affirming Him as the true Lord rather than Pharaoh.

translation: قال: «آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم؟ إنه لكبيركم الذي علّمكم السحر، فلأقطّعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف، ولأصلبنّكم في جذوع النخل، ولتعلمنّ أينا أشدّ عذابًا وأبقى».
interpretation: يكشف هذا القول عن استبداد فرعون؛ فقد جعل الإيمان جريمةً لأنه وقع بغير إذنه، واتهم المؤمنين بالتواطؤ مع موسى لستر عجزه عن مواجهة الحق. ثم لجأ إلى التهديد بأبشع العقوبات لإرهابهم وصرف الناس عن صدق المعجزة، بينما يدل ثباتهم على أن الإيمان إذا استقر في القلب لا تزعزعه سلطة الطغيان ولا وعيده.

translation: They said, “We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us, nor over Him who created us. So decree whatever you are going to decree; you can only decree concerning this worldly life.”
interpretation: The magicians reject Pharaoh’s demand with unwavering faith: no worldly ruler can be preferred over the truth God has made evident or over the Creator Himself. They accept whatever punishment he imposes, knowing that his authority is temporary and limited to this life, while their commitment to God transcends fear of worldly consequences.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, so that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to perform. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: The magicians, having recognized the truth of Moses’ sign, chose faith despite Pharaoh’s threats. They declare that Allah’s forgiveness and everlasting reward are superior to Pharaoh’s power and the temporary worldly benefits he offered, while attributing to him the responsibility for forcing them into practicing magic.

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal will have Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: The verse warns that meeting God while persisting in guilt and rejecting His guidance leads to a punishment from which there is no escape: death will not end the suffering, nor will life there offer any comfort or meaningful relief.

translation: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds—for them are the highest ranks.
interpretation: True faith is shown through righteous action, and those who meet Allah with both sincere belief and good deeds will be honored with the loftiest levels of Paradise.

translation: Gardens of everlasting residence beneath which rivers flow, remaining therein forever. That is the reward of whoever purifies himself.
interpretation: Allah promises lasting Paradise to those who cleanse themselves from disbelief, sin, and corrupt character, showing that true purification is reflected in sincere faith and righteous conduct; their reward is permanent bliss with no end.

translation: And We revealed to Moses: “Set out by night with My servants, and make for them a dry path through the sea; fear neither being overtaken nor be afraid.”
interpretation: Allah commanded Moses to lead the Children of Israel away under His protection and promised to open a safe passage through the sea for them. The verse teaches that when obedience is joined with trust in Allah, apparent impossibilities can become means of deliverance, and the believer should not be overcome by fear of the pursuing enemy or anxiety about what lies ahead.

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his armies, and the sea overwhelmed them with that which overwhelmed them.
interpretation: Pharaoh relentlessly followed Moses and the believers in arrogance and hostility, but the sea engulfed him and his forces completely, bringing about their ruin and showing that oppressive power cannot escape God’s judgment.

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray, and he did not guide them.
interpretation: Pharaoh misled his people by turning them away from faith and truth, while claiming authority over them; his leadership brought them only toward ruin, not true guidance.

translation: O Children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemy, appointed for you the right side of Mount Sinai, and sent down upon you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Israelites of God’s successive favors: He delivered them from oppression, honored them with the revelation given at Mount Sinai, and sustained them with provision beyond ordinary means. These blessings were meant to awaken gratitude and obedience, showing that divine rescue and provision carry with them the responsibility to remain faithful to God’s guidance.

translation: Eat from the wholesome things We have provided for you, but do not transgress regarding them, lest My wrath fall upon you; and whoever My wrath falls upon has surely perished.
interpretation: Allah permits people to enjoy His pure provisions with gratitude and moderation, while warning them not to misuse them through excess, ingratitude, or violating His commands. Persisting in such transgression leads to divine wrath and ruin.

translation: Indeed, I am Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains rightly guided.
interpretation: Allah’s forgiveness is open to those who sincerely turn away from sin, affirm faith, demonstrate that faith through righteous action, and persevere in following divine guidance rather than returning to their former wrongdoing.

translation: “And what has hastened you ahead of your people, O Moses?”
interpretation: Allah asks Moses why he left his people and came ahead of them, drawing attention to the importance of remaining with them and fulfilling his responsibility toward them.

translation: He said, “They are close behind me, and I have hastened to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased.”
interpretation: Moses explains that his haste was driven by eagerness to draw near to Allah and attain His pleasure, while trusting that his people were following behind him.

translation: He said, “Indeed, We have tested your people after you, and al-Sāmirī has led them astray.”
interpretation: Allah informed Moses that, during his absence, his people were being tested by the worship of the calf, and that al-Sāmirī had misled them into this deviation from true worship.

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, “O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Has the time seemed too long to you, or did you wish that the wrath of your Lord should befall you, so that you broke your promise to me?”
interpretation: Moses rebuked his people because, in his absence, they abandoned the covenant of worshipping Allah alone and followed the calf. His words express both sorrow over their deviation and warning that disobedience can bring divine anger; the delay of a promised blessing or the absence of a messenger is not a justification for abandoning faith and obedience.

translation: They said, “We did not break our promise to you of our own accord, but we were made to carry burdens of the ornaments of the people, so we cast them away—and that is how al-Sāmirī cast them.”
interpretation: They pleaded that their making of the calf was not a deliberate act of defiance, but resulted from their casting away the jewelry they had been carrying; by mentioning al-Sāmirī’s similar action, they revealed how he exploited this opportunity to lead them into idolatry.

translation: Then he brought out for them a calf—merely a body that made a lowing sound. They said, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but he has forgotten.”
interpretation: The calf was only a lifeless form made to produce a sound, yet the people were deceived into worshipping it. Their claim that it was the god of Moses was a false excuse, suggesting that Moses had forgotten where his Lord was, whereas the true God cannot be represented by a manufactured image or confined to any physical form.

translation: Do they not see that it cannot respond to them in speech, nor possess the power to harm or benefit them?
interpretation: This rebukes those who worship something incapable of hearing, answering, or controlling any benefit or harm, showing that true worship belongs only to the One who possesses absolute power and responds to His servants.

translation: And Aaron had already said to them before this, “O my people, you have only been tested by it, and surely your Lord is the Most Merciful. So follow me and obey my command.”
interpretation: Aaron clarified that the calf was a trial exposing their obedience and faith, not a true deity. He called them back to worship the Merciful Lord alone and urged them to follow his guidance rather than the impulses that had led them astray.

translation: They said, “We will remain devoted to it until Moses returns to us.”
interpretation: They stubbornly refused to abandon worship of the calf, insisting that they would continue in this devotion until Moses came back and settled the matter.

translation: He said, “O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,”
interpretation: Moses questioned Aaron about why he had not intervened more decisively when he witnessed his people abandoning true guidance, expressing reproach while seeking to understand his brother’s response.

translation: Why did you not follow me? Have you then disobeyed my command?
interpretation: Moses reproached Aaron for not following his directive to restrain the people from the calf, expressing serious concern that his brother had failed to carry out his command.

translation: He said, “O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. I feared that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel and disregarded my word.’”
interpretation: Aaron responds gently to Moses, explaining that he did not confront the people with force because he feared that a harsh intervention would fracture the Israelites further and make them reject his leadership. His words show his concern to preserve the community’s unity while clarifying that his restraint was not disregard for Moses’ command.

translation: He said, “What is the matter with you, O Samiri?”
interpretation: Moses addresses the Samiri in reproach, demanding that he explain the motive and justification behind his actions.

translation: He said, “I perceived what they did not perceive, so I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger and cast it away. Thus my soul enticed me.”
interpretation: The speaker confesses that he acted on a private perception and then allowed his desires to justify his disobedience. His claim of special knowledge did not excuse him; rather, it exposed how the soul can adorn wrongdoing and lead a person away from obedience to God.

translation: He said, “Then go away. It is yours in this life to say, ‘No contact.’ And you have an appointed time that you will not fail to meet. Now look at your god to which you remained devoted: We will surely burn it, then scatter its remains into the sea completely.”
interpretation: Moses condemned the Samiri to isolation and disgrace as the worldly consequence of leading people into idolatry, while reminding him that an unavoidable appointed judgment still awaited him. He then exposed the helplessness of the calf by destroying it utterly, showing that anything fashioned by human hands cannot be worthy of worship or possess divine power.

translation: Your only God is Allah; there is no deity except Him. His knowledge encompasses all things.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute oneness of Allah and directs worship exclusively to Him. Nothing lies beyond His complete and limitless knowledge, so He alone is worthy of trust, obedience, and devotion.

translation: Thus We relate to you some of the news of what has passed; and We have given you, from Us, a Reminder.
interpretation: Allah consoles and strengthens the Prophet by recounting the lessons of earlier peoples, while granting him the Qur’an as a divine reminder that guides hearts, preserves truth, and remains a lasting source of admonition.

translation: Whoever turns away from it will surely bear a burden of sin on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: Turning away from the Qur’an after its truth has been made clear is not a harmless neglect; it becomes a moral burden for which a person will be held accountable before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: They will remain therein, and evil indeed will it be for them as a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse portrays the lasting punishment awaiting those who persist in grave wrongdoing: their punishment will not be temporary, and on the Day of Resurrection it will weigh upon them as a terrible and unbearable burden.

translation: On the Day the Trumpet is blown, We will gather the criminals on that Day, their eyes turned blue.
interpretation: When the Trumpet announces the Resurrection, those who persisted in wrongdoing will be raised and assembled in a state of terror and humiliation, with their altered, blue or discolored eyes revealing the severity of their fear and distress.

translation: They will whisper among themselves, “You remained no more than ten days.”
interpretation: Overwhelmed by the terror of the Resurrection, they will privately discuss how briefly they believe they remained in the world, perceiving their former life as no more than ten days in comparison with the eternal Hereafter.

translation: We know best what they say when the most sound of them in judgment says, “You remained only a day.”
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, their worldly life will seem so brief and insignificant that even the wisest among them will estimate it as no more than a single day. This reveals how fleeting worldly existence is when compared with the everlasting Hereafter.

translation: They ask you about the mountains. Say, “My Lord will utterly pulverize them.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, even the most massive and seemingly immovable features of creation will be completely reduced by Allah’s command, demonstrating His absolute power and the fleeting nature of the material world.

translation: Then He will leave it as a smooth, level plain.
interpretation: The verse portrays the complete removal of every mountain and elevation, leaving the earth utterly flat and exposed—an image of the overwhelming transformation of the world on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: You will see in it neither crookedness nor unevenness.
interpretation: The earth will be made completely level and smooth, free from every depression, elevation, or irregularity, so that nothing obstructs the gathering of creation before God.

translation: في ذلك اليوم سيتبعون الداعي دون انحراف عنه، وتخشع الأصوات للرحمن، فلا يُسمع إلا همسًا.
interpretation: يبيّن الآية أن الخلق يوم القيامة ينقادون لأمر الداعي إلى المحشر انقيادًا لا يستطيعون معه الميل أو التخلّف، ويغلبهم الخوف والهيبة أمام الرحمن، فلا يملكون إلا كلامًا خافتًا لا يكاد يُسمع.

translation: On that Day, intercession will benefit none except those whom the Most Merciful permits and whose words He approves.
interpretation: Intercession belongs entirely to Allah’s authority: no one may intercede unless He grants permission, and no intercession is accepted unless it is for someone whose faith and words accord with His approval.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they cannot encompass Him with knowledge.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge completely encompasses all that lies before and behind His creatures, whereas their limited understanding can never fully comprehend His essence or encompass the reality of His knowledge.

translation: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. And whoever bears wrongdoing has truly failed.
interpretation: On that Day, every person will stand in complete submission before Allah, the One whose life and authority are perfect and everlasting; those who come carrying injustice and sin will find no success or refuge.

translation: Whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer need fear neither injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: True faith joined with righteous action assures a person that God will judge him with perfect justice: no sin will be added to his account, and no reward for his good deeds will be reduced or withheld.

translation: Thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an, and We have varied within it the warnings, so that they may become mindful of God or it may awaken remembrance in them.
interpretation: God revealed the Qur’an in clear Arabic and presented its warnings in varied forms so that people might develop reverent awareness, turn away from wrongdoing, and have their hearts awakened to remember and obey Him.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the True King. Do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation to you has been completed, and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that revelation belongs entirely to Allah, the supreme and perfectly true Sovereign, so the Prophet ﷺ must receive it with patience and attentiveness rather than rushing to recite or respond before its meaning is fully conveyed. It also establishes that seeking greater knowledge is a lifelong duty, expressed through humility before Allah and continual dependence on Him for understanding.

translation: And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve.
interpretation: This verse portrays Adam’s lapse as arising from forgetfulness and a momentary weakness of resolve in keeping God’s command, rather than from deliberate, persistent rebellion.

translation: And when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” they all prostrated except Iblīs; he refused.
interpretation: This verse portrays Iblīs’s refusal as a deliberate act of disobedience to God’s command, revealing his pride and rejection of Adam’s honored position. It teaches that true submission to God requires obedience even when one’s own judgment or sense of superiority objects.

translation: So We said, “O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, lest you suffer.”
interpretation: Allah warns Adam that Satan’s enmity threatens the peace and blessing granted to him and his wife. Remaining in Paradise means security and ease, whereas being expelled through Satan’s deception would bring them into the toil, hardship, and vulnerability of earthly life.

translation: Indeed, it is assured for you there that you will neither hunger nor be unclothed.
interpretation: Allah assures Adam that Paradise provides complete security and dignity: his essential needs will always be fulfilled, with no deprivation of food or clothing.

translation: And you will not thirst therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun’s heat.
interpretation: The verse portrays the garden as a place of complete comfort and protection, free from the basic hardships of thirst and scorching heat.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, “O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that never fades?”
interpretation: Satan lured Adam with a deceptive promise of immortality and everlasting power, taking advantage of the human longing to endure and possess what does not perish.

translation: So they both ate from it, and their private parts became exposed to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves from Paradise. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray.
interpretation: The verse portrays the immediate consequence of yielding to temptation: Adam and his wife became aware of their nakedness and instinctively sought to cover themselves. Adam’s disobedience was a lapse in judgment that caused him to depart from the guidance given by his Lord, emphasizing human vulnerability to temptation and the seriousness of disobeying divine instruction.

translation: Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.
interpretation: After Adam’s lapse, God did not abandon him; rather, He selected him for His grace, enabled him to repent sincerely, accepted that repentance, and directed him back to the path of obedience.

translation: He said, “Descend from it, all of you, as enemies to one another. Then, whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.”
interpretation: Human beings are sent into earthly life amid the ongoing conflict between truth and falsehood, but they are not left without direction. God promises that whoever sincerely follows the guidance He reveals will be protected from losing the right path and from the misery that results from turning away from Him.

translation: But whoever turns away from My remembrance will certainly have a miserable, constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: Turning away from God’s guidance deprives a person of the inner peace and spiritual assurance that give life its true breadth, even if worldly comforts are present. As a consequence of deliberately ignoring the truth, he will be raised blind on the Day of Resurrection—without the insight and direction he rejected in this world.

translation: He will say, “My Lord, why have You raised me blind, though I was able to see?”
interpretation: This is the regret of one who, despite having access to divine guidance in worldly life, turned away from it; as a fitting consequence, he is deprived of the light and clarity he once possessed.

translation: He will say, “Thus Our signs came to you, but you disregarded them; and so today you will be disregarded.”
interpretation: The verse conveys that the person who deliberately turns away from Allah’s clear signs and neglects the guidance brought to him will, on the Day of Judgment, be deprived of mercy and left without care or support. Allah’s being described as “forgetting” him does not mean that He lacks knowledge, but that He will treat him as one abandoned because of his own rejection.

translation: Thus do We recompense whoever transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: This is a warning that persistent excess and rejection of God’s signs bring fitting consequences: although worldly punishment may be temporary, the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and enduring because it follows deliberate unbelief and unrepentant wrongdoing.

translation: أفلم يتبيّن لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من الأمم، يمشون في مساكنهم وآثارهم؟ إن في ذلك لآيات لأصحاب العقول.
interpretation: ألا يعتبر هؤلاء بما يرونه من ديار الأمم السابقة وآثار هلاكها، فيدركوا أن الإصرار على التكذيب والعصيان يعرّضهم لمثل عاقبتهم؟ إن مشاهدة تلك الآثار تذكير واضح ينتفع به أصحاب العقول الراجحة.

translation: And had it not been for a decree that had already gone forth from your Lord, and an appointed term, it would have been inevitable.
interpretation: Allah’s prior decree of postponing judgment until the appointed time is the only reason punishment is not immediately imposed; once that term arrives, it cannot be averted.

translation: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset; and glorify Him during some hours of the night and at the edges of the day, so that you may be content.
interpretation: The verse teaches that patience in the face of hurtful denial is sustained by continual remembrance and praise of God at every part of the day and night; through this worship, the heart is strengthened and brought to inner contentment.

translation: Do not fix your eyes upon the worldly delights We have granted to some groups among them—the splendor of this present life—with which We test them. The provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse teaches the believer not to become envious or captivated by the temporary wealth and adornments enjoyed by others, since such possessions are a test rather than a measure of true honor. One should remain content with what God provides and seek His lasting spiritual reward, which is superior to every fleeting worldly enjoyment.

translation: Enjoin prayer upon your family and remain steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the ultimate outcome belongs to righteousness.
interpretation: A believer must establish prayer within the household with patience and perseverance, trusting that devotion is not a burden that threatens one’s worldly provision. Allah alone sustains His servants, and true success ultimately belongs to those who remain mindful of Him and steadfast in obedience.

translation: And they say, “Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?” Has there not come to them clear evidence of what was contained in the earlier scriptures?
interpretation: Their demand for a further miracle is not a sincere search for proof, because the Qur’an itself is a clear confirmation of the truths preserved in the earlier revelations. The evidence already given should be sufficient for anyone willing to recognize the continuity of God’s guidance.

translation: Had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would surely have said, “Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we might follow Your revelations before we were humbled and disgraced?”
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah’s justice: He does not punish a people before giving them clear guidance through a messenger. On the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to claim that they were condemned without warning, for divine revelation establishes the proof and leaves people responsible for how they respond to it.

translation: Say, “Everyone is waiting, so wait. Then you will know who are the people of the even path and who is rightly guided.”
interpretation: This is a warning to those who reject the truth: if they persist in waiting for the Prophet’s failure, they should wait for the outcome, for time will reveal which side truly follows the sound, upright way and possesses genuine guidance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they remain heedless and turning away.
interpretation: The verse warns that the Day of Judgment is approaching, yet many people remain absorbed in worldly distraction and deliberately avoid reflection, repentance, and preparation to meet Allah.

translation: No new reminder comes to them from their Lord without their listening to it while they are engaged in play.
interpretation: Whenever divine revelation reaches them, they receive it inattentively and frivolously rather than with seriousness and reflection, revealing their heedlessness toward the guidance of their Lord.

translation: Their hearts are distracted, and those who do wrong secretly confer: “Is this anything but a human being like you? Will you then follow magic while you can see?”
interpretation: The verse portrays the deniers as inwardly heedless of the truth while privately conspiring to dismiss the Prophet’s message. They use his human nature as an excuse for rejection and label revelation as sorcery, revealing that their objection is not sincere examination but deliberate denial despite the signs before them.

translation: He said, “My Lord knows every word spoken in heaven and on earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: Nothing said openly or secretly escapes Allah’s knowledge; He hears every utterance and fully knows its reality, intention, and consequence.

translation: Rather, they say, “A medley of dreams!” Rather, “He has fabricated it!” Rather, “He is a poet! Let him bring us a sign like those with which the earlier messengers were sent.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the deniers’ wavering accusations: unable to confront the truth of the revelation, they alternately dismiss it as confused dreams, fabrication, or poetry, then demand a miraculous sign. Their changing claims reveal not sincere investigation, but evasion and a refusal to accept the message despite its evidence.

translation: No town before them that We destroyed ever believed; will they then believe?
interpretation: The verse warns that persistent rejection of clear signs leads to destruction, and that those who follow the same defiant path should not assume they will believe merely when punishment becomes evident.

translation: We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.
interpretation: God clarifies that His messengers were human beings chosen to receive revelation, not angels. The verse also establishes that when a person lacks knowledge, they should seek guidance from those qualified and knowledgeable about the matter rather than relying on uninformed assumptions.

translation: We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: God clarifies that His messengers were human beings subject to ordinary human needs, including eating, and were not divine or everlasting in this world; their mortality affirms that ultimate permanence belongs to God alone.

translation: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, saving them and whoever We willed, and We destroyed those who exceeded all bounds.
interpretation: Allah confirms that His promise of support and deliverance to His messengers is certain: He rescues them and those whom He chooses from among the believers, while bringing ruin upon people who persistently transgress beyond every limit.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The Qur’an contains what gives humanity true dignity, guidance, and lasting remembrance through faith and obedience to God. Its revelation is therefore an invitation to reflect rationally and recognize that true honor and well-being are found by following its guidance.

translation: How many a town that was unjust have We utterly destroyed, and raised up after it another people!
interpretation: This is a warning that persistent injustice brings about decisive destruction, and that no community is indispensable: when one is removed for its wrongdoing, God can replace it with another community.

translation: Then, when they perceived Our punishment, behold, they were fleeing from it.
interpretation: When divine punishment became unmistakably present, they tried to escape, but their flight was futile; this portrays the belated realization that worldly power cannot protect those who persist in wrongdoing from God’s judgment.

translation: Do not flee; return to the luxury in which you lived and to your homes, so that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to a people fleeing from the punishment after having lived in arrogance and indulgence. They are sarcastically told to return to the comforts and positions they once enjoyed, because they will be held accountable for their disbelief, injustice, and misuse of those blessings.

translation: They said, “Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: They acknowledge with deep regret that their punishment is deserved because they had wronged themselves through disbelief and wrongdoing, realizing the truth only after it is too late to escape its consequences.

translation: And that continued to be their cry until We made them like a harvested crop, utterly still.
interpretation: Their pleas and cries persisted without avail until divine punishment reduced them to lifeless ruin, like a field cut down after harvest.

translation: We did not create the heaven and the earth and everything between them in play.
interpretation: This verse teaches that creation is not purposeless or merely an amusement. The heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them have been brought into existence with wisdom and a deliberate purpose, calling human beings to recognize their Creator and live responsibly before Him.

translation: ولو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوًا، لاتخذناه من لدنّا، إن كنّا فاعلين.
interpretation: يبين الله تعالى استحالة أن يكون خلقه لعبًا أو أنه اتخذ ولدًا أو شريكًا؛ فلو أراد الله لهوًا لكان قادرًا على أن يجعله من عنده، لكنه منزّه عن العبث واللهو، وقد خلق الخلق بالحق والحكمة.

translation: Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you attribute to God.
interpretation: The verse affirms that truth, by God’s power, decisively overcomes falsehood and exposes its weakness until it disappears. It also warns those who invent false claims about God, since such distortion cannot withstand the truth and brings them ruin.

translation: To Him belongs everyone in the heavens and the earth. Those who are with Him do not disdain worshipping Him, nor do they ever grow weary.
interpretation: All beings belong to Allah and are wholly subject to His authority. The angels, honored by their nearness to Him, neither regard His worship as beneath them nor become exhausted by it; their continual devotion demonstrates that true honor lies in obedient servitude to Allah.

translation: They glorify Him night and day, never tiring.
interpretation: The angels remain constantly devoted to Allah, praising and worshipping Him without interruption, weariness, or neglect.

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can resurrect the dead?
interpretation: The verse refutes the worship of earthly idols by challenging whether they possess any power to bring the dead back to life; true divine power belongs only to Allah, the Creator and Resurrector.

translation: Had there been gods in them besides Allah, both would surely have fallen into ruin. So glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they attribute to Him.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the ordered harmony of the heavens and the earth points to one sovereign Creator; multiple independent gods would entail conflicting wills and disorder. Allah alone governs all existence, and He is exalted above the false descriptions and partners people ascribe to Him.

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: God, as the absolute Creator and sovereign, is not subject to judgment or accountability from His creation; human beings, however, are responsible before Him for their beliefs and actions.

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, “Bring your proof.” This is the reminder for those with me and the reminder of those before me. Yet most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim that any beings besides Allah deserve worship, demanding clear evidence rather than inherited assumption. Revelation confirms the same call to worship Allah alone across all communities, but many reject this truth because of ignorance and deliberate refusal to heed it.

translation: And We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him: “There is no god but Me, so worship Me.”
interpretation: This verse establishes that the essential message of all divinely sent messengers was the oneness of God: He alone deserves worship, obedience, and ultimate devotion. Despite differences in laws and circumstances among prophets, their call was united in directing people away from all forms of associating partners with God and toward sincere worship of Him alone.

translation: And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken a son.” Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.
interpretation: The verse rejects attributing offspring to Allah, affirming His absolute transcendence and uniqueness. Those whom people associate with Him are instead created servants whom He honors; they remain completely dependent on Him and possess no share in divinity.

translation: They do not speak before He speaks, and they act according to His command.
interpretation: This describes the angels’ perfect obedience to Allah: they neither presume to speak or decide independently of Him nor deviate from what He commands.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for those with whom He is pleased; and they are apprehensive out of awe of Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah’s knowledge completely encompasses the angels and all they do, while intercession is not an independent power they possess. It occurs only by Allah’s permission and for those whose faith and deeds He approves; even the angels remain humble and fearful before His majesty.

translation: And whoever of them should say, “I am a deity besides Him,” We will repay him with Hell. Thus do We repay the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This warns that claiming divine status or sharing in God’s exclusive sovereignty is the gravest form of injustice, deserving punishment in Hell; no created being has any right to be worshipped alongside Allah.

translation: Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were once joined together, then We separated them, and We made every living thing from water? Will they not then believe?
interpretation: The verse directs people to reflect on the heavens, the earth, and the dependence of all life on water as clear signs of Allah’s deliberate creation and sustaining power; such reflection should lead them to affirm His oneness and believe rather than remain heedless.

translation: And We placed firm mountains in the earth lest it should shake with them, and We made in it broad passages as pathways, so that they may be guided.
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the earth’s ordered design: its firmly established mountains and accessible pathways are signs of His wisdom and mercy, directing people to recognize their Creator and follow the way of guidance.

translation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, yet they turn away from its signs.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the sky as a divinely maintained protection and calls people to reflect on its order and benefits; however, many disregard these evident signs instead of recognizing the Creator’s power and wisdom.

translation: And He is the One who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each moves in an orbit.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the alternation of night and day and the ordered motion of the celestial bodies are deliberate signs of God’s power and wisdom, not random occurrences.

translation: And We did not grant immortality to any human being before you. So, if you die, will they live forever?
interpretation: God reminds the Prophet that earthly life is not everlasting for anyone, including those who reject his message. Since every human being is destined to die, no one can reasonably treat the Prophet’s death as proof that falsehood will prevail or that his opponents will escape the same fate; all remain subject to God’s decree and ultimate judgment.

translation: Every soul shall taste death. We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: Human life is a temporary test: both hardship and blessing reveal the sincerity, patience, gratitude, and obedience of a person. Since everyone will ultimately return to God, worldly circumstances are not the final measure of success; what matters is how one responds to them before divine judgment.

translation: When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only as an object of ridicule: “Is this the one who speaks against your gods?” Yet they themselves reject the mention of the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse portrays the arrogant response of the disbelievers to the Prophet: instead of considering his warning, they mock him for challenging their idols. Their contradiction is exposed in that they object to criticism of their false gods while refusing to accept the remembrance and worship of Allah, the Most Merciful.

translation: Humankind was created hasty. I will show you My signs, so do not urge Me to hasten them.
interpretation: The verse rebukes humanity’s impatient nature: people demand that divine promises and warnings be fulfilled immediately, while God reveals His signs according to His wisdom and appointed time. It therefore calls people to abandon haste and trust the timing of God’s judgment and signs.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: The deniers ask this mockingly, challenging the believers about the promised judgment because they reject its certainty and demand its immediate arrival as though delay were proof that it will never occur.

translation: If only those who disbelieve knew the time when they will be unable to repel the Fire from their faces or from their backs, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who deny the truth will eventually confront the punishment without any ability to protect themselves from it or any ally capable of rescuing them; their present denial is therefore rooted in heedlessness of a certain and powerless-to-be-avoided consequence.

translation: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and leave them stunned; they will be unable to repel it, nor will they be given any respite.
interpretation: The verse warns that Allah’s punishment may arrive without warning, overwhelming those who deny the truth and leaving them powerless to avert it or obtain even a moment’s delay.

translation: Messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who ridiculed them were surrounded by what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ and warns those who mock revelation: ridicule does not diminish the truth, and the very punishment they dismiss will ultimately overtake them if they persist in denial.

translation: Say, “Who can protect you, by night and by day, from the Most Merciful?” Yet they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in rejecting God: no one can safeguard people from His decree or preserve them except Him, even though His mercy sustains them continually. Despite this constant dependence, the disbelievers respond by neglecting the reminder of their Lord instead of recognizing His mercy and turning to Him.

translation: Or do they have gods besides Us who can protect them? They cannot even help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
interpretation: إنكارٌ على المشركين اتخاذهم آلهةً يظنون أنها تدفع عنهم العذاب؛ فهذه المعبودات عاجزة عن نصرة نفسها، ولا تملك أن تمنع عن عابديها شيئًا من قهر الله أو عذابه.

translation: Rather, We have allowed these people and their forefathers to enjoy life until their lives became prolonged. Do they not see that We are gradually reducing the land from its borders? Are they then the ones who will prevail?
interpretation: The verse warns that prolonged prosperity and worldly security are not signs of lasting power. God steadily diminishes the dominion and strength of those who reject the truth—through the loss of their territory, influence, and lives—until it becomes clear that ultimate victory belongs to Him, not to them.

translation: Say, “I warn you only through revelation.” Yet the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: The Prophet’s role is to convey the warning revealed by God, while those who have become spiritually deaf refuse to benefit from it, just as a physically deaf person cannot hear a warning when it is given.

translation: And if even a breath of your Lord’s punishment were to touch them, they would surely say, “Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how even the slightest encounter with divine punishment would strip away denial and compel the wrongdoers to acknowledge their injustice. It warns that those who persistently ignore God’s signs may recognize the truth only when punishment leaves them no room for self-deception.

translation: And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth; and sufficient are We as Reckoners.
interpretation: Allah’s judgment on the Day of Resurrection will be perfectly just and exact: no deed, however small, will be overlooked or diminished, and every person will receive the consequence of what they have done.

translation: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون التوراة الفاصلة بين الحق والباطل، ونورًا يهدي، وتذكيرًا للمتقين.
interpretation: يبين الله أنه منح موسى وهارون وحيًا يجمع بين إظهار الحق وإبطال الباطل، ويضيء للناس طريق الهدى، ويوقظ قلوب أهل التقوى لتتذكر عهد الله وتلتزم بأوامره.

translation: Those who fear their Lord without seeing Him, and who are apprehensive of the Hour.
interpretation: This describes sincere believers whose reverence for God is rooted in inner faith rather than direct sight or worldly compulsion; their awareness of the coming Judgment makes them vigilant, humble, and careful in how they live.

translation: And this is a blessed Reminder that We have sent down. Will you then deny it?
interpretation: The Qur’an is described as blessed because it brings enduring guidance, goodness, and spiritual benefit to those who follow it. Since it has been revealed by God as a reminder and proof, the verse rebukes those who reject it despite its clear source and guidance.

translation: And indeed, We had granted Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were well aware of him.
interpretation: Allah had already bestowed upon Abraham the insight and wisdom to recognize the truth before his people’s rejection of it became manifest. This guidance was not accidental; Allah knew Abraham’s sincerity, readiness, and inner qualities, and chose him to stand against false worship with clear understanding.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are devoted?”
interpretation: Abraham was challenging the unquestioned religious practice of his father and people. By asking what these statues were, he exposed the weakness of directing devotion toward lifeless objects that could neither hear, benefit, nor harm, urging them to reconsider inherited beliefs through reason and recognize that worship belongs only to Allah.

translation: They said, “We found our forefathers worshipping them.”
interpretation: They defended their idolatry by appealing to ancestral tradition, treating the practices of their forefathers as sufficient proof rather than seeking the truth through reason and revelation.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you and your forefathers have been in clear error.”
interpretation: Ibrahim condemns the worship of idols practiced by his people and their ancestors, making clear that inherited beliefs are not necessarily true and that following them blindly can lead to obvious misguidance.

translation: They said, “Have you come to us with the truth, or are you merely jesting?”
interpretation: They questioned Abraham with doubt and sarcasm, asking whether his call to abandon their idols was a serious declaration of truth or only a playful claim, revealing their refusal to recognize the certainty of his message.

translation: He said, “Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am one of those who bear witness to that.”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm rejects the false assumption that the idols deserve worship and declares that true lordship belongs exclusively to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. His statement is a confident testimony grounded in the manifest signs of creation, affirming that worship must be directed to the One who brought all things into existence.

translation: By Allah, I will surely devise a plan against your idols after you have turned away and gone.
interpretation: Abraham swore to challenge and expose the idols’ powerlessness once their worshippers had left, demonstrating that objects unable to protect themselves could not deserve worship.

translation: So he reduced them to fragments, except for the largest of them, so that perhaps they would return to it.
interpretation: Abraham shattered the idols while leaving the largest one intact so that his people would confront the absurdity of seeking help from powerless statues and recognize that none of them could deserve worship.

translation: قالوا: «من فعل هذا بآلهتنا؟ إنه لمن الظالمين».
interpretation: يكشف قولهم عن إنكارهم الشديد لتحطيم أصنامهم، إذ عدّوا من اعتدى عليها ظالمًا، مع غفلتهم عن أن تلك الأصنام لا تملك نفعًا ولا ضرًّا ولا تستحق العبادة.

translation: They said, “We heard a young man speaking about them; he is called Abraham.”
interpretation: The people identified Abraham as the young man who had been challenging and condemning the worship of their idols.

translation: They said, “Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may bear witness.”
interpretation: They decided to bring Abraham before the gathered people publicly, intending for everyone to witness the accusation against him and the proceedings that would follow.

translation: They said, “Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?”
interpretation: They confronted Abraham with an accusatory question, recognizing that he had challenged their idolatry by breaking the idols, while treating those powerless objects as worthy of worship.

translation: He said, “Rather, this largest of them did it, so ask them, if they are able to speak.”
interpretation: Abraham said this as a rhetorical challenge to expose the idols’ powerlessness: if they could truly act as gods, they should be able to speak and identify what happened. His statement directed the people to recognize the absurdity of worshipping objects unable to benefit, harm, or even communicate.

translation: So they turned to one another and said, “Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: When confronted with the truth of their powerless idols, they briefly reflected and recognized that their own worship of them was the real injustice.

translation: Then they lowered their heads in shame and said, “You certainly know that these do not speak.”
interpretation: Their response reveals that they recognized the idols’ inability to speak or defend themselves, yet their shame led them to retreat rather than accept the truth and abandon their false worship.

translation: He said, “Do you worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you in any way nor harm you?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke of attributing worship to powerless beings: true worship belongs only to Allah, because no created object possesses independent power to bring benefit or avert harm.

translation: Fie upon you and upon what you worship besides Allah! Will you not then use your reason?
interpretation: This is a forceful condemnation of idolatry: Ibrahim rejects both the idols and the false devotion directed toward them, challenging his people to abandon inherited beliefs and recognize through sound reason that only Allah deserves worship.

translation: They said, “Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to do anything.”
interpretation: Those who rejected Abraham’s message resorted to violence when they could not answer his challenge, seeking to defend their false gods and preserve their authority. Their words reveal the weakness of falsehood: instead of responding with truth and evidence, they attempted to silence its caller through destruction.

translation: We said, “O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.”
interpretation: يُبيّن الله تعالى أن النار لا تعمل بذاتها، بل بأمره؛ فلما أراد نجاة إبراهيم جعلها بردًا وسلامًا عليه، فحفظه من أذاها وأظهر قدرته المطلقة على تسخير الأسباب ونقض آثارها.

translation: They plotted against him, but We made them the greatest losers.
interpretation: Those who sought to harm Abraham were ultimately defeated by God’s power: their scheme not only failed, but turned into loss and humiliation for them, while Abraham was protected and vindicated.

translation: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all peoples.
interpretation: Allah rescued Abraham and Lot from the oppression of their people and guided them to the blessed land of the Levant, a place from which goodness, revelation, and guidance would spread to humanity.

translation: And We granted him Isaac, and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made them both righteous.
interpretation: God blessed Abraham beyond what he had asked or expected by granting him Isaac and then Jacob, extending the blessing through his descendants. Both were guided to righteousness and made worthy of carrying forward Abraham’s faithful legacy.

translation: And We made them leaders who guided by Our command, and We inspired them to do good deeds, establish prayer, and give zakāh; and they were devoted worshippers of Us.
interpretation: This verse shows that true leadership is a divine trust: those chosen to guide others must themselves submit to God, respond to His guidance, and embody righteous action. Their guidance was not based on personal authority, but on obedience to God’s command, expressed through good deeds, prayer, charity, and sincere worship.

translation: And Lot—we granted him sound judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town whose people committed vile deeds. Indeed, they were an evil, defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: Allah bestowed upon Lot wisdom to discern truth and knowledge to guide his people, then rescued him from a society whose corruption had become deeply rooted. Their punishment was not merely for isolated sins, but for persistent, arrogant rebellion against moral and divine boundaries; this teaches that steadfastness in faith may require separation from an environment that normalizes wrongdoing.

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed, he was among the righteous.
interpretation: Allah granted him special protection, compassion, and favor because his faith and conduct placed him among those devoted to righteousness.

translation: And Noah, when he called out before that, We answered him, and We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse presents Noah’s supplication as an example of sincere appeal to God: when he called upon Him in the midst of overwhelming hardship, God answered by rescuing him and his believing household from the devastating trial of the flood. It affirms that divine deliverance comes through God’s response to genuine faith and reliance upon Him.

translation: And We supported him against the people who rejected Our signs. Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: God granted His faithful servant protection and victory over a people who persistently denied His revelation. Their destruction was the consequence of deliberate, collective wrongdoing and rejection of the truth, while the verse affirms that divine justice ultimately prevails over entrenched evil.

translation: And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the people’s sheep had wandered by night—and We were witnesses to their judgment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates that even righteous rulers may exercise differing judgments in a dispute, while God remains fully aware of their deliberation and guides them toward justice and sound judgment.

translation: So We gave Solomon understanding of it, and to each of them We granted judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains and the birds with David, glorifying [Us]; and We were the Doers.
interpretation: This verse shows that God grants different levels of insight and understanding according to His wisdom: Solomon was given a deeper understanding in that particular case, while David also possessed sound judgment and knowledge. It also displays God’s power in granting David the extraordinary favor that the mountains and birds joined him in glorifying God, demonstrating that all creation responds to its Creator in ways beyond ordinary human perception.

translation: And We taught him the craft of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. Will you then be grateful?
interpretation: Allah reminds people that even the knowledge and skills by which they protect themselves in conflict are gifts from Him, illustrated by His teaching David the making of armor. Such blessings should lead them to recognize Allah’s favor, use their abilities responsibly, and respond with sincere gratitude rather than pride or heedlessness.

translation: And for Solomon We subjected the stormy wind, which sailed by his command to the land We had blessed; and We are Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse portrays Solomon’s extraordinary authority as a gift granted by God: even the powerful wind was made obedient to his command and carried him toward the blessed land. It also emphasizes that such miracles occur only through God’s knowledge and permission, for He fully knows every matter.

translation: And among the devils were those who dived for him and carried out other work besides that; and We were watching over them.
interpretation: This indicates that Allah subjected certain jinn to Solomon, enabling them to perform extraordinary tasks such as diving and other works, while Allah remained in complete control of them and protected Solomon from their harm or disobedience.

translation: And [mention] Job, when he called upon his Lord, “Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
interpretation: Job’s supplication expresses humble reliance upon God: he presents his suffering without complaint or demand, while affirming that God’s mercy surpasses all mercy. The verse teaches that in hardship one may turn to God with trust, recognizing one’s need and leaving the manner and time of relief to His compassion.

translation: So We answered his prayer, removed the affliction that had afflicted him, restored to him his family, and gave him the like of them along with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that Allah responds to sincere supplication and can transform prolonged suffering into mercy and restoration. The relief granted to Job was not merely a reward for enduring hardship, but also a sign for those devoted to worship: affliction does not mean abandonment by Allah, and steadfastness, trust, and turning to Him remain meaningful even when relief is delayed.

translation: And Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl—all were among the patient.
interpretation: This verse presents Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl as exemplary servants of God whose steadfast patience enabled them to remain faithful and endure hardship. Their mention teaches that patience is a mark of righteousness and a quality honored by God.

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed, they were among the righteous.
interpretation: Allah granted them His special mercy and protection because they were devoted to righteousness, showing that true moral obedience is a means through which divine mercy is received.

translation: And [mention] Dhū al-Nūn, when he departed in anger, thinking that We would not constrain him. Then he cried out in the depths of darkness: “There is no deity except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.”
interpretation: Prophet Jonah departed from his people before receiving permission, distressed and displeased with their rejection, and came to realize that no matter how difficult his situation became, God’s authority and decree encompassed him. In the darkness, he confessed God’s absolute perfection, acknowledged his own error, and turned to Him with sincere repentance; thus the verse teaches that deliverance begins with recognizing God’s oneness and humbly admitting one’s fault.

translation: So We answered his prayer and delivered him from distress; and thus We save the believers.
interpretation: Allah assures those who turn to Him sincerely that He can remove their deepest anguish and grant them deliverance, just as He rescued Jonah; this promise calls believers to maintain hope and seek His help in hardship.

translation: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called upon his Lord: “My Lord, do not leave me without an heir, though You are the best of inheritors.”
interpretation: Zakariya turns to Allah in humble dependence, asking not to be left without a righteous successor to carry on his mission and preserve the good he has served, while affirming that Allah alone is the ultimate guardian and inheritor of all things.

translation: So We answered him, and granted him John, and made his wife fit for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to do good deeds, and they called upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us.
interpretation: Allah accepted Zakariyya’s supplication and restored his family life, showing that sincere prayer is answered by His wisdom. The verse presents the prophets’ devotion as a model: they actively hastened toward righteous deeds, sought Allah with hope in His mercy and fear of His displeasure, and maintained a heart of genuine humility before Him.

translation: And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for all the worlds.
interpretation: Maryam’s purity and the miraculous creation of Jesus demonstrate that Allah’s power transcends ordinary causes: He brings about life by His command and makes this mother and son a universal sign of His majesty and ability.

translation: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: Humanity’s true religious foundation is the unity of God and the unity of the community that submits to Him. Since Allah alone is the Lord and source of guidance, worship must be directed exclusively to Him, and believers should not allow differences to sever the bond of faith and obedience.

translation: But they divided their affair among themselves; all will return to Us.
interpretation: Although people divide into conflicting groups and follow different paths, their ultimate return is to Allah, who will judge them all with perfect justice.

translation: So whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer—his efforts will not be denied, and We are recording them for him.
interpretation: True faith gives righteous action lasting value before God: no sincere deed is overlooked or lost, because every effort is preserved and will be accounted for with perfect justice.

translation: It is forbidden for a town We have destroyed that its people should ever return.
interpretation: Allah declares that a people destroyed for persistent disbelief will not be restored to worldly life or granted another opportunity to repent after destruction; His decree concerning them is final until the appointed Resurrection.

translation: Until, when Gog and Magog are released, they will swarm down from every elevation.
interpretation: This portrays the release of Gog and Magog as a moment of overwhelming upheaval near the end of history: they will pour forth rapidly from every direction, signifying the approach of God’s promised judgment.

translation: And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved are transfixed in horror: “Woe to us! We were heedless of this; indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: When the promised Resurrection and Judgment become imminent, those who denied them will be overwhelmed by terror and forced to recognize the truth they had ignored. Their confession shows that their loss resulted not from lack of warning, but from heedlessness and deliberate injustice toward themselves by rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, you and whatever you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will enter it.
interpretation: The verse warns those who worship other than Allah that their false objects of worship cannot save them, and that both the worshippers and what they worship will be associated with Hell as a consequence of directing worship away from Allah.

translation: Had these been gods, they would not have entered it; yet all will abide therein.
interpretation: The verse exposes the falsehood of treating created beings or idols as divine: true gods would possess power over the Fire and could not be subjected to it. Their entry into it demonstrates their helplessness and the baselessness of worshipping them.

translation: They will have groaning in it, and there they will not hear.
interpretation: This portrays the inhabitants of Hell overwhelmed by anguish: their painful groans fill it, while they are deprived of hearing anything that could comfort, benefit, or relieve them.

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already been decreed by Us will be kept far away from it.
interpretation: Those whom Allah has honored with His prior promise of goodness will be protected from Hell and will not come near it, as a manifestation of His mercy and fulfillment of His promise to the righteous.

translation: They will not hear even the faintest sound of it, and they will abide forever in whatever their souls desire.
interpretation: Those granted Paradise will be completely shielded from Hell—its terror will not reach them even as a sound—and their joy will remain enduringly fulfilled, without fear of loss or interruption.

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, “This is your Day which you were promised.”
interpretation: Those who were faithful and steadfast will be protected from the distress of the Day of Resurrection; instead, the angels will welcome them with reassurance, confirming that the promised Day of reward has arrived.

translation: On the Day We will fold up the heaven like the folding of a scroll for the records. Just as We began the first creation, We will bring it back again—a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever able to do so.
interpretation: The verse portrays the certainty and ease of the Resurrection: the ordered universe will be brought to its appointed end, and God will recreate all beings just as He originated them, fulfilling a promise that cannot fail.

translation: And We have certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: Allah has decreed that ultimate stewardship and inheritance of the earth belong to those who are righteous—those who remain faithful to Him and uphold justice and goodness. Their eventual ascendancy is a divine promise, not merely the result of worldly power.

translation: Indeed, in this is a sufficient message for people who worship.
interpretation: This revelation contains all the guidance and admonition needed by those devoted to Allah, because their sincere worship makes them receptive to its truth and willing to follow it.

translation: We have not sent you, O Muhammad, except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: Allah sent the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as a mercy extending to all creation: through his guidance, compassionate example, and message of justice and worship, people are shown the path to faith, moral goodness, and salvation. This mercy is realized by those who accept and follow his guidance, while his mission also brought benefit and protection more broadly to the world.

translation: Say, “It is only revealed to me that your God is One God; will you then submit?”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to make clear that the essence of the revelation is the oneness of God, leaving people to respond through sincere submission and obedience rather than merely acknowledging this truth intellectually.

translation: But if they turn away, say, “I have warned you all equally, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.”
interpretation: If they reject the message, the Prophet is to declare that he has conveyed the warning openly and impartially to everyone. The timing of the promised judgment is known only to God, whether it comes soon or after a long delay.

translation: Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly, and He knows what you conceal.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses every word uttered publicly and every matter hidden within the hearts, so nothing can be concealed from Him.

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a delayed matter may be a test rather than a sign of approval, and that worldly enjoyment is temporary; therefore, people should respond with patience, awareness, and preparation for accountability before God.

translation: He said, “My Lord, judge with truth. Our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you describe.”
interpretation: The Prophet entrusts the dispute to Allah’s perfectly just judgment, affirming that only His mercy and help can overcome the false claims and accusations made against the truth.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O humankind, be mindful of your Lord; indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This is a universal call to live in reverent awareness of Allah, because the upheaval accompanying the Day of Resurrection will be so overwhelming that nothing can compare with it. Awareness of that inevitable reality should awaken people from heedlessness and lead them to obedience, repentance, and moral responsibility before they stand before their Lord.

translation: On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from the child she nurses, every pregnant woman will miscarry her burden, and you will see people as though intoxicated, though they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse portrays the overwhelming terror of the Resurrection: its reality will be so powerful that even the deepest instinctive bonds and the composure of people will be eclipsed. Their apparent staggering is not caused by wine, but by the sheer shock and fear of witnessing Allah’s severe judgment.

translation: Among people are those who argue about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This condemns speaking about Allah on the basis of ignorance and allowing one’s beliefs and arguments to be shaped by forces that defy the truth. Genuine understanding requires sound knowledge and resistance to misleading influences rather than arrogant disputation.

translation: It has been decreed concerning him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will lead him astray and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns that the rebellious tempter has been destined to mislead those who follow and obey him, gradually drawing them away from truth until their path ends in the punishment of Hellfire.

translation: O humanity, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, so that We may make clear to you. We settle in the wombs whatever We will for an appointed term; then We bring you forth as infants, then let you reach your full strength. Some of you are taken in death, and some are returned to the weakest stage of life so that, after having known, they know nothing. You see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs, swells, and produces every delightful kind of plant.
interpretation: The verse establishes the certainty of resurrection by directing attention to the successive stages of human creation and the revival of barren earth. One who brought humanity from dust, developed life in the womb, and restores the dead earth possesses the power to recreate people after death. The changing stages of human life also reveal that existence is governed by God’s deliberate wisdom, while human weakness and the loss of knowledge remind people that their life and abilities are temporary and entirely dependent on Him.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, that He gives life to the dead, and that He is capable of all things.
interpretation: Everything described is grounded in Allah’s absolute reality and truth: since He alone possesses unlimited power, bringing the dead back to life is fully within His ability, just as all other acts of creation and transformation are.

translation: And indeed, the Hour is coming—there is no doubt about it—and indeed, Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty of the Day of Resurrection: the final Hour will inevitably arrive, and God will bring the dead back to life for judgment. It calls people to live with awareness of their accountability before Him, since death is not the end but a passage to the divinely appointed reckoning.

translation: And among the people are those who argue about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or an illuminating Book.
interpretation: This condemns disputing about God while lacking sound knowledge, divine guidance, or revealed evidence. Such argument is driven by conjecture and arrogance rather than a sincere search for truth, and therefore has no valid foundation.

translation: He turns his neck away in arrogance to lead others astray from the path of Allah. For him is disgrace in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection We will make him taste the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse portrays the arrogant person who rejects divine guidance and tries to divert others from it. His pride brings humiliation in this life, while his deliberate misguidance and opposition to Allah’s way lead to the severe punishment of the Hereafter.

translation: ذلك بسبب ما قدّمت يداك، وأن الله ليس بظالمٍ للعبيد.
interpretation: ما ينزل بالإنسان من جزاءٍ أو عاقبةٍ إنما يكون نتيجةً لما اختاره وعمله، والله منزّه عن ظلم أحد؛ فلا يعاقب بغير حق ولا ينقص أحدًا شيئًا من جزائه.

translation: And among the people is one who worships Allah on the edge: if good befalls him, he is reassured by it; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter; that is the clear loss.
interpretation: This verse portrays the person whose faith is conditional and unstable: he worships Allah while expecting worldly comfort, but abandons devotion when tested by hardship. Such a person has not surrendered sincerely to Allah; therefore, by turning away during trials, he loses both the worldly steadiness and honor that come through faith and the everlasting reward of the Hereafter.

translation: He calls upon, besides Allah, that which can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the farthest error.
interpretation: This describes the profound misguidance of directing worship and supplication to powerless beings instead of Allah, since they possess no ability to bring benefit or avert harm; true reliance and worship therefore belong solely to Allah.

translation: He invokes one whose harm is closer than his benefit. Truly evil is such a protector, and truly evil is such a companion.
interpretation: This describes the one who turns to a false deity or helpless being for aid, though that being is more likely to bring loss—through misguidance and disappointment—than any real benefit. Such a supposed protector is utterly worthless, and relying on it is a miserable companionship.

translation: Indeed, Allah admits those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: Allah promises the believers who live by righteous action an eternal reward in Paradise, while affirming that His decree and power are absolute: He grants, judges, and governs all things according to His perfect will and wisdom.

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the sky and then cut it off; then let him see whether his scheme can remove what enrages him.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who resent Allah’s support for His Messenger and imagine that they can prevent or end it. It challenges their frustration by portraying a desperate, self-defeating attempt to sever the connection between divine help and its recipient: no human scheme can stop what Allah has decreed. The passage also teaches that resentment does not alter divine judgment; whoever cannot accept Allah’s support will only harm himself through futile opposition.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as clear verses, and indeed Allah guides whom He wills.
