interpretation: The Qur’an has been revealed with clear signs and meanings so that the truth may be recognized; yet benefiting from its guidance ultimately depends on Allah’s granting guidance to those who sincerely turn toward it.

translation: Indeed, those who believe, those who are Jews, the Sabians, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associate partners with Allah—Allah will decide between them on the Day of Resurrection. Surely Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse entrusts the final judgment of all religious communities to Allah alone. He will distinguish truth from falsehood and render each person the judgment they deserve, for nothing about their beliefs, deeds, or sincerity is hidden from His complete knowledge and witness.

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrate all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth, as well as the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the creatures—and many of humankind? Yet many are deserving of punishment. And whoever Allah disgraces, none can honor. Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the entire universe is subject to Allah’s authority: every created thing submits to Him according to its nature, while human beings are distinguished by their choice to obey or resist. Those who willingly submit share in true honor, whereas those who reject Allah’s authority bring upon themselves humiliation that no worldly status can undo; Allah’s will alone determines honor, disgrace, and judgment.

translation: These are two adversaries who dispute about their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and scalding water will be poured over their heads.
interpretation: The verse depicts the ultimate consequence of rejecting God: the very punishment surrounding the disbelievers becomes an inescapable garment, while boiling water poured over their heads conveys the intensity and totality of their torment. Their dispute with the truth is therefore not a matter without consequence, but one that culminates in decisive divine judgment.

translation: By it will be melted whatever is in their bellies and their skins.
interpretation: This describes the intense torment of Hell: the scalding substance is so extraordinarily hot that it dissolves the internal organs and burns through the skin, conveying the severity and inescapability of the punishment.

translation: And for them are maces of iron.
interpretation: This depicts the severe and terrifying punishment prepared for those who reject the truth, emphasizing the force and humiliation of their chastisement in Hell.

translation: Whenever they try to escape from it in anguish, they will be returned to it, and it will be said to them, “Taste the punishment of the Burning.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter hopelessness of those who reject God: every attempt to escape the torment of Hell is thwarted, and their suffering continues without relief, as a consequence of their persistent defiance.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse conveys that sincere faith, demonstrated through righteous action, leads by Allah’s grace to everlasting bliss. The gardens, flowing rivers, precious adornments, and silk clothing represent honour, beauty, purity, and complete comfort in the Hereafter—rewards that contrast with the limitations and hardships of worldly life.

translation: And they were guided to wholesome speech, and guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Those whom God honors are granted both the ability to speak words of faith, truth, and goodness and the guidance to follow the straight way that leads to Him, the One deserving of all praise.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder people from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque—which We have made for all people, where its resident and visitor are equal—and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns disbelief and any attempt to obstruct people from worshipping Allah or reaching the Sacred Mosque, emphasizing that access to it is a shared right for those who remain there and those who visit. Because of its sanctity, even a deliberate intention to commit injustice or deviate from righteousness there is treated as a grave offense deserving painful punishment.

translation: وإذ بيَّنّا لإبراهيم موضع البيت الحرام ووطَّأنا له مكانه، قلنا: لا تُشرك بي شيئًا، وطهِّر بيتي للطائفين حوله، والقائمين للصلاة، والراكعين الساجدين.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الكعبة موضعٌ أسّسه الله لعبادته الخالصة، وأمر إبراهيم عليه السلام بتطهيره من الشرك والنجاسات وكل ما ينافي حرمته، ليكون مكانًا يتقرب فيه الناس إلى الله بالطواف والصلاة والخضوع، وأن حقيقة تعظيم البيت لا تكون إلا بتوحيد الله وإخلاص العبادة له.

translation: And proclaim to humanity the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant mountain pass.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the pilgrimage is a universal call from God, inviting people to leave behind comfort and undertake a sincere journey toward Him. Their coming on foot or through arduous travel reflects devotion, humility, and readiness to endure hardship in response to that sacred summons.

translation: So that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on appointed days over the livestock He has provided for them. So eat from them and feed the distressed poor.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the rites of pilgrimage bring both spiritual and worldly benefits: believers gather to worship Allah, remember Him while offering the animals He has provided, and show gratitude by eating from the sacrifice and sharing it with those in hardship. Worship is therefore joined with remembrance, gratitude, and care for the poor.

translation: Then let them complete their prescribed rites, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House.
interpretation: After completing the essential acts of pilgrimage, pilgrims should cleanse and groom themselves, fulfill any vows made for God, and perform the circumambulation of the Kaʿbah, the ancient sanctuary established for His worship.

translation: That is so. Whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah—it is better for him in the sight of his Lord. Livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you; so keep away from the impurity of idols and avoid false speech.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true reverence for Allah is shown by respecting everything He has declared sacred, obeying His limits, and avoiding what He has prohibited. Though animals are generally lawful as food, the exceptions established by revelation must be observed. Idolatry and false speech are especially condemned because they corrupt faith and undermine truth, justice, and sincere devotion to Allah.

translation: Devoted exclusively to Allah, without associating anything with Him. Whoever associates partners with Allah is like one who falls from the sky, then birds snatch him away, or the wind carries him to a distant place.
interpretation: True devotion requires sincere affirmation of Allah’s oneness. Shirk tears a person away from spiritual security and leaves him exposed to confusion and destruction, just as someone falling from the sky is scattered and carried far from safety.

translation: That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah—indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: Reverence for the rites and sacred signs established by Allah is not merely an outward act; it reflects a heart filled with sincere awareness of Him and devotion to His commands.

translation: For you there are benefits in them until an appointed time; then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.
interpretation: The sacrificial animals designated for Allah may provide people with lawful benefits—such as riding, milk, and other uses—until the time appointed for sacrifice arrives, after which they are brought to the Sacred House, the Kaʿbah, to be offered in worship to Allah.

translation: For every community We have appointed a rite so that they may mention the name of Allah over the livestock He has provided for them. Your God is One, so submit to Him. And give glad tidings to the humble-hearted.
interpretation: Although religious communities may differ in their prescribed rites, their true purpose is one: to remember Allah, recognize that all provision comes from Him, and worship Him alone. Therefore, sincere faith requires surrendering oneself to the One God, while the humble-hearted—those whose hearts are softened by His remembrance and who accept His guidance—are promised good news.

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble; those who patiently endure whatever befalls them; those who establish prayer; and who spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: True believers are marked by reverent awareness of Allah that moves their hearts, steadfastness through trials, faithful observance of prayer, and generosity from the blessings entrusted to them. Their inner awe is expressed through patience, worship, and selfless giving.

translation: And the sacrificial animals—we have made them among the symbols of Allah for you; in them is good for you. So mention the name of Allah over them as they stand in rows. Then, when they fall on their sides, eat from them and feed the contented poor and the needy who ask. Thus We have subjected them to you so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: Allah teaches that sacrificial animals are sacred signs of devotion, yet He has made them beneficial and accessible to people. Believers should invoke His name over them, partake of their meat after the sacrifice, and share it with both the poor who preserve their dignity and those who openly seek help. The true purpose of this provision is gratitude: recognizing Allah’s generosity and expressing it through worship, humility, and care for others.

translation: Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah; rather, it is your God-consciousness that reaches Him. Thus He has subjected them to you so that you may glorify Allah for guiding you. And give glad tidings to those who do good.
interpretation: Allah does not benefit from the physical offering itself; what is accepted is the sincere devotion, obedience, and reverence behind it. The animals are made available as a means for believers to express gratitude and magnify Allah for His guidance, while those who offer their worship and conduct with excellence are promised good news.

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Surely Allah does not love anyone treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: Allah assures sincere believers that He protects and supports them against hostility and injustice in the ways He knows best, while making clear that His support is not for those who betray trusts, persist in treachery, and deny His blessings.

translation: Permission to fight has been given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged. Indeed, Allah is fully capable of granting them victory.
interpretation: This verse establishes that fighting is permitted as a response to persecution and injustice, not as a means of aggression or oppression. It reassures the wronged that their victory ultimately depends on Allah, whose power is absolute.

translation: Those who were expelled from their homes unjustly, for no reason other than their saying, “Our Lord is Allah.” Had Allah not restrained some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques—places in which Allah’s name is mentioned often—would surely have been destroyed. Allah will certainly support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: The verse affirms the innocence of those persecuted for their faith and establishes that resisting oppression protects not only Muslims but all places devoted to the worship of God. Supporting Allah means upholding truth, justice, and the freedom to worship, and those who undertake this cause can rely on His strength and ultimate victory.

translation: Those who, when We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.
interpretation: This describes the qualities of people whom God grants authority: they use their position not for personal dominance, but to worship Him, fulfill social responsibilities, promote righteousness, and restrain wrongdoing. The ultimate outcome of every affair remains with God, reminding them that their power is a trust and that their success and accountability are ultimately in His hands.

translation: And if they deny you, then before them the people of Noah, ʿĀd, and Thamūd also denied.
interpretation: Do not be distressed by the denial of your people: rejection of a messenger is not something unprecedented. Earlier nations likewise denied their prophets, yet their denial did not invalidate the truth or save them from its consequences. This verse therefore consoles the Messenger and warns those who reject him that persistent denial follows a pattern already seen in past communities.

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot,
interpretation: This phrase refers to the communities of Abraham and Lot as peoples known through their prophets, evoking the lessons of their response to divine guidance and warning.

translation: And the people of Midian [were also destroyed], and Moses was denied. I granted the disbelievers respite, then seized them; so how severe was My reproach and punishment!
interpretation: The verse warns that denying God’s messengers does not mean escaping accountability. God may grant the disbelievers time, but when His judgment comes, it is decisive and reveals the grave consequence of persistent rejection.

translation: How many a town have We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so that it lies in ruins upon its foundations, and how many a well has been abandoned and a lofty palace left empty.
interpretation: This portrays the fate of communities that persisted in injustice: their power and prosperity could not protect them from destruction. The collapsed dwellings, deserted wells, and empty palaces stand as enduring signs that worldly grandeur is worthless when it is built upon wrongdoing and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land, so that they may have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For it is not the eyes that become blind, but the hearts within the chests that become blind.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true insight is not merely physical sight or hearing; it is the heart’s willingness to reflect, recognize truth, and learn from the signs found in history and the world. A person may possess sound senses yet remain spiritually blind when the heart refuses understanding.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will never fail in His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those you count.
interpretation: The delay of punishment is not a breach of God’s promise; it unfolds according to His perfect wisdom and decree, not according to human impatience. What people experience as a long period is, in relation to God’s judgment, insignificant, so they should not mistake postponement for escape.

translation: How many a town have I given respite while it was committing ظلم, then seized it; and to Me is the final return.
interpretation: The verse warns that God’s delaying punishment is not approval or safety for wrongdoing. When a community persists in injustice, it may be granted time to repent, but eventual accountability is certain, and all will return to God for judgment.

translation: Say, “O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you.”
interpretation: يأمر الله نبيه أن يبيّن للناس أن مهمته هي إنذارهم بوضوح من عواقب الكفر والمعصية، وإقامة الحجة عليهم، أما الهداية القلبية والحساب فبيد الله وحده.

translation: So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a generous provision.
interpretation: True faith is shown through righteous action; those who live by it are promised that Allah will pardon their sins and grant them an honorable, abundant reward, especially in the Hereafter.

translation: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك أصحاب الجحيم: أما الذين جاهدوا لإبطال آياتنا، ظانّين أنهم سيعجزوننا ويفلتون من جزائنا، فأولئك ملازمو الجحيم.
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن مقاومة الحق والتشكيك في آيات الله، مع الغرور بالقدرة على الإفلات من حسابه، ليست مجرد خطأ فكري، بل موقف متعمد يستوجب العذاب؛ لأن صاحبه يعاند دلائل الله ويصدّ عنها.

translation: We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that, when he recited, Satan cast something into his recitation. But Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah firmly establishes His verses. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Whenever a messenger conveys divine revelation, Satan may attempt to confuse people by introducing falsehood or casting doubts around it; yet Allah removes that interference and preserves the truth of His revelation, establishing His verses with perfect knowledge and wisdom.

translation: So that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those whose hearts contain disease and those whose hearts are hardened. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in deep opposition.
interpretation: God permits Satan’s whisperings to become a test: those whose faith is corrupted or whose hearts have hardened are inclined to accept them, while the wrongdoers thereby become increasingly distant from the truth and entrenched in opposition.

translation: And so that those who have been granted knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, and thus believe in it, and their hearts humble themselves before it. Indeed, Allah guides those who believe to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah allows the truth to become unmistakable to people of sincere understanding, so their knowledge leads them to faith and their hearts submit humbly to revelation. Those who believe and respond with such humility are guided by Allah toward the straight path.

translation: And those who disbelieve will continue to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day.
interpretation: Those who reject the truth will remain trapped in uncertainty and doubt until divine judgment overtakes them without warning, or until they face a devastating day from which no relief, escape, or benefit can come. Their delay in believing does not weaken the truth; it only postpones their recognition until recognition is of no avail.

translation: On that Day, sovereignty belongs to Allah; He will judge between them. Those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in gardens of bliss.
interpretation: The verse affirms that on the Day of Judgment all authority and final judgment belong exclusively to Allah. True faith is demonstrated through righteous action, and those who unite both will receive lasting happiness and reward in Paradise.

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: Those who knowingly reject faith and treat God’s revealed signs as false will face a punishment that not only causes suffering but also strips them of honor, as a fitting consequence of their arrogance and denial of the truth.

translation: And those who emigrated in the cause of Allah, then were killed or died—Allah will surely provide them with a good provision. Indeed, Allah is truly the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse consoles and honors those who leave their homes for Allah’s sake, affirming that neither martyrdom nor death causes their sacrifice to be lost; Allah will grant them a pure and lasting reward beyond what worldly means can provide.

translation: He will surely admit them to a place of entry with which they will be pleased. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: Allah knows perfectly the sincerity, sacrifices, and hardships of those who obey Him, and in His forbearance He does not hasten to punish; rather, He assures them that their patience and devotion will lead to a blessed abode that fully satisfies them.

translation: That is so. Whoever responds with the equivalent of what was inflicted upon him, and is then wronged again, Allah will surely help him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse permits a person who has been wronged to seek proportionate redress, but not to exceed the harm suffered. If the aggressor persists in wrongdoing, Allah promises support to the oppressed, while affirming that forgiveness and restraint remain noble qualities reflected in His own pardon and forgiveness.

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: The gradual interweaving and changing of night and day manifests Allah’s power to govern creation with perfect order. Nothing escapes His hearing or sight, including every event and every deed carried out within this ordered world.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This establishes that Allah alone possesses ultimate and absolute reality, authority, and worthiness of worship. Everything invoked besides Him is powerless and baseless, while His exaltedness and greatness surpass all comparison.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and then the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.
interpretation: The renewal of the earth through rain is a visible sign of Allah’s gentle, precise care and complete knowledge: He brings life and beauty from seemingly lifeless soil according to His wise order.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, Allah is truly the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Everything in existence belongs to Allah and depends entirely upon Him, while He is independent of all creation and possesses every perfection for which He deserves constant praise.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth, and the ships sail through the sea by His command? And He keeps the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Most Kind and Most Merciful to people.
interpretation: The verse directs human attention to Allah’s sustaining power and mercy: He has made the earth and its means of travel serviceable to people, while preserving the ordered structure of the heavens. These blessings are not independent or accidental; they continue only by His command, revealing both His absolute authority and His compassionate care for humanity.

translation: وهو الذي أحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم؛ إن الإنسان لكفور.
interpretation: يذكّر الله الإنسان بأن حياته وموته وبعثه كلها بقدرته وحده، فكما أنشأه أول مرة بعد أن لم يكن، فهو قادر على إحيائه بعد الموت للحساب. ومع وضوح هذه الآية، يميل الإنسان إلى جحود نعم الله وإنكار قدرته على البعث.

translation: For every community We have appointed a rite which they perform. So let them not dispute with you concerning this matter. Call to your Lord; indeed, you are upon straight guidance.
interpretation: Allah affirms that every community was given its own prescribed acts of worship and directs the Prophet not to be unsettled by those who dispute over them. He is to remain devoted to calling people to his Lord, confident that the revelation and path he follows are true, upright, and leading to Him.

translation: And if they argue with you, say, “Allah knows best what you do.”
interpretation: When confronted with stubborn dispute, the believer should avoid fruitless argument and entrust the truth and the judgment of people’s deeds to Allah, whose knowledge is complete and whose judgment is perfectly just.

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: The verse entrusts all disputes in belief and religious truth to Allah’s perfect judgment on the Day of Resurrection, when He will distinguish what was true from what was false and reward or hold accountable each person according to their response to the truth.

translation: ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم ما في السماء والأرض ۗ إن ذلك في كتاب ۚ إن ذلك على الله يسير
interpretation: ألم تعلم أن علم الله محيط بكل ما في السماوات والأرض، وأن جميع الأشياء وأحوالها مقدَّرة ومثبتة في كتاب عنده؟ وليس حفظ هذا العلم وإحاطته بكل شيء بعسير على الله، مهما كثر الخلق وتنوّعت أحداثهم.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority and of which they have no knowledge. The wrongdoers will have no helper.
interpretation: The verse condemns directing worship to anything besides Allah without revealed proof or sound knowledge, showing that faith cannot be founded on conjecture or blind imitation. Such rejection of the truth is ظلم, and those who persist in it will find no one able to protect or support them against Allah’s judgment.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you can recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly attack those who recite Our verses to them. Say, “Shall I inform you of something worse than that?” The Fire—Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve—and what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse portrays how stubborn rejection of divine truth can turn into visible resentment and even aggression toward those who convey it. It warns that such hostility is not merely a passing emotional response but a path whose ultimate consequence is the Fire, the most grievous of destinations.

translation: O people, a parable is set forth, so listen to it: Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah will never be able to create even a fly, even if they all gathered together for it. And if the fly were to take something away from them, they could not recover it from it. Weak indeed are the pursuer and the pursued.
interpretation: This parable exposes the utter helplessness of all beings worshipped besides Allah: they lack even the power to create the smallest creature and cannot reclaim from it what it takes. Thus, relying on them for worship, help, or protection is irrational, while Allah alone possesses absolute creative power and deserves to be worshipped.

translation: They have not appraised Allah with the true measure of His greatness. Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.
interpretation: Those who deny or associate partners with Allah fail to recognize His absolute greatness, power, and authority; nothing they worship can rival Him, and He is fully capable of overcoming every false claim and every opponent.

translation: Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: Allah alone determines whom to entrust with conveying His revelation, selecting from both the angelic and human realms according to His perfect knowledge. His complete hearing and sight encompass every word, deed, and inner quality, so His choice is based on absolute wisdom and discernment.

translation: He knows what lies before them and what lies behind them, and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything that concerns them—what has preceded, what is present, and what is yet to come—and every affair ultimately returns to Him for judgment and final determination.

translation: O you who believe, bow, prostrate, worship your Lord, and do good so that you may prosper.
interpretation: The verse directs believers to combine humble submission to Allah through prayer with sincere worship and beneficial good deeds. True success is attained by living in obedience to Him and extending goodness beyond oneself.

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has placed no hardship upon you in the religion—the faith of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this [Qur’an], so that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over humanity. So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent is the Protector, and how excellent is the Helper.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to devote themselves fully to Allah through sincere effort and steadfast obedience, while assuring them that Islam is not meant to impose unbearable difficulty. Their faith continues the pure monotheistic path of Abraham, and their identity as Muslims carries a responsibility: by living according to revelation, they testify to its truth before humanity. Prayer and zakah express this commitment in worship and social responsibility, while reliance upon Allah gives believers strength, since ultimate protection and help belong to Him alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, the believers have attained success.
interpretation: True success belongs to those whose faith is sincere and whose lives reflect obedience to Allah, bringing them lasting well-being in this world and ultimate salvation in the Hereafter.

translation: Those who are humble and deeply attentive in their prayer.
interpretation: They perform prayer with hearts humbled before God, maintaining reverence, sincerity, and focused awareness of standing in His presence rather than treating it as a mere outward ritual.

translation: And those who turn away from vain speech and deeds.
interpretation: They do not involve themselves in words or activities that are pointless, harmful, or unbecoming; instead, they preserve their time and dignity for what is beneficial and pleasing to Allah.

translation: And those who are active in giving zakah,
interpretation: They faithfully fulfill the obligation of zakah, purifying their wealth and themselves by giving the rightful share to those entitled to it.

translation: And those who guard their private parts,
interpretation: They maintain sexual chastity by restraining themselves from forbidden sexual relations and protecting their modesty.

translation: Except with their wives or those whom their right hands possess—for then they are not blameworthy.
interpretation: The verse identifies the lawful bounds of sexual intimacy: it is permitted within marriage and, in the historical legal context addressed by the Qur’an, with enslaved women under one’s recognized ownership; intimacy outside these permitted relationships is blameworthy.

translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors.
interpretation: Those who seek sexual gratification outside the lawful bounds established by God—through marriage or what the verse otherwise permits—have exceeded His limits and are therefore blameworthy.

translation: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants,
interpretation: They conscientiously fulfill every trust placed in their care and honor their promises and commitments, recognizing that faith requires integrity toward both God and people.

translation: And those who faithfully preserve their prayers.
interpretation: They consistently guard their prayers by observing them at their appointed times and performing them with sincere devotion, allowing prayer to remain a steadfast part of their lives.

translation: Those are the inheritors.
interpretation: This refers to those who, through sincere faith and righteous conduct, inherit Paradise as their lasting reward.

translation: Those who inherit Paradise will abide therein forever.
interpretation: They are granted the highest abode of eternal bliss as the lasting reward for their faith and righteous deeds; they will never leave it or experience its blessings coming to an end.

translation: Indeed, We created humankind from an extract of clay.
interpretation: The verse points to humanity’s humble earthly origin and affirms that human existence is the deliberate creation of God, not something independent or self-originating.

translation: Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a secure place.
interpretation: The verse describes the beginning of human existence as being placed in the protected womb, emphasizing the careful preservation and ordered stages through which God brings human life into being.

translation: ثم حوّلنا النطفة إلى علقة، فحوّلنا العلقة إلى مضغة، فحوّلنا المضغة إلى عظام، فكسونا العظام لحمًا، ثم أنشأناه خلقًا آخر؛ فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين.
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن خلق الإنسان يمرّ بمراحل دقيقة متتابعة بتقدير الله، حتى يكتمل إنسانًا حيًّا مكرّمًا، وفي ذلك دليل على كمال قدرته وحكمته، واستحقاقه وحده للتعظيم والثناء.

translation: Then, after that, you will surely die.
interpretation: Every human being is destined to experience death after the period of earthly life, regardless of status or circumstance.

translation: Then, indeed, you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: After death, every human being will be brought back to life for the final judgment before God, when each person will be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: And We have created above you seven layered heavens, and We have never been unaware of creation.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the ordered creation above humanity and affirms that Allah’s knowledge, care, and watchfulness encompass all creatures without negligence.

translation: And We sent down from the sky water in a measured amount, then We settled it in the earth; and surely We are able to take it away.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection toward God’s precise provision and control of water: its descent, storage within the earth, and availability are all governed by His wisdom. Human life depends on this mercy, yet it is never guaranteed, for God alone has the power to withhold or remove it; this should awaken gratitude, humility, and awareness of dependence upon Him.

translation: Then We brought forth for you by it gardens of date palms and grapevines; in them you have many fruits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that rain is a manifestation of His sustaining power: through it He produces abundant, varied nourishment, showing that their provision is a deliberate mercy and a sign of His oneness and care.

translation: وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ
interpretation: يشير الله تعالى إلى شجرة الزيتون التي تنبت في أرض طور سيناء، فيخرج من ثمرها زيتٌ نافع يُستضاء به ويُنتفع به، ويكون إدامًا وطعامًا يُحسِّن مذاق الطعام للآكلين؛ وفي ذلك تذكير بنعمة الله وتدبيره في إخراج المنافع من النبات.

translation: And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and you have many benefits in them, and from them you eat.
interpretation: The livestock are a sign of God’s wisdom and care: from creatures under human stewardship He brings forth nourishment and provides diverse means of benefit. Their usefulness should lead people to recognize His provision and respond with gratitude.

translation: And upon them and upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that He has subjected livestock and ships to their service, enabling them to travel and transport themselves by land and sea through His provision and power.

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, “My people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: Noah calls his people to devote worship exclusively to Allah, affirming that no other being is worthy of worship. His question urges them to awaken their conscience, abandon idolatry, and adopt reverent awareness of Allah by obeying Him and avoiding what displeases Him.

translation: The chiefs who disbelieved among his people said, “This is nothing but a human being like you who seeks to assert superiority over you. Had Allah willed, He would have sent down angels. We have never heard of such a thing from our earliest forefathers.”
interpretation: The statement reflects the arrogant rejection of prophetic guidance: the disbelieving leaders judged revelation by the prophet’s human nature and feared that accepting him would undermine their authority. They also imposed their own assumptions about how God should communicate, using the absence of a familiar precedent among their ancestors as an excuse to deny the truth rather than consider the message itself.

translation: He is only a man afflicted with madness, so wait concerning him for a while.
interpretation: The deniers dismiss the prophet’s message by accusing him of insanity and urge one another to withhold judgment, hoping that time will expose or silence him rather than accepting the truth he brings.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me because they have rejected me as false.”
interpretation: The prophet turns to God for support after his people persistently deny his message, entrusting the outcome to divine justice rather than responding to their rejection with personal retaliation.

translation: So We revealed to him: “Build the Ark under Our watchful care and by Our revelation. Then, when Our command comes and the oven overflows, take aboard it two of every kind, along with your family—except those against whom the decree has already been pronounced—and do not plead with Me concerning those who have wronged; surely they will be drowned.”
interpretation: God instructed Noah to construct the Ark under His protection and guidance, assuring him that deliverance would come at the appointed time. The command to take pairs of living beings and the believing members of his household shows the comprehensive nature of God’s preservation, while the exclusion of those already condemned—including members of Noah’s family who rejected faith—demonstrates that kinship cannot replace righteousness. Noah was also forbidden to intercede for the persistent wrongdoers, for divine judgment had become irrevocable after their rejection and injustice.

translation: Then, when you and those with you are settled aboard the Ark, say: “Praise belongs to Allah, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: Once safety is granted after escaping oppression and destruction, respond not with pride or self-congratulation but with gratitude to Allah, recognizing that deliverance is His mercy and that injustice ultimately cannot prevail.

translation: And say, “My Lord, let me land at a blessed place, for You are the best of those who bring people to land.”
interpretation: This is a prayer asking God to grant a safe arrival and make the place of settlement a source of goodness, protection, and blessing, while acknowledging that true security and welcome come from Him.

translation: Indeed, in that are surely signs, and indeed We are testing.
interpretation: The events referred to contain clear signs of Allah’s power, wisdom, and the truth of His guidance; through them, people are tested by whether they recognize the truth, obey it, and learn from what befell those who rejected it.

translation: Then We brought forth after them another generation.
interpretation: After the destruction of the earlier people, Allah created and established another community in their place, demonstrating that human generations succeed one another only by His will and power.

translation: Then We sent among them a messenger from themselves, saying, “Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: Allah’s message is conveyed through a messenger familiar to his people, calling them to sincere worship of Allah alone. The question “Will you not then be mindful?” urges them to recognize His sole right to worship and to protect themselves from disbelief and disobedience.

translation: And the leaders of his people who disbelieved, denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had indulged in the comforts of worldly life said, “This is only a human being like you: he eats from what you eat and drinks from what you drink.”
interpretation: Their rejection was rooted in arrogance and attachment to worldly privilege: they assumed that a true messenger could not be an ordinary human who shared their physical needs. By reducing prophethood to outward human similarity, they dismissed the possibility that God could choose a person to convey His revelation and warn them of the Hereafter.

translation: “And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then you will surely be losers.”
interpretation: The deniers reject the messenger merely because he is human, claiming that following someone of their own kind would lead to ruin; this exposes their flawed assumption that truth must come from a being unlike humanity rather than being judged by the messenger’s evidence and message.

translation: Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth again?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question expressing denial and mockery of the resurrection: the disbelievers regard returning to life after bodily decay as impossible, while the verse exposes their rejection of God’s promise of resurrection and judgment.

translation: Far, far beyond belief is what you are being promised.
interpretation: This is the dismissive response of those who deny resurrection: they regard the promised return to life and divine judgment as impossibly remote, revealing their rejection of the truth rather than its actual impossibility.

translation: It is only our worldly life: we die and live, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This expresses the denial of resurrection by those who reduce existence to the life of this world, believing that death is the end and that no return to God or accountability in the Hereafter will occur.

translation: He is only a man who has fabricated a lie against Allah, and we will never believe him.
interpretation: The speakers reject the messenger’s claim, accusing him of inventing revelation and refusing to accept his message as truth.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have denied me.”
interpretation: Noah turns to God after his people persistently reject the truth, seeking divine support and justice rather than relying on his own strength.

translation: He said, “Before long, they will surely become regretful.”
interpretation: This is a divine assurance that those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing will soon face its consequences, when their regret can no longer benefit them.

translation: Then the Cry seized them justly, and We reduced them to worthless debris. So away with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse portrays the decisive destruction of a people who persisted in injustice: when divine judgment came upon them with perfect truth and justice, their power and existence were reduced to something discarded and insignificant. It is a warning that persistent wrongdoing ultimately leads to ruin and exclusion from divine mercy.

translation: Then We brought forth after them other generations.
interpretation: After the destruction or passing away of those earlier peoples, Allah brought into existence successive nations and communities, demonstrating that human civilizations rise and pass away according to His decree.

translation: No nation can advance its appointed time, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: Every community has an appointed limit determined by God; it cannot bring that time forward or postpone it, regardless of its desires or efforts.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers one after another. Whenever a messenger came to a nation, they denied him. So We made them follow one another, and We reduced them to tales of the past. So away with a people who do not believe.
interpretation: God explains that the rejection of truth was repeated by successive nations despite the continuous arrival of messengers bearing clear guidance. Their persistent denial brought about their downfall, until they became nothing more than a warning remembered in stories. The verse conveys a grave condemnation of those who knowingly refuse faith and thereby deprive themselves of God’s mercy and guidance.

translation: ثم أرسلنا موسى وأخاه هارون بآياتنا وسلطانٍ مبينٍ.
interpretation: أرسل الله موسى وأخاه هارون إلى فرعون وقومه مزوَّدين بالمعجزات الدالة على صدق رسالتهما، وبحجة واضحة قاهرة تُظهر حقهما وتبطل ما عند المكذبين من دعوى.

translation: إلى فرعون وملئه فاستكبروا وكانوا قوماً عالين
interpretation: أُرسل موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وأعيان قومه، فرفضوا الحق تكبّراً واستعلاءً، ورأوا أنفسهم فوق الخضوع لله أو اتباع رسله، فاستمروا في ظلمهم وطغيانهم.

translation: They said, “Shall we believe in two human beings like us, while their people are subject to us?”
interpretation: They rejected Moses and Aaron out of arrogance, using their own social power over the Israelites as evidence of superiority. Their refusal was not based on the truth of the message, but on contempt for its bearers and an unwillingness to surrender their authority.

translation: But they rejected them both, so they became among those destroyed.
interpretation: Their denial of the two messengers led them to ruin, showing that persistent rejection of divine guidance brings about destruction.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture so that they might be guided.
interpretation: The revelation given to Moses was a divine means of guidance, intended to lead his people from error to faith and obedience to God; guidance, however, requires that they receive and follow the revelation sincerely.

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We sheltered them in a highland of settled terrain and flowing water.
interpretation: This points to the miraculous birth and extraordinary status of Jesus and Mary, while also showing God’s care for them by providing a secure, elevated refuge with stable dwelling and abundant water.

translation: O messengers, eat from the good and wholesome things, and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am All-Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This address teaches that pure provision should be joined with righteous conduct: what a person consumes ought to support obedience rather than corruption. It also reminds the messengers—and, through them, all believers—that every deed is fully known to God, leaving no action outside His knowledge or accountability.

translation: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so be mindful of Me.
interpretation: Humanity’s true religious identity is meant to be united in devotion to one Lord; therefore, believers must guard themselves against disobedience, division, and anything that contradicts sincere God-consciousness.

translation: But they divided their affair among themselves into sects; each faction rejoices in what it has.
interpretation: Although the prophets brought one unified message of faith and obedience to God, people fragmented it into competing sects, each becoming self-satisfied with its own beliefs and refusing to measure them against the original truth.

translation: So leave them in their heedlessness for a time.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persist in confusion and rejection may be left to their chosen state for a limited period; such respite is not approval of their conduct, but a delay before the consequences of their denial become manifest.

translation: Do they think that what We provide them of wealth and children
interpretation: They are mistaken if they regard their abundance of wealth and children as proof that they are favored by God or safe from accountability; such blessings may instead be a test and a temporary respite.

translation: We hasten good things to them, but they do not perceive it.
interpretation: The apparent worldly success of those who reject the truth is not necessarily a sign of divine favor; they may mistake temporary blessings and respite for true goodness, unaware that these can be a test rather than an honor.

translation: Indeed, those who are in awe of their Lord,
interpretation: هم الذين يستشعرون عظمة الله ومراقبته، فيخافون تقصيرهم بين يديه خوفًا ممزوجًا بالتعظيم والرجاء، فيدفعهم ذلك إلى الطاعة واجتناب المعصية.

translation: And those who believe in the signs of their Lord,
interpretation: They sincerely accept the evidence and revelations from their Lord, trusting in their truth and allowing that faith to shape their obedience and conduct.

translation: And those who do not associate anything with their Lord.
interpretation: They affirm God’s absolute oneness, directing worship, reliance, and devotion to Him alone, without attributing any partner or rival to Him.

translation: And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, because they will return to their Lord.
interpretation: The believers perform acts of charity and obedience sincerely, yet remain humble and apprehensive that their deeds may not be accepted, knowing that they will stand before Allah and be accountable to Him.

translation: Those are the ones who hasten to good deeds, and they are foremost in them.
interpretation: This praises believers who do not delay obedience or righteous action; their sincere eagerness places them among those who lead in goodness and strive to attain Allah’s acceptance.

translation: We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. With Us is a record that speaks the truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: Allah’s commands and responsibilities are always within a person’s ability, and every deed is preserved and presented truthfully. Therefore, Allah’s judgment is perfectly just: no one will be held accountable beyond their capacity or deprived of anything they rightfully deserve.

translation: Rather, their hearts are immersed in heedlessness concerning this, and they have other deeds besides that which they will persist in doing.
interpretation: Although the truth has been presented to them, their hearts remain distracted and confused by worldly preoccupations, so they continue choosing actions contrary to faith and obedience, persisting in them despite the warning.

translation: Until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, they will suddenly cry out for help.
interpretation: This warns that worldly privilege does not protect those who persist in wrongdoing: when divine punishment overtakes them, their power and comfort vanish, and they desperately plead for relief after having ignored the truth.

translation: Do not cry out today; indeed, you will not be helped against Us.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who rejected the truth: their pleas and cries for relief on the Day of Judgment will be futile, because they will have no power or protection against God’s judgment.

translation: My verses were recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who, when confronted with God’s revelations, respond with deliberate rejection and retreat instead of humility, reflection, and obedience.

translation: Arrogantly rejecting it, you would spend the night in frivolous talk.
interpretation: This rebukes those who responded to the Qur’an with pride and contempt, turning away from sincere reflection and occupying themselves with vain, dismissive speech instead.

translation: أفلم يدبروا القول أم جاءهم ما لم يأت آباءهم الأولين
interpretation: أفلا يتأمل هؤلاء القرآن ويتدبرون معانيه ليدركوا صدقه وهدايته، أم أنهم يرفضونه لمجرد أنه جاءهم بما لم يألفه آباؤهم الأولون؟ فالآية تذم جعل العادة والتقليد عذرًا لترك الحق، وتدعو إلى النظر فيه بعقل وإنصاف.

translation: Or have they not recognized their Messenger, and so they reject him?
interpretation: Their denial cannot be excused by claiming that the Messenger is unknown to them; they knew his character, truthfulness, and identity, yet knowingly refused to accept his message.

translation: Or do they say, “There is madness in him”? Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them dislike the truth.
interpretation: They dismiss the Messenger by falsely attributing madness to him, yet the reality is that he has brought clear truth from God. Their rejection is not because the truth is unclear, but because most of them resent its demands and refuse to submit to it.

translation: Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens, the earth, and everyone in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, yet they turn away from their reminder.
interpretation: Truth is not shaped by human wishes; it is the standard by which desires must be corrected. If reality and divine guidance were made to conform to conflicting human inclinations, the order of creation and human life would collapse. God has instead given them a reminder suited to their welfare and dignity, but they reject the very guidance meant to reform them.

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment? The provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.
interpretation: The verse reminds the Prophet that his call is not motivated by any worldly compensation from people; what Allah grants—of provision, reward, and support—is better and more lasting than anything they could offer.

translation: Indeed, you are surely inviting them to a straight path.
interpretation: The Prophet’s call leads people toward the clear, upright way of faith and obedience to God, free from deviation and confusion.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.
interpretation: Those who deny the Hereafter become inclined away from the straight path because they reject accountability before God; this denial allows their desires to lead them away from guidance and righteousness.

translation: And even if We had mercy on them and removed the affliction they suffer, they would still persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: The verse portrays people whose hardship has not softened their hearts or turned them toward truth: even if God relieved their suffering, their deep attachment to rebellion and heedlessness would lead them to continue blindly in wrongdoing. It warns that relief from hardship benefits a person only when it is met with humility, gratitude, and repentance.

translation: And We certainly seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate.
interpretation: Even when confronted with suffering meant to awaken them, they remained stubborn and refused to turn to God with humility and sincere prayer; the hardship therefore did not benefit them because their hearts did not respond.

translation: Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment, behold, they are therein utterly despairing.
interpretation: When persistent denial brings upon them the punishment they were warned about, every false hope and source of relief collapses, leaving them overcome by despair and unable to find a way out.

translation: وهو الذي أنشأ لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة؛ قليلًا ما تشكرون.
interpretation: الله تعالى هو الذي وهبكم وسائل الإدراك الظاهرة والباطنة، لتسمعوا الحق وتبصروا آياته وتتفكروا فيها بقلوبكم؛ ومع عِظَم هذه النعم ودوامها فإن أكثر الناس لا يؤدون حقها من شكر الله واستعمالها في طاعته.

translation: And He is the One who brought you forth and spread you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that their presence and dispersion across the earth are by His creative power and wisdom, not by chance. Since He originated and sustained them, their return to Him is certain, when all people will be gathered for judgment and held accountable for how they lived.

translation: And He is the One who gives life and causes death, and to Him belongs the alternation of night and day. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: The succession of life and death and the continual change between night and day are signs of Allah’s exclusive power and governance, calling people to recognize His oneness and worship Him rather than remain heedless.

translation: Rather, they say what the former peoples said.
interpretation: They reject the truth by repeating the same objection made by earlier deniers, relying on inherited disbelief rather than recognizing the possibility and certainty of resurrection.

translation: They said, “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?”
interpretation: This expresses the deniers’ rejection of resurrection: they considered bodily restoration impossible after death and decomposition, overlooking that the One who created them initially is fully capable of bringing them back to life.

translation: “We and our forefathers were promised this before; this is nothing but the tales of the ancients.”
interpretation: This expresses the stubborn denial of resurrection and divine revelation: the rejecters rely on the fact that earlier generations heard the same warning, using that familiarity to dismiss it as fabricated legends rather than considering its truth.

translation: Say, “To whom belongs the earth and all who are in it, if you have knowledge?”
interpretation: This question challenges people to acknowledge that the earth and every being within it belong entirely to Allah, whose ultimate ownership and authority should therefore be recognized.

translation: They will say, “It belongs to Allah.” Say, “Will you not then take heed?”
interpretation: When people themselves acknowledge that ultimate ownership belongs to Allah, they are being called to reflect on the consequence of that admission: exclusive authority and worship should belong to Him alone.

translation: Say, “Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge calling people to acknowledge that Allah alone governs the entire celestial realm and possesses supreme authority over all creation; recognizing His lordship should lead to exclusive worship of Him.

translation: They will say, “It belongs to Allah.” Say, “Will you not then be mindful of Him?”
interpretation: When they acknowledge that all ownership and authority belong to Allah, they are being confronted with the duty that follows from this truth: to fear Him, obey Him, and abandon associating partners with Him. Their admission should lead them to sincere worship and righteous conduct.

translation: Say, “In whose hand is the dominion of all things, and He protects, while none can protect against Him, if you know?”
interpretation: This is a challenge to recognize that Allah alone possesses complete authority over creation: He can grant safety and protection to whomever He wills, while no power can shield anyone from His judgment or overcome Him. Therefore, ultimate dependence and worship belong solely to Him.

translation: They will say, “To Allah.” Say, “How then are you deluded?”
interpretation: They acknowledge that ultimate ownership and authority belong to Allah, yet they still deny His oneness and reject the truth; this contradiction shows that they are overcome by deception and heedlessness rather than guided by their own admission.

translation: Rather, We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars.
interpretation: The truth has been conveyed to them clearly by God, so their rejection is not due to a lack of evidence; rather, they falsely deny what has been revealed and contradict the reality of their own claims.

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor is there any god besides Him. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have dominated others. Glory be to Allah, far above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse establishes that divine unity is necessary: if there were multiple independent gods, each would claim authority over a separate creation, and their competing wills would lead to conflict or one overpowering the others. The ordered harmony of existence therefore points to one absolute Lord, while Allah is exalted above the attributes falsely ascribed to Him.

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen; exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: God alone possesses perfect knowledge of everything hidden and manifest, so He is far above all partners, attributes, or rival objects of worship that people ascribe to Him.

translation: Say, “My Lord, if You show me what they are promised…”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to turn to Allah in humble supplication, acknowledging that the promised punishment is entirely under Allah’s control and seeking His protection from witnessing it while being associated in any way with those who deserve it.

translation: My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This is a plea to Allah for protection from sharing the fate, company, or judgment of those who persist in injustice and disobedience.

translation: And indeed, We are fully capable of showing you what We have promised them.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that He has complete power to make him witness the punishment promised to those who reject the truth, even though its timing and manner remain according to His wisdom.

translation: Repel evil with that which is best. We know best what they describe.
interpretation: Respond to hurtful words and wrongful behavior with the most virtuous conduct—patience, forgiveness, and dignified speech—rather than answering evil with evil. God is fully aware of the false claims and insults people make, so leave their judgment to Him while maintaining moral excellence.

translation: And say, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils.”
interpretation: The verse teaches the believer to turn to Allah for protection from the devils’ whispers, provocations, and attempts to stir sinful thoughts, anger, or harmful impulses within the heart.

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.
interpretation: The believer turns to Allah for protection from the devils’ presence, whispering, and influence, recognizing that only Allah can shield the heart and life from their harm.

translation: When death comes to one of them, he says, “My Lord, send me back.”
interpretation: At the moment of death, the heedless person realizes the truth and regrets how he lived, pleading for another chance to return to the world and rectify his deeds; yet this plea comes after the period of worldly action has ended.

translation: “Perhaps I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind.” No! It is merely a word he utters; and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: After death, the sinner will recognize the truth and plead for another chance to return to worldly life and act righteously, but this plea will not be accepted. The barzakh is an intervening barrier that prevents return until resurrection, showing that repentance and righteous action must be undertaken before death, not postponed until its arrival.

translation: فإذا نُفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذٍ ولا يتساءلون
interpretation: عندما تقوم القيامة ويبدأ الحساب، تزول فاعلية روابط النسب التي كان الناس يعتمدون عليها في الدنيا، فلا تنفع قرابةٌ ولا يستطيع أحد أن يحمل عن غيره شيئًا، ويشتد الهول حتى ينشغل كل إنسان بمصيره فلا يتساءلون أو يتعاضدون كما كانوا يفعلون في الدنيا.

translation: So those whose scales are heavy—it is they who are successful.
interpretation: Those whose good deeds, sincere faith, and obedience outweigh their wrongs on the Day of Judgment will attain true success: salvation from punishment and entry into God’s mercy and reward.

translation: And those whose scales are light—those are the ones who have lost themselves; they will remain in Hell forever.
interpretation: The verse portrays the ultimate failure of those whose deeds have no sufficient weight before God: they have squandered their own souls, and their loss is made permanent by abiding in Hell.

translation: The Fire will scorch their faces, and there they will grimace.
interpretation: This portrays the humiliating and agonizing punishment of those who rejected the truth: the flames will burn their faces, leaving them distorted in pain and unable to escape their suffering.

translation: Were My verses not recited to you, yet you used to deny them?
interpretation: This is a reproach from God to those who rejected the truth despite having His revelations clearly conveyed to them; their punishment is therefore not due to lack of guidance, but to their deliberate denial.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, our misery overcame us, and we were a people astray.”
interpretation: They confess that their persistent pursuit of wrongdoing and their surrender to destructive desires led them away from the truth, yet this admission comes only after the consequences of their choices have become undeniable.

translation: Our Lord, bring us out of it; if we return to wrongdoing, then indeed we will be wrongdoers.
interpretation: This is the plea of those suffering punishment in Hell: they ask Allah for another chance and acknowledge that returning to the same disobedience would prove their own injustice. Their words reveal regret, but also the consequence of having exhausted the opportunity to repent in worldly life.

translation: He will say, “Be despised therein, and do not speak to Me.”
interpretation: This is a declaration of absolute rejection to those who persistently denied the truth: they are humiliated and deprived of any further appeal, because their chance to believe and reform has already been exhausted.

translation: Indeed, there was a group of My servants who used to say: “Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy on us; You are the best of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: Allah presents these servants as an example of sincere faith joined with humility: despite believing, they do not rely on their deeds, but seek forgiveness and mercy, recognizing that Allah’s mercy is the greatest and most perfect.

translation: Then you took them as objects of ridicule, until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.
interpretation: This rebuke exposes how mockery of the righteous can become a means of heedlessness: by ridiculing believers, the wrongdoers became so absorbed in contempt and amusement that they neglected God’s remembrance and their own accountability, while treating the believers’ steadfastness as something laughable.

translation: Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience; surely they are the successful.
interpretation: Allah declares that those who remained steadfast in faith and obedience despite hardship and the mockery of others will receive their full reward in the Hereafter. Their patience has led them to true success: salvation and lasting blessedness with Allah.

translation: He will say, “How many years did you remain on earth?”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, they will be made to recognize how brief their worldly life was compared with the everlasting life of the Hereafter, exposing how they wasted it and misjudged its true worth.

translation: They will say, “We remained for a day or part of a day, so ask those who keep count.”
interpretation: This portrays how, when confronted with the reality of the Hereafter, the disbelievers will perceive their worldly life and time in the grave as astonishingly brief. Their uncertain answer reveals how insignificant worldly existence appears beside the eternal consequences that follow it.

translation: He will say, “You remained only a little, if only you had known.”
interpretation: Allah will expose the insignificance of worldly life compared with the everlasting Hereafter: when the disbelievers are confronted with the truth, the long span they once pursued will seem like only a brief moment, and they will regret not having recognized its fleeting nature.

translation: Did you then think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?
interpretation: The verse rebukes the assumption that human life is meaningless or without accountability. Every person was created with a purpose—to worship God and live responsibly—and will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: Allah is far above every imperfection and is the absolute, rightful ruler of all existence. Since He alone possesses ultimate authority and sustains the majestic Throne, worship and obedience belong exclusively to Him.

translation: And whoever invokes another deity alongside Allah—there is no proof for him—then his reckoning is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will never prosper.
interpretation: Worship and supplication belong exclusively to Allah, because no created being has any legitimate share in divinity. Whoever assigns such worship to another has rejected the truth without valid evidence; although Allah alone will judge that person, this path cannot lead to true success, because it is rooted in disbelief and separation from the source of guidance.

translation: And say, “My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the best of those who show mercy.”
interpretation: This is a supplication teaching the believer to seek both God’s forgiveness for sins and His encompassing mercy, trusting that His mercy is greater, purer, and more perfect than all mercy found among His creation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. This is a surah that We have sent down and made obligatory, and in it We have revealed clear signs so that you may take heed.
interpretation: Allah declares that this chapter is divinely revealed and binding in its guidance and commands. Its clear verses are intended to awaken people from heedlessness, enabling them to remember Allah, understand His limits, and live by them.

translation: The woman who commits fornication and the man who commits fornication—flog each of them one hundred lashes. Let not compassion for them restrain you from upholding God’s law, if you believe in God and the Last Day. And let a group of believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes a fixed legal punishment for proven fornication, applying equally to the woman and the man. It instructs the believing community not to let misplaced leniency undermine justice, while requiring the punishment to be witnessed so that the seriousness of the offense is publicly recognized and moral order is protected.

translation: The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist; and that has been forbidden to the believers.
interpretation: The verse forbids believing men and women from marrying someone who persists openly in fornication, since marriage is meant to unite people upon chastity and faith. It portrays such a person as suited only to one of similar conduct or to a polytheist, while making clear that believers must not accept this kind of union. Repentance and sincere reform remove the وصف of persistent fornication, so the prohibition does not treat a repentant person as permanently condemned.

translation: And those who accuse chaste women without producing four witnesses—flog them eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony. They are truly defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse establishes that accusing chaste people of adultery is a grave offense when the accuser cannot substantiate the charge with four witnesses. The prescribed punishment protects personal honor and social trust, while the rejection of the accuser’s testimony reflects the loss of credibility caused by such reckless accusation; it also warns believers that claims affecting someone’s chastity must not be made without exceptionally clear proof.

translation: Except those who repent after that and rectify themselves—indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Those who sincerely turn back from their wrongdoing and demonstrate their repentance through genuine reform and righteous conduct are not left condemned; Allah may forgive them and encompass them with His mercy.

translation: As for those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is to swear four times by Allah that he is surely telling the truth.
interpretation: The verse establishes a solemn procedure for a husband who accuses his wife without witnesses: he must repeatedly swear before Allah to affirm his truthfulness. This protects both the sanctity of marriage and the wife from an unproven accusation, while placing the matter under divine accountability.

translation: And the fifth oath is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars.
interpretation: After giving four solemn testimonies, the husband invokes God’s curse upon himself as the final confirmation that he is truthful; this grave self-imprecation underscores the seriousness of accusing one’s spouse without truth.

translation: And it will avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is truly among the liars.
interpretation: If a wife rejects her husband’s accusation and solemnly swears four times by Allah that his claim is false, these oaths protect her from the prescribed punishment, establishing a formal procedure in which the matter is entrusted to Allah’s judgment.

translation: And the fifth oath is that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among those who speak the truth.
interpretation: This is the wife’s final solemn oath in the procedure of mutual imprecation: she calls upon herself Allah’s wrath if her husband’s accusation is true, thereby emphasizing the grave seriousness of falsely denying his claim before God.

translation: Were it not for Allah’s grace upon you and His mercy—and that Allah is Ever-Accepting of repentance, All-Wise—
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that their protection from error and the acceptance of their repentance come solely through Allah’s grace and mercy. His readiness to forgive is joined with perfect wisdom, so His judgments and guidance are always just and purposeful.

translation: Indeed, those who brought forth the slander are a group from among you. Do not consider it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. Each of them shall bear the sin he has earned, and the one among them who took the greatest part in it will have a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the false accusation against the Prophet’s household, teaching that believers must not hastily regard painful trials as pure harm: through this ordeal, the truth was exposed, the community was instructed in moral responsibility, and the innocence of the accused was vindicated. Every participant is held accountable for the part he or she spread, while the chief instigator bears the gravest punishment because of the greater harm caused.

translation: Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and women not think well of one another and say, “This is an obvious slander”?
interpretation: Believers are expected to presume the innocence and good character of fellow believers, especially when confronted with unverified accusations, and to reject such claims as clear falsehood rather than repeating or entertaining them.

translation: لِمَ لَمْ يَأْتُوا عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ؟ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِالشُّهَدَاءِ، فَأُولَئِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن اتهام الناس في أعراضهم لا يُقبل بالظن أو الكلام المجرد، بل لا بد من أربعة شهود يشهدون شهادة واضحة. فإذا عجز المدّعون عن تقديم هذا الدليل، عُدَّوا كاذبين في حكم الله، حمايةً لكرامة الناس ومنعًا للبهتان.

translation: Had it not been for Allah’s فضل and mercy upon you in this world and the Hereafter, a tremendous punishment would have afflicted you because of what you indulged in.
interpretation: Allah’s mercy spared you from the immediate consequences of recklessly engaging in false accusations and spreading harmful talk, yet the verse warns that such conduct is extremely serious and can bring severe punishment unless met with repentance and restraint.

translation: When you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and thought it insignificant, while it is great in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: This verse warns that repeating unverified claims and speaking about others without knowledge is a serious moral offense, even when people treat such words as harmless or trivial; before Allah, careless speech and the harm it causes are grave matters.

translation: If only, when you heard it, you had said, “It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a grave slander.”
interpretation: Believers are taught to reject unverified accusations immediately, recognizing that spreading such words is a serious moral offense and declaring God exalted above any injustice or falsehood attributed to His servants.

translation: Allah admonishes you never to return to anything like it, if you are believers.
interpretation: Allah firmly warns believers against repeating such grave wrongdoing and teaches that sincere faith must restrain them from returning to it.

translation: And Allah makes the verses clear to you; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah clarifies His signs and guidance so that people may understand what is right and live by it. His explanation is complete because it comes from perfect knowledge of His creation and perfect wisdom in directing them.

translation: Indeed, those who love for indecency to spread among the believers will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: The verse warns against not only committing immorality, but also desiring, promoting, or spreading it among believers. Such conduct corrupts individuals and society, violates people’s dignity, and carries consequences in this life as well as the Hereafter. Allah alone fully knows the harm concealed in these actions, whereas human beings may underestimate their seriousness.

translation: Were it not for Allah’s grace upon you and His mercy—and that Allah is Most Kind, Most Merciful—
interpretation: This reminds people that their protection from wrongdoing and its consequences, and their opportunity to repent and be forgiven, exist only through Allah’s gracious mercy and compassionate care.

translation: O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, then indeed he commands obscenity and wrongdoing. Were it not for Allah’s grace and mercy upon you, none of you would ever have been purified; but Allah purifies whom He wills. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Believers are warned that evil usually draws them through gradual steps, beginning with seemingly small acts that lead toward indecency and wrongdoing. Moral purity is not achieved by human strength alone; it is a gift of Allah’s grace, sustained by obedience, repentance, and His guidance.
