interpretation: Abraham declares that everything worshipped besides Allah is hostile to him because it leads people away from the truth, whereas Allah alone is his true Lord, protector, and source of guidance.

translation: He is the One who created me, and He guides me.
interpretation: Ibrahim affirms that since Allah alone brought him into existence, guidance to truth and righteous conduct comes from Him alone; therefore, he places his trust and dependence entirely upon Allah.

translation: And He is the One who feeds me and gives me drink.
interpretation: This expresses Abraham’s recognition that all nourishment and sustenance come from Allah, affirming his complete dependence on Him and gratitude for His continual care.

translation: And when I am ill, it is He who heals me.
interpretation: The verse teaches that although illness may occur through natural causes, healing ultimately comes from Allah alone; medicines and physicians are merely means through which He may grant recovery.

translation: And it is He who causes me to die, then gives me life.
interpretation: This affirms that death and resurrection are entirely in God’s power, reminding us that earthly life is temporary and that God alone grants the final life after death.

translation: And the One in whom I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse expresses sincere humility before Allah: despite striving to obey Him, the believer recognizes his need for divine mercy and places his hope in Allah’s forgiveness when all deeds are judged.

translation: My Lord, grant me sound judgment and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This is a prayer for wise, discerning judgment that enables one to recognize and follow the truth, together with a sincere longing to be included among those whose faith and conduct are pleasing to God.

translation: And grant me an honorable mention among later generations.
interpretation: Abraham asks Allah to leave him a lasting legacy of truth, righteousness, and sincere praise among those who come after him—not mere worldly fame, but remembrance founded on faith and virtuous deeds.

translation: And make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This is a supplication to be granted entry into Paradise and to receive its everlasting blessings through Allah’s mercy and righteousness.

translation: And forgive my father; indeed, he was among those who had gone astray.
interpretation: This is Abraham’s compassionate supplication for his father, asking Allah to pardon him for his deviation from faith; it reflects Abraham’s concern for his family and his hope in Allah’s mercy.

translation: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This is a humble supplication to Allah for protection from humiliation and exposure on the Day of Resurrection, when every person’s deeds will be revealed and judgment will be carried out.

translation: The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit anyone,
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, worldly possessions and family ties will have no power to save a person; only sincere faith and a sound heart purified from disbelief and corruption will matter.

translation: Except for the one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.
interpretation: A sound heart is one purified from disbelief, hypocrisy, rancor, and corrupt desires, sincerely devoted to Allah and submitting to His truth; such inner sincerity is what benefits a person before Him.

translation: And Paradise was brought near to the righteous.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, Paradise will be presented close at hand to those who lived in reverent awareness of Allah and guarded themselves from disobedience, signifying that their steadfast devotion has led them to their promised reward.

translation: And Hellfire will be brought into view for those who went astray.
interpretation: Hell will be made plainly visible to those who rejected the truth and deviated from the right path, so they will directly confront the consequence of their choices.

translation: And it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to worship?”
interpretation: This is a scene from the Day of Judgment in which the idolaters are confronted with the utter helplessness and absence of the beings they relied upon instead of Allah.

translation: Besides Allah, can they help you or help themselves?
interpretation: Those whom people invoke instead of Allah possess no real power: they are unable to protect their worshippers from harm or even to protect themselves, so reliance and worship belong solely to Allah.

translation: Then they will be hurled into it—both they and the deviators.
interpretation: The verse depicts the humiliating downfall of those who rejected the truth, together with those who led them astray or followed them in deviation; all will be cast into Hell without distinction.

translation: And all the forces of Iblis.
interpretation: This refers to every follower and ally of Satan, all gathered together in disgrace and punishment for their rebellion against God.

translation: They will say, while they are arguing therein,
interpretation: The condemned will dispute within Hell, blaming one another and quarrelling over the causes of their ruin.

translation: By Allah, we were indeed in clear error.
interpretation: They will acknowledge with certainty and regret that their former beliefs and worship were plainly misguided, having led them away from the truth.

translation: When we considered you equal to the Lord of all worlds,
interpretation: This is a confession of the wrongdoers that they committed shirk by giving created beings a status of worship and obedience comparable to Allah, the sole Lord and Creator of all existence.

translation: “And none led us astray except the criminals.”
interpretation: The unbelievers will confess that their misguidance came through their willing allegiance to wicked people who led them away from the truth; yet this confession does not absolve them, because they followed those criminals by their own choice.

translation: So we have no intercessors,
interpretation: The condemned acknowledge that no one has come forward to plead their case or rescue them from the consequences of their rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: ولا صديق حميم
interpretation: ولا يجدون في ذلك اليوم صديقًا مقرّبًا مخلصًا يستطيع أن ينفعهم أو يدفع عنهم العذاب.

translation: If only we could return, we would be among the believers.
interpretation: This expresses the regret of those who recognize the truth only after facing its consequences, wishing for another opportunity to believe and obey—but that opportunity is no longer available.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them would not be believers.
interpretation: The signs of God’s power and truth are evident in what has been shown, but many people remain unwilling to believe because they reject or disregard the evidence before them.

translation: And indeed, your Lord—He is truly the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: Allah possesses absolute might and authority, yet His treatment of His creation is governed by mercy; His power does not negate His compassion.

translation: The people of Noah denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although Noah alone was sent to them, their rejection of him amounted to rejecting all messengers, because their message was one in calling people to worship Allah alone and obey His guidance.

translation: When their brother Noah said to them, “Will you not be mindful of Allah?”
interpretation: Noah addressed his people as their brother—sharing their lineage and community—to convey sincere concern, calling them to abandon disobedience and recognize their duty to fear Allah and live righteously.

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: The messenger affirms that he faithfully conveys God’s revelation without deceit, betrayal, or alteration, so his people should accept his guidance with confidence.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The command calls people to maintain reverence and obedience to Allah, and to follow the guidance conveyed by His messenger rather than merely claiming faith without submitting to divine instruction.

translation: I ask no payment from you for it; my reward is only with the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The message is conveyed sincerely for God’s sake, not for worldly gain, praise, or compensation from people; therefore, its reward and recompense are entrusted entirely to God, the Lord of all creation.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to live in reverent awareness of Allah and to follow his guidance as a messenger conveying Allah’s command, since true obedience to him is obedience to God’s revealed guidance.

translation: They said, “Should we believe you while the lowest of people follow you?”
interpretation: The people of Noah rejected his message out of arrogance, judging the truth by the humble social standing of his followers rather than by the truth of what he preached.

translation: He said, “What knowledge do I have of what they used to do?”
interpretation: Noah replied that he was not responsible for judging the hidden deeds, motives, or past conduct of those who followed him; his duty was to accept their sincere faith, while their ultimate accountability belonged to God.

translation: Their reckoning is only with my Lord—if only you could understand.
interpretation: The speaker declares that judging these people and holding them accountable belongs solely to God, who knows their true faith and deeds; humans have no right to reject them based on outward status or worldly standing.

translation: And I am not one to drive away the believers.
interpretation: The speaker declares that genuine faith, not social status or worldly rank, determines who is welcomed; believers must not be rejected merely because they are poor, weak, or looked down upon by others.

translation: I am only a clear warner.
interpretation: The speaker declares that his role is to convey the warning plainly and unmistakably, leaving people responsible for how they respond; he does not claim power to compel faith or control the consequences of their choices.

translation: They said, “If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those who are stoned.”
interpretation: Noah’s people responded to his persistent call to faith with intimidation and a threat of violence, revealing their refusal to engage with the truth and their determination to silence him rather than reconsider their beliefs.

translation: He said, “My Lord, indeed my people have rejected me as a liar.”
interpretation: Noah turns to God after his people persistently deny his message, expressing his helplessness and entrusting the matter to God’s judgment and support.

translation: So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and the believers who are with me.
interpretation: This is a supplication for God to settle the conflict between the prophet and those who reject the truth through a clear and final judgment, while granting deliverance to him and the believers who remain faithful.

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the fully laden Ark.
interpretation: Allah rescued Noah and the believers who accompanied him from the overwhelming flood, showing that obedience and trust in Him lead to deliverance even when falsehood and rejection prevail.

translation: Then We drowned the rest.
interpretation: After saving those who believed, God destroyed those who remained in persistent denial, showing that continued rejection of His truth ultimately leads to punishment.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them would not be believers.
interpretation: The evidence of God’s power and truth is clear in what has been described, but many people refuse to believe despite witnessing such signs, because recognition of truth does not by itself overcome denial or heedlessness.

translation: And indeed, your Lord—He is surely the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah’s absolute might is joined with perfect mercy: He cannot be overcome, yet He does not deal with His servants unjustly, instead extending mercy to those who turn to Him.

translation: The people of ʿĀd denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although ʿĀd rejected the messenger sent to them, their denial is described as rejecting all the messengers because the message of every prophet is one in its foundation: worship God alone and obey His guidance. Thus, rejecting one messenger after the truth has reached a people is a rejection of the divine mission itself.

translation: When their brother Hūd said to them, “Will you not be mindful of Allah?”
interpretation: Hūd’s appeal begins by reminding his people that he is one of them, not an outsider seeking power over them; he calls them to abandon arrogance and heedlessness and to live in reverent obedience to Allah.

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: The messenger affirms that he has been sent by God and that his complete trustworthiness makes him deserving of being believed and obeyed.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls people to uphold reverence and obedience to Allah, and to follow his guidance as a messenger entrusted to convey His command.

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The message is conveyed purely for God’s sake, without seeking wealth, status, or personal benefit from people; the messenger entrusts his recompense entirely to God, the Lord of all creation.

translation: Do you build a monument on every high place, merely to amuse yourselves?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of the people of ʿĀd for constructing grand structures in prominent places out of vanity and boastfulness, without a worthy purpose or benefit, treating their power and wealth as an occasion for frivolous display.

translation: And you build imposing structures, hoping that you will live forever.
interpretation: You devote yourselves to constructing magnificent, fortified buildings as though material grandeur could secure lasting life, while neglecting the certainty of death and accountability before God.

translation: And when you seize people by force, you seize them with ruthless tyranny.
interpretation: This condemns using power with excessive cruelty and arrogance, treating those who are overcome without justice, mercy, or restraint.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls his people to reverence Allah by avoiding disobedience and fulfilling His commands, and to accept his guidance as the messenger conveying Allah’s will.

translation: And be mindful of Him who has provided you with what you know.
interpretation: This is a call to recognize that the knowledge, abilities, and means people possess are gifts from God, and therefore to respond to them with reverence, obedience, and gratitude rather than pride or self-reliance.

translation: He has provided you with livestock and sons.
interpretation: This points to God’s blessings in both material provision and family, reminding people that such sources of strength and prosperity come from Him and should lead to gratitude and obedience.

translation: And gardens and springs.
interpretation: This evokes abundant, life-giving blessings: lush gardens nourished by flowing springs, signifying prosperity, comfort, and divine provision.

translation: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This is a sincere warning that turning away from God’s guidance may lead to severe punishment on the Day of Judgment, whose terror and seriousness are beyond ordinary human reckoning.

translation: They said, “It makes no difference to us whether you admonish us or are not among those who admonish.”
interpretation: They responded with stubborn rejection, declaring that their hearts were closed to the prophet’s counsel and that his warnings would neither change their beliefs nor deter them from their ways.

translation: This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples.
interpretation: The speaker dismisses the prophet’s warning as merely an old practice or inherited tradition, refusing to recognize it as a genuine divine message.

translation: And We would not punish.
interpretation: Allah declares that He does not inflict punishment without justice and clear grounds; punishment is not imposed arbitrarily or without establishing the truth and the responsibility of those who reject it.

translation: But they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The destruction of those who rejected the truth is a warning that persistent denial brings ruin, while the signs of God benefit only those who respond with faith and humility.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is truly the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah is unconquerable in His power and judgment, yet His dealings with His creation are founded upon boundless mercy.

translation: Thamūd denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although Thamūd rejected only their messenger Ṣāliḥ, their rejection amounted to denying all messengers because they shared the same call to worship God alone and obey His guidance.

translation: When their brother Ṣāliḥ said to them, “Will you not be mindful of God?”
interpretation: Ṣāliḥ addresses his people with familiar compassion, calling them to abandon their rebellion and recognize their responsibility before God. His question is a gentle but serious reminder that true piety means guarding oneself from wrongdoing and responding obediently to divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: The speaker affirms that he has been sent by God and that his character is marked by complete honesty and trustworthiness; therefore, his people should accept his message with confidence rather than suspicion.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The command calls people to live with reverent awareness of Allah by avoiding disobedience, and to follow the guidance conveyed by His messenger.

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The message is conveyed sincerely for God’s sake, not for worldly gain or personal benefit; therefore, its truth is not dependent on receiving payment or praise from people.

translation: أتُتركون آمنين في ما هنا؟
interpretation: هذا استفهام إنكاري يوبّخ قوم ثمود على ظنّهم أن النعم والمساكن التي يعيشون فيها ستبقى لهم أمانًا دائمًا، من غير حساب أو عقوبة على كفرهم وفسادهم.

translation: In gardens and springs,
interpretation: This portrays a state of everlasting bliss, where the righteous dwell amid lush gardens and flowing springs as a reward from Allah.

translation: And crops and date palms whose clusters are tender and succulent.
interpretation: This portrays the abundance and fertility of the land, where crops flourish and date palms produce soft, nourishing fruit, as a blessing that should lead people to gratitude rather than arrogance.

translation: And you skillfully carve homes out of the mountains.
interpretation: You were granted the ability to carve secure and impressive dwellings into the mountains, yet this craftsmanship led you to pride and heedlessness rather than gratitude and obedience to God.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This is a call to remain conscious of Allah and to follow the guidance of His messenger with sincere obedience.

translation: And do not obey the command of those who commit excesses.
interpretation: Do not follow the directives or ways of people who exceed the limits set by God, for their influence leads away from righteousness and toward corruption.

translation: Those who spread corruption throughout the land and do not set things right.
interpretation: This describes people whose actions cause harm, disorder, and injustice in society, while they make no sincere effort to restore what has been damaged or promote righteousness.

translation: They said, “You are only one of those bewitched.”
interpretation: They rejected the prophet’s call by alleging that he was under the influence of magic, using this accusation to dismiss his message rather than consider its truth.

translation: You are only a human being like us, so bring us a sign if you are truthful.
interpretation: This expresses the people’s rejection of the messenger’s claim on the grounds that he shares their human nature. They demand a miraculous sign as proof of his truthfulness, revealing their refusal to accept revelation through an ordinary human messenger.

translation: He said, “This is a she-camel; she has her share of water, and you have your share on a specified day.”
interpretation: Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام establishes a divinely ordained division of the water between the miraculous she-camel and his people, making obedience to this arrangement a test of their faith and warning them not to violate it.

translation: And do not harm her, lest the punishment of a tremendous day seize you.
interpretation: This is a stern warning not to violate God’s command by harming the she-camel presented as a sign; those who defy His clear guidance expose themselves to overwhelming punishment.

translation: So they hamstrung her, and then became remorseful.
interpretation: They deliberately violated the divine sign and command by harming the she-camel, but their regret came only after the irreversible consequences of their defiance had become clear.

translation: So the punishment seized them. Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them would not believe.
interpretation: The destruction that befell them demonstrates that God’s warnings are true and that persistent rejection of His signs brings consequence; nevertheless, most people do not respond with faith even when such evidence is made clear.

translation: And surely your Lord is indeed the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah possesses absolute might over all things, yet His power is accompanied by vast mercy toward His servants.

translation: The people of Lot denied the messengers.
interpretation: Although the people of Lot rejected only Lot, denying him amounted to denying all the messengers because they rejected the same divine message of faith and obedience that every messenger conveyed.

translation: When their brother Lot said to them, “Will you not be mindful of Allah?”
interpretation: Lot addressed his people as their brother, highlighting his closeness and sincere concern for them, and began his call by urging them to develop reverent awareness of Allah that would restrain them from wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.
interpretation: The messenger affirms that he has been entrusted by God to convey His revelation faithfully and that his honesty and reliability should lead his people to accept his message.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: The speaker calls his people to fulfill their duty to Allah by avoiding disobedience and to accept and follow his guidance as Allah’s messenger.

translation: I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The messenger declares that he seeks no worldly compensation for conveying the truth; his intention is sincere, and he entrusts his recompense entirely to God, the Lord of all creation.

translation: Do you approach males among all people,
interpretation: The verse rebukes Lot’s people for pursuing sexual relations with men rather than the lawful marital path, presenting this conduct as a grave transgression against the natural and moral order.

translation: And you abandon what your Lord has created for you of your spouses. Rather, you are a people who transgress all bounds.
interpretation: The verse condemns Lot’s people for rejecting the lawful marital relations God provided and pursuing forbidden desire instead, thereby exceeding the moral limits established by Him.

translation: They said, “If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled.”
interpretation: Lot’s people responded to his warning with intimidation rather than repentance, threatening to drive him from his home and community if he continued condemning their wrongdoing. Their words reveal how deeply arrogance and moral corruption had made them reject truth and treat the righteous as outsiders.

translation: He said, “Indeed, I am among those who utterly detest your deeds.”
interpretation: The speaker declares his complete repudiation of their immoral conduct, distancing himself from it in both conviction and allegiance.

translation: My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.
interpretation: This is a prayer by Lot, peace be upon him, asking Allah to protect him and his household from the corrupt actions of his people and from the punishment that would result from their wrongdoing.

translation: So We saved him and all his family.
interpretation: God rescued the prophet and every member of his household who believed from the punishment that befell the wrongdoing people.

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: The phrase refers to the wife of Lot: she was excluded from salvation because she remained aligned with the sinful people and shared in their rejection, so she was left among those who were destroyed.

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This expresses that after saving the believers, Allah brought about the destruction of those who persisted in rejecting His messenger and truth, demonstrating the consequence of defiance and wrongdoing.

translation: And We rained down upon them a rain; evil indeed was the rain of those who had been warned.
interpretation: The rain was a destructive punishment that befell the people after they rejected the warnings delivered to them, showing that divine warning, when persistently ignored, can be followed by severe retribution.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them would not be believers.
interpretation: The matter referred to contains a clear proof of God’s power and truth, but most people fail to respond with faith because they turn away from the lesson and reject the signs before them.

translation: And indeed, your Lord—He alone is the Mighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: Allah’s absolute power is joined with perfect mercy: nothing can overcome Him, yet His treatment of His servants is grounded in compassion and care.

translation: The companions of the thicket denied the messengers.
interpretation: The people of the thicket rejected the truth brought by their prophet Shuʿayb, and by denying him they were treated as deniers of all the messengers, because every messenger calls to the same foundation of faith and obedience to God.

translation: When Shuʿayb said to them, “Will you not be mindful of God?”
interpretation: Shuʿayb urged his people to awaken their conscience and abandon wrongdoing by recognizing that they are accountable to God.

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: The messenger affirms that he has been sent by God and that he is entirely reliable in conveying the divine message, neither betraying the trust nor altering what he has been commanded to deliver.

translation: So be mindful of Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This is a call to live with reverent awareness of Allah and to follow the guidance conveyed by His messenger, since true devotion to Allah is demonstrated through obedience to His commands.

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only with the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The messenger makes clear that he seeks no worldly payment, status, or personal benefit for conveying the truth. His reward and recompense are entrusted entirely to God, demonstrating the sincerity and purity of his call.

translation: Give full measure and do not be among those who cause loss.
interpretation: This commands absolute honesty in trade: fulfill people’s rights completely and do not deceive them by giving less than what is due, whether through measurement, weighing, or any other form of unfair dealing.

translation: And weigh with the straight balance.
interpretation: Conduct all weighing and measuring with precise fairness, giving people their full due without cheating or diminishing what is owed to them.

translation: And do not deprive people of what is rightfully theirs, nor spread corruption throughout the land.
interpretation: This commands justice and honesty in all dealings: no one may diminish another person’s rights, wealth, work, or dignity, and people must not use their actions to create harm, disorder, or corruption in society.

translation: And be mindful of Him who created you and the former generations.
interpretation: Worship and obey Allah with reverent awareness, for He is the Creator of both you and the peoples who came before you; their existence and fate should remind you that no one is beyond His authority or accountability.

translation: They said, “You are only one of those bewitched.”
interpretation: They rejected the prophet’s call by portraying him as mentally or spiritually affected by magic, thereby dismissing his message instead of considering its truth.

translation: You are nothing but a human being like us, and we truly think you are among the liars.
interpretation: The people reject the messenger’s claim to divine authority because they see him as an ordinary human being, and their arrogance leads them to dismiss his message as false rather than consider the truth of what he conveys.

translation: “So make a fragment of the sky fall upon us, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: This is a defiant demand from those rejecting the messenger: they challenge him to bring immediate punishment as alleged proof, exposing their arrogance and stubborn refusal to accept the truth.

translation: He said, “My Lord knows best what you do.”
interpretation: This affirms that God has complete knowledge of people’s deeds and intentions, so nothing they do is hidden from Him and they will be held accountable accordingly.

translation: But they rejected him, so the punishment of the Day of the Cloud overtook them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.
interpretation: After the people of Shuʿayb persisted in denying him, Allah seized them with the punishment of the ominous cloud—a terrifying affliction that appeared to offer relief but brought destruction—revealing the grave consequence of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The matter referred to is a clear indication of God’s power and truth, but the evidence does not benefit most people because they remain unwilling to believe.

translation: And indeed, your Lord—He is truly the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah’s absolute might is joined with perfect mercy: He cannot be overcome, yet He does not punish or deal with His servants unjustly, but shows mercy to those who turn to Him.

translation: And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is affirmed to come from Allah, the Lord and Creator of every realm, rather than being a human composition; its source is divine and universal in authority.

translation: The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down.
interpretation: The verse refers to the angel Gabriel, entrusted by God with revelation, conveying the Qur’an from God to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ faithfully and without alteration.

translation: upon your heart, so that you may be one of the warners.
interpretation: The revelation was conveyed to the Prophet’s heart so that he could faithfully deliver God’s warning and call people away from disbelief and wrongdoing.

translation: In a clear Arabic tongue.
interpretation: The Qur’an was revealed in lucid Arabic, making its guidance accessible and unmistakable to its first audience.

translation: And indeed, it is mentioned in the scriptures of the earlier peoples.
interpretation: The Qur’an is affirmed to be consistent with the revealed books given to earlier nations, which contained indications and prophecies of the same divine guidance and the coming of God’s Messenger.

translation: أولم يكن لهم علامةٌ على صدقه أن علماء بني إسرائيل كانوا يعرفونه؟
interpretation: إن معرفة علماء بني إسرائيل بالقرآن وإدراكهم موافقته لما عرفوه من الوحي والحق تُعدّ دليلاً على أنه وحيٌ من الله، لا كلامٌ مختلق من عند النبي ﷺ.

translation: Had We revealed it to one of the non-Arabs,
interpretation: Even if the Qur’an had been revealed in a language unfamiliar to the Arabs, their stubborn rejection would have remained; thus their denial was not caused by any genuine lack of clarity, but by obstinacy and refusal to accept the truth.

translation: Then he recited it to them, but they would not have believed in it.
interpretation: Even if the Qur’an had been revealed in a language they fully understood and recited directly to them, those who were determined to reject the truth would still not have believed; their rejection arose from stubbornness and denial, not from a lack of clarity in the revelation.

translation: Thus We cause it to enter the hearts of the guilty.
interpretation: God makes His revelation reach the hearts of those who persist in wrongdoing, yet their ingrained arrogance and denial prevent them from accepting it or submitting to its truth.

translation: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: Their persistent denial will continue until the truth becomes undeniable through the punishment they witness; at that point, belief will come only after its opportunity for beneficial response has passed.

translation: Then it will come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse warns that divine punishment may overtake people without warning while they remain heedless, so relying on delay or feeling secure from accountability is dangerous.

translation: فسيقولون: هل نحن مُمهَلون؟
interpretation: عند حلول العذاب، يتمنّى المكذّبون تأجيله ومنحهم مهلة للنجاة أو التدارك، لكن طلبهم يأتي بعد فوات الأوان ولا يُستجاب لهم.

translation: Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who mockingly demand that divine punishment come sooner, revealing their arrogance and heedlessness toward the certainty of God’s warning.

translation: Have you considered: if We let them enjoy themselves for years,
interpretation: Even if the deniers are granted long lives filled with worldly comfort, that temporary enjoyment cannot protect them from the punishment they have been warned of or make their eventual reckoning any less certain.

translation: Then there came to them what they had been promised.
interpretation: The warning they had repeatedly ignored eventually became a reality, showing that divine promises and threats are certain even if their fulfillment is delayed.

translation: What benefit did all that they had been enjoying bring them?
interpretation: The worldly pleasures and comforts they enjoyed could not protect them or avail them when God’s punishment came; temporary enjoyment is worthless against the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: And We never destroyed a town without it having warners.
interpretation: Allah does not punish a people with destruction until warning and guidance have reached them, so that no one is wronged or left without a clear opportunity to recognize the truth.

translation: A reminder—and We were never unjust.
interpretation: Allah clarifies that His warnings are meant to awaken people before judgment; therefore, when punishment comes after clear warning and persistent rejection, it is not oppression or arbitrary injustice.

translation: And the devils did not bring it down.
interpretation: This verse rejects the claim that the Qur’an was inspired or conveyed by devils. Its revelation came from Allah through the trustworthy angel, not through satanic forces, whose nature and power are wholly incompatible with the truth and guidance contained in it.

translation: It is neither befitting for them nor are they capable of it.
interpretation: False and evil beings are unworthy of carrying divine revelation and have no power to produce or convey it truthfully.

translation: Indeed, they are excluded from hearing it.
interpretation: The devils are prevented from reaching the heavenly revelation, so they cannot secretly listen to it or convey it as a source of truth to soothsayers.

translation: So do not invoke any other god alongside Allah, lest you become among those who are punished.
interpretation: This is a firm prohibition of associating any partner with Allah in worship or supplication, warning that abandoning pure monotheism leads to punishment.

translation: And warn your closest relatives.
interpretation: Begin conveying the message of faith and warning against accountability with those nearest to you, since religious responsibility applies first within one’s own household and close community, without exempting relatives from truth or judgment.

translation: And lower your wing in humility to the believers who follow you.
interpretation: You are commanded to treat sincere believers with gentleness, humility, and compassionate care, rather than with pride or harshness.

translation: But if they disobey you, then say, “I am free of what you do.”
interpretation: If people reject your guidance and persist in wrongdoing, you must clearly dissociate yourself from their actions and bear no responsibility for conduct you neither approve nor follow, while entrusting their judgment to God.

translation: And place your trust in the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Entrust your affairs to Allah, relying on His unmatched power and compassionate care, while remaining steadfast in obedience to Him.

translation: He who sees you when you stand.
interpretation: Allah is ever aware of you as you rise to worship, act, or undertake your responsibilities, witnessing your outward actions and the sincerity within your heart.

translation: and your movements among those who prostrate,
interpretation: This affirms that Allah fully observes the Prophet ﷺ as he worships and moves among the congregation of believers in prayer.

translation: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: God hears every word and sound, whether spoken openly or concealed, and knows every intention, thought, and circumstance. Nothing escapes His hearing or knowledge.

translation: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question introducing a clarification: the devils do not descend upon the sincere messengers or truthful believers, but upon those inclined to falsehood, deception, and sinful speech, who readily receive and spread their whisperings.

translation: They descend upon every sinful liar.
interpretation: This means that the devils find influence and access among those who habitually fabricate falsehood and persist in wickedness, rather than among people devoted to truth and righteousness.

translation: They eagerly listen in, and most of them are liars.
interpretation: The verse describes devils who try to eavesdrop on what is conveyed from the unseen and pass it on to soothsayers, mixing the little truth they obtain with much falsehood; thus their claims cannot be trusted.

translation: And the poets—the misguided follow them.
interpretation: This verse condemns poets whose words are driven by falsehood, exaggeration, and desire, causing those who follow them to stray from divine guidance; it is not a condemnation of every form of poetry.

translation: Do you not see that they wander aimlessly through every valley?
interpretation: This describes poets whose speech is driven by imagination and impulse rather than truth, so they drift from one subject and claim to another without firm purpose or commitment.

translation: And that they say what they do not do.
interpretation: This condemns the poets who make claims and promises without living by them, exposing the hypocrisy of words that are unsupported by action.

translation: Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah often, and defend themselves after having been wronged. And those who do wrong will soon know to what end they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse makes clear that speech or poetic expression is not blameworthy when it is joined with faith, righteous conduct, frequent remembrance of Allah, and a just defense against oppression. It also warns the wrongdoers that their injustice will ultimately lead them to a grievous consequence before Allah.

translation: Ṭā Sīn. These are the verses of the Qur’an and a clear Book.
interpretation: The opening letters, whose full meaning is known to Allah, introduce a revelation whose divine origin and guidance are made clear through its precise, illuminating verses.

translation: A guidance and glad tidings for the believers.
interpretation: It indicates that divine revelation guides believers toward truth and righteous conduct, while promising them mercy, success, and reward from God.

translation: Those who establish prayer, give zakāt, and are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: True faith is manifested through devoted worship, generosity toward others, and firm certainty that life will culminate in accountability before God; this conviction gives spiritual purpose and moral seriousness to a person’s actions.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter—We have made their deeds pleasing to them, so they wander blindly.
interpretation: Because they reject accountability in the Hereafter, they become attached to their worldly actions and perceive them as good, even when those actions lead them away from truth; thus they remain confused and directionless.

translation: Those are the ones who will have the worst punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.
interpretation: This describes people who persist in rejecting the truth and denying the Hereafter: their stubbornness brings them severe punishment, and they ultimately lose the greatest possible good—faith, salvation, and the reward of the eternal life.

translation: And surely you receive the Qur’an from the One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
interpretation: The Qur’an is revealed to you directly by Allah, whose perfect wisdom and complete knowledge guarantee that its guidance is true, purposeful, and free from error.

translation: When Moses said to his family, “Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you some news from it, or bring you a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves.”
interpretation: This portrays Moses’ care for his family and his practical hope in a difficult, cold journey: he intends either to obtain useful guidance from the fire or to bring them warmth. Yet behind this ordinary search for help lies the beginning of a momentous divine encounter, showing how God may open great guidance through seemingly modest human aims.

translation: Then, when he came to it, he was called: “Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it. Glory be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: When Moses approached the fire, Allah addressed him through a sacred manifestation, declaring the place and those honored around it to be blessed. The verse affirms Allah’s transcendence above any physical location or form: the blessing belongs to the divine sign and the angelic presence surrounding it, while Allah remains exalted beyond all created qualities and is the Lord of the entire universe.

translation: O Moses, indeed it is I—Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: Allah identifies Himself to Moses as the One who is supreme in power and perfect in wisdom, assuring him that the call he is receiving comes from the true Lord whose commands are always governed by might and wisdom.

translation: “And throw down your staff.” Then when he saw it moving as though it were a serpent, he turned away, retreating and did not look back. “O Moses, do not fear. Indeed, My messengers have no fear in My presence.”
interpretation: When Moses witnessed the miraculous transformation of his staff, he instinctively recoiled, so God reassured him that the miracle was under divine control and that those chosen as His messengers are secure in His presence. The verse teaches that awe and initial fear may arise naturally, but trust in God should overcome them.

translation: Except for whoever has done wrong, then replaces evil with good; indeed, I am Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: الوعيد لا يشمل من تاب من ظلمه توبة صادقة، فأصلح عمله واستبدل الإساءة بالإحسان؛ فالله يغفر له ويتفضل عليه برحمته.

translation: And put your hand into your breast pocket; it will come out white, without harm. This is among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a rebellious people.
interpretation: Moses was given a visible miracle: his hand would shine with whiteness without illness or injury, confirming his prophetic mission. It was one of nine signs sent to Pharaoh and his people, yet their persistent defiance and departure from obedience prevented them from accepting the truth.

translation: So when Our signs came to them, clear and illuminating, they said, “This is unmistakable magic.”
interpretation: When God’s miraculous signs were presented to them with undeniable clarity, they rejected them rather than submitting to the truth, dismissing them as sorcery despite recognizing their evident power.

translation: They denied them, although their hearts were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance. So observe how terrible was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: The verse portrays denial not as the result of genuine uncertainty, but as a deliberate refusal to submit to truth that had become inwardly certain. Injustice and pride led them to oppose it, and their fate demonstrates that persistent corruption and arrogant rejection ultimately bring ruin.

translation: And We certainly gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, “Praise be to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.”
interpretation: Allah granted David and Solomon knowledge that enabled them to judge, govern, and fulfill their responsibilities. Their response shows that true knowledge produces gratitude and humility: they attributed their distinction entirely to Allah, while recognizing that His favor is a gift and not a cause for arrogance or contempt toward others.

translation: And Solomon inherited David, and he said, “O people, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been granted something of everything. Indeed, this is clearly the فضل (bounty) from Allah.”
interpretation: Solomon’s inheritance of David refers to the succession of prophethood, wisdom, authority, and knowledge—not merely worldly wealth. By understanding the communication of birds and receiving diverse means of governance and benefit, Solomon recognized that his abilities and kingdom were divine gifts. His words express gratitude and humility: every remarkable capacity is a manifest bounty from Allah, not a basis for pride or self-glorification.

translation: And Solomon’s armies of jinn, humans, and birds were gathered for him, arranged in ordered ranks.
interpretation: The verse portrays the extraordinary kingdom God granted Solomon: diverse creatures were placed under his command and disciplined into an organized force, revealing both divine favor and Solomon’s remarkable authority.

translation: حتى إذا أتوا على وادي النمل قالت نملة: يا أيها النمل، ادخلوا مساكنكم، لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية حرص النملة على إنقاذ قومها، مع تنزيه سليمان وجنوده عن قصد الظلم؛ فالضرر قد يقع أحيانًا بغير تعمّد، ولذلك ينبغي التنبه إلى عواقب الأفعال وحماية الضعفاء منها.

translation: So he smiled, amused by her words, and said, “My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You, and admit me, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants.”
interpretation: Prophet Solomon’s smile reflects compassionate understanding of the ant’s warning, not mockery. His prayer shows that recognizing one’s blessings should lead to gratitude, righteous action, and humility: even one who has been given great authority depends on God’s enabling grace and seeks acceptance among the righteous through divine mercy.

translation: And he inspected the birds and said, “Why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?”
interpretation: This portrays Solomon’s attentiveness to those under his authority: even the absence of a seemingly insignificant creature did not escape his notice, reflecting responsible leadership and accountability.

translation: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him, unless he brings me a clear justification.
interpretation: This is the statement of Prophet Solomon concerning the hoopoe, expressing that authority and responsibility require accountability for absence or disobedience, while leaving room for a valid, clear explanation before judgment is carried out.

translation: Then he remained away for only a short while and said, “I have learned what you have not learned, and I have brought you certain news from Sheba.”
interpretation: The hoopoe returns to Prophet Solomon with verified knowledge of a distant people and presents it confidently, showing that Allah may reveal important information through even a seemingly insignificant creature and that claims should be grounded in certainty rather than conjecture.

translation: “I found a woman ruling over them; she has been given everything, and she possesses a magnificent throne.”
interpretation: The hoopoe informs Solomon that the people are governed by a woman endowed with extensive worldly authority, wealth, and power, symbolized by her magnificent throne; this introduces the contrast between her material sovereignty and the guidance Solomon will call her people toward.

translation: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. Satan had made their deeds seem pleasing to them, so he turned them away from the path, and they are not guided.
interpretation: The verse portrays how false worship can become deeply entrenched when evil makes it appear attractive and legitimate, causing people to abandon the truth and lose the ability to recognize the way to Allah.

translation: Why do they not prostrate themselves before Allah, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal and what you reveal?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who turn to created things instead of worshipping Allah, whose perfect knowledge encompasses every hidden reality and every secret or public act; such complete knowledge and power make Him alone worthy of submission.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne.
interpretation: This affirms Allah’s absolute oneness and sovereignty: none is worthy of worship besides Him, and He is the supreme Lord and Master of the majestic Throne, possessing perfect authority over all creation.

translation: He said, “We shall see whether you have spoken the truth or are among the liars.”
interpretation: Solomon did not accept the report without verification; he intended to investigate its evidence and establish whether the claim was truthful or false.

translation: Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them and see what response they give.
interpretation: Solomon instructs the messenger to present his message to the people with dignity and then observe their reaction from a distance, reflecting careful judgment, patience, and strategic wisdom in dealing with them.

translation: She said, “O chiefs, indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me.”
interpretation: The Queen of Sheba recognized the message as serious and dignified, so she presented it respectfully to her council, acknowledging its importance before deciding how to respond.

translation: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
interpretation: هذه رسالة سليمان عليه السلام، افتتحها بذكر اسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، معلنًا أن ما يدعو إليه قائم على طاعة الله ورحمته، لا على القوة المجردة أو التعالي.

translation: Do not exalt yourselves above me, and come to me in submission.
interpretation: This is a command calling the addressed people to abandon pride and resistance to the truth, and to submit sincerely to God’s authority rather than remain attached to worldly power.

translation: She said, “O council, advise me concerning my affair. I would never decide a matter until you are present with me.”
interpretation: The queen’s words show her deliberate and consultative leadership: she refuses to act hastily in a serious matter and seeks the counsel of those entrusted with the affairs of her kingdom before reaching a decision.

translation: They said, “We possess great strength and formidable might, but the command is yours; so consider what you will order.”
interpretation: The leaders acknowledge their military power while deferring the final decision to their queen, indicating that authority and wise judgment—not strength alone—should determine how they respond to a serious threat.

translation: She said, “Indeed, when kings enter a land, they ruin it and reduce its honored people to humiliation. That is what they do.”
interpretation: The queen recognized that military conquest by rulers commonly brings destruction and strips a people of their dignity and authority, so her words express caution against responding to Solomon’s message through rash confrontation.

translation: “I am going to send them a gift and then await what the messengers bring back.”
interpretation: The queen chose diplomacy and a measured test rather than immediate confrontation, intending to gauge Solomon’s response and discern whether his message was truly prophetic or merely an attempt to exert worldly power.

translation: When they came to Solomon, he said, “Would you supplement me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.”
interpretation: Solomon rejected the attempted gift because divine guidance, authority, and blessings are far greater than worldly wealth. His response exposes the emptiness of taking pride in material offerings when they are used to influence truth or purchase favor.

translation: Return to them, for we shall certainly come upon them with forces they will have no power to resist, and we shall surely drive them out of it humbled and disgraced.
interpretation: This is a firm warning from Solomon that the queen’s kingdom will face overwhelming defeat if it persists in resisting his call; worldly power cannot protect those who respond to truth with arrogance, and such defiance ends in humiliation.

translation: He said, “O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?”
interpretation: Solomon, peace be upon him, sought to have the Queen of Sheba’s throne brought to him before her arrival, demonstrating the extraordinary power Allah had granted him and preparing a clear sign that would guide her toward recognizing the truth and submitting to Allah.

translation: A powerful one among the jinn said, “I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it.”
interpretation: The jinn servant presents his extraordinary ability as being accompanied by both strength and reliability: he claims he can transport the throne swiftly and will preserve it faithfully without loss or betrayal. The verse also shows that such power remains subordinate to the command and judgment of Solomon.

translation: قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب: «أنا آتيك به قبل أن يرتدَّ إليك طرفك». فلما رآه مستقرًّا عنده قال: «هذا من فضل ربي ليبلوني أأشكر أم أكفر؛ ومن شكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه، ومن كفر فإن ربي غنيٌّ كريم».
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن ما يقع من النعم والقدرات الخارقة ليس استقلالًا من العبد، بل هو فضل من الله وتسخير منه؛ ولذلك كان الواجب أن يقود ظهور النعمة إلى شكرٍ صادق، لأن منفعة الشكر تعود إلى صاحبه بزيادة الهداية والفضل، أما كفران النعمة فلا يضر الله، إذ هو غني عن خلقه، ومع ذلك يظل كريمًا لا يعاجلهم بالعقوبة.

translation: He said, “Disguise her throne for her; let us see whether she will recognize it or be among those who are not guided.”
interpretation: Solomon ordered the throne to be altered as a test of the queen’s discernment and judgment, revealing whether she would perceive the truth through careful understanding or fail to be guided by it.

translation: Then when she arrived, it was said, “Is your throne like this?” She said, “It seems to be it.” And we had been given knowledge before her, and we had submitted [to Allah].
interpretation: The queen’s cautious reply reflects wisdom and discernment: she recognized the throne without making an unwarranted absolute claim, while the verse indicates that the truth had already begun to reach her before this encounter. Her eventual submission was therefore grounded in sincere recognition of Allah’s signs and guidance, not merely in amazement at Solomon’s power.

translation: What she had been worshipping besides Allah had kept her from faith; indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.
interpretation: Her former devotion to other than Allah had veiled her from recognizing the truth, and she belonged to a society whose disbelief had shaped her beliefs and practice.

translation: It was said to her, “Enter the palace.” When she saw it, she thought it was a deep body of water and uncovered her legs. He said, “It is a palace paved with smooth glass.” She said, “My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit, with Solomon, to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: The scene revealed to her the limits of her assumptions and the truth of Solomon’s message. Recognizing that she had been deceived by false beliefs, she humbly acknowledged her wrongdoing and submitted herself, together with Solomon, to the one true Lord of all creation.

translation: And We certainly sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ, saying, “Worship Allah.” Then suddenly they became two parties disputing.
interpretation: Allah sent Ṣāliḥ as a familiar and trustworthy member of Thamūd to call them to exclusive worship of Him. Yet instead of uniting around the truth, they divided into believers and rejecters, showing how guidance can expose people’s opposing responses and turn faith into a matter of dispute when pride and denial prevail.

translation: He said, “O my people, why do you hasten toward evil before good? Why do you not seek Allah’s forgiveness, so that you may receive mercy?”
interpretation: The speaker rebukes his people for demanding punishment and treating the coming evil as more urgent than repentance and obedience, even though Allah’s mercy remains open to them through sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness.

translation: They said, “We take you and those with you as an evil omen.” He said, “Your omen is with Allah. Rather, you are a people being tested.”
interpretation: The people blamed Ṣāliḥ and the believers for the hardships they faced, treating their presence as a bad omen instead of recognizing their own rejection and wrongdoing. Ṣāliḥ corrected them by affirming that whatever befalls them is under Allah’s decree and connected to His judgment, while their denial itself is a test through which their faith, sincerity, and response to truth are exposed.

translation: And in the city there were nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform.
interpretation: These nine influential men had made corruption their deliberate way of life: they abused their power, undermined righteousness, and had no genuine intention of setting matters right. The verse warns that organized wrongdoing by a small but powerful group can threaten an entire society when it is pursued without repentance or reform.

translation: They said, “Swear to one another by Allah: we will surely attack him and his family by night, then we will say to his guardian, ‘We did not witness the destruction of his family, and we are certainly telling the truth.’”
interpretation: This portrays the conspirators’ deliberate use of oaths and fabricated testimony to conceal their intended crime, revealing how hostility can lead people to combine violence with deceit while falsely invoking Allah as a witness.

translation: They devised a plot, and We devised a plan, while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse portrays the conspirators’ false confidence: they secretly planned harm, unaware that God had already encompassed their scheme with His knowledge and was directing its consequences against them. It warns that human plotting cannot escape divine awareness or overturn God’s judgment.

translation: So look at what the outcome of their plotting was: We destroyed them and their people, all together.
interpretation: This is a warning that schemes founded on wrongdoing cannot escape divine judgment; those who plotted evil were destroyed along with the community that supported or shared in their crime.

translation: Those are their houses, lying desolate because of their wrongdoing. Indeed, in that is a sign for people who possess knowledge.
interpretation: The abandoned homes of those people stand as a lasting warning that injustice and corruption ultimately destroy those who commit them; those who reflect with understanding recognize this as a sign of God’s justice and power.

translation: And We saved those who believed and were mindful of God.
interpretation: God’s deliverance is granted to those whose faith is sincere and whose awareness of Him leads them to avoid wrongdoing and remain obedient; their belief and reverent conduct become a means of salvation from the consequences of evil.

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, “Do you commit this outrage while you see?”
interpretation: Prophet Lot rebukes his people for knowingly engaging in a grave sexual immorality, emphasizing that they were not acting out of ignorance but were consciously witnessing the wrongfulness of their conduct.

translation: “Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people acting ignorantly.”
interpretation: This is Prophet Lot’s rebuke of his people for pursuing sexual desire in a manner that defied the moral guidance revealed to them; their conduct is described as ignorance because it reflected rejection of divine limits rather than a lack of knowledge alone.

translation: So the only response of his people was to say, “Expel the family of Lot from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.”
interpretation: Rather than answering Lot’s call or confronting the wrongdoing among themselves, his people resorted to expulsion and mockery. They regarded his family’s moral purity as something offensive and alien, revealing how corruption can cause people to reject those who uphold righteousness and portray virtue as a threat to their way of life.

translation: So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We had destined her to be among those who remained behind.
interpretation: Allah rescued Lot and his believing household, while his wife was excluded because she persisted with the disbelieving people; family ties alone could not save her from the consequence of her chosen allegiance and conduct.

translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones]; how evil was the rain of those who had been warned.
interpretation: This describes the divine punishment that befell the people of Lot after they rejected the warning: the rain was not mercy-giving water, but a destructive shower of stones, showing the dreadful consequence of persisting in wrongdoing after clear admonition.

translation: Say, “Praise belongs to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen.” Is Allah better, or what they associate with Him?
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet to declare that all perfect praise belongs to Allah and that His chosen servants are honored with peace, then confronts the polytheists with a decisive question: can the One who creates, guides, and bestows every blessing ever be compared with powerless beings they associate with Him? The question exposes the absurdity of assigning worship to anything besides Allah.

translation: أمَّن خلق السماوات والأرض، وأنزل لكم من السماء ماءً فأنبتنا به حدائقَ ذاتَ بهجة، ما كان لكم أن تُنبتوا شجرها؟ أإلهٌ مع الله؟ بل هم قومٌ يعدلون.
interpretation: تُقيم الآية حجةً على وحدانية الله بلفت النظر إلى خلق السماوات والأرض وإنزال المطر وإخراج الحدائق الجميلة التي يعجز البشر عن إنباتها استقلالًا؛ فهذه النعم تدل على أن الله وحده المستحق للعبادة، وأن إشراك غيره به انحرافٌ عن الحق وتسويةٌ بين الخالق العاجز عنه سواه والمخلوق المحتاج.

translation: أمَّن جعل الأرض قرارًا، وجعل خلالها أنهارًا، وجعل لها رواسي، وجعل بين البحرين حاجزًا؟ أإلهٌ مع الله؟ بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون.
interpretation: تُقيم الآية الحجة على وحدانية الله بذكر تدبيره المحكم للأرض: ثباتها، وجريان أنهارها، ورسّو جبالها، والفصل بين المياه المختلفة بحاجز لا يطغى أحدها على الآخر. فهذه الآيات الدالة على القدرة والحكمة تنفي أن يكون مع الله شريك، غير أن أكثر الناس لا يدركون دلالتها ولا يقدّرون حق قدرها.

translation: Is He not the One who answers the desperate when he calls upon Him, removes affliction, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a deity alongside Allah? Little do you remember.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to recognize Allah alone as the true refuge in moments of helplessness: He hears the distressed person’s sincere plea, lifts hardship, and grants human beings the ability to inhabit, inherit, and exercise responsibility over the earth. These signs expose the weakness of every supposed rival to Him, yet people often remember this truth only briefly and fail to live by exclusive reliance, gratitude, and obedience to Allah.

translation: Or who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea, and sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that guidance and protection through the dangers of land and sea, as well as the winds that herald rain and mercy, come from Allah alone. These signs expose the inability of all supposed partners to provide such care, so attributing divine power to them is false and Allah is far above every form of association.

translation: أمَّن يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده، ومن يرزقكم من السماء والأرض؟ أإلهٌ مع الله؟ قل: هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين.
interpretation: يُقيم الله الحجة على المشركين بأن الذي يقدر على ابتداء الخلق ثم إعادته، والذي يرزق الخلق بما ينزل من السماء وما تُخرج الأرض، هو وحده المستحق للعبادة؛ أما دعوى وجود شريك له فلا تقوم على أي برهان، ولذلك يُطالَب من يدّعيها بدليل صادق.

translation: Say: “No one in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not know when they will be resurrected.”
interpretation: The knowledge of the unseen belongs exclusively to Allah; therefore, no created being—whether in the heavens or on earth—can independently know hidden realities or determine the time of resurrection. This calls people to reject claims of absolute knowledge of the unseen and to trust Allah’s revelation concerning what lies beyond human perception.

translation: Rather, their knowledge has failed regarding the Hereafter. Indeed, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it.
interpretation: Those who deny the Hereafter do not possess sound knowledge that proves it impossible; their uncertainty arises from deficient understanding and a refusal to recognize the signs pointing to resurrection and accountability. Their doubt has deepened into spiritual blindness, preventing them from perceiving the truth of the life to come.

translation: And those who disbelieved said, “When we have become dust, and our forefathers as well, will we truly be brought out?”
interpretation: The disbelievers reject the resurrection because they regard the return of bodies after death and decay as impossible, using the fate of themselves and their ancestors as an argument against God’s promise of being raised for judgment.

translation: لقد وُعِدنا بهذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل، وما هذا إلا أساطير الأولين.
interpretation: يعبّر المشركون عن إنكارهم للبعث والجزاء، محتجّين بأنهم سمعوا هذا الوعد من قبل من غير أن يتحقق في نظرهم، ولذلك يصفون خبر الوحي بأنه خرافات منقولة عن الأمم السابقة، بدل أن يتدبروا دلائله ويؤمنوا به.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land and observe how the fate of the criminals was.”
interpretation: This is a warning to those who persist in wrongdoing: they are urged to examine the remains and history of earlier peoples who rejected truth and committed injustice, so that they recognize that wrongdoing ultimately leads to ruin and take heed before suffering the same end.

translation: Do not grieve over them, nor be distressed by the schemes they devise.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet not to let the rejection and hostility of his opponents overwhelm him. Their plotting cannot thwart Allah’s purpose, so he should remain steadfast, patient, and reliant upon Him rather than consumed by sorrow or anxiety over their actions.

translation: And they say, “When is this promise, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They ask this mockingly, demanding the promised judgment or punishment as though its delay disproves it. The verse exposes their arrogance and reminds that disbelief often seeks to challenge divine warnings by treating delayed consequences as if they were false.

translation: Say, “Perhaps some of what you are hastening to receive has already drawn near to you.”
interpretation: This is a warning to those who mockingly demand the promised punishment: its delay should not be mistaken for denial, for part of what they challenge may already be approaching them by God’s decree. The wording also reflects divine forbearance, allowing them time to repent before the consequence arrives.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is truly gracious to people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: Allah continually bestows blessings, mercy, and opportunities for guidance upon people despite their shortcomings; yet most fail to recognize these favors, attribute them to their true Giver, and respond with sincere gratitude and obedience.

translation: And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: Nothing hidden within people or expressed openly escapes Allah’s knowledge; therefore, their inner intentions and outward actions are equally subject to His judgment.

translation: There is nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth except that it is recorded in a clear Book.
interpretation: Nothing that is concealed or unknown to people escapes Allah’s knowledge; every matter, whether apparent or hidden, is preserved and fully recorded in the clear Record.

translation: Indeed, this Qur’an recounts to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a decisive revelation that clarifies the major disputes among the Children of Israel, distinguishing truth from distortion and guiding people back to the judgment of God rather than to conflicting human claims.

translation: And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: The Qur’an guides believers to truth and righteous conduct, and through that guidance brings them spiritual mercy, protection, and success.

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His judgment; and He is the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah alone has the ultimate authority to settle their disputes and reveal the truth, judging with irresistible power and complete knowledge that leaves no injustice or uncertainty.

translation: So put your trust in Allah; indeed, you are upon the clear truth.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to depend confidently on Him, because the message he conveys is unmistakably true, regardless of how strongly those who reject it oppose him.

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.
interpretation: The verse teaches that those whose hearts are spiritually dead or deaf cannot benefit from the truth when they deliberately turn away from it; guidance may be conveyed, but it cannot be forced upon one who refuses to listen.

translation: And you cannot guide the blind out of their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, for they are Muslims.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Messenger’s role is to convey the truth, not to compel faith. Those whose hearts are spiritually receptive benefit from revelation, believe in Allah’s signs, and respond by submitting to Him, while persistent inner blindness prevents a person from accepting guidance.

translation: And when the decree is fulfilled against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, saying that people did not have certainty in Our signs.
interpretation: This describes a decisive sign before the final reckoning: a creature brought forth by God will confront those who persistently rejected His revelations and expose their lack of genuine certainty. Its appearance marks the point at which denial is unmistakably revealed and repentance can no longer be based on unseen faith.

translation: And on the Day We gather from every nation a group of those who deny Our signs, they will be marshalled in ranks.
interpretation: This portrays a terrifying stage of judgment in which the chief deniers from every community are assembled and restrained under divine command, emphasizing that rejection of God’s signs will be confronted collectively and with complete accountability.

translation: When they arrive, He will say, “Did you deny My signs without having comprehended them in knowledge? Or what were you doing?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who rejected God’s revelations without sincerely seeking to understand them. On the Day of Judgment, their denial will be exposed as baseless negligence, and they will have no valid explanation for turning away from the truth and misusing their lives.

translation: And the decree will be fulfilled against them because of their wrongdoing, and they will not speak.
interpretation: The punishment promised to those who persist in injustice will become unavoidable, and when it overtakes them, they will be deprived of any effective defense or excuse before God.

translation: Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest in, and the day bright and illuminating? Indeed, in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is a clear sign of God’s wisdom and mercy: He has ordered creation so that people may find rest in darkness and pursue their work and perceive the world in daylight. Those who believe recognize in this balanced rhythm evidence of God’s power, purposeful design, and care for His creation.

translation: And on the Day the Trumpet will be blown, all those in the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except those whom Allah wills; and all will come to Him in humble submission.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming terror of the Day of Resurrection: every creature in the heavens and on earth will be shaken by the divine summons, while those granted Allah’s protection will be spared its terror. Ultimately, all creation will appear before Him powerless and completely humbled.

translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them to be still, while they pass like clouds. This is the work of Allah, who perfected everything. Indeed, He is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن ما يبدو ثابتًا راسخًا قد يجري بأمره وتدبيره، وأن إحكام خلقه لا يخفى معه شيء من أعمال الناس؛ ففي الآية تذكير بقدرته التامة وإحاطته الدقيقة بما يفعلون، ولا سيما في مشاهد يوم القيامة حين تتغير معالم الكون.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day.
interpretation: Allah promises that sincere good deeds will be rewarded with something greater than the deed itself, and that those who come with such deeds will be granted security from the fear and distress of the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrust into the Fire: “Are you recompensed for anything other than what you used to do?”
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in wrongdoing will face a humiliating punishment corresponding to their own deeds; the question emphasizes that this judgment is just and not arbitrary, but the consequence of what they themselves chose to do.

translation: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred; and to Him belongs everything. I have been commanded to be among those who submit to Him.
interpretation: The verse expresses the Prophet’s complete devotion to God alone: the Lord of Makkah, who granted it sanctity, is also the owner and sovereign of all creation. It teaches that true submission consists in worshipping Him exclusively and accepting His command with humility, obedience, and wholehearted faith.

translation: And to recite the Qur’an. So whoever follows guidance, follows it only for his own benefit; and whoever goes astray, then say, “I am only one of the warners.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s duty is to convey and recite Allah’s revelation, not to compel people to accept it. Guidance benefits the person who embraces it, while misguidance harms only the one who turns away; the messenger’s responsibility is to warn clearly and faithfully.

translation: And say, “All praise belongs to Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. Your Lord is not unaware of what you do.”
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to affirm His perfect praise and reminds people that His signs will become unmistakably clear to them. Since Allah fully knows and observes their actions, they should not persist in denial or wrongdoing, imagining that their deeds escape His knowledge or judgment.

translation: طهٰ سِين مِيم — طسم
interpretation: هذه من الحروف المقطَّعة التي افتتحت بها بعض السور، وحقيقتها التفصيلية مما استأثر الله بعلمه؛ وفيها تنبيه إلى إعجاز القرآن المؤلَّف من حروف الهجاء نفسها التي يعرفها الناس.

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s message is presented as a clear, manifest revelation whose verses plainly convey guidance and truth to those who listen with understanding.

translation: We recite to you, in truth, some of the account of Moses and Pharaoh for a people who believe.
interpretation: This revelation presents the history of Moses and Pharaoh as truthful divine guidance, so believers may recognize that God supports truth and justice, exposes tyranny, and grants deliverance to those who remain faithful.

translation: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, weakening one group among them: he slaughtered their sons and spared their women. Indeed, he was among the corrupters.
