interpretation: The verse exposes how tyranny is sustained through arrogance, division, and the deliberate oppression of a vulnerable people. Pharaoh’s persecution of the Israelites was not merely personal cruelty; it was systematic corruption that sought to preserve power by weakening a targeted community and destroying its future, while affirming that such domination ultimately places its perpetrator among those who spread ruin.

translation: And We desired to show favor to those who had been oppressed in the land, to make them leaders, and to make them the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah’s promise that oppression does not have the final word: He can raise the downtrodden to dignity, authority, and stewardship, transforming their weakness into leadership and enabling them to inherit the land after enduring injustice.

translation: ونُمكِّن لهم في الأرض، ونُري فرعونَ وهامانَ وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن تمكين المستضعفين في الأرض وإظهار قوتهم سيكون سببًا في إبطال سلطان فرعون؛ إذ سيرى هو وأعوانه بأعينهم تحقق الأمر الذي خافوه، وهو أن ينشأ من بني إسرائيل من يهدد ملكهم ويقلب موازين القوة عليهم.

translation: And We inspired the mother of Moses: “Nurse him; then, when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear or grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers.”
interpretation: This verse shows that divine care can guide a believer through an impossible situation: Moses’ mother was commanded to entrust her child to the river, not as an act of despair, but with certainty that God would protect him, restore him to her, and prepare him for a greater mission.

translation: Then the household of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he would become for them an enemy and a source of grief. Indeed, Pharaoh, Hāmān, and their armies were sinners.
interpretation: Although Pharaoh’s people rescued Moses as an infant, God’s decree made him the very means through which their power would be challenged and their downfall brought about. Their oppression and wrongdoing led them unknowingly to nurture the one who would oppose them.

translation: And Pharaoh’s wife said, “He is a source of joy for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son,” while they were unaware.
interpretation: This verse portrays how God’s providence can preserve the vulnerable through unexpected means: the child whom Pharaoh’s tyranny sought to eliminate was protected within Pharaoh’s own household. Pharaoh’s wife recognized his innocence and potential, while their failure to perceive his true significance shows how human plans can unknowingly serve a divine purpose.

translation: And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty; she was about to reveal what had happened, had We not strengthened her heart so that she might be among the believers.
interpretation: After entrusting her infant son to the river by God’s command, Moses’ mother was overwhelmed by anxiety and longing, nearly disclosing that he was her child. God steadied her heart with patience and faith, enabling her to endure the trial and trust His promise of protection.

translation: And she said to his sister, “Follow him.” So she watched him from a distance, while they were unaware.
interpretation: Moses’ mother instructed his sister to discreetly trace what happened to him after he was placed in the river. His sister kept watch from afar without those caring for him realizing that she was connected to him.

translation: And We had forbidden him all nursing mothers before that, so she said, “Shall I direct you to a household who will care for him for you and be sincere toward him?”
interpretation: Allah caused Moses to reject every nurse so that he would not accept nourishment from anyone but his own mother, while guiding his sister to suggest a trustworthy household. Through this means, Moses was returned to his mother, whose care and affection were assured, and Allah’s promise to protect and restore him was fulfilled.

translation: So We restored him to his mother, so that her eyes might be comforted and she would not grieve, and so that she would know that God’s promise is true—yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: God arranged for Moses to return safely to his mother after she had been overwhelmed by fear and sorrow. This fulfilled His promise to her and taught that divine promises remain true even when circumstances appear hopeless; people often fail to recognize this wisdom because their knowledge is limited.

translation: And when he reached maturity and attained full strength, We granted him wisdom and knowledge. Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: When Moses reached complete physical and intellectual maturity, God bestowed upon him sound judgment and sacred knowledge, showing that sincere excellence in faith and conduct is met with divine guidance and favor.

translation: And he entered the city at a time when its people were unaware, and found there two men fighting—one from his own people and the other from his enemies. The one from his own people appealed to him for help against the one from his enemies, so Moses struck him, and it brought about his death. He said, “This is from the work of Satan; indeed, he is a manifest enemy who leads astray.”
interpretation: Moses intervened to defend the oppressed man from his own people, but his forceful blow unintentionally caused the other man’s death. Recognizing that the incident had resulted from Satan’s prompting toward conflict and its disastrous consequences, Moses immediately disavowed it, acknowledged the gravity of what had occurred, and understood Satan as an evident enemy who misleads people through anger and strife.

translation: قال: «ربِّ، إني ظلمتُ نفسي، فاغفر لي»، فغفر له؛ إنه هو الغفور الرحيم.
interpretation: يُظهر هذا الدعاء صدقَ التوبة؛ فقد اعترف موسى عليه السلام بتبعة فعله، والتجأ إلى الله وحده طالبًا مغفرته، فبادره الله بعفوه ورحمته. وفي ذلك بيانٌ أن الإقرار بالخطأ والرجوع الصادق إلى الله من أسباب المغفرة.

translation: He said, “My Lord, because of the favor You have bestowed upon me, I will never support the criminals.”
interpretation: Moses recognizes God’s grace and commits himself to justice, declaring that he will never assist wrongdoing or stand with those who perpetrate it.

translation: So he became in the city fearful and watchful; then suddenly the man who had sought his help the day before cried out to him for help. Moses said to him, “Indeed, you are clearly misguided.”
interpretation: Moses realized that the man’s repeated quarrelsome behavior was leading him into trouble and exposing the whole situation, so he rebuked him for acting in an evidently misguided and reckless manner.

translation: Then, when he intended to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, “O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to become a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be one of those who set things right.”
interpretation: The man’s words reveal that Moses’ previous act had become known and portray his intervention as dangerous violence rather than rightful reform. His accusation exposes Moses to suspicion before the authorities, showing how a good intention can be undermined when force is used impulsively and without a secure means of achieving justice.

translation: And a man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, “O Moses, the chiefs are consulting together about killing you, so leave. Truly, I am one of those who sincerely advise you.”
interpretation: This verse portrays sincere counsel expressed through courage and urgency: the man risked himself to warn Moses of a hidden plot, while Moses was called to respond to danger with prudence by leaving the city. It also shows that truth and loyalty may come from unexpected people, and that offering timely protection to the innocent is a noble duty.

translation: So he left it, fearful and vigilant. He said, “My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: This depicts Moses fleeing Pharaoh’s tyranny while remaining alert to danger, and turning in sincere reliance to God for protection from the oppressors.

translation: And when he turned his direction toward Midian, he said, “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.”
interpretation: After leaving Egypt with no clear destination or worldly support, Moses placed his trust in Allah and set out toward Midian. His prayer expresses humility and hope: he recognized that only Allah could guide him to the safest and most upright path, both in reaching a place of refuge and in finding the course of life meant for him.

translation: When he came to the well of Midian, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and apart from them he found two women holding theirs back. He said, “What is your situation?” They said, “We cannot water until the shepherds have driven their flocks away, and our father is a very old man.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Moses’ compassion and sense of justice: he notices the vulnerability of the two women, asks about their circumstances rather than ignoring them, and reveals the hardship they endure because their elderly father cannot tend the flock himself. Their restraint reflects modesty and an unwillingness to compete with the men, while their words explain their genuine need for assistance.

translation: So he watered their flocks for them, then withdrew into the shade and said, “My Lord, I am truly in need of whatever good You may send down to me.”
interpretation: This portrays sincere service followed by humble reliance on God: Moses helped others without seeking reward, then acknowledged that every form of provision and goodness comes from God and that he was completely dependent on Him.

translation: Then one of the two women came to him, walking modestly, and said, “My father invites you so that he may reward you for watering our flocks for us.” When he came to him and recounted his story, he said, “Do not be afraid; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The verse portrays modesty, gratitude, and compassionate protection: the woman approaches with dignified reserve, her father seeks to repay the stranger’s kindness, and upon hearing Moses’ account, he reassures him that leaving the oppressive society was a deliverance from danger and injustice.

translation: One of the two women said, “O my father, hire him; surely the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.”
interpretation: She recommends Moses for employment because he has demonstrated both competence and integrity: the strength to carry out demanding responsibilities and the trustworthiness to safeguard what is entrusted to him. The verse teaches that sound judgment in choosing a worker rests not merely on ability, nor merely on good character, but on the combination of capability and trust.

translation: He said, “I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on the condition that you serve me for eight years. If you complete ten, that will be of your own generosity. I do not wish to burden you; you will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous.”
interpretation: The verse portrays a lawful marriage agreement founded on clarity, mutual consent, and fairness. The father specifies the required period of service, presents the additional two years as voluntary rather than obligatory, and assures that he does not intend hardship or exploitation. It therefore teaches that agreements should be transparent, obligations should not exceed what was agreed upon, and dealings should be governed by integrity, kindness, and trust in Allah.

translation: He said, “That is settled between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me. And Allah is Witness over what we say.”
interpretation: This is a confirmation of the agreement between Moses and his prospective father-in-law: Moses accepts either the shorter or longer period of service, and once he completes the term he chooses, neither party may accuse him of failing in his obligation. By invoking Allah as Witness, they affirm that their covenant is made openly and must be honored with fairness and integrity.

translation: And when Moses had completed the appointed term and was traveling with his family, he perceived a fire on the side of the mountain. He said to his family, “Stay here; I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you some news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves.”
interpretation: This scene shows how Allah’s guidance can begin through an ordinary need: while Moses sought fire and information for his family, Allah was leading him toward the moment of revelation and his prophetic mission. His concern for his family also reflects his responsible and caring character.

translation: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين
interpretation: حين وصل موسى إلى النار، ناداه الله من جانب الوادي الأيمن، في الموضع المبارك، عند الشجرة، معلنًا له أنه الله وحده رب جميع العوالم، فكان ذلك ابتداء وحيه وتكليفه بالرسالة.

translation: “And throw down your staff.” But when he saw it writhing as though it were a serpent, he turned away, fleeing, and did not look back. “O Moses, come forward and do not fear; surely you are among those who are safe.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Moses’s instinctive fear before an extraordinary sign, while affirming that God’s command is accompanied by protection. His retreat is met not with blame but with reassurance, teaching that genuine faith may begin with human apprehension yet must ultimately rest in trust in God’s safeguarding power.

translation: “Put your hand into the opening of your garment; it will come out shining white, without any affliction. And draw your arm close to yourself to calm your fear. These, then, are two proofs from your Lord for Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they were a rebellious people.”
interpretation: God equips Moses with two unmistakable signs: the radiant hand and the restoration of his composure after fear. Together they demonstrate that his mission is divinely supported, while Pharaoh and his leaders are condemned for persistently exceeding God’s bounds and rejecting the truth.

translation: He said, “My Lord, I killed one of them, and I fear that they will kill me.”
interpretation: Moses appeals to God while expressing his fear that Pharaoh’s people will retaliate for the man he unintentionally killed, revealing his awareness of the danger he faces and his dependence on God’s protection.

translation: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech, so send him with me as a helper to affirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: Moses asks Allah to send Aaron with him because Aaron’s greater eloquence will support the delivery of the message and help establish its truth before a people he fears will reject or accuse him.

translation: He said, “We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant both of you authority, so they will not be able to reach you. By Our signs, you two and those who follow you will be victorious.”
interpretation: God reassures Moses that Aaron’s support will reinforce his mission and that divine authority and protection will prevail over Pharaoh’s power. The promised victory belongs not to their personal strength, but to God’s signs and to those who faithfully follow them.

translation: Then when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, “This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have never heard of anything like this among our earliest forefathers.”
interpretation: When confronted with unmistakable divine signs, Pharaoh’s people rejected them without genuine examination, dismissing them as invented magic and appealing to ancestral custom as a justification for refusing revelation. This reflects how pride, attachment to inherited beliefs, and fear of change can lead people to deny clear truth.

translation: And Moses said, “My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him and who will have the favorable outcome of the abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper.”
interpretation: Moses entrusts the judgment of truth and ultimate success to Allah, affirming that genuine guidance is known by Him and that the final victory belongs to those who follow it. Those who reject the truth and oppress others may appear powerful temporarily, but they cannot attain lasting success with Allah.

translation: Pharaoh said, “O council, I know of no god for you other than me. So kindle a fire for me over the clay, O Hāmān, and build me a lofty tower, that I may look upon the God of Moses, though I truly think he is among the liars.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s words reveal how tyranny turns political authority into a claim of absolute divinity. By demanding a tower to search for Moses’ God, he disguises arrogance and deliberate denial as an appeal to physical evidence, attempting to make the unseen subject to his control. His accusation that Moses is lying reflects not a sincere pursuit of truth, but the ruler’s effort to preserve his power by discrediting the message that challenges it.

translation: And he and his armies acted arrogantly in the land without right, thinking that they would not be returned to Us.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s tyranny arose from an unjust sense of superiority and from denying accountability before God. Their worldly power deceived them into believing that death and resurrection would never bring them before Him for judgment.

translation: So We seized him and his armies and cast them into the sea. See, then, how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: God brought Pharaoh and his forces to a decisive end by drowning them, demonstrating that tyranny and injustice may persist for a time but ultimately lead to ruin when confronted by divine judgment.

translation: And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.
interpretation: Because they chose arrogance, disbelief, and rebellion, they became examples whose influence led others away from faith and toward punishment. Their worldly power will not benefit them in the Hereafter, nor will anyone be able to rescue them from God’s judgment.

translation: And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the disgraced.
interpretation: Their wrongdoing brought upon them rejection and loss of honor in this life, and it will culminate in humiliation and disgrace before all on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations, as clear insights for the people, and as guidance and mercy, so that they might take heed.
interpretation: After the destruction of earlier peoples because of their rejection and wrongdoing, God gave Moses the Scripture to illuminate the truth for humanity. It was not merely a record of laws, but a means of spiritual vision, guidance toward the right path, and mercy that could save people from repeating the fate of those who came before them—if they reflected and took heed.

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses, nor were you among the witnesses.
interpretation: This affirms that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did not learn the account of Moses through personal observation or human testimony; rather, its detailed revelation is evidence that it came to him from Allah.

translation: But We brought forth generations, and a long span of time passed over them. You were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting Our revelations to them; rather, We have been sending messengers.
interpretation: Allah clarifies that the Prophet’s knowledge of the people of Madyan and their history did not come from personal presence or human instruction; it was conveyed to him through divine revelation, as part of Allah’s continuing practice of sending guidance to humanity.

translation: You were not on the side of the Mount when We called, but this is a mercy from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that he did not witness the calling of Moses at the Mount; his knowledge of such unseen events came through divine revelation. This revelation is an act of mercy, granting guidance and warning to a people who had lacked a messenger, so that they might awaken from heedlessness and return to the truth.

translation: And if it were not that, when a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, they would say, “Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so that we might follow Your revelations and be among the believers?”
interpretation: Allah makes clear that sending messengers establishes the proof against people, so they cannot claim ignorance or use the consequences of their own wrongdoing as an excuse for rejecting faith. The verse also shows that their appeal would come only after affliction, whereas true faith requires responding to divine guidance before punishment arrives.

translation: When the truth came to them from Us, they said, “Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?” Did they not disbelieve before in what Moses was given? They said, “Two works of magic supporting one another,” and they said, “Indeed, we disbelieve in all of it.”
interpretation: When the Qur’an came with the truth, the rejecters demanded signs like those associated with Moses, yet their objection was not sincere, for they had already rejected Moses and his revelation. They therefore dismissed both revelations as mutually reinforcing magic, revealing that their real motive was refusal to submit to divine truth rather than a genuine search for evidence.

translation: Say, “Then bring a scripture from Allah that is more guiding than either of them, and I will follow it, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who reject the Qur’an: if they claim that another revelation is more rightly guided than it and the Torah, they must produce a genuine divine scripture that offers clearer and truer guidance; otherwise, their claim is without proof.

translation: So if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: When a person rejects revealed truth without a valid response, the rejection is driven not by sincere pursuit of knowledge but by desire and self-interest. Following personal inclination instead of divine guidance leads to the greatest misguidance, and persistent injustice prevents a person from receiving Allah’s guidance.

translation: And We have conveyed the Word to them repeatedly, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: God has continually delivered His guidance to them through revelation and successive reminders, leaving them no excuse for neglecting it and giving them every opportunity to reflect, remember, and return to the truth.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it.
interpretation: This refers to sincere people among the earlier scriptural communities who, having knowledge of divine revelation, recognize the truth of the Qur’an and accept it when it comes to them.

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, “We believe in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Surely, even before it came, we had submitted.”
interpretation: This describes sincere believers among the People of the Scripture who recognize the Qur’an as confirming the truth they had already accepted from their revelation. Their submission to God leads them to accept the Qur’an when its message is recited to them, rather than rejecting it out of prejudice.

translation: Those will be granted their reward twice over for their perseverance. They repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This describes people whose steadfastness in faith and obedience earns them multiplied reward. Their character is shown by responding to harm and wrongdoing with goodness rather than revenge, and by recognizing God’s provision through generously giving from it.

translation: And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say, “Our deeds are for us, and your deeds are for you. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the company of the ignorant.”
interpretation: The verse teaches believers to preserve their dignity and peace by refusing to engage in futile or offensive speech. They should separate themselves from ignorance without responding with hostility, leaving others accountable for their own choices and actions.

translation: Indeed, you cannot guide whoever you love, but Allah guides whom He wills; and He knows best who are rightly guided.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that a messenger or any person may convey truth, counsel, and sincerely desire guidance for someone beloved, but the inner acceptance that leads to faith is granted by Allah alone. His guidance is based on His perfect knowledge of people’s hearts, choices, and receptiveness, so believers should fulfill their duty to convey truth without assuming responsibility for controlling another person’s faith.

translation: They say, “If we follow the guidance with you, we will be driven away from our land.” Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of all things are brought as provision from Us? Yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: They used fear of losing their homeland and security as an excuse for rejecting the truth, but God reminds them that He had already granted them safety and abundant provision in the sacred sanctuary. Their concern for worldly security blinded them to the fact that true security and sustenance come from God, not from resisting His guidance.

translation: And how many a town We have destroyed that exulted in its prosperity! Those are their dwellings, scarcely inhabited after them; and We alone are the inheritors.
interpretation: The verse warns that prosperity becomes a cause of ruin when it produces arrogance, heedlessness, and rebellion against God. The abandoned homes of former peoples testify that worldly comfort is temporary, while God remains after all possessors and civilizations have passed away.

translation: Your Lord would never destroy a people until He had sent a messenger to their central city, reciting to them Our revelations. Nor would We destroy any people unless they were wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse affirms God’s perfect justice: He does not punish a community without first establishing the truth through a messenger and clear signs. Destruction comes only after people persist in wrongdoing despite that guidance.

translation: Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment and adornment of the life of this world; but what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: Whatever worldly possessions, pleasures, and status people receive are temporary provisions that beautify this passing life, whereas the reward and nearness granted by Allah are enduring and far superior. True understanding requires not allowing fleeting worldly benefits to become the ultimate aim, but valuing what lasts with Allah above what inevitably fades.

translation: Is one to whom We have promised a good promise—and he will surely attain it—like one whom We have allowed to enjoy the pleasures of worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward for judgment?
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن مَن ينتظر وعد الله بالنعيم ويلقاه لا يستوي مع مَن أُعطي متاع الدنيا الزائل ثم يُحضَر يوم القيامة للمحاسبة؛ فالعبرة بالعاقبة الباقية لا بالمتعة المؤقتة.

translation: And on the Day He will call them and say, “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will confront those who attributed partners to Him, exposing the falsehood of their claims and showing that the beings they worshipped cannot help them or answer His call.

translation: Those against whom the decree has been fulfilled will say, “Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray; we led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We declare our innocence before You; they did not worship us.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the leaders of misguidance will acknowledge that they influenced their followers toward disbelief and error, while admitting that they themselves were already astray. They will disown those followers and deny having been worthy of worship, but this repudiation will come too late: both the misleaders and those who followed them remain accountable for choosing falsehood instead of worshipping Allah alone.

translation: And it will be said, “Call upon your partners.” So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been rightly guided!
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who attributed partners to Allah will be challenged to seek help from the beings they worshipped. Their complete inability to answer will expose the falsehood of their worship, while the punishment before them will bring them profound regret that they had not followed the guidance of true faith.

translation: And on the Day He will call them and say, “What response did you give to the messengers?”
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment when people will be held accountable for how they received and responded to God’s messengers, with their own choices standing as evidence against them.

translation: Then all arguments will be obscured to them on that Day, and they will not be able to question one another.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be overwhelmed and left without any convincing response; their former excuses will fail them, and they will be unable even to consult one another or find a way to defend themselves.

translation: As for whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful.
interpretation: True repentance is shown not only by turning away from wrongdoing, but also by sincere faith and righteous action; such a person may hope for success through God’s mercy and acceptance.

translation: And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses; they have no choice in the matter. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute authority over creation and over the destinies and roles He assigns, so no creature may challenge His wisdom or claim a share in His choice. Human beings must submit to His judgment with trust and humility, while recognizing that attributing partners or divine authority to anything besides Him is utterly incompatible with His transcendence.

translation: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: God’s knowledge encompasses both the hidden intentions within people and the words and deeds they make apparent, so nothing about them is beyond His awareness.

translation: And He is Allah—there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs all praise in this world and the Hereafter. His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Allah alone deserves worship, gratitude, and praise in every circumstance, both in this life and the next. All authority and final judgment belong exclusively to Him, and every person will ultimately return to Him for accountability.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah were to make the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen?”
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the light and alternation of night and day are entirely in Allah’s control; no other being could remove an unending darkness. It therefore urges them to listen attentively, acknowledge Allah’s exclusive power, and turn away from associating partners with Him.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah were to make the daylight perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then perceive?”
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that the alternation of day and night is entirely under Allah’s power and mercy. Just as no one besides Him could provide the darkness and rest needed after continuous daylight, no created being deserves worship; awareness of this dependence should lead to faith, gratitude, and exclusive devotion to Allah.

translation: And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day, so that you may rest during it and seek of His bounty, and so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is a deliberate mercy from Allah: the night provides relief and restoration, while the day enables people to work and pursue their livelihoods. Recognizing this orderly provision should awaken gratitude, leading people to use both rest and activity in ways that acknowledge Allah’s favor.

translation: And on the Day He will call them and say, “Where are My partners whom you used to claim?”
interpretation: Allah will confront the polytheists with the very claim they once made, exposing the helplessness and nonexistence of the beings they associated with Him. The question is a rebuke that reveals their worship to have been based on false assumptions rather than any true authority or power.

translation: And We shall bring forth from every community a witness and say, “Bring your proof.” Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every nation will be confronted with testimony against its beliefs and deeds, leaving it no valid excuse or argument. At that moment, the certainty of Allah’s absolute truth and authority will become undeniable, while the false claims and invented objects of worship on which they relied will prove utterly baseless and disappear.

translation: Indeed, Korah was one of the people of Moses, but he wronged them. We had granted him treasures whose keys would have burdened a group of strong men. When his people said to him, “Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love those who exult,”
interpretation: The verse teaches that immense wealth becomes a cause of ruin when it leads its possessor to oppress others and take arrogant delight in worldly power. True prosperity is therefore not measured by abundance, but by humility, gratitude, and just conduct before Allah.

translation: And seek, through what Allah has granted you, the abode of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of this world. Do good, just as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.
interpretation: Use the blessings and abilities Allah has given you primarily to prepare for the Hereafter, while responsibly enjoying the lawful portion of worldly life. Let gratitude be shown through generosity and goodness toward others, and never allow worldly ambition or power to become a means of oppression and corruption, for Allah’s favor is not a license for wrongdoing.

translation: He said, “I was given it only because of knowledge I possess.” Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in power and greater in wealth? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins.
interpretation: Qārūn attributed his wealth to his own merit and knowledge, forgetting that it was a test and a gift from Allah. The destruction of people more powerful and wealthier than him demonstrates that worldly ability cannot protect anyone from divine judgment. Allah’s knowledge of the criminals’ sins is complete, so they will not be questioned for investigation; rather, they will face the consequences of what they knowingly committed.

translation: Then he went out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, “If only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is truly a man of great fortune.”
interpretation: The verse portrays how outward wealth can captivate those whose aspirations are confined to worldly life, leading them to mistake material abundance for true success and blessing.

translation: And those who were given knowledge said, “Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, and none attain it except the patient.”
interpretation: Those grounded in true knowledge reject the allure of worldly wealth and status, recognizing that Allah’s reward is lasting and superior. It is attained through sincere faith, righteous action, and steadfast patience in resisting temptation and remaining obedient to Allah.

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling. He had no group to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.
interpretation: The verse shows that Qarun’s immense wealth and worldly influence could not protect him from divine judgment. When punishment came, neither his followers nor his own power could save him, demonstrating that protection and success ultimately belong only to Allah.

translation: And those who had longed for his position the day before began to say, “Ah, indeed Allah extends provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had Allah not shown us His favor, He could have caused the earth to swallow us. Ah, indeed the disbelievers never prosper.”
interpretation: After witnessing Qarun’s destruction, they realized that wealth and status are not signs of lasting success or divine approval. Provision is granted and restricted according to Allah’s wisdom, and only His favor protects people from being deceived by worldly riches; those who reject the truth and become arrogant ultimately fail.

translation: That home of the Hereafter We reserve for those who do not seek superiority on earth or spread corruption; and the good outcome belongs to the mindful of God.
interpretation: God grants the lasting reward of the Hereafter to those who do not pursue arrogance, domination, or elevated status over others, nor use their power to cause injustice and corruption. True success ultimately belongs to those who remain conscious of God and live by that awareness.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have something better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed—the evildoers will be recompensed only for what they used to do.
interpretation: Allah’s justice and generosity are both expressed here: every good deed is rewarded with an increase beyond its intrinsic worth, while evil is punished only in proportion to the deeds actually committed, without injustice or excess.

translation: Indeed, the One who has ordained the Qur’an for you will surely bring you back to a place of return. Say, “My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error.”
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet that the One who entrusted him with conveying the Qur’an will not abandon him, but will restore him to the honored destiny He has promised. Therefore, he need not be troubled by his opponents’ rejection; ultimate knowledge of who follows guidance and who has strayed belongs to Allah alone.

translation: You did not expect that the Book would be conveyed to you, except as a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers.
interpretation: The revelation came to you solely through your Lord’s gracious mercy, not through personal expectation or human power. Therefore, remain steadfast in your mission and never give the enemies of faith any support—whether through allegiance, compromise, or assistance against the truth.

translation: Let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you. Call people to your Lord, and never be among those who associate partners with Him.
interpretation: The verse commands steadfastness in revealed truth: neither opposition nor pressure should divert a person from accepting and conveying Allah’s guidance. One must direct worship and دعوت solely to Allah and remain completely free of every form of shirk.

translation: And do not invoke any other deity alongside Allah. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. Judgment belongs to Him, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse calls for exclusive devotion to Allah, affirming that all created things are transient while Allah alone is everlasting. Since He alone possesses ultimate authority and judgment, every person will ultimately return to Him for accountability.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: “Alif, Lām, Mīm” are among the Qur’an’s disjointed letters; their precise intended meaning is known to Allah, and they draw attention to the miraculous revelation composed from the very letters known to its hearers.

translation: Do people think that they will be left to say, “We believe,” without being tested?
interpretation: Faith is not merely a claim; it is proven through trials that reveal a person’s sincerity, steadfastness, and trust in God.

translation: We certainly tested those who came before them. Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: Faith is not established merely by words; it is revealed through trials. Such trials distinguish those whose belief is sincere and steadfast from those whose claims are false, while Allah’s knowing is manifested in the reality of their conduct.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can escape Us? Evil indeed is the judgment they make.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing must not imagine that they can evade Allah’s knowledge, power, or judgment. Their assumption that they will escape accountability is a deeply false and corrupt judgment.

translation: Whoever hopes to meet Allah—then surely Allah’s appointed time is coming. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse reassures those who long to meet Allah that the promised encounter and the reward connected to it are certain, not distant or doubtful. This hope should inspire sincere faith and steadfast obedience, knowing that Allah hears every supplication and knows every intention and deed.

translation: Whoever strives, strives only for his own soul. Indeed, Allah is free of need from all worlds.
interpretation: Striving in faith and obedience benefits the person who undertakes it, refining their character and drawing them nearer to Allah; it does not add anything to Allah’s greatness, for He is completely independent of all creation.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely erase their misdeeds and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: Allah promises that sincere faith expressed through righteous action brings His gracious forgiveness: He removes the burden of a believer’s sins and rewards their deeds with a generosity that surpasses strict measure, treating them according to the highest quality and value of what they did.

translation: And We have enjoined upon the human being kindness toward his parents. But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse establishes that honoring and treating one’s parents with kindness is a serious moral duty, yet obedience to them has a limit: one must not comply with their demand to abandon the worship of God or attribute partners to Him. Faithful devotion to God takes precedence over every human relationship, while the command to maintain good conduct toward one’s parents remains in place even when they are not followed in matters of belief. Ultimately, everyone will return to God and be held accountable for their own choices and deeds.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: Allah promises that sincere faith, when expressed through righteous actions, will bring a person into the company, rank, and reward of the righteous.

translation: Among the people are those who say, “We believe in Allah,” but when they are persecuted for Allah’s sake, they regard the people’s trial as though it were Allah’s punishment. Yet if help comes from your Lord, they will surely say, “We were with you.” Is Allah not most knowing of what is within the hearts of all people?
interpretation: This verse exposes the weakness of those whose faith is only verbal: when devotion brings hardship, they flee as though human persecution were equal to divine punishment, but when believers receive victory, they claim loyalty to share in its benefits. It teaches that sincere faith is tested by steadfastness, and that Allah fully knows whether a person’s claim of faith is genuine or merely motivated by worldly advantage.

translation: And Allah will surely know those who believe, and He will surely know the hypocrites.
interpretation: Allah already knows the reality of every person, but He brings faith and hypocrisy into outward manifestation through trials, so that each person’s sincerity becomes evident and is judged accordingly.

translation: Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, “Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.” Yet they will bear nothing of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: The verse exposes the false reassurance of those who invite others to disbelief by claiming that they will take responsibility for the consequences. No person can remove another’s moral accountability before God; each is answerable for their own choices, while those who mislead others also bear the burden of having led them astray. Their promise is therefore both deceptive and powerless.

translation: And they will surely bear their own burdens, and other burdens along with their burdens; and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: Those who persist in falsehood and lead others astray will not escape responsibility by shifting blame: they will bear the consequences of their own wrongdoing as well as the burden of the misguidance they caused, without diminishing the responsibility of those who followed them. They will also be held accountable for the lies and false claims they invented against God and the truth.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years; then the Flood overtook them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse portrays Noah’s extraordinary perseverance in calling his people to faith over a very long period, while they persisted in wrongdoing. Their destruction came not because they lacked time or warning, but because they refused guidance; thus the verse warns that prolonged respite is not approval of injustice, and that accountability ultimately comes even after long delay.

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the Ark, and made it a sign for all the worlds.
interpretation: God’s rescue of Noah and those who believed with him demonstrates that sincere faith and obedience lead to divine protection, while the Ark and the fate of the deniers remain an enduring warning and lesson for all people.

translation: And Abraham, when he said to his people, “Worship Allah and be mindful of Him; that is best for you, if only you knew.”
interpretation: Abraham called his people to devote worship exclusively to Allah and to protect themselves from disobedience through reverent awareness of Him. This way is better because it brings true spiritual and moral good, though its value is recognized only by those who understand the reality of faith and its consequences.

translation: You worship, instead of Allah, only idols, and you fabricate falsehood. Indeed, those whom you worship instead of Allah possess no power to provide you with sustenance. So seek sustenance from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse calls people to abandon the worship of powerless idols and every invented object of devotion, because none of them can grant provision or benefit. True dependence for sustenance belongs to Allah alone; therefore, a person should seek his needs from Him, devote worship sincerely to Him, and respond with gratitude, mindful that all will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: وإن تكذّبوا فقد كذّبت أممٌ من قبلكم، وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين.
interpretation: إنكاركم للحق لا يضرّ الرسول، فقد سبقكم أقوام كذّبوا رسلهم فنالوا عاقبة تكذيبهم؛ أما مهمة الرسول فمحدودة بإبلاغ الوحي بوضوح، وأما قبول الناس واستجابتهم فمسؤوليتهم هم.

translation: Do they not see how Allah originates creation and then brings it back? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that the One who brought creation into existence without precedent is fully capable of restoring it after death; resurrection is not difficult for Allah, whose power encompasses both the beginning and the return of creation.

translation: Say, “Travel through the earth and observe how He originated creation. Then Allah will bring about the later creation. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.”
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the visible signs of creation and the way life first came into existence, because witnessing Allah’s originating power makes the resurrection understandable and certain. The One who created beings initially can recreate them after death, and nothing lies beyond His power.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Allah alone has complete authority over punishment and mercy, exercising both with perfect knowledge and justice; ultimately, every person will return to Him for judgment.

translation: You cannot escape God’s power on earth or in heaven, nor will you have any protector or helper besides God.
interpretation: No matter where human beings go or how powerful they become, they remain completely subject to God’s authority and cannot thwart His will or evade His judgment. Since no other being possesses independent power, none can serve as a true protector or rescuer apart from Him.

translation: And those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and in the meeting with Him—it is they who have despaired of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting Allah’s revelations and denying resurrection and accountability cuts a person off from the hope of divine mercy, because such denial reflects a deliberate refusal of the truth; therefore, the consequence is a painful punishment.

translation: The only answer of his people was: “Kill him or burn him.” But Allah saved him from the Fire. Surely in this are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: When truth exposes falsehood, those committed to falsehood may respond with violence rather than reason. Yet Allah’s power protected Abraham from the punishment intended for him, demonstrating that no harm can occur except by His will and that those who truly believe will recognize His signs in the triumph of truth over oppression.

translation: He said, “You have taken idols instead of Allah only as a means of affection among yourselves in the life of this world. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disown others, and some of you will curse others. Your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.”
interpretation: This warns that relationships and loyalties built upon idolatry and rejection of Allah may appear to unite people temporarily, but they will collapse in the Hereafter when each person recognizes the others’ responsibility for leading one another astray. False objects of devotion cannot provide salvation, and those who relied on them will find neither mutual support nor any helper against Allah’s judgment.

translation: So Lot believed in him. And he said, “Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. Surely He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”
interpretation: Lot affirmed his faith in Abraham and joined him in turning away from the disbelief of his people. His declaration of migration signifies leaving an environment of rejection and wrongdoing for the sake of obedience to God, trusting that God’s power will protect His servants and His wisdom will guide their path.

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed prophethood and Scripture among his descendants. We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is surely among the righteous.
interpretation: Allah blessed Abraham with Isaac and Jacob and made his descendants a continuing line of prophets and recipients of revealed Scripture. His reward in this life included righteous offspring, honor, and the enduring legacy of guidance; yet his true distinction is that he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter, showing that worldly blessings are only part of Allah’s favor, while ultimate success is measured by righteousness before Him.

translation: And Lot, when he said to his people, “Indeed, you commit an outrageous immorality unlike anyone among all peoples before you.”
interpretation: Lot condemns his people for introducing a grave and unprecedented moral transgression, warning that their behavior represents a deliberate departure from the natural and ethical boundaries established by God.

translation: “Do you indeed approach men, waylay travelers, and commit detestable acts in your gatherings?” Yet the only answer of his people was to say, “Bring us Allah’s punishment, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Prophet Lot’s condemnation of his people’s public moral corruption, including their pursuit of men, their harming or obstructing travelers, and their shameless conduct in their assemblies. Rather than repent or respond to the warning, they mockingly demand the punishment they have been warned about, revealing their denial and defiance.

translation: He said, “My Lord, help me against the corrupting people.”
interpretation: The prophet turns to God for support against a people whose wrongdoing and moral corruption have become persistent and destructive, entrusting the outcome to divine justice.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, “We are going to destroy the people of this town; indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.”
interpretation: The verse shows that divine mercy and warning can arrive together: Abraham was given glad tidings, while the angels announced punishment for a community whose persistent injustice had made it deserving of destruction. Their wrongdoing was not merely a private fault, but a corruption so severe that it brought collective ruin upon the town.

translation: He said, “Indeed, Lot is in it.” They said, “We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she will be among those who remain behind.”
interpretation: Abraham expressed concern for Lot, but the angels assured him that they fully knew the people of the town and would protect Lot and his believing family. Lot’s wife, however, would not be saved because she belonged to those condemned to remain with the people facing destruction.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt powerless to protect them. They said, “Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she will be among those who remain behind.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Lot’s anguish at the danger facing his guests and God’s reassurance that His protection will prevail. It also makes clear that salvation is based on faith and moral loyalty, not merely family ties: although Lot’s wife was his spouse, her alignment with the corrupt people placed her among those destined to remain and perish.

translation: Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town a punishment from the heavens because they persistently defied God.
interpretation: The verse declares that the destruction of the people of Lot was a just divine consequence of their persistent, deliberate immorality and rebellion; the heavenly punishment demonstrates that entrenched wrongdoing, when met with continued defiance, brings about God’s judgment.

translation: And We certainly left therein a clear sign for people who understand.
interpretation: The remains and fate of the people of Lot were preserved as a manifest lesson, so that those who use their reason may recognize the consequences of rejecting God’s guidance and persisting in corruption.

translation: And to Midian We sent their brother Shuʿayb. He said, “O my people, worship Allah, look forward to the Last Day, and do not spread corruption throughout the land.”
interpretation: Shuʿayb calls his people to devote worship exclusively to Allah and to live with the certainty that they will face the Hereafter, since this awareness should restrain them from injustice, wrongdoing, and corrupting society.

translation: فكذّبوه، فأخذتهم الرجفة، فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين.
interpretation: لما أصرّ قوم شعيب على تكذيبه ورفض الحق، نزل بهم عذاب الله في صورة رجفة مهلكة، فأهلكتهم حتى صاروا صرعى لا حراك بهم في مساكنهم؛ وفي ذلك بيان لعاقبة الإعراض عن دعوة الحق بعد قيام الحجة.

translation: And [We destroyed] ʿĀd and Thamūd; their dwellings have become clear to you. Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them and turned them away from the path, though they were capable of discernment.
interpretation: The ruins of ʿĀd and Thamūd stand as a visible warning that destruction does not come merely from ignorance: they had the ability to recognize the truth, yet Satan’s embellishment of their deeds caused them to reject guidance and persist in error.

translation: And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman—Moses came to them with clear proofs, but they acted arrogantly in the land, and they could not escape Us.
interpretation: This verse presents the fate of worldly power when it is joined with pride and rejection of truth. Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman were given clear evidence through Moses, yet their authority and wealth led them to defy God rather than submit to Him. Their apparent dominance did not place them beyond divine judgment: no matter how powerful they became, they could not outrun or overcome God’s will.

translation: So We seized each of them for their sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, among them were those seized by the blast, among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those We drowned. Allah would never wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The varied punishments reflect Allah’s perfect justice: each people was held accountable for the corruption and disbelief they chose, and none was punished unjustly. Their destruction was the consequence of their own persistent wrongdoing, not any oppression from Allah.

translation: The example of those who take protectors besides Allah is like that of the spider: it takes a house. Yet surely the frailest of houses is the spider’s house, if only they knew.
interpretation: Those who rely on beings or powers besides Allah for protection and support place their trust in something as weak and unreliable as a spider’s web; such dependence cannot truly safeguard them, whereas only Allah provides real protection.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah is fully aware of the false objects of worship to which people appeal instead of Him, and none of them can escape His knowledge or challenge His power. His judgment in exposing their impotence and directing worship to Him alone is grounded in perfect might and wisdom.

translation: These are the parables We set forth for people, but none truly comprehend them except those who possess knowledge.
interpretation: Allah indicates that the lessons conveyed through His parables are not grasped merely by hearing or memorizing them; they are understood by people of sound knowledge who reflect deeply, recognize the truth they point to, and allow that understanding to guide their lives.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Surely in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The ordered creation of the heavens and the earth, founded upon truth and wisdom rather than chance or falsehood, is a clear proof of Allah’s power, knowledge, and oneness; believers recognize this sign and are led to trust, worship, and obey Him.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere prayer, grounded in revelation and performed with awareness of Allah, reforms a person’s character by discouraging immoral and wrongful conduct. Yet continual remembrance of Allah is even greater in its power to purify the heart and guide one’s actions, for nothing a person does is hidden from Him.

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in the best manner, except with those among them who commit injustice. And say, “We believe in what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you. Our God and your God is one, and to Him we submit.”
interpretation: This verse establishes a manner of dialogue grounded in courtesy, fairness, and shared belief in the one God and divine revelation. Debate should seek truth through the best words and soundest reasoning, while those who act unjustly or aggressively are exempt from this conciliatory approach. The statement of shared faith affirms Islam’s recognition of the genuine origin of revelation given to earlier communities, while expressing submission to God as the foundation of faith.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you the Book. Those to whom We previously gave the Scripture believe in it, and among these people are some who believe in it as well. No one rejects Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur’an is a divine revelation consistent with the truth originally given to earlier communities. Those who sincerely recognize revelation accept it, whether from the People of the Scripture or from among the Prophet’s own people; rejecting God’s clear signs is therefore not due to a lack of evidence, but to deliberate disbelief.

translation: You did not recite any scripture before this, nor write one with your right hand; otherwise, the false would have had cause to doubt.
interpretation: God points to the Prophet’s lack of prior scriptural reading or writing as evidence that the Qur’an was not composed from earlier books by him. Had he been known to read and write such texts, those who rejected the truth would have had a basis for claiming that the Qur’an was his own invention.

translation: Rather, it is clear signs preserved in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. None deny Our signs except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s truth is made evident and firmly preserved within the understanding of sincere people endowed with knowledge; therefore, deliberate rejection of its signs is not due to a lack of clarity, but to injustice and a refusal to submit to the truth.

translation: They say, “Why have signs not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The unbelievers demanded extraordinary miracles as a condition for accepting the Messenger, but the verse teaches that miracles are granted solely by Allah’s wisdom and authority, not according to people’s demands. The Messenger’s duty is to convey the warning plainly, while guidance and decisive signs remain in Allah’s hands.

translation: أوَلم يكفهم أنَّا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يُتلى عليهم؟ إنَّ في ذلك لرحمةً وذكرى لقومٍ يؤمنون.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن القرآن، بما يحمله من هداية وحقّ وبرهان متجدّد بتلاوته، كافٍ للمؤمنين دليلاً على صدق الرسالة ونِعمةً تهديهم وتزكّيهم، وتذكيراً ينتفع به من فتح قلبه للإيمان.

translation: Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you. He knows all that is in the heavens and the earth. Those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah—it is they who are the losers.”
interpretation: The verse places the truth of the Prophet’s message under Allah’s perfect knowledge and judgment, rather than human opinion. Whoever abandons the reality made evident by Allah and instead relies on false beliefs is ultimately deprived of true guidance and success.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment. Had there not been an appointed time, the punishment would already have come to them. But it will surely come upon them suddenly while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse explains that the delay of punishment is not a sign that it has been dismissed; rather, God grants a fixed period of respite. When that appointed time arrives, punishment will overtake those who demand it unexpectedly, leaving them no opportunity to escape or prepare.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment, while Hell is already encompassing the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who mockingly demand punishment as though it were distant or unlikely: Hell is certain for them, and their rejection has already placed them within the path leading to it, even though its full reality will become manifest in the Hereafter.

translation: On the Day when the punishment envelops them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He says, “Taste what you used to do.”
interpretation: This portrays the complete helplessness of those who rejected the truth: punishment surrounds them from every direction, and they are confronted with the consequences of their own chosen deeds, with no possibility of escape or denial.

translation: O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.
interpretation: This is an exhortation to believers not to let oppression, fear, or an unsuitable environment prevent them from devoted worship. If a place makes obedience to God impossible, they should seek another place where they can preserve their faith and worship Him sincerely, for the earth belongs to God and no circumstance justifies abandoning devotion to Him.

translation: Every soul will taste death; then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse reminds every human being that death is an unavoidable passage, not the end of existence. After it, all people will return to Allah for judgment, so true success lies in preparing for that meeting through faith and righteous deeds.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely settle them in lofty chambers of Paradise beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Excellent indeed is the reward of those who strive in righteousness.
interpretation: Allah promises lasting, honored residence in Paradise to those whose faith is expressed through righteous deeds, showing that true belief is confirmed by action and that steadfast obedience is rewarded with eternal security and bliss.

translation: Those who are patient and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: They endure trials with steadfastness and remain confident in God, relying on Him for support and entrusting their affairs and ultimate outcome to Him.

translation: And how many a creature does not carry its provision! Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Do not let fear of provision drive you to anxiety or disobedience. Many creatures possess no stored provisions or means of securing tomorrow, yet Allah sustains them; likewise, He is fully aware of your needs and hears your supplications. This reliance does not negate effort, but teaches the heart to place its ultimate trust in Allah rather than in worldly means.

translation: And if you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?” they will surely say, “Allah.” So how are they turned away?
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in their beliefs: they recognize that Allah alone created and governs the universe, yet they turn away from worshipping Him alone and follow false beliefs and practices. Their acknowledgment should lead them to faith and devotion, but they are diverted from the truth.

translation: Allah expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it. Surely Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: Abundance or limitation in worldly provision is governed by Allah’s complete knowledge and wisdom, not by human merit alone; therefore, a person should neither become arrogant when given much nor despair when given little, but trust Allah and remain grateful and upright.

translation: And if you ask them, “Who sends down water from the sky and thereby revives the earth after its death?” they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “All praise belongs to Allah.” Yet most of them do not understand.
interpretation: They acknowledge that Allah alone sends the rain that gives life to the barren earth, but they fail to grasp the consequence of this admission: the One who alone controls creation and life deserves exclusive worship and gratitude. Their lack of understanding is therefore not a lack of knowledge, but a failure to follow the truth to its necessary conclusion.

translation: This worldly life is nothing but amusement and play, while the abode of the Hereafter is truly the everlasting life, if only they knew.
interpretation: Worldly existence, with its fleeting pleasures and distractions, is temporary and incomplete; the Hereafter is the real and enduring life, so a person should not let the transient world divert them from preparing for what lasts forever.

translation: When they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting their worship to Him; but when He saves them and brings them safely to land, at once they associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse condemns the inconsistency of those who turn to Allah alone in moments of danger, recognizing His sole power to save them, yet return to associating partners with Him once safety is restored. True faith requires maintaining sincere devotion to Allah in both hardship and ease.

translation: Let them deny what We have given them and enjoy themselves; they will soon know.
interpretation: This is a warning expressed as a rebuke: those who respond to God’s blessings with denial may continue indulging in worldly pleasure for a time, but their ingratitude will ultimately lead them to face the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary secure, while people are being seized around them? Will they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of Allah?
interpretation: Allah reminds the people of Makkah that He granted them safety and protection in a land surrounded by turmoil and danger, even as others nearby were exposed to violence and captivity. This unmistakable favor should lead them to recognize the truth and worship Allah, not follow false beliefs or respond to His blessing with ingratitude.

translation: Who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?
interpretation: The verse declares that the gravest injustice is to attribute falsehood to Allah or knowingly reject the truth when it becomes clear. Its rhetorical question is a warning that persistent disbelief and deliberate distortion lead to the punishment of Hell, which is the fitting abode of those who refuse the truth.

translation: And those who strive for Our sake—We will surely guide them to Our ways. Indeed, Allah is with those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: Those who sincerely exert themselves to obey Allah, resist wrongdoing, and pursue what pleases Him will be granted increasing clarity and guidance. Their striving is not merely effort in itself; it opens the way to recognize and follow the paths of truth and righteousness. Allah’s companionship here signifies His support, care, and nearness to those who act with excellence and sincerity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: These disconnected letters are among the Qur’an’s mysteries; their complete meaning is known to Allah alone, while they also draw attention to the Qur’an’s miraculous composition from the very letters known and used by people.

translation: The Romans have been defeated,
interpretation: This announces the Byzantines’ defeat at the hands of their enemies, while introducing a prophecy that their fortunes will soon be reversed by God’s decree.

translation: في أقربِ الأرض، وهم بعد هزيمتهم سيَغلِبون.
interpretation: يُبيّن الله أن هزيمة الروم ليست نهاية أمرهم، بل سيعقبها نصرٌ لهم، ليظهر أن تقلّب الغلبة بين الأمم جارٍ بتقدير الله، وأن النصر قد يأتي بعد أشدّ مراحل الانكسار.

translation: في بضع سنين، لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد، ويومئذٍ يفرح المؤمنون.
interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن تدبير شؤون الخلق ومآلات الأحداث كلها بيد الله، قبل وقوعها وبعده؛ ولذلك يفرح المؤمنون حين يتحقق وعد الله ويظهر نصره، فيزدادون يقينًا بأن الغلبة والعاقبة له سبحانه.

translation: With the help of Allah. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: All success and victory ultimately come from Allah; He grants them according to His wisdom and will. His might makes victory possible, while His mercy guides its bestowal and gives hope to those who rely on Him.

translation: This is Allah’s promise. Allah never breaks His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: Allah’s promises are certain and cannot fail, even when their fulfillment is delayed or hidden from human perception; people often lack the knowledge and faith to recognize this truth.

translation: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those whose understanding is confined to the visible, immediate affairs of worldly life—such as its means, pleasures, and practical pursuits—while they neglect the deeper purpose of existence and fail to prepare themselves for the lasting reality of the Hereafter.

translation: Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and everything between them except in truth and for an appointed term. Yet many people deny that they will meet their Lord.
interpretation: تدعو الآية الإنسان إلى التأمل في نفسه وفي نظام الكون ليدرك أن الخلق قائم على حكمة وغاية، وأن له نهاية مقدّرة يعقبها الرجوع إلى الله والحساب؛ غير أن كثرة الناس تغفل عن هذه الحقيقة وتنكر لقاء ربها.

translation: Do they not travel through the land and observe how was the end of those who came before them? They were stronger than them, cultivated the land, and developed it more than they have developed it. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would never wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse calls people to learn from the ruins and history of earlier nations: material strength, prosperity, and extensive civilization cannot protect a people who reject divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing. Their destruction was not injustice from Allah, but the consequence of their own choices and oppression.

translation: Then the outcome of those who committed evil was evil, because they rejected the signs of Allah and used to mock them.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing ultimately bring upon themselves a ruinous end: their sins harden them until they deny Allah’s revelations and ridicule them, thereby deserving the very consequence their arrogance and rejection have led to.

translation: Allah originates creation, then repeats it, and then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: Allah is the One who brought creation into existence without a precedent and is fully capable of recreating it after death; ultimately, all people will return to Him for judgment.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will be plunged into despair.
interpretation: When the Resurrection begins, those who persisted in disbelief and wrongdoing will be overcome by utter hopelessness, confusion, and regret, having no argument or escape from the consequences of their deeds.

translation: And they will have no intercessors among their partners, and they will disbelieve in their partners.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who attributed partners to Allah will find that the beings they worshipped cannot intercede for them or offer any help. They will then reject and disavow those partners, but this repudiation will come too late to benefit them.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be divided.
interpretation: When the Day of Judgment begins, humanity will be separated into distinct groups according to their faith and deeds, with each group proceeding toward its fitting recompense.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, rejoicing in bliss.
interpretation: This promises the faithful who express their faith through righteous action an eternal state of profound joy, honor, and contentment in Paradise.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: Those who reject faith, deny God’s clear signs, and refuse to believe in resurrection and accountability will be compelled to face the punishment prepared for them in the Hereafter.

translation: So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.
interpretation: This calls believers to keep Allah’s perfection and transcendence present in their hearts and words at the beginning and end of the day, recognizing that every moment of life unfolds by His will and deserves gratitude and remembrance.

translation: ولَهُ الحمدُ في السماواتِ والأرضِ، وعشيًّا وحينَ تُظهرون.
interpretation: الحمدُ كلُّه لله في جميع السماوات والأرض، فهو المستحق للثناء في كل زمان، ولا سيما عند المساء وحين تبلغون وقت الظهيرة؛ إذ إن تعاقب الأوقات وانتظام الكون من دلائل كمال قدرته واستحقاقه للعبادة.

translation: He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and He revives the earth after its death; and likewise you will be brought forth.
interpretation: The alternation between life and death in creation is a sign of Allah’s limitless power: just as He brings life from what appears lifeless and restores barren earth, He is fully able to resurrect people after their death.

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings spreading throughout the earth.
interpretation: Your humble origin from dust, followed by your emergence as living, intelligent people who populate the earth, is a clear sign of Allah’s creative power and wisdom.
