It calls you to recognize Him as the One who brought you into existence and who is fully able to recreate you after death.

translation: And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy. Surely in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: Marriage is presented as a divine sign: its deepest purpose is not merely companionship or desire, but the creation of inner peace through a bond between two human beings who share one another’s nature. The affection that draws spouses together and the mercy that sustains them through weakness, hardship, and change are gifts from God, inviting thoughtful people to recognize His wisdom and care in human relationships.

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Surely in that are signs for all people of knowledge.
interpretation: The vastness and order of the heavens and earth, together with the diversity found among human beings, point to the wisdom and creative power of God. Differences in language and appearance are deliberate signs of His artistry, not grounds for human superiority or division.

translation: And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed, in that are signs for people who listen.
interpretation: Your alternation between rest and activity, and your ability to pursue provision, are signs of God’s wise ordering of human life and of your dependence on Him. Those who listen attentively recognize in these ordinary experiences evidence of His power, mercy, and sustaining care.

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, inspiring fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky, thereby reviving the earth after its death. Surely in that are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: The alternation of fear and hope in lightning and rain reveals Allah’s power and wisdom: the same cloud may warn of harm yet promise life-giving mercy. The revival of barren earth demonstrates that Allah can likewise bring the dead back to life, and those who reflect recognize these signs.

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand firm by His command. Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, you will immediately emerge.
interpretation: The ordered stability of the universe and the certainty of resurrection both manifest Allah’s absolute power: the One who sustains the heavens and the earth effortlessly can summon humanity from the grave with a single command, leaving no possibility of escape or delay.

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are submissively obedient to Him.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah and is subject to His authority and decree. Every creature is humble before Him and fulfills the role He has assigned it, whether through willing worship or through unavoidable submission to His laws.

translation: And He is the One who originates creation and then brings it back, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah, who brought creation into existence without any precedent, is fully capable of restoring it after death; the act that humans regard as difficult is no obstacle to His power. Nothing resembles Him, and every perfect attribute belongs to Him alone, for His might is absolute and His wisdom governs all that He creates and does.

translation: He presents for you an example from your own lives: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, such that you are equal in it and fear them as you fear one another? Thus We explain the signs in detail for people who understand.
interpretation: Allah exposes the inconsistency of associating partners with Him: people would not willingly share their wealth and authority equally with their dependants or fear them as they fear free equals, yet they attribute partners to the One who alone created and provided for them. The example therefore calls the mind to recognize that divine sovereignty and worship belong exclusively to Allah.

translation: Rather, those who have wronged themselves follow their desires without knowledge. So who can guide one whom Allah has allowed to stray? They will have no helpers.
interpretation: Those who reject truth do so by surrendering to uninformed desires rather than seeking sound guidance. By persistently choosing error, they deprive themselves of divine guidance, and no power or supporter can rescue them from its consequences.

translation: So set your face firmly toward the religion, inclining to truth—the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created humanity. There is no changing Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: Allah commands the believer to turn wholly and sincerely toward the pure worship of Him, in harmony with the innate recognition of truth placed within every human being. This sound disposition is not to be replaced by false beliefs or desires; rather, it is to be preserved and strengthened through faith and obedience. This is the straight and enduring way, though many people fail to recognize its truth.

translation: Turn to Him, be mindful of Him, establish the prayer, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This command calls believers to return sincerely to God, remain conscious of His judgment, and express that devotion through prayer. True faith requires exclusive worship of Him and rejecting every form of associating partners with Him.

translation: [Do not be] among those who divided their religion and became sects; every faction rejoices in what it possesses.
interpretation: The verse warns against turning religion into competing partisan identities, where each group clings proudly to its own views instead of submitting collectively to God’s guidance. Such self-satisfaction with one’s faction obscures truth and replaces sincere faith with division and loyalty to the group.

translation: When harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning back to Him; then, when He lets them taste mercy from Him, a group of them immediately associate partners with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of those who sincerely seek Allah in times of hardship but, once relief and blessings return, forget that He alone saved them and direct worship or gratitude to others. It warns that true faith requires remaining devoted to Allah in prosperity just as in adversity.

translation: So let them be ungrateful for what We have given them. Enjoy yourselves—for you will soon know.
interpretation: This is a stern warning: those who respond to God’s blessings with denial and ingratitude may pursue worldly pleasure for a time, but their enjoyment is temporary and they will soon face the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority that speaks in support of what they used to associate with Him?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rejection of the polytheists’ claims: they possess no revelation or valid proof from God authorizing them to associate partners with Him; their shirk rests only on conjecture and false invention.

translation: And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent ahead, they immediately despair.
interpretation: When people receive blessings, they often respond with delight, yet when hardship comes as a consequence of their own deeds, they quickly lose hope. The verse exposes the weakness of relying on changing circumstances and teaches that faith should remain steady in both ease and adversity, with hope in Allah’s mercy and repentance rather than despair.

translation: Do they not see that Allah enlarges provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Surely in that are signs for people who believe.
interpretation: The variation in people’s provision is governed by Allah’s wisdom, not by human merit alone; believers therefore recognize these changes as signs of His power and respond with trust, gratitude, and patience rather than judging their worth by worldly abundance.

translation: So give the near relative his due, and the needy and the traveler in need. That is better for those who seek the pleasure of Allah, and it is they who will prosper.
interpretation: Allah commands that relatives, the poor, and stranded travelers be given the material and moral rights owed to them. Such generosity is not merely social kindness; it is an act of sincere devotion, valuable when done for Allah’s sake rather than for recognition or worldly return. Those who prioritize these obligations and seek only His pleasure attain true success.

translation: Whatever you give in usury, seeking to increase through people’s wealth, does not increase with Allah; but whatever you give in charity, seeking the pleasure of Allah—those are the ones whose reward is multiplied.
interpretation: Allah distinguishes between wealth pursued for worldly increase through exploiting others and wealth given sincerely for His sake: the former may appear to grow but has no blessed increase before Him, whereas sincere charity is accepted and multiplied in reward.

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, and then gives you life. Is there any of your partners who can do any of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse establishes that creation, provision, death, and resurrection belong solely to Allah. Since the beings whom the polytheists associate with Him possess no share in these decisive acts, they cannot rightly be worshipped; Allah is far above every claim that assigns partners to Him.

translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people’s hands have earned, so that He may make them taste some of what they have done, perhaps they will return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that human wrongdoing produces consequences that spread through society and the natural world. The hardships and disorder people experience may serve as a warning and an opportunity to repent, reform their conduct, and return to obedience to God.

translation: Say, “Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those who came before. Most of them were polytheists.”
interpretation: Allah calls people to reflect on the ruins and history of earlier nations, recognizing that their destruction resulted from rejecting divine guidance and associating partners with Him. Their fate is a warning that worldly power cannot protect those who persist in shirk and wrongdoing.

translation: So set your face steadfastly toward the upright religion before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back. On that Day they will be divided apart.
interpretation: Remain firmly devoted to the true faith and orient your life toward obedience to Allah before the inevitable Day of Judgment arrives, when people will be separated according to their faith and deeds, with no possibility of postponing or escaping its reckoning.

translation: Whoever disbelieves, then upon him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteous deeds, they are preparing a place for themselves.
interpretation: Disbelief ultimately harms only the one who chooses it, while righteous action benefits its doers by preparing for them a secure and honored outcome with Allah. This establishes that each person bears the consequence of their own choice, and that faith must be expressed through deeds.

translation: So that He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Surely, He does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: Allah grants the believers who combine sincere faith with righteous action a reward that exceeds what their deeds alone would merit, by His grace and generosity. His lack of love for the disbelievers refers to those who knowingly reject faith and persist in opposing the truth, not to injustice toward anyone; rather, it warns of the spiritual consequence of choosing disbelief.

translation: And among His signs is that He sends the winds bearing good tidings, so that He may let you taste of His mercy, ships may sail by His command, and you may seek of His bounty—so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: The verse invites people to recognize that the winds, which bring rain, enable travel, and facilitate the pursuit of livelihood, operate by Allah’s command and are manifestations of His mercy. Awareness of these blessings should lead them to sincere gratitude and obedience rather than taking them for granted.

translation: And We certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, who brought them clear proofs; then We took retribution against those who committed crimes. And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet that rejection of truth after clear evidence has always led to the downfall of the guilty, while supporting the believers is a promise He has bound Himself to fulfill—whether through granting them victory, protecting their faith, or ultimately vindicating them.

translation: Allah is the One who sends the winds, which stir up clouds; then He spreads them across the sky as He wills and makes them into fragments, and you see rain emerge from within them. Then, when He causes it to fall upon whoever He wills of His servants, they immediately rejoice.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to Allah’s complete control over the stages of rain—from sending the winds and forming and dispersing the clouds to bringing forth the rain—showing that provision and relief come solely by His wisdom and will. The immediate joy of people when rain reaches them illustrates their dependence on His mercy and calls them to recognize His blessings with gratitude.

translation: Although, before it was sent down upon them, they had been utterly despondent.
interpretation: Before Allah sent the rain upon them, these people had been overcome by despair because of the drought; the verse portrays how swiftly divine mercy can transform hopelessness into relief and joy.

translation: So look at the آثار of Allah’s mercy—how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, He is the One who gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The renewal of barren earth through rain is a visible sign that Allah can restore life after death; the One who brings lifeless soil back to life is fully capable of resurrecting every human being and accomplishing whatever He wills.

translation: And if We were to send a wind and they saw their crops turn yellow, they would thereafter persist in disbelief.
interpretation: This reveals the fickleness of those who lack steadfast faith: they rejoice in blessings when they receive them, yet quickly deny God when a hardship or loss removes them, rather than recognizing that both prosperity and adversity are within His power and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.
interpretation: This is a metaphor for those whose hearts are spiritually unresponsive: persistent rejection and deliberate turning away from truth make them unable to benefit from revelation, just as the dead cannot hear and the deaf cannot hear a call when they turn away.

translation: Nor can you guide the blind out of their error. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, and so they submit.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true guidance cannot be forced by the Messenger or by mere outward instruction; it is received by those whose hearts are open to faith. Those who recognize and believe in God’s signs respond with willing submission, whereas spiritual blindness prevents a person from benefiting from the truth even when it is clearly conveyed.

translation: Allah is He who created you from weakness, then brought forth strength after weakness, then brought forth weakness and gray hair after strength. He creates whatever He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: The verse directs people to reflect on the stages of human life: helplessness at birth, vigor in maturity, and renewed frailty in old age. These changes reveal that human strength is temporary and entirely subject to Allah’s will, while His knowledge encompasses every stage and His power brings creation through all its transformations.

translation: And on the Day the Hour is established, the guilty will swear that they remained for no more than an hour. Thus were they turned away from the truth.
interpretation: When resurrection comes, those who denied it will perceive their worldly life as vanishingly brief and, in confusion, insist that they stayed only a short while. Their claim reflects the same delusion and rejection of truth that characterized them in worldly life.

translation: Those who were given knowledge and faith will say, “You remained according to Allah’s decree until the Day of Resurrection. This is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.”
interpretation: The people of knowledge and faith will correct the deniers’ mistaken estimate of time by explaining that their worldly stay was fixed by Allah until the Resurrection. When that promised Day arrives, its reality will become undeniable, exposing the ignorance and heedlessness that had prevented them from believing in it.

translation: “On that Day, the excuses of those who committed wrongdoing will not benefit them, nor will they be given the opportunity to seek forgiveness or make amends.”
interpretation: يبين الله تعالى أن يوم القيامة ليس يوم اعتذارٍ يقبل، ولا يوم استرضاءٍ أو رجوعٍ لإصلاح ما أفسده الظالمون؛ فقد انتهى زمن الاختبار والعمل، وثبتت تبعات ظلمهم، فلا تنفعهم الأعذار ولا يُمهلون لاستدراك ما فات.

translation: Indeed, We have set forth for people in this Qur’an every kind of example. Yet if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, “You are nothing but purveyors of falsehood.”
interpretation: Allah has made the truth clear through varied explanations and proofs so that people may understand and take heed. However, those who reject faith do not deny the message because it lacks evidence; rather, their stubbornness leads them to dismiss even clear signs and accuse the messengers of falsehood.

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: Allah causes the hearts of those who persist in ignorance and refuse to seek or accept the truth to become unreceptive to guidance, so they remain unable to perceive it clearly.

translation: So be patient; surely Allah’s promise is true. And do not let those who have no certainty provoke you into losing your composure.
interpretation: The verse calls the believer to remain steadfast and trusting in Allah’s promised judgment and help, rather than being shaken or provoked by those whose denial and doubt are rooted in lack of conviction.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. Alif. Lam. Mim.
interpretation: The phrase begins by invoking Allah’s name and seeking His mercy and blessing. The isolated letters “Alif, Lam, Mim” are among the mysteries of the Qur’an; their ultimate meaning is known to Allah, while their presence draws attention to the miraculous revelation composed of ordinary letters yet beyond human imitation.

translation: These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The Qur’an’s verses are presented as signs of a revelation grounded in perfect wisdom, whose guidance is authoritative and whose teachings lead people toward what is true and right.

translation: A guidance and mercy for those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: The Qur’an guides those who sincerely seek what is right and, through their faith and righteous conduct, brings them divine mercy.

translation: Those who establish prayer, give zakāh, and have firm certainty in the Hereafter.
interpretation: True faith is demonstrated through devoted worship, responsibility toward others, and unwavering conviction that life continues with accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are successful.
interpretation: True success belongs to those who receive guidance from Allah, follow it with faith and obedience, and thereby attain well-being and salvation in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Among the people are those who purchase distracting talk in order to mislead others from the way of Allah without knowledge, and who take it as a subject of mockery. For them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns using entertaining or misleading speech to turn people away from faith and obedience to Allah, especially when done ignorantly and with contempt for divine guidance; such deliberate misguidance and mockery merit a punishment that disgraces its perpetrators.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as though he had not heard them, as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him the tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person who knowingly refuses to listen to and reflect upon God’s revelation, treating it with arrogant disregard. His “deafness” is spiritual and deliberate rather than physical, and the warning of painful punishment reflects the consequence of rejecting truth after it has been made clear.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith is demonstrated through righteous action, and that those who combine belief with obedience and goodness will be rewarded with eternal joy and blessing in Paradise.

translation: Abiding therein; the promise of Allah is true, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Their everlasting dwelling is certain because it rests on Allah’s unfailing promise; His might ensures its fulfillment, and His wisdom places everything in its rightful measure.

translation: He created the heavens without pillars that you can see, and He set firm mountains upon the earth lest it should shake with you; and He spread throughout it every kind of creature. And We sent down water from the sky, then We caused every noble kind to grow in it.
interpretation: The verse directs the heart to recognize Allah’s sustaining wisdom and power in the order of creation: the heavens are upheld without visible supports, the mountains contribute to the earth’s stability, life is spread in diverse forms, and rain brings forth beneficial growth. These signs call human beings to acknowledge that the harmony and provision woven into the world are deliberate acts of its Creator, not purposeless chance.

translation: This is the creation of Allah; so show me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error.
interpretation: Allah challenges those who associate partners with Him to point to anything created by their idols, exposing the idols’ powerlessness and showing that worshipping them is clear and profound misguidance.

translation: And We certainly gave Luqmān wisdom: “Be grateful to Allah.” Whoever is grateful is grateful only for his own benefit; and whoever is ungrateful—surely Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Allah granted Luqmān sound judgment and insight, and the first expression of that wisdom was recognizing Allah’s blessings and responding with gratitude. Gratitude does not increase Allah’s perfection or benefit Him; it purifies and enriches the grateful person, guiding them to use blessings rightly and drawing them nearer to their Lord. As for ingratitude, it cannot diminish Allah in the least, for He is completely independent of creation and worthy of praise whether people acknowledge His favors or deny them.

translation: And when Luqman said to his son, while advising him, “My dear son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, associating partners with Him is truly a great injustice.”
interpretation: Luqman teaches that the first and most essential foundation of faith is to worship Allah alone and reject every form of associating partners with Him. Shirk is called a great injustice because it gives the worship due exclusively to the Creator to created beings, thereby violating the greatest truth and right.

translation: And We have enjoined upon the human being kindness toward his parents. His mother carried him, weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years: “Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return.”
interpretation: The verse establishes gratitude to parents—especially recognition of the mother’s successive hardships in pregnancy, birth, and nursing—as part of obedience to God. Yet this gratitude remains subordinate to gratitude toward God, since He alone is the ultimate source of every blessing and to Him all people will return for judgment.

translation: And if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. Yet keep their company in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: Even the immense right of parents does not permit obedience in matters that oppose the oneness of God. Nevertheless, rejecting their belief or disobeying them in that matter must not lead to cruelty: they should still be treated with respect, kindness, and good companionship in worldly life. A believer should instead follow those who sincerely repent and devote themselves to God, knowing that everyone will ultimately return to Him and be held accountable for both belief and conduct.

translation: “O my son, even if it were the weight of a mustard seed, hidden within a rock, or anywhere in the heavens or on earth, Allah would bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and All-Aware.”
interpretation: Luqman teaches his son that no deed, however tiny or concealed, escapes Allah’s knowledge and judgment. His perfect subtlety reaches what is hidden in the most inaccessible places, while His complete awareness encompasses every detail, so a person should remain mindful of Allah in both public and private.

translation: “O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient with whatever befalls you. Indeed, that is among the matters requiring firm resolve.”
interpretation: Luqman counsels his son to build his life upon worship, to promote righteousness and resist wrongdoing with wisdom, and to endure the difficulties that come with obeying God and advising others. These duties require steadfastness, courage, and sincere determination.

translation: Do not turn your cheek away from people in contempt, nor walk on the earth arrogantly. Surely Allah does not love anyone who is self-conceited and boastful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that true dignity is not expressed through despising others or displaying superiority. A believer should meet people with humility and respect, remembering that arrogance and boastfulness are traits detested by Allah.

translation: Be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the harshest of voices is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: This teaches that a believer should walk with calm dignity, avoiding both arrogance and affected weakness, and should speak gently without needless loudness or harshness. Excessive shouting is portrayed as ugly and disruptive, reminding people that good character is shown through restraint and consideration for others.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to your service whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and has showered you with His blessings, outward and inward? Yet among people are those who argue about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or an enlightening scripture.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize Allah’s comprehensive gifts and the order of creation made beneficial to them, both in visible blessings and in hidden ones such as faith, understanding, and protection. In contrast, disputing about Allah without sound knowledge, divine guidance, or revealed evidence is a form of arrogant ignorance, because genuine belief must rest on clear truth rather than conjecture and empty argument.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,” they say, “Rather, we will follow what we found our forefathers following.” Even if Satan were inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: This verse condemns the rejection of divine guidance merely out of loyalty to inherited customs. Ancestral practice is not a valid proof when it conflicts with revelation; people must examine what they follow, since blind imitation can lead them—under Satan’s influence—to ruin and punishment.

translation: And whoever submits himself to Allah while doing good has grasped the firmest handhold. And to Allah belongs the final outcome of all matters.
interpretation: True devotion to Allah is not merely an inward claim; it is sincere surrender expressed through righteous conduct. Whoever entrusts himself wholly to Allah and lives with excellence gains an unbreakable source of faith and security, because every affair ultimately returns to Him.

translation: And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet that the rejection of disbelievers should not overwhelm him, since their choice does not escape divine justice. They will ultimately return to Allah, who will fully disclose and judge their deeds, motives, and hidden convictions; therefore, the Prophet’s duty is to convey the truth faithfully, while judgment belongs to Allah.

translation: We will allow them brief enjoyment, then compel them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that the worldly pleasures granted to those who reject the truth are only temporary respite; afterward, they will have no escape from the grave punishment that awaits them.

translation: And if you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “All praise belongs to Allah.” Yet most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction between acknowledging Allah as the Creator and failing to recognize His exclusive right to worship and obey. Their admission is a proof against them, while their ignorance lies in not understanding the implications of that truth and not giving Allah the gratitude and devotion He deserves.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah alone is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs wholly to Allah and exists by His will and sustaining care. He has no need of any creation, while all creation depends on Him; therefore, all true praise belongs to Him alone, regardless of whether people recognize it.

translation: And if all the trees on earth were pens, and the sea—reinforced by seven seas after it—were ink, the Words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the limitless vastness of Allah’s knowledge, wisdom, decrees, and expressions of truth. Even if every tree became a pen and all the seas became ink, they would run out before Allah’s words could be fully recorded. His might is absolute, so nothing can hinder His will, and His wisdom is perfect, so everything He decrees and reveals is grounded in ultimate knowledge and purpose.

translation: Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: Although humanity is countless, creating and resurrecting all people is no more difficult for Allah than creating or resurrecting one person; His perfect hearing and sight encompass every individual and every deed.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running until an appointed term? And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The gradual interweaving of night and day and the precisely ordered movement of the sun and moon point to Allah’s complete power, wisdom, and control over creation. Since nothing in the universe escapes His knowledge, human actions are likewise known to Him and carried out under His watch, making people responsible for how they live.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and whatever they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: All reality and ultimate authority belong to Allah alone; anything worshipped or called upon besides Him has no true power or rightful claim to worship. His absolute transcendence and greatness therefore require that devotion, reliance, and submission be directed exclusively to Him.

translation: Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by Allah’s grace, so that He may show you some of His signs? Surely in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful.
interpretation: The ordered movement of ships across the sea reveals Allah’s sustaining power and mercy, inviting people to recognize that human skill and the forces of nature operate only by His permission. Those who truly benefit from such signs are the steadfast in hardship and the grateful in blessing.

translation: And when waves cover them like canopies, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting their faith to Him. But when He delivers them safely to land, some of them take a moderate course. Yet none rejects Our signs except every treacherous, ungrateful person.
interpretation: The verse portrays how overwhelming danger strips away false reliance and awakens genuine recognition of Allah, so people call upon Him with undivided sincerity. Once rescued, however, some return to a measured acknowledgement rather than remaining steadfast in gratitude and obedience. Their denial of Allah’s signs is therefore described as both treachery—because they betray the sincerity they showed in crisis—and ingratitude for the deliverance they received.

translation: O mankind, be mindful of your Lord and fear a Day when no parent can benefit their child in the least, nor can any child benefit their parent. Surely, Allah’s promise is true. So do not let the life of this world deceive you, nor let the deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.
interpretation: The verse calls every person to sincere awareness of Allah and to prepare for the Hereafter, where family ties cannot replace personal faith and responsibility. Worldly pleasures and false hopes—especially the belief that Allah’s judgment may be escaped or delayed without consequence—must not distract a person from obedience and repentance.

translation: Indeed, Allah alone has knowledge of the Hour, sends down the rain, knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse teaches that certain dimensions of the unseen belong exclusively to Allah: the exact time of the Resurrection, the full reality and timing of rain, all that concerns life in the wombs, the events and provisions of the coming day, and the place and time of each person’s death. Human knowledge is limited and dependent, whereas Allah’s knowledge encompasses every hidden detail. Therefore, a person should remain humble before the unseen, rely on Allah, and prepare through righteous action rather than claiming certainty about what only He knows.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lām, Mīm.
interpretation: “Alif, Lām, Mīm” are among the Qur’anic disjointed letters whose ultimate meaning is known to Allah; their placement at the beginning calls attention to the revelation and suggests that this divine Book is composed of the very letters known to humanity, yet remains beyond human ability to produce.

translation: The revelation of the Book—there is no doubt about it—is from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur’an is certainly divine revelation, originating from the Lord who sustains and governs all creation; therefore, its truth is not subject to genuine doubt.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you, that they may be guided.
interpretation: The verse rejects the accusation that the Qur’an was invented by the Prophet, affirming that it is revelation from God. His mission is therefore a divine mercy and warning for a people who had not received a messenger in their recent past, giving them the opportunity to recognize the truth and follow the path of guidance.

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize Allah’s absolute authority over all creation: since He alone brought the universe into existence and governs it, no being can independently protect, aid, or intercede for anyone apart from His permission. Awareness of this should lead to sincere devotion, reliance upon Him, and thoughtful reflection on the purpose of life.

translation: He directs the affair from heaven to earth, then it ascends to Him on a day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: Allah governs every matter throughout the heavens and the earth, and all affairs ultimately return to Him. The mention of a day equal to a thousand human years conveys the vast difference between divine measure and human reckoning, while affirming that nothing lies outside His control.

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah possesses complete knowledge of all that is hidden from creation and all that is openly perceived; His might is absolute, yet His dealings with His creation are governed by perfect mercy.

translation: He perfected everything He created, and began the creation of humankind from clay.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah fashioned every created thing with wisdom, proportion, and purpose, while reminding human beings that their origin is humble clay and that their existence depends entirely upon their Creator.

translation: Then He made his offspring from an extract of a humble fluid.
interpretation: Humanity’s continuation comes from a small and seemingly insignificant drop, reminding people of their humble origin and of God’s power to bring life and generations into being.

translation: Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little is the gratitude you show.
interpretation: Allah brought the human being into being in a complete form and endowed him with the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding, all of which are gifts entrusted to him. Yet people often fail to recognize the Giver and use these blessings in obedience and gratitude, so their thankfulness remains scarce.

translation: And they say, “When we have vanished into the earth, will we truly be brought forth in a new creation?” Rather, they deny the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: They reject resurrection because they focus on the disintegration of the body after death, treating it as impossible for God to recreate it. Their real problem, however, is not lack of evidence but their denial that they will stand before their Lord for judgment and accountability.

translation: Say, “The angel of death entrusted with you will take your souls; then to your Lord you will be returned.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that death occurs by God’s appointed command through the angel entrusted with taking souls, and that every person will ultimately return to God for judgment.

translation: If only you could see when the guilty bow their heads before their Lord, saying, “Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back and we will do righteous deeds. Indeed, we are now certain.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the remorse of those who denied the truth when they finally stand before Allah. Their lowered heads express humiliation and regret, while their claim that they now see, hear, and are certain reveals that faith at that stage comes only after witnessing the reality of the Hereafter. Their request to return to worldly life is rejected in meaning, because genuine accountability requires believing and acting before the unseen becomes plainly visible.

translation: Had We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but My word has come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind altogether.
interpretation: Allah declares that universal, compelled guidance was within His power, yet He ordained that people and jinn would be tested through their choices. Those who knowingly persist in disbelief and disobedience will fulfill the divine warning and deserve Hell; this is not injustice, but the consequence of their freely chosen rejection of the truth.

translation: “So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have forsaken you. And taste the everlasting punishment for what you used to do.”
interpretation: This is a declaration that those who deliberately neglected accountability before God will be left to the consequences of their rejection on the Day of Judgment; their punishment is a just recompense for the deeds they persisted in committing.

translation: Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration, glorify their Lord with praise, and are not arrogant. ۩
interpretation: True faith is shown by humility before God: when His revelations awaken the heart, the believer submits in worship, praises Him, and does not let pride prevent obedience.

translation: Their sides withdraw from their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This portrays sincere believers whose longing for God leads them to rise from sleep for devoted prayer, balancing fear of His judgment with hope in His mercy, while expressing gratitude for His blessings through generosity and charity.

translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of joy and comfort of the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: God has reserved for those who sincerely obey Him rewards of such indescribable beauty and delight that no human being can presently imagine them; these blessings are granted in proportion to their faithful deeds and perseverance.

translation: Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith and persistent rebellion against God are fundamentally different states, and that a believer cannot be regarded as equal to one who knowingly departs from obedience. Their beliefs, conduct, moral standing, and ultimate consequences are distinct, even if worldly appearances sometimes make them seem alike.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge as a welcome lodging, because of what they used to do.
interpretation: Those who unite sincere faith with righteous action will be honored by God with Paradise as their lasting home and gracious reception. Their deeds are the cause by which they attain this reward, while God’s generosity makes that reward abundant and welcoming.

translation: أما الذين خرجوا عن طاعة الله فمأواهم النار؛ كلما حاولوا الخروج منها أُعيدوا إليها، وقيل لهم: تذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم تكذبون به.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الإصرار على الفسوق وتكذيب الحق يورث صاحبه عذابًا لا مهرب منه، وأن الندم عند ظهور الحقيقة لا ينفع؛ إذ يُقابلون بالتذكير بتكذيبهم السابق.

translation: And We shall surely make them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, so that perhaps they may return.
interpretation: The nearer punishment refers to trials and consequences in this worldly life, through which God awakens people to the truth and gives them an opportunity to repent before facing the everlasting punishment of the Hereafter.

translation: And who is more wrongdoer than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: The greatest injustice is to knowingly disregard the clear signs and reminders of God after they have reached a person. Such deliberate rejection is not overlooked; those who persist in wrongdoing will face God’s just punishment.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt about receiving it; and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet that the revelation given to Moses was a genuine divine scripture and a source of guidance for the Children of Israel. The command not to doubt its meeting refers to certainty that Moses truly received the revelation and that the Prophet will encounter the same divine truth through revelation; thus, the verse affirms the continuity and authenticity of Allah’s guidance across His messengers.

translation: And We made from among them leaders who guided by Our command when they were patient and firmly convinced of Our signs.
interpretation: Allah made those who endured hardship with steadfast patience and possessed unwavering certainty in His signs into leaders of guidance, showing that true spiritual leadership is granted through perseverance and firm faith, not merely through status or claim.

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed.
interpretation: Allah alone will settle the disputes and disagreements among people with perfect justice on the Day of Resurrection, revealing the truth and rewarding or holding accountable each person according to what they believed and did.

translation: Have they not been guided by the fact that We destroyed before them many generations, through whose dwellings they now walk? Surely in that are signs. Will they not then listen?
interpretation: The ruins and abandoned homes of past peoples are a clear warning that worldly power and heedlessness cannot protect anyone from divine judgment. Those who encounter such evidence should listen attentively, reflect, and turn away from the ways that led earlier nations to destruction.

translation: Have they not seen that We drive water to barren land, bringing forth by it crops from which their livestock and they themselves eat? Will they not then see?
interpretation: The revival of barren earth through rain is a clear sign of God’s power to provide life and sustenance, and it should awaken people to recognize that the One who brings the dead land to life is also able to resurrect human beings.

translation: And they say, “When will this decisive judgment come, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They ask mockingly when God’s promised judgment and separation between truth and falsehood will occur, challenging the believers’ warning as though it were untrue.

translation: Say, “On the Day of Decision, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be given respite.”
interpretation: The verse warns that faith adopted only when divine judgment becomes undeniable will not be accepted as genuine repentance; once the decisive moment arrives, the opportunity for belief and amendment has ended.

translation: So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: Disengage from those who persist in rejection and leave the outcome to Allah, while remaining steadfast and confident that the truth will ultimately prevail and that their own awaited consequences will come.

translation: O Prophet, be mindful of Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet ﷺ to remain firmly devoted to Him and not yield to the pressure or demands of those who reject faith or conceal hostility beneath outward belief. This command affirms that obedience must be governed by divine guidance rather than by the wishes of opponents, for Allah fully knows people’s intentions and wisely directs what is best.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: This commands steadfast adherence to divine revelation as the guiding authority in belief and conduct, while reminding people that Allah knows their actions completely, including their sincerity and hidden motives.

translation: And place your trust in Allah; Allah is sufficient as a Trustee.
interpretation: Rely upon Allah with confidence, entrusting your affairs to Him while fulfilling your responsibilities, for He alone is fully sufficient to protect, support, and manage the outcome of what you cannot control.

translation: Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body. Nor has He made your wives whom you declare to be like your mothers into your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons into your sons. That is merely what you say with your mouths; and Allah speaks the truth and guides to the right way.
interpretation: The verse teaches that words and social conventions cannot alter the realities established by God: a wife does not become a mother through the declaration of zihar, and an adopted child does not become a biological son merely through attribution. Believers are therefore called to honor the truth in family relationships and lineage, following God’s guidance rather than treating verbal claims as changes to reality.

translation: Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. If you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your wards. There is no blame upon you for what you do by mistake, but only for what your hearts deliberately intend. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah establishes that a person’s lineage must be preserved and that adopted children should not be attributed to anyone other than their biological fathers when they are known. When their parentage is unknown, they remain honored members of the believing community, described as brothers and dependents rather than falsely assigned a lineage. Unintentional errors are excused, while deliberate misattribution is morally accountable; this ruling reflects both justice in preserving identity and mercy toward human fallibility.

translation: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. Blood relatives are closer to one another, according to the Book of Allah, than the other believers and the emigrants, except that you may show kindness to your close friends. This has been inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: Believers must give the Prophet ﷺ priority over their own desires and submit to his guidance because of his care and authority over them. His wives hold the honor and sanctity of mothers, though they are not actual mothers in lineage. In matters of mutual rights and inheritance, kinship takes precedence over bonds formed merely through faith or migration; nevertheless, believers may still honor their allies and friends through generosity and good treatment. This ordering of obligations is an established decree of Allah.

translation: And when We took a covenant from the prophets—and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary—and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that He established a firm and binding covenant with the prophets, beginning with Noah and including Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad ﷺ. This covenant signifies their unwavering commitment to convey Allah’s revelation faithfully, uphold His guidance, and call their peoples to worship Him alone. Its description as “solemn” emphasizes the immense responsibility of prophethood and the certainty that these messengers fulfilled their trust before Allah.

translation: So that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness; and He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This signifies that truthfulness is not merely a claim but a responsibility that will be examined before God: those who were sincere in faith and faithful to their commitments will be distinguished from those who rejected the truth, for whom painful punishment has been prepared.

translation: O you who believe, remember Allah’s blessing upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a wind and forces you could not see. Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: Allah reminds the believers that their deliverance from the hostile armies was achieved by His unseen support, teaching them that victory and protection ultimately come from Him. They should therefore remain grateful, steadfast, and conscious that Allah observes their actions, especially in times of fear and trial.

translation: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes became distraught and hearts reached the throats, while you entertained various thoughts about Allah.
interpretation: This depicts the believers’ extreme terror when the enemy surrounded them from every direction during the Battle of the Trench. Their fear became so intense that it affected their perception and nearly overwhelmed their hearts, exposing the uncertainty and anxious assumptions some of them formed about Allah’s support and promise.

translation: There the believers were put to the test and shaken with a tremendous shaking.
interpretation: This refers to the moment of extreme fear and hardship during the Battle of the Trench, when the believers’ faith, steadfastness, and trust in Allah were profoundly tested.

translation: And when the hypocrites and those whose hearts were afflicted with doubt said, “Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion.”
interpretation: This reveals the inner disbelief and distrust of those who, during hardship, regarded Allah’s promise of support as deception rather than truth. Their words exposed that their faith was conditional upon immediate ease and victory, so the trial brought their concealed hypocrisy and spiritual weakness into the open.

translation: And when a group of them said, “O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you to remain, so return.” And another group of them sought permission from the Prophet, saying, “Indeed, our homes are exposed and unprotected,” though they were not exposed. They sought nothing but to flee.
interpretation: This verse exposes the weakness and insincerity of those who abandoned the believers during the siege: they used concern for their homes as an excuse to escape, while their real motive was fear and unwillingness to stand firm. It also shows how fear can lead people to discourage others and disguise cowardice as a legitimate necessity.

translation: And if it had been entered upon them from its outskirts, and they had then been asked to abandon faith, they would have done so, and would have delayed only a little.
interpretation: This exposes the weakness of the hypocrites’ commitment: had the enemy entered Madinah from any side and demanded that they renounce the faith, they would have yielded readily, with scarcely any hesitation. Their professed loyalty was therefore superficial, sustained only while it served their worldly interests.

translation: They had already pledged to Allah before that they would not turn their backs; and Allah’s covenant is one for which they will be held accountable.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who broke their solemn promise to remain steadfast in the face of danger. A covenant made with Allah is not a casual oath: it creates a moral responsibility, and those who violate it will be answerable for their betrayal.

translation: Say: “Fleeing will never benefit you if you flee from death or being killed; and then you will enjoy life only briefly.”
interpretation: No escape can ultimately prevent the destiny Allah has decreed. Even if fleeing delays death or danger, it cannot grant lasting security or a long worldly life, so a person should not let fear govern them or neglect their duty.

translation: Say, “Who can protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you, or intends mercy for you?” And they will find for themselves, apart from Allah, neither a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: The verse affirms that all affairs are ultimately under Allah’s authority: no person, power, or ally can avert what He decrees or prevent the mercy He grants. Therefore, relying on anything besides Him for ultimate protection is futile, since none can serve as a true guardian or helper against His judgment.

translation: Allah certainly knows those among you who hinder others, and those who say to their brothers, “Come over to us,” while they themselves scarcely take part in the fighting.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who discourage believers from fulfilling their duty and call others away from danger while refusing to face it themselves. Allah is fully aware of their conduct, their deceptive words, and their unwillingness to sacrifice; their claim of solidarity is therefore empty, revealed by their minimal participation when courage and commitment are required.

translation: They are miserly toward you. Then, when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one overcome by death. But when the fear has passed, they assail you with sharp tongues, being miserly toward all good. Those have not believed, so Allah has rendered their deeds worthless; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who seek the benefits of belonging to the believers while withholding support and courage in times of danger. Fear reveals their inner weakness, whereas safety emboldens them to speak harshly and demand worldly gains. Their conduct shows that outward association with faith has no value when the heart lacks sincere belief, so their deeds are deprived of acceptance by Allah.

translation: They think that the confederates have not withdrawn. If the confederates were to come, they would wish they were living among the desert Arabs, asking about your news from afar. And if they were among you, they would fight only a little.
interpretation: This portrays the hypocrites as consumed by fear and self-preservation: even after the enemy has departed, they remain convinced that danger is imminent, and they would rather hide among the Bedouins than stand with the believers. Their question about the community’s news is not accompanied by genuine solidarity, for even if present, their weakness and reluctance would keep them from making any meaningful effort in its defense.

translation: Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to follow the Prophet’s character, conduct, patience, and obedience as the practical model of faith, for sincere hope in Allah and the Hereafter, together with frequent remembrance of Him, leads a person to emulate his example.

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, “This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.” And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: The believers understood the approaching alliance not as evidence that Allah’s promise had failed, but as its fulfillment and a test of their sincerity. Their trust in Allah therefore deepened under hardship, leading them to submit to His command with steadfastness rather than fear or doubt.

translation: Among the believers are men who have remained true to the covenant they made with Allah. Some of them have fulfilled their pledge, and some are still awaiting it; they have never changed in the least.
interpretation: الآية تُبيّن أن صدق الإيمان يظهر في الثبات على عهد الله، سواء أدّى ذلك إلى بذل النفس والوفاء الكامل بالعهد، أم إلى الاستمرار في انتظاره دون تراجع أو تبديل؛ فالقيمة ليست في مجرد الادعاء، بل في دوام الإخلاص والاستقامة حتى النهاية.

translation: So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that steadfast sincerity is honored by Allah, while hypocrisy carries the consequence of divine judgment. Yet punishment is not presented as inevitable for every hypocrite: Allah may forgive through repentance, showing that His justice is accompanied by mercy and that the door of return remains open.

translation: And Allah turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good. Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting, and Allah is Powerful, Almighty.
interpretation: Allah frustrated the coalition that had come against the believers, causing them to withdraw in anger without achieving their objective. This shows that victory may come through Allah’s protection and intervention, relieving the faithful from conflict, while His power and might remain beyond all opposition.

translation: And He brought down from their fortresses those from the People of the Scripture who had supported them, and He cast terror into their hearts: some you killed, and some you took captive.
interpretation: This verse portrays God’s decisive intervention against those who had aided the hostile coalition and violated their covenant: their fortified security could not protect them once fear entered their hearts, and their fate was divided between death and captivity according to the judgment that followed.

translation: وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم وأرضًا لم تطئوها، وكان الله على كل شيء قديرًا.
interpretation: يبين الله أن ما آل إلى المؤمنين من أرض بني قريظة وديارهم وأموالهم، وما سيفتحونه من أراضٍ لم تطأها أقدامهم بعد، إنما تحقق بقدرته وتدبيره؛ فلا يعجزه نصر أوليائه ولا تمكينهم فيما يشاء.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives: “If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release.”
interpretation: The Prophet’s wives were given a clear and dignified choice: to prefer worldly comforts and part from the Prophet amicably, receiving suitable provision and no harm or humiliation, or to remain with him while accepting the greater responsibilities and spiritual priorities of their position.

translation: But if you desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, then surely Allah has prepared a tremendous reward for those of you who do good.
interpretation: The verse teaches that choosing closeness to Allah, loyalty to His Messenger, and the lasting life of the Hereafter over worldly comforts is the path of sincere righteousness, for Allah promises abundant and enduring reward to those who live by that choice.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever among you commits a manifest indecency, the punishment for her will be doubled; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse places a heightened responsibility upon the Prophet’s wives because of their exceptional closeness to him and their public role as examples for the believers: a plainly immoral act from them would carry a doubled punishment, reflecting the greater harm caused by misconduct associated with the Prophet’s household. This warning is not due to any inherent inferiority, but to the elevated standard and accountability that accompany their honored status.

translation: And whoever among you is devoutly obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will grant her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger, when expressed through righteous action, is honored with an increased reward. The special emphasis on the women addressed reflects their distinctive responsibility and status, while the “noble provision” signifies a dignified and blessed recompense from Allah in this life and, ultimately, in the Hereafter.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest one whose heart is diseased should be tempted; rather, speak in a manner that is appropriate and honourable.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet’s wives—and, by extension, believing women—to preserve dignity and clear boundaries in their speech, avoiding a tone or manner that may invite improper desire or be exploited by morally corrupted people. It does not prohibit women from speaking; rather, it calls for respectful, purposeful, and appropriately firm communication grounded in consciousness of Allah.

translation: “Remain in your homes and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former Days of Ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakāt, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the Household, and to purify you completely.”
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet’s household to embody modesty, dignity, worship, and obedience, while declaring Allah’s will to cleanse the People of the Household from spiritual impurity and perfect their purification through faith and righteous conduct.

translation: واذكرن ما يُتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة؛ إن الله كان لطيفًا خبيرًا.
interpretation: يأمر الله أمهات المؤمنين أن يستحضرن ما يُتلى في بيوتهن من القرآن وما تعلّمنه من حكمة النبي ﷺ، وأن يعظّمن هذه النعمة بحفظها والعمل بها وتعليمها؛ فالله لطيف بأوليائه، خبير بأحوالهم وأعمالهم.

translation: Indeed, Muslim men and Muslim women, believing men and believing women, devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, truthful men and truthful women, patient men and patient women, humble men and humble women, charitable men and charitable women, fasting men and fasting women, men who guard their chastity and women who guard theirs, and men who remember Allah often and women who do so—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse affirms that spiritual worth and divine reward are equally open to men and women. It describes the qualities of genuine faith: willing submission to Allah, sincere belief, obedience, truthfulness, perseverance, humility, generosity, fasting, chastity, and continual remembrance of Allah. Whoever cultivates these qualities may hope for Allah’s forgiveness and an immense reward.

translation: It is not for a believing man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: True faith requires willingly submitting to Allah’s and His Messenger’s binding guidance rather than placing personal preference above it; knowingly rejecting their command is clear deviation from the straight path.

translation: And when you said to the one whom Allah had favored and you had favored, “Keep your wife and be mindful of Allah,” while concealing within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and fearing the people, though Allah has greater right that you fear Him. Then, when Zayd had ended his marriage with her, We married her to you so that there would be no blame upon the believers regarding the wives of their adopted sons when they have ended their marriages with them. And Allah’s command is always accomplished.
interpretation: This verse establishes that adoption does not create the same legal relationship as biological parenthood: an adopted son’s former wife is not permanently forbidden in marriage. Zayd’s divorce and the Prophet’s subsequent marriage to Zaynab served as a public, deliberate reform of a deeply rooted social custom. The Prophet’s hesitation arose from concern about people’s reactions, but the verse teaches that obedience to Allah’s revealed command must take precedence over fear of social criticism, while also affirming that divine decrees are ultimately fulfilled.

translation: There is no blame upon the Prophet regarding what Allah has ordained for him. This is Allah’s established way with those who came before; and the command of Allah is a decree destined to be fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the Prophet ﷺ bears no reproach for faithfully carrying out what Allah has prescribed for him. Divine revelation and duty take precedence over people’s customs and accusations, and Allah’s established way with His messengers is certain and cannot be thwarted.

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah, fear Him, and fear no one except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner.
interpretation: This describes sincere messengers and those who faithfully carry divine guidance: they communicate Allah’s revelation without concealing or altering it, remain conscious of His judgment, and do not abandon the truth out of fear of people. Their reliance is upon Allah alone, knowing that He fully accounts for their deeds and is sufficient as the One who judges and holds them to account.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that Muhammad ﷺ was not the biological father of any adult man among the believers, while affirming his supreme spiritual authority as Allah’s Messenger and the final prophet. Thus, no prophet will come after him, and Allah knows fully the wisdom and consequences of His decree.

translation: O you who believe, remember Allah with abundant remembrance.
interpretation: Believers are called to keep Allah continually present in their hearts, words, and actions, so that remembrance becomes a lasting source of faithfulness and awareness rather than an occasional practice.

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: Keep Allah continually free of all imperfection and praise Him regularly at the beginning and end of the day, maintaining remembrance of Him throughout your daily life.

translation: He is the One who blesses you, and His angels pray for you, that He may bring you out of the darknesses into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: Allah shows special care for the believers by honoring them, granting them mercy, and causing the angels to seek goodness for them. Through His guidance, He brings them from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and sin into the light of faith, knowledge, and obedience; His mercy remains continuously extended to them.

translation: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, “Peace.” And He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will honor the believers with a greeting of peace and security as they meet Him, and He has prepared for them the lasting reward of Paradise.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner.
interpretation: God commissions the Prophet ﷺ to testify to the truth before humanity, to give hope to those who respond to faith and righteousness, and to warn those who reject guidance and persist in wrongdoing.

translation: And as one who calls to Allah by His permission, and as a radiant lamp.
interpretation: The Prophet is presented as one who guides people toward Allah with divine authorization and illuminates the way of faith, truth, and righteousness for them.

translation: And give the believers good tidings that for them is a great bounty from Allah.
interpretation: The verse assures believers that Allah has prepared for them immense grace and reward, encouraging them to remain steadfast and hopeful in their faith.

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, disregard their harm, and put your trust in Allah. And Allah is sufficient as a Guardian.
interpretation: Do not let the demands or pressure of those who reject faith or conceal hypocrisy lead you away from God’s guidance. Respond to their hostility with patience and dignified restraint, entrusting your protection, support, and ultimate outcome to Allah, who is fully sufficient for those who rely on Him.

translation: O believers, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period for them to observe. So provide them with a gift and release them graciously.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a woman divorced before marital consummation is not required to observe a waiting period, since pregnancy is not a concern in that circumstance. Nevertheless, the husband must not end the marriage harshly or leave her without consideration; he is commanded to offer her a suitable parting provision and to let her go with dignity, kindness, and no harm or humiliation.

translation: O Prophet, We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their bridal gifts, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has granted you as spoils, and the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who migrated with you; and any believing woman who offers herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her—this is exclusively for you, not for the other believers. We know what We have prescribed for them regarding their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there may be no constraint upon you. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse specifies the categories of women whom the Prophet was permitted to marry, including wives whose bridal gifts had been given, women from his close extended family who had migrated with him, and—by a special concession— a believing woman who offered herself in marriage to him. It also distinguishes the Prophet’s particular marital permissions from the rules binding on other believers, affirming that these provisions were granted to remove hardship from his exceptional responsibilities and circumstances, while all such relationships were subject to the obligations and protections established by divine law. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah’s forgiveness and mercy.

translation: You may defer whichever of them you will, and receive whichever you will; and if you desire any of those whom you had set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more likely to comfort their eyes, relieve them of grief, and make them content with what you have given them—all of them. Allah knows what is in your hearts, and Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse grants the Prophet ﷺ flexibility in arranging the time he spent with his wives, relieving him of the usual obligation to maintain an equal schedule. The wisdom was to remove hardship for him while preserving the wives’ reassurance and contentment; it also reminds everyone that Allah knows the sincerity and intentions hidden in their hearts and deals with them with perfect knowledge and forbearance.

translation: “لا يحلّ لك النساء من بعد، ولا أن تستبدل بهنّ من أزواج، ولو أعجبك حسنهنّ، إلا ما ملكت يمينك. وكان الله على كلّ شيء رقيبًا.”
interpretation: يفيد هذا الحكم تقييد النبيّ ﷺ بعدد زوجاته القائمات آنذاك، فمنعَه الله من الزواج بغيرهنّ أو استبدال واحدة منهنّ بامرأة أخرى، ولو نال إعجابه جمالها، مع استثناء الإماء اللاتي دخلن في ملكه وفق نظام الأسر والاسترقاق المعروف في ذلك العصر. وخُتم الحكم بتذكيرٍ بأن الله مطّلع على أفعال عباده، فلا يتجاوز أحدٌ حدود ما شرعه الله.

translation: O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are granted permission for a meal, without waiting for it to be prepared. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, then disperse, without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that would trouble the Prophet, yet he is too shy to ask you to leave; but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a barrier. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor ever to marry his wives after him. Indeed, that would be عظیم in the sight of Allah.
interpretation: This verse establishes a code of respectful conduct toward the Prophet’s household: believers must honor the privacy of his home, accept invitations without arriving early or overstaying afterward, and avoid imposing social conversation that causes him discomfort. It also directs that interactions with his wives concerning personal requests take place through a barrier, protecting the inward purity and dignity of everyone involved. Finally, it emphasizes the exceptional sanctity of the Messenger’s personal life by forbidding any harm to him and permanently prohibiting marriage to his wives after his death, presenting such conduct as a grave matter before Allah.

translation: Whether you reveal something or conceal it, surely Allah is ever Knowing of all things.
interpretation: Nothing in a person’s words, actions, or hidden intentions is outside Allah’s knowledge; therefore, one should be sincere and mindful of Him both publicly and privately.

translation: There is no blame upon them regarding their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers’ sons, their sisters’ sons, their women, or those whom their right hands possess. And be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is ever Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that women may appear without the same restrictions before these specified close relatives, their fellow women, and those under their lawful authority, while remaining within the bounds of modesty and propriety. The command to be mindful of Allah shows that these permissions do not remove the duty of moral conduct, for Allah observes every circumstance and intention.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels bless the Prophet. O believers, invoke blessings upon him and offer him abundant peace.
interpretation: Allah honors the Prophet and elevates his mention, while the angels pray for his honor and mercy. Believers are therefore commanded to show their devotion and respect by invoking Allah’s blessings and peace upon the Prophet sincerely and abundantly.

translation: Indeed, those who offend Allah and His Messenger—Allah has condemned them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: Those who deliberately oppose Allah’s commands and insult, reject, or wrong His Messenger place themselves under divine condemnation: they are deprived of guidance and honor in this life and face disgraceful punishment in the Hereafter. “Offending Allah” does not mean that anyone can harm Him; rather, it refers to acts and words that incur His displeasure.
