translation: Yet they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping that they might be helped.
interpretation: They turned to other beings as objects of worship, imagining that these false gods could protect or support them, while in reality they possess no power to help anyone and are themselves powerless before Allah.

translation: They cannot help them, although they themselves are troops brought forth in their service.
interpretation: The false deities possess no power to rescue their worshippers; instead, the worshippers devote themselves to defending and serving powerless objects, revealing the futility of their devotion.

translation: So do not let their words grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: God consoles the Prophet, assuring him that the denial and hurtful words of his opponents cannot escape divine knowledge. Their inner intentions and outward claims are fully known to Him, so the Prophet should remain steadfast and not be distressed, trusting that God will judge their rejection with perfect justice.

translation: أوَلم يرَ الإنسانُ أنّا خلقناه من نطفة، فإذا هو خصيمٌ مبينٌ؟
interpretation: في الآية تعجّبٌ من جحود الإنسان؛ فقد بدأ خلقه من أصلٍ متواضعٍ ضعيف، ثم صار يجادل في قدرة الله ويعترض عليها بجرأة، مع أن نشأته الأولى دليلٌ واضح على قدرة خالقه على بعثه وإعادته.

translation: And he sets forth for Us an argument, forgetting his own creation. He says, “Who will give life to bones when they have crumbled into dust?”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny resurrection despite knowing that God created them from nothing; the One who originated human life is fully capable of restoring it after death, even when the body has completely decayed.

translation: Say, “The One who created them the first time will bring them to life; and He is All-Knowing of every creation.”
interpretation: Allah’s ability to resurrect the dead is established by His having created them initially; the One who originated every person from nothing can restore them completely, for nothing about His creation is beyond His knowledge.

translation: He is the One who made fire for you from the green tree, and behold, from it you kindle a flame.
interpretation: Allah points to His power through the seemingly opposite qualities of living greenery and burning fire: just as He brings fire from what is green, He is fully able to bring life out of death and resurrect creation.

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Indeed, He is; and He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The One who originated the immense heavens and earth without precedent certainly has the power to recreate human beings after death; His perfect creative power is accompanied by complete knowledge of every detail.

translation: His command, when He intends something, is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.
interpretation: When Allah wills an occurrence, He brings it into existence effortlessly by His absolute command; nothing can resist His power or delay what He decrees.

translation: So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: God alone possesses complete authority and control over every created thing, and every human being will ultimately return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: By those who line themselves up in ranks,
interpretation: Allah swears by the obedient servants—understood by many interpreters to be the angels—who stand in ordered rows before Him, emphasizing their disciplined worship and complete submission to His command.

translation: By those who drive away forcefully,
interpretation: This refers to angels who vigorously repel falsehood and disorder, carrying out Allah’s commands with complete obedience and firmness.

translation: Then those who recite the Reminder,
interpretation: This refers to the angels who recite and proclaim Allah’s revelation, affirming that the divine message is preserved and conveyed by His appointed servants.

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This affirms that the true deity is uniquely one, without partner or equal, and that worship belongs to Him alone.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever lies between them, and Lord of all points of sunrise.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses and governs the heavens, the earth, and everything between them; the changing places of sunrise further display His complete authority over creation and the order of the universe.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the beauty of the stars.
interpretation: Allah points to the splendor and order of the nearest heaven, making the stars a visible sign of His creative power and wisdom. Their beauty invites people to recognize the majesty of their Creator and reflect on the vastness and harmony of His creation.

translation: And as a protection from every rebellious devil.
interpretation: The heavens are guarded by Allah against every defiant satanic force, so that such beings cannot freely intrude upon the divine order or gain access to what has been concealed from them.

translation: They cannot eavesdrop on the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side.
interpretation: The verse portrays the divine protection of heavenly revelation: the devils are barred from overhearing the angels’ discourse and are driven away from every direction, so they cannot steal or distort the news of the unseen.

translation: Repelled, and for them is a lasting punishment.
interpretation: The devils are cast away from the heavenly realm in humiliation, and they face an unending punishment for their defiance and attempts to eavesdrop on the unseen.

translation: Except one who snatches a fleeting fragment, then a piercing flame pursues him.
interpretation: The verse portrays a rebellious being attempting to overhear a fragment of the heavenly decree, but divine protection swiftly prevents him through a blazing projectile. It signifies that access to the unseen is not open to devils and that revelation is guarded from their interference.

translation: So ask them: Are they stronger in creation, or those We have created? Indeed, We created them from clinging clay.
interpretation: The verse challenges those who deny resurrection: if human beings were created from humble, adhesive clay, they have no grounds to consider resurrection impossible. The One who created them initially is fully able to recreate them, and the greater creations around them testify to His power.

translation: Rather, you are amazed, while they ridicule.
interpretation: The verse portrays the striking contrast between the Prophet’s astonishment at their denial of clear signs and the disbelievers’ response of mockery, revealing their arrogance and spiritual blindness.

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not take heed.
interpretation: When the truth is brought to their attention, they refuse to reflect on it or allow it to guide their hearts and actions.

translation: And when they see a sign, they mock it.
interpretation: When these deniers witness a clear sign of God’s power or truth, instead of reflecting upon it and accepting its message, they respond with ridicule and contempt.

translation: And they said, “This is nothing but clear magic.”
interpretation: They rejected the revealed message by dismissing it as obvious sorcery, rather than considering its truth and guidance; this reflects their denial and attempt to discredit the messenger.

translation: “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we truly be resurrected?”
interpretation: This is a question of denial, expressing the skeptics’ refusal to believe that God can restore human beings to life after their bodies have decayed and become dust and bones.

translation: “Or even our forefathers of old?”
interpretation: They express their skeptical objection by asking whether their ancient ancestors, long dead and reduced to dust, will also be resurrected.

translation: قل: نعم، وأنتم صاغرون.
interpretation: يأمر الله نبيَّه أن يجيب المنكرين للبعث بأن الرجوع إلى الحياة واقع لا محالة، وأن من جحده سيُبعث ذليلًا خاضعًا لحكم الله، عاجزًا عن دفع الجزاء.

translation: It will be only one blast, and then suddenly they will be looking on.
interpretation: The resurrection will occur through a single command from God: one overwhelming blast will instantly bring the dead back to life, leaving them awake and witnessing the reality of the Hereafter.

translation: And they will say, “Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.”
interpretation: They will recognize with despair that the promised reckoning has arrived, and their cry reflects remorse and fear when they can no longer deny accountability for their deeds.

translation: This is the Day of Judgment that you used to deny.
interpretation: On this decisive Day, the truth becomes undeniable, and those who rejected the resurrection and accountability are confronted with the consequences of their denial.

translation: Gather those who did wrong, their associates, and whatever they used to worship.
interpretation: This is a command on the Day of Judgment to assemble the wrongdoers together with those who shared their ways and the objects of worship they relied upon, so that their false beliefs and deeds are exposed and they face the consequences of their wrongdoing.

translation: Those besides Allah—then guide them to the path of Hellfire.
interpretation: The verse commands that those who were worshipped instead of Allah, together with those who followed them in false worship, be led to the punishment of Hell, exposing the ultimate failure of associating partners with Allah.

translation: “Stop them, for they are to be questioned.”
interpretation: The command portrays the certainty of divine accountability: no one will pass beyond judgment without being confronted about their beliefs, deeds, and responsibilities.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?
interpretation: This is a rebuke addressed to those who denied the truth: on the Day of Judgment, the allies and false gods they relied upon will be powerless, and none of them will be able to protect or support the others.

translation: Rather, today they are utterly subdued.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who once acted arrogantly and relied on their power will be completely overcome, unable to resist God’s decree or help one another.

translation: And they will turn to one another, asking questions.
interpretation: When confronted with the truth and the consequences of their choices, they will face one another in bewilderment, questioning how they reached this fate and exposing the failure of the relationships and excuses they once relied upon.

translation: They will say, “Indeed, you used to come to us from the right.”
interpretation: The followers will accuse their leaders of approaching them under the guise of truth, righteousness, and sincere guidance, thereby making their falsehood appear trustworthy and leading them astray.

translation: They will say, “Rather, you were not believers.”
interpretation: This is a repudiation of the claim that they were compelled or misled into disbelief: they are told that their rejection arose from their own lack of genuine faith, not from an unavoidable excuse.

translation: We had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: The leaders of misguidance will disown their followers, declaring that they did not compel or control them. The followers chose rebellion and followed falsehood willingly, so they cannot shift responsibility for their deeds onto those who led them astray.

translation: So the word of our Lord has come true against us: indeed, we will taste the punishment.
interpretation: The disbelievers acknowledge that God’s promised judgment has become inevitable for them, and that they will personally endure the punishment they were warned about because of their rejection and misguidance.

translation: So we led you astray; indeed, we ourselves were astray.
interpretation: The misleaders acknowledge that they caused others to deviate because they were themselves already deviated, revealing that those who follow falsehood share responsibility with those who promote it.

translation: Indeed, on that Day they will share in the punishment.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who joined in disbelief and wrongdoing will jointly endure the consequences of their actions, with none able to escape or lessen the punishment of the others.

translation: Indeed, this is how We deal with the criminals.
interpretation: God establishes that the fate of those who persist in guilt and reject the truth is not arbitrary; He treats them with the justice they have earned, just as He has shown in the punishment of earlier wrongdoers.

translation: Indeed, when it was said to them, “There is no deity except Allah,” they would act arrogantly.
interpretation: They rejected the call to pure monotheism not because its truth was unclear, but because pride prevented them from abandoning the beliefs and status they had inherited and submitting themselves to Allah alone.

translation: And they say, “Are we really to abandon our gods for a mad poet?”
interpretation: They reject the Prophet’s call to worship Allah alone by mockingly labeling him a poet and a madman, using these accusations to justify their refusal to abandon the idols inherited from their forefathers.

translation: Rather, he has brought the truth and affirmed the messengers.
interpretation: The Qur’an declares that the Prophet Muhammad did not invent falsehood; he came with the truth from God, confirming the genuine message brought by all earlier messengers.

translation: Indeed, you will surely taste the painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing will inevitably experience the severe consequences of their denial in the Hereafter.

translation: You will be recompensed only for what you used to do.
interpretation: This establishes that every person’s reward or punishment is based on their own deeds, affirming God’s perfect justice and excluding any arbitrary judgment.

translation: Except the devoted servants of Allah.
interpretation: This refers to those whom Allah has purified through sincere faith and obedience, so Satan cannot lead them away from the truth.

translation: Those will have a provision that is known.
interpretation: The righteous are promised a provision whose goodness, abundance, and permanence are assured by God, free from uncertainty or deprivation.

translation: Fruits, and they will be honored.
interpretation: The righteous will receive abundant, delightful fruits in Paradise as a form of generous provision, while being treated with dignity, welcome, and honor by God.

translation: In the Gardens of Bliss.
interpretation: It signifies dwelling in a state of enduring divine favor, peace, and joy.

translation: Upon couches, facing one another.
interpretation: The righteous will dwell in Paradise in peaceful companionship, seated comfortably and facing each other with affection, free from estrangement or hostility.

translation: A cup of pure, flowing drink will be passed around among them.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise receiving their drink with ease and honor: it is pure, abundant, and ever available, free from the impurities and harmful effects associated with worldly intoxicants.

translation: White and delightful to those who drink.
interpretation: This describes the drink of Paradise as pure and radiant in appearance, offering the drinkers complete pleasure without the unpleasant effects or impurities associated with worldly beverages.

translation: There is no harmful effect in it, nor will they become intoxicated by it.
interpretation: The drink of Paradise is pure and free from the physical and mental harms associated with worldly intoxicants; it brings pleasure without clouding the mind, causing pain, or leading to loss of control.

translation: And with them are those who restrain their gaze, with beautiful, wide eyes.
interpretation: This portrays the companions of Paradise as embodying purity, modesty, and devoted affection, free from indiscriminate desire or distraction.

translation: As though they were well-guarded eggs.
interpretation: This portrays their purity, delicacy, and untouched beauty through the image of eggs carefully protected from harm or impurity.

translation: Then they will turn to one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This depicts the people of the Hereafter confronting one another and asking questions as they reflect on the choices and influences that led them to their final fate.

translation: One of them will say, “I had a companion.”
interpretation: A person in Paradise recalls a worldly companion who used to influence him and cast doubt on faith, revealing how companionship can profoundly affect a person’s beliefs and spiritual path.

translation: He would say, “Are you indeed among those who believe?”
interpretation: The speaker expresses astonishment and skepticism toward his companion’s belief in resurrection and the Hereafter, treating such faith as unlikely or unfounded.

translation: “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be held accountable?”
interpretation: This is the skeptical objection of those who deny resurrection: they regard returning to life after bodily decay as impossible and mock the idea that they will be brought before God for judgment and recompense.

translation: He said, “Will you take a look?”
interpretation: The speaker invites his companions to observe the fate of the one who had misled him, revealing the stark contrast between divine salvation and the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: Then he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire.
interpretation: The believer is granted a view of his former companion and recognizes him suffering at the very center of Hell, revealing the final consequence of rejecting faith and denying the Resurrection.

translation: He will say, “By Allah, you almost ruined me.”
interpretation: The speaker acknowledges that his companion’s influence nearly led him away from faith and obedience, bringing him close to spiritual destruction; he recognizes this only after witnessing the truth of the Hereafter.

translation: Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would surely have been among those brought forth for punishment.
interpretation: The verse expresses that deliverance from punishment is ultimately due to Allah’s grace and guidance; a person should therefore remain humble, grateful, and never rely solely on their own deeds.

translation: Will we then not die?
interpretation: This rhetorical question expresses certainty that, after the one death of worldly life, there will be no further death or end to their existence.

translation: Except for our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: The speaker affirms that after the one death experienced in worldly life, there will be no further death and no punishment in the Hereafter; this reflects the certainty and security granted to the people of Paradise.

translation: Indeed, this is surely the supreme success.
interpretation: The greatest success is attaining Allah’s reward and everlasting salvation, far surpassing any temporary worldly achievement.

translation: For such a reward, let those who strive exert themselves.
interpretation: The verse directs people to make the greatest effort toward the lasting reward of God, treating it as the true goal worthy of their deeds rather than being consumed by temporary worldly gains.

translation: Is that a better welcome, or the tree of Zaqqūm?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge contrasting the delightful provision prepared for the people of Paradise with the tree of Zaqqūm, the dreadful food prepared for the people of Hell, thereby exposing the foolishness of preferring disobedience over faith and obedience.

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The punishment mentioned in the preceding verses—represented by the tree of Zaqqūm—serves as a test for those who persist in wrongdoing: its description exposes their denial and arrogance, while confirming the truth for those who believe.

translation: إنها شجرةٌ تنبت في أصل الجحيم.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية شجرة الزقّوم بأنها نابتة في أعمق موضع من جهنم، فيكون أصلها ومصدرها مرتبطًا بعذابها، مما يبرز فظاعة هذا الطعام وشدة التنفير منه.

translation: Its fruit is as though it were the heads of devils.
interpretation: يُصوِّر القرآن قبح ثمر شجرة الزقوم وبشاعته بصورة رؤوس الشياطين، وهي صورة مرعبة تنفّر منها النفوس، للدلالة على شدة سوء هذا الطعام وعذاب أهل النار به.

translation: Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: This depicts the people of Hell being compelled to consume the bitter, repulsive food of punishment, finding no nourishment or comfort in it despite filling themselves with it.

translation: Then indeed, for them upon it is a mixture of scalding water.
interpretation: The food prepared for the people of Hell is accompanied by boiling water mixed into it, so that what might otherwise nourish them becomes another source of torment.

translation: Then surely their return will be to Hellfire.
interpretation: Despite whatever brief enjoyment they may experience, their ultimate destination is Hell, where they will face the consequence of their rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, they found their forefathers astray.
interpretation: They persisted in error because they blindly followed the beliefs of their ancestors, treating inherited custom as proof rather than seeking guidance and truth.

translation: So they hasten along in their footsteps.
interpretation: They rush to imitate their forefathers, following their beliefs and practices blindly without reflecting on the truth.

translation: Indeed, most of those who came before them had gone astray.
interpretation: The verse warns that the majority of earlier peoples were not a measure of truth; despite their numbers, they strayed from God’s guidance, so those who reject the message should not find reassurance in following the crowd.

translation: And We certainly sent among them warners.
interpretation: God emphasizes that He did not leave those people without guidance; He sent messengers and admonishers to warn them of the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing and to call them back to obedience and righteousness.

translation: So observe what was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This is a warning to reflect on the fate of peoples who were cautioned by God’s messengers but persisted in denial and wrongdoing; their destruction demonstrates the consequence of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Except the sincerely devoted servants of Allah.
interpretation: Those who dedicate themselves wholly and sincerely to Allah are distinguished from others because their faith and devotion protect them from being led astray.

translation: And Noah certainly called upon Us, and how excellent are We in answering prayers.
interpretation: Noah’s supplication was met by Allah with perfect care and deliverance, showing that Allah responds generously and faithfully to the sincere calls of His servants.

translation: And We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: God rescued Noah and those of his household who believed from the overwhelming suffering of the Flood, showing that sincere faith and obedience are a means of divine deliverance from even the gravest trials.

translation: And We made his descendants the survivors.
interpretation: After the Flood, God preserved Noah’s descendants, making them the continuing human lineage while the others who rejected the truth were destroyed.

translation: And We left for him a lasting mention among later generations.
interpretation: Allah preserved Noah’s honorable reputation among those who came after him, making his faithfulness and steadfastness remembered as a lasting reward.

translation: Peace be upon Noah among all the worlds.
interpretation: Allah grants Noah enduring honor and praise among all peoples and generations, making his sincere faith and steadfastness worthy of continual remembrance and blessing.

translation: Indeed, this is how We reward those who do good.
interpretation: Allah establishes that sincere excellence in faith and conduct is met with generous divine recompense, affirming that goodness is never overlooked.

translation: Indeed, he is among Our believing servants.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the person referred to belongs to His sincere servants whose faith is genuine, thereby honoring him for devotion and submission to Him.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: This refers to the people of Pharaoh who pursued Moses and the believers; after Allah saved the faithful, He destroyed the pursuers by drowning as a consequence of their persistent rejection and oppression.

translation: And indeed, Abraham was surely among his followers.
interpretation: Abraham belonged to the same community of faith as Noah, sharing his sincere devotion to the oneness of God and his rejection of idolatry, even though he came after him.

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
interpretation: This describes Abraham’s sincere devotion to God: he approached Him with a heart purified from idolatry, hypocrisy, doubt, and corrupt desires, relying wholly on the truth and submitting himself to his Lord.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, “What is it that you worship?”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm confronted his father and his people with a question that challenged them to examine the legitimacy of their worship, exposing that their devotion was directed toward objects and beings unable to provide any true divine authority.

translation: Do you desire false gods besides Allah?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of worshipping other beings besides Allah, exposing such devotion as a fabricated falsehood with no rightful basis.

translation: “Then what is your assumption about the Lord of all worlds?”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm challenges them to reflect on who Allah truly is: the sovereign Creator and Sustainer of everything, utterly beyond the powerless idols they worship, and therefore deserving of exclusive worship and complete trust.

translation: Then he cast a glance at the stars.
interpretation: Ibrāhīm looked toward the stars as part of a deliberate pretext, preparing to excuse himself from joining his people in their idolatrous festival and to expose the weakness of their beliefs.

translation: So he said, “Indeed, I am ill.”
interpretation: Abraham used this statement as a lawful excuse to remain behind while his people went to their festival, enabling him to expose the falsehood of their idols; his “illness” may refer to physical illness or to his deep distress at their idolatry.

translation: So they turned away from him, retreating.
interpretation: They rejected what he called them to and deliberately withdrew, turning their backs rather than considering the truth.

translation: Then he turned stealthily toward their gods and said, “Will you not eat?”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm spoke to the idols sarcastically, exposing their powerlessness: they could neither eat the food offered to them nor respond to him, revealing that they were lifeless objects unworthy of worship.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: Abraham rebuked the idols by exposing their helplessness: beings unable to speak, respond, or defend themselves cannot rightly be treated as gods or relied upon for worship.

translation: Then he turned upon them, striking them with his right hand.
interpretation: Ibrahim decisively destroyed the idols to expose their helplessness and demonstrate that they could neither protect themselves nor deserve worship.

translation: Then they came rushing toward him.
interpretation: When the people realized what had happened to their idols, they hurried angrily toward Abraham to confront him and demand an explanation.

translation: He said, “Do you worship what you yourselves carve?”
interpretation: Abraham condemned the worship of idols fashioned by human hands, emphasizing that something created and shaped by people cannot rightfully be treated as a god or worshipped.

translation: And Allah created you and whatever you do.
interpretation: Everything human beings do exists by Allah’s creative power and permission, yet they choose their actions and are therefore responsible for them.

translation: They said, “Build a furnace for him and cast him into the blazing fire.”
interpretation: After Ibrahim عليه السلام exposed the falsehood of idol worship, his people resorted to cruel punishment: they constructed a great fire and intended to throw him into it, believing they could silence the truth through force.

translation: So they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest.
interpretation: When Abraham’s people sought to defeat and harm him through their scheme, God frustrated their efforts, deprived them of power, and caused their falsehood to be overcome.

translation: And he said, “Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.”
interpretation: Abraham declares his resolve to leave behind a people who reject the truth and turn wholly toward Allah, trusting that his Lord will guide and support him in every step of this journey.

translation: My Lord, grant me a child from among the righteous.
interpretation: This is a humble supplication to Allah for offspring who possess faith, virtue, and obedience, showing that the true blessing lies not merely in having a child but in being granted one whose character and conduct are righteous.

translation: So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy.
interpretation: Allah announced to Abraham the coming of a son distinguished by patience, gentleness, and steadfast obedience, qualities that would enable him to endure hardship and fulfill his responsibilities faithfully.

translation: When he had reached the age of working alongside him, he said, “My dear son, I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so consider what you think.” He replied, “My dear father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among those who are steadfast.”
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound submission of both father and son to Allah’s command: the father presents the matter with tenderness and consultation, while the son responds with trust, courage, and patience. Their obedience is not portrayed as blind impulse, but as willing surrender to divine guidance, accompanied by reliance on Allah and confidence that steadfastness comes by His will.

translation: Then, when they had both submitted themselves, and he had laid him down upon his forehead,
interpretation: Ibrāhīm and his son fully yielded to Allah’s command; the father placed his son face down, prepared to carry out the sacrifice with complete obedience and trust in Allah.

translation: And We called out to him: “O Abraham!”
interpretation: Allah called Abraham directly after his complete submission, signaling that the test had reached its decisive moment and that divine mercy and guidance were about to intervene.

translation: You have indeed fulfilled the vision. Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: Allah declares that Abraham proved his complete obedience by being fully prepared to carry out the vision, and shows that sincere submission and willingness to sacrifice for His command are rewarded with His grace.

translation: Indeed, this was surely the clear trial.
interpretation: This was a profound test of sincere submission to God: Ibrahim’s willingness to obey, even in the most painful command, demonstrated that his devotion placed God’s command above every personal attachment.

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: God spared the one offered in obedience and replaced him with a sacrificial offering, showing that sincere submission to God is accepted and that human life is not to be sacrificed in His worship.

translation: And We preserved for him a good name among later generations.
interpretation: Allah granted Noah lasting honor and praise among the generations that came after him, as a reward for his faithfulness and perseverance.

translation: سلامٌ على إبراهيمَ
interpretation: يُكرم الله إبراهيم عليه السلام بسلامٍ دائمٍ ورحمةٍ وذكرٍ حسن، جزاءً لإخلاصه وثباته في طاعته.

translation: Thus do We reward those who excel in goodness.
interpretation: Allah establishes that sincere excellence in faith and conduct is met with His gracious reward, showing that righteous deeds are never overlooked.

translation: Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This affirms that he belonged to God’s chosen servants whose faith was sincere, acknowledging their devotion and spiritual standing before Him.

translation: وبشّرناه بإسحاق نبيًّا من الصالحين.
interpretation: يبين الله أن إسحاق عليه السلام كان بشارةً لإبراهيم، وأن هذه البشارة لم تكن بمولده فحسب، بل بكونه نبيًّا مستقيمًا من عباد الله الصالحين، جامعًا بين شرف النبوة وكمال الصلاح.

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac; and among their descendants are those who do good and those who plainly wrong themselves.
interpretation: The blessing bestowed upon Abraham and Isaac extended through their descendants, but lineage alone does not guarantee righteousness. Among them would be people who live virtuously and others who, by rejecting guidance and committing wrongdoing, clearly bring harm upon themselves.

translation: And We certainly bestowed Our favor upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: God reminds that He granted Moses and Aaron special blessings, support, and honor, enabling them to fulfill their mission and lead their people in accordance with His guidance.

translation: And We saved them both, along with their people, from the tremendous distress.
interpretation: Allah rescued Moses, Aaron, and the Children of Israel from the oppression, humiliation, and persecution inflicted upon them by Pharaoh, showing that divine deliverance comes to those who remain faithful and seek refuge in Him.

translation: And We supported them, so they became the victors.
interpretation: Allah strengthened Moses and Aaron against their opponents, granting them victory and establishing that divine support ultimately enables the truth to prevail over falsehood.

translation: And We gave them both the clear Scripture.
interpretation: God granted Moses and Aaron a revealed Book whose guidance was plain and decisive, making the truth evident and distinguishing it from falsehood.

translation: And We guided them both to the straight path.
interpretation: Allah granted Moses and Aaron steadfast guidance to the path of truth and obedience, enabling them to fulfill their mission rightly.

translation: And We preserved for them both a good remembrance among later generations.
interpretation: Allah caused Moses and Aaron to be remembered with praise and honor by successive generations because of their faithfulness and obedience to Him.

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: الله يكرّم موسى وهارون بذكرهما بالسلام، جزاءً لإخلاصهما في تبليغ رسالته ومقاومة الباطل، وإشارةً إلى دوام الرحمة والذكر الحسن لهما.

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward those who do good.
interpretation: Allah’s consistent way is to honor those who act with sincere faith and righteousness, rewarding their excellence with His protection, favor, and a good outcome.

translation: Indeed, both of them were among Our believing servants.
interpretation: Allah honors them by describing them first as His servants and then as believers, showing that true distinction comes through sincere devotion to Him and firm faith.

translation: And indeed, Ilyas was truly one of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Ilyas was chosen by God as a genuine messenger, entrusted with conveying divine guidance to his people.

translation: When he said to his people, “Will you not be mindful of Allah?”
interpretation: The speaker admonishes his people for neglecting their duty to God and calls them to awaken their conscience, abandon disobedience, and live with reverent awareness of Him.

translation: Do you call upon Baal and leave the Best of creators?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of the people of the prophet Elijah for worshipping Baal, an idol, while abandoning Allah—the One whose creative power and perfection surpass all others. It calls them to abandon false gods and devote worship exclusively to Allah.

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.
interpretation: Allah alone is the true Lord of both you and your ancestors; therefore, worship and obedience belong exclusively to Him, not to anything inherited from past generations.

translation: So they denied him, yet they will surely be brought before Us.
interpretation: Those who reject the truth cannot escape its consequences; they will inevitably be summoned before God for judgment and held accountable for their denial.

translation: Except for the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: Allah exempts those who worship Him with genuine devotion, free from associating partners with Him and from seeking praise or worldly gain.

translation: And We left for him a good mention among later generations.
interpretation: God preserved Noah’s honorable reputation so that succeeding generations would remember him with praise for his faithfulness and steadfastness.

translation: Peace be upon the family of Ilyas.
interpretation: Allah grants enduring peace, honor, and protection to Prophet Ilyas and the righteous people devoted to his path.

translation: Indeed, this is how We reward those who do good.
interpretation: Allah establishes that sincere excellence and righteousness are met with His gracious reward; whoever acts with faith, obedience, and goodness may trust that such goodness is never overlooked.

translation: Indeed, he was one of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This affirms that he belonged to Allah through sincere servitude and genuine faith, indicating that his honor and righteousness came from his devotion to Allah.

translation: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.
interpretation: This affirms that Lot was chosen by Allah as a true messenger, sharing in the honored mission of conveying divine guidance to his people.

translation: When We saved him and all his family,
interpretation: This refers to God’s saving the prophet and everyone of his household who believed, protecting them from the punishment that overtook those who rejected the truth.

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This refers to the wife of Lot, who was left behind with the doomed people because she did not join the believers and shared in their rejection.

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: Those who rejected the truth and persisted in wrongdoing were destroyed after the believers were saved, demonstrating that divine punishment overtakes persistent rebellion while God grants deliverance to those who obey Him.

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning.
interpretation: The verse points to the people of Lot, whose ruined dwellings were visible along the travelers’ route. Their remains stood as an evident warning that denying God and persisting in wrongdoing leads to destruction, yet many who saw them failed to take heed.

translation: And by night—will you not then understand?
interpretation: The repeated sight of these signs, even during the night, should awaken the mind to reflect, draw lessons, and recognize the truth rather than pass by heedlessly.

translation: And indeed, Jonah was truly among the messengers.
interpretation: This affirms that Yunus (Jonah), despite the trial he endured, was chosen by God as a genuine messenger and honored member of the prophetic mission.

translation: When he fled to the laden ship,
interpretation: This refers to Jonah’s leaving his people in haste and boarding a fully loaded ship, seeking escape before God had granted him permission to depart.

translation: Then he took part in the casting of lots and was among those who lost.
interpretation: When the ship was overwhelmed by the storm, the passengers cast lots to determine who should be cast overboard, and Jonah’s name was drawn. Thus, by Allah’s decree, he was among those overcome and removed from the ship.

translation: Then the fish swallowed him, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: Jonah was swallowed because he had departed from his people in a state that exposed him to blame, before receiving God’s permission; the verse portrays this as a moment of accountability and divine discipline, not abandonment by God.

translation: Had he not been among those who glorified Allah,
interpretation: بيّن الله أن يونس عليه السلام نجا من بطن الحوت بفضل ملازمته للتسبيح والعبادة؛ فذكره الصادق في وقت الشدة كان سببًا لرحمته وفرجه.

translation: He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: Had Jonah not glorified and supplicated Allah, he would have continued confined within the fish until the Resurrection, showing that his deliverance was a mercy granted through repentance and remembrance of Allah.

translation: فطرحناه في أرضٍ مكشوفةٍ وهو مريض.
interpretation: يبين الله أن يونس عليه السلام أُخرج من بطن الحوت إلى مكانٍ عارٍ لا يستره فيه شيء، وقد أنهكه المرض، فكان ذلك مظهراً لعناية الله به وإنقاذه بعد محنته.

translation: And We caused a gourd plant to grow over him.
interpretation: Allah caused the gourd vine to grow over Jonah, providing him with shade and protection after he was cast ashore, as an expression of divine care and mercy.

translation: And We sent him to a hundred thousand, or even more.
interpretation: This describes the vast number of people to whom Jonah was sent, with “or more” emphasizing that their population exceeded one hundred thousand; it is not uncertainty on God’s part, but a manner of expressing their immense number.

translation: So they believed, and We allowed them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: When they responded with faith, Allah accepted their repentance and granted them continued worldly life until the time He had appointed for them.

translation: So ask them: Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of those who attributed female offspring to Allah while claiming male offspring for themselves. It exposes the inconsistency and injustice of their belief, affirming that Allah is far above such human categories and fabricated claims.

translation: Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who claimed that the angels were female: on what basis could they make such a claim when they were not present to witness their creation? The verse exposes the claim as mere conjecture without knowledge or evidence.

translation: Indeed, it is out of their falsehood that they say…
interpretation: This exposes their claim as a deliberate fabrication rooted in deception rather than truth or sound evidence.

translation: “Allah has begotten a child,” yet they are certainly liars.
interpretation: This is a categorical denial of the claim that Allah has offspring. It affirms that attributing a child to Him is false, because Allah is utterly independent and unlike His creation, and therefore cannot be described by lineage or procreation.

translation: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question denouncing the claim that Allah has daughters while people regard sons as superior; it exposes the contradiction and falsehood in attributing offspring to Him.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This is a rebuke for making a baseless judgment that contradicts truth and sound reason, urging reflection before forming conclusions.

translation: Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: This is a reproachful invitation to awaken the mind and heart, reflect on the truth, and remember what should lead one to faith and obedience.

translation: Or do you possess clear authority?
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who make claims about God without revelation: do they have any decisive proof or valid authority to support what they say?

translation: Then bring your scripture, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who make claims about God without proof: if their claim is true, they should present an authoritative revelation supporting it.

translation: And they have claimed a kinship between Him and the jinn, while the jinn certainly know that they will be brought before Him.
interpretation: The verse condemns the false claim that Allah has a family connection or offspring among the jinn. Such beings, far from sharing in His divinity, know that they themselves are servants accountable to Him and will be brought before Him for judgment.

translation: Glory be to Allah, far above what they describe.
interpretation: This declares Allah’s absolute transcendence and purity from every false attribute, limitation, or claim that people ascribe to Him.

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: Those who devote their worship and obedience purely to Allah are exempted from the fate described in the surrounding passage, because their faith is genuine and free from idolatry and hypocrisy.

translation: Indeed, you and whatever you worship,
interpretation: This is the beginning of a declaration that the idolaters and their objects of worship have no independent power to mislead or overcome anyone; ultimate authority belongs to Allah alone.

translation: You cannot lead anyone astray concerning it.
interpretation: The false gods and those who promote them have no power to compel people away from the truth; their influence affects only those who willingly follow the path leading to Hell.

translation: Except for the one who will enter the Blaze.
interpretation: The exception refers to those destined for Hell because of their rejection and disobedience; they are the ones who can be led astray from the path of truth.

translation: There is none among us except that he has a known station.
interpretation: The angels affirm that each of them has a divinely appointed rank and place in Allah’s service, which they neither exceed nor neglect; this expresses their complete obedience, order, and humility before Him.

translation: And indeed, we are those who stand in orderly ranks.
interpretation: The angels affirm their complete discipline and unwavering devotion to Allah: they remain arranged in ranks, ready to carry out His commands and worship Him with perfect obedience.

translation: And indeed, we are those who glorify Allah.
interpretation: The angels affirm that their true role is devoted worship: they continually declare Allah’s perfection and exalt Him above every imperfection, rather than possessing any divine status themselves.

translation: And indeed, they used to say,
interpretation: This expression introduces a statement they repeatedly made in the past, emphasizing that their words were a habitual claim rather than a single remark.

translation: If only we had a reminder from the former peoples,
interpretation: They express a hypothetical excuse, claiming that possessing a revealed reminder like those given to earlier nations would have led them to obey God; the statement exposes their attempt to shift blame from their own rejection to the supposed absence of revelation.

translation: But not so with the servants of Allah who are sincerely devoted.
interpretation: Those whom Allah has purified and enabled to remain wholly devoted to Him are protected from being led astray and are exempt from the fate of those who reject His guidance.

translation: Yet they denied it, so they will soon come to know.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth will not shield them from its consequences; when the reality becomes unmistakable, they will recognize what they had denied.

translation: ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين.
interpretation: هذا إخبارٌ بأن وعد الله وقضاءه قد تقدّما لعباده المرسلين، وهو أن يؤيدهم ويحفظ دعوتهم ويجعل العاقبة والنصر لهم على أعدائهم، ولو بعد ابتلاءٍ أو تأخرٍ في ظهور الغلبة.

translation: Indeed, they will surely be granted victory.
interpretation: This is a firm assurance that those whom God supports will not be abandoned: He will aid them, strengthen their position, and ultimately cause their cause to prevail over opposition.

translation: And indeed, Our forces will be victorious.
interpretation: Allah assures that those who support His truth will ultimately prevail over falsehood, even if they face temporary hardship or apparent defeat.

translation: So turn away from them for a time.
interpretation: This is a command to withdraw from those who persist in rejecting the truth, leaving them temporarily to their chosen course until the time appointed by God, when His judgment or the fulfillment of His promise will become manifest.

translation: And watch them, for they will soon see.
interpretation: Remain mindful of their fate; the truth they reject will soon become unmistakably clear to them when its consequences appear.

translation: Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who mockingly demand the punishment promised to them, treating it as something to be challenged, while the delay granted to them is only a reprieve and not an indication that they are safe from God’s judgment.

translation: But when it descends upon their dwelling, evil indeed will be the morning of those who were warned.
interpretation: The verse portrays the arrival of divine punishment among those who rejected the warning as a devastating dawn, emphasizing that heedlessness does not avert the consequence once it comes.

translation: And turn away from them for a time.
interpretation: This instructs the Prophet to temporarily distance himself from those who persist in rejection, leaving their matter to Allah’s judgment and awaiting the time when His promise and decree become manifest.

translation: And observe, for they will soon observe.
interpretation: This is a warning that the truth will soon become unmistakable: the Messenger is to remain steadfast, while those who deny will come to recognize the reality and consequences of their rejection when it is too late to escape them.

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, far above what they attribute to Him.
interpretation: Allah is utterly exalted in power and perfection, transcending every false description, limitation, or claim that people ascribe to Him.

translation: And peace be upon the messengers.
interpretation: Allah bestows honor, protection, and благessing upon all His messengers, affirming the truth of their mission and the soundness of the guidance they conveyed.

translation: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: Every form of perfect praise and gratitude is due to Allah alone, who creates, sustains, governs, and cares for all existence.

translation: Ṣād. By the Qur’an, full of remembrance.
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the Qur’an’s elevated status by swearing by it as a source of remembrance: it awakens people to the truth, reminds them of their Lord, and preserves the guidance they need. The meaning of the opening letter Ṣād is known fully to Allah.

translation: Rather, those who disbelieve are steeped in arrogance and opposition.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth does not arise from a lack of clarity, but from proud defiance and a stubborn willingness to oppose it.

translation: How many generations before them We have destroyed! Then they cried out, but it was no longer the time for escape.
interpretation: The verse warns that those who persist in rejecting the truth may eventually face divine punishment, at which point their cries for rescue and repentance will no longer avail them; therefore, heedfulness and return to God must occur before the moment of judgment arrives.

translation: And they are amazed that a warner from among themselves has come to them. The disbelievers say, “This is a magician, a liar.”
interpretation: The disbelievers rejected the Prophet ﷺ because they found it strange that God would send a human being from their own people as a messenger. Rather than consider his warning sincerely, they dismissed him with false accusations of sorcery and lying.

translation: “Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is surely a wondrous thing!”
interpretation: The disbelievers reject the Prophet’s call to worship Allah alone because abandoning the many deities they inherited from their forefathers seems to them astonishing and unacceptable; their reaction exposes their attachment to tradition rather than a reasoned response to the truth of monotheism.

translation: And the leading figures among them went away, saying, “Go on and remain steadfast in devotion to your gods. Indeed, this is something intended against you.”
interpretation: The chiefs of the disbelievers urged one another to cling firmly to their inherited idols, portraying the call to worship one God as a deliberate scheme against their authority and religious traditions. Their response reveals that they recognized the challenge posed by monotheism but resisted it out of attachment to their established beliefs and status.

translation: “We have never heard of this in the latter religion. This is nothing but an invention.”
interpretation: The disbelievers rejected the Prophet’s call to worship one God alone, claiming that such teaching had no basis in the religious tradition they knew and accusing him of fabricating it.

translation: “Has the Reminder been sent down to him alone from among us?” Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder; rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
interpretation: The deniers reject the Prophet ﷺ out of envy and disbelief, questioning why revelation was given to him instead of one of their leaders. Their uncertainty is not evidence against the truth; it persists only because they have not yet experienced the consequence of rejecting God’s message.

translation: Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Bestower?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: no one controls or owns the treasures of Allah’s mercy, including revelation and prophethood. Allah alone, in His might and generosity, grants them to whomever He wills.

translation: Or do they possess dominion over the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who oppose the truth: they possess no authority over the universe or its affairs, so if they claim power to control divine decree or prevent God’s revelation, let them ascend through whatever means they can find and prove it.

translation: There is but a host there destined to be defeated, among the factions.
interpretation: This is a warning that the forces opposing the truth, regardless of their numbers or alliances, will ultimately be defeated and humiliated, as were the hostile factions before them.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah, ʿĀd, and Pharaoh, the possessor of the stakes, denied the truth.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Prophet that rejection of divine messengers is an old pattern: powerful peoples and rulers—despite their strength and authority—denied the truth and were not spared its consequences. Pharaoh is described as “the possessor of the stakes,” alluding to his immense power and possibly his brutal instruments of punishment, emphasizing that worldly dominance cannot protect anyone from God’s judgment.

translation: And Thamūd, the people of Lot, and the dwellers of the thicket—all these were the factions.
interpretation: The verse recalls earlier nations who opposed their prophets and were destroyed, emphasizing that the disbelievers in Mecca are following the same path of defiance and should therefore heed the warning before facing a similar fate.

translation: None of them but denied the messengers, so My punishment became inevitable.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the downfall of those peoples was not due to their powerlessness, but to their deliberate rejection of God’s messengers; therefore, divine punishment became deserved and unavoidable.

translation: These people await nothing but a single blast, one that allows no delay.
interpretation: They are being warned that the punishment may come suddenly and without any opportunity for respite, recovery, or escape; therefore, their continued denial is perilous.

translation: And they say, “Our Lord, hasten for us our share before the Day of Reckoning.”
interpretation: They say this defiantly and mockingly, challenging the warning of the Day of Judgment by demanding that their allotted punishment come immediately rather than waiting for the promised reckoning.

translation: Be patient with what they say, and remember Our servant David, a man of strength. Indeed, he was ever turning back to Allah.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to remain steadfast in the face of opposition and presents David as an example of strength joined with constant repentance, devotion, and return to Allah.

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains to him; they glorified along with him in the evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: God bestowed upon David the extraordinary blessing that the mountains joined him in praising God at the times of evening and sunrise, revealing both the harmony of creation in worship and the special honor granted to him.

translation: And the birds were gathered together; all were repeatedly turning to Him.
interpretation: Allah granted David the extraordinary favor that the birds assembled with him and joined in glorifying Him, showing that all creation responds to its Lord in worship and praise.

translation: ونحن قوَّينا مُلكه، وآتيناه الحكمة والقدرة على الفصل في الخصومات ببيانٍ حاسم.
interpretation: أي أن الله ثبّت سلطان داود وأمدّه بالحكمة والرشد، ومنحه قوة البيان وحسن القضاء، حتى يميّز الحق من الباطل ويفصل بين الناس بالعدل والقول الفاصل.

translation: And has the account of the disputants reached you, when they climbed over the wall into the sanctuary?
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the remarkable and unexpected arrival of two litigants who entered David’s secluded place by scaling its walls, preparing the listener for the serious moral lesson contained in their dispute.

translation: When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them, they said, “Do not fear. We are two disputants; one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that a judge must seek truth with fairness and impartiality, resisting fear, haste, or deviation from justice, while the disputing parties must submit their case to a ruling that leads them toward what is right.

translation: “Indeed, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes, while I have only one. Yet he said, ‘Entrust it to me,’ and he overpowered me in speech.”
interpretation: The speaker presents a case of clear imbalance: despite already possessing great abundance, his brother seeks to take the one ewe belonging to him, relying on persuasive authority to prevail. The passage portrays how greed and rhetorical power can become instruments of injustice, and it calls for judgment based on truth rather than influence.

translation: He said, “He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe in addition to his ewes. Indeed, many partners transgress against one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds—and they are few.” And David realized that We had tested him, so he sought his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down bowing, and turned in repentance.
interpretation: David’s judgment exposed how easily power, partnership, or personal desire can lead one person to violate another’s rights. The verse emphasizes that justice and restraint are uncommon unless they are rooted in faith and righteous conduct. When David recognized that the case was also a test of his own judgment, he did not persist in self-assurance; instead, he immediately sought forgiveness and returned humbly to God, showing that true righteousness includes recognizing one’s vulnerability to error and responding with sincere repentance.

translation: So We forgave him that; and indeed, he has nearness with Us and an excellent final return.
interpretation: Allah accepted David’s repentance and pardoned his lapse, assuring that sincere repentance restores a servant to divine favor, closeness, and a noble destiny in the Hereafter.

translation: O David, We have appointed you as a successor on earth, so judge between people with truth and do not follow personal desire, lest it lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who stray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: Allah instructs David that authority is a trust requiring justice, impartial judgment, and obedience to divine guidance. Personal desires can distort truth and lead a person away from Allah’s path; neglecting accountability on the Day of Reckoning is a root cause of such deviation and brings severe punishment.

translation: We did not create the heaven and the earth and everything between them without purpose. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve; so woe to those who disbelieve because of the Fire.
interpretation: The order and existence of creation are not meaningless or accidental; they point to divine wisdom and an ultimate purpose. Denying this purpose leads people to reject accountability before God, and the verse warns that such denial has a grave consequence in the Hereafter.

translation: Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or shall We treat the God-fearing like the wicked?
interpretation: The verse rejects any notion that faith, righteousness, and piety are equal to corruption and wickedness. Divine justice requires that people be judged according to their moral choices, so the two groups cannot have the same standing or final outcome.

translation: A blessed Book We have revealed to you, so that they may reflect deeply on its verses and those possessed of sound understanding may take heed.
interpretation: This revelation is meant to be engaged with thoughtfully: its blessings become transformative when people ponder its guidance with sincere understanding, allowing its truths to awaken their hearts and shape their lives.

translation: And We granted David Solomon. What an excellent servant he was! Indeed, he was ever turning to Allah.
interpretation: Solomon’s excellence is attributed not merely to his status or power, but to his constant return to Allah in devotion, repentance, and obedience.

translation: When there were displayed before him in the afternoon, the noble, swift steeds,
interpretation: The verse portrays the magnificent horses being presented before Solomon for his inspection, emphasizing their grace, strength, and disciplined readiness.

translation: He said, “Indeed, I have come to love these fine horses more than the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun disappeared behind the veil.”
interpretation: Solomon acknowledges that his intense attention to the noble horses occupied him until the time of remembrance or prayer passed, with “the sun disappearing behind the veil” indicating sunset.

translation: “Bring them back to me.” Then he began striking their legs and necks.
interpretation: Solomon, realizing that the horses had distracted him from remembering his Lord, ordered them returned and sacrificed them as an act of repentance and renewed devotion to God.

translation: And We certainly tested Solomon and cast a body upon his throne; then he turned back to Allah.
interpretation: Allah tested Solomon by stripping him, for a time, of the strength and authority associated with his kingship, leaving him like a lifeless body upon his throne. Through this trial, he recognized his complete dependence on Allah and returned to Him with repentance and humility.

translation: He said, “My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom unlike any that will belong to anyone after me. Surely, You are the Ever-Giving.”
interpretation: Prophet Solomon turns first to repentance and forgiveness, then asks Allah for an extraordinary kingdom suited to his mission—one whose unique authority and blessings would testify to Allah’s power. By ending with “You are the Ever-Giving,” he acknowledges that such gifts can come only from Allah’s generosity.

translation: So We subjected the wind to him, blowing gently at his command wherever he directed.
interpretation: God granted Solomon authority over the wind, yet its movement remained governed by God’s command; this teaches that extraordinary power is a divine trust, not an independent possession.

translation: And the devils—every builder and diver.
interpretation: Allah subjected the devils to Solomon’s authority, making them serve him in constructing buildings and diving into the sea to retrieve what was needed, all by Allah’s permission.

translation: And others bound together in shackles.
interpretation: This portrays rebellious beings held in severe restraint, chained and confined so that they cannot escape or cause harm.

translation: هذا عطاؤنا، فامنح منه أو أمسك بغير حساب.
interpretation: يبين الله لسليمان عليه السلام أن ما وهبه من الملك والتصرف فضلٌ خالص منه، وقد خوّله أن يعطي منه من يشاء أو يمسكه عمّن يشاء، دون مؤاخذة أو تضييق في الحساب.

translation: And indeed, he has a position of nearness with Us and an excellent place of return.
interpretation: Allah affirms that he is honored by being brought near to Him through His favor and acceptance, and that his ultimate destination is a blessed and commendable abode.

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord, “Indeed, Satan has afflicted me with weariness and suffering.”
interpretation: The verse portrays Job turning to God in humble supplication after prolonged hardship, recognizing Satan’s role in intensifying his distress while directing his plea solely to his Lord for relief.

translation: Stamp your foot; this is a cool spring for washing and drinking.
interpretation: Allah commands Job to strike the ground with his foot, bringing forth a spring whose water becomes a means of cleansing, healing, and refreshment—an immediate sign of divine mercy after his long trial.

translation: And We granted him his family, and the like of them along with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of sound understanding.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah’s mercy can restore and even increase what sincere servants have lost after enduring hardship with patience, making Job’s experience a lesson for people who reflect and trust in divine wisdom.

translation: “Take in your hand a bundle of grass, strike with it, and do not break your oath.” Indeed, We found him patient; what an excellent servant! Truly, he was ever turning to God.
interpretation: After Job swore to discipline his wife, God mercifully instructed him to use a bundle containing many blades and strike her once, thereby fulfilling the oath without causing harm. This ruling reflects God’s compassion and wisdom, while the verse praises Job for his steadfast patience through hardship and his constant return to God.

translation: And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—men of strength and insight.
interpretation: Allah presents these prophets as exemplary servants who combined steadfast power in obedience and action with clear spiritual understanding, enabling them to carry out their mission with wisdom and devotion.

translation: Indeed, We purified them with a special quality: remembrance of the Hereafter.
interpretation: Allah granted them a sincere and enduring awareness of the Hereafter, so that their hearts and actions remained focused on seeking His pleasure and preparing for the eternal abode.

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent.
interpretation: Allah declares that these servants hold an honored rank in His presence, having been selected for their purity, righteousness, and excellence.

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhū al-Kifl; each was among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to recall these honored servants as examples of goodness and steadfast obedience. By affirming that each belonged to the best and most righteous, it teaches that true distinction before God lies in faith, virtue, and devoted service, not merely in worldly status.

translation: This is a reminder. Indeed, for the God-conscious is an excellent final abode.
interpretation: This revelation serves to awaken hearts and guide them toward God-consciousness, promising those who remain mindful of Allah and obey Him a noble and blessed return in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, with their gates opened for them.
interpretation: They will enter everlasting dwellings of complete honor and security, where the gates are opened in welcome and no barrier prevents them from enjoying Allah’s promised blessings.

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise enjoying complete comfort and freely receiving plentiful varieties of food and drink, with no hardship or deprivation.

translation: And with them are those who restrain their gazes, of equal age.
interpretation: This portrays the companions of Paradise as modest, devoted, and harmonious with one another, sharing a state of youthful equality and perfect compatibility.

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: It points to the reward Allah has prepared for the righteous on the Day when every person is held accountable, affirming that His promise of recompense is certain and will be fulfilled.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; it will never run out.
interpretation: This is a declaration that the provision Allah grants in Paradise is everlasting, continuously available, and never diminished or exhausted.

translation: This is so. Indeed, for the transgressors is an evil destination.
interpretation: After the blessings prepared for the righteous, Allah contrasts them with the fate of those who transgress His limits: their final return will be a place of misery, punishment, and ruin rather than honor or security.

translation: They will burn in Hell—what a wretched resting place.
interpretation: This warns that those deserving punishment will face Hell as their abode, an utterly miserable and agonizing place with no comfort or relief.

translation: This is what they shall taste: scalding water and a foul, icy fluid.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment prepared for those who reject the truth: they will be forced to endure both burning liquid and a loathsome, freezing drink, reflecting the severity and humiliation of their recompense.

translation: And other kinds of the same sort, in pairs.
interpretation: This refers to further forms of punishment resembling the preceding ones, diverse and recurring in matching kinds, awaiting those who rejected the truth.

translation: “This is a troop rushing in with you; no welcome for them. Indeed, they will enter the Fire.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the inhabitants of Hell confronting another group being driven into it alongside them. Their words of rejection and hostility reveal that shared punishment does not create fellowship among the wicked; rather, those who followed one another in wrongdoing disown each other when the consequences become manifest.

translation: They will say, “Rather, you are not welcome; you are the ones who brought this upon us. How miserable is this abode!”
interpretation: The people in Hell exchange blame with those who led them astray, each rejecting the other’s claim to honor and welcome. They recognize that the leaders’ misguidance helped prepare this punishment for them, yet the mutual blame cannot remove their shared responsibility or the misery of their final dwelling.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase his punishment twofold in the Fire.”
interpretation: The people of Hell will blame those who led them into misguidance and ask Allah to intensify their punishment, because they regard their leaders and tempters as having compounded their own suffering by causing others to follow them into ruin.

translation: And they will say, “Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Hell realizing that those they had regarded as evil or contemptible are not there, prompting them to question their own judgment and recognize that worldly accusations and standards of righteousness can be completely mistaken before God.

translation: هل اتخذناهم موضعًا للسخرية، أم زاغت عنهم أبصارنا؟
interpretation: هذا استفهام يعبّر عن حيرة أهل النار وندمهم؛ فقد كانوا يستهزئون بالمؤمنين ويحتقرونهم، ثم لم يجدوهم في العذاب، فأدركوا أن سخريتهم لم تكن قائمة على حق، وأن من استهانوا بهم قد يكونون من الناجين.

translation: Indeed, this is the truth: the mutual disputing of the people of Hell.
interpretation: The fierce arguments and mutual accusations among the inhabitants of Hell are a certain reality, not an imagined warning; their conflict reveals their regret and their attempts to shift blame after judgment has been decreed.

translation: Say, “I am only a warner; there is no deity except Allah—the One, the Overpowering.”
interpretation: The Messenger’s role is to warn people of the consequences of rejecting the truth, while affirming that worship belongs exclusively to Allah. He is uniquely One, and His absolute power prevails over all creation, leaving no rival or authority comparable to Him.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving.
interpretation: Allah alone is the sovereign Lord of all existence: His power is irresistible, yet His forgiveness remains open to those who turn to Him in repentance.

translation: Say: “It is a tremendous message.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that what the Qur’an conveys is not an ordinary announcement, but a momentous divine truth whose significance surpasses worldly concerns and demands serious attention.

translation: You are turning away from it.
interpretation: You deliberately disregard the truth and refuse to give it your attention or acceptance.

translation: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: This affirms that the Prophet’s knowledge of the unseen events involving the heavenly assembly came solely through divine revelation, demonstrating that he did not learn them from personal experience or human sources.

translation: It is only revealed to me that I am nothing but a clear warner.
interpretation: The Prophet’s role is to convey God’s warning plainly and unmistakably; guidance and judgment ultimately belong to God, while the Prophet is responsible for delivering the message faithfully.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, “Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay.”
interpretation: This announces that the creation of the human being is a deliberate act of divine wisdom, while his origin from clay reminds him of his humble material beginning and his dependence upon his Creator.

translation: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين
interpretation: When I have formed him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him in prostration.

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together.
interpretation: Every angel obeyed Allah’s command without exception, demonstrating their complete submission to Him and honoring the position He had granted Adam.

translation: Except Iblis; he acted arrogantly and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: Iblis refused to obey Allah’s command because of pride, revealing his rejection of the truth and placing himself among those who disbelieve.

translation: He said, “O Iblīs, what prevented you from prostrating before what I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?”
interpretation: Allah rebukes Iblīs for refusing the commanded prostration of honour to Adam, whom He distinguished by creating him with His two hands. The question exposes that Iblīs’s refusal arose either from arrogance or from falsely considering himself above obedience; in either case, his pride led him to reject Allah’s command. Allah’s mention of His two hands is affirmed as He revealed it, without comparing them to the creation or asking how.

translation: He said, “I am better than him: You created me from fire and created him from clay.”
interpretation: Iblīs objected to God’s command out of arrogant self-regard, judging honor by the material of creation rather than by obedience to God. His claim reveals the error of preferring personal reasoning and worldly criteria over divine instruction, and it became the beginning of his rejection and downfall.

translation: He said, “Then leave it, for you are indeed accursed.”
interpretation: Allah commands Iblis to depart from the divine presence because his arrogance and disobedience have made him rejected and deprived of honor.

translation: And indeed, My curse is upon you until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: Allah declares that Satan is permanently excluded from His mercy and favor until the Day of Judgment, as a consequence of his arrogance and disobedience.

translation: He said, “My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected.”
interpretation: After being condemned for his arrogance and disobedience, Iblīs asks Allah to prolong his life until the Resurrection, seeking time to continue his opposition and mislead humanity.

translation: He said, “Indeed, you are among those granted respite.”
interpretation: Allah granted Satan reprieve until the appointed time, allowing the divine test to unfold while making clear that this delay is limited and does not absolve him of responsibility for his rebellion.

translation: Until the day of the appointed time.
interpretation: This refers to the fixed deadline Allah has decreed for the existence of worldly life, when all beings will be brought to account and the respite granted to Satan will come to an end.

translation: He said, “By Your might, I will surely lead them all astray.”
interpretation: Iblīs swears by Allah’s might that he will relentlessly try to divert all human beings from obedience and truth, revealing his determined hostility toward them; yet his claim expresses an attempt and intention, not power independent of Allah.

translation: except those of Your servants who are sincerely devoted.
interpretation: Satan acknowledges that he cannot lead astray the servants whom Allah has purified through sincere faith and devotion to Him.

translation: He said, “Then the truth is this—and I speak the truth.”
