interpretation: Allah affirms that His decree concerning Iblīs and those who follow him is absolute truth, free from any falsehood, and that whatever He declares is certain and inevitably fulfilled.

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and all those among them who follow you.
interpretation: This is Allah’s decisive declaration to Iblīs that he and every human being who knowingly follows his path of arrogance, disobedience, and misguidance will be gathered in Hell; Satan’s influence does not remove personal responsibility from those who accept his call.

translation: Say, “I ask of you no reward for it, nor am I one of those who feign what they do not possess.”
interpretation: The Messenger affirms that he conveys the revelation solely as a sincere duty, seeking no worldly compensation and neither inventing its message nor imposing upon himself a role beyond what God has entrusted to him.

translation: It is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is presented as a universal reminder, calling every people and every generation to remember the truth about God, their purpose, and their accountability, rather than being guidance intended for one nation alone.

translation: And you will surely come to know its truth after some time.
interpretation: The reality and truth of this revelation will become unmistakably clear when its promised consequences unfold, even to those who presently deny it.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This Book comes from Allah alone, whose absolute power guarantees its authority and whose perfect wisdom is reflected in its guidance and judgment.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth; so worship Allah, devoting the religion sincerely to Him.
interpretation: Since the Qur’an is a true revelation from Allah, worship must be directed to Him alone, with one’s faith and intentions purified from every form of shirk, ostentation, or devotion to anything besides Him.

translation: Surely, sincere devotion belongs to Allah alone. As for those who take protectors besides Him, they say, “We worship them only so that they may bring us nearer to Allah.” Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning what they differ over. Surely, Allah does not guide one who is a persistent liar and ungrateful disbeliever.
interpretation: The verse establishes that worship and religious devotion must be directed purely to Allah, without intermediaries being invoked or worshipped as a means of approaching Him. The claim that such beings merely bring people nearer to Allah does not justify associating them with Him; rather, it is condemned as a false belief and a rejection of Allah’s exclusive right to worship. The final judgment belongs to Allah, who exposes the falsehood of those who knowingly persist in this claim.

translation: Had Allah intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the All-Subduing.
interpretation: The verse decisively rejects attributing offspring to Allah: even on the impossible supposition that He wished to do so, He would choose whatever He pleased from His creation. In reality, His absolute transcendence, oneness, and sovereign power make such an attribution incompatible with His nature; He alone possesses irresistible authority over all things.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and purpose. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He subjected the sun and the moon; each runs for an appointed term. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Most Forgiving.
interpretation: The ordered alternation of night and day and the precise movement of the sun and moon reveal that creation is governed by divine wisdom rather than chance. The One who commands this vast order possesses absolute power, yet He combines that might with forgiveness for those who turn to Him.

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate. And He provided for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three layers of darkness. That is Allah, your Lord; sovereignty belongs to Him. There is no god except Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: Allah points to the unity of humanity’s origin, the ordered stages of human development, and the provision of livestock as signs of His absolute power, wisdom, and lordship. The “three darknesses” refer to the enveloping layers surrounding the developing child, emphasizing its complete dependence on Allah’s care. Since He alone creates, sustains, and governs all things, worship belongs exclusively to Him; turning toward any other object of devotion is therefore a departure from evident truth.

translation: If you disbelieve, surely Allah is independent of you; He does not approve disbelief for His servants. But if you are grateful, He approves it for you. No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Surely, He knows what is within the hearts.
interpretation: Allah has no need of human faith or worship; disbelief does not diminish His sovereignty, nor does obedience increase it. Yet He calls people to gratitude because it is the response He approves and the path that benefits them. Each person will be judged individually, without being held accountable for another’s wrongdoing, and upon returning to Allah, even the deeds and intentions hidden within the heart will be fully known and brought to account.

translation: And when affliction touches a person, he calls upon his Lord, turning sincerely to Him. Then, when He grants him a blessing from Himself, he forgets what he had prayed for before and assigns equals to Allah, seeking to lead others away from His path. Say, “Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; surely you are among the inhabitants of the Fire.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of one who turns humbly to Allah in hardship but, after receiving relief, forgets his dependence on Him and directs devotion to other supposed powers. Such temporary prosperity is not approval of disbelief; it is a brief opportunity before the consequences of rejecting Allah and misleading others become manifest.

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient, worshipping during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, like one who does not? Say, “Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” Only people of understanding take heed.
interpretation: The verse portrays sincere worship as a life shaped by humility, vigilance, and hope: the believer turns to God in the solitude of night, conscious of accountability yet confident in divine mercy. It then contrasts the insight of those who possess beneficial knowledge—knowledge that leads to obedience and awareness of God—with the heedlessness of those who lack it. True understanding is shown not merely by information, but by recognizing the difference between these states and allowing that recognition to reform one’s life.

translation: Say, “O My servants who believe, be mindful of your Lord. For those who do good in this world is goodness. And Allah’s earth is vast. Indeed, those who endure patiently will be given their reward without measure.”
interpretation: Allah calls believers to protect themselves from disobedience through reverence and obedience to Him, assuring them that righteous conduct brings goodness and that they need not remain in circumstances that prevent them from living faithfully, since His earth is spacious. Their steadfastness through hardship, obedience, and sacrifice is honored with a reward beyond human calculation.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, devoting the religion sincerely to Him.”
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet—and all believers through him—to make worship exclusively for Allah, free from showing off, associating partners with Him, or seeking any rival purpose. True devotion is measured by sincerity of intention and complete submission to Allah alone.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the foremost of those who submit to God.
interpretation: This expresses the command for the speaker to lead by complete submission to God—accepting His guidance, obeying Him sincerely, and exemplifying devotion before all others.

translation: Say, “Indeed, I fear that if I disobey my Lord, I will suffer the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that even the Messenger ﷺ expresses profound fear of divine punishment, affirming that no one is exempt from accountability before Allah. This fear is meant to restrain disobedience and cultivate sincere submission to Him.

translation: Say: “It is Allah alone that I worship, devoting my religion sincerely to Him.”
interpretation: This is a declaration that worship must be directed exclusively to Allah, with sincere devotion free from associating partners with Him or seeking the approval of others.

translation: So worship whatever you will besides Him. Say, “Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.” Surely, that is the clear loss.
interpretation: The command to worship whatever one wishes is not permission, but a warning expressed as a challenge: whoever turns away from Allah chooses the path of ruin. The true loss is not merely losing worldly possessions, but forfeiting one’s own soul and being separated from those who would have shared in faith and salvation on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: They will have canopies of fire above them and canopies beneath them. That is how Allah warns His servants: “O My servants, be mindful of Me.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment surrounding those who reject Allah from every direction, leaving them no refuge. This fearful image is intended as a merciful warning, calling people to protect themselves from such an end through reverence, obedience, and avoidance of disobedience to Allah.

translation: And those who shun false gods, refusing to worship them, and turn in repentance to Allah—for them is good news. So give good tidings to My servants—
interpretation: Those who consciously reject every form of false worship and return sincerely to Allah with repentance and obedience are promised divine favor and glad tidings. Their turning away from falsehood is not merely avoidance; it is an active return to Allah, grounded in sincere faith and submission.

translation: Those who listen attentively to what is said and follow the best of it—those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding.
interpretation: True guidance is shown by a receptive and discerning mind: believers listen carefully, distinguish what is most sound and righteous, and then act upon it. Their willingness to follow the best reflects both divine guidance and mature understanding.

translation: Is one against whom the word of punishment has been decreed [like the guided]? Can you save one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who persist in rejecting the truth until divine judgment becomes due cannot be rescued by anyone, even by the Messenger; guidance and deliverance belong to Allah alone, while the one who knowingly refuses faith bears the consequence of that choice.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have lofty chambers, with chambers built above them, beneath which rivers flow. This is the promise of Allah; Allah never breaks His promise.
interpretation: The verse portrays the honored reward prepared for those who remain conscious of Allah and live in obedience to Him: a secure, elevated dwelling in Paradise, marked by beauty, abundance, and lasting dignity. It reassures the believers that this reward is a certain divine promise, because Allah’s promises can never fail.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, then causes it to flow as springs through the earth? Then He brings forth with it crops of varying colors; thereafter they wither, and you see them turn yellow; then He reduces them to debris. Surely in this is a reminder for those who possess understanding.
interpretation: Allah directs attention to the cycle of rain, growth, maturity, withering, and decay as a sign of His power and wisdom. Just as the earth is revived and vegetation later returns to dust, worldly life is temporary and constantly changing; those who reflect deeply recognize that lasting life and ultimate return belong to Allah.

translation: فهل من وسّع الله صدره لقبول الإسلام، فهو على نور من ربه؟ فهلاكٌ وقسوةٌ لمن جمدت قلوبهم عن ذكر الله؛ أولئك في ضلال بيّن.
interpretation: المعنى أن الهداية ليست مجرد معرفةٍ ظاهرة، بل انشراحٌ في القلب لقبول الحق والعمل به، فيعيش صاحبه مستنيرًا ببصيرة من الله. أما من قسا قلبه حتى لا يتأثر بذكر الله ولا يخضع له، فقد حُرم هذا النور وانحرف عن الطريق الواضح، ولذلك استحق الوعيد.

translation: Allah has sent down the finest discourse: a Book whose verses resemble one another and are repeated in pairs. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it; then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is Allah’s guidance; He guides by it whoever He wills. And whoever Allah leaves astray, no guide can lead.
interpretation: The verse portrays genuine receptivity to the Qur’an as a movement from awe to tenderness: awareness of Allah’s majesty first causes fear and trembling, then transforms the heart into humility, comfort, and loving remembrance. This change is itself a gift of divine guidance, not merely the result of human effort, and those who reject that guidance cannot find a true direction elsewhere.

translation: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة، وقيل للظالمين: ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون؟
interpretation: ليس من يلقى العذاب يوم القيامة مضطرًّا إلى أن يقي وجهه منه كمن نجا منه؛ ففي ذلك تصوير لشدة العذاب وإذلال الظالمين، إذ يُقال لهم إن ما يذوقونه هو جزاء أعمالهم التي اكتسبوها في الدنيا.

translation: Those before them denied the truth, so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This warns that rejecting God’s guidance does not avert accountability; punishment may arrive unexpectedly, when those who persist in denial feel secure and are unaware of its approach.

translation: So Allah made them taste humiliation in the life of this world; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: Worldly disgrace is only a limited foretaste of the far greater punishment awaiting those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth; true awareness of the Hereafter would lead them to repent and reform.

translation: Indeed, We have set forth for people in this Qur’an every kind of example, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: Allah presents varied examples in the Qur’an to make truth understandable and awaken people from heedlessness, enabling them to reflect, remember their responsibility, and return to guidance.

translation: An Arabic Qur’an, free of any crookedness, so that they may become mindful of God.
interpretation: Its clear and harmonious Arabic guidance contains no contradiction or deviation; it is given so that people may understand the truth, avoid wrongdoing, and live with reverent awareness of God.

translation: Allah sets forth the example of a man owned by several quarrelling partners, and a man wholly devoted to one master. Are the two alike in comparison? All praise belongs to Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This illustrates that associating others with Allah leaves a person divided among competing claims and loyalties, whereas worshipping Allah alone brings clarity, unity, and freedom from servitude to false powers. The two conditions cannot be equal, though many fail to recognize this truth.

translation: Indeed, you will die, and they too will die.
interpretation: This verse affirms that death is an unavoidable destiny for every human being, including the Prophet and those who oppose or reject him. It reminds people that worldly power, disputes, and differences cannot exempt anyone from returning to God for judgment.

translation: Then, indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all disagreements and claims concealed in this life will be brought before God, whose perfect judgment will distinguish truth from falsehood and give each person their due.

translation: Who, then, is more unjust than one who fabricates lies against Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?
interpretation: No one is more grievously wrong than the person who attributes falsehood to Allah—by inventing beliefs or commands in His name—and then rejects the truth when it is plainly presented to him. The concluding question is a stern warning that persistent disbelief and deliberate distortion lead to the punishment of Hell.

translation: And the one who brought the truth and those who affirmed it—those are the mindful of God.
interpretation: The verse praises the Messenger who conveyed the truth from God and the believers who sincerely accepted and lived by it. Their truthful response to revelation is the mark of genuine God-consciousness.

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: Those who sincerely worship God and live righteously will receive from Him complete and lasting fulfillment in the Hereafter, beyond anything they could attain through their own efforts.

translation: So that Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This expresses Allah’s mercy toward those who turn to Him: He removes the consequences of their gravest sins and rewards their righteous deeds by the highest standard of goodness, rather than treating them merely according to their shortcomings.

translation: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those besides Him. Whoever Allah allows to stray will have no guide.
interpretation: The verse reassures the believer that Allah alone is fully sufficient for protection and support, so threats invoking false gods or other powers cannot ultimately harm one who relies on Him. True guidance belongs to Allah; whoever turns away from it and is left to his misguidance will find no one able to lead him back.

translation: And whoever Allah guides, none can mislead; is Allah not Almighty, the Possessor of retribution?
interpretation: Whoever sincerely follows the guidance Allah grants cannot be ultimately led astray by any force. The verse affirms that Allah’s power is absolute: He protects the guided and is fully capable of requiting those who knowingly oppose His truth.

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, “Allah.” Say, “Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?” Say, “Allah is sufficient for me; upon Him the reliant place their trust.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of acknowledging Allah as the Creator while turning to powerless beings for protection, benefit, or relief. Since no created thing can avert a harm or prevent a mercy decreed by Allah, true reliance must be directed to Him alone; trusting Allah as sufficient frees the believer from dependence on intermediaries that possess no independent power.

translation: Say, “O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. Soon you will know.”
interpretation: The verse is a firm declaration that each side may continue upon its chosen path, while leaving the final judgment to God. It encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in obedience and warns those opposing him that the truth of their choices will become evident through the consequences that follow.

translation: You will come to know upon whom a punishment will come that humiliates him, and upon whom an everlasting punishment will descend.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing will ultimately be exposed and disgraced, suffering a punishment that is not temporary but lasting.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own good; and whoever goes astray, only goes astray to his own detriment. You are not appointed as their guardian.
interpretation: The Qur’an has been revealed as the truthful guidance by which people are to live, but their response to it remains their own responsibility: guidance benefits the one who accepts it, while rejection harms only the rejecter. The Messenger’s duty is to convey the revelation clearly, not to control people’s choices or bear responsibility for their refusal.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until an appointed term. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: The verse teaches that life, death, and even the temporary state of sleep are entirely under Allah’s authority. Sleep resembles a temporary withdrawal of the soul, while death is its permanent separation until resurrection; the return of the soul upon waking is therefore a daily reminder of Allah’s power and of humanity’s dependence on Him.

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, “Even if they possess nothing and understand nothing?”
interpretation: The verse rejects relying on beings other than Allah for intercession, since they have neither independent power nor understanding; true intercession belongs only to Allah and occurs by His permission.

translation: Say: “All intercession belongs to Allah. To Him belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and to Him you will all be returned.”
interpretation: No one can intercede independently of Allah or compel Him to accept intercession; it exists only by His authority and permission, because all sovereignty belongs to Him and every person will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil with aversion; but when those besides Him are mentioned, they suddenly rejoice.
interpretation: Those who deny the Hereafter are unsettled by the call to worship Allah alone, because it challenges their desires and exposes their accountability before Him. Yet they readily welcome the mention of other objects of devotion, revealing their attachment to false beliefs and their resistance to sincere monotheism.

translation: Say, “O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.”
interpretation: This is a prayer entrusting all disputes to Allah, whose perfect knowledge encompasses both what is hidden and what is manifest. Since He alone knows the truth behind every claim and intention, His judgment between people is absolute and just, and human beings should submit to His decision rather than rely on limited perception or personal desire.

translation: If those who did wrong possessed everything on earth, and twice as much besides, they would offer it as ransom to escape the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they never expected.
interpretation: The verse portrays the utter helplessness of those who rejected truth and persisted in wrongdoing when judgment arrives: even if they owned all worldly wealth and more, they would willingly surrender it to be spared, but no material compensation could rescue them. Allah will then confront them with the full consequences of their deeds—realities and punishment they had dismissed or never imagined.

translation: And the evil consequences of what they had earned will become manifest to them, and what they used to mock will encompass them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the reality of their deeds will become undeniable: the sins and wrongdoing they had pursued will appear in their true destructive form, and the punishment they had ridiculed will overtake them completely, leaving them unable to escape or deny it.

translation: When hardship touches a person, he calls upon Us; then, when We grant him a blessing from Us, he says, “I was given it only because of my knowledge.” Rather, it is a test, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse exposes the human tendency to turn to God in distress but to attribute prosperity to personal ability once relief comes. Knowledge, skill, and effort may be means, yet they do not make a person independent of God or entitle him to blessings. Wealth and success are a test of gratitude, humility, and responsible conduct, though many fail to recognize this and become deceived by their own accomplishments.

translation: Those before them said the same, but what they used to earn did not benefit them.
interpretation: Their wealth, power, and worldly achievements could not protect them from God’s punishment; reliance on such gains is therefore futile when faith and obedience are absent.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they had earned befell them. And those among these who committed wrongdoing will also be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: Those who persist in injustice should not assume that they are exempt from divine accountability. The harmful consequences of their choices will reach them, and no power or strategy can place them beyond God’s judgment.

translation: أولم يعلموا أن الله يوسّع الرزق لمن يشاء ويضيّقه على من يشاء؟ إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون.
interpretation: ينبغي للمؤمن أن يدرك أن سعة الرزق وضِيقه يجريان بحكمة الله ومشيئته، فلا يجعل وفرة المال دليلًا على الكرامة ولا قلّته دليلًا على الهوان، بل يطمئن إلى تدبير الله ويشكره في السعة ويصبر في الضيق.

translation: Say, “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Truly, He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse calls those who have committed even grave wrongs not to let guilt become despair. Allah’s mercy remains open to them when they sincerely turn back to Him, abandoning sin, seeking His forgiveness, and striving to repair the harm they have caused. It teaches that no sin is beyond Allah’s forgiveness for the one who returns to Him before death, while reliance on His mercy must be joined with genuine repentance rather than persistence in wrongdoing.

translation: Turn in repentance to your Lord and submit yourselves to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: في الآية دعوة إلى المبادرة بالتوبة الصادقة والرجوع إلى الله بالطاعة والخضوع قبل حلول العذاب؛ لأن تأخير التوبة إلى وقت نزول العقوبة يفوّت على الإنسان فرصة النجاة، وحينها لا يجد من يدفع عنه ما نزل به.

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: This is a warning to hasten toward sincere obedience to God and to put His revelation into practice, rather than delay or remain heedless, for the opportunity to repent and reform may end unexpectedly before a person realizes it.

translation: Lest any soul should say, “Alas, my regret for what I neglected concerning Allah, while I was surely among those who mocked.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the remorse of a person who, after the opportunity for repentance and obedience has passed, realizes that neglecting Allah’s commands and ridiculing faith brought about their ruin. It warns that excuses and regret on the Day of Judgment cannot replace sincere devotion and repentance in this life.

translation: Or lest it should say, “If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the God-conscious.”
interpretation: This is the regretful plea of a person who rejected the truth and, on the Day of Judgment, wishes to escape responsibility by attributing his misguidance to a lack of divine guidance. The verse indicates that such an excuse will not avail him, because guidance had been conveyed and his failure arose from turning away from it.

translation: Or lest it should say, when it sees the punishment, “If only I could have another chance, then I would be among those who do good.”
interpretation: This portrays the remorse of one who neglected faith and righteous action until witnessing the Hereafter, when regret can no longer lead to a second opportunity or change the outcome.

translation: Yes indeed, My signs came to you, but you denied them, acted arrogantly, and were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to the person who will offer excuses on the Day of Judgment: the truth and divine guidance had already reached him, but he consciously rejected them, refused to submit out of arrogance, and thereby joined those who disbelieved.

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who fabricated lies against Allah with their faces darkened. Is Hell not a dwelling for the arrogant?
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who knowingly attributed falsehood to Allah will be exposed in disgrace, and their darkened faces will manifest the humiliation and anguish brought upon them by their arrogance. Their rejection of truth and presumption in speaking about Allah without right lead them to the fitting abode of Hell.

translation: وسيُنجي الله الذين اتقوا بفوزهم ونجاتهم؛ لا يمسّهم سوء ولا هم يحزنون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن التقوى، وهي خشيته وطاعته واجتناب معصيته، سبب النجاة يوم القيامة؛ فيفوز أهلها برحمة الله وحمايته، فلا يصيبهم عذاب ولا يلحقهم حزن على ما خلّفوا أو فاتهم.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.
interpretation: Everything that exists is brought into being and sustained by Allah, so ultimate authority and reliance belong to Him alone; nothing lies beyond His knowledge, power, or care.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah—it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses complete authority over the heavens and the earth and controls all that occurs within them. Therefore, rejecting His signs means turning away from the One who holds all power and provision, leading ultimately to the loss of faith, guidance, and true success.

translation: قل: أفغيرَ الله تأمرونني أن أعبد، أيها الجاهلون؟
interpretation: في الآية إنكارٌ شديد على من يدعو إلى عبادة غير الله، وبيانٌ أن صرف العبادة لغيره جهلٌ بحقيقة التوحيد ومقام الله تعالى.

translation: And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: “If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely become worthless, and you will certainly be among the losers.”
interpretation: This is a grave warning that associating any partner with Allah destroys the spiritual value of one’s deeds and leads to ultimate loss. Though addressed to the Prophet ﷺ and earlier messengers as a hypothetical warning, it teaches their communities that sincere, exclusive worship of Allah is the foundation upon which every righteous deed depends.

translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: Turn away from every form of associating partners with Allah and devote worship exclusively to Him, expressing gratitude for His guidance and blessings through sincere obedience.

translation: They have not appreciated Allah with the appreciation due to Him. The whole earth will be within His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who diminish Allah’s majesty by associating partners with Him. It portrays the earth and heavens as entirely subject to His absolute power and command, affirming His transcendence and incomparable greatness without likening Him to creation or implying human-like physical attributes.

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious—or die—except those whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse portrays the decisive transition from the present creation to the Resurrection: by Allah’s command, the first blast brings the created order to an end, with only those He wills exempted; the second blast restores the dead, who rise immediately and await the judgment that Allah has appointed.

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the Record will be set down, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forth, and judgment will be passed between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as the unveiling of ultimate reality: divine light and justice will encompass creation, deeds will be openly recorded, the prophets and witnesses will testify, and God will judge every person with perfect fairness, leaving no one deprived of what is rightfully due.

translation: And every soul will be fully repaid for what it did, and He knows best what they do.
interpretation: Every person will receive the complete and exact consequence of their deeds, with nothing overlooked or treated unjustly, for Allah has perfect knowledge of all that people do, including their outward actions and inner intentions.

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups. When they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, “Did messengers not come to you from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day?” They will say, “Yes indeed, but the decree of punishment became due against the disbelievers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the disbelievers’ arrival in Hell as an orderly, collective procession, emphasizing that their punishment is not arbitrary. The guardians’ question makes clear that they had received clear warnings through messengers from their own people, who conveyed God’s signs and warned them of the Hereafter. Their admission—“Yes”—removes any claim of ignorance or lack of guidance; they recognize that the punishment came after persistent rejection, until the consequence decreed for those who deny the truth became deserved.

translation: It will be said, “Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant!”
interpretation: This is a declaration of the final humiliation and lasting punishment of those who rejected truth out of arrogance, choosing pride over submission to God; their end is a fittingly miserable dwelling.

translation: And those who were mindful of their Lord will be ushered into Paradise in groups. When they reach it and its gates are opened, its keepers will say to them, “Peace be upon you; you have become pure and good, so enter it, remaining forever.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the honored reception of the righteous: they enter Paradise collectively, welcomed by angels with peace and recognition of their purified faith and conduct. Their entry is not temporary but an eternal reward for their reverence and obedience to their Lord.

translation: And they will say, “Praise belongs to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, settling in Paradise wherever we wish.” How excellent is the reward of those who strive in righteousness!
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise recognizing that their salvation and everlasting dwelling are the fulfillment of Allah’s promise, not merely the result of their own deeds. Their gratitude affirms Allah’s faithfulness, while their freedom to dwell wherever they wish expresses the abundance and honor of the reward granted to those who lived righteously.

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise. Judgment will be passed among them in truth, and it will be said, “Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a scene of perfect majesty and justice: the angels encircle the Divine Throne in continual praise, while every matter is settled with absolute truth and fairness. The final proclamation of praise to Allah affirms that all judgment, order, and outcome belong to Him, whose lordship encompasses every world.

translation: Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters; their precise meaning is known to God, and they draw attention to the revelation’s extraordinary nature despite being composed of the familiar letters of human speech.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah—the Mighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The Qur’an is sent down by Allah, whose absolute power ensures its authority and whose perfect knowledge makes its guidance true, precise, and free from error.

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Possessor of abundant bounty. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This portrays Allah’s perfect balance of mercy and justice: He welcomes sincere repentance and grants His abundant grace, yet warns those who persist arrogantly in wrongdoing of His punishment. Since He alone possesses divinity and ultimate authority, every person will return to Him for judgment.

translation: No one disputes the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the lands deceive you.
interpretation: Those who reject faith may argue against Allah’s clear signs and appear to prosper, travel freely, and enjoy influence in the world; yet this outward success is not proof of truth or divine approval, so believers should not be misled by it.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied the truth, as did the factions after them. Every nation plotted against its messenger, intending to seize him, and they argued with falsehood in order to refute the truth by it. So I seized them; and how terrible was My punishment!
interpretation: Those who reject divine guidance often repeat the same pattern: they unite against the messenger sent to them, use deceptive arguments to make falsehood appear victorious, and seek to silence the truth rather than follow it. Yet their power and schemes cannot protect them from God’s judgment, as the fate of earlier nations demonstrates.

translation: And thus the decree of your Lord was fulfilled against those who disbelieved: they are the inhabitants of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse signifies that persistent rejection of truth leads, by God’s just and certain judgment, to the consequence decreed for the disbelievers: abiding in the Fire.

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, believe in Him, and seek forgiveness for those who believe: “Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your path, and protect them from the punishment of Hell.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the angels nearest to God as servants whose worship is joined with compassion for believers. Their prayer teaches that sincere repentance and commitment to God’s way are means of receiving His vast mercy, and that salvation ultimately depends on being forgiven and safeguarded from the consequences of sin.

translation: Our Lord, admit them into the Gardens of everlasting residence which You have promised them, along with whoever among their fathers, spouses, and descendants was righteous. Indeed, You alone are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This supplication asks Allah to honor the believers with eternal Paradise and to reunite them there with their righteous family members. It reflects the mercy of Allah in joining faithful families together, while affirming that His granting of this blessing is governed by absolute power and perfect wisdom.

translation: And protect them from evil deeds; whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have surely shown mercy. And that is the great triumph.
interpretation: This is a prayer that Allah shield the believers from the sins and harmful consequences that bring punishment on the Day of Judgment. Being spared from them is itself a sign of Allah’s mercy, and the greatest success is to receive that mercy and attain salvation.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: “Allah’s abhorrence of you was greater than your abhorrence of yourselves when you were invited to faith, yet you disbelieved.”
interpretation: This describes the unbelievers’ remorse in the Hereafter: they will despise themselves for their ruin, but they will be told that Allah’s rejection and displeasure toward them was even greater because they knowingly turned away when faith was offered to them.

translation: They will say, “Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. We confess our sins; is there any way out?”
interpretation: They acknowledge on the Day of Judgment that they passed through two deaths—the state of nonexistence before worldly life and death at the end of it—and two lives—the life of this world and the resurrection life. Their confession comes only after witnessing the truth, so it cannot benefit them; they ask to return, but the opportunity for repentance and righteous action has already ended.

translation: That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of those who reject pure monotheism while accepting false gods: their faith is not based on truth, but on preference for associating partners with Allah. It declares that ultimate authority and judgment belong solely to Allah, whose absolute supremacy cannot be challenged.

translation: He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. Yet none takes heed except one who turns to Him.
interpretation: Allah continually presents clear evidence of His power and mercy through His signs and through the provision brought down from the sky. True reflection on these blessings awakens the heart to return humbly and sincerely to Him.

translation: So call upon Allah, devoting your worship sincerely to Him, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: True devotion requires directing worship and supplication exclusively to Allah, without compromising this sincerity because of the opposition or displeasure of those who reject faith.

translation: Exalter of ranks, Owner of the Throne, He sends the Spirit by His command upon whomsoever He wills of His servants, so that he may warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute majesty and authority, and He raises His servants in rank according to His wisdom. He conveys revelation through the Spirit—by His command and to whomever He chooses—so that His messengers may awaken people to the certainty of the Day when all creation will stand before Him and meet their judgment.

translation: The Day when they will all come forth; nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. “To whom belongs sovereignty today?” “To Allah, the One, the Overpowering.”
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, every person will stand fully exposed before Allah, with no deed, intention, or secret concealed from Him. All worldly claims to power and ownership will disappear, revealing that absolute authority has always belonged solely to Allah, whose oneness and irresistible dominion leave no power able to oppose Him.

translation: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There will be no injustice today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Day of Judgment as a time when every person receives the exact consequence of their deeds, with no one’s rights diminished or anyone punished without cause. God’s swift reckoning signifies that His perfect knowledge and justice require no delay or difficulty in judging His creation.

translation: And warn them of the approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with anguish. The wrongdoers will have no devoted friend and no intercessor whose plea will be heeded.
interpretation: The verse warns that the Day of Judgment will bring overwhelming fear and distress, leaving those who persisted in wrongdoing without any trusted ally or effective intercession. On that Day, neither worldly relationships nor appeals for help will avail them; only sincere faith and righteous deeds can benefit a person.

translation: He knows the furtive betrayal of the eyes and what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: Nothing escapes Allah’s knowledge: He is aware even of the secret glance that a person tries to hide and of the intentions and thoughts concealed within the heart.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him cannot judge anything. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute authority to judge and decide with perfect justice, whereas the beings invoked besides Him have no power to govern or render judgment. His judgment is flawless because He hears every word and sees every action, whether apparent or hidden.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how the end of those before them was? They were stronger than them and left greater آثار upon the land, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the ruins and history of past nations: despite their greater power, achievements, and lasting traces, they could not escape divine judgment when they persisted in wrongdoing. Material strength and worldly accomplishments cannot protect anyone from Allah’s justice; only turning to Him and abandoning sin can avert such an end.

translation: That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved; so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong and severe in punishment.
interpretation: Their destruction was not arbitrary: they knowingly rejected the clear evidence brought by Allah’s messengers. Thus, when punishment overtook them, it demonstrated that no people can evade divine judgment through denial, for Allah possesses absolute power and deals decisively with persistent rejection of the truth.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
interpretation: God sent Moses supported by evident miracles and decisive proof, so that his people would recognize the truth of his message and have no valid excuse for rejecting it.

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah; but they said, “He is a magician and a liar.”
interpretation: The messengers were sent to the leading figures of tyranny and wealth, yet these rulers rejected the truth by dismissing its bearer as merely a magician and a liar. Their accusation reflects denial and arrogance rather than a sincere examination of the message.

translation: When he brought them the truth from Us, they said, “Kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women.” Yet the schemes of the disbelievers are nothing but futile error.
interpretation: This portrays how tyrannical people respond to undeniable truth with persecution, seeking to weaken believers by murdering their sons and humiliating or controlling their women. Their plot may cause suffering temporarily, but it cannot defeat the truth or escape God’s judgment; ultimately, their schemes are misguided and destined to fail.

translation: وقال فرعون: دعوني أقتل موسى، وليدعُ ربَّه؛ إنني أخاف أن يغيّر دينكم أو أن يُظهر في الأرض الفساد.
interpretation: يكشف قول فرعون عن استبداده وخوفه من دعوة موسى؛ فهو يتذرّع بحماية دين قومه ونظامهم ليبرّر قتله، مع أن مقصوده الحقيقي إسكات الحق ومنع الناس من اتباعه، ويصوّر دعوة الإصلاح فسادًا حفاظًا على سلطانه.

translation: And Moses said, “Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.”
interpretation: Moses declares that his protection lies with Allah against those whose arrogance makes them reject truth and deny accountability before Him; this shows that tyranny is ultimately rooted in pride and disbelief in the Hereafter.

translation: And a believing man from Pharaoh’s family, who concealed his faith, said, “Will you kill a man merely because he says, ‘My Lord is Allah,’ while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is lying, then the burden of his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he warns you of will surely befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is excessive and persistently deceitful.”
interpretation: The believer from Pharaoh’s household appeals to reason and justice: Moses should not be persecuted when he has presented clear evidence. Even if his opponents doubt him, killing him is unjustified—his falsehood, if any, would harm only him, whereas rejecting a truthful messenger could bring divine punishment. The verse also shows that sincere counsel may require courage and wisdom, while arrogance and persistent lying prevent a person from being guided to the truth.

translation: “O my people, you possess the kingdom today, dominant in the land; but who will protect us from Allah’s punishment if it comes upon us?” Pharaoh said, “I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the way of sound judgment.”
interpretation: The believer from Pharaoh’s household warns that worldly power cannot shield a people from divine justice, but Pharaoh answers by disguising his personal opinion as wise guidance. The verse exposes how tyrannical authority dismisses sincere warning and presents self-interest and control as the only rational path.

translation: And the believing man said, “O my people, indeed I fear for you a fate like that of the Day of the Confederates.”
interpretation: The believer warns his people that their rejection of truth may bring upon them the same devastating consequences suffered by earlier nations that united against their messengers and persisted in defiance. His concern reflects sincere counsel: power, solidarity, and worldly confidence cannot protect a people from divine judgment when they oppose God’s guidance.

translation: Like the fate and way of the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those who came after them. And Allah does not intend ظلم for His servants.
interpretation: This is a warning that rejecting truth and persisting in oppression follows the pattern of earlier nations who were destroyed; their punishment was not injustice from Allah, but the just consequence of their own wrongdoing.

translation: And, O my people, I fear for you the Day of Mutual Calling.
interpretation: The speaker warns his people that the Day of Resurrection will be a day of overwhelming fear, when people call out to one another amid confusion and distress, and every person faces the consequences of their deeds before God.

translation: On the Day you will turn away in flight, you will have no one to protect you from Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: The verse warns that when the Day of Judgment comes, fleeing will offer no escape from Allah’s reckoning, nor will anyone be able to provide protection from it. Whoever persists in rejecting guidance and is consequently left astray will find no one capable of leading him to the truth.

translation: “Indeed, Joseph came to you before with clear proofs, yet you continued to doubt what he brought you. Then, when he died, you said, ‘Allah will never send a messenger after him.’ Thus Allah leaves astray those who transgress and doubt.”
interpretation: The verse condemns a persistent refusal to accept truth: even when clear evidence is presented, people may cling to doubt, and after the messenger’s death they may use his absence as an excuse to deny any future guidance. Such deliberate excess and continual suspicion lead a person further away from the truth.

translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them—it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: The verse condemns arguing against Allah’s clear signs without knowledge or valid proof, driven instead by pride and obstinacy. Such arrogance is detestable to Allah and to believers, and persistent rejection causes the heart to become sealed, leaving the tyrant increasingly unable to recognize or accept the truth.

translation: Pharaoh said, “O Haman, build for me a lofty tower, so that I may reach the ways.”
interpretation: Pharaoh’s command reveals his arrogance and his attempt to dismiss the truth brought by Moses by demanding a grand, seemingly rational means to investigate the unseen, while actually seeking to mislead his people and reinforce his claim to power.

translation: “The means of access to the heavens, so that I may look upon the God of Moses—though I truly think him a liar.” Thus Pharaoh’s evil deed was made appealing to him, and he was turned away from the path. Pharaoh’s scheme was doomed only to destruction.
interpretation: Pharaoh’s demand to reach the heavens was not a sincere search for truth but an arrogant attempt to ridicule Moses and deny God. His pride made his corruption appear justified to him, while it blinded him to the truth; consequently, all his plotting could lead only to ruin.

translation: And the one who believed said, “O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right guidance.”
interpretation: The believing man calls his people to abandon Pharaoh’s misleading commands and follow the truth revealed by God, for genuine guidance lies in faith, obedience, and the way that leads to salvation.

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, while the Hereafter is truly the abode of permanence.
interpretation: The verse calls people to recognize that worldly life, despite its pleasures and attractions, is brief and passing, whereas the Hereafter is lasting and everlasting. Therefore, a person should not make temporary worldly gains the ultimate purpose of life, but should prepare for the enduring life by faith and righteous deeds.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will be recompensed only with its like; but whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—such will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without account.
interpretation: The verse establishes God’s perfect justice: wrongdoing is repaid only in proportion to itself, never with added injustice. In contrast, righteous action joined with sincere faith earns a reward beyond measure, showing that God’s grace greatly exceeds the strict measure of human deeds and that both men and women are equally honored in His judgment.

translation: “O my people, why do I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?”
interpretation: The believing man reproaches his people for their contradiction: he invites them to faith in Allah and obedience to Him, which lead to salvation, while they urge him toward disbelief and rejection of the truth, whose end is punishment. The verse exposes the painful inversion whereby sincere guidance is treated as danger and destructive error as safety.

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I invite you to the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving.
interpretation: يبيّن القائل بطلان دعوتهم إلى عبادة ما لا دليل على ألوهيته، ويدعوهم بدل ذلك إلى توحيد الله القوي الغالب، الذي مع كمال قدرته يفتح باب المغفرة لمن تاب ورجع إليه.

translation: There is no doubt that what you call me to has no power to be invoked in this world or the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: The speaker rejects the false gods being promoted to him, declaring that they possess neither real authority nor the ability to answer prayer in either life. He affirms that all people will ultimately return to Allah for judgment, and warns that those who exceed the limits of truth and obedience will be condemned to Hell.

translation: "You will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah sees His servants."
interpretation: The speaker remains sincere and composed despite being opposed: he entrusts his fate to Allah, confident that Allah fully perceives the circumstances, intentions, and deeds of His servants, and that the truth of his counsel will ultimately become clear.

translation: So Allah protected him from the evil consequences of what they plotted, and Pharaoh’s people were encompassed by the evil punishment.
interpretation: Allah saved the believing man from the harm of Pharaoh’s scheme, while the very people who pursued injustice were overtaken by punishment as the consequence of their rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: The Fire—they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour is established, it will be said: “Admit the people of Pharaoh to the severest punishment.”
interpretation: This verse indicates that the people of Pharaoh are subjected to punishment before the Resurrection, as shown by their being exposed to the Fire morning and evening; when the Day of Judgment arrives, they will enter an even more severe and everlasting punishment. Their fate is presented as a consequence of their persistent disbelief, tyranny, and rejection of the truth.

translation: And when they argue with one another in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, “We were your followers; can you then spare us a share of the Fire?”
interpretation: The verse portrays the regret of those who blindly followed powerful and arrogant people, imagining that their influence would protect them. In the Hereafter, the followers discover that neither their dependence nor their leaders can lessen their punishment; each person remains accountable for choosing whom to follow.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, “Indeed, we are all in it. Surely Allah has judged between His servants.”
interpretation: The arrogant leaders will acknowledge that their authority and influence cannot rescue them or their followers from Hell; Allah’s judgment has been decisively made, leaving no possibility of escape or appeal.

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, “Call upon your Lord to lessen our punishment for one day.”
interpretation: In their despair, the inhabitants of Hell will beg its guardians to plead with God for even a temporary reduction in their torment. The verse portrays their belated recognition of the severity of their fate: although they seek only a single day of relief, their request reflects helplessness and does not indicate escape from punishment.

translation: They will say, “Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?” They will say, “Yes.” They will say, “Then call upon them.” But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in vain.
interpretation: This exchange exposes the disbelievers’ blameworthiness: they had already received clear guidance through messengers, yet rejected it. In the Hereafter, their appeals will bring no relief, because they have turned away from the truth and their supplication can no longer avail them.

translation: Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses arise.
interpretation: This is God’s firm promise to grant His messengers and sincere believers His support: in this world through protection, clear proof, steadfastness, and the eventual triumph of truth, and on the Day of Resurrection by vindicating them before all witnesses and honoring them while falsehood and its people are exposed.

translation: On the Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them; theirs will be the curse, and theirs will be the evil abode.
interpretation: This depicts the final judgment, when those who persisted in wrongdoing will have no excuse capable of saving them from God’s justice. They will be deprived of His mercy and face the wretched abode prepared for those who rejected the truth and acted unjustly.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses guidance and made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture.
interpretation: Allah granted Moses clear divine guidance and entrusted the Children of Israel with the revealed Scripture after him, making them responsible for preserving its teachings, understanding them, and living according to them.

translation: A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This describes revelation as a source of direction and spiritual awakening for people who use sound reason and reflect sincerely, enabling them to recognize the truth and live by it.

translation: So be patient; indeed, Allah’s promise is true. Seek forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and in the early morning.
interpretation: This verse teaches steadfastness in the face of opposition by relying on the certainty of Allah’s promise, while combining perseverance with humility, repentance, and continual remembrance of Him at all times.

translation: Indeed, those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them have nothing in their hearts but arrogance, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah; surely He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse teaches that disputing divine revelation without knowledge or valid proof is often driven not by a sincere search for truth, but by pride and a desire to exalt oneself beyond one’s proper limits. Such arrogance cannot achieve the greatness it seeks. The believer is therefore directed to turn to Allah for protection from the impulses of pride and from fruitless contention, trusting in His complete awareness of both spoken arguments and hidden intentions.

translation: Indeed, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of humankind, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The vastness and precision of the heavens and the earth demonstrate that God’s power to resurrect and judge human beings is entirely within His ability; people fail to recognize this because they overlook the greater signs surrounding them.

translation: The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer. Little do you reflect.
interpretation: The verse teaches that spiritual blindness—refusing truth and guidance—cannot be equated with inner insight, just as sincere faith expressed through righteous action cannot be equated with wrongdoing. True understanding is shown by recognizing this moral distinction and allowing it to transform one’s conduct.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is surely coming—there is no doubt about it—but most people do not believe.
interpretation: The Day of Resurrection is an inevitable reality, even if many people deny or disregard it; therefore, faith should be grounded in certainty about God’s promised return and accountability.

translation: And your Lord has said, “Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled.”
interpretation: الله تعالى يأمر عباده أن يتوجهوا إليه وحده بالدعاء والعبادة، ويعدهم بالإجابة بما تقتضيه حكمته؛ فالإجابة قد تكون بإعطاء المطلوب، أو بدفع ضرر، أو بادخار الأجر. أما الإعراض عن دعائه وعبادته تكبرًا فهو جحود لافتقار العبد إلى ربه، وعاقبته الذل والعذاب.

translation: Allah is the One who made the night for you to rest in and the day bright. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day is a deliberate mercy from Allah: the night provides stillness and renewal, while the daylight enables people to see, work, and pursue their needs. These continual blessings reveal His care and generosity, yet human beings often overlook their dependence on Him; true gratitude is to recognize the Giver, praise Him, and use His blessings in obedience.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but Him. So how are you turned away?
interpretation: Allah alone is the true Lord because He created everything, so directing worship or ultimate reliance toward anything else is a grave departure from the truth.

translation: Thus are those who used to deny the signs of Allah turned away.
interpretation: Their persistent rejection of Allah’s signs causes them to be diverted from recognizing the truth and following guidance; this turning away is a consequence of their own denial.

translation: It is Allah who made the earth a settled abode for you, the sky a canopy, shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with wholesome provisions. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize Allah’s sole lordship through the ordered blessings that sustain their lives: the stability of the earth, the protective expanse of the heavens, the excellence of human creation, and pure provision. Since these gifts come from Him alone, gratitude and worship should be devoted to Him, acknowledging His perfect goodness and authority over every realm.

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him. So call upon Him, sincerely devoting the religion to Him. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses perfect, everlasting life and is therefore the only One worthy of worship and supplication. Believers are commanded to direct their prayers and worship to Him alone, free from associating partners or seeking the approval of others, recognizing that all praise belongs to Him as the Lord and Sustainer of all creation.

translation: Say, “I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah, after clear proofs have come to me from my Lord; and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet to declare that true worship must be directed exclusively to Allah, because revelation and clear evidence have established His oneness and invalidated the worship of anything besides Him. It also teaches that genuine faith is not merely recognizing the truth, but surrendering oneself in obedience to Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of every world.

translation: He is the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you forth as infants, then allows you to reach your full strength, then to become elderly. Some of you die before that, and so that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you may understand.
interpretation: The stages of human life reveal that existence unfolds by God’s deliberate decree, from humble beginnings through strength and old age, while each person’s lifespan follows a fixed limit known only to Him. This should awaken people to their dependence on God, the certainty of mortality, and the need to use their understanding before their appointed time arrives.

translation: He is the One who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it comes to be.
interpretation: The verse affirms that life and death are entirely under Allah’s authority, and that nothing can resist His will: whatever He decrees comes into existence effortlessly and without dependence on any created means.

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah—how are they turned away?
interpretation: The verse expresses astonishment at those who knowingly argue against Allah’s clear signs, showing that their persistence in denial is not due to a lack of evidence but because they have been diverted from accepting the truth.

translation: Those who denied the Book and what We sent Our messengers with will soon come to know.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject divine revelation and the truth brought by God’s messengers will eventually face the consequences of their denial, when the reality they refused becomes unmistakable.

translation: When shackles are around their necks and chains, they are dragged.
interpretation: This portrays the utter humiliation and helplessness of those who rejected the truth: bound by shackles and chains, they are forcibly dragged toward their punishment.

translation: In the boiling water, then in the Fire they will be burned.
interpretation: The verse portrays the escalating punishment of those who reject the truth: they are first subjected to scalding water and then cast into the Fire, where their torment is intensified without relief.

translation: Then it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to associate with Allah?”
interpretation: They will be confronted with the false objects of worship they relied upon in worldly life, yet those supposed partners will be absent and unable to help them, exposing the futility of their idolatry.

translation: They will say, “They have vanished from us; rather, we never used to invoke anything before.” Thus does Allah lead the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: When confronted on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will realize that the beings they invoked besides Allah have no power and have abandoned them. Their denial that they ever worshipped anything reveals the futility of their former devotion, and their persistence in falsehood results in Allah leaving them lost from the path of truth.

translation: That is because you used to rejoice on earth without right, and because you used to revel.
interpretation: The punishment is a just consequence of their arrogant, heedless delight in worldly life—celebrating power and pleasures while acting unjustly and refusing accountability before God.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. How miserable is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This is a declaration of the final humiliation of those who rejected the truth out of arrogance: they are commanded to enter Hell and remain there eternally, and their punishment is described as a fittingly wretched dwelling because their pride led them to refuse submission to God.

translation: So be patient. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true. Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or We cause you to die, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ and commands steadfastness: the fulfillment of Allah’s promise does not depend on his witnessing it during his lifetime. Whether the promised consequences appear before his death or afterward, all people will ultimately return to Allah, where His justice and judgment will be fully realized.

translation: ولقد أرسلنا رسلًا من قبلك، منهم من قصصنا عليك، ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك. وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله، فإذا جاء أمر الله قُضي بالحق، وخسر هنالك المبطلون.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الرسل جميعًا عبادٌ اصطفاهم الله، وأن ما أُيّدوا به من الآيات والمعجزات لا يقع بقدرتهم المستقلة، بل بإذن الله وحكمته. كما تشير إلى أن علم الإنسان بسيرة الرسل محدود، وأن العبرة ليست بمعرفة تفاصيل كل رسول، وإنما بالإيمان برسالتهم وبأن الله يفصل في النهاية بالحق، فيظهر بطلان المكذبين وأهل الباطل ويخسرون.

translation: Allah is the One who made livestock for you so that you may ride some of them, and from some of them you may eat.
interpretation: تدلّ الآية على أن الأنعام نعمةٌ سخّرها الله للإنسان؛ ينتفع بها في الركوب والغذاء، مما يقتضي الاعتراف بفضله وشكره، واستعمال هذه النعمة فيما ينفع دون إسراف أو ظلم.

translation: And for you in them are benefits, and so that you may reach, by them, a need held in your hearts; and upon them and upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that the animals He created serve not only as sources of food and other benefits, but also as means by which their purposes and journeys can be fulfilled. Their ability to carry people, together with the ships that carry them across the seas, is a sign of His provision, wisdom, and power.

translation: And He shows you His signs; so which of Allah’s signs will you deny?
interpretation: Allah continually displays clear signs of His power, wisdom, and mercy in creation and in human life. The question is a rebuke: after witnessing these signs, there is no sound basis for rejecting or denying any of them.

translation: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ۚ كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارًا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون
interpretation: أفلم يسافر هؤلاء المكذبون في الأرض ليتأملوا مصير الأمم السابقة؟ لقد كان أولئك أكثر عددًا وأقوى بأسًا وأعظم عمرانًا وآثارًا في الأرض، لكن قوتهم وما جمعوه من أعمال وأموال لم يدفع عنهم الهلاك حين كذبوا واستكبروا؛ فليحذر هؤلاء أن يصيبهم مثل ما أصابهم.

translation: When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they possessed, and what they used to mock encompassed them.
interpretation: They arrogantly relied on their own limited understanding and dismissed the revealed truth, but when the consequences they had ridiculed came upon them, their presumed knowledge could neither guide nor save them.

translation: So when they saw Our punishment, they said, “We believe in Allah alone, and we reject what we used to associate with Him.”
interpretation: This describes the futile confession of those who postponed sincere faith until divine punishment became unmistakable. Their acknowledgment at that moment was compelled by what they witnessed, not the willing submission and repentance that are accepted before the consequences arrive.

translation: But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. Such is Allah’s established way that has already applied to His servants; and there the disbelievers were utterly lost.
interpretation: When the reality of divine punishment became visible, it was too late for their faith to be genuine and beneficial, because it arose from compulsion and fear rather than willing submission before judgment. This is Allah’s consistent decree: those who persist in disbelief until the final consequence appears cannot escape its result, and their denial ends in complete loss.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: Ḥā Mīm is one of the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters, whose precise meaning is known only to Allah; its presence directs the listener to the divine mystery and miraculous character of the revelation that follows.

translation: A revelation from the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This Qur’an is revealed by Allah, whose revelation is an expression of His all-encompassing compassion and mercy toward His creation.

translation: A Book whose verses are explained in detail—an Arabic Qur’an for people who know.
interpretation: The Qur’an has been revealed with its teachings clarified and expressed in the Arabic language so that people who seek understanding may comprehend its guidance and recognize its truth.

translation: As a bearer of good news and a warner; yet most of them turned away, so they do not listen.
interpretation: The Qur’an offers hope to those who accept guidance and warns those who reject it, but many people deliberately turn away from its message; therefore, they remain unreceptive to its truth.

translation: They said, “Our hearts are veiled from what you invite us to, in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier. So do as you will; indeed, we are doing as we will.”
interpretation: They are expressing deliberate rejection of the Prophet’s message: their hearts have become unreceptive, their ears unwilling to listen, and their hostility has created a barrier between them and the truth. Their words, “Do as you will, and we will do as we will,” convey defiance and a refusal to reconsider their position.

translation: Say, “I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is only One God. So remain steadfastly directed toward Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to the polytheists.”
interpretation: The verse establishes that the Prophet’s distinction is not humanity but revelation: he conveys that worship belongs exclusively to Allah. True faith therefore requires turning to Him with unwavering devotion, while continually seeking forgiveness for human shortcomings; associating partners with Him is a grave departure from this path and carries a severe warning.

translation: Those who do not give the prescribed alms and who, regarding the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This describes people whose refusal to give zakat reflects a deeper rejection of accountability before Allah: they withhold the rights owed to others because they do not truly believe they will be raised and judged in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that is never cut off.
interpretation: This promises enduring divine recompense for sincere faith expressed through righteous action—a reward that neither ends nor diminishes, and is not followed by reproach or obligation.

translation: Say, “Do you truly disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days and set up equals for Him? He is the Lord of all worlds.”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny God despite the clear evidence of His creative power, exposing the contradiction in assigning partners or rivals to the One who created the earth and is sovereign over all existence.

translation: And He placed therein firm mountains rising above it, blessed it, and determined therein its provisions in four days, equally for all who ask.
interpretation: Allah established the earth with firmly rooted mountains, endowed it with goodness and life-sustaining blessings, and apportioned within it the means of nourishment needed by its creatures according to a precise and sufficient measure. The phrase “for those who ask” indicates that these provisions are made available to all who seek them, without distinction, within the order Allah has decreed.

translation: Then He directed Himself toward the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, “Come, willingly or unwillingly.” They said, “We come willingly.”
interpretation: After creating the earth, Allah turned His command and power toward the heaven when it was in a smoke-like state, ordering both heaven and earth to submit to His decree. Their response expresses that all creation is inherently subject to Him and fulfills His will without resistance, whether human beings recognize this submission or not.

translation: So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and revealed to each heaven its command. We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and for protection. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
