interpretation: Allah brought the heavens into ordered completion according to His wise command, assigning each its proper function and order. The stars that adorn the nearest heaven also serve as part of its divinely appointed protection, demonstrating that creation is governed by the perfect power and knowledge of Allah.

translation: But if they turn away, say, “I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt that struck ʿĀd and Thamūd.”
interpretation: If they reject the truth and persist in turning away, they are warned that divine punishment may overtake them just as it overtook the peoples of ʿĀd and Thamūd, who refused their messengers and were destroyed for their defiance.

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying, “Worship none but Allah,” they said, “Had our Lord willed, He would have sent down angels. So indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people’s persistent refusal of divine guidance: despite receiving the same call through messengers who addressed them openly and repeatedly, they rejected human messengers as unworthy of conveying revelation. Their demand for angels was not a sincere search for truth but an excuse for disbelief, revealing that arrogance and denial—not lack of evidence—stood between them and submission to Allah.

translation: As for ʿĀd, they acted arrogantly on earth without right and said, “Who is mightier than us in strength?” Did they not see that Allah, who created them, was mightier than them in strength? Yet they continued to deny Our signs.
interpretation: The verse portrays ʿĀd’s downfall as the result of allowing physical power and worldly dominance to produce arrogance and denial. Their question, “Who is mightier than us?” reflects a blindness to the fact that the very strength they possessed was created and sustained by Allah. True strength belongs to the Creator, while human power is limited and accountable; therefore, pride in it cannot protect anyone from divine judgment when it leads to rejecting the truth.

translation: So We sent upon them a furious, piercing wind during days of misfortune, so that We might make them taste the torment of disgrace in this worldly life; and the torment of the Hereafter is even more humiliating, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse explains that the people who rejected God were punished through a relentless wind during appointed days, making them experience humiliation in this life as a consequence of their arrogance and denial. Yet worldly punishment is only a lesser warning, for the punishment of the Hereafter is more degrading, and no one will be able to rescue them from it.

translation: As for Thamūd, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance; so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: Allah made the path of truth clear to Thamūd and enabled them to recognize it, yet they deliberately chose denial and misguidance over faith and obedience. Their punishment was therefore a just consequence of their persistent rejection and the deeds they continued to commit.

translation: And We saved those who believed and were mindful of Allah.
interpretation: Allah’s protection and deliverance are granted to those whose faith is sincere and whose awareness of Him leads them to avoid disobedience and live righteously.

translation: And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered toward the Fire, they will be held back and driven together in ordered ranks.
interpretation: This depicts the enemies of Allah being brought under complete control on the Day of Judgment: none will be able to escape or advance independently, as they are gathered, restrained, and driven collectively toward the Fire.

translation: حتى إذا وصلوا إليها، شهدت عليهم أسماعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية مشهدًا من مشاهد الحساب، حيث يجعل الله جوارح الإنسان نفسها شاهدة على أعماله، فلا يستطيع إنكار ما اقترف، وتظهر الحقيقة كاملة بعد أن كان يظن أن أفعاله قد تخفى.

translation: And they will say to their skins, “Why have you testified against us?” They will reply, “Allah has caused us to speak—the One who causes everything to speak. He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.”
interpretation: When people deny their wrongdoing on the Day of Judgment, Allah will make their own bodies testify against them. Their bodily members do not speak independently; they speak by Allah’s command, demonstrating that nothing is beyond His power and that every person will return to Him for a complete and undeniable judgment.

translation: You did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins testify against you; rather, you thought that Allah did not know much of what you were doing.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who sinned while imagining that their deeds could remain hidden from Allah. Their own faculties and bodies, which they used in wrongdoing, will testify against them, revealing that their false sense of secrecy arose from a mistaken and heedless view of Allah’s complete knowledge.

translation: And that was your assumption about your Lord which ruined you, so you became among the losers.
interpretation: The verse warns that false assumptions about Allah—such as believing He does not know one’s hidden deeds, will not hold one accountable, or will not judge with justice—can deceive a person into persistent disobedience until those assumptions lead to his destruction and loss.

translation: If they endure patiently, the Fire will be their abode; and if they seek to make amends, they will not be among those whose repentance is accepted.
interpretation: The verse depicts the ultimate futility of the rejecters’ responses in the Hereafter: enduring the punishment will not save them, while seeking pardon or another chance will be refused because the time for repentance and correction has already passed.

translation: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the decree became binding upon them among nations that had passed away before them, of jinn and humans. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: Allah allowed corrupting companions—devils from among the jinn and humans—to influence them, making their present actions and their future hopes appear pleasing while concealing the truth of their consequences. Because they persisted in this deception and followed it, they deserved the same judgment that had overtaken earlier rebellious nations, losing both guidance in this world and salvation in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieved said, “Do not listen to this Qur’an, and make noise during its recitation so that you may prevail.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the deliberate strategy of those who reject the truth: they sought to prevent people from hearing and reflecting on the Qur’an by creating distraction and disorder, hoping that suppressing its message would make their opposition appear victorious.

translation: We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.
interpretation: This is a warning that persistent rejection of the truth will lead to severe divine punishment, and that God will judge such people with complete justice, holding them accountable for the gravest of their deeds.

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire. For them therein is the abode of eternity, as recompense for their rejection of Our signs.
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as the enduring consequence for those who knowingly and stubbornly reject Allah’s signs, making their denial the cause of their everlasting punishment.

translation: وقال الذين كفروا: ربنا أرِنا اللذين أضلّانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين.
interpretation: يعبّر أهل الكفر يوم القيامة عن غضبهم وندمهم، إذ يطلبون رؤية من زيّن لهم الضلال وأغواهم من شياطين الجن وأهل الإنس، ليهينوهما ويحمّلوهما مسؤولية ما انتهوا إليه. وفي ذلك بيان أن اتباع المضلّين لا يعفي الأتباع من الحساب، وأن الندم عند ظهور الحق لا ينفع صاحبه.

translation: Indeed, those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, “Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in the Paradise that you were promised.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that true faith is not merely a statement of belief; it is a life of steadfast obedience and constancy upon the truth. Those who remain firm in this way are granted divine reassurance: fear of what lies ahead and sorrow over what has passed are removed, and they receive the glad news of Paradise as the fulfillment of Allah’s promise.

translation: “We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There you will have whatever your souls desire, and there you will have whatever you request.”
interpretation: The angels reassure the steadfast believers that Allah’s care accompanies them throughout their worldly life and will continue into the Hereafter: they will be granted security, companionship, and the fulfillment of every pure desire and rightful request as a reward for their faith and perseverance.

translation: As a welcome from One who is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The blessings prepared for the righteous are an honored reception from Allah, whose forgiveness removes their faults and whose mercy grants them lasting comfort and nearness.

translation: And who is better in speech than one who calls people to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, “Indeed, I am one of those who submit to Allah”?
interpretation: The verse teaches that the noblest speech is that which sincerely invites people to Allah, is confirmed by righteous conduct, and is accompanied by humble commitment to Islam; true calling is therefore made credible by the caller’s deeds and devotion.

translation: The good deed and the bad deed are not equal. Repel evil with what is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.
interpretation: Goodness should not be answered with wrongdoing; rather, respond to harm with the noblest and most gracious conduct. Such patience and kindness can soften hostility, transform an enemy’s attitude, and open the way to sincere friendship.

translation: And none are granted this quality except those who are patient, and none are granted it except one who possesses a great share of goodness.
interpretation: Responding to evil with what is better is a form of moral strength that cannot be sustained without patience and self-restraint; it is a great blessing granted to those whose character and reward are elevated.

translation: And if a prompting from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: When satanic whispers stir anger, hostility, or the urge to respond wrongly, the believer should immediately turn to Allah for protection rather than follow the impulse. Seeking refuge in Him restores self-control, trusting that Allah hears the servant’s plea and knows the inner struggle behind it.

translation: And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon; rather, prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him alone that you worship.
interpretation: The alternation of night and day and the majesty of the sun and moon are signs directing the heart to their Creator, not objects worthy of worship themselves. True devotion requires turning entirely to Allah, recognizing that all created powers are dependent upon Him and that worship belongs exclusively to the One who brought them into existence.

translation: But if they are too arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him by night and by day, and they never grow weary.
interpretation: If the rejecters disdain worship, God is not in need of their submission: the angels near Him continually glorify Him without fatigue, showing that sincere devotion belongs to those who recognize His majesty rather than those who arrogantly refuse it.

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren; then, when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, the One who gives it life is surely the One who will give life to the dead. Truly, He is capable of all things.
interpretation: The revival of lifeless earth after rain is a visible proof that resurrection is within Allah’s power: the One who restores life to the soil can likewise restore life to the dead, for nothing is beyond His ability.

translation: Indeed, those who deviate regarding Our verses are not hidden from Us. So is the one who is cast into the Fire better, or the one who comes safely on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; surely He sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse warns that denying, distorting, or treating God’s signs with hostility cannot escape His knowledge. It contrasts the inevitable end of such a person with the security granted to those who meet God in faith and obedience. “Do whatever you will” is not permission to sin, but a stern threat: every choice is fully seen and will be judged.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them—truly, it is a mighty Book.
interpretation: Those who reject the Qur’an after it has reached them are turning away from a revelation whose truth and authority cannot be overcome; it is preserved from falsehood and will ultimately prevail.

translation: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The Qur’an is safeguarded from contradiction, corruption, and any means by which falsehood could undermine its truth, because it comes from Allah, whose perfect wisdom and praiseworthy authority guarantee its reliability and permanence.

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is truly Possessor of forgiveness and Possessor of painful punishment.
interpretation: The opposition and hurtful words directed at the Prophet are not new; earlier messengers endured the same rejection. This consoles him and warns those who reject the truth that God’s mercy remains open to repentance, while persistent denial and wrongdoing lead to a severe punishment.

translation: Had We made it a non-Arabic Qur’an, they would have said, “Why have its verses not been explained clearly? What—non-Arabic and Arabic?” Say, “For those who believe, it is guidance and healing.” But those who do not believe have deafness in their ears, and it is blindness to them; they are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction of those who reject revelation: had the Qur’an been in another language, they would have objected to its language, and when it was revealed in clear Arabic, they still refused it. Its benefit depends not on language alone but on a receptive heart; believers find in it guidance from error and healing from spiritual doubts and ailments, while persistent rejection makes a person deaf to its truth and unable to perceive its light, like someone called from far away.

translation: Indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture, but disagreement arose concerning it. Had it not been for a decree that had already come from your Lord, judgment would have been made between them. Surely they are in profound doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse teaches that receiving divine revelation does not by itself prevent people from disputing and rejecting the truth. God, in His wisdom, has deferred the decisive judgment according to a decree already established, while those who dispute revelation remain trapped in troubling uncertainty rather than possessing any sound basis for their denial.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is never unjust to His servants.
interpretation: يقرر الله أن الإنسان هو أول من ينتفع بعمله الصالح، وهو الذي يتحمل عاقبة عمله السيئ؛ فلا يضيع خيرٌ يفعله ولا يُحمَّل ذنبَ غيره. وعدل الله كامل، فلا يعاقب أحدًا بغير حق ولا ينقصه شيئًا من جزائه.

translation: To Him alone belongs the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit emerges from its coverings, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. And on the Day He calls to them, “Where are My partners?” they will say, “We declare to You that none of us bears witness to them.”
interpretation: The verse affirms that God alone possesses complete knowledge of the Last Hour and of every hidden detail in creation, from the growth of fruit to conception and birth. When the deniers are confronted about the partners they attributed to Him, they will disavow them and admit that no true witness can establish those alleged partners.

translation: And what they used to invoke before will have vanished from them, and they will realize that they have no escape.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the false gods and imagined sources of help that they relied upon will prove utterly powerless and absent, leaving them to recognize that there is no refuge or way of escape from God’s judgment.

translation: Man never tires of asking for good; but when evil touches him, he becomes despairing and despondent.
interpretation: The verse portrays the human tendency to persistently seek blessings and worldly good, yet quickly lose hope when hardship strikes. It cautions against allowing adversity to extinguish faith and calls the believer to meet suffering with patience, trust in Allah, and steadfast hope.

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, “This is due to me,” and I do not think the Hour will come. Yet if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him.” So We will certainly inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse exposes the delusion of the ungrateful person who, after hardship is removed, attributes blessing to his own entitlement, denies the Resurrection, and—despite that denial—presumes that God would favor him in the Hereafter. It warns that worldly relief is not proof of righteousness; every deed will be brought to account, and persistent ingratitude and disbelief will lead to severe punishment.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon the human being, he turns away and withdraws to his side; but when adversity touches him, he is full of prolonged supplication.
interpretation: The verse portrays the human being’s tendency, when ungrateful, to become heedless and distant from God during ease, while turning intensely to prayer when afflicted. It warns against making devotion dependent on hardship and calls for steadfast gratitude and worship in both prosperity and adversity.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who could be more astray than one who is in profound opposition?”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who reject the Qur’an to consider the grave possibility that it truly comes from Allah. If they deny it despite that possibility, their rejection is not mere uncertainty but stubborn opposition to the truth, placing them in the furthest error.

translation: We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not enough that your Lord is Witness over all things?
interpretation: Allah will continue to reveal the truth of His message through the signs spread throughout the universe and through the realities within human beings themselves, so that sincere people recognize its divine source. Yet the decisive proof is already found in Allah’s complete knowledge and witness over everything: His testimony is sufficient, even before every sign becomes apparent to them.

translation: ألا إنهم لفي شكٍّ من لقاء ربهم، ألا إنه محيطٌ بكل شيء.
interpretation: إن شكَّهم في البعث والوقوف بين يدي الله لا يغيّر من حقيقة ذلك شيئًا؛ فالله محيطٌ علمًا وقدرةً بكل الخلق، لا يخفى عليه شيءٌ من أعمالهم ولا يفلت أحدٌ من حكمه.

translation: Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’anic disjointed letters whose ultimate meaning is known to Allah; their presence at the opening calls attention to the revelation’s distinctive, inimitable nature.

translation: ʿAyn, Sīn, Qāf.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’anic disjointed letters; their precise meaning is known only to Allah, and they signal the extraordinary, inimitable nature of the revelation that follows.

translation: Thus Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise, reveals to you and to those who came before you.
interpretation: This revelation follows the same divine source and essential guidance given to earlier prophets, affirming that God’s messages are consistent in truth while proceeding from His absolute power and perfect wisdom.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and on earth belongs entirely to Allah, affirming His absolute ownership and authority over all creation. His exaltedness places Him above every limitation and imperfection, while His greatness is beyond comparison with anything He has created.

translation: The heavens are almost torn apart from above them, while the angels glorify their Lord with praise and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Indeed, Allah is the Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming majesty of God’s command: even the heavens are nearly rent asunder beneath its weight. In contrast, the angels respond with continual glorification and humble supplication for the forgiveness of earthly beings, illustrating the vast mercy of God, whose forgiveness and compassion remain open to His creation.

translation: And those who take protectors besides Him—Allah is watching over them, and you are not their guardian.
interpretation: Those who turn to other beings or powers for ultimate protection and authority remain fully within Allah’s knowledge and judgment; the Messenger’s duty is to convey the truth, not to control or be accountable for their choice.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an, so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering—there is no doubt about it—when one group will be in Paradise and another group in the Blaze.
interpretation: The Qur’an was revealed in clear Arabic to the Prophet so that he could begin by warning Makkah and its surrounding peoples, while conveying a universal message. It calls humanity to prepare for the certain Day of Resurrection, when all people will be gathered and their final destinies will be distinguished according to their response to God’s guidance: Paradise for one group and Hellfire for another.

translation: Had Allah willed, He could have made them one single community; but He admits into His mercy whom He wills. And the wrongdoers will have neither protector nor helper.
interpretation: Allah has allowed people to differ and has not compelled them all to follow one path, while making His mercy available to those who turn to Him in faith and obedience. Those who persist in wrongdoing will find no one able to protect them from the consequences of their rejection and injustice.

translation: Or have they taken protectors besides Him? Yet Allah alone is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: The verse rejects relying on any supposed guardians or authorities besides Allah, affirming that true protection belongs solely to Him. Since He alone possesses power to restore life after death and controls everything without limitation, devotion and ultimate dependence must be directed to Him alone.

translation: Whatever you differ about, its judgment belongs to Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn in repentance.
interpretation: When people disagree about beliefs, principles, or matters of conduct, the ultimate and decisive authority is Allah, whose knowledge and justice surpass human opinion. Recognizing this calls the believer to trust Him, seek His guidance, and continually return to Him rather than allowing disputes to be governed by ego or speculation.

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth, He has made for you spouses from among yourselves and pairs from among the livestock. By this He multiplies you. Nothing is comparable to Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: Allah alone brought the heavens and the earth into existence and established the means through which life continues and humanity increases. Yet, despite His granting these created blessings, He remains utterly unlike anything He created; no being shares His essence or attributes. His perfect transcendence does not prevent Him from hearing every sound and seeing every thing, so worship and trust belong to Him alone.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: All authority and control over creation belong exclusively to God, so the abundance or limitation of a person’s provision occurs according to His perfect wisdom and knowledge, not by chance or independent human power. Therefore, prosperity should lead to gratitude rather than pride, and hardship to patience and trust in God, while recognizing that material measure is not itself a measure of a person’s worth.

translation: He has ordained for you in religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: uphold the religion and do not be divided regarding it. What you call them to is grievous to the polytheists. God chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the essential call of all the prophets is one: to establish sincere worship and obedience to God while preserving unity in faith rather than allowing division over its foundations. This pure devotion is difficult for those committed to associating partners with God, yet guidance ultimately belongs to God, who draws toward Himself those who sincerely turn to Him.

translation: وما تفرّق أهل الكتاب واختلفوا إلا من بعد أن جاءهم العلم الواضح، وكان اختلافهم بغيًا وحسدًا وعدوانًا فيما بينهم. ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك بتأخير الفصل إلى أجلٍ مسمّى، لقُضي بينهم بإهلاك الظالمين وإظهار الحق. وإن الذين ورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شكٍّ شديد مقلق منه.
interpretation: يبين الله أن سبب الانقسام ليس غموض الحق أو نقص الدليل، بل البغي والحسد بعد قيام العلم؛ ولذلك فاختلاف الناس بعد ظهور الحق قد يكون نتيجة أهوائهم لا قصور البرهان. وقد أمهلهم الله إلى وقت معلوم لحكمة، غير أن من جاء بعدهم وورث كتبهم دون يقين ظل واقعًا في شكٍّ مضطرب، مما يدل على أن العلم وحده لا ينفع صاحبه إذا لم يصحبه إخلاص وتسليم للحق.

translation: So call to the faith and remain steadfast as you have been commanded. Do not follow their desires, but say, “I believe in whatever Scripture Allah has revealed, and I have been commanded to judge justly among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. Our deeds are for us and your deeds are for you. There is no need for argument between us and you. Allah will bring us all together, and to Him is the final return.”
interpretation: This verse directs the Prophet to remain firmly committed to revelation and to invite people to the truth without being swayed by their competing desires. It establishes justice as the proper basis for dealing with others, recognizes Allah as the common Lord of all, and teaches that each person bears responsibility for their own deeds. Therefore, disputes should not become a cause for hostility or endless contention; ultimate judgment belongs to Allah, who will gather everyone and determine their accountability.

translation: And those who argue about Allah after His call has been answered, their argument is futile before their Lord; upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: Those who persist in disputing the truth about Allah after clear evidence has been presented and people have accepted His guidance have no valid basis for their opposition. Their arguments are rejected by Allah because they arise not from sincere pursuit of truth, but from obstinacy; therefore they incur His displeasure and the punishment that follows from knowingly resisting guidance.

translation: الله هو الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان، وما يدريك لعلّ الساعة قريبة.
interpretation: يبين الله أن كتابه نازل بالحق الذي لا باطل فيه، وأن «الميزان» هو معيار العدل الذي تُقاس به الأقوال والأعمال والحقوق؛ ثم يوقظ القلوب من الغفلة بالتنبيه إلى أن الساعة قد تكون قريبة، فينبغي للإنسان أن يستقيم على الحق ويقيم العدل قبل فوات الأوان.

translation: Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Surely, those who dispute concerning the Hour are far astray.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the heedlessness of those who deny the Resurrection with the reverent awareness of believers: denial makes people demand that the promised judgment come immediately, whereas faith makes a person fear its consequences and prepare for it. To argue against the certainty of the Hour is therefore not honest inquiry but a departure far from the truth.

translation: Allah is gracious and gentle toward His servants; He provides for whom He wills. He is the All-Strong, the Almighty.
interpretation: Allah’s care reaches His servants in subtle and often unseen ways, and He grants provision according to His wisdom and will. His generosity is never limited by weakness, for He possesses perfect strength and irresistible authority.

translation: من كان يريد ثواب الآخرة وسعيها، نزد له في ثوابه وسعيه، ومن كان يريد متاع الدنيا، نؤته بعض ما يطلب منها، وليس له في الآخرة نصيب.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن قيمة العمل وتمام ثمرته مرتبطان بالغاية التي يقصدها الإنسان؛ فمن جعل رضوان الله والدار الآخرة مقصده، بارك الله في عمله وضاعف أثره وثوابه، أما من حصر همّه في الدنيا، فقد يُعطى منها بقدر ما قُدّر له، لكن طلب الدنيا وحده لا ينشئ له استحقاقًا في الآخرة.

translation: Or do they have partners who have ordained for them a religion which Allah has not permitted? Had it not been for the decisive word, judgment would already have been passed between them. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns attributing religious laws and practices to Allah without His authorization, warning that no person or authority may make its own innovations binding as divine religion. Allah postpones the final judgment by His decree, but those who legislate against His guidance and persist in wrongdoing will face severe punishment.

translation: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will surely befall them. But those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens’ meadows, having whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great فضل.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the inevitable anxiety of those who caused harm through their deeds with the complete security and generous reward granted to believers who lived righteously: in Paradise, their deepest legitimate desires will be fulfilled by God as an expression of His immense grace.

translation: That is the glad tidings Allah gives to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, “I ask of you no reward for it except affection for my near relatives.” Whoever earns a good deed, We increase its goodness for him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: The Prophet’s call is offered without worldly compensation; its fitting response is sincere faith, righteous action, and loving regard for his close family. Allah, in His generosity, multiplies the value of every good deed, forgives shortcomings, and gratefully rewards obedience.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated a lie against Allah”? If Allah willed, He could seal your heart. But Allah erases falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He knows best what hearts conceal.
interpretation: The verse refutes the accusation that the Prophet ﷺ invented revelation: the Qur’an is not sustained by his own ability, since Allah could silence or seal his heart whenever He willed. Instead, Allah actively nullifies falsehood and confirms the truth through His revelation, whose authenticity is known to Him through His complete knowledge of what lies within people’s hearts.

translation: And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants, pardons misdeeds, and knows all that you do.
interpretation: This verse assures that Allah welcomes the sincere repentance of His servants and erases their sins by His mercy, while His complete knowledge of their actions means that repentance must be genuine and accompanied by a real turning away from wrongdoing.

translation: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty. As for the disbelievers, they will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: Allah accepts the sincere prayers and deeds of believers, grants them what is best for them, and generously gives them beyond what they deserve. In contrast, those who reject faith and persist in denial face a severe punishment because of their rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: Had Allah expanded provision for His servants, they would surely have transgressed throughout the earth; but He sends down in measured proportion whatever He wills. Surely He is All-Aware, All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: Allah distributes provision according to His perfect wisdom, knowing that unrestricted abundance may lead people toward arrogance, injustice, and corruption. Both affluence and limitation are therefore part of His wise care, and no person’s circumstances escape His complete knowledge and sight.

translation: And He is the One who sends down rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protecting Guardian, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse teaches that relief can come from Allah after hope has nearly vanished, and that His mercy encompasses creation in ways that restore life and hope. Therefore, believers should rely on Him, remain hopeful in hardship, and praise Him as the One who lovingly cares for and sustains them.

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the living creatures He has spread throughout them. And He is fully capable of gathering them whenever He wills.
interpretation: The vastness and ordered diversity of life in the heavens and the earth testify to Allah’s limitless creative power. The One who brought all these creatures into existence can also gather them together whenever He wills, including for the final resurrection and judgment.

translation: Whatever calamity befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الإنسان مدعوّ إلى مراجعة أعماله عند نزول الشدائد، إذ قد تكون بعض المصائب أثرًا لما اقترفته يداه، مع بيان سعة عفو الله؛ فهو لا يؤاخذ العباد بكل ذنوبهم، بل يتجاوز عن كثير منها رحمةً بهم.

translation: You cannot escape God’s power on earth, nor have you besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: No matter where people go or how powerful they become, they cannot evade Allah’s knowledge, authority, or judgment; and no created being can independently protect them from Him or rescue them from the consequences of rejecting Him.

translation: And among His signs are the ships sailing through the sea like mountains.
interpretation: The immense ships moving across the sea, resembling towering mountains, are a sign of Allah’s power and wisdom, inviting people to recognize His control over creation and the forces that enable them to travel safely.

translation: If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface. Surely in that are signs for everyone steadfast and grateful.
interpretation: The movement of ships depends entirely on Allah’s permission and the forces He governs; their sudden stillness reveals human dependence and the limits of worldly means. Those who reflect upon this respond with patience in hardship and gratitude in ease.

translation: Or He may destroy them because of what they have earned, while He pardons much.
interpretation: This expresses that people may face destruction as a consequence of their wrongdoing, yet God’s mercy is greater than their faults, for He overlooks and forgives much rather than holding them accountable for everything they have done.

translation: And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know that they have no escape.
interpretation: Those who reject or challenge Allah’s clear revelations will eventually confront the truth and realize that no refuge, evasion, or escape from His judgment is possible.

translation: Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment of the life of this world; but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: The verse redirects the believer’s priorities: worldly possessions and pleasures, however abundant, are temporary gifts that will pass away, whereas Allah’s reward is superior in value and everlasting. True faith is shown by relying on Allah rather than treating material means as the ultimate source of security or happiness.

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and indecencies, and when they become angry, they forgive.
interpretation: The verse portrays true righteousness as combining self-restraint with mercy: believers distance themselves from grave wrongdoing, and when anger arises, they do not let it drive them to revenge or injustice; instead, they choose to pardon when forgiveness is appropriate.

translation: And those who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs through mutual consultation, and spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse portrays the believers as people who submit to God in worship, organize their communal affairs through consultation rather than domination, and recognize that their wealth is a provision from Him, so they share it generously for righteous purposes.

translation: And those who, when wronged, defend themselves.
interpretation: This praises those who do not accept oppression passively, but seek justice and repel wrongdoing with measured self-defense, without exceeding the limits of what is right.

translation: The recompense of an evil is an evil like it. But whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Justice permits a person to respond to harm only to the same extent, without excess or transgression; however, forgiveness accompanied by genuine reconciliation is a higher virtue whose reward Allah Himself guarantees. Those who go beyond what is deserved and commit injustice are not loved by Allah.

translation: And whoever defends himself after being wronged—there is no blame upon such people.
interpretation: Allah does not hold a person blameworthy for seeking justice or defending their rights after suffering ظلم, provided they do not exceed the limits of fairness or commit further wrongdoing.

translation: The way of blame is only against those who wrong people and transgress throughout the land without right. For them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: Accountability and punishment are directed at those who deliberately oppress others and abuse their power by spreading injustice, not at those who defend themselves against wrongdoing. The verse warns that such oppression is a grave moral offense before God and will have painful consequences.

translation: And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is truly among matters requiring firm resolve.
interpretation: True strength is shown by restraining anger, enduring harm, and choosing forgiveness when one has the ability to retaliate; such self-control reflects exceptional determination and moral resolve.

translation: And whoever Allah leads astray will have no protector after Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, “Is there any way to return?”
interpretation: Whoever knowingly turns away from Allah and is left to the consequences of that choice will find no power or protector capable of rescuing them. When the wrongdoers finally witness the punishment, they will desperately wish to return to worldly life so they might repent and act righteously, but that opportunity will have passed.

translation: And you will see them exposed to it, humbled by disgrace, looking from a furtive glance. Those who believe will say, “Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.” Surely, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the profound humiliation and fear of those brought before the Fire: they cannot face it openly, but glance toward it furtively under the weight of disgrace. Their ultimate loss is not merely the loss of worldly possessions, but the loss of their own salvation and the separation from their families in the Hereafter. This lasting punishment is the consequence of persistent wrongdoing and injustice toward the truth.

translation: And they will have no protectors to help them besides Allah. Whoever Allah allows to stray, for him there is no way.
interpretation: Those who turn away from Allah will find that the powers and allies they rely upon cannot protect or rescue them; when a person persists in misguidance and Allah leaves him to it, he has no path to truth or salvation.

translation: Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be averted. On that Day you will have no refuge, nor will you be able to deny your deeds.
interpretation: The verse urges people to turn obediently to God while repentance and action are still possible, warning that the coming Day of Judgment cannot be postponed or escaped. At that time, no protection will remain outside God, and a person will have no means of rejecting or concealing the truth of what they have done.

translation: If they turn away, We have not sent you as their guardian. Your duty is only to convey the message. Indeed, when We let a person taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but when adversity befalls him because of what his hands have sent ahead, the human being is ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the Messenger’s responsibility is to communicate the truth, not to compel people to accept it. It also exposes a weakness in human nature: people readily celebrate blessings, yet often respond to hardship with ingratitude, even when their own actions have contributed to it. True faith requires recognizing both mercy and adversity as occasions for humility, accountability, and turning back to God.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills. He grants female children to whomever He wills, and He grants male children to whomever He wills.
interpretation: The verse affirms that creation and parenthood are entirely under Allah’s sovereignty and wisdom. Children are not possessions earned by human control, and neither sons nor daughters are signs of greater worth; each is a gift determined by Allah’s will, calling people to humility, gratitude, and acceptance of His decree.

translation: Or He gives them both males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: Allah alone determines the form of each person’s family life and offspring: He may grant sons, daughters, both, or no children. These outcomes occur according to His perfect knowledge and wisdom, and no one can compel or limit His power.

translation: It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except through revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills. Indeed, He is Most High, Most Wise.
interpretation: Allah’s communication with human beings occurs only in ways befitting His transcendence: by placing guidance directly into the heart, by addressing a servant without being seen, or by sending an angelic messenger to convey His command. The verse establishes that divine speech is real while its manner is governed by Allah’s wisdom and majesty, and that revelation reaches the recipient solely by His permission.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Scripture was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. Indeed, you guide to a straight path.
interpretation: The revelation is called a spirit because it gives life to hearts, and a light because it removes the darkness of ignorance and misguidance. Before revelation, the Prophet ﷺ did not possess knowledge of the revealed Scripture or the details of faith through his own means; Allah then entrusted him with this divine guidance. Allah alone grants guidance to whomever He wills, while the Prophet ﷺ guides people by conveying the revelation and directing them toward the upright path of truth and obedience.

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Surely, to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: Allah’s way is the straight path that leads to Him, for He alone possesses and governs all creation. Since every affair ultimately returns to His judgment and authority, people should follow His guidance and entrust their lives to His command.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ha, Mim.
interpretation: “Ha, Mim” is among the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters; their precise meaning is known only to Allah, while their placement points to the miraculous nature of the Qur’an, composed from the same letters familiar to its hearers.

translation: By the clear Book.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Qur’an, a Book whose truth is evident and whose verses clearly distinguish guidance from error.

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an so that you may understand.
interpretation: Allah has revealed the Qur’an in clear Arabic so that its meanings can be understood, reflected upon, and followed, rather than remaining inaccessible or obscure to those addressed by it.

translation: Indeed, it is with Us, in the Mother of the Book, exalted and wise.
interpretation: The Qur’an has its origin in the preserved divine record with Allah; it is honored in status and perfect in the wisdom of its guidance and judgments.

translation: Shall We then turn away the Reminder from you because you are a transgressing people?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: your excesses and disobedience do not make you exempt from divine guidance; rather, the Qur’an continues to admonish you so that you may return to the truth and abandon wrongdoing.

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples.
interpretation: This is a reminder that God repeatedly sent prophets to earlier nations to guide them, showing that sending messengers is an established part of His mercy and guidance to humanity.

translation: Whenever a messenger came to them, they mocked him.
interpretation: This verse portrays the persistent arrogance of those who reject divine guidance: rather than reflect on the message brought by each prophet, they respond with ridicule. It warns that mocking God’s messengers is a recurring form of denial that prevents people from recognizing the truth.

translation: So We destroyed those who were mightier than them, and the example of the former peoples has already passed.
interpretation: This is a warning that worldly power and strength cannot protect those who reject truth and persist in arrogance; earlier nations stronger than them were destroyed, leaving their fate as a precedent for those who follow their path.

translation: And if you ask them, “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will surely say, “The Almighty, the All-Knowing created them.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction in the polytheists’ belief: they acknowledged that creation belongs to Allah alone, whose might is absolute and whose knowledge encompasses all things, yet they still directed worship to others. Recognizing Allah as the sole Creator necessarily entails recognizing Him as the only One deserving worship.

translation: He is the One who made the earth a resting place for you and placed pathways in it, so that you may find your way.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to Allah’s wisdom in making the earth habitable and accessible, with its routes and means of movement arranged for human benefit; this provision should lead people to recognize His guidance and follow the path that brings them to Him.

translation: And He is the One who sends down water from the sky in due measure, and We revive with it a lifeless land. In the same way, you will be brought forth.
interpretation: The measured descent of rain and the revival of barren earth are a sign of Allah’s perfect power and wisdom: just as He brings life to dead land, He can bring human beings back to life after death for resurrection and judgment.

translation: And He is the One who created all pairs and made for you ships and livestock on which you ride.
interpretation: This verse directs people to recognize God’s creative wisdom and providence: He established creation in complementary pairs and subjected means of transport—both ships and animals—to human use. Such blessings should lead to humility, gratitude, and acknowledgment that their ability to benefit from them comes from God.

translation: So that you may settle firmly upon their backs, then remember the blessing of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say: “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, for we could never have mastered it ourselves.”
interpretation: When people are given the ability to ride and benefit from animals or other means of transport, they are to recognize that this capability is a gift from God, not merely the result of their own strength or skill. The verse teaches gratitude and humility by directing them to glorify God and acknowledge their dependence on His power and provision.

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we shall surely return.
interpretation: This expresses the believer’s certainty that every journey and ultimately all life end in returning to Allah, acknowledging His sovereignty and accountability before Him.

translation: And they have assigned to Him a portion from His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This rebukes those who attribute offspring or a share of divine status to Allah from among His creatures, despite acknowledging that He is their Creator. Such a claim is a profound contradiction and reveals humanity’s manifest ingratitude for Allah’s blessings and oneness.

translation: Or has He taken daughters from what He creates, while choosing sons exclusively for you?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of those who attributed daughters to Allah while regarding sons as superior for themselves. The verse exposes the inconsistency and injustice of assigning to Allah what they themselves considered inferior, even though He is the Creator and has no need of offspring.

translation: And when one of them is given the news of what he has attributed to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face darkens, and he is filled with suppressed grief.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who attributed daughters to Allah while considering daughters a source of shame for themselves: when one of them is informed that a daughter has been born, his face darkens with distress. It therefore rejects both their false claim about Allah and their contempt for women.

translation: Or one who is brought up in adornment and is not clear in argument?
interpretation: The verse exposes the inconsistency of those who attributed daughters to God while regarding daughters as inferior for themselves. It invokes their own social assumptions rhetorically, rather than declaring that women are inherently incapable of clear speech or reasoning.

translation: And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, female. Were they witnesses to their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse condemns the unfounded claim that the angels are female, since those who make it have no knowledge or evidence from witnessing their creation. It warns that such assertions are documented and that those who utter them will be held accountable before God.

translation: And they say, “If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.” They have no knowledge of this; they do nothing but speculate.
interpretation: They invoke God’s will as an excuse for their idolatry, but this claim is unsupported by revelation or sound knowledge. Their words are mere conjecture used to evade responsibility for knowingly following false worship.

translation: Or have We given them a scripture before it, to which they are holding fast?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question rejecting their claim that their beliefs have divine authority: they possess no earlier revelation that supports what they assert or provides a justification for abandoning the truth brought by the Qur’an.

translation: Rather, they said, “We found our forefathers following a way, and surely we are guided by their footsteps.”
interpretation: They rejected the truth by relying on inherited tradition, assuming that following their ancestors was itself proof of guidance rather than examining the truth with understanding and evidence.

translation: And thus We never sent before you a warner to any town except that its affluent people said, “Indeed, we found our forefathers following a way, and we are following in their footsteps.”
interpretation: The verse shows that opposition to divine guidance often arises from privileged people who cling to inherited customs simply because they are inherited. Their attachment to ancestral practice becomes a substitute for examining the truth, and their social influence encourages others to follow them without evidence.

translation: He said, “Even if I bring you better guidance than what you found your forefathers following?” They replied, “Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the stubbornness of those who reject truth merely because it challenges inherited beliefs: even when confronted with guidance superior to their ancestral customs, they choose loyalty to tradition over sincere consideration and openly reject the message brought by the prophets.

translation: So We took retribution from them; see, then, what was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This warns that persistent rejection of truth and arrogant refusal to heed clear signs ultimately lead to divine judgment and ruin, while urging reflection on the fate of earlier deniers.

translation: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, “Indeed, I am disassociated from whatever you worship,”
interpretation: Abraham openly rejected every object of worship besides Allah, declaring that true faith requires complete freedom from association with false gods and steadfast commitment to the worship of the One God.

translation: Except for Him who created me; indeed, He will guide me.
interpretation: This expresses Abraham’s disavowal of all objects of worship except Allah, the Creator, together with his firm trust that the One who brought him into existence will guide him to the truth and keep him upon the right path.

translation: And he made it an enduring word among his descendants, so that they might return.
interpretation: God preserved the word of monotheism in Abraham’s descendants as a lasting testimony, so that those who stray from it may remember the truth and return to worshipping God alone.

translation: Rather, I allowed these people and their fathers to enjoy life until the truth came to them and a clear messenger.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who mistook prolonged worldly enjoyment for divine approval: their prosperity was only a temporary respite, lasting until God sent them unmistakable truth through a messenger who clearly conveyed and explained it.

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and indeed we disbelieve in it.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the obstinate rejection of divine revelation: rather than consider the truth sincerely, they dismissed it as magic and openly chose disbelief.

translation: And they said, “Why was this Qur’an not revealed to a great man from either of the two cities?”
interpretation: They objected to the Prophet’s message because they judged worthiness by worldly status, wealth, and influence, assuming revelation should be given to a prominent leader from Makkah or Ta’if. The verse exposes their error in trying to impose human standards on God’s choice of His messenger.

translation: Or do they distribute your Lord’s mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in درجات, so that some may employ others in service. Yet your Lord’s mercy is better than whatever they accumulate.
interpretation: The verse rebukes people for presuming to judge or control the distribution of God’s mercy. Just as worldly provisions and differing abilities, circumstances, and responsibilities are assigned by divine wisdom, spiritual mercy—especially guidance and closeness to God—belongs to God alone. Human differences are meant to create mutual dependence and cooperation, not arrogance or oppression; therefore, the lasting mercy of God is far more valuable than wealth, status, or possessions that people compete to gather.

translation: Had it not been that people might all become one community in disbelief, We would have provided those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful with roofs of silver for their houses and stairways by which they could ascend.
interpretation: Allah makes clear that worldly wealth is not a sign of honor or divine favor. He could have granted immense riches even to those who reject Him, but He withholds such abundance lest people be deceived by material splendor and follow disbelief for its sake. True worth therefore lies in faith and obedience, not in the possessions a person receives.

translation: And We would have made for their houses doors and couches upon which they recline.
interpretation: This describes the abundance of worldly luxury Allah could grant, showing that ornate homes and comfortable possessions are not signs of true honor or divine approval, but merely temporary adornments of worldly life.

translation: And gold ornaments. Yet all of that is only the enjoyment of worldly life, while the Hereafter with your Lord is for the God-conscious.
interpretation: Worldly wealth and adornment are temporary provisions, not signs of true honor or divine approval; lasting success is reserved for those who remain mindful of God and live righteously.

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his constant companion.
interpretation: Whoever deliberately neglects Allah’s guidance and remembrance becomes vulnerable to a devilish influence that remains with him, beautifying error, distracting him from truth, and accompanying him until he is led further away from the right path.

translation: And indeed, they turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided.
interpretation: Evil companions can mislead a person from the way of truth while making that deviation appear correct, so the person persists in error believing that he is following guidance.

translation: Until, when he comes to Us, he says, “Would that between me and you were the distance between the two easts! What a wretched companion!”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the person who allowed Satan to accompany and mislead him will recognize the truth and desperately wish to be separated from him by the greatest possible distance. Yet this regret will come too late, revealing the terrible consequence of choosing a corrupt companion and following his influence.

translation: Today, since you acted unjustly, it will not benefit you that you share in the punishment.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who wronged themselves through disbelief and wrongdoing will find no comfort or relief in suffering alongside others. Shared punishment does not lessen anyone’s responsibility or pain, because each person bears the consequences of their own injustice.

translation: Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in manifest error?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question showing that the Messenger cannot compel those who have closed themselves to truth to accept guidance; his duty is to convey the message, while guidance belongs to God and is received only by hearts willing to see and hear.

translation: So if We take you away, We will surely take retribution from them.
interpretation: Even if the Prophet is taken from this world before witnessing the outcome, God’s punishment of those who persist in rejecting the truth is certain and will not be prevented by his absence.

translation: Or We will show you what We have promised them; surely We have full power over them.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that, whether he witnesses the promised punishment of the rejecters or it occurs after him, its fulfillment is entirely within Allah’s power, and none can escape His authority.

translation: So hold firmly to what has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: Remain steadfastly committed to the revelation and follow its guidance without wavering, for adherence to it is the way that keeps a person rightly guided.

translation: Indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: The Qur’an is both an honor and a moral responsibility for the Prophet and his people: they are called to remember its guidance, live by it, and will be held accountable for how they responded to it.

translation: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: “Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical affirmation that every messenger before Muhammad taught the worship of Allah alone and rejected all partners or intermediaries falsely worshipped besides Him.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his assembly, and he said, “Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.”
interpretation: Moses was sent to confront Pharaoh’s tyranny with clear divine signs and to call him and his leaders to recognize that authority belongs not to earthly rulers, but to the Lord who governs all creation.

translation: When he came to them with Our signs, they immediately began to laugh at them.
interpretation: Their laughter reveals their arrogant rejection: instead of reflecting on the clear signs brought by the messenger, they treated them with mockery and contempt.

translation: We did not show them any sign except that it was greater than its counterpart, and We seized them with punishment so that they might return.
interpretation: الله تعالى يبيّن أن الآيات المتتابعة التي أرسلها إلى فرعون وقومه كانت تزداد وضوحًا وقوة، ومع ذلك لم يحملهم ظهورها على الإيمان؛ فأصابهم بالعذاب تنبيهًا لهم وردعًا، لعلهم يرجعون عن تكذيبهم وطغيانهم إلى الحق.

translation: And they said, “O sorcerer, call upon your Lord for us by virtue of the covenant He has made with you; indeed, we will surely be guided.”
interpretation: In their distress, Pharaoh’s people appealed to Moses to pray for the removal of the punishment, claiming that they would then follow the truth. Their address as “sorcerer” reflects their continued arrogance and refusal to honor him as a prophet, while their promise of guidance was conditional and exposed the insincerity of faith based only on escaping hardship.

translation: فلمّا كشفنا عنهم العذاب، إذا هم ينكثون.
interpretation: حين رفع الله عنهم البلاء استجابةً لطلبهم، عادوا إلى نقض عهدهم وترك الوفاء بما التزموا به؛ وفي ذلك بيانٌ لذمّ من يلجأ إلى الله عند الشدة ثم يتراجع عن عهده بعد زوالها.

translation: And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, “O my people, does the kingdom of Egypt not belong to me, with these rivers flowing beneath me? Do you not see?”
interpretation: Pharaoh uses his material power and control over Egypt’s wealth to deceive his people into viewing him as worthy of obedience and authority. By drawing attention to the rivers and prosperity under his command, he appeals to worldly status while diverting them from recognizing that true sovereignty belongs to God.

translation: “Or am I better than this one who is contemptible and can scarcely express himself?”
interpretation: Pharaoh spoke these words arrogantly to demean Moses, using his speech difficulty as a supposed sign of inferiority while presenting his own worldly power and status as evidence of superiority. The verse exposes how arrogance distorts judgment: it dismisses truth by attacking the messenger rather than answering the message.

translation: “Why, then, have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels not come with him in succession?”
interpretation: Pharaoh used these demands to mock Moses and undermine his prophethood, judging divine authority by worldly adornment and visible supernatural spectacle rather than by the truth of his message.

translation: So he made fools of his people, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: Pharaoh weakened his people’s judgment through deception and contempt for the truth, and they followed him because they willingly accepted his authority despite their persistent rebellion against God.

translation: Then, when they angered Us, We took retribution against them and drowned them all.
interpretation: When Pharaoh’s people persisted in rejecting the truth and wronging others despite the clear signs given to them, they brought upon themselves God’s punishment. Their collective destruction by drowning was a consequence of their deliberate rebellion and injustice.

translation: So We made them a precedent and an example for those who came after.
interpretation: Their destruction was made a lasting warning, so that later peoples would learn from their rebellion and recognize the consequences of rejecting God’s guidance.

translation: And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, your people immediately raised an uproar over it.
interpretation: When Jesus, son of Mary, was mentioned as an example in response to the claim that anything worshipped besides God would be condemned, the unbelievers seized upon the comparison and loudly objected, using it to evade the truth rather than consider the intended argument.

translation: And they said, “Are our gods better, or is he?” They put this example to you only for the sake of argument; rather, they are a disputatious people.
interpretation: The unbelievers invoked Jesus merely to challenge the Prophet and defend their worship of idols, trying to exploit the Qur’an’s mention of him as an example. Their question was not a sincere search for truth, but a contentious argument intended to create confusion and evade the clear distinction between Jesus, a servant honored by God, and their lifeless idols.

translation: He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed Our favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: Jesus is presented as a honored human servant of God, not divine. His miraculous birth and mission were blessings from God, and his life was made a sign and model through which the Children of Israel could recognize God’s power and guidance.

translation: And if We willed, We could make angels from among you, succeeding one another on the earth.
interpretation: Allah declares His absolute power over creation: He could replace humankind with angels inhabiting and succeeding one another on earth, showing that human existence is by His choice and not by necessity or independence from Him.

translation: And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour. So do not doubt it, and follow Me; this is a straight path.
interpretation: Jesus is presented as a clear sign pointing to the nearness and certainty of the Final Hour; therefore, people must not waver about the Resurrection, but follow God’s guidance along the straight path.

translation: And let not Satan turn you away; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: Do not allow Satan to divert you from faith, obedience, and the truth through doubt, temptation, or distraction, for his hostility toward you is open and deliberate.

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, “I have come to you with wisdom and to clarify for you some of that over which you differ. So be mindful of Allah and obey me.”
interpretation: Jesus’s mission was to illuminate disputed matters through divinely granted wisdom and clear evidence, guiding people away from confusion and toward obedience to Allah through obedience to His messenger.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, and Lord of all, and therefore worship belongs exclusively to Him. True guidance consists in recognizing His oneness and directing one’s devotion and obedience to Him without associating partners with Him.

translation: Then the factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who wronged, because of the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: After the clear truth was brought to them, the disputing groups divided over it and followed conflicting claims. This warning declares that those who reject or distort the truth and thereby wrong themselves will face severe punishment on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Are they waiting for anything but the Hour to come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware?
interpretation: They persist in heedlessness and delay repentance, not realizing that the Day of Judgment may arrive without warning, when there will be no opportunity left to believe, repent, or prepare.

translation: Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.
interpretation: Friendships founded on disobedience, worldly interests, or mutual wrongdoing will turn into enmity on the Day of Judgment, when each person recognizes how the other contributed to their ruin. The friendship of the God-conscious is different: because it was grounded in faith and obedience, it remains a source of benefit and loyalty rather than blame.

translation: O My servants, no fear will there be for you today, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: Allah reassures His sincere servants on the Day of Judgment that they will be secure from the terror of what lies ahead and free from sorrow over what they left behind, because His mercy and acceptance have granted them lasting peace.

translation: Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims.
interpretation: This describes believers whose faith in Allah’s signs is joined with sincere submission to Him, expressed through obedience and devotion rather than mere acknowledgment.

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing and honored.
interpretation: It is said to the righteous that they will enter Paradise together with their believing spouses, welcomed into a state of lasting joy, dignity, and delight, free from every sorrow or hardship.

translation: Among them will be passed around dishes and cups of gold, containing whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in; and you will remain there forever.
interpretation: This portrays Paradise as a place of complete and enduring fulfillment, where every worthy desire is granted, every sight brings joy, and its blessings never diminish or come to an end.

translation: And this is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do.
interpretation: Allah grants the believers Paradise as an enduring inheritance, while their righteous deeds are the cause by which they attain it and a testimony to their faith and obedience.

translation: For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you eat.
interpretation: Allah describes Paradise as a place of plentiful, varied, and readily available nourishment, granted to its inhabitants for their enjoyment without scarcity or hardship.

translation: Indeed, the criminals will remain forever in the punishment of Hell.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who persist in criminal disbelief and rebellion against God, refusing repentance, will face an enduring punishment in Hell; their permanence there reflects the seriousness of knowingly rejecting divine guidance and wrongdoing.

translation: It will not be eased for them, and they will be therein despairing.
interpretation: The punishment will continue without any reduction or respite, leaving them in utter hopelessness, unable to escape or find relief.

translation: We did not wrong them; rather, they themselves were the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the punishment or misfortune that befell them was not unjustly imposed upon them; it resulted from their own wrongdoing, rejection, and persistent disobedience.

translation: And they will call, “O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us.” He will say, “Indeed, you will remain.”
interpretation: The inhabitants of Hell, overwhelmed by suffering, will plead for death as a means of escape, but Mālik’s reply shows that death will not be granted to them; they are condemned to remain in punishment, with no release or end.

translation: We have brought you the truth, but most of you dislike the truth.
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who reject divine guidance because it conflicts with their desires, habits, or worldly interests; their aversion does not diminish the truth, but reveals their unwillingness to submit to it.

translation: Or have they devised a plan? Indeed, We too are devising.
interpretation: If the rejecters are determined to plot against the truth and its messenger, their scheme cannot escape Allah’s knowledge or power; He decisively brings about His decree and frustrates whatever opposes it.

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Indeed, Our messengers are with them, recording.
interpretation: They should not imagine that anything they conceal or whisper escapes divine knowledge. Their words and deeds are being carefully recorded by the angels assigned to them, so they will be accountable for what they say and hide.

translation: Say, “If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers.”
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge that exposes the falsehood of attributing a son to God: if such a claim were true, the Prophet would be the first to acknowledge and worship him, yet the conditional statement underscores that God is exalted above having offspring.

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, far above what they describe.
interpretation: Allah is utterly exalted beyond every false claim and imperfection attributed to Him; His sovereignty over all creation affirms that no description contrary to His majesty can be true.

translation: So leave them to indulge in vain discourse and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persist in heedlessness and treat the truth as a game will not escape accountability; they are left temporarily to their distractions until the promised Day exposes the consequences of their choices.

translation: And He is the One who is God in heaven and God on earth; and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: Allah alone is worthy of worship in every realm, whether above the heavens or upon the earth. His absolute wisdom governs all things, and His complete knowledge encompasses everything.

translation: Blessed is He to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything between them. With Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse declares God’s absolute sovereignty over all existence and affirms that the exact knowledge of the Resurrection lies solely with Him. Since every person will ultimately return to Him for judgment, true blessing and security are found in recognizing His authority and living in accountability before Him.

translation: Those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth with knowledge.
interpretation: Intercession is not an independent power possessed by the idols or beings invoked besides Allah. It belongs only to those whom Allah permits—those who affirm the truth of His oneness knowingly and sincerely.

translation: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, “Allah.” So how are they turned away?
interpretation: They acknowledge that Allah alone is their Creator, yet their worship and beliefs contradict this recognition by turning toward false deities; the verse exposes the irrationality of such deviation from the truth they themselves admit.

translation: And he said, “O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.”
interpretation: This expresses the Messenger’s appeal to Allah after his people persistently rejected the truth: their continued disbelief is presented as a matter entrusted to Allah’s judgment, despite the clarity of the message conveyed to them.

translation: So turn away from them and say, “Peace.” They will come to know.
interpretation: The verse instructs the believer to respond to persistent rejection with dignified restraint rather than argument or retaliation, leaving their ultimate realization to the consequences of truth and their future accountability before God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: “Ḥā Mīm” is one of the Qur’an’s mysterious opening letters; its ultimate meaning is known to Allah, while its presence draws attention to the revelation that follows and to the Qur’an’s inimitable nature, formed from the same letters known to humanity.

translation: By the Clear Book.
interpretation: This is an oath by the Qur’an, which is clear in its language and guidance and makes truth, falsehood, and the path of salvation evident.

translation: Indeed, We sent it down on a blessed night; indeed, We have always been warners.
interpretation: Allah declares that the Qur’an was revealed on a night filled with blessing and divine favor, marking the beginning of His final guidance for humanity. Its revelation is also an act of warning, calling people to recognize the truth, abandon wrongdoing, and prepare themselves for accountability before Allah.

translation: In it, every wise matter is determined.
