interpretation: This refers to the blessed night in which Allah decrees and clarifies the affairs destined to unfold, according to His perfect wisdom and knowledge.

translation: A command from Us; indeed, We are ever sending [messengers].
interpretation: This indicates that what occurs is established by God’s deliberate decree and wisdom, and that He conveys His guidance to humanity through messengers whom He sends.

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: What has been granted or decreed is an expression of Allah’s mercy, grounded in His perfect awareness of His servants’ words, needs, and circumstances; nothing escapes His hearing or knowledge.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them—if you would be certain.
interpretation: The verse directs those who seek certainty to recognize that the entire universe belongs to and is governed by one Lord; true conviction begins with acknowledging His absolute sovereignty over all existence.

translation: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. He is your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.
interpretation: This affirms God’s absolute oneness and sovereignty: life and death are solely under His power, and His lordship encompasses both the present generation and all preceding generations. Therefore, no created being or inherited tradition can share in His divinity or deserve worship besides Him.

translation: Rather, they are in doubt, amusing themselves.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth does not arise from sound understanding, but from uncertainty that they leave unresolved while becoming absorbed in heedless distractions.

translation: So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a manifest smoke.
interpretation: This is a warning to remain alert for the arrival of a clear divine punishment, when a smoke will appear as a sign of the truth of God’s warning and of the consequences awaiting those who persist in disbelief.

translation: It will envelop the people. This is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays a punishment that completely overwhelms the people, leaving them unable to escape its suffering, and warns of the grave consequence of rejecting the truth.

translation: Our Lord, remove from us the torment; indeed, we are believers.
interpretation: This is the desperate plea of those who face divine punishment and profess faith only when its reality becomes undeniable. It warns that belief expressed after the consequences of rejection have appeared is not the sincere faith that benefits a person before punishment arrives.

translation: How can they take heed, when a clear Messenger has already come to them?
interpretation: Their excuse for failing to believe is untenable, because God had already sent them a messenger who made the truth plain; therefore their later awakening or regret cannot erase their deliberate rejection.

translation: Then they turned away from him and said, “He is taught by others, a madman.”
interpretation: They rejected the messenger’s warning instead of considering its truth, resorting to the contradictory accusation that he was merely instructed by someone else while also being insane—an expression of stubborn denial rather than a reasoned response.

translation: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while, but you will return.
interpretation: The verse warns that a temporary relief from suffering does not mean true repentance or lasting change; those who turn away may return to their former disbelief and wrongdoing once the hardship is lifted.

translation: On the Day We will seize with the greatest seizure, We will surely take retribution.
interpretation: This warns that God will bring about a decisive and overwhelming punishment against those who persist in rejecting the truth, demonstrating His justice and power and avenging the wrongs they have committed.

translation: And We certainly tested before them the people of Pharaoh, when a noble messenger came to them.
interpretation: Allah reminds the believers that the people of Pharaoh were also subjected to a decisive trial: they were confronted with a dignified messenger who conveyed the truth clearly. Their response would reveal whether they would submit to guidance or persist in arrogance, just as later nations are tested by how they respond to divine revelation.

translation: “Deliver Allah’s servants to me; indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger sent to you.”
interpretation: Moses calls Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel from oppression and to recognize that he is conveying Allah’s command faithfully, without deceit or personal betrayal.

translation: And do not exalt yourselves above Allah. Indeed, I bring you a clear authority.
interpretation: Moses warns Pharaoh and his people not to arrogantly defy Allah or claim superiority over His command, affirming that he has come with clear and decisive proof of his divine mission.

translation: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
interpretation: Moses declares that he is placing himself under Allah’s protection from the people’s hostility and threats, affirming that the same Lord who created and sustains them is his protector as well.

translation: And if you do not believe me, then keep away from me.
interpretation: The speaker warns those who reject his message not to oppose or obstruct him, but to leave him free to follow and convey what God has commanded.

translation: So he called upon his Lord, saying, “Indeed, these are a criminal people.”
interpretation: Lut turned to Allah after his people persisted in grave wrongdoing, declaring their corruption and entrusting their matter to divine judgment and protection.

translation: “So set out with My servants by night; surely, you will be pursued.”
interpretation: Allah commands Moses to lead the believers away under cover of night, assuring them that Pharaoh’s forces will follow them, while implying that this pursuit is part of the unfolding of Allah’s decree and the eventual deliverance of His servants.

translation: “And leave the sea parted and still; indeed, they are an army destined to be drowned.”
interpretation: God commands Moses to move on without returning to the opened sea, assuring him that Pharaoh’s pursuing forces will enter it and be destroyed. The verse conveys that once God grants deliverance, the believer should proceed with trust rather than fear the power pursuing them.

translation: How many gardens and springs they left behind,
interpretation: The verse portrays the sudden downfall of a people who once lived amid abundant gardens and flowing springs, emphasizing that worldly prosperity cannot protect a nation from ruin when it rejects truth and persists in wrongdoing.

translation: and crops and noble dwellings,
interpretation: This portrays the abundant, prosperous life that the people had been granted—fertile lands and honorable places of residence—yet all of it was taken from them when they were destroyed because of their arrogance and wrongdoing.

translation: And delights in which they had been enjoying themselves.
interpretation: This describes the worldly luxury and pleasures that Pharaoh’s people possessed and enjoyed, which Allah removed from them when they persisted in arrogance and disbelief.

translation: Thus it was; and We made another people inherit them.
interpretation: This refers to the wealth, lands, dwellings, and authority of Pharaoh’s people: after their destruction, Allah transferred these blessings to another people as a consequence of their rejection and oppression.

translation: Neither the heaven nor the earth wept over them, nor were they given respite.
interpretation: When Pharaoh and his people were destroyed, they had no righteous deeds or honored standing that would cause heaven and earth to mourn their loss; instead, their punishment came without any further delay or reprieve.

translation: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment.
interpretation: Allah rescued the Children of Israel from Pharaoh’s degrading oppression, demonstrating that He protects the oppressed and can restore their dignity after severe persecution.

translation: From Pharaoh—indeed, he was arrogant and one of the transgressors.
interpretation: Pharaoh considered himself superior to others and exceeded all limits in oppression, tyranny, and disobedience to God.

translation: And We chose them knowingly above all the worlds.
interpretation: Allah favored the Children of Israel over the peoples of their time, selecting them with perfect knowledge of their qualities and appointing among them prophets and blessings; this distinction was a divine responsibility, not an unconditional guarantee of superiority regardless of their deeds.

translation: And We gave them signs in which was a clear trial.
interpretation: Allah granted them manifest miracles and blessings, thereby testing whether they would recognize His favor, obey Him, and remain grateful rather than turn away.

translation: Indeed, these people surely say,
interpretation: The verse introduces a false claim uttered with insistence by those being condemned, preparing to expose and refute their error.

translation: It is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This expresses the denial of those who reject resurrection: they claim that death occurs only once in this worldly life and that no one will be raised again for judgment.

translation: Then bring back our forefathers, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The deniers challenge the believers mockingly, demanding that their deceased ancestors be brought back to life as supposed proof of resurrection, thereby revealing their rejection and defiance rather than a sincere search for truth.

translation: Are they better, or the people of Tubbaʿ and those before them? We destroyed them, for they were criminals.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who reject the truth: despite their power and status, they are not superior to the mighty nations that came before them, including the people of Tubbaʿ. Those nations were destroyed when their persistent wrongdoing and denial made them deserving of punishment, showing that worldly strength cannot protect a people from divine judgment.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in play.
interpretation: Creation is not purposeless or a mere amusement; it has been brought into existence with wisdom and a serious purpose, so human beings should recognize their responsibility before God and not live heedlessly.

translation: We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The heavens and the earth were created with wisdom, purpose, and justice—not in vain or without meaning. Yet most people fail to recognize the divine purpose behind creation and therefore neglect the accountability and guidance it implies.

translation: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all.
interpretation: The verse establishes that every person will be gathered at a निश्चित, divinely appointed time when truth will be distinguished from falsehood and all will face their just judgment together.

translation: The Day when no protector can avail another protector in the least, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, worldly bonds, alliances, and sources of support will have no power to protect anyone from God’s judgment; each person will stand dependent on the truth of their own faith and deeds.

translation: Except those upon whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah’s mercy is the sole means of deliverance from punishment and ruin; although He possesses absolute power over all creation, His mercy reaches those whom He chooses to guide and save.

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqūm.
interpretation: This refers to the cursed tree in Hell, whose mention serves as a warning of the dreadful punishment prepared for those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing.

translation: The food of the sinful.
interpretation: It refers to the humiliating and agonizing nourishment prepared in the Hereafter for those who persist in grave sin and rebellion against Allah.

translation: Like molten metal, boiling in the bellies.
interpretation: It depicts the severe torment of the people of Hell: what they consume is like intensely heated molten substance, boiling within them and causing unbearable agony.

translation: Like the boiling of scalding water.
interpretation: This portrays the torment of the people of Hell as intensely painful and unbearable, likening it to violently boiling water.

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hellfire.
interpretation: هذا أمرٌ ملائكيٌّ بإذلال المجرم وسوقه قسرًا إلى قلب جهنم، جزاءً على عناده وكفره، حيث لا يستطيع الإفلات من العذاب.

translation: Then pour over his head the torment of scalding water.
interpretation: This depicts the severe and humiliating punishment awaiting the arrogant rejecter, whose torment encompasses him from above with burning water as a consequence of his defiance of the truth.

translation: “Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, noble one.”
interpretation: This is a humiliating rebuke in Hell, said mockingly to the arrogant person who had considered himself powerful and honored in the world; it exposes the false pride that led him to reject the truth.

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to doubt.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who denied the truth: what they once treated with uncertainty is now confronted as undeniable reality, leaving no room for doubt or escape.

translation: Indeed, the God-conscious will be in a secure place.
interpretation: Those who remain mindful of God and avoid disobedience will be granted a protected, peaceful abode in which they are safe from fear, harm, and every form of insecurity.

translation: In gardens and springs,
interpretation: This portrays Paradise as a place of flourishing gardens and abundant, pure springs, signifying lasting comfort, beauty, and divine reward.

translation: They will wear garments of fine silk and brocade, facing one another.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise in honored comfort and mutual fellowship, adorned with luxurious garments and seated together in harmony, free from estrangement or conflict.

translation: Thus, We will pair them with maidens of beautiful, wide eyes.
interpretation: This describes the reward prepared for the righteous in Paradise: companionship with pure and beautiful spouses, expressing the honor, joy, and perfect fulfillment they will experience there.

translation: They will call there for every kind of fruit, in safety.
interpretation: In Paradise, the believers will have unrestricted access to whatever fruits they desire, enjoying them in complete security, without fear of harm, loss, or deprivation.

translation: They will not taste death therein, except the first death; and He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: The people of Paradise will live in everlasting security and bliss, never experiencing death again. The mention of the first death refers to the death they underwent before entering Paradise, while God’s protection from Hell signifies complete deliverance from its punishment.

translation: As a bounty from your Lord; that is the supreme success.
interpretation: The believers’ attaining Paradise is not merely the result of their deeds, but a gracious gift from Allah. True success is therefore to receive His mercy and eternal blessing.

translation: We have only made it easy in your tongue so that they may take heed.
interpretation: Allah made the Qur’an accessible through the Prophet’s clear Arabic speech so that people could understand its guidance, reflect upon it, and allow its reminder to awaken them to faith and obedience.

translation: So wait; surely they are waiting.
interpretation: Remain steadfast and await God’s judgment and support, for those who reject the truth are also awaiting the outcome; ultimately, the matter will be decided in accordance with God’s promise.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm.
interpretation: Ḥā Mīm is one of the Qur’anic disjointed letter combinations whose full meaning is known only to Allah; its presence invites reflection on the divine origin and miraculous nature of the revelation.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: The Qur’an comes from Allah, whose absolute power guarantees its authority and whose perfect wisdom ensures that its guidance is true, purposeful, and suited to the needs of creation.

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: The order, harmony, and wonders evident throughout the heavens and the earth testify to Allah’s power, wisdom, and oneness; believers recognize these signs and let them strengthen their faith.

translation: And in your creation and in the creatures He has scattered throughout the earth are signs for people who are certain.
interpretation: The intricate design of human life and the diversity of living creatures testify to the wisdom, power, and purposeful governance of their Creator; those who seek certainty recognize these realities as evidence of God’s oneness and perfect knowledge.

translation: And in the alternation of night and day, and in the provision that Allah sends down from the sky, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and in the directing of the winds are signs for people who reason.
interpretation: The continual succession of night and day, the life-giving rain, and the varied movement of the winds reveal Allah’s power, wisdom, and sustaining mercy. Those who reflect on these ordered signs recognize that the One who revives barren earth is fully able to revive creation after death.

translation: These are the verses of Allah that We recite to you in truth. So, in what discourse after Allah and His verses will they believe?
interpretation: Since Allah’s revelation is the ultimate truth and the clearest proof, turning away from it leaves no sound foundation for faith; no later claim or human discourse can replace the guidance contained in His verses.

translation: Woe to every habitual liar and persistent sinner.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that those who repeatedly fabricate falsehood and persist in sinful conduct expose themselves to ruin and divine punishment.

translation: He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays a person whose rejection is not due to ignorance, but to deliberate arrogance: he hears Allah’s revelation clearly, yet behaves as though it has no authority over him. Such willful disregard of the truth warrants the severe punishment of the Hereafter.

translation: And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in mockery. For such people is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who respond to divine guidance with contempt and ridicule rather than reflection, warning that deliberate mockery of God’s signs leads to disgraceful punishment.

translation: Behind them is Hell, and whatever they have earned will avail them nothing, nor will those they have taken as protectors besides Allah benefit them. And for them is a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This warns that once they face the Hereafter, worldly gains and the false protectors they relied upon cannot shield them from Allah’s judgment; only sincere faith and righteous obedience would have been of lasting benefit.

translation: This is guidance; and those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord will have a painful punishment of torment.
interpretation: The revelation is a clear means of guidance, but those who knowingly reject God’s signs and refuse to follow the truth expose themselves to a severe and painful consequence in the Hereafter.

translation: Allah is the One who subjected the sea for you, so that ships may sail upon it by His command, and so that you may seek from His bounty, and so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: Allah reminds people that the sea and its forces are made accessible to them only through His sustaining command, enabling travel, livelihood, and the pursuit of beneficial provision. These blessings are meant to awaken sincere gratitude—expressed through recognizing His favor, obeying Him, and using what He has provided responsibly.

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—all from Him. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: God has made the resources and forces of the universe available for human benefit, not through human power alone but by His grace and provision. Their ordered availability points to His wisdom, unity, and mercy, and invites thoughtful people to recognize the Creator behind what they use and experience.

translation: قل للذين آمنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله ليجزي قوما بما كانوا يكسبون
interpretation: أي قل للمؤمنين أن يعفوا عمّن لا يتوقعون وقائع الله وعقابه، ولا يقابلوا أذاهم بالانتقام؛ فالحساب والجزاء عند الله، وهو يجازي كل إنسان بما عمل، مما يربي المؤمن على الحلم وترك التشفي مع بقاء العدل الإلهي محفوظًا.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: Every person bears the consequence of their own deeds: righteous actions benefit the one who performs them, while wrongdoing harms its perpetrator. Ultimately, all people will return to God for the final judgment of what they have done.

translation: And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, judgment, and prophethood, provided them with wholesome provisions, and favored them above all peoples.
interpretation: This verse reminds that Allah granted the Children of Israel immense blessings: revealed guidance, sound authority, prophetic leadership, lawful and good sustenance, and distinction among the nations of their time. These favors were a trust requiring gratitude and obedience, not a guarantee of permanent superiority independent of faithfulness to Allah.

translation: And We gave them clear evidence concerning the matter. They did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of mutual envy and transgression. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed.
interpretation: God granted the Children of Israel clear proofs and guidance, so their disagreement was not caused by lack of knowledge. Rather, rivalry, envy, and the desire to prevail led some of them to reject or distort what they knew to be true. This warns that knowledge benefits only when it is accompanied by sincerity and humility; otherwise, it can become a basis for dispute. The final judgment over such deliberate disagreements belongs to God, who will distinguish truth from falsehood and hold each person accountable for the motives behind their opposition.

translation: Then We placed you upon a clear way of the command, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to adhere firmly to the divinely revealed law and not let the uninformed opinions or desires of those lacking true knowledge divert him from it. The verse teaches that guidance must be based on revelation rather than speculation, custom, or the shifting inclinations of people.

translation: They will never avail you against Allah in any way. Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Protector of the mindful.
interpretation: بيّن الله أن اتباع أهل الباطل أو الاعتماد على نصرتهم لا يدفع عن الإنسان شيئًا من قضاء الله وعقابه؛ فهم يتناصرون على أساس الظلم، أما الحماية الحقيقية والنصرة الثابتة فهما من الله وحده لمن اتقاه واستقام على طاعته.

translation: This is clear insight for humanity, and guidance and mercy for people who are certain.
interpretation: The Qur’an opens the truth to human understanding, directing those who are convinced of it toward the right path and granting them mercy; its guidance bears fruit most fully in hearts that receive it with sincere certainty.

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them equal to those who believe and do righteous deeds—so that their lives and deaths are alike? Evil is the judgment they make.
interpretation: The verse condemns the assumption that persistent wrongdoing carries the same ultimate outcome as sincere faith and righteous action. God’s justice does not treat these opposing paths as equal, whether in their consequences during life or in the final return after death; believing otherwise is a grave error in judgment.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth and wisdom, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The ordered creation of the heavens and the earth is not without purpose; it points to a just moral order in which people are held accountable for their deeds. Allah’s judgment will give each person precisely what they deserve, without any loss, excess, or injustice.

translation: Have you considered the one who takes his own desire as his god, whom Allah lets go astray despite knowledge, seals his hearing and heart, and places a veil over his sight? Who, then, can guide him after Allah? Will you not reflect?
interpretation: The verse warns that when a person consistently follows desire instead of truth, desire becomes an object of devotion. Although he may possess knowledge, his persistent rejection and arrogance cause him to become deprived of guidance: he no longer listens with receptivity, understands with his heart, or sees the truth clearly. No one can guide such a person unless he turns back to Allah and becomes willing to accept guidance.

translation: They say, “There is nothing but our worldly life: we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time.” Yet they have no knowledge of this; they only speculate.
interpretation: They deny resurrection and reduce existence to the cycle of birth and death, attributing life’s end to the passage of time rather than to God’s decree. The verse exposes this as an unsubstantiated assumption, not a conclusion grounded in knowledge.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is to say, “Bring back our forefathers, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: They have no sound evidence against the truth of resurrection; instead, they challenge the believers to produce their dead ancestors, treating the delay of resurrection as proof against it and refusing to accept that God will bring all people back to life at the appointed time.

translation: Say, “Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you for the Day of Resurrection—there is no doubt about it; but most people do not know.”
interpretation: Allah alone possesses power over human existence: He brings people to life, ends their worldly lives, and will reunite them for certain judgment on the Day of Resurrection. The denial or ignorance of most people does not lessen the certainty of this promised gathering.

translation: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض، ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذٍ يخسر المبطلون.
interpretation: الملك والتدبير كله لله وحده، وعند قيام القيامة يظهر بطلان أهل الباطل ظهورًا لا يخفى، فيخسرون أعمالهم وأمانيهم ويُحرمون النجاة بسبب تكذيبهم واتباعهم للباطل.

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be summoned to its record: “Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.”
interpretation: يصور الله مشهد القيامة حين تجثو الأمم من شدة الهول والخضوع، وتُدعى كل أمة إلى سجل أعمالها الذي أحصى ما قدمته في الدنيا، ثم تُجازى بالعدل وفق أعمالها، فلا يضيع خير ولا يفلت شر.

translation: This is Our Record that speaks against you with the truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed all that you used to do.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the record of each person’s deeds will testify truthfully and without omission, leaving no room for denial or injustice; every action has been preserved by God’s command and will be presented as decisive evidence of how that person lived.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear success.
interpretation: True faith, expressed through righteous action, leads by God’s grace to His mercy and acceptance; this divine mercy is the unmistakable and ultimate success.

translation: As for those who disbelieved: “Were My verses not recited to you, yet you acted arrogantly and were a people given to sin?”
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who rejected faith despite having received clear divine revelation. Their condemnation is not due to lack of guidance, but to their proud refusal to accept the truth and their persistence in wrongdoing.

translation: And when it was said, “Indeed, Allah’s promise is true, and there is no doubt about the Hour,” you said, “We do not know what the Hour is. We can only make assumptions, and we are not convinced.”
interpretation: This portrays the attitude of those who reject resurrection: when confronted with the certainty of Allah’s promise and the coming Judgment, they respond with uncertainty and speculation rather than sincere reflection. Their lack of conviction is not based on sound evidence, but on a refusal to accept what lies beyond their immediate perception.

translation: The evil deeds they committed will become evident to them, and they will be encompassed by that which they used to mock.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the consequences of their wrongdoing will be exposed without concealment, and the punishment they once ridiculed will surround them completely, leaving them unable to escape it.

translation: And it will be said, “Today We will leave you, just as you neglected the meeting of this Day of yours. Your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment of those who denied the Hereafter: because they deliberately ignored accountability and failed to prepare for it, they will be abandoned to the Fire without protection or anyone able to save them. “We will leave you” does not mean forgetfulness, but that they will be deprived of mercy and aid in accordance with their own neglect.

translation: That is because you took Allah’s signs in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to seek pardon.
interpretation: Their punishment is portrayed as the consequence of deliberate contempt for divine revelation and being misled by worldly pleasures. Since they neither honored God’s signs nor turned back in repentance during life, their pleas for another chance will not be accepted in the Hereafter.

translation: So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: All praise is rightfully due to Allah alone, because He is the Lord, sustainer, and sovereign of every realm in the heavens and the earth and of all creation.

translation: To Him belongs all grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All greatness, majesty, and absolute authority belong solely to Allah throughout creation. Nothing shares in His exaltedness or sovereignty; He acts with irresistible power and perfect wisdom.

translation: Ḥā. Mīm.
interpretation: These are among the Qur’an’s disjointed opening letters; their precise meaning is known to Allah, while their appearance at the beginning calls attention to the revelation that is composed of ordinary Arabic letters yet remains beyond human imitation.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This affirms that the Qur’an is divinely revealed, originating from Allah whose absolute might guarantees its authority and whose perfect wisdom is reflected in every command, teaching, and guidance it contains.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever lies between them except in truth and for an appointed term. Yet those who disbelieve turn away from what they have been warned of.
interpretation: Creation is neither purposeless nor everlasting in its present form: it was brought forth according to divine wisdom and will remain until the time God has appointed. Therefore, rejecting the warnings about accountability and the final outcome is a deliberate turning away from the truth of existence and its ultimate purpose.

translation: Say: “Have you considered what you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth—or do they have any share in the heavens? Bring me a scripture revealed before this, or some surviving trace of knowledge, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges those who invoke other than Allah to provide real evidence for the power and divine status they attribute to such beings. Neither observable creation nor any revealed or trustworthy knowledge supports their claims; therefore, worship must not be based on imitation, assumption, or unsupported assertions, but on clear proof from Allah.

translation: And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of his call?
interpretation: This verse declares that directing worship and supplication to beings other than Allah is the height of misguidance, because those invoked possess neither the power nor the awareness to respond, and the one who relies on them is pursuing an object incapable of helping him.

translation: And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who were worshipped besides Allah will disown their worshippers and oppose them, declaring that they never accepted or approved of being worshipped. The verse warns that false objects of devotion cannot protect those who relied on them; instead, their worship will become a cause of mutual repudiation and loss.

translation: When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, “This is clearly magic.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the rejection of divine revelation by those who refuse to accept it: instead of considering the truth of the signs and their message, they dismiss them as magic, revealing their denial rather than any defect in the revelation itself.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say, “If I had fabricated it, you would have no power to protect me from Allah in any way. He knows best what you engage in. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: The verse answers the accusation of fabrication by placing the matter before Allah, whose knowledge encompasses all that people say and pursue. The Prophet’s confidence rests not on human defense but on Allah’s witnessing and judgment, while His mention as Forgiving and Merciful leaves the door open for those who abandon false accusations and turn back to Him.

translation: Say, “I am not unprecedented among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The Prophet ﷺ declares that his mission is consistent with the missions of earlier messengers and that he possesses no independent knowledge of the unseen or of the final outcome for himself or others. His role is to follow divine revelation faithfully and to warn people with unmistakable clarity, leaving judgment and ultimate consequences to Allah.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if this Qur’an is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, while a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to something like it and believes, yet you act arrogantly? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: The verse presents a decisive challenge to those who reject the Qur’an: if its message truly accords with the revelation known to the Children of Israel, then the testimony and faith of an informed witness from among them should expose the rejection of those who refuse it out of pride. Their lack of guidance is not due to a lack of evidence, but to persistent wrongdoing and arrogance.

translation: Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, “If it were something good, they would not have preceded us to it.” And since they have not been guided by it, they will say, “This is an ancient fabrication.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the arrogance of those who judge truth by social status and precedence rather than by its evidence. Because the believers accepted the revelation before them, they dismiss it out of envy and pride; when they fail to receive guidance from it, they wrongly label the Qur’an an old falsehood instead of examining their own refusal.

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and mercy. And this is a confirming Book, in an Arabic tongue, to warn those who do wrong and to give good tidings to those who excel in good.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as continuing the divine message given to Moses: it confirms the truth preserved in earlier revelation, while addressing its audience clearly in Arabic. Its warning is directed at those who persist in wrongdoing, whereas its promise of glad tidings belongs to those who respond to revelation by living righteously and doing good.

translation: Indeed, those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: True faith is not merely a statement; it is demonstrated by steadfastly living in obedience to Allah. Whoever remains firm upon this path is granted security from the fears of the Hereafter and comfort from the grief that troubles the believers.

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein forever, as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This affirms that those who attain Paradise will remain in it eternally, and that their enduring reward is granted in accordance with the righteous deeds they consistently performed.

translation: We have commanded the human being to show kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning together take thirty months. When he reaches full maturity and reaches forty years, he says, “My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds that please You, and make my offspring righteous for me. I have truly turned to You in repentance, and I am truly among those who submit.”
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the profound duty of honoring one’s parents, especially recognizing the mother’s sacrifices in pregnancy, childbirth, and nursing. It presents forty as a stage of mature awareness at which a person should consciously respond to divine blessings with gratitude, righteous action, sincere repentance, and concern for the spiritual well-being of future generations. True gratitude is therefore shown not merely in words, but by living in a way that pleases God, repairing one’s relationship with Him, and seeking that righteousness continue through one’s family.

translation: Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds; they will be among the companions of Paradise. This is the true promise they were promised.
interpretation: God promises that sincere believers who live righteously will have their good deeds accepted, while their faults are forgiven by His mercy. Their admission to Paradise is therefore the fulfillment of a certain and truthful promise that God had given them.

translation: And the one who says to his parents, “Fie upon you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth from the grave, when generations have already passed away before me?” While they seek Allah’s help, saying, “Woe to you! Believe; surely Allah’s promise is true.” But he says, “This is nothing but the legends of former peoples.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the destructive arrogance of a person who responds to his parents’ sincere call to faith with contempt and ridicule. His denial of resurrection is not presented as a reasoned conclusion, but as a rejection rooted in pride and attachment to inherited skepticism. The parents’ plea reveals both their compassion and their anguish: they call him to believe in Allah’s certain promise even as he dismisses it as ancient fables. Thus, the verse warns that contempt for truth and for those who lovingly call one to it can lead a person to deny realities merely because they lie beyond immediate experience.

translation: Those are the ones against whom the decree has taken effect, among nations that passed away before them, of jinn and humankind. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: They are condemned because they persisted in rejection and followed the path of earlier rebellious peoples from both jinn and humankind; by choosing that path, they incurred divine judgment and forfeited true success.

translation: ولكلٍّ درجاتٌ مما عملوا، وليوفيهم أعمالهم وهم لا يُظلمون.
interpretation: لكل إنسان منزلة ومقام يحددهما عمله، فيجازيه الله جزاءً كاملًا على ما قدّم، من غير أن ينقص من ثوابه أو يُحمَّل ما لم يعمل.

translation: And on the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, it will be said: “You exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; so today you will be repaid with the punishment of humiliation because you were arrogant on earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient.”
interpretation: The verse warns that when people devote themselves to worldly pleasures while rejecting God, acting arrogantly, and persisting in disobedience, those pleasures cannot benefit them in the Hereafter; instead, they will face humiliating punishment as a fitting consequence of their conduct.

translation: And remember the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people in the sand dunes, while warners had already come before him and after him: “Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.”
interpretation: This verse recalls Hūd, the prophet of the people of ʿĀd, who warned them in the region of al-Aḥqāf and called them to sincere worship of Allah alone. His message was not an isolated warning: messengers had repeatedly come to humanity before and after him with the same call. His fear for them expresses compassionate concern that their rejection of monotheism would lead to the grave punishment of the Day of Judgment.

translation: They said, “Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: They responded to the call to worship Allah alone with stubborn denial, viewing the abandonment of their false gods as deception and arrogantly challenging the promised punishment instead of considering the truth of the warning.

translation: He said, “Knowledge belongs only to Allah, and I convey to you what I have been sent with. But I see you as a people who act in ignorance.”
interpretation: The messenger makes clear that the timing and reality of the promised punishment are known only to Allah; his responsibility is solely to deliver the revelation faithfully. Their demand for immediate punishment does not reflect wisdom or strength, but ignorance expressed through arrogance, impatience, and disregard for divine warning.

translation: Then, when they saw it approaching their valleys as a cloud, they said, “This is a cloud bringing us rain.” Rather, it is what you sought to hasten—a wind containing a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays how the people of ʿĀd mistook the approaching sign of destruction for a blessing they desired. Their confident expectation of rain exposed their failure to recognize that divine punishment can arrive disguised as what appears beneficial, especially after they had defiantly demanded that it be brought swiftly.

translation: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and by morning nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We requite the wicked people.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming power of the divine punishment: when God’s decree came upon the people who persisted in wrongdoing, their strength and worldly possessions were swept away, leaving only their empty homes as evidence that they had once lived there. Their fate illustrates that persistent injustice ultimately brings a fitting recompense by God’s command.

translation: Indeed, We had established them in what We have not established you in; We gave them hearing, sight, and hearts, but neither their hearing, nor their sight, nor their hearts benefited them in the least, because they used to deny the signs of Allah. And what they used to mock encompassed them.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly strength and faculties are gifts whose value depends on accepting truth. Those people possessed the means to perceive and understand Allah’s signs, but their deliberate denial rendered those means useless; ultimately, the punishment they mocked became the very reality that overtook them.

translation: Indeed, We destroyed the towns around you, and We presented the signs in various ways so that they might return.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the ruin of earlier communities was not without warning: God repeatedly demonstrated the truth through clear and varied signs, giving people the opportunity to abandon wrongdoing and return to Him before punishment came.

translation: So why did the gods they took besides Allah as a means of seeking nearness not help them? Rather, they abandoned them. That was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: The verse exposes the failure of the false deities whom the people relied upon to draw nearer to Allah. When hardship came, those idols could neither protect nor assist their worshippers; instead, they disappeared from them. Their reliance on them was built on invented claims and baseless falsehood, not on any real power or proof.

translation: And when We directed a group of the jinn toward you to listen to the Qur’an, when they attended it, they said, “Listen attentively.” Then, when it was concluded, they turned back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse portrays how the Qur’an’s recitation deeply affected a group of jinn: they recognized its truth, listened with disciplined attention, and then assumed the responsibility of conveying its warning to their people. It teaches that sincere reception of revelation should lead not merely to personal conviction, but to faithfully guiding others toward awareness of God and accountability before Him.

translation: They said, “O our people, indeed we have heard a Scripture revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.”
interpretation: This verse conveys the testimony of a group who, having listened attentively to the Qur’an, recognized its continuity with the divine revelation given to Moses and its confirmation of the enduring truths in earlier scripture. Their words show that genuine recognition of revelation leads to calling others toward the truth and a way of life characterized by sound belief, upright conduct, and clear guidance.

translation: O our people, respond to Allah’s caller and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is the earnest call of those who recognized the truth to their people: accept the Messenger who invites you to Allah and affirm his message. Faith and obedience become a means of receiving Allah’s forgiveness and being saved from the punishment that awaits those who reject the truth.

translation: Whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah cannot escape Him on earth, nor will they have protectors besides Him. Such people are in clear error.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting Allah’s call does not enable anyone to evade His power or accountability. Those who turn away will find no true protector or refuge apart from Him, and their refusal is a manifest departure from the path of truth.

translation: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by creating them, is surely able to give life to the dead? Yes indeed; He has power over all things.
interpretation: The creation of the immense heavens and earth, accomplished without weakness or exhaustion, is evidence that resurrection is entirely within Allah’s power. The One who originated creation without any limitation can restore life after death, for nothing is beyond His absolute power.

translation: And on the Day those who disbelieved are presented before the Fire, it will be said, “Is this not the truth?” They will say, “Yes, by our Lord.” He will say, “Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when denial can no longer be sustained: those who rejected the truth will be compelled to acknowledge its reality, yet this acknowledgment comes only after judgment and cannot avert the consequence of their persistent disbelief.

translation: So be patient, as those messengers endowed with resolve were patient, and do not seek to hasten the punishment for them. On the Day they see what they have been promised, it will seem to them as though they had remained only an hour of a day. This is a proclamation. So who is destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ to remain steadfast and not be distressed by the unbelievers’ rejection or wish that their promised punishment be hastened. The trials of worldly life are brief when viewed from the certainty of the Hereafter, and the final ruin belongs only to those who persistently abandon obedience and defy God’s truth.

translation: Those who disbelieve and hinder others from the path of Allah—He has rendered their deeds fruitless.
interpretation: Disbelief combined with actively obstructing people from divine guidance deprives one’s actions of their true benefit and reward, so their efforts ultimately lead to no lasting good.

translation: And those who believe, do righteous deeds, and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad—and it is the truth from their Lord—He will erase their sins and set their affairs right.
interpretation: True faith is demonstrated through righteous action and sincere acceptance of the revelation brought by Muhammad. Because they combine belief with obedience, Allah removes the effects of their sins through His forgiveness and brings well-being, guidance, and soundness to their inner and outward affairs.

translation: ذلك لأن الذين كفروا اتبعوا الباطل، وأن الذين آمنوا اتبعوا الحق من ربهم؛ وكذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم.
interpretation: يبين الله أن اختلاف حال الناس ومصيرهم ناشئ عن اختلاف ما يتبعونه: فالكافر يختار الباطل المبني على الوهم والضلال، والمؤمن يتبع الحق الذي أنزله الله وهدى إليه؛ وبالأمثال يوضح الله للناس عاقبة كل طريق ليعتبروا ويهتدوا.

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve in battle, strike their necks until you have thoroughly subdued them, then bind them firmly. Thereafter, either release them graciously or ransom them, until the war lays down its burdens. That is the command. Had Allah willed, He could have overcome them Himself, but He tests some of you through others. As for those who are killed in Allah’s way, He will never let their deeds go to waste.
interpretation: This verse regulates conduct during an actual armed conflict: once the opposing force has been decisively subdued, captives are to be secured and then dealt with through release by grace or ransom, rather than treated as objects of vengeance. The continuation of war is limited until its burdens are laid down, while the verse reminds believers that victory is a test and that those who sacrifice their lives in Allah’s cause will have their sincere deeds preserved and rewarded.

translation: He will guide them and set their affairs right.
interpretation: Allah will lead them to what is right, grant them steadfastness, and bring their spiritual and worldly condition into harmony and well-being.

translation: And He will admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: God will honor the believers who sacrifice for His cause by admitting them into Paradise, whose blessings and dwelling places He has already made familiar to them and prepared for them.

translation: O you who believe, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.
interpretation: Supporting Allah means upholding His faith through sincere obedience, defending truth and justice, and remaining steadfast in worship and conduct. Whoever gives such support is granted divine help, strength, and firmness when facing trials and opposition.

translation: As for those who disbelieve, misery is theirs, and He has rendered their deeds futile.
interpretation: Their persistent rejection of the truth leads to ruin, and the works they rely upon lose their value because they are not founded on faith and obedience to God.

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: Their rejection and aversion to divine revelation revealed their lack of sincere faith; therefore, the deeds they relied upon had no spiritual worth or reward before Allah.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those who came before them? Allah brought destruction upon them, and the disbelievers will have similar consequences.
interpretation: The verse urges people to learn from the ruins and fate of earlier peoples who rejected the truth: their destruction was not accidental, but a consequence of persistent disbelief and wrongdoing. Those who follow the same path should not assume that they will be exempt from the consequences of their rejection.

translation: That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, while the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: Allah grants the believers His care, guidance, and support, whereas those who reject Him are deprived of any true protector who can ultimately save or aid them.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. As for those who disbelieve, they enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire will be their abode.
interpretation: The verse contrasts two ways of life and their ultimate outcomes: faith joined with righteous action leads to lasting bliss, while disbelief reduces a person’s purpose to temporary worldly enjoyment, like an animal’s concern with eating and pleasure, without regard for accountability. The Fire is described as the final dwelling of those who persist in that rejection.

translation: How many a town was mightier in strength than your town, which drove you out? We destroyed them, and they had no helper.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who oppose the Prophet and reject the truth: worldly power and strength cannot protect a people from God’s judgment when they persist in oppression and disbelief. The fate of earlier, mightier nations shows that when divine punishment comes, no ally or protector can avert it.

translation: أفمن كان على بيّنةٍ من ربه كمن زُيِّن له سوء عمله واتبعوا أهواءهم؟
interpretation: ليس من استنار قلبه بدليلٍ من ربه واستقام على الحق كمن أُلبس عليه قبح عمله حتى رآه حسنًا، فصار تابعًا لهواه؛ فالفارق بينهما هو البصيرة التي تهدي إلى الحق والهوى الذي يزيّن الباطل.

translation: The description of the Paradise promised to the mindful is that in it are rivers of water that never becomes stagnant, rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine delightful to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey. They will have every kind of fruit therein, as well as forgiveness from their Lord. Is such a person like one who will abide forever in the Fire and be given scalding water that tears apart their intestines?
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as the lasting fulfillment of every wholesome delight, joined with the greater blessing of forgiveness from God. Its pure, unchanging rivers contrast sharply with the painful drink of Hell, showing that the fate of those who accept righteousness and those who persist in rejection cannot be considered equal.

translation: Among them are those who listen to you until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge, “What did he say just now?” They are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and they follow their desires.
interpretation: The verse describes people who hear revelation outwardly but do not listen with sincerity or seek to understand it; their dismissive question reveals indifference and mockery. Because they persistently reject the truth and give precedence to their desires, their hearts become sealed from benefiting by guidance.

translation: As for those who are rightly guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their God-consciousness.
interpretation: Those who sincerely follow the truth are given further clarity and steadfastness by God; their obedience opens the way to deeper guidance and strengthens their awareness of Him.

translation: Do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come. But how will their admonition benefit them when it comes to them?
interpretation: The verse warns those who persist in denial that the Final Hour will not wait for their readiness; its preceding signs are already evident, yet once its reality arrives, regret and recognition will no longer benefit them because the opportunity to believe and act has already passed.

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah, and seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. Allah knows your movements and your resting place.
interpretation: The verse establishes sincere knowledge of Allah’s oneness as the foundation of faith, joined with continual repentance and seeking forgiveness for oneself and the believing community. It also reminds that Allah fully knows every person’s activities and every place of return, so one should live with humility, vigilance, and accountability before Him.

translation: Those who believe say, “Why has no sūrah been revealed?” But when a clear sūrah is revealed and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those whose hearts are diseased looking at you with the look of one overcome by death. So woe to them.
interpretation: The verse contrasts sincere believers, who await divine guidance with readiness, with hypocrites whose hidden fear and weakness become exposed when obedience requires real sacrifice. Their death-like stare reveals that their professed faith has not produced willing submission, and therefore they face humiliation and ruin.

translation: Obedience and good words. Then, when the matter is decided, if they were true to Allah, it would be better for them.
interpretation: True faith is shown not by promises or agreeable speech alone, but by sincere obedience when action becomes necessary. Once a divine command is firmly established, remaining faithful to Allah and carrying it out is better for a person than hesitation, reluctance, or insincere words.

translation: So, if you were to turn away, would you then spread corruption throughout the land and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: The verse warns that abandoning obedience to God may lead people to corruption, oppression, and the destruction of family bonds. It exposes the contradiction of claiming faith while neglecting justice and severing the relationships that God has commanded people to preserve.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their eyes.
interpretation: Because they persistently reject the truth and sever the ties Allah commands them to uphold, they are deprived of the willingness to hear guidance and the insight to recognize it; this is a punishment that confirms the consequences of their deliberate resistance.

translation: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها
interpretation: في الآية توبيخ لمن يعرض عن تدبر القرآن، وبيان أن الإعراض قد يكون بسبب قسوة القلب وانغلاقه عن قبول الحق، فهي دعوة إلى فتح القلب والتفكر في هداية القرآن.

translation: Indeed, those who turned back after guidance had become clear to them—Satan enticed them and filled them with false hopes.
interpretation: This warns that knowingly abandoning the truth after recognizing it is not merely a momentary lapse; it is the result of allowing Satan to beautify deviation and prolong one’s hopes, thereby making repentance and return seem unnecessary or easy to postpone.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah had revealed, “We will obey you in some matters.” And Allah knows their secret conversations.
interpretation: Their hypocrisy led them to ally themselves with those who rejected divine revelation, promising to follow them in certain matters while concealing their true intentions. Yet no private agreement or hidden motive escapes Allah’s knowledge, and this warning exposes the danger of compromising revealed truth for the sake of worldly allegiance.

translation: So how will it be when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who persist in disbelief and rebellion will meet a humiliating and painful death: the angels will seize their souls while striking them from every direction, as a manifestation of divine punishment and disgrace.

translation: That is because they followed what displeased Allah and disliked His approval, so He rendered their deeds fruitless.
interpretation: Their deliberate preference for actions that incur Allah’s displeasure, together with their aversion to obedience and divine approval, deprived their deeds of acceptance and reward.

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will never reveal their spite?
interpretation: This is a warning to hypocrites who conceal hatred and hostility toward the truth: Allah will expose what they hide in their hearts through their words, actions, and trials, so their inner malice cannot remain concealed from Him.

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would recognize them by their marks. And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: Allah informs the Prophet that He could have exposed the hypocrites plainly, but instead gives indications by which their inner reality may be discerned: their expressions, conduct, and especially the evasive or revealing manner of their speech. Their hidden intentions are never hidden from Allah, who fully knows and will judge all their actions.

translation: We will certainly test you until We make evident those among you who strive and those who remain steadfast, and We will reveal the truth about your deeds.
interpretation: Allah tests people through hardship and responsibility so that their sincere striving and patience become manifest in their actions, exposing the reality of their conduct and claims.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, hinder others from the path of Allah, and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them will never harm Allah in the least; and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse warns that knowingly rejecting the truth and obstructing people from following it—especially while opposing the Messenger after the guidance is evident—does not diminish Allah’s authority or cause Him any loss. Rather, such defiance destroys the value of the deeds they relied upon, because actions performed in persistent opposition to revealed guidance are deprived of their accepted reward.

translation: O believers, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds.
interpretation: True faith requires sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger; acts of worship and righteousness must not be ruined by disobedience, disbelief, hypocrisy, or conduct that strips them of their reward.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and hindered others from the way of Allah, then died while they were disbelievers—Allah will never forgive them.
interpretation: Those who knowingly reject faith and actively prevent others from following Allah’s guidance, persisting in that state until death, have forfeited forgiveness because they died without repentance or belief; their deliberate opposition to truth and obstruction of others’ faith leads to an irrevocable judgment.

translation: So do not falter and call for peace while you are the ones in the stronger position; Allah is with you, and He will not deprive you of the reward of your deeds.
interpretation: The verse urges believers not to abandon their rightful firmness or seek peace from a position of fear and weakness when they possess the strength to uphold justice. It reassures them that Allah supports them and that none of their sincere efforts and sacrifices will be diminished or left unrewarded.

translation: The life of this world is only play and amusement. If you believe and are mindful of Allah, He will grant you your rewards and will not ask you for all your wealth.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly pursuits, when treated as the ultimate purpose, are fleeting and trivial; lasting value comes through faith and God-consciousness. Allah’s command to give from one’s wealth is not meant to strip people of everything, but to guide them toward righteousness without undue hardship.

translation: If He were to ask you for it and press you, you would withhold, and He would bring out your grudges.
interpretation: God does not burden people by demanding all their wealth, for excessive demands would reveal their reluctance and the resentment concealed within their hearts; the verse exposes human stinginess and calls for sincere generosity rather than giving accompanied by inner resistance.

translation: Here you are, being called to spend in the way of Allah; yet among you are those who withhold. Whoever withholds does so only against himself. Allah is Self-Sufficient, while you are the needy. If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you.
interpretation: Allah calls believers to give generously for His cause, not because He needs their wealth, but because they need the spiritual benefit of obedience and generosity. Refusing to give harms only the one who withholds, since Allah is independent of all creation. Persistent rejection of this duty may lead to a people who are more willing to obey and sacrifice, while those who turn away lose their distinction and opportunity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We have granted you a clear triumph.
interpretation: Allah announces to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that He has opened for him a manifest victory—one whose truth and consequences will become unmistakably clear—thereby assuring him of divine support and the success of his mission.

translation: So that Allah may forgive you for what preceded of your sin and what followed, complete His blessing upon you, and guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah’s complete favor upon the Prophet ﷺ: He grants him forgiveness, perfects His blessings upon him, and firmly guides him along the straight path. It teaches that divine forgiveness, blessing, and guidance are interconnected gifts through which Allah honors His chosen servants and enables them to fulfill their mission. يعلم

translation: And Allah will grant you a mighty victory.
interpretation: Allah promises the Prophet ﷺ powerful and enduring support through which his mission will prevail, making clear that true victory comes from Allah alone.

translation: He is the One who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they may increase in faith upon their faith. To Allah belong the forces of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah grants believers inner calm and steadfastness, especially in moments of trial, and this tranquility strengthens the faith they already possess. The unseen and visible forces of the universe are under His command, so the believers can trust that His wise and perfect knowledge governs every outcome.

translation: That He may admit the believing men and believing women into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever, and absolve them of their sins. That, in the sight of Allah, is a supreme triumph.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن من أعظم ثمرات الإيمان الصادق دخول الجنة والخلود في نعيمها، مع مغفرة الذنوب ومحو آثارها بفضل الله. وقد خصّت الآية الرجال والنساء معًا لتقرر شمول وعد الله لكل مؤمن ومؤمنة، وأن الفوز الحقيقي ليس في متاع الدنيا الزائل، بل في رضوان الله والنجاة يوم القيامة.

translation: And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who hold evil assumptions about Allah. Upon them is the turn of evil; Allah is angry with them, has condemned them, and has prepared Hell for them—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse warns that hypocrisy and associating partners with Allah are deepened by harboring false and evil beliefs about Him, such as doubting His wisdom, truthfulness, or promise. Those who persist in such attitudes expose themselves to Allah’s anger, rejection, and the ultimate punishment of Hell.

translation: To Allah belong the forces of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah has complete authority over every power and means of support in creation, whether visible or unseen. Nothing can resist His decree, and His might is always exercised with perfect wisdom.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: God sent the Prophet Muhammad to testify to the truth before humanity, to bring hope of God’s mercy and reward to those who believe and obey, and to warn those who reject the truth of the consequences of their denial.

translation: So that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, support him, honor him, and glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: True faith is expressed by standing with the Messenger, treating him with due reverence, and devoting continual glorification to Allah at all times, both early and late.

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah. Allah’s hand is above their hands. So whoever breaks the pledge does so only to his own detriment; and whoever fulfills the covenant he made with Allah, He will grant him a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse presents the believers’ pledge to the Messenger as a solemn covenant with Allah Himself: their loyalty, obedience, and commitment are not merely directed toward a human leader but are acts of devotion to God. “Allah’s hand is above their hands” signifies His authority, support, and confirmation over their pledge, while the warning makes clear that betrayal harms only the betrayer. Those who remain faithful to their covenant will receive an immense reward from Allah.

translation: Those of the desert Arabs who stayed behind will say to you, “Our possessions and families kept us occupied, so ask forgiveness for us.” They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, “Who can avail you against Allah in anything if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you?” Rather, Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse exposes the excuse of those who abandoned the believers: their claim of being prevented by family and property was not sincere, as shown by their request for forgiveness without genuine repentance. It teaches that worldly circumstances cannot protect a person from Allah’s decree or secure His favor; benefit and harm are entirely in His control, and He knows the truth behind every outward claim and action.

translation: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made pleasing in your hearts. You harbored evil suspicions and were a people destined for ruin.
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who, because of their weak faith and mistrust, assumed that the Messenger and the believers would be defeated and never come back. Their pessimistic expectations became attractive to them, revealing a corrupt inner outlook; by persisting in such evil assumptions and failing to trust God’s promise, they placed themselves among those who are spiritually ruined.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse warns that rejecting faith in Allah and His Messenger leads to the punishment of Hell, which Allah has prepared for those who persist in disbelief.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: All creation is under Allah’s absolute authority, and His judgment is governed by perfect wisdom rather than human entitlement. His power to punish is real, yet His forgiveness and mercy remain continually open to those who turn to Him sincerely.

translation: Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out to take spoils: “Let us follow you.” They wish to change the word of Allah. Say: “You shall not follow us; thus Allah said before.” Then they will say: “Rather, you envy us.” No indeed, they scarcely understand.
interpretation: This verse exposes the insincerity of those who held back from the believers’ difficult expedition but sought to share in its gains once success appeared likely. Their request was not accepted because the divine command had already distinguished the sincere from the opportunistic. Their accusation of envy reveals their failure to understand that obedience to Allah’s decree—not personal preference or material advantage—is what governs the believers’ conduct.

translation: Say to those of the Bedouins who stayed behind: “You will be called to face a people of great military strength; you will fight them, or they will submit. If you obey, Allah will grant you a good reward; but if you turn away as you did before, He will punish you with a painful punishment.”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who held back from the believers’ cause and reveals that genuine faith is proven by responding when sacrifice and danger are required. Their future invitation to confront a formidable enemy is a test of sincerity: obedience brings Allah’s reward, while repeating their earlier refusal exposes their hypocrisy and incurs punishment.

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: Allah excuses those whose physical conditions prevent them from fulfilling duties that require physical ability, while obedience remains the path to His reward. The promise and warning apply to everyone: sincere obedience leads to Paradise, whereas deliberate rejection of Allah and His Messenger brings painful punishment.

translation: Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you beneath the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah’s approval of the believers who pledged themselves to the Prophet ﷺ with sincere hearts, despite the uncertainty and tension surrounding their situation. Because Allah knew their sincerity and steadfastness, He granted them inner peace and promised them an imminent victory, showing that sincere faith and loyalty are met with divine reassurance and support.

translation: And abundant spoils that they will take. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This indicates that God would grant the believers material gains in addition to victory, but that these blessings come by His power and wisdom, not merely through human effort or worldly causes.

translation: Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will take. He has hastened this one for you, restrained the hands of people from you, and made it a sign for the believers, and to guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: Allah reassures the believers that their success and material gains are part of His promise, while the immediate victory and His protection from their enemies demonstrate His support. These blessings are meant to strengthen their faith, direct them toward steadfast obedience, and lead them along the straight path.

translation: And other gains which you were not able to attain—Allah has encompassed them. And Allah is over all things powerful.
interpretation: يشير الله إلى مكاسب وفتوحات لم يكن المسلمون قادرين على بلوغها في ذلك الوقت، لكنه أحاط بها علمًا وقدرةً، وهيأ أسباب تحققها في المستقبل؛ فالعجز البشري لا يحدّ من قدرة الله، ولا يعجزه شيء.

translation: And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would surely have turned their backs and then found neither a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: Allah assures the believers that, had the disbelievers engaged them in battle, they would have been defeated and fled, with no one able to protect them or provide them support against Allah’s decree.

translation: Such is Allah’s established way, which has prevailed in the past; and you will never find any change in Allah’s established way.
interpretation: Allah’s judgments and laws operate with unwavering consistency: those who persist in opposing His truth and harming His messengers will inevitably face the consequences He has ordained, and no one can alter this divine pattern.

translation: And He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after He had granted you victory over them. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse reminds believers that the peaceful restraint at Mecca was a divine act of protection and mercy: although victory had placed them in a position to retaliate, God prevented further bloodshed and showed that true victory includes self-control and obedience to His guidance. Nothing they did in that encounter was hidden from Him.

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and prevented the sacrificial animals from reaching their appointed place. Had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know, and whom you might have trampled, thereby incurring blame on their account unknowingly, matters would have been decided differently. This was so that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills.
