Had the believers been clearly separated from the disbelievers, We would have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment.
interpretation: Allah explains that the believers were prevented from entering Makkah not because they lacked the right to worship, but through the hostility of those who rejected faith. Yet He restrained immediate punishment because unknown believers were living among the opponents, and any attack could have harmed them unintentionally. This shows that divine mercy may delay judgment in order to protect the innocent and open a path for people to enter His mercy, while also warning that deliberate rejection and oppression will not escape accountability.

translation: When those who disbelieved filled their hearts with arrogant zeal—the zeal of the Age of Ignorance—Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the believers, and made them hold firmly to the word of piety. They were most deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse contrasts the hostile arrogance of the disbelievers with the calm, disciplined faith granted to the Messenger and the believers. Their adherence to the word of piety reflects sincere submission to Allah, self-restraint, and conduct grounded in truth rather than tribal pride or ignorant passion; this moral and spiritual state made them worthy of Allah’s support and guidance.

translation: Allah has truly fulfilled His Messenger’s vision in truth: you will certainly enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved or your hair shortened, without fear. He knew what you did not know, and before that He granted a near victory.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that the Prophet’s vision would come to pass, even though its fulfillment would be delayed. Their eventual entry into the Sacred Mosque would occur peacefully and safely, with the rites of pilgrimage completed, while the immediate treaty and opening that preceded it were already part of Allah’s wise plan. It teaches that divine promises are certain, although their timing and the path to their fulfillment may exceed human understanding.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may cause it to prevail over every religion. And sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the Messenger’s guidance and the true religion he brought will ultimately be made manifest and prevail over all rival beliefs and ways of life. This promise rests on Allah’s authority and testimony, which are sufficient to establish the truth of the Messenger’s mission.

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him are firm against the disbelievers, compassionate toward one another. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the أثر of prostration. That is their description in the Torah; and their description in the Gospel is like a seed that produces its shoot, then strengthens it, making it grow thick and stand upright upon its stalk, delighting the sowers, so that through them He may enrage the disbelievers. Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a tremendous reward.
interpretation: This verse portrays the Prophet’s companions as a community whose strength is directed toward defending faith and whose relationships with one another are founded on mercy. Their repeated worship is driven not by appearance or worldly recognition but by sincere longing for Allah’s favor, and this devotion becomes visible in their character and conduct. The imagery of the growing plant signifies that the believing community develops from a small beginning into a strong, balanced, and fruitful body, whose vitality fulfills Allah’s promise and frustrates those who oppose the truth; the promised forgiveness and immense reward belong to those among them who combine faith with righteous action.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who believe, do not put yourselves ahead of Allah and His Messenger, and be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: Believers are instructed not to make religious judgments, decisions, or demands before guidance from Allah and His Messenger, nor to place their own opinions above revealed instruction. True piety requires humility, obedience, and careful adherence to divine guidance, knowing that Allah hears what they say and knows the intentions behind their actions.

translation: O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor address him loudly as you address one another, lest your deeds become void while you are unaware.
interpretation: Believers are instructed to show the Prophet ﷺ the highest level of respect and humility in speech and conduct. This warning teaches that even outwardly ordinary behavior can become spiritually destructive when it reflects disregard for the dignity of God’s Messenger; sincere faith therefore requires reverence, restraint, and careful manners when addressing him.

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested and prepared for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: True reverence for the Messenger is shown through humility and respectful conduct, and this outward restraint reflects hearts refined by Allah for sincere piety. Such people are promised forgiveness for their shortcomings and an immense reward.

translation: Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers—most of them do not understand.
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who addressed the Prophet ﷺ loudly and impatiently from outside his private quarters, showing disregard for his dignity and proper etiquette. Their behavior reflected a lack of sound judgment, teaching believers to approach others respectfully, patiently, and with awareness of personal boundaries.

translation: Had they been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This teaches that believers should honor the Prophet’s position and exercise patience rather than calling out to him impatiently from outside his private quarters. Such restraint reflects proper respect and obedience, while Allah’s mention of His forgiveness and mercy shows that sincere repentance and improved conduct are met with pardon.

translation: O you who believe, if a transgressor brings you news, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and then become regretful for what you have done.
interpretation: Believers are commanded not to act on reports without establishing their truth, especially when the source is morally unreliable. Careful verification protects people from unjust harm and protects the community from the remorse that follows decisions made in ignorance.

translation: And know that Allah’s Messenger is among you. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would surely suffer hardship. But Allah has made faith beloved to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to you. Those are the rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse teaches the believers to trust the Prophet’s judgment rather than allowing impulsive opinions or unverified demands to direct communal affairs. Their sound guidance is a divine gift: genuine faith becomes inwardly cherished, while disbelief and sinful rebellion become repugnant, enabling them to act with wisdom, restraint, and obedience.

translation: As a favor from Allah and a blessing; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: Faith and obedience are gifts granted through Allah’s grace and blessing, not achievements independent of Him; He knows who is deserving of guidance and wisely bestows His favor.

translation: And if two groups of believers fight one another, reconcile between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the transgressing group until it returns to the command of Allah. If it returns, reconcile between them fairly and act justly. Surely Allah loves those who uphold justice.
interpretation: This verse establishes that preserving peace and justice is a collective responsibility among believers: conflict must first be met with sincere reconciliation, but aggression must be restrained when necessary until the aggressor ceases and returns to lawful conduct. Once hostilities end, reconciliation must be restored without favoritism, and justice must govern the resolution, because true communal harmony depends not merely on ending the fighting but on correcting oppression and treating both sides fairly.

translation: The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers, and be mindful of Allah so that you may be shown mercy.
interpretation: Faith creates a bond of brotherhood that requires believers to reconcile disputes rather than deepen them; seeking peace and maintaining reverence for Allah are means of attaining His mercy.

translation: O you who believe, let not one people mock another people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women mock other women; perhaps they may be better than them. Do not defame one another, nor call one another by insulting nicknames. Wretched is the name of wickedness after faith. Whoever does not repent—those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the dignity of every believer and forbids contempt, ridicule, humiliation, slander, and hurtful labels, because outward status or appearance does not reveal a person’s true worth before God. Believers are therefore commanded to guard one another’s honor, and persistent abuse after knowing this command is an act of wrongdoing unless one sincerely repents.

translation: O you who believe, avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin. Do not spy on one another, nor backbite one another. Would any of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. And be mindful of Allah; surely Allah is Most Relenting, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to protect the dignity and brotherhood of others by refusing to treat unverified suspicions as facts, refraining from investigating people’s private affairs, and not mentioning them in their absence with words they would dislike. Backbiting is portrayed as abhorrent as eating the flesh of a dead brother: it violates the honor of someone unable to defend himself and corrupts the bonds of the community. The call to God-consciousness also leaves the door open to repentance, for Allah forgives those who abandon these harms and sincerely return to Him.

translation: O humanity, We created you from a male and a female, and made you peoples and tribes so that you may come to know one another. Surely, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the most God-conscious of you. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse teaches that human diversity in origin and communities is meant to foster mutual recognition and understanding, not pride, prejudice, or domination. Since all people share the same human origin, distinctions of race, ethnicity, lineage, and social group do not make one person superior to another; true honor before Allah belongs only to the one whose conduct reflects the deepest awareness of Him and the greatest integrity. Allah alone fully knows the sincerity and reality of each person’s character.

translation: The Bedouins say, “We have believed.” Say, “You have not believed; rather say, ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything from your deeds. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse distinguishes between outward submission and the inward reality of faith. A person may enter the community and comply outwardly without faith having yet become firmly rooted in the heart; therefore, claiming complete faith requires sincerity and inner conviction, not merely words or affiliation. Yet the verse does not close the door to spiritual growth: sincere obedience to Allah and His Messenger leads toward genuine faith, and Allah, in His forgiveness and mercy, does not disregard the good deeds of those who strive to obey Him.

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then do not doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. It is they who are truthful.
interpretation: True faith is shown not merely by words, but by firm conviction free from doubt and sincere sacrifice in obedience to Allah. Those who devote their possessions and lives to His cause, according to His guidance, demonstrate that their claim of faith is genuine.

translation: Say, “Do you inform Allah about your religion, while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? And Allah has knowledge of all things.”
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who present their professed faith as though they are informing Allah of something He does not know. True faith is not a claim made for Allah’s benefit; He fully knows what is outwardly declared and what is sincerely held within, and nothing about a person’s belief or conduct is hidden from Him.

translation: They consider it a favor to you that they have submitted. Say, “Do not consider your submission a favor to me; rather, Allah has favored you by guiding you to faith, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: True faith is not a favor that people confer upon the Messenger or upon Allah; it is Allah’s favor upon them, because He enabled them to recognize the truth and guided their hearts to believe. Therefore, claiming superiority or expecting credit for embracing Islam contradicts sincere faith, which should produce humility and gratitude to Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: لا يخفى على الله شيءٌ مما استتر في السماوات والأرض، ولا تخفى عليه أعمال الناس ونياتهم؛ ولذلك ينبغي للإنسان أن يراقب الله في السر والعلن، موقنًا بأن أعماله كلها معلومة لديه ومجازى عليها.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an.
interpretation: Allah swears by the Qur’an in all its majesty and perfection, affirming its truth, divine origin, and authoritative message. “Qaf” is one of the mysterious disjoined letters whose full meaning is known to Allah.

translation: Rather, they were astonished that a warner from among themselves had come to them, so the disbelievers said, “This is something astonishing.”
interpretation: The disbelievers rejected the message not because it was unclear, but because they found it astonishing that God would choose an ordinary human from among them to warn them and call them to faith. Their amazement reflected arrogant denial of revelation rather than a sincere search for truth.

translation: “When we have died and become dust, shall we be brought back? That is a far-fetched return.”
interpretation: The disbelievers reject resurrection because they consider restoration after bodily decay impossible, revealing their denial of God’s power to recreate them after death.

translation: We certainly know what the earth consumes of them, and with Us is a preserved record.
interpretation: Allah affirms that nothing of a person’s body is lost from His knowledge after death, even what the earth decomposes and absorbs. Every detail remains recorded and preserved with Him, demonstrating His complete knowledge and power to resurrect people and hold them accountable.

translation: Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused and contradictory state.
interpretation: Their rejection was not caused by a lack of clarity in the truth, but by refusing to accept it when it was presented to them; consequently, they remain trapped in doubt, inconsistency, and disorder of thought.

translation: أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج
interpretation: أفلا يتأمل هؤلاء المكذبون السماء المرفوعة فوقهم، فيرون إحكام خلقها وجمال تزيينها وخلوَّها من الخلل والتصدع، فيستدلون بذلك على قدرة الله ووحدانيته وكمال تدبيره، ويوقنون بإمكان البعث؟

translation: And the earth We have spread out, placed upon it firm mountains, and caused every delightful kind of plant to grow in it.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection on the earth’s carefully ordered design: its vastness, its stabilizing mountains, and the abundance and beauty of its living growth all point to the wisdom, power, and generosity of its Creator.

translation: An insight and a reminder for every servant who turns to God.
interpretation: The signs of divine power are meant to awaken understanding and renew the heart’s awareness, benefiting those who sincerely return to God in repentance and obedience.

translation: And We sent down from the sky blessed water, then We brought forth by it gardens and grain to be harvested.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection on rain as a blessing from God: through water He revives the earth and produces varied plants and nourishment, demonstrating His power, mercy, and provision.

translation: And lofty date palms, bearing neatly clustered blossoms and fruit.
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the date palms rising high and producing their fruit in ordered clusters, presenting their growth and fruitful abundance as a clear sign of Allah’s wisdom, power, and ability to bring life and provision from the earth.

translation: As provision for the servants, and We revive with it a dead land. Thus will be the emergence.
interpretation: Just as Allah brings barren land to life through rain and makes it a source of sustenance, He will likewise bring people back to life after death for the Resurrection.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah, the inhabitants of the Well, and Thamud denied the truth.
interpretation: This verse reminds the deniers that rejecting God’s messengers is not a new path: earlier nations, including Noah’s people, the people of the Well, and Thamud, followed the same course and were ultimately destroyed for their persistent denial.

translation: And [the people of] ʿĀd, Pharaoh, and the brethren of Lot.
interpretation: This phrase invokes earlier peoples who rejected God’s messengers and were destroyed, warning that power, wealth, or social influence cannot protect a community from the consequences of persistent arrogance and denial.

translation: And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubbaʿ—each denied the messengers, so My threat became deserved.
interpretation: This verse warns that peoples who reject God’s messengers persistently expose themselves to the fulfillment of divine punishment; worldly power or historical prominence cannot protect a community from the consequences of deliberate denial.

translation: أفعَيِينا بالخلق الأول؟ بل هم في لَبْسٍ من خلقٍ جديدٍ.
interpretation: ليس عجزُ الله عن الإيجاد الأول هو الذي يجعل البعث مستبعدًا، بل إن إنكارهم ناشئ عن حيرة واضطراب في فهم قدرة الله على إعادة الخلق بعد الموت؛ فالذي أنشأهم أول مرة قادر على إنشائهم مرة أخرى.

translation: And indeed We created the human being, and We know what his soul whispers to him; and We are closer to him than his jugular vein.
interpretation: Allah knows the innermost thoughts and hidden impulses of every person with complete and immediate knowledge. His closeness is not bodily, but signifies the perfection of His awareness, power, and guardianship over the human being, leaving nothing concealed from Him.

translation: When the two receivers receive [and record], seated—one on the right and one on the left.
interpretation: This depicts the angels assigned to every person, constantly observing and recording their words and deeds from both sides, emphasizing that nothing a person does escapes precise accountability.

translation: He does not utter a word except that there is with him an ever-present watcher, ready to record it.
interpretation: Every spoken word is known and recorded by the angels assigned to a person, so the believer should guard their speech and speak only what is truthful, beneficial, and pleasing to God.

translation: And the agony of death comes with the truth; that is what you used to avoid.
interpretation: The verse portrays death as an undeniable reality that arrives at its appointed time, removing every illusion of escape and confronting a person with the truth they had tried to evade.

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown; that is the Day of the Threat.
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment when the promised Resurrection becomes a witnessed reality: the blowing of the Trumpet signals the end of worldly life and the beginning of judgment, fulfilling God’s warning to those who denied it.

translation: And every soul will come, accompanied by a driver and a witness.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, each person will be brought before God under the escort of an angel who drives them forward, while another angel bears witness to their deeds. No one will be able to evade judgment, because their life and actions will be fully accounted for.

translation: You were certainly heedless of this, so We have removed your veil from you, and your sight today is sharp.
interpretation: The verse portrays the moment of resurrection, when a person’s worldly distractions and denial are stripped away and the reality they previously ignored becomes unmistakably clear; the enhanced sight signifies profound certainty and insight, not merely physical vision.

translation: And his companion will say, “This is what I have ready.”
interpretation: The angel entrusted with the person’s record presents the deeds that have been carefully preserved, leaving nothing hidden or omitted for the judgment before Allah.

translation: Cast into Hell every persistent disbeliever.
interpretation: هذا أمرٌ بإلقاء من أصرَّ على الكفر وعاند الحق في جهنم؛ فالعذاب جزاءٌ لإعراضه المتعمد ومكابرته بعد ظهور الحق له.

translation: A hinderer of good, a transgressor, and one steeped in doubt.
interpretation: This describes a person whose character combines selfish obstruction of goodness, violation of others’ rights, and a persistent distrust that corrupts judgment and conduct.

translation: He who set up another deity alongside Allah—cast him into the severe punishment.
interpretation: This is a command to the two angels to cast into Hell the person who attributed divinity or worship to another besides Allah, because such association is a grave rejection of His exclusive right to be worshipped.

translation: His companion said, “Our Lord, I did not lead him into transgression; rather, he was himself in far-reaching error.”
interpretation: The companion—understood as the devil who accompanied him—denies forcing the person into disbelief or sin and attributes his misguidance to the person’s own deliberate choice; this emphasizes that Satan may tempt, but cannot compel someone to abandon the truth.

translation: He will say, “Do not argue before Me; I had already warned you.”
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will reject the excuses and disputes of those who disobeyed, reminding them that they had already received clear warning and therefore bear responsibility for their choices.

translation: The decree with Me is not changed, nor am I unjust to My servants.
interpretation: God’s judgment is perfectly true and cannot be altered or revoked; He does not punish anyone without justice, but recompenses each person precisely according to their deeds and the truth known to Him.

translation: On the Day We will say to Hell, “Are you full?” and it will say, “Are there any more?”
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as an overwhelming reality whose capacity seems boundless, intensifying the warning of divine judgment and the terrible consequence of persistent rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away.
interpretation: This portrays Paradise as an assured and readily accessible reward for those who remain mindful of God and live in obedience to Him; its nearness expresses their honored status and the certainty that their striving will lead them to it.

translation: This is what you were promised—for every one who constantly turns back to God and faithfully safeguards His commands.
interpretation: The promised reward is prepared for those who repeatedly repent, return to God, and remain vigilant in preserving their faith and obedience.

translation: Who feared the Most Merciful without seeing Him and came with a repentant heart.
interpretation: This describes the sincere believer whose reverence for God is genuine even in private, and whose heart continually turns back to Him in repentance, humility, and obedience.

translation: Enter it in peace; this is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: The righteous are welcomed into Paradise with complete safety from every fear, harm, and loss, where their blessed life will never end.

translation: For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is even more.
interpretation: The people of Paradise will receive everything they desire, yet God’s generosity will exceed all that they can imagine, granting them an abundance of blessing beyond their wishes.

translation: How many generations before them We destroyed—though they were mightier than these in strength—and they explored the lands. Was there any escape for them?
interpretation: The verse warns that worldly power, strength, and extensive dominion cannot protect a people from divine judgment. Even those who were stronger and more advanced than the deniers were ultimately destroyed, and when punishment came, they found no refuge or way to escape.

translation: Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or listens attentively while being present.
interpretation: The verse teaches that divine guidance benefits the person whose heart is alive and receptive to truth, or who listens with focused awareness and sincere attention. Mere physical hearing is not enough; understanding requires inward readiness and a present, attentive spirit.

translation: Indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.
interpretation: Allah affirms that He created the entire universe with complete power and authority, while declaring Himself utterly free from weakness, exhaustion, or fatigue. The creation taking six days reflects His deliberate ordering and wisdom, not any limitation in His ability.

translation: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in the face of their words and rejection, finding strength and tranquility by continually praising and glorifying Allah, especially at the prescribed times that mark the beginning and end of the day.

translation: And glorify Him during part of the night and after the prostrations.
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet—and all believers—to persist in remembering and praising Allah during the night, especially after completing the acts of prayer, so that worship and remembrance remain continuous beyond the formal prostration itself.

translation: And listen for the Day when the caller will call from a nearby place.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Resurrection as an undeniable summons: the call will reach all people clearly and directly, leaving no one distant from the moment of being raised and brought before God for judgment.

translation: On the Day they hear the Cry in truth—that is the Day of emergence.
interpretation: This refers to the Resurrection, when the divine trumpet call will be heard as an undeniable reality and all people will emerge from their graves to stand before God for judgment.

translation: Indeed, We alone give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute authority over life and death, and every person will ultimately return to Him to be judged for their deeds.

translation: On the Day when the earth splits open around them, they will emerge swiftly. That gathering is easy for Us.
interpretation: The verse reassures that resurrecting all people and assembling them for judgment, despite the vastness of their number, is effortless for God; their swift emergence emphasizes the certainty and immediacy of that final gathering.

translation: We know best what they say, and you are not appointed to compel them. So remind by the Qur’an those who fear My warning.
interpretation: The verse directs the Prophet to convey the Qur’an faithfully without forcing belief, since God fully knows the objections and words of those who reject it. Its warning and guidance are especially received by people whose awareness of accountability before God makes them willing to listen and respond.

translation: By those that scatter forcefully,
interpretation: Allah swears by the winds that disperse dust and other things, drawing attention to their powerful, ordered movement as a sign of His might and wisdom.

translation: Then those bearing burdens,
interpretation: This refers to the clouds carrying the heavy burden of rain, by which Allah brings life and benefit to the earth.

translation: Then by those that sail smoothly,
interpretation: Allah swears by ships that move effortlessly across the sea, directing attention to His power in enabling them to travel steadily over the vast waters.

translation: Then by those who distribute affairs by command,
interpretation: Allah swears by the angels entrusted with distributing and carrying out the affairs of creation according to His command and decree.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised is surely true.
interpretation: The verse affirms with certainty that God’s promised resurrection, judgment, reward, and punishment will inevitably come to pass, even if people doubt or fail to see them in the present.

translation: And indeed, the Judgment is certain to come.
interpretation: God affirms that the Day of Recompense will unquestionably occur, when every person will be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: By the sky woven with intricate patterns,
interpretation: The verse draws attention to the sky’s finely ordered structure and beauty, pointing to the wisdom and power of its Creator.

translation: Indeed, you are in conflicting speech.
interpretation: You are divided and contradictory in your claims about the truth, speaking inconsistently rather than accepting the clear message revealed by God.

translation: Turned away from it is whoever is turned away.
interpretation: Only those who are themselves inclined to deviation are diverted from the truth and prevented from accepting it.

translation: Perish the conjecturers!
interpretation: Those who speak about divine truth without knowledge, relying on speculation and inventing false claims, are condemned to ruin.

translation: Those who are immersed in heedlessness, distracted and unaware.
interpretation: It describes people whose hearts are overwhelmed by ignorance and neglect, so they remain heedless of the truth and fail to reflect on the consequences of their actions.

translation: They ask, “When will the Day of Judgment be?”
interpretation: This question is posed in a tone of denial and mockery, reflecting their refusal to believe that resurrection and accountability will truly occur.

translation: On the Day they are tormented in the Fire,
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment when those who denied the truth will be subjected to the Fire as a consequence of their rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: “Taste your trial; this is what you used to hasten.”
interpretation: They are being rebuked as they endure the punishment they once demanded to come quickly, exposing the arrogance of their denial and the consequence of treating divine warning with contempt.

translation: Indeed, the God-conscious will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: Those who remain mindful of God and steadfast in obedience to Him will be granted an eternal life of peace, delight, and abundant blessings in Paradise.

translation: Receiving what their Lord has given them; indeed, before that they were virtuous.
interpretation: They are enjoying the blessings and reward granted by their Lord because, during their worldly life, they consistently lived righteously, obeyed Him, and did good deeds.

translation: They used to sleep but little of the night.
interpretation: This praises the devoted believers who sacrifice much of their nighttime rest for prayer, remembrance, and drawing near to God, while taking only the limited sleep they need.

translation: And in the hours before dawn, they would seek forgiveness.
interpretation: They devoted the quiet time before dawn to sincere repentance and asking Allah to pardon their shortcomings, reflecting their humility and constant awareness of their need for His mercy.

translation: And in their wealth there was a rightful share for the beggar and the deprived.
interpretation: Those who are mindful of God recognize that their wealth is not theirs to withhold entirely; within it is an obligation toward people in need, including those who ask openly and those whose poverty prevents them from asking. This teaches that generosity and care for the vulnerable are duties, not merely acts of optional kindness.

translation: And on the earth are signs for those who are certain.
interpretation: The earth, through its ordered systems, living forms, and sustaining provisions, contains clear indications of Allah’s power, wisdom, and oneness; those whose hearts possess certainty recognize these signs and are guided by them to faith.

translation: And in yourselves—will you not then see?
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on their own creation, bodies, minds, and inner life, where the signs of God’s wisdom, power, and mercy are evident, so that they may recognize Him rather than remain heedless.

translation: And in heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised.
interpretation: Your sustenance and the fulfillment of God’s promises are under His heavenly decree, so rely on Him rather than treating worldly means as independent sources of provision.

translation: So, by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is surely true, just as surely as you speak.
interpretation: Allah swears by Himself, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, affirming that His promise—including resurrection, provision, and judgment—is an undeniable reality, as certain and evident as the human ability to speak.

translation: Has the account of Abraham’s honored guests reached you?
interpretation: في هذا الاستفهام تنبيهٌ إلى عِظَم شأن القصة، ودعوةٌ إلى التأمل في ضيوف إبراهيم الذين أكرمهم الله بمكانةٍ خاصة، وما تحمله قصتهم من دلائل قدرته وتدبيره.

translation: When they entered upon him and said, “Peace,” he replied, “Peace—you are an unfamiliar people.”
interpretation: Abraham returned their greeting courteously, while noting that they were unknown to him, which reflects his alertness toward unexpected guests and prepares for the disclosure of who they truly were and why they had come.

translation: Then he withdrew to his household and brought a fattened calf.
interpretation: This portrays Abraham’s prompt, discreet hospitality: he quietly went to his family, prepared a generous meal, and honored his guests without delay.

translation: Then he brought it near to them and said, “Will you not eat?”
interpretation: Abraham offered the food to his guests, but their refusal to eat made him uneasy and alerted him that they were not ordinary visitors.

translation: But he sensed fear from them. They said, “Do not fear,” and gave him the glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.
interpretation: When the unfamiliar guests did not eat, Abraham felt apprehensive, but they reassured him that no harm was intended and announced the birth of a son distinguished by knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Then his wife came forward with a loud cry, struck her face, and said, “An old woman who is barren?”
interpretation: Upon hearing the glad tidings of a child, Abraham’s wife reacted with astonishment because she was advanced in age and had never been able to bear children; her words express disbelief at what seemed naturally impossible, highlighting the extraordinary power of Allah.

translation: They said, “Thus has your Lord said. Indeed, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.”
interpretation: The statement affirms that what was announced will certainly occur by Allah’s decree, whose wisdom is perfect and whose knowledge encompasses every matter, even when His plan is beyond human understanding.

translation: He said, “What is your mission, O messengers?”
interpretation: Ibrāhīm, recognizing that these visitors were divine messengers, asked them to explain the serious matter for which they had been sent.

translation: They said, “Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals.”
interpretation: The angels explain that Allah has sent them to the people of Lot, whose persistent rejection and corruption have made them deserving of divine punishment.

translation: “That We may send down upon them stones of clay.”
interpretation: This refers to the divinely decreed punishment of the people of Lot: stones made of hardened clay were sent upon them as a consequence of their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of the truth.

translation: Marked by your Lord for those who commit excesses.
interpretation: These stones were divinely designated and prepared as punishment for the people who transgressed all limits in wrongdoing and defied God’s commands.

translation: So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers.
interpretation: This signifies that Allah, in His mercy, rescued the believers from the punishment destined for the corrupt people, showing that faith and righteousness are a means of divine deliverance.

translation: So We found there only one household of Muslims.
interpretation: This means that among the people of Lot, only Lot’s household had submitted to Allah and remained faithful, while the rest persisted in corruption; thus righteousness may be found in a small minority, and deliverance belongs to those who obey Allah.

translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: The remains of the people who were destroyed serve as a lasting warning: those who are mindful of God’s punishment should reflect on their fate and turn away from disobedience before they too face its consequences.

translation: And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority, there is a sign.
interpretation: Moses’ mission demonstrates that God supports His messengers with unmistakable proof and power, while Pharaoh’s rejection reveals that arrogance can cause a person to deny even manifest truth.

translation: But he turned away with his forces and said, “A sorcerer or a madman.”
interpretation: Pharaoh arrogantly rejected the truth brought by Moses, relying on his power and influence while dismissing the messenger with false accusations rather than confronting his message.

translation: So We seized him and his armies and cast them into the sea, while he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This portrays Pharaoh’s downfall as the consequence of his arrogance, oppression, and persistent rejection of the truth: the power with which he sought to dominate others could not protect him from God’s judgment.

translation: And in ʿĀd, when We sent upon them the barren wind.
interpretation: This refers to the devastating wind sent against the people of ʿĀd as punishment for their rejection and wrongdoing. It was called “barren” because it brought neither rain nor benefit, but destruction and no good outcome.

translation: It leaves nothing it reaches except that it reduces it to decayed remains.
interpretation: This portrays the devastating power of the wind sent against the people of ʿĀd: whatever it touched was utterly destroyed, leaving behind only lifeless, crumbling remnants.

translation: And in Thamūd, when it was said to them, “Enjoy yourselves for a while.”
interpretation: This refers to the brief respite granted to Thamūd despite their rejection: they were allowed to continue their worldly life only for a limited time before the promised punishment overtook them. The verse warns that temporary ease is not proof of divine approval or lasting security.

translation: فتمرّدوا بعناد على أمر ربهم، فأخذتهم الصاعقة وهم ينظرون.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن قوم ثمود أصرّوا على الاستكبار ورفض أمر الله بعد ظهور الحجة لهم، فجاءهم العذاب فجأة وهم يشاهدون وقوعه ولا يملكون دفعه، وفي ذلك تحذير من عاقبة العناد بعد قيام الحق.

translation: They were unable to rise, nor could they defend themselves.
interpretation: The people were utterly overcome by the punishment: they had no strength to recover or escape, and no power to protect themselves from Allah’s decree.

translation: And the people of Noah before them—indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The people of Noah are cited as an earlier example of a nation that persistently violated God’s commands and departed from obedience, so their rejection ultimately brought about their punishment.

translation: And the heaven We built with strength, and indeed We are expanding it.
interpretation: Allah declares His limitless power in creating the heavens and indicates that His creation is vast and continually expanding by His command.

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and excellent are We as its spreaders.
interpretation: Allah depicts the earth as deliberately made spacious, stable, and suitable for life, directing people to recognize His perfect power and care in preparing their dwelling place.

translation: And of everything We created pairs, so that you may take heed.
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the complementary pairs present throughout creation as a sign of His wisdom and power, so that people may recognize their own dependence and be reminded that the Creator is One and unlike His creation.

translation: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse calls people to turn urgently and sincerely to Allah—away from disbelief, sin, and anything that distances them from Him—and to seek His guidance and protection, before the consequences of rejecting the truth arrive.

translation: And do not set up another god alongside Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: Do not associate any partner with Allah in worship or devotion, for the Messenger warns plainly, by Allah’s command, of the consequences of turning away from His exclusive oneness.

translation: Thus, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, “A sorcerer or a madman.”
interpretation: This reveals the recurring response of those who reject divine guidance: rather than consider the messenger’s truth and message, they dismiss him with accusations of magic or madness—labels rooted in denial, not evidence.

translation: Have they enjoined this upon one another? Rather, they are a people who transgress.
interpretation: Their similar accusations against the messengers do not arise from a secret agreement among them; they arise from a shared rebellion against truth, driven by arrogance and a refusal to submit to divine guidance.

translation: So turn away from them, for you are not to blame.
interpretation: Withdraw from those who persistently reject the truth, for after conveying the message faithfully, you bear no blame for their refusal to accept it.

translation: And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers.
interpretation: Continue to offer sincere admonition, because those who truly believe remain receptive to guidance; remembrance awakens their hearts, strengthens their faith, and encourages them to obey Allah.

translation: I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me.
interpretation: Human existence has a divinely appointed purpose: to recognize Allah, submit to Him, and live in devoted obedience to Him. Worship encompasses not only ritual acts but every sincere action carried out in accordance with His guidance and for His sake.

translation: I do not seek any provision from them, nor do I seek that they feed Me.
interpretation: Allah is completely free of need from His creation; He created them to worship Him, not because He requires their sustenance or assistance. Their acts of worship and obedience benefit them alone, while He remains independent of all beings.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of all strength, the Firm and Unshakable.
interpretation: Allah alone guarantees the provision of every creature, and His ability to provide is limitless because all power belongs to Him. Therefore, reliance and gratitude should be directed to Him, for He is never weakened, overcome, or in need of anyone.

translation: Indeed, those who have wronged will have a share of punishment like the share of their predecessors, so let them not hasten Me.
interpretation: The unjust will inevitably receive a punishment comparable to that which befell earlier peoples who followed the same path of denial and wrongdoing; their demand for it to come sooner cannot avert or hasten the appointed decree.

translation: So woe to those who disbelieve because of the Day they are promised.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject faith will face grievous ruin and punishment when the promised Day of Judgment arrives, a day whose certainty cannot be escaped.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the Mount.
interpretation: Allah swears by the sacred Mount associated with His revelation to Moses, drawing attention to its honored status and to the certainty and gravity of the truths that follow.

translation: And a written Book,
interpretation: This refers to a revelation written and preserved, whose recorded words bear witness to the truth and guidance Allah has sent to humanity.

translation: على رقٍّ منشورٍ.
interpretation: يشير إلى كتابٍ مكتوبٍ على صحيفةٍ من الجلد مبسوطةٍ ظاهرة، بما يدلّ على وضوح ما فيها وإتاحته للقراءة والاطّلاع.

translation: And by the Much-Frequented House.
interpretation: This refers to the sacred house in the heavens, continually visited by angels in worship, signifying the vastness and ordered sanctity of God’s creation.

translation: And by the raised ceiling,
interpretation: This refers to the sky, elevated above the earth and held in its ordered structure, as a sign of God’s power and wisdom.

translation: And by the sea set ablaze,
interpretation: Allah swears by the sea whose depths are filled and whose waters will be kindled by fire, pointing to the immense power and inevitable judgment of the Creator.

translation: Indeed, your Lord’s punishment will surely come to pass.
interpretation: This is a firm warning that God’s judgment and punishment are certain realities, not matters of doubt or possibility, urging people to take accountability before Him seriously.

translation: There is no one who can avert it.
interpretation: This refers to the inevitable divine punishment: once God decrees it, no power, protector, or means can prevent it from reaching those deserving it.

translation: On the Day when the sky will shake violently,
interpretation: This depicts the terrifying upheaval of the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, when the ordered structure of the universe will be shaken as a manifestation of God’s overwhelming power and the certainty of judgment.

translation: And the mountains will move with a mighty motion.
interpretation: This depicts the upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when the mountains—seemingly immovable symbols of stability—will be uprooted and set in motion, revealing the complete transformation of the earthly order before God’s judgment.

translation: So woe, on that Day, to those who deny.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who persistently reject the truth will face ruin, punishment, and profound loss.

translation: Those who amuse themselves in vain discourse.
interpretation: It describes people who are absorbed in falsehood and frivolous argument, treating the truth and matters of ultimate accountability as mere entertainment instead of responding to them with seriousness and humility.

translation: On the Day they will be violently driven into the Fire of Hell.
interpretation: This depicts the humiliating and forceful punishment awaiting those who rejected the truth: they will be driven unwillingly toward Hell, with no ability to resist or escape.

translation: This is the Fire that you used to deny.
interpretation: The verse depicts the deniers being confronted with the very punishment they rejected as false, showing that their former denial cannot protect them from the reality of God’s warning.

translation: Is this then magic, or do you not see?
interpretation: This is a rebuke to those who denied the truth: when confronted with the punishment they once rejected, they are challenged to recognize that it is real—not an illusion or magic—and that their former blindness was willful denial.

translation: Enter it and endure patiently, or do not endure—it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This is a statement of the hopelessness of the deniers’ condition in Hell: whether they bear its punishment patiently or protest against it, nothing can lessen or remove it, because its cause is the consequences of their own deliberate deeds.

translation: Indeed, the God-conscious will be in gardens and bliss.
interpretation: This affirms that those who remain mindful of God, obey Him, and avoid wrongdoing will receive lasting comfort, joy, and honor in the Hereafter.

translation: Rejoicing in what their Lord has granted them, and because their Lord has shielded them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: The people of Paradise enjoy their blessings with genuine delight, recognizing them as gifts from their Lord, while their joy is completed by the security He has given them from the ultimate suffering of Hellfire.

translation: Eat and drink with delight, in reward for what you used to do.
interpretation: This is a gracious welcome to the righteous in Paradise: they are invited to enjoy its blessings freely and without harm, as an honor and recompense for their faith and obedient deeds in the world.

translation: Reclining on couches arranged in rows, We will unite them with pure, wide-eyed companions.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise in complete comfort and honor, surrounded by orderly repose and blessed companionship, with no hardship or loneliness remaining.

translation: And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will unite their descendants with them, and We will not diminish anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.
interpretation: Allah graciously reunites believing families in Paradise, elevating the descendants to the rank of their righteous forebears without reducing the reward earned by anyone. Yet this honor does not erase personal responsibility: each person remains accountable for his or her own faith and deeds.

translation: And We will provide them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire.
interpretation: Allah describes the believers’ provision in Paradise as abundant and perfectly suited to their desires, signifying complete comfort, generosity, and fulfillment without deprivation.

translation: They will pass around among themselves a cup; there will be no vain talk in it, nor any sinful speech.
interpretation: The cup symbolizes a pure and joyful drink shared in fellowship, free from the harmful effects, foolishness, and moral corruption associated with worldly intoxicants.

translation: And there will circulate among them youths belonging to them, as though they were hidden pearls.
interpretation: The verse portrays the honored inhabitants of Paradise being served by attendants of exceptional purity and beauty. Their comparison to pearls preserved within their shells conveys their radiance, immaculate appearance, and untouched perfection, emphasizing the dignity and delight prepared for them.

translation: And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This depicts people confronting one another and seeking explanations for what led them to their shared fate, revealing their mutual blame and helplessness before the consequences of their choices.

translation: They will say, “Indeed, before this, we were apprehensive among our families.”
interpretation: They acknowledge that, while living among their families in the world, they remained conscious and fearful of Allah’s judgment, which led them to obedience and guarded them from wrongdoing.

translation: “So Allah has graciously favored us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching fire.”
interpretation: The believers acknowledge that their deliverance from Hell is solely a mercy and favor from Allah, inspiring them to remain grateful and obedient rather than relying on their own deeds.

translation: Indeed, before this we used to call upon Him. Surely, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This expresses the believers’ recognition that their deliverance and blessing came through their persistent devotion to God, whose perfect kindness and mercy respond to sincere supplication.

translation: So remind them, for by the grace of your Lord, you are neither a soothsayer nor mad.
interpretation: God commands the Prophet to continue delivering the reminder without being deterred by the accusations of his opponents: the revelation he conveys is a divine favor, not the speech of a fortune-teller or the product of madness.

translation: Or do they say, “He is a poet; we await for him the calamity of fate”?
interpretation: They dismiss the Messenger as merely a poet and hope that death or the turns of fortune will silence him, revealing that their rejection is based not on evidence but on wishful expectation.

translation: Say, “Wait, then; I am waiting with you.”
interpretation: The verse is a warning to those who reject the truth: they may persist in expecting the Prophet’s failure, but he confidently entrusts the outcome to God and awaits the decisive manifestation of truth alongside them.

translation: Or do their minds command them to say this, or are they a transgressing people?
interpretation: Their denial is not grounded in sound judgment; rather, they are either following distorted reasoning or persisting in arrogant rebellion against the truth.

translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Rather, they do not believe.
interpretation: The deniers accuse the Prophet of inventing the Qur’an, but their accusation is not based on proof; it arises from their refusal to accept the truth and submit to faith.

translation: Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful.
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who deny that the Qur’an is revelation: if their claim is sincere, they should be able to compose something comparable to it in its eloquence, guidance, coherence, and profound impact.

translation: Or were they created from nothing, or are they themselves the creators?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge exposing the impossibility of denying the Creator: human beings neither brought themselves into existence nor came into being without a cause, so their existence necessarily points to Allah, the one true Creator.

translation: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they have no certainty.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge exposing the weakness of their denial: if they did not create the heavens and the earth, they have no rational basis for rejecting their Creator. Their refusal to believe arises not from evidence, but from the absence of true certainty.

translation: Or do they possess the treasures of your Lord, or are they the ones in control?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who reject the truth as though they had authority over God’s provisions, mercy, revelation, and decree. They possess no such control; all these belong exclusively to God, so their objections have no legitimate basis.

translation: Or do they have a ladder by which they listen? Then let their listener bring a clear authority.
interpretation: This is a challenge to those who make claims about the unseen: do they possess access to the heavens that enables them to hear divine secrets? If so, let whoever claims to have heard them provide clear, undeniable proof.

translation: Or does He have daughters while you have sons?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of those who attributed daughters to God while reserving sons for themselves, revealing the inconsistency and prejudice of their belief. It rejects assigning offspring to God altogether and exposes the injustice of preferring sons over daughters.

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are weighed down by a burden of debt?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question rejecting any excuse for their refusal: the Messenger does not demand worldly compensation from them, so their rejection cannot be attributed to financial hardship imposed upon them.

translation: Or do they possess knowledge of the unseen, so that they write it down?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who reject the truth: do they truly possess access to the unseen and thereby have authority to make such claims, or are they speaking without knowledge? Only God knows the unseen, so their assertions have no divine basis.

translation: Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve are the ones ensnared by the plot.
interpretation: They may scheme against the truth and its messenger, but their plotting will ultimately turn against them, while God’s decree brings their plans to failure and exposes their own weakness.

translation: Or do they have a god other than Allah? Glory be to Allah, exalted far above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse rejects the notion that anyone besides Allah possesses divine authority or deserves worship. It declares Allah utterly transcendent above the partners and false attributes people ascribe to Him.

translation: And if they were to see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, “Piled-up clouds.”
interpretation: Even a visible sign as overwhelming as part of the sky descending would not move the deniers to acknowledge the truth; they would explain it away as an ordinary natural phenomenon, revealing their deliberate refusal to believe.

translation: So leave them until they meet their Day on which they will be struck down.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persist in denial are being given temporary respite, not spared from judgment; an unavoidable day will come when they are overwhelmed by the punishment of God.

translation: On the Day when their schemes will avail them nothing, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment, when every worldly plan, deception, or attempt to escape accountability will be powerless, and those who relied on such means will find no one able to rescue or defend them from God’s judgment.

translation: And indeed, those who have wronged will have a punishment before that, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing may face consequences and punishment even before the final punishment of the Hereafter, though many remain unaware that their worldly suffering and downfall can be a warning and a consequence of their deeds.

translation: So be patient with the decree of your Lord, for truly you are under Our watchful care; and glorify your Lord with praise when you rise.
interpretation: The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ that steadfastness in carrying out his mission and bearing opposition is made possible by Allah’s constant protection and care. It directs him to meet hardship not with resentment, but with patience and continual remembrance and praise of Allah, beginning when he rises.

translation: And glorify Him during part of the night and at the setting of the stars.
interpretation: The verse calls the Prophet—and through him the believers—to persist in praising and remembering Allah during the night, including the quiet time when the stars fade, expressing devotion and gratitude beyond the prescribed acts of worship.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the star when it sets.
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the star as it descends or disappears, directing reflection toward His perfect power and the ordered signs of His creation.

translation: Your companion has neither gone astray nor erred.
interpretation: God affirms that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is not misguided in the truth he conveys, nor has he deviated from the right way; his guidance and message are not the result of error or personal whim.

translation: Nor does he speak from his own desire.
interpretation: In conveying God’s revelation and guidance, the Prophet does not speak according to personal whim; his message is grounded in divine direction.

translation: It is nothing but revelation that is revealed.
interpretation: The verse affirms that what the Prophet conveys concerning divine guidance is not produced from personal desire or human speculation; rather, it comes through revelation from Allah.

translation: Taught to him by one mighty in strength.
interpretation: This refers to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ receiving the revelation through Jibrīl, an angel endowed with immense power and strength, affirming that the Qur’an was conveyed by a trustworthy, divinely empowered messenger.

translation: Possessor of mighty strength, then he stood poised.
interpretation: This describes Gabriel as possessing immense power and perfect strength, and then appearing in a firm, majestic, and complete form as he conveyed the revelation.

translation: And he was on the highest horizon.
interpretation: This refers to the Messenger being shown the angel in his true, majestic form at the loftiest boundary of the heavenly realm, emphasizing the extraordinary nature and certainty of the revelation.

translation: Then he drew near and descended.
interpretation: This refers to the angel Gabriel drawing near to the Prophet ﷺ and descending to him in the course of conveying the revelation, signifying the immediacy and certainty of the divine message.

translation: Then he was at a distance of two bow-lengths, or even nearer.
interpretation: This expresses the extraordinary closeness between the Messenger and the one who appeared to him, emphasizing the directness and certainty of the divine revelation he received.

translation: Then He revealed to His servant whatever He revealed.
interpretation: Allah conveyed to Muhammad, His servant, the revelation He willed through the angel Gabriel, while leaving its exact content unspecified to emphasize its profound importance and divine origin.

translation: The heart did not deny what it saw.
interpretation: The Prophet’s heart remained certain and truthful regarding the profound vision granted to him, accepting it without doubt or distortion.

translation: Will you then argue with him about what he saw?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who deny or challenge the Prophet’s account of the unmistakable vision granted to him, treating their disputation as baseless in the face of divine revelation.

translation: And indeed, he saw him another time.
interpretation: This refers to the Prophet Muhammad’s second sighting of Gabriel in his true form, confirming the extraordinary revelation and the signs shown to him during the heavenly ascent.

translation: Near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.
interpretation: It refers to the sublime limit reached by the Prophet ﷺ during the heavenly ascent—a boundary marking the utmost extent of created beings’ knowledge and access, beyond which lies what Allah alone knows.

translation: Near it is the Garden of Refuge.
interpretation: This refers to the blessed nearness of Paradise to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, portraying it as the eternal abode of security and rest prepared by God for the faithful.

translation: When that which covered the lote tree covered it,
interpretation: The lote tree was enveloped by an awe-inspiring manifestation of the unseen—so magnificent that its full nature cannot be expressed or comprehended by human description.

translation: The sight did not waver, nor did it overreach.
interpretation: The Prophet’s vision remained firm and focused during the heavenly encounter, neither turning away from what was shown nor exceeding the limits set for him.

translation: لقد رأى من آيات ربه الكبرى.
interpretation: تشير الآية إلى أن النبي ﷺ شاهد في رحلته آياتٍ عظيمةً من دلائل قدرة الله وعظمته، دون أن يعني ذلك رؤية ذات الله تعالى.

translation: Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to the idolaters: reflect on the reality of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, false deities that possess no true power or authority, and recognize that they do not deserve worship.

translation: And Manāt, the third—the other one?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the pagan claim that Manāt, one of their female deities and the third of the idols mentioned, possessed divine status; the wording conveys contempt for assigning such partners to Allah.

translation: Is the male for you and the female for Him?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the idolaters for assigning sons to themselves—whom they considered superior—while attributing daughters to God, exposing the contradiction and injustice in their beliefs.

translation: That, then, is an unjust division.
interpretation: This is a condemnation of the claim that Allah has daughters while people prefer sons for themselves: a distribution of qualities and status that is inherently biased and unacceptable.

translation: They are nothing but names that you and your forefathers have given them; Allah has not sent down any authority for them. They follow nothing but conjecture and what their souls desire, even though guidance has come to them from their Lord.
interpretation: The verse rejects treating invented names and inherited beliefs as evidence of divine truth. It teaches that faith must rest on revelation and sound guidance, not speculation, ancestral imitation, or desires that a person mistakes for truth.

translation: Or does man have whatever he wishes?
interpretation: الآية استفهام إنكاري يقرر أن مجرد تمني الإنسان لا يوجب حصول ما يريد؛ فالأمر كله لله، يجريه بحكمته وعدله، لا وفق الأهواء والرغبات وحدها.

translation: To Allah belong the Hereafter and the worldly life.
interpretation: Both this world and the Hereafter are wholly under Allah’s ownership, authority, and judgment; therefore, ultimate power and the final outcome belong to Him alone.

translation: And how many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing, except after Allah has granted permission to whom He wills and is pleased with.
interpretation: Even the angels, despite their honored rank, possess no independent power to intercede. Intercession is entirely subject to Allah’s permission and approval: He permits it only for those whose faith and deeds He accepts. Thus, no one should rely on status, lineage, or imagined intermediaries instead of turning sincerely to Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with feminine names.
interpretation: Those who deny the Hereafter speak about the unseen without sound knowledge, assigning femininity to the angels based on conjecture rather than revelation; the verse condemns such claims as unfounded and reveals their inconsistency in rejecting accountability while asserting matters they cannot know.

translation: They have no knowledge of it; they follow nothing but conjecture, and surely conjecture is of no avail against the truth.
interpretation: This verse rejects claims that are made without revealed knowledge or sound evidence, teaching that assumptions and speculation cannot establish what is true or replace certainty grounded in divine guidance.

translation: So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance and seeks nothing but the life of this world.
interpretation: This is a directive not to become consumed by those who deliberately reject divine guidance and make worldly gain their sole aim. Their persistent indifference should not divert the believer from obedience to God; rather, one should maintain distance from their influence while continuing to convey truth with wisdom.

translation: That is the extent of their knowledge. Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best who is rightly guided.
interpretation: Their understanding is confined to the fleeting concerns of worldly life, so they fail to recognize the truth and the consequences of their choices. Allah alone fully knows who has turned away from His guidance and who has sincerely followed the right path.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so that He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done, and recompense those who do good with the best reward.
interpretation: Since all creation belongs to Allah and remains under His authority, no deed escapes His knowledge or judgment: wrongdoing will receive its fitting recompense, while righteousness will be met with the finest reward—Allah’s gracious acceptance and abundant blessing.

translation: Those who avoid the major sins and indecencies—except for minor lapses. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knows you best, when He brought you forth from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers’ wombs. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He knows best who is mindful of Him.
interpretation: This verse teaches that righteousness lies in sincerely striving to avoid grave sins and immorality, while recognizing that human beings may occasionally fall into lesser lapses. Such lapses should not become a justification for wrongdoing, but neither should they lead a person to despair, for God’s forgiveness is immense. Since God knows every person’s origin, weakness, inner reality, and degree of reverence, no one should boast of purity or regard himself as superior; true piety is known fully only to God.

translation: Have you seen the one who turned away?
interpretation: This is a rebuke directed at the person who turns away from faith and obedience after being reminded of the truth, exposing his deliberate withdrawal rather than ignorance or lack of guidance.

translation: And he gave a little, then stopped giving.
interpretation: This describes a person who offers only a small amount of charity or obedience, then withdraws and refuses to continue, revealing that his effort is neither sincere nor steadfast.

translation: Does he possess knowledge of the unseen, so that he can see?
interpretation: The verse rejects the assumption that a person can claim certainty about hidden realities or the consequences of his actions merely by personal judgment; knowledge of the unseen belongs to God, and human claims to such knowledge are unfounded.

translation: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reminder that the truths being taught are not new; they were already revealed to Moses, including guidance toward faith, responsibility, and accountability before God.

translation: And Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations].
interpretation: Abraham is praised for completely fulfilling what God commanded him, remaining faithful and steadfast through every trial.

translation: No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.
interpretation: Each person is accountable for their own deeds before God; no one will be punished for another person’s wrongdoing.

translation: And that each person will have only what they strive for.
interpretation: A person’s true share is determined by their own sincere effort and deeds; mere claims or reliance on another’s accomplishments cannot replace what they themselves strive to do.

translation: And that his striving will be seen.
interpretation: A person’s efforts are never hidden or wasted; God will bring them to light, and their worth and consequences will become evident.

translation: Then he will be repaid with the fullest recompense.
interpretation: A person will receive from Allah the complete and exact reward or consequence of his deeds, with nothing of what he deserves omitted.

translation: And that to your Lord is the final destination.
interpretation: Every ultimate end, return, and matter leads to Allah, so He alone is the final authority and the one to whom all creation will ultimately return.

translation: And indeed, it is He who causes laughter and weeping.
interpretation: Human joy and sorrow occur within God’s knowledge, will, and sustaining power; therefore, people should recognize their dependence on Him in both happiness and grief.

translation: And that it is He who causes death and gives life.
interpretation: Life and death are wholly under Allah’s power, affirming that human existence is dependent on Him from beginning to end.

translation: And that He created the two mates—the male and the female.
interpretation: تدل الآية على أن الله تعالى هو الخالق لأصلَي الذكورة والأنوثة، وأن وجودهما وتمايزهما قائم بتقديره وحكمته، فلا يخرج شيء من نظام الخلق عن علمه وإرادته.

translation: From a drop of fluid when it is emitted.
interpretation: This points to the humble origin of human life: a person is brought forth from a tiny drop of reproductive fluid, reminding humanity that its existence depends entirely on Allah’s creative power.

translation: And that upon Him rests the other creation.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah alone has the power to bring about the second creation—the resurrection after death—and that returning all beings to life is entirely within His authority.

translation: And that it is He who enriches and grants possession.
interpretation: All true provision and the ability to attain and retain wealth come from God; therefore, prosperity should be recognized as His gift rather than as something dependent solely on human effort.

translation: And that He alone is the Lord of Sirius.
interpretation: God is the sole Lord and Creator of every power and object of worship, including Sirius, the star that some people revered; therefore, no created thing deserves worship alongside Him.

translation: And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd,
interpretation: This refers to the ancient people of ʿĀd, the nation of Prophet Hūd, whom Allah destroyed because of their persistent rejection of the truth and arrogant defiance.

translation: And Thamūd—He left none of them.
interpretation: God completely destroyed the people of Thamūd, leaving no one among them to survive their rejection and defiance.

translation: And the people of Noah before them—indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the extreme injustice and defiance of Noah’s people: despite receiving clear guidance, they persisted in rejecting their messenger and opposing the truth, becoming an example of how arrogance and rebellion can reach their utmost degree.

translation: And He brought down the overturned cities.
interpretation: This refers to God’s destruction of the towns of Lot, which were overturned and cast down as a consequence of their persistent corruption and defiance.

translation: Then there covered it whatever was to cover it.
interpretation: The cities of Lot were overwhelmed by the punishment that Allah sent upon them, a calamity whose full nature and severity are beyond ordinary description.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you doubt?
interpretation: The verse rebukes a person who persists in doubt despite the clear signs of God’s power and mercy, calling them to recognize that His blessings and truths are not matters for futile dispute.

translation: This is a warner like the former warners.
interpretation: The Prophet’s warning is part of the same continuing divine call delivered by earlier messengers: people are being cautioned to turn back to God before facing the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: اقتربت الواقعة الوشيكة.
interpretation: إن يوم القيامة الذي توعّد الله به قد دنا، فلا مجال للغفلة، بل ينبغي الاستعداد له بالإيمان والعمل الصالح.

translation: None besides Allah can reveal it.
interpretation: The approaching Hour is known in its timing only to Allah, and no created being has the power to avert or bring it about; its full reality and occurrence rest solely with Him.

translation: فهل من هذا الحديث تعجبون؟
interpretation: يعاتب الله المكذبين على استغرابهم من القرآن ووحيه، مع أن الأولى بهم أن يتلقوه بالإيمان والتدبر لا بالدهشة والإنكار.

translation: And you laugh and do not weep.
interpretation: This rebukes those who hear the truth yet respond with heedlessness and amusement instead of humility, fear of God, and sincere repentance.

translation: while you are absorbed in heedlessness and amusement.
interpretation: You remain distracted and frivolous instead of humbling yourselves before God and responding seriously to His warning.

translation: So prostrate before Allah and worship Him.
interpretation: This is a command to devote oneself wholly to Allah, expressing humility and submission through prostration and sincere worship, rather than directing any act of devotion to other than Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that the Day of Resurrection is approaching. The splitting of the moon is understood as a manifest miracle shown to the people, yet it also exposes how signs alone do not benefit those who persist in denial and heedlessness.

translation: And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, “Persistent magic.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the deniers’ stubborn rejection of divine signs: rather than reflect on the evidence, they dismiss it as merely a recurring or continuing spell.

translation: Yet they denied the truth and followed their desires, while every matter has its settled outcome.
interpretation: Their rejection was not due to lack of evidence, but to their preference for personal desires; nevertheless, God’s decree will prevail and the truth will ultimately reach its appointed consequence.

translation: And indeed, there has come to them news containing a deterrent.
interpretation: The accounts of earlier peoples and the warnings revealed to them contain lessons powerful enough to restrain them from denial and disobedience, if they would reflect upon them.

translation: Profound wisdom—but the warnings are of no avail.
interpretation: The revealed message contains complete and decisive wisdom, yet those who stubbornly reject the truth gain no benefit from warnings because they refuse to reflect and respond.

translation: So turn away from them. On the Day when the caller calls to a dreadful thing,
