interpretation: This is a warning that when the appointed resurrection arrives, the disbelievers will be summoned to face a horrifying and utterly unfamiliar ordeal; at that point, their rejection will offer them no escape.

translation: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as though they were scattered locusts.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, people will rise in a state of utter fear and humiliation, unable to lift their gazes, and will pour forth from their graves in countless, disorderly multitudes like swarming locusts.

translation: They will hasten toward the caller, their necks outstretched. The disbelievers will say, “This is a difficult day.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the terror and urgency of the Resurrection: the disbelievers will be compelled to rush toward the summons, unable to resist or delay it, and will recognize that the Day of Judgment is one of overwhelming hardship because they face the consequences of their rejection.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied the truth. They rejected Our servant and said, “He is insane,” and he was threatened and driven away.
interpretation: تكشف الآية عن عناد قوم نوح؛ فقد قابلوا دعوته إلى توحيد الله بالتكذيب والإهانة، ووصفوه بالجنون ليصدّوا الناس عن اتباعه، ثم آذوه وضيّقوا عليه، غير أن ذلك لم يغيّر من صدقه ولا من ثباته على دعوته.

translation: So he called upon his Lord: “Indeed, I am overcome, so grant me victory.”
interpretation: This is Noah’s humble appeal after his people’s persistent rejection and oppression: acknowledging that he has no power to overcome them himself, he entrusts the matter entirely to God and asks Him to establish justice and support the truth.

translation: So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water.
interpretation: This portrays the overwhelming rain sent by God as a decisive act of punishment, descending in an unceasing torrent beyond human ability to resist.

translation: And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Flood as unfolding by Allah’s precise command: water emerged from the earth and descended from the sky until the two sources converged, carrying out a divinely determined judgment that could not be delayed or averted.

translation: And We carried him aboard a vessel made of planks and fastenings.
interpretation: This refers to Noah, whom God saved from the overwhelming flood by carrying him in a firmly constructed ark. The verse highlights that deliverance came through God’s care and power, using even a simple vessel as the means of salvation.

translation: Sailing under Our watch, as a reward for the one who had been rejected.
interpretation: The Ark moved safely under Allah’s direct care and protection, and its preservation was a vindication and recompense for Noah, whom his people had denied and opposed.

translation: And We certainly left it as a sign, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: The remains or account of Noah’s ark were preserved as a lasting reminder of God’s power and of the fate awaiting those who reject His warning, inviting people to reflect and learn from it.

translation: So how were My punishment and warnings?
interpretation: This is a forceful reminder that the fate of those who rejected God’s warnings was severe and undeniable, urging people to reflect on their destruction and take divine warnings seriously before suffering the same consequence.

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: Allah has made the Qur’an accessible for reflection, understanding, memorization, and guidance, while calling people to approach it with attentive hearts and learn from its lessons. The closing question urges each person to respond to this opportunity by remembering Allah and allowing the Qur’an to transform their faith and conduct.

translation: The people of ʿĀd denied the truth—so how were My punishment and warnings?
interpretation: This verse warns that denying God’s messengers and disregarding His warnings ultimately brings a punishment that demonstrates the certainty and seriousness of His threat.

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them a howling, bitterly cold wind on a day of unremitting misfortune.
interpretation: This verse portrays the wind as a decisive punishment inflicted upon the people who rejected God’s warning: its relentless force made that day one of continuing calamity, demonstrating that persistent defiance can bring consequences that cannot be escaped.

translation: It tore the people away as though they were the trunks of uprooted palm trees.
interpretation: This depicts the devastating force of the wind sent against the people of ʿĀd: it violently lifted and cast them down, leaving their bodies scattered like the massive, uprooted trunks of palm trees.

translation: So how were My punishment and warnings?
interpretation: This is a grave reminder that when people reject divine warnings, God’s punishment becomes a decisive reality, demonstrating the truth of what they had been warned about.

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: Allah has made the Qur’an accessible for understanding, memorization, and spiritual reflection, then calls people to respond by sincerely receiving its guidance and learning its lessons.

translation: Thamūd denied the warnings.
interpretation: The people of Thamūd rejected the admonitions and warnings brought to them by God’s messenger, refusing to heed the truth and the consequences of their rebellion.

translation: So they said, “Are we to follow a single human being from among us? Indeed, then we would be in error and madness.”
interpretation: They rejected the truth because it was conveyed through an ordinary human being from their own community, allowing arrogance and disbelief to make them regard obedience to him as foolishness rather than guidance.

translation: “Has the Reminder been bestowed upon him alone from among us? No; he is an insolent liar.”
interpretation: The people rejected the message because they could not accept that one person from among them had been chosen to receive revelation. Instead of considering his call, they arrogantly dismissed him as a deceitful and presumptuous liar.

translation: Tomorrow they will know who the insolent liar is.
interpretation: This is a warning to those who rejected Ṣāliḥ and accused him of lying: the truth will soon become unmistakable, and the disgrace will fall upon the arrogant deniers rather than upon the messenger they mocked.

translation: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient.
interpretation: Allah made the she-camel a clear test for Thamūd: their response to His sign would reveal whether they would obey His command or persist in denial. The Prophet is therefore commanded to await their response with steadfast patience.

translation: And inform them that the water is apportioned between them; each drinking turn is to be attended.
interpretation: The verse establishes that the water is a shared trust governed by a divinely assigned order: each party has a rightful turn, and no one may seize what has been allotted to another. Their obedience to this arrangement is a test of whether they will submit to justice rather than follow selfish desire.

translation: So they called their companion, and he took up the task and hamstrung her.
interpretation: When they persisted in their defiance, they summoned the one among them who was willing to carry out their plot. He boldly seized the she-camel and slaughtered her, thereby committing the crime they had collectively resolved upon.

translation: So how were My punishment and warnings?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question calling people to reflect on the devastating fate of those who rejected God’s warnings and to take heed before facing the same punishment.

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast, and they became like the dry, crushed remnants gathered by an animal-pen builder.
interpretation: The verse portrays the complete and sudden destruction of a people who persisted in defiance: one divine command was enough to reduce their strength and proud society to something fragile, scattered, and worthless, demonstrating that human power cannot withstand God’s judgment.

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: Allah has made the Qur’an accessible as a source of guidance and reflection, inviting every sincere person to engage with it, remember its teachings, and allow them to transform their life.

translation: The people of Lot rejected the warnings.
interpretation: They refused to believe the cautions and admonitions conveyed to them by Prophet Lot, persisting in their wrongdoing despite the clear warning of divine punishment.

translation: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot; We saved them before dawn.
interpretation: This portrays the destruction of Lot’s people as a deliberate divine punishment for their persistent corruption, while showing that God protects those who remain faithful by rescuing Lot’s household before the punishment fell.

translation: A favor from Us; thus do We reward those who are grateful.
interpretation: Allah’s saving grace is bestowed by His mercy, and those who recognize His blessings with sincere gratitude and obedience are promised His favor and reward.

translation: And he surely warned them of Our mighty seizure, but they disputed the warnings.
interpretation: The verse portrays a people who were clearly cautioned about God’s punishment, yet responded by rejecting and arguing against the warnings instead of taking them seriously. Their defiance shows how denial can persist even after the truth has been plainly conveyed.

translation: Indeed, they sought to entice him concerning his guests, so We obliterated their eyes: “Taste My punishment and warnings.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people’s aggression and their attempt to violate the guests’ dignity as a grave transgression. Their loss of sight is a divine punishment and a sign that those who deliberately refuse moral guidance may be deprived of the very perception needed to recognize the truth, while the warning calls them to face the consequences of their defiance.

translation: And indeed, a lasting punishment struck them in the morning.
interpretation: The punishment came upon them at daybreak exactly as warned, becoming an established and unavoidable consequence of their persistent wrongdoing.

translation: So taste My punishment and My warnings.
interpretation: This is a stern divine warning that rejecting God’s messengers and persisting in wrongdoing leads to experiencing the consequences God has cautioned against.

translation: ولقد يسّرنا القرآن للذِّكر فهل من مُدَّكِر
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن القرآن ميسّر للفهم والتدبّر والاتعاظ لمن أقبل عليه بصدق، ثم يحثّ الناس على اغتنام هذا التيسير والانتفاع به في إصلاح قلوبهم وأعمالهم.

translation: And indeed, warnings came to the people of Pharaoh.
interpretation: The people of Pharaoh were given clear admonitions and signs through which they were warned of God’s punishment, leaving them no excuse when they rejected the truth.

translation: They denied all Our signs, so We seized them with the seizure of the Almighty, All-Powerful.
interpretation: Their persistent rejection of every clear proof brought upon them a decisive punishment from God, whose might and power no force can resist.

translation: Are your disbelievers better than those people, or do you have an exemption in the Scriptures?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke: the deniers among the Quraysh have no superiority over earlier peoples who were destroyed for rejecting the truth, nor any written guarantee that God will spare them from judgment.

translation: Or do they say, “We are a victorious multitude”?
interpretation: This is a rebuke of the disbelievers’ misplaced confidence: their strength in numbers and worldly power cannot protect them from God’s decree or guarantee victory over the truth.

translation: The assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs in flight.
interpretation: Despite their apparent strength and unity, those who oppose the truth will ultimately be overcome and forced to retreat, for victory belongs to God and unfolds according to His decree.

translation: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter.
interpretation: Their worldly opposition and defeat are not the ultimate end; the Day of Resurrection is the appointed time for their final reckoning, whose suffering and consequences are far more severe and bitter than anything they may experience in this life.

translation: Indeed, the criminals are in error and blazing fire.
interpretation: Those who persist in wrongdoing and reject the truth have strayed from the right path, and their rebellion leads them to the torment of Hell.

translation: On the Day they will be dragged on their faces into the Fire: “Taste the touch of Saqar.”
interpretation: This depicts the humiliation and torment awaiting those who reject the truth: they will be dragged helplessly into Hell, where they will be told to experience its painful punishment, with “Saqar” referring to one of the names of Hellfire.

translation: Indeed, We have created everything according to a precise measure.
interpretation: Everything that exists comes into being by Allah’s determined decree, with exact proportion, order, and wisdom; nothing is created randomly or beyond His knowledge and control.

translation: Our command is only one, like the blink of an eye.
interpretation: Allah’s decree is carried out instantly and effortlessly; when He wills a matter, it comes into existence without delay or resistance.

translation: And We have indeed destroyed those like you before; so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: The fate of earlier peoples who followed the same path of denial and wrongdoing is a warning to those who come after them. A person of sound reflection should learn from their destruction and turn away from disobedience before suffering the same end.

translation: And everything they did is recorded in the scriptures.
interpretation: Nothing of their deeds is lost or overlooked; every action has been preserved in the divinely recorded registers and will be brought forth for judgment.

translation: And everything small and great is recorded.
interpretation: Nothing is overlooked: every deed, word, and intention—whether seemingly insignificant or momentous—is preserved in the divine record and will be brought forth for judgment.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and by a flowing river.
interpretation: Those who remain mindful of God and live in obedience to Him will be granted eternal peace, surrounded by the delights of Paradise and its pure, ever-flowing blessings.

translation: في مقام صدق، عند ملكٍ مقتدر.
interpretation: أي إن المتقين ينعمون عند الله في مقام كريم ثابت، تحيط بهم فيه الطمأنينة والرضوان والقرب، لدى ربٍّ كامل الملك والقدرة.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The Most Compassionate.
interpretation: The passage opens by invoking Allah through His encompassing mercy, then singles out “the Most Compassionate” as the defining name through which His blessings, care, and grace are understood.

translation: He taught the Qur’an.
interpretation: Allah is the source of the Qur’an’s teaching, having revealed it and made its guidance accessible to humanity.

translation: He created the human being.
interpretation: This affirms that human existence is brought about by Allah’s creative power, not by independent origin or chance.

translation: He taught him expression.
interpretation: Allah endowed the human being with the ability to understand meanings and articulate them clearly through speech and communication.

translation: The sun and the moon move according to precise calculation.
interpretation: The ordered movement of the sun and moon reflects Allah’s perfect wisdom and control over the universe, whose regularity follows exact measures rather than chance.

translation: And the stars and the trees prostrate.
interpretation: All created beings, whether celestial bodies or earthly plants, submit to Allah’s command and glorify Him in the manner appropriate to their nature, even if humans do not perceive how that prostration occurs.

translation: And the heaven He raised, and He set the balance.
interpretation: God has established the universe upon precise order and balance, teaching human beings to uphold justice and not violate the proper measure in their dealings.

translation: So that you do not transgress in the balance.
interpretation: God commands that justice and fairness govern all acts of weighing and measuring, forbidding deception, excess, or deficiency that violates people’s rights.

translation: And establish the balance with justice, and do not fall short in the measure.
interpretation: This commands people to uphold fairness and honesty in every transaction and judgment, never deceiving others by giving them less than what is due.

translation: And the earth He laid out for all beings.
interpretation: The earth is presented as a divinely arranged and hospitable dwelling, prepared to sustain every creature that lives upon it.

translation: In it are fruits and date palms with sheathed clusters.
interpretation: The earth contains varied nourishment, including dates whose developing fruits are protected within their coverings, reflecting the care and wisdom embedded in God’s provision.

translation: And grain with husks, and fragrant plants.
interpretation: This points to God’s provision in its diverse forms: nourishing grain protected by its husk and plants endowed with pleasing fragrance, both manifesting His wisdom and generosity in creation.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a repeated divine challenge to humankind and the jinn: in light of God’s countless blessings, signs, and acts of mercy, neither can truthfully reject or deny His grace.

translation: He created man from sounding clay like pottery.
interpretation: This signifies that human beings were created from humble earthly matter, fashioned by God with precise order and purpose; the comparison to pottery evokes clay that has been shaped and hardened, while still reminding humanity of its dependence on its Creator.

translation: And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.
interpretation: The verse teaches that the jinn are a distinct creation of God, brought into existence from a fiery, mingled flame, unlike human beings who were created from earthly material.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you two deny?
interpretation: This rhetorical question addresses both humans and jinn, urging them to recognize their Lord’s countless favors and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests.
interpretation: He is the Lord of every place from which the sun rises and sets, including the differing points of sunrise and sunset across the year. This expresses His complete sovereignty over the order and variation of the heavens.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you two deny?
interpretation: This verse repeatedly calls both humankind and the jinn to recognize Allah’s countless blessings and confront their ingratitude, leaving no excuse for denying His favors or failing to give thanks.

translation: He has released the two seas, meeting one another.
interpretation: This portrays Allah’s power in causing two bodies of water to come together while preserving the distinct boundaries He has ordained between them.

translation: Between them is a barrier; neither encroaches upon the other.
interpretation: The two bodies of water meet, yet by God’s command they remain separated within their distinct limits, demonstrating the order and precision of His creation.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a reproachful question addressed to humankind and the jinn, urging them to recognize and not deny the countless blessings and signs of their Lord.

translation: From both of them emerge pearl and coral.
interpretation: Allah reminds us that even from the meeting of two distinct seas He brings forth precious treasures, displaying His perfect power and blessing in the natural world.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humans and jinn, challenging them to acknowledge that none of their Lord’s blessings and signs can rightly be denied.

translation: And to Him belong the ships, sailing high upon the sea like mountains.
interpretation: The verse directs attention to the immense ships moving across the sea, likening them to mountains in their grandeur, as a sign that their creation, power, and movement all ultimately belong to Allah.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a solemn address to both humankind and the jinn, challenging them to recognize that none of their Lord’s blessings, signs, and acts of mercy can reasonably be denied.

translation: Everyone upon it will perish.
interpretation: All created beings on the earth are mortal and temporary; enduring permanence belongs only to Allah.

translation: And the Face of your Lord remains, Possessor of majesty and honor.
interpretation: Everything created is destined to perish, whereas Allah alone is everlasting. His divine Being remains, perfect in majesty and worthy of all honor and glorification.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This repeated question addresses humans and jinn, confronting them with the abundance of God’s blessings and calling them to recognize His grace rather than deny or overlook it.

translation: All those in the heavens and the earth ask of Him; every day He is engaged in a matter.
interpretation: Every creature is dependent upon Allah for its existence, sustenance, guidance, and relief. He continuously governs creation with wisdom, bringing about new states and events without ever being occupied or diminished by one act from attending to another.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humans and jinn, challenging them to recognize that none of their Lord’s blessings and signs can rightly be denied, and calling them to respond with gratitude and acknowledgment.

translation: We will attend to you, O two weighty beings.
interpretation: Allah warns humankind and the jinn that He will devote Himself to judging and recompensing them for their deeds; no one will be able to escape His reckoning.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humans and jinn, challenging them to acknowledge that every blessing, provision, and sign of divine mercy comes from Allah and cannot truthfully be denied.

translation: O assembly of jinn and humankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond them. You will not pass beyond them except with authority.
interpretation: This verse challenges jinn and human beings to recognize that they cannot escape the limits and dominion established by Allah through their own power. Any ability to penetrate the vast realms of creation or overcome its boundaries would depend entirely on an authority, power, and permission granted by Him—not on independent human or jinn capability.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Allah addresses humankind and jinn, reminding them that His countless blessings and signs leave no rightful basis for denial; they are called to recognize His grace and respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: عليكما ستُرسَل لهبٌ من نارٍ ودخانٌ أو نحاسٌ مذاب، فلن تنتصرا.
interpretation: المعنى أن الإنس والجن، إذا حاولوا الفرار من سلطان الله يوم القيامة، يُحاصَرون بعذابٍ لا يستطيعون دفعه ولا الإفلات منه؛ فلا نجاة لهم إلا برحمة الله وإذنه.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humankind and jinn, urging them to recognize the countless favors of their Lord and warning them against denying or taking any of them for granted.

translation: Then, when the sky is split apart and becomes rose-red like oil.
interpretation: This portrays the terrifying upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when the sky loses its familiar order and takes on a molten, crimson appearance, revealing the overwhelming power of God.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: The verse challenges both humans and jinn to acknowledge the countless blessings and signs of Allah rather than denying or taking them for granted.

translation: Then, on that Day, neither human nor jinn will be asked about his sin.
interpretation: المعنى أن أهوال القيامة وظهور الحقائق تجعل الذنوب معلومة ظاهرة، فلا يكون السؤال يومئذ طلبًا للمعرفة أو الاستعلام، بل يُحاسَب كل إنسان على ما اقترف ويُجازى عليه؛ وهذا لا يتعارض مع ورود سؤالٍ آخر في مواقف الحساب للتوبيخ وإقامة الحجة.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humankind and the jinn, confronting them with the abundance of Allah’s blessings and calling them to acknowledge His favors with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: The guilty will be recognized by their marks, then seized by their forelocks and their feet.
interpretation: This portrays the unmistakable exposure and humiliation of those who persisted in sin: their outward signs reveal their inner state, and they are forcibly dragged by the forelocks and feet to face judgment and punishment.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: يخاطب الله الإنس والجن معًا، مستنكرًا إنكار نعمه الظاهرة والباطنة، وداعيًا إلى الاعتراف بفضله وشكره بدل الجحود.

translation: This is Hell, which the criminals denied.
interpretation: It is a rebuke to those who rejected the truth: the Hell they denied is now made manifest before them as the undeniable consequence of their defiance.

translation: They will circulate between it and scalding water of unbearable heat.
interpretation: The verse portrays the punishment of Hell as an inescapable torment: its inhabitants are driven back and forth between the blazing Fire and intensely boiling water, finding no relief or place of refuge.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical admonition addressed to both humans and jinn: in view of God’s countless signs, blessings, and acts of mercy, neither can reasonably deny His grace or fail to acknowledge it with gratitude and submission.

translation: And for whoever fears standing before his Lord are two gardens.
interpretation: Whoever remains conscious of standing before Allah and therefore restrains himself from disobedience and lives in obedience will be honored with two gardens of Paradise.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: This verse repeatedly calls humankind and the jinn to recognize that every blessing they enjoy comes from Allah, leaving them no valid excuse to deny His favors or fail to show gratitude and obedience.

translation: Having abundant, spreading branches.
interpretation: The two gardens are described as lush and flourishing, with plentiful branches that provide beauty, shade, and signs of abundant life.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: The verse challenges humans and jinn to honestly recognize and not reject any of the countless blessings, signs, and mercies bestowed by their Lord.

translation: In them are two flowing springs.
interpretation: The two gardens contain two springs whose water runs continuously and abundantly, symbolizing the unfailing provision and delight prepared for their inhabitants.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a repeated admonition to humans and jinn to recognize that every blessing and sign from Allah is undeniable, and to respond with gratitude rather than denial.

translation: In both of them are two kinds of every fruit.
interpretation: The two gardens contain an abundance of fruits, with each kind presented in varied forms and qualities, reflecting the completeness and richness of the bliss prepared for their inhabitants.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a repeated admonition to humankind and the jinn, calling them to recognize that every blessing, sign, and act of mercy from their Lord deserves gratitude rather than denial.

translation: Reclining on couches whose linings are brocade, with the fruits of the two gardens close at hand.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise in complete comfort and honor: their resting places are richly adorned, and the gardens’ fruits are brought so near that they can reach them with ease.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question addresses both humankind and the jinn, urging them to recognize that none of Allah’s blessings, signs, and acts of mercy can rightly be denied.

translation: In them are maidens of restrained gaze, whom no human or jinn has touched before them.
interpretation: This portrays the companions of Paradise as embodying modesty, purity, and exclusive devotion, untouched by anyone before the believers who are granted them.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This question is a profound admonition to humankind and jinn: in the face of God’s countless blessings, signs, and mercies, neither can honestly reject or disregard His grace and sovereignty.

translation: As though they were rubies and coral.
interpretation: This portrays the women of Paradise as possessing exceptional beauty, purity, and radiance, comparable to the clarity and preciousness of rubies and coral.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This recurring question challenges both humankind and the jinn to recognize that none of their Lord’s blessings can rightly be denied, and calls them to respond with gratitude and obedience.

translation: Is the reward for excellence anything other than excellence?
interpretation: This is a divine affirmation that sincere goodness—faith, worship, gratitude, and kindness—will not be lost; God repays it with goodness, mercy, and a fitting reward.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: The verse repeatedly confronts both humans and jinn with the undeniable blessings, signs, and acts of mercy bestowed by their Lord, urging them to acknowledge His favors with gratitude rather than deny them.

translation: And besides them are two other gardens.
interpretation: This indicates two additional gardens of Paradise, distinct from the two previously described, as another form of divine reward.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This repeated question calls both humankind and the jinn to recognize that every blessing they possess comes from Allah and to reject the ingratitude of denying His favors.

translation: They are intensely green.
interpretation: The two gardens are described as lush and deep green, expressing their abundant vegetation, freshness, and flourishing beauty.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a repeated admonition to humans and jinn: in the face of the countless blessings, signs, and acts of mercy bestowed by God, neither can honestly deny His favors or the duty of gratitude they entail.

translation: In them are two gushing springs.
interpretation: The verse depicts the two gardens as possessing springs that flow abundantly and continuously, expressing the ease, freshness, and perfect delight prepared for their inhabitants.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: Allah repeatedly challenges humankind and the jinn to recognize His countless blessings and proofs, leaving no valid excuse for denying His generosity, power, and signs.

translation: In both are fruits, date palms, and pomegranates.
interpretation: This portrays the two gardens as places of abundant, varied, and wholesome nourishment, where familiar fruits such as dates and pomegranates are singled out to emphasize the richness and excellence of their blessings.

translation: So which of your Lord’s blessings will you both deny?
interpretation: Allah repeatedly addresses both humankind and the jinn, challenging them to acknowledge His countless favors and warning that denying or failing to appreciate them is a form of ingratitude.

translation: In them are women of noble character and beauty.
interpretation: This describes the companions of Paradise as possessing both inner virtue and outward beauty, reflecting the complete and pure nature of the blessings prepared for its inhabitants.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This verse is a repeated divine challenge to humans and jinn: in the face of the countless blessings, signs, and acts of mercy granted by their Lord, they have no valid basis for denying or being ungrateful for any of them.

translation: Fair maidens, secluded in pavilions.
interpretation: This describes purified companions of Paradise who are honored, protected, and reserved within splendid dwellings, conveying their chastity, dignity, and the security of the blessed life in Paradise.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a repeated divine admonition to humankind and the jinn: in the face of God’s countless blessings, signs, and acts of mercy, neither should deny or remain ungrateful for any of them.

translation: No human or jinn has touched them before them.
interpretation: This describes the purity and untouched state of the women of Paradise, emphasizing that they have been preserved exclusively for their companions and have had no previous intimate relationship with either humans or jinn.

translation: فبأيِّ نعمِ ربِّكما تُكذِّبان؟
interpretation: يُخاطِب اللهُ الإنسَ والجنَّ مؤكِّدًا كثرة نعمه عليهما، ومتحدِّيًا إيّاهما أن ينكرا شيئًا منها أو يجحدا استحقاقه للشكر.

translation: Reclining on green cushions and splendid carpets.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise resting in complete comfort and honor, surrounded by exquisite furnishings that reflect the beauty, abundance, and serenity of their everlasting reward.

translation: So which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reminder to humankind and the jinn that, in the face of God’s countless blessings and signs, they have no valid basis for denying or being ungrateful for any of them.

translation: Blessed and exalted is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor.
interpretation: Allah’s name is supremely exalted and a source of abundant blessing, for He alone possesses perfect majesty and generosity; therefore, He deserves the deepest reverence, gratitude, and devotion.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the Inevitable Event occurs,
interpretation: The verse opens by announcing the certain arrival of the Day of Resurrection, an event whose occurrence cannot be prevented or denied, signaling the beginning of the ultimate judgment before Allah.

translation: There is no denying its occurrence.
interpretation: When the Final Hour arrives, its reality will be undeniable; no claim, excuse, or falsehood will be able to reject that it has truly come.

translation: Bringing some low and raising others.
interpretation: The Day of Judgment will abase the arrogant and those who rejected the truth, while elevating the believers and the righteous to honor and everlasting success.

translation: When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking,
interpretation: This portrays the earth’s complete upheaval at the onset of the Day of Resurrection, when its familiar stability is destroyed and humanity is confronted with the absolute power of God and the certainty of judgment.

translation: And the mountains will be utterly pulverized.
interpretation: This depicts the mountains losing their immense solidity and being crushed into fine dust, signifying the total upheaval of the created world on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Then they will become scattered dust.
interpretation: The mountains, once firmly rooted, will be shattered and dispersed into countless particles, illustrating the overwhelming transformation of the world on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And you will be three kinds.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, all people will be divided according to their faith and deeds into three distinct ranks: the foremost in righteousness, the people of the right, and the people of the left.

translation: Then the companions of the right—what can be known of the companions of the right?
interpretation: This expresses profound exaltation of those who receive their record in the right hand, indicating their honored status and the greatness of the blessings prepared for them.

translation: And the companions of the left—what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This expression magnifies the dreadful fate of those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing: they will be distinguished by their miserable position and will face a terrifying outcome in the Hereafter.

translation: And the foremost are the foremost.
interpretation: Those who hasten ahead in faith, obedience, and righteous deeds are the foremost in attaining Allah’s nearness and honor.

translation: Those are the ones brought near [to Allah].
interpretation: They are the people granted a special rank of closeness to Allah because of their sincere faith, devoted worship, and righteous deeds.

translation: In gardens of bliss.
interpretation: This describes the eternal abode of the righteous, where they will enjoy complete and lasting happiness, peace, and divine favor.

translation: A multitude from the former peoples,
interpretation: This refers to a large number of people from the earlier generations who will attain the honored rank of those brought near to Allah.

translation: And only a few of the later ones.
interpretation: This indicates that, compared with the earliest believers, relatively few people from later generations attain the foremost rank in faith and obedience.

translation: Upon couches richly woven and adorned.
interpretation: This depicts the people of Paradise resting upon seats of exceptional beauty and honor, symbolizing their everlasting comfort and exalted status.

translation: Reclining upon them, facing one another.
interpretation: The people of Paradise will rest comfortably on their couches, sitting in harmony and affection, with each person turned toward the others rather than isolated or estranged.

translation: Immortal youths will circulate among them.
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Paradise being served continuously by youthful attendants whose beauty, freshness, and unchanging condition reflect the everlasting comfort and honor of the life to come.

translation: With cups, pitchers, and a goblet of flowing drink.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية كرامة أهل الجنة ووفرة شرابهم الطيب، فهو حاضر بين أيديهم في أوانٍ متنوعة، مستمدّ من عين جارية لا تنقطع.

translation: They will neither suffer headache from it nor become intoxicated.
interpretation: The drink of Paradise brings pure pleasure without the pain, harm, or loss of reason associated with worldly intoxicants.

translation: And fruits of whatever they choose,
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise enjoying an abundance of fruits, with complete freedom to choose whatever they desire, reflecting their honored and effortless state of bliss.

translation: And the flesh of birds of whatever they desire.
interpretation: This portrays the people of Paradise receiving whatever nourishing and delightful food they desire, expressing the complete fulfillment and generosity of their eternal reward.

translation: And fair companions with beautiful eyes.
interpretation: This describes among the blessings of Paradise pure and beautiful companions, signifying the honor, joy, and intimate companionship granted to its inhabitants.

translation: Like pearls preserved within their shells.
interpretation: This portrays purity, beauty, and preciousness, emphasizing something untouched, perfectly preserved, and free from every impurity.

translation: As a recompense for what they used to do.
interpretation: This means that the reward or outcome granted to them is a just consequence of their persistent deeds, reflecting God’s perfect justice in repaying people according to what they earned.

translation: They will hear therein neither vain talk nor sinful speech.
interpretation: The people of Paradise will be surrounded by pure and harmonious speech, free from useless words, lies, insults, and anything that causes guilt or harm.

translation: Except for the saying: “Peace, peace.”
interpretation: The people of Paradise will hear no futile or harmful speech; their words and the words addressed to them will be expressions of peace, safety, and mutual goodwill.

translation: And the companions of the right—what are the companions of the right?
interpretation: This rhetorical question magnifies the honor and blessed status of those who receive their records in their right hands, indicating their exalted rank and immense felicity with God.

translation: في أشجار السِّدر المنزوعة الشوك.
interpretation: أي أنهم ينعمون في ظلال أشجار سِدر لطيفة أزيلت أشواكها، فلا تنغّص راحتهم ولا تؤذيهم.

translation: And clustered banana trees,
interpretation: This depicts the abundant, luxuriant trees of Paradise, bearing fruit in successive, densely packed clusters and offering continual nourishment and delight.

translation: And extended shade,
interpretation: This depicts the enduring comfort and serenity prepared for the people of Paradise, where shade is plentiful, expansive, and never disappears.

translation: And water poured forth,
interpretation: It signifies abundant, pure water flowing continuously as one of the blessings prepared in Paradise.

translation: And abundant fruit,
interpretation: This describes the plentiful and ever-available fruits of Paradise, offered in abundance without scarcity or interruption.

translation: Neither exhausted nor withheld.
interpretation: The provision of Paradise is everlasting and freely available: it does not run out, and no one deserving of it is prevented from enjoying it.

translation: And elevated couches,
interpretation: The verse depicts the honored people of Paradise resting on lofty, splendid furnishings prepared for their comfort and dignity.

translation: Indeed, We have brought them into being in a unique creation.
interpretation: Allah describes the women of Paradise as being created anew in a perfect, pure, and everlasting form, free from the deficiencies and limitations of worldly life.

translation: So We made them virgins.
interpretation: Allah describes the women of Paradise as being created in a state of perpetual freshness, purity, and renewed youth, free from the effects of age and earthly decline.

translation: Loving companions, of equal age.
interpretation: This describes the purified spouses of Paradise as deeply affectionate and harmonious with their companions, sharing the same age and thus enjoying perfect compatibility and companionship.

translation: For those on the right.
interpretation: This refers to the righteous whom Allah honors with salvation and felicity, symbolized by receiving their records in their right hands.

translation: A multitude from the former peoples.
interpretation: This refers to a large number of the foremost believers being from the earlier generations and nations.

translation: And a group of the later ones.
interpretation: This indicates that, in addition to the foremost believers, many people from later generations will also attain nearness to Allah and the honor of Paradise through faith and righteousness.

translation: And the companions of the left—what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical expression of astonishment and dread, emphasizing the terrible condition and fate awaiting those who rejected the truth and lived in disobedience.

translation: في ريحٍ حارّةٍ وماءٍ شديدِ الغليان.
interpretation: تصوّر العبارة حالَ أهل العذاب، إذ يحيط بهم هواءٌ لافحٌ يحرق الأجساد وماءٌ بالغُ الحرارة، فلا يجدون ملجأً من شدة العذاب.

translation: وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ: and a shade of black smoke.
interpretation: This describes the punishment of Hell: a dark, suffocating shadow of smoke that offers neither coolness nor relief, unlike the comforting shade enjoyed by the righteous.

translation: Neither cool nor refreshing.
interpretation: It refers to a shade that provides no relief, comfort, or benefit; it is oppressive rather than pleasant or generous.

translation: Indeed, before that they had lived in luxury.
interpretation: They were accustomed to ease and indulgence, which led them to become heedless of their duty to God and unresponsive to the truth.

translation: And they persisted in the great sin.
interpretation: They knowingly continued in grave disobedience—especially associating partners with Allah—without repentance or abandoning their wrongdoing.

translation: And they used to say, “When we have died and become dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?”
interpretation: They expressed disbelief in the resurrection, considering it impossible that God could restore human beings after their bodies had decayed into dust and bones.

translation: “Or our forefathers of old?”
interpretation: They object mockingly, questioning whether their ancient ancestors will also be resurrected, as though the passage of time makes resurrection impossible.

translation: Say: Indeed, the earlier generations and the later generations,
interpretation: This opening affirms that all human generations—those who came before and those who come after—are equally included in God’s judgment and reckoning.

translation: You will surely all be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day.
interpretation: This affirms that resurrection and judgment will occur at a निश्चित, divinely determined time; no person will be able to escape being brought before God for accountability.

translation: Then indeed you, O those who have gone astray and denied the truth,
interpretation: This is a stern address to those who knowingly reject divine guidance, describing their denial as the result of having strayed from the path of truth.

translation: You will surely eat from a tree of Zaqqūm,
interpretation: This portrays the condemned in the Hereafter being forced to consume the bitter, terrifying tree of Zaqqūm as a punishment, in stark contrast to the nourishing food of Paradise.

translation: Then you will fill your bellies with it.
interpretation: This depicts the people of Hell being compelled by intense hunger to eat from the tree of Zaqqūm, an agonizing form of punishment rather than nourishment.

translation: Then you will drink boiling water over it.
interpretation: This portrays the severe punishment of those who reject the truth: after consuming the bitter, tormenting food, they are forced to drink scalding water, intensifying their suffering rather than relieving it.

translation: Then you will drink as thirsty camels drink.
interpretation: You will drink the scalding water of Hell with desperate, repeated thirst, like camels afflicted by a disease that makes them endlessly crave water, yet without ever finding relief.

translation: This is their welcome on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: It means that the punishment described for those who deny the truth will be their appointed reception and provision when they are raised for judgment, presented as a fitting consequence of their rejection.

translation: We created you, so why do you not believe?
interpretation: God reminds humanity that their very existence is proof of His creative power and authority; therefore, they should affirm His truth, accept resurrection, and live in submission to Him rather than deny His signs.

translation: Have you considered the sperm you emit?
interpretation: Reflect on the humble origin of human life: what a person emits is merely a small, powerless substance, yet from it God brings forth a living human being. This reveals that creation and its outcome belong to God, not to human control.

translation: Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?
interpretation: The verse reminds human beings that although they may take part in natural processes, they possess no power to originate life independently; its true creation and determining power belong solely to Allah.

translation: We have decreed death among you, and We cannot be thwarted.
interpretation: Death comes to every person by Allah’s appointed decree, and no one can escape, delay, or prevent what He has ordained; His power and judgment always prevail.

translation: لِنُبَدِّلَ أمثالكم وننشئكم فيما لا تعلمون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن قدرته مطلقة؛ فكما أنشأ الإنسان أول مرة، يستطيع أن يستبدل به خلقًا آخر أو يعيده في هيئة ونشأة لا يدركها البشر، فلا يعجزه البعث ولا إعادة الخلق.

translation: You have already known the first creation, so why will you not take heed?
interpretation: Since you have witnessed how Allah brought you into existence from nothing, you should recognize that recreating you after death is within His power and heed the certainty of the resurrection.

translation: Have you considered what you cultivate?
interpretation: Reflect on the crops you plant and tend: although people exert effort in cultivating the earth, the power that brings the seed to life and produces the harvest ultimately belongs to Allah.

translation: Is it you who grow it, or are We the Growers?
interpretation: The verse directs people to recognize that although they plant and cultivate, the power that causes crops to grow and produce lies with Allah. It calls them to humility and gratitude for His sustaining provision.

translation: If We willed, We could turn it into dry, broken debris, leaving you bewildered.
interpretation: The verse reminds people that the crops and blessings they rely upon remain entirely subject to Allah’s will; He could destroy them instantly, leaving them astonished and regretful over their dependence and lack of gratitude.

translation: Indeed, we are burdened with debt.
interpretation: This expresses the despair of people who, after losing what they expected to gain, find themselves financially ruined and unable to recover their losses.

translation: Rather, we are deprived.
interpretation: They recognize that they have been denied the harvest they expected, realizing that their misjudgment and refusal to acknowledge the rights of others has brought about their loss.

translation: Have you considered the water that you drink?
interpretation: Reflect on the water that sustains your life: its existence, purity, and availability are not ultimately within human control, but are blessings provided by Allah and signs of His power and mercy.

translation: أفأنتم أنزلتموه من السحاب الممطر، أم نحن المنزلون له؟
interpretation: يذكّر الله الإنسان بأن نزول المطر ليس بقدرته ولا بتدبيره، بل هو من تقدير الله وإنزاله؛ ليوقظ فيه الاعتراف بربوبية الله وشكره على أصل الحياة والرزق.

translation: Had We willed, We could have made it bitter and undrinkable; so why are you not grateful?
interpretation: The verse reminds people that the drinkable water they depend on is a divine blessing, not something guaranteed by nature alone. Since God can withhold its sweetness and make it unusable, recognizing His power should lead to sincere gratitude and obedience.

translation: Have you considered the fire that you kindle?
interpretation: Reflect on the fire you ignite: although its causes and fuel are within your control, its existence and power ultimately depend on God, reminding you of His creative authority and the blessings He has placed at your disposal.

translation: Is it you who brought forth its tree, or are We the One who brought it forth?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question exposing human dependence and affirming that the power behind the creation and growth of the tree—and thus the means by which fire is produced—belongs solely to God, not to human beings.

translation: We have made it a reminder and a provision for travelers.
interpretation: The fire is a reminder of God’s power and of the Fire of the Hereafter, while also serving as a practical benefit for people journeying through barren lands, providing them warmth, light, and a means to prepare food.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: Exalt your Lord by declaring His perfection and greatness, recognizing that He is far above every imperfection and worthy of supreme praise and worship.

translation: فلا، أقسم بمواقع النجوم.
interpretation: يقسم الله تعالى بمواقع النجوم ومنازلها الدقيقة؛ لما فيها من عظيم الصنعة وإحكام التدبير، تمهيدًا لتأكيد عظمة الوحي وصدقه.

translation: And indeed, it is a mighty oath, if only you knew.
interpretation: This emphasizes the immense significance and truth of the divine oath, whose greatness surpasses ordinary human understanding.

translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an.
interpretation: This affirms the Qur’an’s exalted status, purity, and profound worth: it is divine revelation honored in its source, message, and guidance, and therefore deserves reverence and careful adherence.

translation: في كتابٍ مكنونٍ.
interpretation: المقصود أن القرآن محفوظٌ مصونٌ في كتابٍ مستورٍ عن العبث والتحريف، بما يدل على علوّ منزلته وقداسة مصدره.

translation: None touch it except the purified.
interpretation: الضمير في «يمسّه» يعود إلى الكتاب المكنون المذكور في السياق؛ أي إن هذا الكتاب المصون لا يباشره إلا الملائكة المطهّرون، وفي ذلك بيان لعلوّ منزلة الوحي ونزاهته عن أيدي الشياطين.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This affirms that the Qur’an comes directly from God, the Creator and Sustainer of every realm, and therefore carries divine authority rather than being a human composition.

translation: أفبهذا الحديث أنتم مدهنون؟
interpretation: أفبهذا القرآن تتهاونون وتساومون في الحق، فتلقونه بالفتور أو التملّق بدل الإيمان به وتعظيمه؟

translation: And you make your share of provision that you deny the truth.
interpretation: You respond to the blessings through which God sustains you not with gratitude, but with denial—attributing them to other causes or rejecting the One who bestowed them.

translation: So why, when it reaches the throat—
interpretation: When the soul reaches the throat at the moment of death, this exposes human helplessness: despite all claims of power, no one can prevent its departure or return it to the body.

translation: And you, at that moment, will be watching.
interpretation: You will witness the person’s final moments, yet remain powerless to prevent what is taking place.

translation: And We are nearer to him than you are, but you do not see.
interpretation: Allah is nearer to the dying person than those gathered around him through His complete knowledge, authority, and control over his soul, although this divine nearness is beyond human perception.

translation: So why, if you are not to be held accountable,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge: if you deny that you are subject to God’s judgment and recompense, then you should be able to prevent the soul from departing at death—but you cannot.

translation: If you are truthful, then bring it back.
interpretation: This is a challenge to those witnessing death: if they truly possess power and control, let them return the departing soul. Their inability reveals that life and death lie solely in Allah’s power.

translation: فأما إن كان من المقرَّبين
interpretation: فإن كان المتوفّى من عباد الله الذين قرّبهم إليه بطاعته وإخلاصه، فله عند الله كرامة وأمان ورحمة.

translation: Then there will be rest, fragrance, and a Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This promises the believer whose soul is welcomed by God a state of peace and comfort, pleasant provision, and eternal residence in Paradise.

translation: But if he is one of those on the right,
interpretation: This refers to the person who receives his record with his right hand and is counted among the people of faith and righteousness, signifying his salvation and honor in the Hereafter.

translation: So peace be upon you; you are among the companions of the right.
interpretation: This is a greeting of divine reassurance and honor for those who lived in faith and obedience, affirming their safety and blessed rank in the Hereafter.

translation: But if he was one of those who denied the truth and went astray,
interpretation: This refers to the person who rejected faith and deviated from divine guidance; such denial and misguidance lead to a deprived and grievous end in the Hereafter.

translation: Then his welcome will be scalding water.
interpretation: The phrase depicts the condemned person’s reception in the Hereafter: instead of honor or comfort, he is met with boiling water as a humiliating punishment.

translation: and burning in Hellfire
interpretation: It signifies being subjected to the intense torment of the blazing Hellfire.

translation: Indeed, this is surely the truth of certainty.
interpretation: What has been described is not conjecture or mere report; it is an absolutely certain reality, established beyond any doubt.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.
interpretation: Exalt and sanctify your Lord by praising Him and affirming His absolute greatness, perfection, and transcendence above all shortcomings.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Everything in the universe declares Allah’s perfection and submits to His order, whether through conscious worship or through the way it follows the laws He established. His absolute might ensures that nothing can resist His decree, while His perfect wisdom gives purpose and harmony to all that exists.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: All creation is under Allah’s complete ownership and authority; life and death occur solely by His will, and nothing lies beyond His ability or control.

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: Allah is without beginning or end; nothing precedes Him and nothing outlasts Him. His existence and power are evident through His signs, yet His essence is beyond created perception. Nothing, whether apparent or concealed, lies outside His complete knowledge.

translation: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne. He knows what enters the earth, what emerges from it, what descends from the sky, and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees all that you do.
interpretation: The verse affirms Allah’s absolute sovereignty over creation and His complete knowledge of every occurrence, whether hidden within the earth, emerging from it, descending from above, or rising upward. His being “with you” means that His knowledge, awareness, and power encompass people wherever they are, while His sight of their deeds reminds them that nothing they do is concealed from Him.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all affairs return.
interpretation: All authority and control belong exclusively to Allah, and every matter ultimately comes back to Him for judgment, resolution, and accountability.

translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He knows well what is within the hearts.
interpretation: The alternation and gradual interweaving of night and day display God’s complete power and governance over creation, while His knowledge encompasses not only what people openly do but also the intentions, thoughts, and secrets concealed within them.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from what He has entrusted to you. Those among you who believe and spend will have a great reward.
interpretation: The wealth and resources people possess are a trust from Allah, not an absolute possession. True faith is therefore shown by using that trust generously for righteous purposes, with the assurance that sincere belief and giving are greatly rewarded.

translation: And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are truly believers?
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who hesitate to embrace faith despite the Messenger’s clear invitation and the evidence that establishes their responsibility before God. The covenant refers to the innate recognition of God and the binding commitment conveyed through revelation; therefore, true faith requires responding sincerely to the Messenger rather than remaining in heedlessness.

translation: He is the One who sends down clear verses to His servant so that he may bring you out of darkness into the light. Indeed, Allah is Most Kind and Most Merciful to you.
interpretation: Allah reveals unmistakable guidance through His Messenger to free people from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and moral confusion and lead them into the light of faith, truth, and righteous living. This act of guidance reflects His profound gentleness and mercy toward humanity.

translation: And why should you not spend in the way of Allah, while the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah? Those among you who spent and fought before the Victory are not equal to those who spent and fought afterward. They are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterward—yet Allah has promised the finest reward to all. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: Allah urges believers to spend for His cause, reminding them that everything ultimately returns to Him and that withholding wealth is misplaced attachment. Those who supported the faith through sacrifice and struggle before its decisive triumph demonstrated greater sincerity and courage, so their rank is higher than that of those who acted when Islam was already strengthened. Nevertheless, every sincere believer who spends and strives is promised Allah’s gracious reward, while Allah perfectly knows the motives and deeds of each person.

translation: Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan, so that He may multiply it for him, and he will have a generous reward?
interpretation: Allah uses the expression “a good loan” to honor sincere acts of charity and obedience offered for His sake, although He is free of all need. Such giving is promised abundant multiplication in reward, together with an ennobling recompense from Him.

translation: On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light hastening before them and on their right, [they will be told], “Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which you will abide forever. That is the supreme triumph.”
interpretation: The light accompanying the believers signifies the faith and righteous guidance that Allah grants them, becoming a source of honor and security on the Day of Judgment. Their being welcomed into everlasting gardens shows that true success is not worldly achievement, but attaining Allah’s acceptance and eternal nearness through sincere faith and righteous deeds.

translation: On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believe, “Wait for us so that we may draw from your light.” It will be said, “Go back and seek light.” Then a wall will be placed between them, with a gate: within it is mercy, while outside it, facing them, is punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays the ultimate exposure of hypocrisy: those who appeared outwardly among the believers but lacked sincere faith will find themselves separated from them when the reality of the Hereafter becomes manifest. Their plea to share the believers’ light is rejected because spiritual light cannot be borrowed at the moment of judgment; it is the outcome of genuine faith and righteous commitment cultivated in worldly life. The wall symbolizes a decisive barrier between divine mercy and punishment, with its inward side indicating the security granted to the sincere and its outward side revealing the deprivation of those who concealed disbelief behind religious appearance.

translation: They will call out to them, “Were we not with you?” They will say, “Yes, but you tempted yourselves, waited for misfortune to befall us, doubted, and were deceived by false hopes until Allah’s command came. And the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah.”
interpretation: This depicts the hypocrites’ false claim of belonging to the believers being exposed in the Hereafter. Their outward association brought them no benefit because they corrupted themselves through insincerity, hesitation, doubt, and reliance on empty hopes, while Satan misled them into presuming that Allah’s mercy and delay meant they could persist without repentance. The verse warns that faith is not established by mere outward affiliation, but by sincere conviction and steadfast obedience before the final judgment arrives.

translation: So today no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your abode is the Fire; it is your fitting companion—and what an evil destination.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, faith and repentance can no longer be acquired, and wealth or any substitute cannot avert punishment; those who persisted in disbelief and hypocrisy will find only the Fire as the consequence and fitting result of their choices.

translation: Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of Allah and at what has been revealed of the truth, and that they should not become like those who were given the Scripture before them? Then a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This is a tender but urgent call for believers to respond inwardly to Allah’s remembrance and revelation with humility, reverence, and obedience. Faith must not be allowed to become mere habit, for prolonged heedlessness and delay in acting upon the truth can harden the heart, weaken spiritual sensitivity, and lead a person toward disobedience, as happened to many earlier communities.

translation: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have indeed made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand.
interpretation: Just as Allah revives barren land with rain, He can revive hardened hearts through faith and guidance, and this visible renewal is a sign that the dead will likewise be raised and that people should reflect and understand.

translation: Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and who lend Allah a good loan—it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: Allah honors sincere charitable giving by describing it as a good loan to Him, although He is in no need of anyone’s wealth. This expression emphasizes that what believers spend for His sake is securely preserved and abundantly multiplied, with an excellent reward beyond the value of their worldly contribution.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and His messengers—it is they who are the steadfastly truthful. And the martyrs are with their Lord; they have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—they are the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: True faith in Allah and His messengers produces sincerity, steadfastness, and truthfulness, while those who sacrifice their lives for that faith are honored in God’s presence with lasting reward and spiritual light. In contrast, rejecting faith and treating God’s signs as false leads to the punishment of the Hellfire.

translation: Know that the life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment, mutual boasting among you, and rivalry in the abundance of wealth and children. It is like rain whose resulting vegetation pleases the disbelieving farmers; then it dries up, and you see it turn yellow, then become debris. In the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse teaches that worldly attractions are temporary and easily become objects of vanity when pursued as ends in themselves. Like vegetation that flourishes briefly before withering away, wealth, status, beauty, and family prosperity inevitably fade; therefore, a wise person should not be deceived by them, but should seek Allah’s forgiveness and approval, which alone endure beyond this life.

translation: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and toward a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to hasten toward repentance, faith, and righteous action rather than delay, seeking Allah’s forgiveness and the immense reward He has prepared. Paradise is described in terms of vastness beyond human measure, while its attainment is ultimately an expression of Allah’s grace, which He bestows according to His wisdom—not something anyone can claim by deeds alone.

translation: No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves except that it is recorded in a Book before We bring it into being. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse teaches that every event affecting the world and human beings occurs within Allah’s prior knowledge and decree, recorded before its occurrence. This affirms His complete wisdom and control, while reminding people that nothing happens beyond His knowledge or power.

translation: So that you may not grieve excessively over what has escaped you, nor exult arrogantly over what He has granted you. And Allah does not love anyone who is conceited and boastful.
interpretation: The verse teaches that a believer should maintain balanced reliance on Allah: worldly losses should not lead to despair, and worldly blessings should not produce pride or self-glorification, since both the giving and withholding of them occur by Allah’s wisdom.

translation: Those who are miserly and urge people to miserliness. And whoever turns away—surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse condemns not only withholding the blessings one has been given, but also encouraging others to adopt the same selfishness. Whoever rejects obedience and generosity does not diminish Allah in any way, for He is completely independent of creation and worthy of praise in all circumstances.

translation: We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Scripture and the balance, so that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is great strength and benefits for people, so that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Almighty.
interpretation: Allah established justice through revelation and the moral balance by which people distinguish truth from falsehood and right from wrong. He also placed in iron the power and practical benefits needed to protect justice and build human life. Thus, faith is not merely inward belief; it requires standing with truth and supporting Allah’s messengers even when they are unseen, while Allah remains entirely powerful and independent of His creation.

translation: ولقد أرسلنا نوحًا وإبراهيم، وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب؛ فمنهم مهتدٍ، وكثيرٌ منهم فاسقون.
interpretation: يبين الله أن اصطفاء نوح وإبراهيم بالرسالة، وما أكرم به ذريتهما من النبوة والكتب، فضلٌ إلهي لا يستلزم صلاح جميع الأبناء؛ فالهداية ثمرة قبول الحق واتباعه، بينما انحرف كثير منهم عن طاعة الله رغم قيام الحجة ووصول الوحي إليهم.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers, following in their footsteps, and We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. We placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. As for monasticism, they introduced it themselves; We did not prescribe it for them, except that they sought God’s pleasure through it. Yet they did not observe it as it ought to have been observed. So We granted those among them who believed their reward, while many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse teaches that sincere faith may produce compassion and mercy, but religious practices invented by people cannot replace what God has prescribed. Even an intention to seek God’s pleasure does not make an innovation rightly guided if it is neglected, distorted, or fails to fulfill its moral purpose. God therefore distinguishes between those who remain faithful and upright and those who abandon obedience, judging each according to belief and conduct.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will grant you a double share of His mercy, appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and forgive you. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse calls believers to deepen their faith through sincere mindfulness of Allah and obedience to His Messenger. In return, Allah promises them abundant mercy, spiritual clarity that guides their conduct through life, and forgiveness for their shortcomings—blessings that arise from His perfect forgiveness and mercy.

translation: So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no control over any of Allah’s bounty, and that all bounty belongs to Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: This teaches that divine grace is not the possession or exclusive right of any people. No one can restrict, claim authority over, or determine whom Allah blesses; revelation, guidance, and every other favor are granted solely according to His wisdom and generosity.

translation: Allah has certainly heard the words of the woman who pleaded with you concerning her husband and complained to Allah. Allah hears your conversation with each other. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse assures that no person’s grievance is overlooked by Allah, even when voiced privately and amid personal distress. He fully hears the dialogue and sees the circumstances surrounding it, so the oppressed may turn to Him with confidence that their complaint is known and will be dealt with in perfect justice.

translation: Those among you who declare their wives to be like their mothers—they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. Indeed, they are uttering words that are reprehensible and false. Yet surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse rejects the pre-Islamic practice of ẓihār, in which a husband likened his wife to his mother as a form of repudiation. Such words do not change the wife’s status into that of a mother; rather, they are sinful falsehoods. Allah’s mention of forgiveness shows that sincere repentance remains open to those who abandon this practice and follow the prescribed remedy.

translation: Those who declare their wives unlawful to them by zihār, then retract what they have said, must free a slave before the two of them touch one another. That is what you are admonished by; and Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse establishes that zihār—a pre-Islamic declaration comparing one’s wife to a permanently forbidden relative—does not actually end the marriage, but it is a grave and harmful statement that requires expiation before marital intimacy can resume. The prescribed freeing of a slave emphasizes the seriousness of the words and calls the husband to repair the harm he caused through a concrete act of responsibility.

translation: But whoever cannot find the means must fast for two consecutive months before the two spouses have intimacy. And whoever is unable to do so must feed sixty needy people. That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. These are the limits set by Allah, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes a graduated expiation for the one who declares his wife unlawful through ẓihār: if he cannot free a slave, he must fast two uninterrupted months before marital intimacy; if he is genuinely unable to fast, he must feed sixty needy people. The order and strict timing show that repentance requires both practical accountability and restraint, while the command to observe these limits is an expression of faithful obedience to Allah and His Messenger; deliberately rejecting them exposes a person to painful punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humiliated, just as those before them were humiliated. We have sent down clear verses, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberately resisting Allah’s guidance and opposing His Messenger leads to disgrace and defeat, as happened to earlier peoples who rejected the truth. The clear revelations remove any excuse for denial, and those who persist in disbelief will face a punishment that reflects the humiliation they brought upon themselves by rejecting divine guidance.

translation: On the Day when Allah raises them all, He will inform them of what they did. Allah has recorded it, while they have forgotten it. And Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This warns that no deed can disappear from divine knowledge: even what people forget or overlook remains fully preserved by Allah, and on the Day of Resurrection He will confront everyone with the complete truth of their actions, since nothing escapes His witness.

translation: Have you not seen that Allah knows all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth? No secret conversation takes place among three without Him being their fourth, nor among five without Him being their sixth, nor fewer or more than that, wherever they may be; then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah has knowledge of all things.
interpretation: This verse teaches that no private gathering, hidden intention, or secret exchange escapes Allah’s encompassing knowledge.
