His being “with” people means that His knowledge and awareness surround them wherever they are, so nothing they conceal is beyond His perception; on the Day of Resurrection, every deed will be disclosed and judged with perfect justice.

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel, then return to what they were forbidden from, conferring secretly in sin, hostility, and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you, saying to themselves, “Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?” Sufficient for them is Hell; they will enter it—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse exposes the hypocrisy of people who persist in forbidden private plotting and hostile speech despite being warned, then conceal their contempt behind deceptive greetings and mock the possibility of divine punishment. Their delay in punishment is not approval or safety; Hell awaits those who knowingly defy Allah and His Messenger.

translation: O believers, when you converse privately, do not converse about sin, hostility, or disobedience to the Messenger; rather, converse about righteousness and piety. And be mindful of Allah, to whom you will all be gathered.
interpretation: This verse teaches that private conversations must not be used to plot wrongdoing, harm others, or oppose the guidance of the Messenger. Believers should instead use them for what is morally sound and pleasing to Allah, remembering that every hidden intention and action will ultimately be brought before Him.

translation: Secret conversation is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who believe; yet he cannot harm them in the slightest except by Allah’s permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse teaches that covert plotting and whispering meant to cause fear or sorrow among believers are satanic in purpose, but they possess no independent power to harm. The believer should therefore refuse to be overcome by such anxiety and place complete trust in Allah, knowing that nothing occurs outside His wisdom and permission.

translation: O you who believe, when you are told, “Make room in gatherings,” then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, “Rise,” then rise. Allah will raise those among you who believe and those who have been granted knowledge by degrees. And Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith is demonstrated through gracious conduct and readiness to cooperate: believers should make space for others and respond respectfully when asked to move or rise, rather than clinging to privilege or position. In return, Allah promises them greater room in His mercy and honor. It also establishes that sincere faith joined with beneficial knowledge elevates a person in rank, while reminding everyone that Allah knows whether such conduct and pursuit of knowledge are genuine.

translation: O you who believe, when you privately consult the Messenger, offer a charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you cannot find the means, then surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches believers to approach private counsel with sincerity, respect, and consideration for the Messenger’s time and the needs of others. Giving charity beforehand served to distinguish genuine and necessary consultation from unnecessary requests, while the exemption for those unable to give shows that the command was not meant to impose hardship; Allah forgives their inability and is merciful toward them.

translation: Do you fear that you will have to offer charities before your private consultations? Since you did not do so, and Allah has relented toward you, then establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah is fully aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse teaches that acts of devotion should not become burdensome formalities or a means of seeking privilege; when the prescribed charity before private consultation proved difficult and was not practiced, Allah eased the matter while directing believers toward the enduring obligations of prayer, zakat, and obedience. Their outward actions remain known and accountable before Him.

translation: Have you not considered those who ally themselves with a people upon whom Allah is angry? They are neither from you nor from them, and they swear to falsehood while they know.
interpretation: The verse exposes people who outwardly associate with the believers yet secretly align themselves with those opposed to God’s guidance. Their divided loyalty leaves them belonging truly to neither side, and their deliberate false oaths reveal hypocrisy and conscious deceit rather than genuine faith.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Truly, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: توعّد الله هؤلاء بعقوبة بالغة الشدة؛ لأن أعمالهم التي أصرّوا عليها كانت قبيحة وفاسدة، فاستحقوا هذا الوعيد بسبب سوء اختيارهم وإفسادهم.

translation: They have taken their oaths as a shield, and thus turned people away from the way of Allah; so for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: They use false or insincere oaths to protect themselves from blame and conceal their hypocrisy, thereby obstructing others from faith and obedience to Allah. Their deliberate deception and resistance to the truth will result in disgraceful punishment.

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah in anything. They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: Material possessions and family ties cannot protect a person from Allah’s judgment or compensate for rejection of the truth. Lasting salvation depends on faith and obedience, not worldly status or attachments.

translation: On the Day when Allah resurrects them all, they will swear to Him just as they swear to you, thinking that they have something to stand on. Indeed, they are truly the liars.
interpretation: When they are brought before Allah, these hypocrites will persist in their false oaths, as though their worldly excuses could protect them. Their self-deception will be exposed, for they rely on falsehood while imagining that it gives them a valid defense; yet before Allah, their lies and baseless claims will be unmistakably revealed.

translation: Satan has gained mastery over them, causing them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan. Surely, the party of Satan—they are the losers.
interpretation: When people allow Satan’s influence to dominate their hearts, they become heedless of Allah and lose the moral awareness that protects them from wrongdoing. Their true loss is that, by choosing Satan’s path over obedience to Allah, they forfeit guidance and the lasting success of the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated.
interpretation: Those who persist in resisting Allah’s guidance and challenging the authority of His Messenger will ultimately suffer disgrace and become utterly deprived of honor and strength.

translation: Allah has decreed: “I will surely prevail—I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is Strong, Almighty.
interpretation: Allah has firmly established that His truth and the mission entrusted to His messengers will ultimately prevail, even if falsehood appears dominant for a time. This victory occurs by His power and decree, while those who support His messengers are called to remain steadfast and trust in His unmatched strength and authority.

translation: You will not find a people who truly believe in Allah and the Last Day showing affection and allegiance to those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they are their fathers, sons, brothers, or close relatives. They are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him. He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah. Surely, the party of Allah are the successful.
interpretation: True faith establishes a believer’s deepest allegiance to Allah and His Messenger, so no family bond may outweigh commitment to truth and righteousness. This does not permit injustice or hostility toward relatives; rather, it means that affection and loyalty must never become support for opposition to God’s guidance. Those who preserve this priority are strengthened by divine help, attain inner contentment, and receive the lasting pleasure of Allah.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation continually declares Allah’s perfection through its existence, order, and submission to the laws He has established. His absolute might is joined with perfect wisdom, so nothing occurs beyond His power or outside His wise purpose.

translation: He is the One who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, cast terror into their hearts, and they demolished their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O people of insight.
interpretation: This verse portrays the expulsion of the treacherous Jewish tribe of Banū al-Naḍīr from Medina as a lesson in the limits of worldly security. They relied on their fortified homes and assumed they were beyond defeat, while the believers initially did not expect them to depart. Yet Allah’s decree reached them through an unforeseen weakness: fear entered their hearts, leading them to destroy their own dwellings, while the believers completed what was necessary. The command to take heed calls people of understanding to recognize that power, wealth, and defensive means cannot protect those who violate divine guidance, and that apparent security is subject to Allah’s will.

translation: And had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would surely have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: Allah made their expulsion from their homeland the worldly consequence of their defiance, sparing them a more severe punishment in this life; however, exile does not remove their accountability before Him, and their ultimate punishment in the Hereafter remains the Fire.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah—surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns that deliberate defiance of Allah and rejection of His Messenger place a person in opposition to divine truth, for which Allah’s justice entails a severe punishment.

translation: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing upon their roots, it was by Allah’s permission, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse affirms that the believers’ actions in the conflict were governed by Allah’s permission and wisdom, not by arbitrary destruction. Even the differing treatment of the palm trees served a just purpose: weakening those who had persistently violated faith and covenant, and exposing their humiliation before Allah’s judgment.

translation: And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur for it any horses or camels; rather, Allah gives His messengers authority over whomever He wills. And Allah is Powerful over all things.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the property taken from the opposing people was not gained through a military expedition requiring the believers’ horses or camels, but was granted by Allah’s decree to His Messenger. It therefore belongs to Allah’s divinely established disposition through His Messenger, affirming that victory and authority come from Allah alone, not from human strength or effort.

translation: Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, the Messenger, close relatives, orphans, the needy, and the stranded traveler, so that it does not circulate only among the wealthy among you. Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it. And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes that communal wealth and resources must be administered according to divine justice, serving the public good and those in need rather than remaining concentrated among the rich. It also makes obedience to the Messenger a binding expression of obedience to Allah: believers must accept his commands, avoid what he prohibits, and maintain reverence for Allah, whose punishment is severe for those who violate His guidance.

translation: It is for the poor emigrants who were driven from their homes and their possessions, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. They are truly sincere.
interpretation: This verse honors the believers who sacrificed their homes, wealth, and worldly security for the sake of faith, seeking only Allah’s grace and approval. Their willingness to endure such loss and to support the Messenger demonstrates that their claim to faith is genuine and sincere.

translation: And those who had settled in the abode and faith before them love those who emigrated to them, and find no resentment in their hearts toward what they have been given, and give them preference over themselves, even when they are in need. And whoever is protected from the selfish greed within themselves—it is they who are successful.
interpretation: This verse portrays the believers of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants from Makkah with sincere love and generosity. Their virtue was not merely in giving, but in having hearts free from envy and resentment, preferring the needs of others to their own despite personal hardship. It teaches that true success comes through overcoming possessiveness and selfish desire, allowing faith to produce genuine brotherhood, selflessness, and generosity.

translation: And those who came after them say, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Most Kind, Most Merciful.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that sincere believers honor those who preceded them in faith by praying for their forgiveness, while purifying their own hearts from hatred, envy, and hostility toward fellow believers. It presents mercy, brotherhood, and freedom from rancor as signs of genuine faith.

translation: Have you not seen those who play the hypocrite, saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, “If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you. And if you are fought, we will surely support you”? But Allah bears witness that they are truly liars.
interpretation: The verse exposes the false loyalty of the hypocrites: they secretly assure the hostile People of the Scripture that they will share their exile and defend them, yet these promises are merely deception and will not be fulfilled. Their claim of solidarity is contradicted by Allah’s testimony, showing that allegiance built on opposition to truth is unreliable and that hidden motives cannot escape divine knowledge.

translation: If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not help them. And even if they were to help them, they would surely turn their backs and flee; then they would not be helped.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hollowness of the promises made by the hypocrites to support those opposed to the believers. Their assurances would collapse in the face of real danger: they would abandon their allies, flee from confrontation, and receive no lasting protection themselves. It teaches that reliance on deceptive political pledges is futile, for fear and betrayal reveal the weakness behind such claims.

translation: You are more terrifying in their hearts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: They fear the visible power and immediate consequences represented by the believers more intensely than they fear Allah, because their hearts lack true understanding of His greatness, authority, and ultimate judgment.

translation: They will not fight you all together except from fortified settlements or from behind walls. Their hostility among themselves is severe. You think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse portrays people who appear to stand together against a common opponent but lack genuine unity within themselves. Their mutual resentment is so strong that they avoid direct confrontation and depend on fortified positions for protection. Their division reflects a failure to understand that real strength requires sound judgment, shared purpose, and inward solidarity—not merely outward alliance.

translation: Like those shortly before them: they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who plot against truth and support wrongdoing will ultimately suffer the harmful consequences of their own actions, just as earlier peoples did, both in this world and through a painful punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: مثلُ الشيطان حين قال للإنسان: اكفر، فلما كفر قال: إني بريءٌ منك، إني أخاف الله ربَّ العالمين.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الشيطان يغوي الإنسان ويزين له الكفر، ثم يتخلى عنه عند ظهور العاقبة ولا ينفعه، متبرئًا منه خوفًا من الله؛ وفي ذلك تحذير من اتباع وعود الشيطان، إذ لا يملك لمن يطيعه نجاةً ولا يدفع عنه عذابًا.

translation: So the outcome for both of them was that they would be in the Fire, remaining there forever; and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse portrays the ultimate end of those who follow deception and persist in ظلم: they are abandoned to the consequence of their own rejection and wrongdoing, and their punishment in the Fire is a manifestation of God’s justice.

translation: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah, and let every soul consider what it has sent ahead for tomorrow. And be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to live with reverent awareness of Allah and to examine their deeds before the Day of Judgment, asking what they are preparing for their eternal future. The repetition of the command to be mindful emphasizes that sincere self-accountability must govern one’s actions, since nothing a person does is hidden from Allah.

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. They are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: Do not let neglect of Allah become so deep that you lose awareness of your true purpose, moral responsibility, and ultimate well-being. When people turn away from Him, they become spiritually heedless of what benefits or harms their own souls, and this self-neglect leads them into persistent disobedience.

translation: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the successful.
interpretation: This declares that true success is not measured by worldly status or temporary gain, but by attaining God’s acceptance and the everlasting reward of Paradise; therefore, a person should choose faith and obedience over the path that leads to punishment.

translation: Had We revealed this Qur’an to a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and splitting apart out of awe of Allah. These examples We present to people so that they may reflect.
interpretation: The verse portrays the immense power and gravity of the Qur’an: even a mountain, despite its firmness, would be overcome by awe if it truly received and understood Allah’s revelation. It therefore calls people to let the Qur’an soften their hearts and awaken sincere reflection rather than remaining unmoved by its guidance.

translation: He is Allah—there is no deity except Him—Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This affirms Allah’s absolute uniqueness and complete knowledge: nothing hidden or apparent is beyond Him. His dealings with creation are governed by encompassing compassion and mercy.

translation: He is Allah—there is no deity except Him: the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Source of Peace, the Giver of Security, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Majestic. Glory be to Allah, far above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah alone possesses absolute sovereignty and perfection. His holiness is free from every defect, He grants peace and security, watches over and protects His creation, and has irresistible power and majesty. Therefore, attributing partners or divine qualities to anyone besides Him is a falsehood that diminishes His uniqueness and glory.

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah alone brings creation into existence, gives it its distinct form, and governs it with perfect wisdom. Every being, whether consciously or by its very nature, declares His perfection, while His beautiful names reveal His absolute perfection, power, and mercy.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O believers, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, offering them affection, while they have denied the truth that has come to you and have expelled the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have gone forth striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure, how can you secretly show them affection? I know what you conceal and what you reveal. Whoever among you does this has certainly strayed from the right path.
interpretation: The verse forbids believers from giving loyal support or intimate allegiance to those who actively oppose the faith and persecute its people, especially when such allegiance conflicts with devotion to Allah. It exposes the contradiction between claiming to strive for Allah’s sake and secretly seeking closeness with His enemies, while reminding believers that Allah knows both their hidden motives and their outward actions. This warning concerns treacherous loyalty to hostile forces, not ordinary justice, kindness, or peaceful dealings with people who do not share the faith.

translation: If they gain power over you, they will be your enemies, stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil, and wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse warns believers that those who harbor hostility toward them may conceal it until they obtain the opportunity to dominate them; then their enmity will appear through harmful actions and abusive speech, accompanied by the desire to turn them away from faith.

translation: Your relatives and children will never benefit you. On the Day of Resurrection, He will judge between you; and Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: Family ties and worldly relationships cannot save a person from accountability before God. On the Day of Resurrection, each person will be judged according to their own faith and deeds, which Allah fully observes and knows.

translation: Indeed, you have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship besides Allah. We reject you, and hostility and hatred have emerged between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone”—except for Abraham’s saying to his father, “I will surely ask forgiveness for you,” though I have no power to obtain anything for you from Allah. “Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return.”
interpretation: The verse presents Abraham and the believers with him as an example of unwavering devotion to the oneness of Allah: they clearly reject idolatry and refuse to compromise the truth of faith. Their opposition is directed at disbelief and false worship, and it remains until their people abandon them and believe in Allah alone. Abraham’s promise to seek forgiveness for his father is identified as an exception, showing that such personal affection or hope for guidance must not be confused with approval of unbelief; ultimately, the believers rely on Allah, repent to Him, and entrust their final judgment to Him.

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a cause of trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This is a supplication asking Allah not to allow believers’ weakness, defeat, or wrongdoing to become a means by which disbelievers are strengthened in their rejection or led to mock the truth, while seeking His forgiveness and relying on His perfect power and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, you have an excellent example in them—for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away, then surely Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: Those who remain faithful to Allah despite pressure to compromise provide a model for believers whose hope is fixed on divine approval and the Hereafter. Turning away from this path does not diminish Allah in any way, for He is independent of all creation and worthy of praise regardless of their obedience.

translation: Perhaps Allah will establish affection between you and those of them whom you have treated as enemies. Allah is Powerful, and Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Even when hostility has divided believers from those who oppose them, they should not regard reconciliation as impossible. Allah can transform enmity into sincere affection through faith, changed circumstances, and acts of mercy; therefore, believers should leave the door open to peace and trust in His power and forgiveness.

translation: Allah does not forbid you from showing kindness and dealing justly with those who have not fought you because of your faith or driven you from your homes. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse permits and encourages benevolent, fair, and respectful relations with people who are peaceful toward Muslims, regardless of their faith. Hostility is not to be assumed merely because of religious difference; rather, justice and good conduct are obligations toward those who do not persecute or expel others.

translation: Allah only forbids you from taking as allies those who fought you because of your faith, drove you from your homes, or supported your expulsion. Whoever takes them as allies—such people are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse restricts the prohibition to people who have actively persecuted the believers through religious warfare, expulsion, or assistance in expulsion. It warns that granting such hostile forces allegiance or support, despite their aggression, is an act of injustice; it does not condemn peaceful and fair relations with those who have not waged such persecution.

translation: O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah knows best the reality of their faith. If you ascertain that they are believers, do not return them to the disbelievers: they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. Give the disbelievers what they have spent. There is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their bridal gifts. Do not retain marriage bonds with disbelieving women; ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that faith creates a moral and legal bond stronger than a marriage tie formed under disbelief. In the context of believing women who left hostile disbelieving communities, the believers were to verify their sincerity as far as humanly possible, protect them from being returned to an incompatible and potentially dangerous marital situation, and regularize any resulting financial obligations with fairness. It also directs believers not to preserve marriages that fundamentally conflict with faith, while requiring reciprocal financial justice rather than permitting either side to suffer wrongful loss. The command is presented as a balanced ruling grounded in Allah’s complete knowledge and wisdom, not in suspicion or arbitrary judgment.

translation: And if any of your wives have gone from you to the disbelievers, and you later gain spoils, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they spent. And be mindful of Allah, in whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of fairness for believers who suffered financial loss when their wives joined the opposing disbelievers: if communal wealth later became available, compensation was to be given to them equal to the marriage expenses they had paid. It directs the community to uphold justice and fulfill people’s rights even amid conflict, while reminding believers that true faith requires reverence for Allah and obedience to His commands.

translation: O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask Allah to forgive them. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This pledge establishes that faith must be demonstrated through protection of pure belief, life, chastity, property, family honor, and obedience to rightful moral guidance. The Prophet is instructed to receive the women’s commitment and pray for their forgiveness, showing that sincere repentance and adherence to these principles are met by Allah’s encompassing forgiveness and mercy.

translation: O you who believe, do not take as allies a people upon whom Allah has become angry. They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to give their deepest loyalty and trust to those who knowingly oppose God and have abandoned hope in the resurrection, lest their rejection and despair influence the believers’ faith and moral commitments. It is a warning about spiritual allegiance and values, not a prohibition against justice, kindness, or dignified dealings with people who differ in belief.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation, whether living or inanimate, declares Allah’s perfection and freedom from every imperfection through its very existence and the order placed within it. His absolute might governs all things, while His perfect wisdom gives every part of creation its proper measure and purpose.

translation: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، لِمَ تقولون ما لا تفعلون؟
interpretation: يعاتب الله المؤمنين على التناقض بين أقوالهم وأعمالهم، وينبّههم إلى أن صدق الإيمان يقتضي أن يوافق الفعلُ القولَ، فلا يعدوا أو يتعهدوا بما لا ينوون الوفاء به.

translation: It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: Allah condemns the serious moral contradiction between one’s words and actions, teaching that claiming righteousness or making promises without embodying them in conduct is deeply detestable to Him.

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as though they were a firmly bonded structure.
interpretation: The verse teaches that those who strive for Allah’s cause should act with sincere unity, discipline, steadfastness, and mutual support, remaining as cohesive and dependable as a solid wall rather than divided or disordered.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, “O my people, why do you harm me when you know that I am Allah’s Messenger to you?” Then when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse teaches that knowingly opposing and hurting a divinely appointed messenger is not a minor offense; it reflects a deliberate turning away from truth. When people persist in such deviation despite clear knowledge, Allah leaves their hearts further astray as a just consequence of their rebellion, and they are deprived of guidance so long as they remain defiantly disobedient.

translation: And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Children of Israel, indeed I am Allah’s messenger to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and bringing good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.” But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, “This is obvious sorcery.”
interpretation: Jesus affirms that his mission is part of the same continuous revelation from Allah: he confirms the truth preserved in the Torah and announces the coming of Ahmad, understood in Islamic interpretation as the Prophet Muhammad. Yet when the promised messenger arrives with unmistakable signs, some reject him and dismiss the truth as sorcery, showing how prejudice and refusal to follow divine guidance can lead people to deny even clear evidence.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents lies against Allah while he is being invited to Islam? Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse portrays deliberate rejection of truth as especially grave when a person has been called clearly to submit to God, yet responds by attributing falsehood to Him. Such stubborn injustice deprives a person of divine guidance, not because guidance is unavailable, but because he knowingly turns away from it.

translation: They seek to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the efforts to suppress Allah’s guidance and truth through denial, propaganda, and words as futile—like trying to extinguish a light by blowing on it. Allah guarantees that His guidance will be brought to completion and prevail, regardless of the opposition of those who reject it.

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may cause it to prevail over every other religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: God sent His Messenger with clear guidance and the true way of worship, promising that its truth and authority would ultimately become manifest above all competing beliefs, regardless of the opposition and resentment of those who associate partners with Him.

translation: O you who believe, shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: Allah presents faith and obedience as a truly profitable transaction: the believer gives up disobedience and worldly preference for sincere devotion and righteous action, and in return receives salvation from punishment. The question is meant to awaken eagerness and show that divine guidance is the greatest and most worthwhile gain.

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if only you knew.
interpretation: True faith is demonstrated not merely by conviction, but by dedicating one’s resources, efforts, and life to what pleases Allah and supports His truth. This sincere sacrifice is ultimately better for a person because it brings spiritual success and lasting reward.

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eternity. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: Allah promises that sincere faith and obedience lead to the removal of sin and to lasting, secure happiness in Paradise, where both the surroundings and the dwellings are pure and excellent; this is the greatest success because it is eternal and granted by divine forgiveness.

translation: And another blessing that you love: help from Allah and a near victory. So give the believers glad tidings.
interpretation: Allah promises believers a cherished blessing beyond forgiveness and Paradise: His support and a victory that is close at hand. This promise is meant to strengthen their resolve and assure them that sincere faith and steadfast obedience will ultimately bring divine assistance and success.

translation: O believers, be supporters of Allah, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, “Who are my supporters for Allah?” The disciples replied, “We are supporters of Allah.” Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, while another group disbelieved. So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became victorious.
interpretation: The verse calls believers to stand firmly with Allah’s truth through sincere faith, obedience, and support for His message, following the example of the disciples. Though people may divide between acceptance and rejection, Allah grants strength and eventual triumph to those who remain faithful and uphold the truth.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah—the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: All creation, whether through its existence, order, or conscious worship, bears witness that Allah is free from every imperfection and alone possesses absolute sovereignty. His might is never separate from wisdom, so everything unfolds under His perfect authority and judgment.

translation: He is the One who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were surely in clear error.
interpretation: This verse shows that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was sent to transform a people who had been deprived of revealed guidance: he recited God’s revelation to them, purified their beliefs, character, and conduct, and taught them the Qur’an and the wisdom needed to live by it. Their former state of clear error highlights that true reform begins with revelation, inner purification, and sound understanding—not merely with worldly knowledge or social change.

translation: And [He sent him] to others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This indicates that the Prophet’s message was not limited to the people present in his time; it would reach later generations who had not yet joined the first believers. Its spread across peoples and ages occurs by Allah’s power and according to His perfect wisdom.

translation: That is the bounty of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty.
interpretation: This affirms that every special favor, guidance, honor, and success comes from Allah’s generosity rather than being something owed to anyone. He bestows His bounty according to His wisdom, and His generosity is vast and unrestricted.

translation: The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah but did not uphold it is like that of a donkey carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of people who deny Allah’s signs. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse teaches that possessing revealed knowledge is of no benefit when a person neither understands its guidance nor lives by it. Sacred scripture must be carried in the heart through faith and practice, not merely carried or recited outwardly; otherwise knowledge becomes a proof against its bearer rather than a source of guidance.

translation: Say, “O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are Allah’s chosen allies to the exclusion of all other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.”
interpretation: The verse challenges the claim of exclusive closeness to Allah: genuine certainty of such a privileged status would make one welcome death as the meeting with Allah, whereas refusing to do so exposes the claim as insincere.

translation: But they will never wish for it because of what their hands have sent ahead; and Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: Those who falsely claim a special closeness to God would not sincerely desire death, because their deeds have filled them with fear of meeting Him. Their reluctance exposes the emptiness of their claim, while God knows the injustice and wrongdoing concealed within their hearts.

translation: Say, “Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.”
interpretation: No one can escape death or delay its appointed time. Therefore, fleeing from it should not distract a person from preparing for the inevitable return to Allah, before whom every hidden and visible deed will be fully disclosed and judged.

translation: O you who believe, when the call to prayer is proclaimed on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trading. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to give priority to the Friday prayer and the remembrance of Allah when its call is made, setting aside business and other worldly transactions so that nothing competes with this communal act of worship. This instruction teaches that obedience and spiritual attentiveness are more valuable than immediate worldly gain.

translation: Then, when the prayer has been concluded, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often so that you may succeed.
interpretation: After fulfilling the congregational prayer, believers may return to their work and worldly pursuits, seeking lawful provision while keeping Allah frequently in their hearts and actions. True success lies in combining responsible effort with continual remembrance of Allah.

translation: And when they see a trade or amusement, they rush toward it and leave you standing. Say, “What is with Allah is better than amusement and trade, and Allah is the best of providers.”
interpretation: The verse reproaches those who abandon the Friday sermon and prayer for worldly attraction, teaching that obedience, remembrance, and worship must take precedence over commerce and entertainment. Whatever reward and provision Allah grants through faithful devotion is better and more lasting than any temporary worldly gain.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the hypocrites come to you, they say, “We testify that you are truly the Messenger of Allah.” Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are surely liars.
interpretation: The verse exposes the contradiction between the hypocrites’ outward profession and their inward denial: although their words affirm the truth, their claim to genuine faith is false because it is uttered insincerely and without conviction. It teaches that Allah judges the truthfulness of testimony by the heart and conduct behind it, not merely by the words spoken.

translation: They have taken their oaths as a shield, so they have turned people away from the way of Allah. Truly evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: They used their false oaths to conceal their hypocrisy and protect themselves from exposure, thereby deceiving others and obstructing them from faith and obedience to Allah; this conduct is profoundly evil.

translation: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون
interpretation: ذلك بسبب أنهم أظهروا الإيمان ثم رجعوا إلى الكفر، فاستحقوا أن تُغلَق قلوبهم عن قبول الحق وفهمه؛ إذ أفسد تكرار الإعراض بصيرتهم، فلم يعودوا ينتفعون بما يسمعون من آيات الله.

translation: And when you see them, their bodies impress you; and when they speak, you listen to their words. They are like propped-up pieces of timber. They think every cry is directed against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah condemn them—how are they turned away from the truth?
interpretation: The verse exposes the hollowness of hypocrisy: outward appearance and persuasive speech may attract people, but without sincere faith the person is spiritually lifeless, like timber merely leaning against a wall. Their guilty insecurity makes them interpret every warning as a threat, revealing their concealed hostility and lack of trust; therefore believers must not be deceived by appearances or eloquence.

translation: And when it is said to them, “Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,” they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away in arrogance.
interpretation: This portrays the hypocrites’ deliberate rejection of sincere repentance and reconciliation: despite being invited to seek the Prophet’s prayer for forgiveness, their pride makes them refuse and turn away, revealing that their outward faith is accompanied by inner resistance to truth.

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This is a declaration that intercession cannot benefit those who knowingly persist in rebellion and hypocrisy after the truth has become clear to them. Their refusal to repent and obey places them beyond the guidance that leads to forgiveness.

translation: They are the ones who say, “Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.” Yet to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The hypocrites sought to weaken the believers by urging people to withhold financial support from those around the Messenger of Allah, assuming that deprivation would force them to abandon him. Their words reveal their ignorance: provision ultimately belongs to Allah, who controls all the resources of the heavens and the earth, not to those who try to manipulate others through wealth.

translation: They say, “If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely drive out the humbler.” Yet all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: This exposes the arrogance of the hypocrites, who judged worth by worldly power and social status and imagined that they could expel the believers. True dignity and authority belong to Allah and are granted to His Messenger and sincere believers; those who rely on hypocrisy and false pride ultimately lack true understanding.

translation: O you who believe, do not let your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. Whoever does so—those are the losers.
interpretation: Believers are warned not to allow the pursuit of wealth or the care and attachment to children to make them neglect prayer, obedience, and awareness of Allah. Material possessions and family are blessings, but when they become a cause of abandoning one’s duties to Allah, they lead to true loss in the Hereafter.

translation: And spend from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you, and he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short while, I would give charity and be among the righteous.”
interpretation: The verse urges believers to use their wealth in obedience and charity while they still have the opportunity, because death ends the period of action and leaves the heedless person with regret and an unfulfilled wish to return and do good.

translation: Allah will never delay a soul when its appointed time has come. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: When a person’s appointed lifespan arrives, it cannot be postponed or extended; therefore, one should not put off obedience and repentance, knowing that Allah fully knows and will judge every deed.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs all sovereignty, and to Him belongs all praise; and He is over all things capable.
interpretation: All creation, whether seen or unseen, declares Allah’s perfection and freedom from every imperfection. Since He alone possesses absolute dominion and deserves all praise, believers should recognize His complete authority, rely upon His power, and submit to Him in every matter.

translation: He is the One who created you, yet among you are disbelievers and among you are believers. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: Although all people are created by Allah, they differ in how they respond to His guidance: some reject faith, while others accept it. Their choices and actions are fully known to Allah, and each person is accountable for them.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth, fashioned you, and perfected your forms; and to Him is the final return.
interpretation: The ordered creation and the beauty of human form testify to God’s wisdom and power, while the return to Him means that human beings will ultimately be judged according to how they lived in light of this truth.

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And Allah is All-Knowing of what the hearts contain.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses all existence and every aspect of human life, including actions openly displayed and intentions hidden within the heart. Nothing can be concealed from Him, so a person should cultivate sincerity and remain mindful of Allah in both private and public.

translation: Has the news not reached you of those who disbelieved before? They tasted the evil consequences of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that rejecting the truth and persisting in disbelief bring destructive consequences in this life and a painful punishment in the Hereafter, as demonstrated by the fate of earlier peoples.

translation: That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, “Are human beings to guide us?” So they disbelieved and turned away. Allah was self-sufficient; and Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse explains that their disbelief arose from arrogant rejection of human messengers: they considered humanity an unworthy source of divine guidance and therefore refused the clear evidence brought to them. Their refusal harmed only themselves, for Allah has no need of their faith or obedience, while He remains perfectly independent and worthy of all praise.

translation: Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, “Yes indeed, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah.”
interpretation: The verse refutes the denial of resurrection by affirming it with a solemn divine oath. Since Allah created humanity in the first place, bringing them back to life is effortless for Him; resurrection will therefore lead to a complete disclosure and reckoning of every deed.

translation: So believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the light We have sent down. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse calls people to affirm faith in Allah and His Messenger and to follow the divine revelation that illuminates truth, guides conduct, and dispels spiritual confusion. It also reminds them that Allah fully knows their actions, so faith must be expressed sincerely through obedient deeds.

translation: On the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering—that is the Day of mutual loss and gain. Whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will erase his sins and admit him into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that they will all be gathered for the final judgment, when the true outcome of every person’s choices will become clear: some will discover that they have gained salvation, while others will realize that they have lost it. Sincere faith expressed through righteous action brings forgiveness and everlasting Paradise, showing that the greatest success is not worldly advantage but attaining Allah’s mercy in the Hereafter.

translation: As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire; they will remain therein forever. And what an evil destination.
interpretation: Those who knowingly reject faith and persist in denying God’s revealed signs are warned that their denial leads to abiding punishment in Hell, a final end of profound loss and misery.

translation: No calamity befalls except by Allah’s permission. Whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse teaches that whatever hardship reaches a person occurs within Allah’s knowledge and decree. True faith enables the believer to respond with trust, patience, and submission, so that Allah steadies the heart and guides it toward the right understanding and conduct amid adversity.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then Our Messenger’s duty is only to deliver the clear message.
interpretation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is the believer’s responsibility, while the Messenger’s responsibility is to convey the revelation plainly and completely. Those who reject or turn away after the truth has been made clear bear the consequences of their own choice; the Messenger is not accountable for forcing them to believe.

translation: Allah—there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: True faith is expressed through sincere dependence on Allah alone: believers entrust their affairs to Him, seek His help, and remain confident in His wisdom while taking the means available to them.

translation: O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and children are those who may be enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive, then surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse cautions believers that attachment to a spouse or child can sometimes become a source of opposition when it obstructs faith, obedience, or the pursuit of what is right. It does not condemn family ties; rather, it calls for vigilance so that love does not lead one into wrongdoing, while encouraging mercy and forgiveness when family members cause harm or fail in their duties.

translation: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم ابتلاءٌ واختبار، والله عنده أجرٌ عظيم.
interpretation: يبيّن الله أن المال والأولاد قد يكونون وسيلةً لامتحان الإنسان؛ فيُنظر هل يشغلونه عن طاعة الله وحقوقه، أم يستعملهم فيما يرضيه. فمن قدّم طاعة الله ولم يفرّط في واجباته بسببهم، فله عند الله ثواب عظيم.

translation: So be mindful of Allah as much as you are able, listen and obey, and spend in charity; that is better for you. Whoever is protected from the greed of their own soul—it is they who will prosper.
interpretation: This verse teaches that devotion to Allah is practiced according to one’s genuine ability, through willing attentiveness, obedience, and generosity. True success comes from overcoming the soul’s possessiveness and selfish greed, allowing faith to produce obedience and beneficial giving.

translation: If you lend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. Allah is Most Appreciative, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: Allah calls sincere acts of charity and obedience a “good loan” to emphasize that nothing given for His sake is lost: He promises to multiply its reward, overlook shortcomings, and respond with appreciation despite having no need of His servants. His forbearance gives them time to repent and do good without hastening their punishment.

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah’s knowledge encompasses everything hidden from creation and everything openly witnessed, while His absolute might and perfect wisdom govern all that He decrees.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period, and carefully calculate the waiting period. Fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their homes, nor should they leave, unless they commit a manifest indecency. These are the limits set by Allah. Whoever transgresses Allah’s limits has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about something new after that.
interpretation: Divorce must be carried out according to a disciplined procedure that preserves the woman’s rights and leaves room for reconciliation: she is divorced at a time when her waiting period can properly begin, and that period is carefully observed. During it, neither spouse should act rashly by expelling her or having her leave, except in the case of clear misconduct. These restrictions are divine safeguards against injustice, and observing them keeps open the possibility that circumstances, feelings, or decisions may change and reconciliation may become possible.

translation: When they are nearing the end of their waiting period, either retain them honorably or part with them honorably. Call two upright men from among you to witness, and uphold the testimony for the sake of Allah. This is an admonition for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for him.
interpretation: The verse commands that the conclusion of marriage be handled with fairness, dignity, and transparency: a husband may resume the marriage only with sincere and honorable intention, or end it without harm or injustice. Witnesses are required to protect both parties’ rights and prevent dispute, while true mindfulness of Allah gives a person a lawful path through difficult circumstances and relief from hardship.

translation: And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His command. Allah has appointed a measure for everything.
interpretation: Whoever entrusts his affairs to Allah with sincere reliance may receive provision and relief through unforeseen means; Allah’s decree will inevitably be fulfilled, and every event unfolds according to His precise wisdom and appointed measure.

translation: As for those of your women who no longer menstruate—if you are uncertain about their waiting period—their waiting period is three months; and likewise for those who have not menstruated. As for those who are pregnant, their waiting period ends when they deliver their burden. Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make ease for them in their affairs.
interpretation: This verse establishes the waiting periods after divorce: three months for women who no longer menstruate and for those whose menstruation has not begun, while a pregnant woman’s waiting period continues until childbirth. These rulings protect lineage, allow clarity concerning pregnancy, and regulate separation with justice. The verse concludes by teaching that obedience to Allah and awareness of Him bring relief and ease in difficult matters.

translation: That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will erase his sins and greatly increase his reward.
interpretation: Allah’s revealed guidance is to be followed with reverent awareness of Him. Whoever obeys Him and avoids what displeases Him will receive the forgiveness of past sins and a reward far greater than his deeds warrant.

translation: Lodge them wherever you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them so as to make things difficult for them. If they are pregnant, spend on them until they deliver their burden. Then, if they nurse the child for you, give them their due payment, and consult together in kindness. But if you both make things difficult for one another, then another woman may nurse the child for him.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a woman undergoing divorce must be provided with suitable housing and financial support according to the man’s ability, particularly throughout pregnancy until childbirth. It forbids using housing or financial pressure to harass, humiliate, or force her into hardship. If she breastfeeds the child after separation, her labor is an acknowledged right for which she must be fairly compensated, and decisions concerning the child should be made through respectful consultation and good conduct. When cooperation breaks down, the child’s welfare remains the priority, and another nursing mother may be engaged without allowing conflict to harm the child or violate the mother’s rights.

translation: Let the one who has abundance spend according to his abundance; and whoever has been restricted in provision, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship.
interpretation: Financial responsibility must be carried out according to one’s actual means, not beyond them: the wealthy should give generously, while the one with limited provision should give only within his capacity. God judges people by what He has enabled them to possess, and hardship is not permanent, for relief will follow difficulty.

translation: وكم من قرية تمردت على أمر ربها ورسله، فحاسبناها حسابًا شديدًا وعذبناها عذابًا منكرًا.
interpretation: يبين الله أن الإعراض المتعمد عن أوامره ورفض رسله ليس أمرًا بلا عاقبة؛ فالأمم التي تجاهر بالعصيان تُواجَه بحساب دقيق وعقوبة شديدة تستنكرها النفوس، وفي ذلك تحذير من الاغترار بالإمهال أو القوة.

translation: So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.
interpretation: Those who persist in defying God’s command will ultimately experience the harmful consequences of their choices, ending in ruin and loss rather than success.

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So be mindful of Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has indeed sent down to you a Reminder.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting divine guidance and persisting in wrongdoing leads to grave punishment, while calling believers of sound understanding to maintain reverent awareness of Allah. The “Reminder” refers to the revelation that awakens people to the truth, guides their conduct, and protects them from heedlessness.

translation: A Messenger reciting to you the clear verses of Allah, so that he may bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light. Whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, remaining there forever. Allah has indeed granted him an excellent provision.
interpretation: Allah’s revelation, conveyed by His Messenger, is a means of guiding sincere believers from the darkness of disbelief, error, and disobedience into the light of faith and righteous living. Those who respond through belief and good deeds receive the lasting blessing of Paradise, a reward that is both eternal and graciously provided by Allah.

translation: Allah is He who created seven heavens, and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them, so that you may know that Allah is capable of all things and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse directs people to recognize Allah’s complete sovereignty: He created the vast heavens and the earth according to His perfect order, and His command governs everything between them. His absolute power and all-encompassing knowledge leave nothing outside His control or beyond His awareness.

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit for yourself what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: Allah gently reproaches the Prophet for voluntarily abstaining from something lawful in order to please his wives, teaching that personal efforts to satisfy others must not turn what Allah permitted into a self-imposed prohibition. The verse also conveys divine mercy and forgiveness for such an act.

translation: Allah has prescribed for you a means of releasing yourselves from your oaths. Allah is your Protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: Allah has established a lawful expiation for oaths, so a person is not trapped by an oath when fulfilling it would lead away from what is right. As the true Protector, He knows people’s intentions and circumstances and legislates with perfect wisdom.

translation: And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, but when she disclosed it and Allah made it known to him, he acknowledged part of it and passed over part. Then, when he informed her of it, she said, “Who told you this?” He said, “The All-Knowing, the All-Aware told me.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that what is entrusted in confidence must be guarded, while affirming that Allah knows every hidden matter. The Prophet’s mentioning only part of what had been disclosed reflects wisdom, restraint, and his avoidance of unnecessary reproach, even when a private trust had been violated.

translation: If you both repent to Allah, then your hearts have inclined away from what is right. But if you support one another against him, then surely Allah is his Protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers; and after that, the angels are his supporters.
interpretation: Allah addresses the two wives involved, urging them to repent because their hearts had turned away from the conduct required toward the Prophet. He warns that opposing him cannot harm him, for Allah Himself protects and supports him, joined by Gabriel, the upright believers, and the angels.

translation: Perhaps, if he divorces you, his Lord will replace you with wives better than you—women who submit, believe, are devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipful, given to fasting, previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse warns the Prophet’s wives that their honored position is not a guarantee independent of obedience to God. Their true excellence lies in sincere submission, faith, repentance, worship, and devotion; if they fail in their responsibility, God is fully able to replace them with women who embody these qualities, whether widowed or divorced or never previously married.

translation: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, stern and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: Believers are commanded to take responsibility for their own spiritual well-being and for those under their care by guiding them toward faith, obedience, and righteous conduct, and by shielding them from the causes that lead to punishment. The verse also warns of the grave reality of the Fire and emphasizes that its guardians carry out Allah’s commands with absolute firmness and without disobedience.

translation: يا أيها الذين كفروا، لا تعتذروا اليوم؛ إنما تُجزَون بما كنتم تعملون.
interpretation: يُقال للكافرين يوم القيامة إن وقت الاعتذار قد فات، لأن الجزاء حينئذٍ قائم على أعمالهم التي اختاروها في الدنيا، فلا تنفعهم الأعذار ولا تدفع عنهم نتيجة كفرهم وأفعالهم.

translation: O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will erase your sins from you and admit you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet nor those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and to their right; they will say, “Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us. Indeed, You are capable of all things.”
interpretation: The verse calls believers to a repentance that is genuine and transformative: abandoning the sin, regretting it sincerely, and resolving not to return to it, while restoring any rights owed to others. Such repentance opens the way to Allah’s forgiveness and eternal honor. The light accompanying the believers signifies the faith and guidance Allah grants them, enabling them to pass safely on the Day of Judgment; yet their plea for its completion teaches that even the righteous remain dependent on Allah’s mercy and steadfastness.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Their abode is Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet to confront opposition to the truth with resolute wisdom: confronting the disbelievers through the appropriate struggle against their aggression, and confronting the hypocrites by exposing their deception and refusing to yield to their harm. It calls for firmness and moral seriousness, not injustice or transgression, and warns that persistent rejection and hypocrisy ultimately lead to divine punishment.

translation: Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were married to two righteous servants of Ours, yet they betrayed them, and they could not avail them at all against Allah. And it was said, “Enter the Fire with those who enter.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that faith and accountability are personal: even being married to righteous prophets cannot save someone who rejects the truth and betrays their religious trust. A person’s salvation depends on their own faith and obedience to Allah, not on family ties or association with the righteous.

translation: And Allah sets forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, “My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise, save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”
interpretation: This verse shows that true faith is an individual choice that can remain firm even under the pressure of a tyrannical household and a corrupt society. The wife of Pharaoh placed nearness to Allah and the eternal home above worldly status, wealth, and security; her prayer also shows that seeking deliverance from oppression includes distancing oneself from both the oppressor and his evil actions. Thus, her steadfastness becomes a model for believers that dignity and salvation come through loyalty to Allah, even when faith brings hardship.

translation: And Mary, the daughter of عمران, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit; and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His Scriptures, and she was among the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: يُبرز الله مريم مثالًا للطهارة والعفة والتصديق الكامل بوحيه؛ فمع عِظَم الابتلاء الذي اصطفاها له، بقيت مستسلمة لأمر ربها، مؤمنة بكلماته وكتبه، ثابتة في طاعته وعبادته. ونفخ الروح فيها بأمر الله تعبير عن المعجزة التي وُلد بها عيسى عليه السلام، لا عن حلولٍ أو اتحاد، بل عن خلقٍ إلهيٍّ خارق للعادة.

translation: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: All authority and control belong exclusively to Allah; His rule is perfect and unrestricted, and nothing in existence lies beyond His power.

translation: He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deeds. And He is the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
interpretation: Allah created life and death as a purposeful trial, through which people are distinguished by the quality and sincerity of their actions—not merely by how many they perform. His might ensures that the test is just, while His forgiveness gives those who turn to Him the hope of mercy despite their shortcomings.

translation: He is the One who created seven heavens, one above another. You will not see any inconsistency in the creation of the Most Merciful. So look again: do you see any flaw?
interpretation: The ordered structure and harmony of the heavens testify to the perfect wisdom and power of Allah. The command to look repeatedly is an invitation to careful reflection: however closely one examines creation, one will find no genuine contradiction, disorder, or defect in it.

translation: Then cast your gaze again and again; your sight will return to you humbled and weary.
interpretation: The verse directs people to repeatedly contemplate the heavens, challenging them to find any flaw in Allah’s creation. Their vision will ultimately return defeated and exhausted, unable to discover any defect, revealing the perfection and harmony of divine creation.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, made them missiles against the devils, and prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: Allah presents the stars as signs of the beauty and order of the nearest heaven, while declaring that the devils are repelled from attempting to intrude upon the unseen. Their defiance does not escape divine power: they are driven away and face the blazing punishment prepared for them.

translation: For those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell—what an evil destination.
interpretation: The verse warns that rejecting the Lord after knowingly turning away from His truth leads to the ultimate consequence: Hell, a destination utterly devoid of goodness and mercy.

translation: When they are cast into it, they will hear it roaring as it boils.
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as violently raging and producing a terrifying roar, conveying the overwhelming severity of its punishment and warning people against the path that leads to it.

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Whenever a group is cast into it, its keepers ask them, “Did no warner come to you?”
interpretation: The verse portrays Hell as intensely enraged at the rejection of truth, and depicts its keepers questioning each group entering it to make clear that divine warning had reached them. This emphasizes that their punishment is not unjust or without prior guidance, but follows their willful refusal to heed the messengers.

translation: They will say, “Yes indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said, ‘Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.’”
interpretation: The verse portrays the people of Hell admitting that they were warned, yet their rejection was deliberate: they denied divine revelation and accused the messengers of being misguided. Their admission exposes that their punishment is not due to a lack of guidance, but to knowingly refusing it.

translation: And they will say, “If only we had listened or understood, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze.”
interpretation: This is a confession of the people of Hell that their punishment was not due to a lack of guidance, but to their refusal to listen with humility and use their reason to recognize the truth. Their regret comes when the opportunity for faith and repentance has already passed.

translation: They will then confess their sin; so away with the inhabitants of the Blaze.
interpretation: This depicts the people of Hell acknowledging that their rejection and refusal to listen were their own fault, but their admission comes only after judgment and therefore cannot benefit them; they are deserving of being cast far from Allah’s mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse praises those whose reverence for Allah is sincere and constant, remaining mindful of Him even when no one else can see them. Their unseen devotion and restraint from disobedience are met with Allah’s forgiveness and an immense reward.

translation: Whether you conceal your words or speak them openly, surely He knows all that is within the hearts.
interpretation: No thought, intention, or secret feeling is hidden from Allah; therefore, a person should be mindful of Him inwardly as well as outwardly.

translation: Would He who created not know, while He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware?
interpretation: The One who brought every being into existence necessarily knows its outward actions, inner thoughts, hidden motives, and finest details; nothing is concealed from His perfect and encompassing knowledge.

translation: He is the One who made the earth manageable for you, so walk through its regions and eat from His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: Allah has subdued the earth and made it suitable for human life and endeavor, permitting people to travel through it and seek their sustenance. Yet their worldly pursuit must remain conscious of the fact that they will return to Allah for resurrection and judgment, so they should use His blessings responsibly and in obedience to Him.

translation: Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, whereupon it begins to shake violently?
interpretation: The verse warns people not to become complacent about their safety or defy God, reminding them that the stable earth remains entirely subject to His power and that He can overturn its apparent security whenever He wills.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not send upon you a shower of stones? Then you will know how severe My warning is.
interpretation: The verse warns people not to become complacent about divine punishment: although they may feel secure, God can swiftly bring upon them a destructive calamity, and only then will they realize the seriousness of the warning delivered to them.

translation: Indeed, those before them denied, so how severe was My rejection of them!
interpretation: This is a warning to those who deny God’s truth: earlier peoples rejected their messengers and were met with a decisive punishment, so the present deniers should not assume that rejection will spare them from divine judgment.

translation: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and then drawing them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He sees all things.
interpretation: The birds’ effortless flight is a sign of God’s sustaining power and precise care: through the abilities and laws He has created, He continuously preserves them in the sky. Those who reflect on this should recognize that the same Lord who watches over every creature is fully aware of human actions and circumstances.

translation: Or who is it that could be an army for you to help you besides the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.
interpretation: Allah challenges those who deny Him to identify any force capable of protecting or supporting them independently of His mercy and power. Their reliance on false gods, worldly strength, or imagined security is merely deception, because no one can grant victory or avert harm except Allah.

translation: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? Yet they persist in arrogance and aversion.
