interpretation: تُبيّن الآية أن الرزق بيد الله وحده، فلا يستطيع أحد أن يعوّض ما يمنعه الله أو يضمن للإنسان معاشه من دونه. ومع وضوح هذا الدليل، يصرّ المكذّبون على التمرّد والإعراض بدل أن يخضعوا للحق ويعترفوا بفضل الله.

translation: أفمن يمشي مكبًّا على وجهه أهدى أم من يمشي سويًّا على صراط مستقيم؟
interpretation: يضرب الله مثلًا للمقارنة بين من يعيش ضالًّا مضطربًا، لا يرى طريق الحق فيتعثر فيه، ومن يسير مستقيماً على الهدى والبصيرة؛ فالثاني أهدى وأقرب إلى السلامة والغاية الصحيحة.

translation: Say, “He is the One who brought you into being and granted you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are the thanks you give.”
interpretation: Allah alone is the Creator who bestowed upon human beings the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding so that they may recognize the truth and live by it. Yet people often use these gifts carelessly or in disobedience, showing how limited their gratitude is; true thankfulness is to acknowledge the Giver and employ these faculties in what pleases Him.

translation: قل: هو الذي أنشأكم وبثَّكم في الأرض، وإليه تُحشرون.
interpretation: تذكِّر الآية بأن وجود الإنسان وانتشاره في الأرض بإيجاد الله وتقديره، وأن هذه الحياة ليست نهاية المطاف؛ فمصير الناس جميعًا الرجوع إلى الله يوم القيامة للحساب والجزاء.

translation: And they say, “When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?”
interpretation: They ask this as a challenge, not as a sincere request for guidance: they doubt the promised resurrection or punishment and mockingly demand that it be brought immediately as proof of the messenger’s truthfulness.

translation: Say, “The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to affirm that knowledge of the unseen and of the time of what people ask about belongs exclusively to Allah; his role is not to claim independent knowledge of it, but to convey Allah’s warning plainly and unmistakably.

translation: When they see it drawing near, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said: “This is what you were calling for.”
interpretation: When the disbelievers witness the promised punishment approaching and no longer doubt its reality, their faces will reveal terror and anguish. They will be reminded, reproachfully, that this is the very judgment they used to deny, challenge, or demand be brought swiftly.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me, or has mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?”
interpretation: The Prophet is instructed to confront the disbelievers with the reality that, whether Allah causes him and the believers with him to perish or grants them mercy, their own rejection leaves them without any protector from Allah’s punishment. The fate of the believers does not determine the truth of the message; each person remains accountable to Allah.

translation: Say, “He is the Most Compassionate; we believe in Him, and upon Him we rely. Then you will come to know who is in clear error.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that true faith is expressed through both belief in Allah and complete reliance upon Him. It also warns those who reject this truth that the reality of their guidance or misguidance will ultimately become unmistakably clear.

translation: Say, “Have you considered: if your water were to sink deep into the earth, who then could bring you flowing water?”
interpretation: This verse confronts human dependence and vulnerability: the water people take for granted is entirely within Allah’s power. It calls them to recognize His sustaining mercy, abandon self-sufficiency, and remain grateful and obedient, since no one besides Him can restore the essential blessings on which life depends.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Nūn. By the pen and what they write.
interpretation: Allah swears by the pen and the written record to emphasize the honor and immense power of knowledge, writing, and the preservation of truth; the mysterious letter “Nūn” also draws attention to the profound, inimitable nature of the revelation that follows.

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not insane.
interpretation: God affirms that, through His favor and care, the Prophet is sound-minded and truthful, and that the accusations of madness directed against him are utterly false.

translation: And indeed, you will have a reward that is never-ending.
interpretation: God assures the Prophet that his perseverance and fulfillment of his mission will be rewarded with a lasting reward that will neither be diminished nor withheld.

translation: And indeed, you are of a عظیم character.
interpretation: Allah affirms that the Prophet Muhammad possesses an extraordinary nobility of character—marked by patience, mercy, truthfulness, humility, and steadfastness—making his conduct a model for humanity.

translation: Then you will see, and they will see.
interpretation: The truth of your mission and the error of your opponents will soon become unmistakably evident to both you and them.

translation: Which of you is afflicted with madness?
interpretation: The verse refutes the disbelievers’ accusation that the Prophet ﷺ was mad, declaring that it will become clear which side is truly deluded and deprived of sound judgment.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse teaches that ultimate judgment of people’s guidance or misguidance belongs to God alone, for He fully knows the inner realities, intentions, and choices of every person. Therefore, one should invite others to the truth with wisdom and humility rather than claim authority over their hearts or hastily judge their final standing.

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: Do not yield to those who reject the truth or compromise your commitment to it in response to their pressure, demands, or opposition.

translation: They wish that you would compromise, so that they could compromise.
interpretation: Those who oppose the truth seek to persuade the Prophet ﷺ to yield in matters of faith, hoping that such concessions would allow them to offer their own in return; the verse therefore warns against compromising divine principles for the sake of mutual accommodation.

translation: ولا تُطع كلَّ حلافٍ مهينٍ.
interpretation: ينهى الله عن الانقياد لمن يكثر الحلف كذبًا أو بغير حاجة، ويتصف بالمهانة وسوء الخُلُق؛ فالإيمان لا يكون بكثرة الأيمان، ولا ينبغي أن يُتَّبع من أفسد لسانه وكرامته بالخداع والابتذال.

translation: A slanderer, going about spreading malicious gossip.
interpretation: It condemns the person who disparages others and carries their words from one person to another in order to create hostility and division.

translation: A preventer of good, a transgressor, and a persistent sinner.
interpretation: This describes a person whose character combines selfishness and moral corruption: he obstructs benefit from reaching others, violates rightful limits, and persistently commits sins without restraint.

translation: Cruel and coarse, and moreover, of ignoble character.
interpretation: This describes a person whose arrogance and hostility are compounded by a harsh, vulgar nature and a deep moral disgrace, marking him as unworthy of honor or trust.

translation: Because he possesses wealth and sons,
interpretation: His wealth and children have made him arrogant, but worldly status is no proof of truth or a justification for rejecting God’s guidance.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: This describes the arrogant rejection of divine revelation: instead of reflecting on the truth and guidance in God’s verses, the denier dismisses them as fabricated tales inherited from earlier generations.

translation: We shall brand him on the snout.
interpretation: This is a warning that the arrogant denier will be disgraced and marked with a humiliating punishment, exposing his shame and contemptible character.

translation: Indeed, We tested them just as We tested the أصحاب of the garden when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruits in the morning.
interpretation: Allah warns that people may be tested through their blessings and intentions, just as the owners of the garden were tested when they arrogantly resolved to take its produce for themselves without recognizing Allah’s right over it. Their story shows that wealth and prosperity are a trial, not a guarantee of security, and that blessings can be removed when people act with selfishness and disregard for Allah.

translation: And they made no exception.
interpretation: They firmly resolved to carry out their plan without saying “if Allah wills,” thereby acting as though their decision and control were independent of God’s will.

translation: Then a visitation from your Lord passed over it while they were sleeping.
interpretation: While the owners of the garden slept, Allah sent a calamity upon it, demonstrating that worldly blessings remain entirely subject to His will and can be taken away without warning.

translation: Then it became like a barren, blackened field.
interpretation: The garden was utterly ruined, its fruits and vegetation gone, leaving it dark and desolate after the divine punishment.

translation: Then they called to one another at daybreak.
interpretation: At the earliest morning, they urged one another to proceed with their plan, confident that they could carry it out before anyone noticed.

translation: Go early to your field, if you intend to harvest it.
interpretation: This command portrays the owners’ firm resolve to gather their crop secretly and at dawn, determined to prevent the needy from sharing in its produce.

translation: So they set out, whispering to one another.
interpretation: They hurried toward their garden while speaking in hushed voices, intending to keep their plan secret and prevent the poor from becoming aware of it.

translation: “Do not let any needy person enter it upon you today.”
interpretation: The owners of the garden secretly agreed to prevent the poor from receiving any of its produce, revealing their resolve to hoard their provision and exclude those entitled to share in their generosity.

translation: And they set out early, determined to carry out their plan, believing themselves fully capable.
interpretation: They hurried confidently toward the garden, firmly resolved to keep its harvest from the needy and convinced that nothing could prevent them; their self-assurance, however, revealed their heedlessness of God’s power and decree.

translation: But when they saw it, they said, “Indeed, we must have lost our way.”
interpretation: Upon seeing the garden in its ruined state, they were so shocked that they initially thought they had gone to the wrong place, before realizing that it was their own garden and that its destruction was a consequence of their wrongdoing.

translation: Rather, we have been deprived.
interpretation: The speakers realize that they have been prevented from receiving the harvest they expected, recognizing that their loss is a consequence of their wrongdoing and that their presumed power over the provision was mistaken.

translation: The most reasonable of them said, “Did I not tell you: Why do you not glorify Allah?”
interpretation: The wisest among them reminded his companions that their arrogance and certainty about controlling the harvest were contrary to recognizing Allah’s authority and blessing; they should have glorified Him, acknowledged His will, and sought His favor.

translation: They said, “Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.”
interpretation: They acknowledge that their Lord is free of all injustice and confess that their own greed and refusal to fulfill the rights of the needy were the wrongdoing that brought about their loss.

translation: Then some of them turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This portrays the painful realization that their shared wrongdoing has brought ruin, causing them to accuse one another rather than accept responsibility before God.

translation: They said, “Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.”
interpretation: They acknowledge, with profound remorse, that their arrogance and excess led them to violate God’s commands and lose His blessings; this admission comes only after the consequences of their wrongdoing have become evident.

translation: Perhaps our Lord will replace it for us with something better than it; indeed, we turn expectantly to our Lord.
interpretation: They express sincere repentance and hope after recognizing their wrongdoing, entrusting themselves to Allah and seeking from Him a better provision than what they lost.

translation: Such is the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This refers to the worldly humiliation and suffering that Allah allowed the rejecters to experience; yet the punishment prepared in the Hereafter is far more severe. The phrase “if only they knew” highlights that their ignorance of its reality led them to persist in denial and wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, for the God-conscious are Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.
interpretation: God promises those who remain mindful of Him and live in obedience a lasting dwelling of perfect joy, granted as an honor and nearness from their Lord.

translation: Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This rhetorical question affirms that Allah’s justice does not equate those who submit to Him and live righteously with those who persist in wrongdoing; their judgment and ultimate outcome must be distinct.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This is a forceful rebuke of judgments that have no sound basis, calling people to recognize the contradiction and irrationality in what they claim.

translation: Or do you have a scripture in which you study [that this is so]?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge exposing the baselessness of their claims: do they possess revealed knowledge or divine authorization supporting what they assert, or are they merely speaking without proof?

translation: Indeed, you will have in it whatever you choose.
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of those who presume that God has guaranteed them whatever they desire; they possess no covenant or proof entitling them to such unrestricted choice.

translation: Or do you have binding oaths from Us, lasting until the Day of Resurrection, that you shall have whatever you decree?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rejection of the unbelievers’ claims: they have no covenant or guarantee from God entitling them to whatever judgment or privilege they choose. No divine promise supports their assumption that they will receive the same favor as the believers while persisting in rejection.

translation: Ask them which of them will guarantee that.
interpretation: This is a challenge exposing the baselessness of their claims: they are asked to identify who among them can assume responsibility and provide a binding assurance that their alleged entitlement or judgment is true.

translation: Or do they have partners who share in this? Then let them bring their partners, if they are truthful.
interpretation: This is a challenge exposing the weakness of those who ascribe partners to Allah: if their alleged deities truly possess authority or a share in what they claim, they should produce clear evidence of it. Their inability to do so demonstrates that such partners are baseless inventions.

translation: On the Day when the gravest ordeal is laid bare, they will be summoned to prostrate, but they will be unable.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment of overwhelming terror and truth fully exposed. Those who refused sincere submission in worldly life will be called to prostrate before God, yet their hardened rejection will leave them powerless to do so.

translation: Their eyes will be cast down; disgrace will overwhelm them. They were indeed called to prostrate while they were sound and able.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who rejected obedience will be overcome by humiliation and will be unable to prostrate, unlike in worldly life when they were healthy, capable, and invited to submit to God.

translation: So leave Me with those who deny this message; We will gradually lead them on to ruin from where they do not know.
interpretation: God commands the Prophet not to be distressed by the deniers, for their apparent prosperity and continued respite are not signs of divine approval. Rather, they are being given time while they persist in denial, until they are brought toward punishment in a manner they neither perceive nor expect.

translation: And I will give them respite; surely My plan is firm.
interpretation: Allah grants those who persist in denial and wrongdoing a period of apparent ease, not out of approval but as a gradual drawing toward the consequences of their actions. His plan is powerful and cannot be escaped.

translation: Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are weighed down by a burden of debt?
interpretation: The verse refutes the idea that the Prophet’s call is motivated by personal gain: he asks nothing from them in return. Their rejection therefore cannot be excused by financial hardship or by any obligation imposed upon them; the message is offered freely, for their guidance and benefit.

translation: Or do they possess knowledge of the unseen, so that they write it down?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical challenge to those who reject the truth: do they truly have access to the unseen and divine knowledge that would justify their claims, or are they speaking without evidence? Only God possesses complete knowledge of the unseen.

translation: So be patient with the decree of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out while overcome with anguish.
interpretation: This commands steadfastness in carrying out the prophetic mission and enduring rejection without becoming impatient with God’s decree. The example of Jonah teaches that intense distress must not lead one to hasten away from the responsibility entrusted by the Lord; patience and trust are required until His wisdom and relief become manifest.

translation: Had a grace from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast upon the barren shore, blameworthy.
interpretation: لولا رحمة الله وتداركه لنبيه يونس عليه السلام، لبقي مطروحًا في المكان الخالي بعد خروجه من بطن الحوت، مستحقًّا للوم بسبب استعجاله ومفارقته قومه قبل أن يؤذن له؛ فنجاته كانت بفضل الله ورعايته لا بقوته وحدها.

translation: So his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
interpretation: Allah restored and honored him through His mercy, accepted his repentance, and elevated him to the rank of those distinguished by faith, obedience, and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve nearly make you stumble with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is surely mad.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the intensity of the disbelievers’ hostility toward the Prophet: their furious, envious gazes are described as nearly causing him harm when they hear the Qur’an, while their accusation that he is mad reveals their attempt to discredit the truth rather than respond to its message.

translation: And it is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds.
interpretation: The Qur’an is a universal reminder that calls all people to remember their Creator, recognize the truth, and live according to divine guidance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The Inevitable Reality.
interpretation: The word “The Inevitable” refers to the Day of Resurrection—the certain event whose occurrence cannot be denied or prevented, when every person will face the truth of Allah’s judgment.

translation: ما الحاقة؟
interpretation: استفهام للتفخيم والتهويل، أي: ما شأن القيامة الواقعة حقًّا التي لا مفرّ منها؟ إنها أمر عظيم يتجاوز إدراك البشر لعظم هوله وحقيقته.

translation: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Reality is?
interpretation: This question magnifies the awe and seriousness of the Day of Resurrection, whose true nature and overwhelming reality surpass human understanding.

translation: Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: Thamūd and ʿĀd rejected the reality of the Day of Judgment and its inevitable reckoning, which will strike all people with overwhelming force.

translation: As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.
interpretation: Thamūd were annihilated by a devastating punishment that surpassed all ordinary limits, as a consequence of their rejection and defiance of God’s messenger.

translation: As for ‘Ād, they were destroyed by a fierce, howling wind, raging violently.
interpretation: The verse portrays the destruction of the people of ‘Ād as a decisive divine punishment: the very force they could not resist brought an end to their arrogance and rebellion, demonstrating that worldly power cannot protect a people from God’s judgment.

translation: He unleashed it upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people lying prostrate, as though they were the hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: The verse portrays the relentless, devastating force of the wind sent against the people of ʿĀd: it continued without interruption until they were utterly destroyed, leaving their lifeless bodies scattered and rigid like the empty, fallen trunks of palm trees. It is a warning that persistent arrogance and rejection of divine guidance can bring a punishment from which worldly power offers no protection.

translation: So do you see any remnant of them?
interpretation: After their destruction, nothing of that people remained to bear witness to their power or continue their legacy; the verse underscores the complete failure of those who defied God.

translation: And Pharaoh, those before him, and the overturned cities came with wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse presents Pharaoh, earlier rebellious nations, and the people of the overturned cities as examples of communities that confronted God’s command through grave sin and defiance, thereby bringing upon themselves the consequences of their rebellion.

translation: But they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an overwhelming punishment.
interpretation: Their rejection of God’s messenger brought upon them a severe and decisive punishment that surpassed ordinary consequence, demonstrating the gravity of persistent defiance after receiving divine warning.

translation: Indeed, when the waters overflowed, We carried you in the sailing vessel.
interpretation: This verse recalls God’s deliverance of Noah and those with him when the flood rose beyond its bounds. By mentioning that humanity was carried in the vessel, it points to God’s power to rescue the faithful from overwhelming calamity and to preserve them through means He provides, while warning against the destructive consequences of rebellion and heedlessness.

translation: so that We may make it a reminder for you, and attentive ears may retain it.
interpretation: Allah made the account of the overwhelming flood and the salvation of those carried in the Ark an enduring lesson, but it benefits those who listen with awareness and preserve its warning in their hearts.

translation: So when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast,
interpretation: This refers to the decisive blowing of the Trumpet that marks the sudden onset of the Resurrection, when the present order of the world is brought to an end and all creation is confronted with the reality of the Hereafter.

translation: And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing.
interpretation: This portrays the overwhelming upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when even the earth and the mighty mountains lose their apparent solidity and are utterly subdued by God’s command.

translation: Then, on that Day, the Inevitable Event will occur.
interpretation: This refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the promised judgment will become an undeniable reality and every person will face the consequences of their deeds.

translation: And the sky will split apart, for on that Day it will be frail.
interpretation: The verse depicts the collapse of the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, revealing that the cosmic order people regard as firm and enduring is completely subject to Allah’s command and will become powerless before His judgment.

translation: والملائكة على أرجائها، ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذٍ ثمانية.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية مشهد القيامة حين تحيط الملائكة بأطراف السماء، ويحمل ثمانيةٌ عرشَ الله فوقهم، فيظهر بذلك جلال السلطان الإلهي وعظمة ذلك اليوم، ويُدرك الخلق أن الحكم والتدبير كله لله وحده.

translation: On that Day you will be presented, and none of your hidden matters will remain concealed.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment as a moment of complete disclosure: every deed, intention, and secret that people concealed in this world will be fully exposed before Allah, leaving no possibility of denial or concealment.

translation: As for the one who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, “Here, read my record!”
interpretation: Receiving the record in the right hand signifies acceptance and salvation; the person speaks with joyful confidence because his deeds have led to success, openly inviting others to witness the proof of his righteousness.

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would face my reckoning.
interpretation: The believer expresses that his faith in the Hereafter and certainty that he would be held accountable guided him toward righteousness and prepared him for the successful outcome he received.

translation: So he will be in a life of contentment.
interpretation: The believer who receives his record in his right hand will enjoy a life of lasting happiness and satisfaction, free from fear, hardship, and regret.

translation: في جَنّةٍ عاليةٍ.
interpretation: أي في جنّة رفيعة القدر، سامية المكانة، عظيمة النعيم.

translation: ثمارها قريبة التناول.
interpretation: يدل ذلك على أن نعيم الجنة ميسّر لأهلها، فثمارها تدنو منهم بلا مشقة، إكرامًا لهم وإتمامًا لراحتهم.

translation: “Eat and drink with pleasure for what you sent ahead in the days that have passed.”
interpretation: This is a welcome to the people of Paradise: they are told to enjoy its blessings as a lasting reward for the righteous deeds and sincere obedience they put forward during their worldly life.

translation: But as for the one who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, “If only I had not been given my record!”
interpretation: This portrays the profound regret of the person whose deeds are exposed for judgment. He wishes he had never received his record because it reveals the consequences of his disbelief and wrongdoing, but this regret comes only after the opportunity for repentance has ended.

translation: And I did not know what my account was.
interpretation: The speaker expresses profound regret and dread, acknowledging that he had been heedless of the reckoning and is now confronted with the disastrous result of his deeds.

translation: If only it had been the final end!
interpretation: The speaker laments that death did not bring complete relief, expressing profound regret and despair over the punishment and suffering that followed.

translation: My wealth has not benefited me.
interpretation: The speaker realizes, with regret, that the riches he relied upon in worldly life cannot protect him from accountability or bring him any salvation in the Hereafter.

translation: My authority has perished from me.
interpretation: The speaker confesses, in utter regret, that the power and influence he once relied upon are now completely useless and have abandoned him before God’s judgment.

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: This is a command to the angels of Hell to restrain the condemned person completely, expressing his humiliation and helplessness under divine judgment.

translation: Then cast him into Hell to burn.
interpretation: This is a command to subject the condemned person to the torment of Hell as a consequence of his wrongdoing and rejection of truth.

translation: Then bind him in a chain seventy cubits long.
interpretation: This depicts the utter humiliation and inescapable punishment awaiting the one who persistently rejected God and refused to care for the needy: he will be restrained in a massive chain, with no possibility of escape.

translation: Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Most Great.
interpretation: His fundamental fault was a deliberate rejection of faith in Allah’s absolute greatness and authority, which left him unprepared to submit to Him or heed His commands.

translation: And he does not urge the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This describes a person whose lack of faith is reflected in indifference to the vulnerable: he neither feeds those in need nor encourages others to care for them, revealing a heart devoid of compassion and social responsibility.

translation: So today he has no devoted friend here.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the denier will find no close companion to comfort, support, or intercede for him against the consequences of his rejection.

translation: Nor any food except the discharge from wounds.
interpretation: The verse portrays the condemned as receiving no nourishing food; instead, they are forced to consume the vile, repulsive discharge of the people of Hell as part of their punishment.

translation: None will eat it except the sinful.
interpretation: This warns that the bitter, loathsome food described is reserved for those who persist in wrongdoing and defy God, serving as a punishment for their sins.

translation: No indeed! I swear by all that you see.
interpretation: God emphatically draws attention to the visible realities before human eyes, making them witnesses to His truth and power, and rejecting any doubt about the revelation and the reality He is affirming.

translation: And by what you do not see.
interpretation: This points to the unseen realities beyond human perception, affirming that what lies outside the senses is still known and witnessed by God.

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.
interpretation: This affirms that the revelation is truthfully conveyed by an honored messenger appointed by God, and is not the invention of a poet, soothsayer, or deceiver.

translation: It is not the word of a poet—little do you believe.
interpretation: The Qur’an is not invented poetry produced by human imagination; it is divine revelation, and your limited belief reflects how little you recognize and accept its truth.

translation: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little is it that you remember.
interpretation: This affirms that the Qur’an is not occult speech or the product of hidden supernatural knowledge conveyed by a diviner. The rebuke indicates that people have too little reflection to recognize its divine source and the clear signs of its truth.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This affirms that the Qur’an comes directly from Allah, the Lord and sustainer of every realm, and therefore its guidance is divine rather than human in origin.

translation: And if he had attributed to Us some sayings,
interpretation: This is a conditional warning affirming that the Messenger conveyed only genuine revelation from God and could not invent words in His name; any such fabrication would incur immediate and severe divine punishment.

translation: We would have seized him by the right hand.
interpretation: This is a forceful expression meaning that if the Messenger had falsely attributed words to God, He would have seized and punished him decisively, leaving him no possibility of escape.

translation: Then We would certainly have severed from him the aorta.
interpretation: This is a forceful expression of absolute divine power: had the Messenger attributed anything falsely to God, Allah would have immediately destroyed him, just as severing the life artery ends life. It therefore affirms the truthfulness of the revelation and the impossibility of fabricating it against God.

translation: And none of you could have shielded him from Us.
interpretation: If the Messenger had falsely attributed anything to Allah, no person or power could have protected him from divine punishment; this affirms that the Qur’an is truly from Allah and that His judgment cannot be obstructed.

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the mindful of Allah.
interpretation: The Qur’an serves as a lasting admonition for those who are conscious of Allah: it awakens their hearts, strengthens their obedience, and guides them toward righteousness.

translation: And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny.
interpretation: Allah affirms His complete knowledge that some among those who hear the revelation reject it, exposing that their denial is known to Him and will not escape His judgment.

translation: And indeed, it is a source of regret for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The disbelievers’ rejection of the Qur’an will become profound remorse when they recognize its truth and face the consequences of denying it.

translation: And indeed, it is surely the ultimate truth of certainty.
interpretation: What has been conveyed is an unquestionably established reality from God, possessing the highest degree of truth and certainty, not something subject to doubt or speculation.

translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.
interpretation: Declare Allah’s transcendence and perfection, honoring Him through sincere praise and worship as the One possessing absolute greatness.

translation: A questioner asked about a punishment bound to fall.
interpretation: The verse conveys that the promised divine punishment is not a matter of doubt or empty threat; its occurrence is certain, even if some people, in arrogance or disbelief, demand to see it brought upon them.

translation: For the disbelievers—there is none to avert it.
interpretation: The punishment ordained for those who reject the truth cannot be prevented or warded off by anyone.

translation: From Allah, Lord of the ascending ways.
interpretation: Allah is described as the possessor of the exalted degrees and means of ascent, emphasizing His supreme transcendence and authority over all creation.

translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as an event of immense duration and gravity by human reckoning, during which the angels and the Spirit ascend in obedience to God; the expression emphasizes the overwhelming magnitude of that Day, not any limitation upon God.

translation: So be patient with gracious patience.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in hardship with dignity and trust in Allah, without despair, resentment, or improper complaint, confident that His wisdom and promise will prevail.

translation: Indeed, they see it as far away.
interpretation: The verse portrays those who deny the promised punishment as viewing it as remote and unlikely, reflecting their heedlessness and false sense of security.

translation: And We see it as near.
interpretation: God declares that what people regard as distant—especially the promised judgment—is, in His knowledge and decree, near and certain.

translation: On the Day when the sky will be like molten metal.
interpretation: This portrays the terrifying upheaval of the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will lose their familiar stability and appear melted and fluid, revealing the overwhelming power of God and the certainty of the final reckoning.

translation: And the mountains will become like carded wool.
interpretation: This portrays the mountains—symbols of firmness and stability—as being torn apart and reduced to something light and scattered, signifying the overwhelming upheaval of the Day of Judgment.

translation: And no close friend will ask about a close friend.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, overwhelming fear will make even the dearest companions so preoccupied with their own fate that they will be unable to concern themselves with one another.

translation: They will be made to see one another. The criminal will wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his sons.
interpretation: On that terrifying Day, people will recognize their loved ones, yet the criminal’s fear will be so overwhelming that he will wish to offer even his own children as payment to escape the punishment—revealing that worldly family bonds and all possible sacrifices will be powerless before divine judgment.

translation: and his wife and his brother
interpretation: It portrays the severity of the punishment and the overwhelming desperation of the guilty person, who would be willing to offer even his closest family members as a ransom to save himself.

translation: and his clan that sheltered him,
interpretation: He would be willing to sacrifice even the family and relatives who had protected and supported him, showing the intensity of his desperation on that Day.

translation: and everyone on earth, all of them, so that it might save him
interpretation: This portrays the desperate wish of the guilty on the Day of Judgment to offer every person on earth as a ransom for himself, yet such a ransom cannot rescue him from the consequences of his deeds.

translation: No indeed! It is the blazing Fire.
interpretation: This emphatic rejection declares that the hoped-for escape or ransom will not avail; the reality awaiting the deniers is Hell, an intensely blazing fire that consumes all before it.

translation: It strips away the skin.
interpretation: This portrays Hellfire as an intensely consuming force that tears away a person’s outer flesh, signifying the severity and inescapability of its punishment.

translation: It calls whoever turned away and turned his back.
interpretation: This describes Hell as an active, inescapable force that draws toward itself those who rejected the truth and deliberately turned away from obedience to God.

translation: And gathered wealth, then hoarded it.
interpretation: It describes one who accumulates possessions obsessively and keeps them from being used in charity or for what is right, treating wealth as something to preserve rather than a trust from God.

translation: Indeed, the human being was created anxious and impatient.
interpretation: Human nature is inclined toward restlessness: adversity quickly makes a person distressed, while fear of losing comfort can make them impatient and unsettled. This describes a natural weakness that must be disciplined through faith and righteous conduct.

translation: When adversity touches him, he is overwhelmed with distress.
interpretation: This describes the human tendency to become impatient and deeply unsettled when hardship strikes, revealing a weakness that requires steadfastness and trust in Allah.

translation: And when good touches him, he becomes withholding.
interpretation: When a person receives wealth or comfort, he may become miserly and refuse to share or fulfill the rights of others, revealing his attachment to possessions and lack of gratitude.

translation: Except those who pray,
interpretation: The exception identifies sincere worshippers whose regular prayer anchors them in obedience to God and protects them from the blameworthy traits described in the surrounding verses.

translation: Those who are constant in their prayer.
interpretation: They preserve their prayer consistently, attending to it at its appointed times and remaining steadfast in worship rather than practicing it only occasionally or when convenient.

translation: And those in whose wealth there is a known right,
interpretation: The righteous recognize that their wealth includes a defined obligation toward those in need, fulfilling it sincerely rather than treating charity as merely optional generosity.

translation: For the one who asks and the deprived.
interpretation: The righteous recognize that part of their wealth is a due right for those who openly seek help and for the needy whose hardship prevents them from asking.

translation: And those who affirm the truth of the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: They are certain that every person will be resurrected and held accountable before God for their deeds, so this certainty guides them to live responsibly and prepare for the Hereafter.

translation: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord,
interpretation: They maintain a deep, reverent fear of their Lord’s accountability, which keeps them away from disobedience and inspires them to remain diligent in obedience and good deeds, without falling into despair of His mercy.

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something from which one can feel secure.
interpretation: A person should not become complacent about disobedience or assume that faith alone makes him immune from accountability; reverence for God requires continual humility, vigilance, and hope joined with fear.

translation: And those who guard their private parts,
interpretation: They preserve their chastity by restraining sexual desire from what Allah has forbidden and by maintaining modesty and moral purity.

translation: Except with their spouses or those whom their right hands possess—for then they are not blameworthy.
interpretation: This passage identifies the lawful bounds of sexual relations in its original legal context: intimacy is permitted within marriage and, at that time, within the institution of legitimately held bondwomen; relations outside these recognized bounds incur blame.

translation: So whoever seeks anything beyond that, they are the transgressors.
interpretation: This warns that sexual desire must remain within the lawful boundaries established by God; pursuing it beyond those boundaries is an act of تجاوز and wrongdoing.

translation: And those who faithfully honor their trusts and covenants.
interpretation: They are people who safeguard whatever is entrusted to them and remain true to their promises and commitments, refusing betrayal or treachery.

translation: And those who uphold their testimonies.
interpretation: They faithfully give truthful testimony, fulfilling their duty to uphold justice without concealing, distorting, or changing what they know.

translation: And those who diligently safeguard their prayers.
interpretation: They remain steadfast in performing the prescribed prayers at their proper times, preserving their obligations and reverence before Allah rather than neglecting or treating them casually.

translation: Those will be honored in gardens.
interpretation: They will reside in Paradise with dignity and honor as a reward from Allah for their faith and righteous deeds.

translation: So what is the matter with those who disbelieve, hastening before you?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical rebuke of the disbelievers who gathered around the Prophet ﷺ, rushing toward him with fixed attention, yet refusing to accept the truth he conveyed.

translation: from the right and from the left, in groups.
interpretation: This portrays the deniers gathering around the Messenger ﷺ from every side in separate circles, observing and discussing the revelation while refusing to accept its truth.

translation: Does every one of them hope to enter a Garden of Bliss?
interpretation: The verse rebukes those who expect the reward of Paradise while persisting in disbelief and disobedience, as though entry into it were guaranteed merely by their wishes.

translation: No indeed! We created them from what they know.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who presume they are entitled to Paradise: they know their own humble origin and dependence, so they have no basis for arrogance or for assuming salvation without faith and obedience. The One who created them from that known origin is fully able to resurrect and judge them.

translation: No! I swear by the Lord of all the points of sunrise and sunset; indeed, We are fully capable.
interpretation: God affirms His absolute power over every place where the sun rises and sets, declaring that nothing is beyond His ability or control.

translation: that We may replace them with better than them, and We cannot be defeated.
interpretation: God affirms that He has complete power to remove those who reject the truth and bring forth others who are better in faith and obedience; no one can prevent or overcome His decree.

translation: So leave them to indulge in vain talk and play until they meet the Day they have been promised.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who persist in mocking truth and treating life as mere amusement will be left to their chosen heedlessness for a time, but they cannot escape the promised Day when they will face its consequences.

translation: The Day they will emerge from their graves swiftly, as though they were rushing toward an erected marker.
interpretation: When resurrection comes, people will rise from their graves and hasten in confusion and urgency toward the place of gathering, like those who race toward a clearly visible landmark.

translation: Their eyes humbled, covered by disgrace; that is the Day they were promised.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, those who rejected the truth will be overwhelmed by humiliation and fear, visibly manifesting the consequences of the warning they had denied.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: “Warn your people before a painful punishment comes upon them.”
interpretation: Allah appointed Noah to warn his people in advance, giving them a clear opportunity to turn back before the consequences of persistent disbelief and wrongdoing reached them. The verse shows that divine punishment is preceded by guidance and warning, so people are not judged without first being made aware.

translation: He said, “O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.”
interpretation: The speaker compassionately addresses his people, declaring that his warning is explicit and unmistakable: he is urging them to recognize the truth and beware of the consequences of rejecting it.

translation: “Worship Allah, be mindful of Him, and obey me.”
interpretation: True devotion to Allah requires reverence that restrains a person from disobedience, together with obedience to His messenger and guidance.

translation: He will forgive you some of your sins and grant you respite until an appointed term. Indeed, when Allah’s appointed time comes, it cannot be postponed—if only you knew.
interpretation: This is a call to respond to faith and obedience without delay: repentance and belief bring Allah’s forgiveness and allow people to continue living until the time He has decreed. Yet that divinely appointed time cannot be extended once it arrives, so people should not assume they can postpone turning to Allah until later.

translation: He said, “My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day.”
interpretation: Noah appeals to God after persistently inviting his people to faith at every time, showing his unwavering devotion and the extraordinary patience he maintained despite their continued rejection.

translation: But my call only increased them in fleeing.
interpretation: Noah’s persistent appeal did not soften his people; because of their stubborn rejection, it only made them turn farther away from the truth.

translation: “Indeed, whenever I called them so that You might forgive them, they thrust their fingers into their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted in rejection, and became exceedingly arrogant.”
interpretation: The verse portrays their deliberate and extreme refusal of guidance: they physically blocked themselves from hearing the truth, hid themselves from the caller, stubbornly continued in disbelief, and allowed arrogance to prevent them from accepting God’s forgiveness.

translation: Then indeed I called them openly.
interpretation: Prophet Noah explains that, after addressing his people privately, he also proclaimed God’s message publicly and without concealment, making the call accessible to everyone.

translation: Then I proclaimed to them openly and addressed them privately.
interpretation: Noah explains that he pursued every suitable means of calling his people to faith: he spoke to them publicly and also approached them discreetly and personally, showing sincere persistence and leaving no appropriate avenue unused in conveying the message.

translation: So I said, “Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed, He is ever Most Forgiving.”
interpretation: This verse calls people to turn sincerely to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness, trusting that His mercy is constant and that He repeatedly forgives those who return to Him.

translation: He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain.
interpretation: This is a promise that sincere repentance and seeking Allah’s forgiveness open the way to His mercy and provision, represented here by plentiful rain and the flourishing blessings it brings.

translation: And He will strengthen you with wealth and sons, and provide you with gardens and provide you with rivers.
interpretation: This is a promise that sincere repentance and seeking Allah’s forgiveness bring His favor and provision, including prosperity, family, fertile lands, and flowing water; these blessings are signs of His mercy and encouragement to remain obedient to Him.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not revere Allah as He deserves to be revered?
interpretation: يعاتب نوحٌ قومه على غفلتهم عن تعظيم الله وخشيته، مع ما يقتضي ربوبيته من إجلالٍ وطاعةٍ واستحضارٍ لقدرته وسلطانه.

translation: And He has created you in stages.
interpretation: God reminds humanity that their creation unfolds through successive stages, demonstrating His wisdom, power, and deliberate care in bringing them from one state of existence to another.

translation: Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens, one above another?
interpretation: The verse calls people to reflect on the ordered, harmonious structure of creation, recognizing in the layered heavens a sign of Allah’s immense power, wisdom, and purposeful design.

translation: And He made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection toward the distinct roles of the moon and the sun: the moon gently illuminates the night, while the sun shines as a powerful source of light and energy. Their ordered functions point to the wisdom and creative power of Allah.

translation: And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth like a plant.
interpretation: Human beings originate from the earth and develop through the stages ordained by Allah, just as a plant grows from the soil; this demonstrates His creative power and humanity’s dependence on Him.

translation: Then He will return you to it and bring you forth again.
interpretation: Allah reminds humanity that its origin and eventual return are tied to the earth: after death, people will be buried in it, and He alone will resurrect them and bring them out for judgment.

translation: And Allah has made the earth for you an expansive resting place.
interpretation: Allah describes the earth as a broad, accessible dwelling prepared for human life, enabling people to settle upon it, travel across it, and benefit from its resources.

translation: So that you may travel along its broad paths.
interpretation: The verse points to how Allah has made the earth accessible, providing wide routes through its terrain so people can move across it, seek their livelihoods, and recognize His provision and wisdom in its design.

translation: Noah said, “My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth and children have only increased them in loss.”
interpretation: Noah appeals to God after his people rejected his call, explaining that they were led by influential figures whose worldly wealth and offspring became a source of arrogance and misguidance rather than gratitude and faith, ultimately deepening their ruin.

translation: And they devised a mighty scheme.
interpretation: The leaders of Noah’s people deliberately crafted an immense and persistent plot to resist his call and keep people from accepting the truth.

translation: And they said, “Never abandon your gods; never abandon Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, or Nasr.”
interpretation: The leaders of Noah’s people urged one another to remain devoted to their idols and not abandon the false worship inherited from their forefathers. The named figures were idols that had come to be venerated instead of Allah, showing how stubbornly they resisted Noah’s call to pure monotheism.

translation: “They have certainly led many astray, so do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance.”
interpretation: This is Noah’s prayer against those who persisted in idolatry and rebellion: their corrupt leaders had misled many, and their continued injustice had made them deserving of being left further in error as a consequence of their deliberate rejection of truth.

translation: Because of their sins, they were drowned, then admitted into the Fire, and they found no helpers for themselves besides Allah.
interpretation: Their persistent wrongdoing and rejection brought upon them both worldly destruction by drowning and punishment in the Hereafter. When Allah’s judgment came, no idol, ally, or worldly power could protect them or provide them with support.

translation: And Noah said, “My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any dwelling of the disbelievers.”
interpretation: Noah appealed to God after his people had persistently rejected the truth and opposed his message, asking that their corruption and defiance no longer be allowed to spread. This expresses the culmination of a long period of patient warning, after which their continued rejection had made their destruction a just consequence.

translation: “Indeed, if You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray and will beget none but wicked disbelievers.”
interpretation: Noah, peace be upon him, expresses that his people’s persistent rejection and corrupting influence had become so deep that, if allowed to continue, they would mislead others and raise offspring within disbelief and defiance. This is a supplication concerning a people who had exhausted the opportunity for repentance, not a judgment that every descendant is inherently wicked.

translation: My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and all believing men and women; and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: This supplication reflects the believer’s humility before God, beginning with a plea for personal forgiveness and extending it to parents and the entire community of faith. Its closing appeal entrusts the fate of persistent oppressors to divine justice, asking that their wrongdoing lead not to greater power but to ruin.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened, and they said, “Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur’an.”
interpretation: This verse reveals that the Qur’an’s guidance and miraculous eloquence affect not only human beings but also the unseen world. The jinn recognized its extraordinary nature through sincere listening, showing that truth is acknowledged by those who approach it with attentiveness and openness.

translation: “It guides to right guidance, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.”
interpretation: The believers affirm that the Qur’an leads to the truth and sound conduct, and their faith in it commits them to pure monotheism, rejecting every form of associating partners with Allah.

translation: And exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a wife or a son.
interpretation: This affirms that Allah is utterly beyond human qualities and needs: He has no partner, spouse, or offspring, because His perfection and absolute independence exclude any such attributes.

translation: And our foolish one used to utter outrageous falsehoods about Allah.
interpretation: The jinn acknowledge that the ignorant and corrupt among them attributed to Allah claims far removed from truth and justice, warning that such reckless speech is a grave form of misguidance.

translation: وأنّا ظننّا أن لن تقولَ الإنسُ والجنُّ على اللهِ كذبًا.
interpretation: يُقرّ الجنّ بأنهم كانوا يظنّون أن الإنس والجن لن يختلقوا على الله قولًا باطلًا، ثم تبيّن لهم أن بعضهم نسب إلى الله ما لا يليق به من الشرك والافتراء، فكان ذلك تنبيهًا إلى ضرورة التثبّت في كل ما يُنسب إلى الله.

translation: And indeed, there were men among humankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so they only increased them in burden and distress.
interpretation: The verse condemns seeking supernatural protection from the jinn instead of turning to God: such reliance emboldens the jinn in their arrogance and leaves people more fearful, vulnerable, and burdened.

translation: And they thought, just as you thought, that Allah would never resurrect anyone.
interpretation: The verse exposes the unfounded assumption shared by them: that death is the end and that no one will be raised for judgment. This belief is not knowledge but mere conjecture, whereas Allah has the power to resurrect every person.

translation: “We sought to reach the heaven, but found it filled with mighty guards and flaming projectiles.”
interpretation: The jinn testify that the heavenly realm had been firmly guarded, with meteors serving as a means of preventing them from secretly listening to the revelation. This portrays the Qur’an as divinely protected from interference and confirms that access to its unseen source is not open to devils.

translation: “And we used to sit there in positions for listening; but whoever listens now will find a flaming meteor lying in wait for him.”
interpretation: The verse conveys that the unseen realm was no longer accessible to the jinn as it had been before; divine revelation was protected from their attempts to overhear it, with the meteors serving as a sign of this newly imposed protection.

translation: “And we do not know whether evil has been intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord has intended guidance for them.”
interpretation: The jinn acknowledge the limits of their knowledge regarding the unseen: they cannot determine whether the coming event will bring punishment to the inhabitants of the earth or whether God intends guidance and goodness for them. Their wording reflects humility before divine wisdom and attributes guidance directly to their Lord, while avoiding the direct attribution of evil to Him.

translation: “Among us are the righteous, and among us are otherwise; we have followed diverse paths.”
interpretation: يقرّ الجن بأنهم ليسوا على حال واحدة؛ فمنهم المستقيمون الطائعون، ومنهم المنحرفون، وأن اختلافهم نابع من تباين مسالكهم ومواقفهم من الحق، لا من انتمائهم إلى جنس واحد.

translation: And we realized that we could never frustrate Allah on earth, nor could we escape Him by fleeing.
interpretation: The verse expresses the jinn’s recognition that Allah’s power encompasses them completely: neither earthly schemes nor flight can place anyone beyond His knowledge, authority, and judgment.

translation: “And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord need fear neither loss of reward nor oppression.”
interpretation: True faith in God gives the believer reassurance that God will not diminish the good he has earned or treat him unjustly; therefore, he need not fear either deprivation or being overwhelmed by wrongdoing and humiliation.

translation: ومنّا المسلمون، ومنّا الجائرون عن الحق؛ فمن أسلم فأولئك قصدوا طريق الرشد.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الجن، كالبشر، مختلفون في مواقفهم: فمنهم من خضع لله واتبع الحق، ومنهم من انحرف عنه وظلم نفسه. ومن يسلّم لله ويطلب رضاه فإنه يسلك بإخلاص طريق الهداية والصواب.

translation: As for those who deviate from justice, they will be fuel for Hell.
interpretation: Those who persist in injustice, rejection of truth, and disobedience to God will face the severe consequence of becoming fuel for Hell, expressing the ultimate loss and punishment brought about by their own wrongdoing.

translation: And if they had remained steadfast on the way, We would have given them abundant water.
interpretation: This indicates that steadfastness upon the path of faith and obedience is a cause for receiving abundant divine provision and blessing.

translation: So that We may test them through it. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will subject him to an increasingly severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse teaches that worldly blessings, including abundance and ease, are a test of whether people remain grateful and obedient to God. Turning away from His remembrance and guidance leads a person into a punishment that is difficult, escalating, and without relief.

translation: And the mosques belong to Allah, so do not invoke anyone alongside Allah.
interpretation: Places of worship are devoted exclusively to Allah, and all acts of prayer, supplication, and worship must be directed to Him alone, without associating any partner or intermediary with Him.

translation: And when the servant of Allah stood calling upon Him, they nearly crowded around him in heaps.
interpretation: When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stood in prayer, worshipping Allah and reciting His words, the jinn gathered densely around him, eager to listen to the Qur’an and learn from his devotion.

translation: Say: “I call only upon my Lord, and I associate no one with Him.”
interpretation: The verse affirms pure devotion to Allah alone: the Messenger directs worship and supplication exclusively to his Lord and completely rejects attributing any partner or intermediary with divine status to Him.

translation: Say, “I have no power to cause you harm or to guide you.”
interpretation: The Prophet is commanded to make clear that he is only a servant and messenger of God: he does not independently control benefit or harm, nor can he grant guidance to anyone. These matters belong solely to God, while the Prophet’s role is to convey the revelation faithfully.

translation: قل: إنني لن يحميني من الله أحد، ولن أجد من دونه ملجأً.
interpretation: في الآية إقرارٌ بأن الحماية الحقيقية لا تكون إلا من الله، وأنه لا ملجأ ولا مهرب من قضائه وسلطانه إلى غيره؛ ولذلك يجب التوكل عليه وحده واللجوء إليه دون سواه.

translation: [My duty is] only to convey [the message] from Allah and His revelations. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger—surely for him is the Fire of Hell, remaining in it forever.
interpretation: The verse clarifies that the Messenger’s responsibility is to faithfully deliver Allah’s revelation, while those who knowingly reject Allah’s command and the Messenger’s guidance face the lasting consequence of Hell; this warning emphasizes the seriousness of obedience to divine revelation.

translation: Until, when they see what they have been promised, they will know who is weaker in support and fewer in number.
interpretation: This is a warning that those who reject the truth and rely on their worldly strength will ultimately recognize, when the promised punishment comes, that the believers were not the weak party; rather, their own supporters and numbers will prove insufficient before God’s judgment.

translation: Say, “I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord has appointed a distant term for it.”
interpretation: The verse teaches that knowledge of the timing of the promised divine judgment belongs solely to Allah; even the Messenger does not claim knowledge of the unseen except what Allah reveals, so people must not demand a timetable for its occurrence.

translation: He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone.
interpretation: All knowledge of what is hidden from human perception belongs to Allah alone; no created being can access it independently or know it except through whatever portion Allah chooses to reveal.

translation: Except for a messenger whom He has chosen; then He appoints watchers before him and behind him.
interpretation: Allah grants knowledge of the unseen only to a messenger whom He has chosen, and He surrounds that messenger with angelic guardians who protect the revelation from interference and ensure that it is conveyed faithfully.

translation: So that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; He encompasses all that is with them and has counted everything precisely.
interpretation: God appoints safeguards around His messengers so that the revelation reaches its recipients intact, while His complete knowledge encompasses the messengers, their circumstances, and every detail of creation without anything escaping His precise reckoning.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who are wrapped in garments,
interpretation: Allah addresses the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with gentleness in his solitude and rest, preparing him to rise from repose and undertake the demanding spiritual responsibility of conveying His revelation.

translation: Rise for prayer at night, except for a little of it.
interpretation: This is a command to devote part of the night to worship and prayer, while allowing a limited portion for rest.

translation: Half of it, or reduce it a little.
interpretation: Spend half the night in prayer, or pray for slightly less than half, allowing a measured degree of ease and flexibility in worship.

translation: Or add to it, and recite the Qur’an with measured, deliberate recitation.
interpretation: This instructs the Prophet to devote more than half the night, when possible, to a calm and precise recitation of the Qur’an, giving each word its due and allowing its meanings to be contemplated and embodied.

translation: Indeed, We shall cast upon you a weighty word.
interpretation: Allah is informing the Prophet ﷺ that the revelation entrusted to him carries immense spiritual, moral, and practical responsibility. It is “weighty” because it contains profound truth, demands steadfast obedience, and requires him to bear the burden of conveying and living by it before humanity.

translation: Indeed, the rising at night is more effective in disciplining the soul and more conducive to upright speech.
interpretation: Night worship has a stronger influence on the heart because its quiet and freedom from distraction make a person more sincere, attentive, and receptive to the Qur’an; therefore, what is recited and contemplated at that time is more firmly established and more truthfully expressed.

translation: Indeed, you have prolonged activity during the day.
interpretation: The verse indicates that the daytime is filled with varied duties, movements, and worldly engagements, making the night the more suitable time for devoted worship, reflection, and recitation.

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.
interpretation: Keep your heart and worship sincerely turned toward God alone, freeing yourself from every distraction and relying on Him with wholehearted dedication.

translation: He is the Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as your Trustee.
interpretation: Since Allah alone governs every direction and all that exists, and none shares His divinity, place your complete trust in Him, entrusting your affairs to Him while relying on no ultimate protector or provider besides Him.

translation: And be patient with what they say, and avoid them with gracious avoidance.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in the face of their hurtful words, and distance yourself from them without retaliation, hostility, or abandoning dignity and good character.

translation: Leave Me to deal with the deniers, those living in comfort, and give them a little respite.
interpretation: God instructs the Prophet not to be distressed by the rejection of those who enjoy worldly prosperity. Their temporary freedom and ease do not mean they have escaped accountability; God is allowing them a brief reprieve before confronting them with the consequences of their denial.

translation: Indeed, We have shackles and a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that those who persist in rejecting truth and opposing God’s guidance will face constraining punishment and an intensely burning Hellfire.

translation: And food that chokes, and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This depicts the severe punishment awaiting the deniers: they will be given food that is difficult to swallow and causes choking, accompanied by unrelenting physical torment.

translation: On the Day when the earth and the mountains will tremble, and the mountains will become heaps of crumbling sand.
interpretation: The verse portrays the overwhelming upheaval of the Day of Judgment: even the earth and the seemingly immovable mountains will lose their stability and collapse, showing that all worldly strength and permanence are subject to God’s power.

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh.
interpretation: God reminds the people that the Messenger has been sent to convey the truth and bear witness to their response, just as Moses was sent to Pharaoh. This establishes that divine guidance brings both a clear opportunity for obedience and a serious accountability for rejecting it.

translation: But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a grievous seizure.
interpretation: The verse warns that knowingly rejecting God’s messenger and persisting in rebellion brings a severe and unavoidable punishment from God.

translation: How, then, will you protect yourselves if you disbelieve in a Day that will turn children’s hair gray?
interpretation: The verse warns that the terror of the Day of Resurrection will be so overwhelming that even children—symbols of innocence and youth—will be affected by it; therefore, disbelief offers no refuge from its consequences, and one must seek protection through faith and obedience before that Day arrives.

translation: The sky will split apart because of it; His promise is bound to be fulfilled.
interpretation: The verse portrays the Day of Judgment as an event so momentous that even the heavens will rupture, affirming that God’s promised reckoning will certainly come to pass without fail.

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder; so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse presents the Qur’an as a means of awakening and guidance, inviting each person to consciously choose the path that leads to Allah through faith, obedience, and sincere devotion.

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand in prayer for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, as does a group of those with you. Allah measures the night and the day. He knows that you will not be able to keep exact count, so He has turned to you in mercy. Therefore, recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that some of you will be ill, others will travel through the land seeking Allah’s bounty, and others will fight in Allah’s cause. So recite whatever is easy of it, establish prayer, give zakah, and lend Allah a good loan. Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allah—better and greater in reward. And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse teaches that devotion is measured by sincere perseverance, not by burdensome precision or exhausting oneself beyond one’s capacity. Allah acknowledges the Prophet’s and his companions’ night worship, then eases the obligation when illness, travel, work, and striving in His cause make prolonged worship difficult. Believers are therefore to maintain whatever portion of Qur’an recitation and prayer they can sustain, while fulfilling their communal duties through zakah and generous charity. Every good deed offered sincerely is preserved by Allah and returned with a reward greater than the deed itself. The verse closes by directing believers to repentance and seeking forgiveness, showing that steadfast worship, service to others, hope in Allah’s reward, and humility before His mercy belong together.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O you who are wrapped in garments,
interpretation: Allah addresses the Prophet ﷺ in his state of being wrapped up, gently calling him to rise from seclusion and prepare himself for the weighty responsibility of conveying the divine message.

translation: قم فأنذر
interpretation: فيه أمرٌ للنبي ﷺ أن ينهض بعزيمة، فيحذّر الناس من الشرك والعصيان، ويدعوهم إلى توحيد الله والاستعداد للقائه.

translation: And proclaim the greatness of your Lord.
interpretation: Recognize Allah as greater than all things, exalt Him above every partner or imperfection, and let this conviction govern your worship and conduct.

translation: And purify your garments.
interpretation: This commands the Prophet to maintain outward cleanliness while embodying inward purity, freeing himself from every impurity and conduct unworthy of his mission.

translation: And shun all impurity.
interpretation: You are commanded to keep completely away from idolatry, sin, and every form of spiritual impurity, remaining devoted solely to Allah.

translation: And do not give expecting to receive more in return.
interpretation: Do not perform acts of generosity or kindness with the expectation of gaining greater worldly benefit, influence, or repayment; give sincerely for God’s sake.

translation: And for the sake of your Lord, be patient.
interpretation: Remain steadfast in obeying your Lord and carrying out His command, seeking only His pleasure, even when the path brings hardship or delay.

translation: Then, when the Trumpet is blown,
interpretation: This evokes the decisive moment when the trumpet announces the Resurrection, ending the world’s present order and summoning all people to stand before Allah for judgment.

translation: That Day will be a difficult day.
interpretation: It refers to the Day of Judgment as a time of immense hardship and distress for those who rejected the truth, when they will face the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Not easy for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The coming divine reckoning will be extremely difficult for those who reject faith, leaving them unable to escape its severity or consequences.

translation: Leave Me to deal with the one whom I created alone.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that God Himself will hold accountable the person who, despite being created helpless and alone, becomes arrogant and hostile toward the truth; no worldly power can shield him from God’s judgment.

translation: And I granted him abundant wealth.
interpretation: The verse indicates that Allah bestowed upon him vast, plentiful wealth as a blessing and a test, making his later ingratitude and rejection all the more blameworthy.

translation: And sons present with him,
interpretation: He was granted sons who were always at his side, representing the worldly blessings and support surrounding him.

translation: And I prepared everything for him thoroughly.
interpretation: Allah reminds him that He generously expanded his means, granted him comfort and influence, and made his path in life easy—blessings that should have led him to gratitude and obedience.

translation: Then he hopes that I will give him more.
interpretation: This portrays the ingratitude of one who, despite receiving abundant blessings, remains consumed by expectation and greed for further increase rather than acknowledging and being grateful for what has already been granted.

translation: No indeed! He has been obstinately opposed to Our signs.
interpretation: This is a stern rebuke of one who knowingly rejects God’s revelations, refusing to submit to their truth despite recognizing their evidence.

translation: I will burden him with an arduous ascent.
interpretation: Allah will subject him to relentless hardship and punishment, making him endure a painful struggle with no relief or escape.

translation: Indeed, he thought and calculated.
interpretation: He carefully considered what to say about the Qur’an and deliberately devised a judgment against it, rather than responding to it with sincerity.

translation: So may he perish—how he plotted!
interpretation: This is a forceful condemnation of the person who schemed against the truth: his deliberate calculation and opposition are so blameworthy that he deserves ruin.

translation: Then may he perish—how he plotted!
interpretation: This is a forceful condemnation of the person who deliberately devised a calculated judgment against the Qur’an, exposing the arrogance and hostility behind his scheme and invoking ruin upon him for it.

translation: Then he looked.
interpretation: He paused to contemplate and assess what he had heard before deciding how to respond.

translation: Then he frowned and scowled.
interpretation: He reacted to the truth with visible displeasure, his face tightening in rejection and hostility.

translation: Then he turned away and acted arrogantly.
interpretation: He deliberately rejected the truth after recognizing it, driven by pride and unwillingness to submit.

translation: So he said, “This is nothing but magic transmitted from others.”
interpretation: He dismisses the Qur’an as an imitation of earlier magical sayings, rather than acknowledging it as divine revelation.

translation: This is nothing but the word of a human being.
interpretation: This is the false claim of those who rejected the Qur’an: they dismissed it as human speech rather than acknowledging it as revelation from Allah.

translation: سأدخله سَقَر.
interpretation: هذا وعيدٌ حازمٌ من الله لمن أعرض عن الحقّ وكذّب به، بأنه سيُلقى في نار جهنم المسماة سَقَر، جزاءً على عناده وإصراره على الكفر.

translation: And what will make you know what Saqar is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes that Saqar is a punishment of such terrifying severity and magnitude that its true reality exceeds human understanding.

translation: It leaves nothing and spares nothing.
interpretation: This describes the overwhelming severity of Hellfire: it consumes everything cast into it and gives its inhabitants no respite or relief.

translation: Scorching the skin.
interpretation: This describes Hellfire as an intensely burning force that chars human flesh, conveying the severity and inescapable pain of its punishment.

translation: Over it are nineteen.
interpretation: Nineteen angels have been appointed as guardians over Hell.

translation: We have appointed only angels as guardians of the Fire, and We have appointed their number only as a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Scripture may become certain, and those who believe may increase in faith, and so that those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt, while those in whose hearts is sickness and the disbelievers may say, “What does Allah intend by this example?” Thus Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.
