translation: And what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes that the true magnitude and terror of the Day when every person is judged and repaid cannot be fully grasped by human understanding.

translation: Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: This expression emphasizes that the reality and immense severity of the Day of Judgment surpass human imagination and cannot be fully grasped without divine revelation.

translation: The Day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul; and on that Day, all authority belongs to Allah.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, every person will stand entirely responsible before Allah, unable to benefit, protect, or rescue another through personal power. All judgment and command will belong solely to Allah, whose authority will be completely manifest.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Woe to those who give less than due.
interpretation: This is a stern warning to those who cheat people in measures, weights, or any form of transaction by taking their full entitlement while giving others less. The verse condemns not merely a commercial practice but the injustice and betrayal underlying it, calling people to uphold honesty and give others their complete rights.

translation: Those who, when they take by measure from people, demand it in full,
interpretation: This describes people who insist on receiving their complete due from others, revealing their selfishness and lack of fairness when dealing with others.

translation: وإذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوهم يُنقِصونهم.
interpretation: تُدين الآية من يطلب حقَّه كاملًا، لكنه حين يبيع أو يزن للآخرين يُنقِصهم حقوقهم، فتبيّن أن العدل في المعاملات يجب أن يكون متبادلًا لا انتقائيًا.

translation: Do those people not think that they will be resurrected?
interpretation: This is a reproachful question challenging their heedlessness: how can they cheat others and act unjustly when they should realize that they will be raised before God and held fully accountable for their deeds?

translation: For a tremendous Day.
interpretation: It refers to the Day of Resurrection, whose immense seriousness and overwhelming events demand that people prepare by living in obedience to God.

translation: The Day when humanity will stand before the Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: It portrays the Day of Resurrection, when every person will rise and stand in complete submission before Allah to be judged for their deeds.

translation: No indeed! The record of the wicked is surely in Sijjīn.
interpretation: This declares that the deeds and destinies of those who persist in wickedness are confined to Sijjīn—a place or register of humiliation and punishment—signifying their complete exclusion from God’s honor and mercy.

translation: And what will make you know what Sijjīn is?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical expression emphasizing the terrifying reality of Sijjīn: the sealed register in which the deeds of the wicked are recorded, signifying their humiliation and confinement under God’s judgment.

translation: A written record.
interpretation: It refers to a precisely recorded register in which the deeds and destinies of those concerned are preserved without ambiguity or omission.

translation: Woe, on that Day, to those who deny the truth.
interpretation: This is a severe warning that, on the Day of Judgment, those who persistently reject God’s signs and deny the truth will face ruin and divine punishment.

translation: Those who deny the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: They are described as rejecting the certainty that all people will be resurrected and held accountable before God for their deeds.

translation: And none denies it except every transgressor and sinner.
interpretation: The truth is rejected only by those whose persistent wrongdoing and sinful conduct have corrupted their judgment and led them to oppose what they know to be true.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Legends of the former peoples.”
interpretation: This portrays the arrogant denier who, rather than reflecting on God’s signs and accepting their truth, dismisses them as ancient myths in order to reject their guidance and avoid accountability.

translation: No indeed! Rather, a stain has covered their hearts because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: Their persistent wrongdoing has gradually formed a spiritual covering over their hearts, weakening their ability to recognize and accept the truth.

translation: No indeed! On that Day they will be veiled from their Lord.
interpretation: This is a decisive rejection of the sinners’ false assumptions: on the Day of Judgment, their denial and corruption will result in their being excluded from closeness to Allah and deprived of His mercy and honor.

translation: Then indeed they will enter the Hellfire.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that those referred to will inevitably face the punishment of Hell, with no escape from its consequences.

translation: Then it will be said, “This is what you used to deny.”
interpretation: When the deniers face the punishment they rejected in worldly life, its reality will become unmistakably clear, leaving them without any excuse for their persistent rejection of the truth.

translation: No indeed! The record of the righteous is surely in ʿIlliyyūn.
interpretation: The deeds and record of the righteous are preserved in a lofty, honored station with Allah, signifying their exalted rank, acceptance, and ultimate reward.

translation: And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?
interpretation: This awe-inspiring question draws attention to the exalted and hidden rank of ʿIlliyyūn, emphasizing that its true reality is beyond ordinary human knowledge.

translation: A written record.
interpretation: It refers to a preserved register in which the deeds and destiny of the wicked are distinctly and irrevocably recorded.

translation: The ones brought near witness it.
interpretation: This indicates that the record or reality referred to is openly witnessed by the angels and righteous servants who are near to Allah, affirming its truth and honour.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
interpretation: Those who remain faithful to God and live virtuously will be granted enduring happiness, peace, and honor as a reward for their righteousness.

translation: Upon couches, they will be looking.
interpretation: This portrays the believers in Paradise resting in dignity and security, calmly witnessing the fulfillment of God’s promise after the trials of worldly life.

translation: تتعرف في وجوههم إشراقة النعيم وبهجته.
interpretation: تظهر على وجوه أهل النعيم آثار الرضا والسرور والكرامة، حتى يُدرك ما هم فيه من نعيم من خلال إشراقة محيّاهم.

translation: They will be given to drink sealed, pure nectar.
interpretation: This depicts the honored people of Paradise enjoying a drink of perfect purity and excellence, preserved from every impurity and offered to them as a special, dignified reward.

translation: Its seal is musk; so for this let those who compete strive.
interpretation: The reward prepared for the righteous is so pure and precious that its very seal carries the fragrance of musk. Therefore, believers should direct their ambition and sincere effort toward attaining God’s eternal pleasure and the blessings of the Hereafter.

translation: And its mixture is from Tasnīm,
interpretation: The pure drink prepared for the righteous is blended with water from Tasnīm, a lofty and honored spring in Paradise, signifying the exceptional purity and exalted reward granted to them.

translation: A spring from which those brought near to Allah drink.
interpretation: It depicts the people nearest to Allah enjoying a pure, honored drink from a blessed spring in Paradise, as a reward for their spiritual excellence and closeness to Him.

translation: Indeed, those who committed sins used to laugh at those who believed.
interpretation: This portrays the arrogance of the wrongdoers, who mocked the believers because of their faith and obedience, mistaking worldly status and conformity to falsehood for proof of superiority. Their ridicule reveals their moral blindness, not any deficiency in the believers.

translation: And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another.
interpretation: This portrays the arrogant mockery of the wrongdoers: whenever they encountered the believers, they exchanged derisive gestures and secretly ridiculed them, revealing their contempt and scorn.

translation: And when they returned to their families, they would return jesting and amused.
interpretation: This portrays the arrogant criminals mocking the believers and returning home pleased with their ridicule, unaware that their worldly amusement would not protect them from accountability before God.

translation: And when they saw them, they said, “Indeed, these are surely astray.”
interpretation: This portrays the arrogant rejection of the believers by those who denied the truth: they judged them as misguided simply because their faith and righteous conduct differed from the ways of worldly people.

translation: Yet they were not sent as guardians over them.
interpretation: The mockers had no authority or responsibility to judge, control, or oversee the believers; their arrogant condemnation was entirely unjustified.

translation: So today those who believed laugh at the disbelievers.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the believers will witness the humiliation of those who mocked and oppressed them, and their joy will arise from seeing divine justice fulfilled.

translation: Upon couches, they will look on.
interpretation: The righteous will rest in honor and serenity, gazing upon the blessings and delightful scene Allah has granted them in Paradise.

translation: Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical affirmation that the disbelievers will receive the fitting recompense for their rejection of truth and the harm they inflicted upon the believers; their punishment is a just consequence of their deeds.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split asunder,
interpretation: This verse portrays the beginning of the Day of Resurrection, when the ordered structure of the heavens will be torn apart by Allah’s command, signaling the end of the present world and the opening of the scene of final judgment.

translation: And it has listened to its Lord and rightly obeyed.
interpretation: The earth will respond fully to Allah’s command on the Day of Resurrection, submitting to the transformation He decrees and thereby revealing that His authority is absolute and that all creation is bound to obey Him.

translation: And when the earth is stretched out,
interpretation: This depicts the earth on the Day of Resurrection being expanded and leveled, with its familiar features removed, as it is prepared for the gathering and judgment of all people.

translation: and casts forth what is within it and becomes empty,
interpretation: This portrays the earth on the Day of Resurrection surrendering all that it has concealed—especially the dead and their remains—until nothing hidden remains within it, in complete submission to God’s command.

translation: And it has listened to its Lord and obeyed as it was bound to do.
interpretation: The earth will submit completely to Allah’s command on the Day of Judgment, responding to His decree without resistance, as befits His absolute authority over it.

translation: O human being, you are striving laboriously toward your Lord, and you will meet Him.
interpretation: Every person is unavoidably journeying through effort, struggle, and the passage of life toward an encounter with God; therefore, one should understand that every deed and choice is leading toward the moment of standing before Him and will be met with its due consequence.

translation: As for the one who is given his record in his right hand,
interpretation: This portrays the honor and acceptance granted to the righteous on the Day of Judgment: receiving the record in the right hand signifies that their faith and deeds have been approved, and that they are destined for salvation.

translation: Then he will be given an easy reckoning.
interpretation: This refers to the believer whose deeds are presented to him with gentleness and without a prolonged, exhaustive interrogation; God overlooks his faults and grants him mercy.

translation: And he will return to his people joyful.
interpretation: This portrays the believer’s profound happiness upon attaining salvation and returning to his loved ones in Paradise, secure from punishment and delighted by Allah’s reward.

translation: But as for the one who is given his record behind his back,
interpretation: This depicts the utter humiliation and condemnation of the person whose deeds are presented to him from behind, signifying that he has been denied honor and acceptance on the Day of Judgment because of his rejection and wrongdoing.

translation: Then he will call for destruction.
interpretation: Overwhelmed by regret and impending punishment, he will plead for death and annihilation as an escape from his fate.

translation: And he will burn in a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This warns that the one who turns away from God’s guidance and persists in wrongdoing will face the severe punishment of Hell.

translation: Indeed, he used to be joyful among his family.
interpretation: He lived in worldly comfort and carefree delight, feeling secure among his family while heedlessly neglecting faith and accountability before God.

translation: Indeed, he thought that he would never return.
interpretation: He lived under the delusion that he would not be brought back to Allah for resurrection and reckoning, so he felt no need to fear accountability for his deeds.

translation: Indeed, his Lord has always been All-Seeing of him.
interpretation: Allah has complete and constant knowledge of this person’s inner state and outward deeds; nothing about him is hidden from Him, and he will therefore be judged with perfect justice.

translation: Nay, I swear by the twilight.
interpretation: Allah calls attention to the twilight as a profound sign of His power: the fading light marks the ordered transition between day and night and invites reflection on the certainty of change and renewal.

translation: By the night and what it gathers in.
interpretation: God draws attention to the night as a sign of His power: it envelops and gathers creation beneath its darkness, bringing the world into a state of stillness and concealment.

translation: And by the moon when it is full.
interpretation: God draws attention to the moon as it reaches its complete brightness and fullness, pointing to His orderly power and the changing stages through which creation unfolds.

translation: You will surely pass from one stage to another.
interpretation: This means that people will move through successive conditions and transformations—life, death, resurrection, and judgment—until they reach their final destiny before God.

translation: So what is the matter with them that they do not believe?
interpretation: This is a reproachful question expressing amazement at people who refuse faith despite the clear signs and reminders presented to them; nothing prevents them from believing except their own rejection and heedlessness.

translation: And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate.
interpretation: This depicts the obstinate refusal of those who reject the truth: although the Qur’an reaches them, pride and denial prevent them from humbly submitting to God and responding with worship.

translation: Rather, those who disbelieve deny the truth.
interpretation: The verse exposes the true cause of their rejection: not a lack of evidence, but a deliberate refusal to accept and affirm the revelation after it has reached them.

translation: And Allah knows best what they store up.
interpretation: Allah is fully aware of everything they conceal and harbor within themselves, including their intentions and rejection, and nothing hidden from Him escapes His knowledge.

translation: So give them the good news of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This is a warning directed at those who knowingly reject God’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly, and oppose those who call for justice: their defiance will lead to a severe and unavoidable punishment.

translation: Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that never ends.
interpretation: Those who combine sincere faith with righteous action are exempt from the consequences of moral decline, and Allah grants them a reward that is continuous, undiminished, and never cut off.

translation: By the sky adorned with constellations,
interpretation: God draws attention to the majestic, ordered heavens as a sign of His power, wisdom, and sovereignty over creation.

translation: And the Promised Day,
interpretation: This refers to the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has appointed as the निश्चित time when all people will be gathered and judged according to their deeds.

translation: والشاهد والمشهود.
interpretation: يقسم الله بكل شاهدٍ يشهد، وبكل مشهودٍ تُشهد عليه أفعال العباد، تنبيهًا إلى أن الأعمال معلومة محفوظة وسيُحاسَب الناس عليها.

translation: Cursed were the companions of the trench.
interpretation: This verse condemns the tyrants who dug trenches and burned believing people alive because of their faith, declaring them deserving of destruction for their brutal persecution and opposition to the truth.

translation: The fire ablaze with fuel.
interpretation: It depicts an intensely burning fire, emphasizing the severity and terrifying power of the punishment prepared for those who oppose the truth.

translation: As they sat beside it,
interpretation: This depicts the persecutors seated around the trench, deliberately watching the fire and the believers cast into it, revealing their coldness and cruel persistence.

translation: And they are witnesses to what they do to the believers.
interpretation: The verse portrays the persecutors as fully aware of the torture and oppression they inflict on the believers, emphasizing their deliberate responsibility and the fact that none of their wrongdoing is hidden from God.

translation: They resented them only because they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse exposes the utter injustice of persecuting the believers: their only supposed offense was their sincere faith in Allah, whose power cannot be overcome and whose perfection merits all praise.

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: Everything in the heavens and the earth is under Allah’s absolute ownership and authority, and nothing—whether hidden or apparent—escapes His knowledge and witnessing.

translation: Indeed, those who persecuted believing men and women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell and the punishment of burning.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who deliberately subject believers to persecution and oppression face a severe punishment because of their wrongdoing; yet it also indicates that sincere repentance remains open to them before death, whereas persisting without repentance leads to the promised punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have Gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great success.
interpretation: True faith is shown through righteous action, and its lasting reward is entry into Paradise—a success far greater than any worldly gain because it is eternal and granted by God.

translation: Indeed, the grip of your Lord is severe.
interpretation: This is a warning that God’s punishment of those who persist in wrongdoing is powerful and inescapable, so no oppressor should feel secure from His justice.

translation: Indeed, He originates creation and brings it back.
interpretation: Allah alone brings creation into existence from nothing, and He alone is able to restore it after death; thus resurrection is fully within His power.

translation: And He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Loving.
interpretation: Allah repeatedly forgives those who turn to Him and lovingly bestows His mercy and favor upon them.

translation: The Possessor of the Glorious Throne.
interpretation: It affirms that Allah alone possesses the Throne, signifying His supreme authority, majesty, and absolute dominion over all creation.

translation: He does whatever He wills.
interpretation: Allah’s will is absolute and unconstrained: whatever He decrees comes to pass, and no power can prevent or limit His action.

translation: هل بلغك خبرُ الجنود؟
interpretation: يُلفت الله تعالى نظر النبي ﷺ إلى مصائر الجبابرة الذين امتلكوا القوة والجيوش، ليُدرك الناس أن كثرة العدد والعدة لا تمنع عذاب الله ولا تُغني عن الظالمين شيئًا.

translation: Pharaoh and Thamūd.
interpretation: This is a reference to two once-powerful peoples who were destroyed after rejecting God’s guidance and acting arrogantly, serving as a warning that worldly power cannot protect those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Rather, those who disbelieve persist in denial.
interpretation: The disbelievers are not rejecting the truth because it is unclear to them; they are entrenched in denial and refuse to accept it despite the signs and evidence before them.

translation: And Allah encompasses them from behind.
interpretation: Nothing they do can escape Allah’s knowledge, power, and control; He completely surrounds them even when they imagine they can evade Him.

translation: Rather, it is a Glorious Qur’an.
interpretation: The Qur’an is exalted in rank, noble in its source and message, and far above the falsehoods attributed to it by those who reject it.

translation: In a Preserved Tablet.
interpretation: This indicates that the Qur’an is recorded in a divinely safeguarded register, protected from loss, alteration, or corruption by Allah’s decree.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the sky and the night visitor.
interpretation: Allah swears by the vast sky and by the striking celestial visitor that appears at night, directing human attention to the signs of His power and wisdom in creation.

translation: And what will make you realize what the Night-Comer is?
interpretation: This verse magnifies the significance of the heavenly visitor mentioned as “the Night-Comer,” emphasizing that its true nature and importance are beyond ordinary human perception and can be known only through the explanation that follows.

translation: The piercing star.
interpretation: This refers to a star whose intense light penetrates the darkness, evoking the unmistakable power and precision of Allah’s creation.

translation: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it.
interpretation: No person is left without divine oversight: Allah has appointed guardians who watch, record, and preserve each soul, so every deed and intention remains known and accountable before Him.

translation: So let man consider from what he was created.
interpretation: The verse calls the human being to reflect humbly on his origin: despite his present strength, dignity, and abilities, he began from a simple substance created by God. Remembering this origin should lead him to recognize God’s power, abandon arrogance, and acknowledge his dependence on Him.

translation: He was created from a gushing fluid.
interpretation: This verse reminds the human being of his humble origin: he was brought into existence from a fluid that emerges forcefully, demonstrating God’s power to create and His authority to resurrect.

translation: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs.
interpretation: The verse refers to the gushing reproductive fluid, indicating that human creation originates through the reproductive organs located in the region between the backbone and the ribs.

translation: Indeed, He is fully capable of restoring him.
interpretation: The verse affirms that Allah has complete power to bring the human being back to life after death, just as He brought him into existence in the first place.

translation: On the Day when secrets are examined,
interpretation: It refers to the Day of Judgment, when a person’s hidden beliefs, intentions, and deeds will be brought to light and judged by Allah, leaving nothing concealed.

translation: Then he will have no power, nor any helper.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the denier will possess neither personal strength to save himself from punishment nor anyone able to rescue or defend him.

translation: والسماء ذات المطر المتكرر.
interpretation: يقسم الله بالسماء التي يعود إليها المطر مرارًا، فينزل منها سببًا لحياة الأرض ونمائها.

translation: And the earth that splits open,
interpretation: This refers to the earth opening and bringing forth vegetation, water, and other provisions by God’s command, signifying His power to create, sustain, and revive.

translation: Indeed, it is a decisive word.
interpretation: This affirms that the Qur’an is a clear and final truth that distinguishes guidance from error, leaving no room for it to be treated as idle speech or falsehood.

translation: And it is not a jest.
interpretation: The Qur’an is serious and truthful revelation, not words spoken for amusement, mockery, or idle entertainment.

translation: Indeed, they are devising a scheme.
interpretation: This conveys that the rejecters are deliberately and secretly planning against the truth, using calculated means to obstruct it.

translation: وأدبّر تدبيرًا محكمًا.
interpretation: أي إن الله يمهل أهل الباطل ويترك لهم مجال الكيد، ثم يردّ كيدهم بتدبير نافذ لا يفلتون منه، إظهارًا لقدرته ونصرًا للحق.

translation: So grant the disbelievers a respite; grant them a brief respite.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet to remain patient with those who reject the truth, for their apparent freedom from immediate punishment is only temporary; Allah’s judgment will come at the appointed time.

translation: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: Declare your Lord’s perfection and transcendence, and honor Him above all imperfection and all that is ascribed to Him falsely, for He alone is supreme in power, rank, and majesty.

translation: Who created and proportioned.
interpretation: He brought every creature into existence and fashioned it with a balanced, harmonious form suited to its purpose.

translation: And He who determined all things and guided them.
interpretation: Allah assigned every created thing its proper nature, measure, and purpose, then guided it toward what fulfills that purpose.

translation: And He is the One who brings forth the pasture.
interpretation: God is the Creator who causes vegetation and grazing plants to emerge from the earth, demonstrating His power to bring life forth and provide sustenance for His creatures.

translation: Then He made it dark, withered stubble.
interpretation: Allah causes the vegetation He brings forth to pass from flourishing growth into dry, dark remnants, reminding us of the transience of worldly life and the perfection of His power over its cycles.

translation: We shall make you recite, so you will not forget.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that He will preserve the Qur’an firmly in his heart and make its recitation secure, so that he will not lose any of what has been revealed to him.

translation: Except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is made public and what is hidden.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that revelation will remain preserved in his heart, while affirming that any exception occurs only by Allah’s wisdom and will. Nothing—whether openly expressed or concealed within the heart—is outside His complete knowledge.

translation: And We will make the way of ease accessible to you.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that He will grant him divine support, making obedience, perseverance, and the fulfillment of his mission easier for him.

translation: So remind, if the reminder benefits.
interpretation: Continue offering sincere admonition, for reminding people of the truth can awaken those whose hearts are receptive and willing to benefit.

translation: He who fears will be reminded.
interpretation: A heart filled with reverent fear of God is receptive to divine admonition and inclined to take heed.

translation: But the most wretched will avoid it.
interpretation: The person most miserable in soul turns away from the reminder and refuses to benefit from its guidance.

translation: He who will enter the Great Fire.
interpretation: This describes the one who, because of persistent rejection and disobedience, is destined to suffer the most severe punishment in Hell.

translation: Then he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This describes a state of unending torment: death will not come to bring relief, while life will remain devoid of comfort or true well-being.

translation: Successful indeed is the one who purifies himself.
interpretation: True success belongs to the person who cleanses the soul from disbelief and sinful traits, nurtures it through faith and obedience, and thereby draws nearer to Allah.

translation: And he remembers the name of his Lord, then prays.
interpretation: The verse portrays sincere worship as beginning with remembrance of God and being expressed through prayer, whereby the believer turns to Him with humility and devotion.

translation: Rather, you prefer the life of this world.
interpretation: You give precedence to fleeting worldly pleasures and benefits over the enduring reward and nearness to God in the Hereafter.

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
interpretation: What Allah has prepared in the Hereafter is superior in value and lastingness to the fleeting pleasures and possessions of this worldly life; therefore, true priority should be given to what endures eternally rather than to what soon passes away.

translation: Indeed, this is found in the former scriptures.
interpretation: The truths and guidance just mentioned are not new; they were also revealed in the earlier divine scriptures given to the prophets before Muhammad ﷺ.

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
interpretation: This refers to the revealed writings given to Abraham and Moses, emphasizing that the guidance calling people to faith, purification, and the Hereafter was affirmed in the revelations of earlier prophets.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Has the account of the Overwhelming Event reached you?
interpretation: This is a solemn rhetorical question directing the listener’s attention to the Day of Resurrection, whose overwhelming terror will encompass all creation.

translation: Faces on that Day will be humbled.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the faces of those overwhelmed by fear and humiliation will reveal their helpless submission before God’s absolute authority.

translation: Laboring and exhausted.
interpretation: It refers to people whose efforts are marked by hardship and fatigue, yet bring them no beneficial reward because they are not grounded in the truth.

translation: They will burn in a blazing fire.
interpretation: It portrays the severe punishment awaiting those who are condemned to Hell, where they are exposed to an intensely scorching fire.

translation: They will be given drink from a boiling spring.
interpretation: This depicts the agonizing drink prepared for the condemned in Hell: instead of relieving their thirst, it is intensely hot and adds to their torment.

translation: They will have no food except thorny, dry herbage.
interpretation: This describes the utter deprivation of the people of Hell: the only sustenance available to them is a harsh, poisonous plant that neither nourishes nor satisfies, intensifying their misery and humiliation.

translation: It neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.
interpretation: This describes a worthless form of food that offers no physical benefit and cannot relieve the suffering of hunger, illustrating the deprivation and punishment of those who rejected the truth.

translation: Faces on that Day will be joyful and radiant.
interpretation: This describes the believers’ visible serenity and delight in the Hereafter, reflecting the honor, comfort, and lasting happiness Allah has granted them.

translation: Pleased with their striving.
interpretation: The believers will be content with the righteous deeds they performed, seeing them accepted and rewarded by Allah.

translation: In a lofty Garden,
interpretation: أي في جنّة رفيعة القدر والمكان، عالية المنزلة، أعدّها الله نعيمًا دائمًا لأهلها.

translation: You will hear therein no vain speech.
interpretation: The people of Paradise will experience perfect peace, with no falsehood, abuse, idle talk, or words that cause distress; every utterance there will be pure and wholesome.

translation: In it is a flowing spring.
interpretation: This portrays Paradise as a place of continual life, freshness, and comfort, where pure water flows without interruption as part of the everlasting blessings prepared for its inhabitants.

translation: In it are couches raised high.
interpretation: The verse portrays Paradise as a place of honor, comfort, and dignity, where its inhabitants are given elevated seats befitting their noble and secure state.

translation: And cups set in place,
interpretation: The cups are arranged and ready for the people of Paradise, signifying their honored reception and complete comfort.

translation: And cushions arranged in rows,
interpretation: This depicts the gardens of Paradise as a place of abundant comfort, beauty, and gracious hospitality, where everything is perfectly prepared for the honor and ease of its inhabitants.

translation: And carpets spread out.
interpretation: This depicts the abundant comfort and honored welcome prepared for the people of Paradise, with luxurious furnishings spread freely before them.

translation: أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خُلقت؟
interpretation: تحثّ الآية الإنسان على التأمل في خلق الإبل وما أودع الله فيها من خصائص عظيمة تلائم حياتها ووظيفتها، ليقوده ذلك إلى إدراك حكمة الخالق وقدرته وتوحيده.

translation: And at the sky—how it has been raised.
interpretation: It invites people to contemplate the sky’s immense elevation and ordered structure as evidence of Allah’s power, wisdom, and creative mastery.

translation: And at the mountains—how they have been firmly set up,
interpretation: The verse directs people to contemplate the mountains’ immense form and steadfastness as signs of the Creator’s wisdom, power, and precise ordering of the world.

translation: And at the earth—how it has been spread out.
interpretation: The verse directs reflection to the earth’s broad, accessible expanse, made suitable for human life, movement, cultivation, and settlement, as a sign of its Creator’s wisdom and power.

translation: So remind them; you are only a reminder.
interpretation: Your responsibility is to convey the truth and remind people sincerely, not to compel them to believe or control their response; guidance ultimately belongs to God.

translation: لستَ عليهم بمُسيطرٍ.
interpretation: لستَ مكلَّفًا بإجبارهم على الإيمان أو التحكم في قلوبهم؛ فدورك البلاغ والتذكير، أما هدايتهم ومحاسبتهم فعلى الله.

translation: Except for whoever turns away and disbelieves.
interpretation: This refers to those who reject the truth after it has been made clear to them and deliberately turn away from faith and obedience to God.

translation: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: This refers to the ultimate punishment in the Hereafter, far more severe than any suffering experienced in this world, for one who turns away from the truth and persists in rejection.

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: All people will ultimately return to Allah, where they will be held accountable for their deeds and receive the judgment they deserve.

translation: Then surely their reckoning is upon Us.
interpretation: Their final accountability is solely with Allah: He will bring them to account for their beliefs and deeds and judge them with perfect justice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the dawn.
interpretation: Allah swears by the dawn as it breaks through the darkness, directing attention to the certainty of renewal, the transition from hardship to relief, and the signs of His power in the ordered turning of time.

translation: And by the ten nights,
interpretation: This refers to the first ten nights of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, whose special sacredness highlights the immense value of worship and righteous deeds during them.

translation: And by the even and the odd,
interpretation: Allah swears by the paired and the singular aspects of creation, directing attention to the harmony of created things and to His unique oneness beyond all pairing.

translation: And by the night as it departs,
interpretation: God draws attention to the night as it quietly passes away, indicating that darkness and hardship are temporary and that all things move onward according to His decree.

translation: Is there in that an oath for one possessed of understanding?
interpretation: إن ما أقسم الله به من الآيات الكونية والأزمنة العظيمة كافٍ لمن أوتي عقلاً راشداً ليتفكر في دلالاتها على قدرة الله وحكمته، فيعتبر ولا يغفل عن طاعته.

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Ād?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical call to reflect on how God dealt with the people of ‘Ād, whose power and prosperity did not save them from destruction when they persisted in arrogance and rebellion; it warns that worldly strength cannot protect a people from divine judgment.

translation: Iram, of the lofty pillars,
interpretation: This refers to Iram, associated with the people of ʿĀd, whose imposing structures and towering pillars expressed their immense power and worldly grandeur.

translation: The like of which had never been created in the land.
interpretation: This refers to the extraordinary strength, grandeur, and civilization of ʿĀd, whose city and achievements were unparalleled among the peoples of their time.

translation: And Thamūd, who carved the rocks in the valley,
interpretation: This refers to the people of Thamūd, who displayed remarkable strength and skill by cutting dwellings into the mountains, yet their material achievements did not protect them from destruction when they rejected God’s guidance and acted arrogantly.

translation: And Pharaoh, the possessor of the stakes.
interpretation: This describes Pharaoh as a ruler of immense power and authority, whose tyranny was firmly established and whose punishments and armies held people in subjugation.

translation: Those who transgressed throughout the lands,
interpretation: This refers to people who exceeded all bounds of justice and obedience, spreading tyranny and corruption wherever they held power.

translation: So they spread abundant corruption therein.
interpretation: They used their power and influence to multiply wrongdoing, oppression, and harm throughout the land, rather than upholding justice and reform.

translation: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
interpretation: The verse portrays God’s punishment as relentless and overwhelming, falling upon those who persisted in tyranny and corruption until their power was completely broken.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
interpretation: God is constantly aware of all that people do, allowing no injustice or wrongdoing to escape His knowledge and judgment.

translation: As for the human being, whenever his Lord tests him by honoring him and blessing him, he says, “My Lord has honored me.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the human tendency to mistake worldly prosperity for proof of divine favor and personal worth, whereas wealth, comfort, and status are themselves tests rather than definitive signs of honor before God.

translation: But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, “My Lord has humiliated me.”
interpretation: The verse exposes the mistaken belief that material abundance is proof of God’s favor and financial hardship is proof of humiliation. Both prosperity and restriction are tests; a person’s true honor lies not in the amount of provision he receives, but in how he responds to God with faith, patience, gratitude, and obedience.

translation: No indeed! Rather, you do not honor the orphan.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of those who mistake worldly abundance or hardship for divine honor or disgrace; true moral failure lies in neglecting the orphan’s dignity, care, and rightful protection.

translation: And you do not urge one another to feed the needy.
interpretation: This condemns a society that neglects the poor not only by failing to help them, but also by abandoning the moral duty to encourage one another to care for their needs.

translation: And you devour the inheritance, consuming it greedily and indiscriminately.
interpretation: This condemns the covetous seizure of inheritance, especially when the strong take the rightful shares of the weak without restraint or regard for justice.

translation: And you love wealth with an immense love.
interpretation: You are deeply attached to worldly wealth, allowing your desire for it to become excessive and to distract you from justice, generosity, and obedience to God.

translation: No indeed! When the earth is crushed, repeatedly crushed,
interpretation: This portrays the earth being utterly pulverized on the Day of Resurrection, marking the collapse of the worldly order and the onset of the final reckoning before God.

translation: And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: This portrays the Day of Judgment, when Allah’s decisive judgment is manifested and the angels stand in ordered ranks before Him, conveying the majesty and overwhelming authority of that moment.

translation: And on that Day Hell will be brought forth. On that Day man will remember, but what good will remembrance be for him?
interpretation: When the reality of the Hereafter becomes unmistakable and Hell is brought before him, the heedless person will recall the truth and recognize his failures; however, that realization will come too late, since earthly life—the time for repentance and righteous action—will have ended.

translation: He will say, “Oh, I wish I had sent ahead something for my life.”
interpretation: The verse portrays the profound regret of one who, on the Day of Judgment, realizes that the lasting life is the Hereafter and that he failed to prepare for it through faith and righteous deeds during his worldly life.

translation: On that Day, no one will punish as He punishes.
interpretation: This portrays the unmatched severity of God’s punishment on the Day of Judgment, a punishment whose intensity and justice are beyond anything known in this world.

translation: And none can bind as He binds.
interpretation: It describes the unmatched severity of Allah’s punishment on the Day of Judgment: no created being can impose restraint or torment comparable to His, and no one can escape the consequence of rejecting Him.

translation: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنّة
interpretation: خطاب تكريم للنفس التي سكنت إلى الإيمان واطمأنّت بذكر الله، فلم تزعزعها الشدائد ولا الشكوك.

translation: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing to Him.
interpretation: هذا نداءٌ للنفس المطمئنّة المؤمنة عند انتقالها إلى ربّها؛ ترجع راضيةً بما أعدّ الله لها من النعيم، وقد رضي الله عنها لقبول إيمانها وصالح عملها.

translation: So enter among My servants.
interpretation: This is a divine invitation to the tranquil soul to join the company of God’s honored, righteous servants, sharing in their nearness and acceptance.

translation: And enter My Paradise.
interpretation: Allah grants the tranquil soul the ultimate honor and reward: admission into Paradise by His mercy and acceptance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. I swear by this city.
interpretation: Allah solemnly draws attention to the sanctity and immense honor of Makkah, the sacred city, whose holiness gives weight to the message that follows.

translation: And you are lawful in this city.
interpretation: Allah emphasizes the Prophet’s honored presence in Mecca, indicating that although the city is sacred, its people have made persecution of him permissible in their conduct; this also points to the time when he would be granted authority there.

translation: And by the parent and what he begot,
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the bond of parenthood and offspring, reminding humanity that every person comes through a lineage and is therefore dependent, created, and accountable before Him.

translation: We have certainly created الإنسان in hardship.
interpretation: Human life is inherently marked by effort, struggle, and responsibility; this is the condition through which people are tested, so they must meet its difficulties with patience, perseverance, and reliance on God.

translation: Does he think that no one has power over him?
interpretation: The verse rebukes the human being who becomes arrogant and heedless, imagining that he is beyond God’s knowledge, authority, and accountability. No matter how strong or secure he feels, he remains entirely subject to God’s power.

translation: He says, “I have squandered vast wealth.”
interpretation: This portrays a person boasting about having spent enormous riches, revealing pride and self-display rather than sincere generosity or gratitude for Allah’s blessings.

translation: Does he think that no one has seen him?
interpretation: He must not imagine that his deeds, wealth, or intentions are hidden, for Allah fully observes him and will hold him accountable.

translation: Have We not given him two eyes?
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the gift of sight as a clear sign of His care and power, reminding the human being that such blessings carry a responsibility to perceive truth and use them rightly.

translation: And a tongue and two lips,
interpretation: God reminds the human being of the precise gifts through which speech, expression, and communication are made possible, inviting gratitude and responsible use of these faculties.

translation: And We guided him to the two paths.
interpretation: Allah has made clear to every person the paths of good and evil, enabling them to recognize the way of righteousness and the way of wrongdoing, and leaving them responsible for the choice they make.

translation: Yet he has not attempted the steep path.
interpretation: He has not chosen the difficult but righteous course of overcoming selfishness and striving for deeds that require genuine sacrifice and moral courage.

translation: And what will make you realize what the steep path is?
interpretation: This question magnifies the difficulty and greatness of the path of righteousness, preparing the listener to understand that it requires serious effort and self-sacrifice.

translation: The freeing of a slave,
interpretation: True righteousness includes liberating a human being from bondage, expressing sincere compassion and a willingness to sacrifice for another’s freedom.

translation: Or providing food on a day of severe hunger,
interpretation: True righteousness calls for relieving people’s suffering by feeding those afflicted by extreme hunger, especially when hardship makes food scarce and difficult to obtain.

translation: An orphan who is a close relative,
interpretation: True righteousness includes caring for an orphan who is also a relative, giving special attention to their vulnerability and the bonds of kinship.

translation: or a poor person lying in the dust,
interpretation: It refers to someone in extreme poverty and utter destitution, with no adequate shelter, support, or means of sustenance; helping such a person is among the highest forms of compassionate righteousness.

translation: Then he became one of those who believed, and urged one another to patience and urged one another to mercy.
interpretation: True salvation is attained not merely through individual effort, but by joining the community of faith and actively encouraging one another to remain steadfast in obedience and hardship, while showing compassion and kindness toward others.

translation: Those are the companions of the right.
interpretation: They are the people who, through faith, compassion, and righteous deeds, attain the honored position and ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who disbelieve in Our signs are the companions of the left.
interpretation: Those who knowingly reject Allah’s revelations and refuse faith are destined for the people of misfortune and punishment, rather than the people of felicity.

translation: عليهم نارٌ مُؤصدةٌ.
interpretation: أي تحيط بهم نارٌ مُغلَقةٌ عليهم إغلاقًا محكمًا، فلا يجدون منها مخرجًا ولا سبيلًا إلى النجاة.

translation: By the sun and its radiant light,
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the sun’s manifest brilliance as a sign of His perfect power and order, preparing the heart to recognize that the human soul likewise requires illumination and purification.

translation: And the moon when it follows it.
interpretation: God swears by the moon as it follows the sun, appearing after it and reflecting its light, directing attention to the precise order and harmony established in creation.

translation: And by the day when it reveals the sun,
interpretation: God swears by the daylight that unveils the sun, drawing attention to the ordered alternation of light and darkness as a sign of His power and wisdom.

translation: And by the night when it covers it—the sun.
interpretation: This oath draws attention to the night as it envelops the sun and conceals its light, revealing the precise alternation established by God and reminding people of His power over creation.

translation: By the sky and He who built it,
interpretation: God draws attention to the sky’s vastness and ordered construction as a sign of His power, wisdom, and creative mastery.

translation: And by the earth and Him who spread it out,
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the earth’s vastness and ordered formation as a sign of His creative power and wisdom.

translation: By the soul and Him who fashioned it perfectly,
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the human soul, created with balance and an innate capacity to recognize right and wrong, reminding us that its moral condition depends on how it is cultivated and directed.

translation: And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.
interpretation: Allah created the human soul with an innate awareness of both corruption and piety, enabling it to recognize the path of sin and the path of obedience and to choose between them.

translation: Indeed, successful is the one who purifies it.
interpretation: True success belongs to the person who purifies the soul from corruption and disobedience, nurturing it through faith, sincere devotion, and righteous action.

translation: And indeed, he has failed who corrupts it.
interpretation: The one who sullies and suppresses the soul’s innate purity through sin and disobedience has deprived himself of true success.

translation: Thamūd denied the truth because of their transgression.
interpretation: The people of Thamūd rejected God’s message not from lack of evidence, but because their rebellious arrogance led them to exceed the limits and refuse obedience.

translation: When the most wretched of them rose up,
interpretation: This refers to the evilest among Thamūd, who boldly arose to carry out the crime of killing the she-camel, embodying the people’s defiance and rejection of their prophet’s warning.

translation: So the Messenger of Allah said to them: “This is Allah’s she-camel, and her allotted drink.”
interpretation: The Prophet Ṣāliḥ warns Thamūd that the she-camel is a divinely appointed sign and that they must not harm her or deprive her of the water Allah has assigned to her; violating this command would be defiance of God.

translation: But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord overwhelmed them with destruction for their sin and leveled them all.
interpretation: Their rejection of the truth culminated in the deliberate killing of the she-camel, so divine punishment encompassed the entire community without distinction, leaving them utterly humbled and destroyed because of their collective wrongdoing.

translation: And He does not fear its consequences.
interpretation: Allah is not concerned about the outcome of His punishment of the people who denied the truth and transgressed, for no one can hold Him accountable or prevent His just decree.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the night as it envelops,
interpretation: Allah draws attention to the night as it spreads over the world and conceals it in darkness, directing reflection toward His power in the alternation of night and day and toward the different conditions through which human beings pass.

translation: And by the day when it shines forth.
interpretation: This divine oath draws attention to the day as a clear manifestation of light, visibility, and renewed activity, inviting reflection on the signs of God revealed through the alternation of darkness and illumination.

translation: And by Him who created the male and the female,
interpretation: Allah swears by His act of creating the male and female, directing attention to His perfect power and wisdom in bringing about the complementary forms of human life.

translation: Indeed, your endeavors are diverse.
interpretation: People’s pursuits and aims differ: some strive for faith, righteousness, and the lasting reward of God, while others pursue fleeting worldly desires; each person’s chosen direction determines the outcome they will meet.

translation: As for the one who gives and is mindful of God,
interpretation: This describes a person who generously gives from what God has bestowed upon them and guards themselves through reverence and obedience to Him.

translation: And believes in the best [promise].
interpretation: He sincerely trusts in Allah’s promise of reward and success, allowing that certainty to guide his faith and righteous conduct.

translation: So We will ease him toward ease.
interpretation: Allah promises to make the path of goodness, obedience, and ultimate success accessible for the person who sincerely turns to Him and chooses righteousness, granting him increasing ease in doing what pleases Him.

translation: As for whoever is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient,
interpretation: This describes a person who withholds what is due—especially charity and obedience—because he believes he has no need of God or His guidance, allowing self-reliance and attachment to worldly wealth to govern his choices.

translation: And denies the finest reward.
interpretation: This describes one who rejects faith in God’s promised reward and refuses to accept the truth that leads to it.

translation: So We will ease him toward hardship.
interpretation: Whoever turns away from faith and withholds goodness will be left to follow the path of wrongdoing, until hardship and ruin become easy and familiar for him.

translation: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?
interpretation: When a person is overtaken by destruction and faces the consequences of his deeds, the wealth he relied upon cannot protect or benefit him.

translation: Indeed, upon Us rests the guidance.
interpretation: Allah affirms that He has taken responsibility for making the path of truth clear and accessible, while people remain accountable for choosing whether to follow it.

translation: Indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life.
interpretation: Allah alone possesses complete authority over both this worldly life and the Hereafter, so all affairs ultimately return to Him.

translation: So I have warned you of a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This is a grave warning that those who turn away from divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing face the punishment of Hell, whose fire burns intensely.

translation: None will enter it except the most wretched.
interpretation: This warns that the ultimate punishment is for those who persist in rejecting the truth and opposing God with deliberate defiance.

translation: The one who denied and turned away.
interpretation: It refers to the person who rejects the truth after it becomes clear and deliberately turns away from faith and obedience to God.

translation: And the most God-fearing will be kept far from it.
interpretation: The person most devoted to God and most careful to obey Him will be protected from the punishment and ruin referred to in the preceding verses.

translation: He who gives his wealth in charity, seeking purification.
interpretation: This describes the sincere believer who spends from his wealth to cleanse his soul from greed and attachment to worldly possessions, seeking only nearness to God rather than praise or worldly return.

translation: And no one has any favor upon him that he must repay.
interpretation: He gives generously solely for God’s sake, not because he owes anyone repayment or seeks to settle a debt of gratitude; his goodness is free from personal obligation and worldly expectation.

translation: Except for seeking the pleasure of his Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: The righteous person gives without seeking worldly recognition or reward; his sole intention is to attain Allah’s approval and draw near to Him.

translation: And he will surely be satisfied.
interpretation: Whoever gives sincerely for Allah’s sake will ultimately receive such a generous reward and divine favor that he will be completely content.

translation: By the morning brightness,
interpretation: Allah swears by the radiant morning light, evoking the return of clarity, warmth, and hope after the darkness of night.

translation: And by the night when it grows still.
interpretation: God draws attention to the tranquil darkness of night, whose stillness conveys a pause, concealment, and calm within the order of creation.

translation: لم يهجرك ربك ولم يبغضك.
interpretation: تطمين للنبي ﷺ بأن انقطاع الوحي أو تأخر الفرج لا يعني تخلّي الله عنه ولا سخطه عليه، بل إن عنايته به ورحمته مستمرتان.

translation: And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life.
interpretation: Allah reassures the Prophet ﷺ that the lasting reward, honor, and nearness to Him in the Hereafter surpass all that can be attained in this worldly life.

translation: And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be pleased.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that He will continue to grant him abundant favor, support, and honor until his heart is fully content and at peace.

translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ of His care and protection from the earliest stage of his life, assuring him that his orphanhood did not leave him abandoned, for Allah provided him with refuge and loving guardianship.

translation: And He found you unaware, so He guided you.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that before revelation He had not yet known the details of divine guidance and the revealed law, so Allah guided him through revelation and made him a guide for humanity; this does not mean that he was upon false belief or sin.

translation: And He found you in need, so He enriched you.
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that He cared for him when he lacked material means and granted him sufficiency through His provision, support, and contentment.

translation: So as for the orphan, do not oppress him.
interpretation: The verse commands that orphans be treated with mercy, dignity, and justice, forbidding any abuse, humiliation, or violation of their rights.

translation: And as for the one who asks, do not rebuke him.
interpretation: Treat anyone who seeks help or asks a question with kindness and dignity; do not humiliate, harshly dismiss, or scold them.

translation: And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it.
interpretation: Recognize and speak gratefully of the blessings Allah has bestowed upon you, using them in obedience to Him rather than boasting about them.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Have We not expanded your heart for you?
interpretation: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ of the spiritual openness, strength, and inner peace He granted him, enabling him to bear revelation, fulfill his mission, and face its burdens with steadfastness.

translation: And We lifted from you your burden.
interpretation: Allah reassured the Prophet ﷺ that He had removed the heavy weight that had burdened him, granting him relief, support, and the ability to fulfill his mission with a cleansed and strengthened heart.

translation: that which weighed heavily upon your back
interpretation: It refers to the heavy burden and distress that had pressed upon the Prophet, making his mission difficult; Allah reminds him that He relieved and supported him through it.

translation: And We have exalted your remembrance for you.
interpretation: Allah has honored the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by making his name and message widely remembered and joined with the remembrance of Allah in faith, worship, and praise.

translation: Indeed, with hardship comes ease.
interpretation: This is a divine assurance that hardship is not lasting or without relief; the believer is called to endure with patience and trust that ease accompanies every trial.

translation: Indeed, with hardship comes ease.
interpretation: This verse assures that hardship is accompanied by relief and that difficulty is never absolute or without openings for ease. It encourages steadfastness and hope, trusting that God brings alleviation alongside every trial.

translation: So when you have completed your task, devote yourself diligently to worship and effort.
interpretation: Once you have finished one responsibility, do not lapse into idleness; turn with renewed resolve toward devotion to God and the next beneficial duty, seeking Him alone in all that you undertake.

translation: And turn your longing toward your Lord.
interpretation: Direct all your hopes, desires, and earnest devotion exclusively to Allah, relying on Him and seeking only His nearness and help.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the fig and the olive.
interpretation: Allah swears by the fig and the olive, pointing to the signs of His wisdom and blessings found in these nourishing plants, and drawing attention to the sacred lands and profound lessons associated with them.

translation: And by Mount Sinai,
interpretation: God swears by the blessed mountain where Moses received revelation, evoking the sanctity of divine guidance and the covenant between God and His messengers.

translation: And this secure city,
interpretation: This refers to Makkah, the sacred city whose security and sanctity Allah has established, making it a place of protection and reverence.

translation: We have certainly created humankind in the finest form.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah fashioned the human being with exceptional balance, dignity, and capacities—both physical and intellectual—so that people may recognize their honor and fulfill the moral responsibility for which they were created.

translation: ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين
interpretation: ثم نُعيد الإنسان إلى أدنى حالاته وأحطّها، حين يبتعد عن الإيمان والاستقامة بعد أن وهبه الله كمال الخِلقة والعقل.

translation: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات، فلهم أجر غير ممنون.
interpretation: لكن الذين صدّقوا بالله وأخلصوا له بالطاعة والعمل الصالح فلهم ثواب دائم لا ينقطع ولا يُنقص، ولا يصاحبه منٌّ أو أذى.

translation: So what, after this, can make you deny the Judgment?
interpretation: After witnessing the signs of human creation, the human being has no sound basis for denying resurrection and accountability before God.

translation: Is Allah not the most wise of all judges?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical affirmation that Allah possesses perfect wisdom and justice in every judgment, so His decisions are the ultimate truth and cannot be surpassed by any other judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. Recite in the name of your Lord who created.
interpretation: This command establishes that true reading and pursuit of knowledge begin with God, are undertaken with reliance upon Him, and should lead the human being to recognize the Creator behind all existence.

translation: He created the human being from a clinging clot.
interpretation: This verse draws attention to the humble origin of human life, teaching that human beings should recognize their complete dependence on Allah and respond with humility rather than pride.

translation: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.
interpretation: God commands the Prophet to seek knowledge and revelation, assuring him that his Lord’s generosity will support, teach, and bestow upon him far beyond what he could attain by his own means.

translation: He who taught by the pen.
interpretation: Allah is the One who enabled humanity to preserve, transmit, and develop knowledge through writing, making the pen a means by which learning extends beyond one person and one generation.

translation: He taught الإنسان what he did not know.
interpretation: This expresses that all human knowledge is bestowed by Allah: He enables people to learn, understand, and discover what was previously beyond their awareness.

translation: No indeed! Surely the human being transgresses.
interpretation: This is a rebuke of the human tendency to overstep God’s limits when arrogance and self-reliance lead a person to forget their dependence on Him.

translation: Because he sees himself self-sufficient.
interpretation: When a person imagines that he has no need for God, wealth, or anyone else, this false sense of independence can lead him to overstep limits and act arrogantly.

translation: Indeed, to your Lord is the return.
interpretation: Every person will ultimately return to Allah for judgment, so worldly power and self-sufficiency cannot exempt anyone from accountability before Him.

translation: Have you seen the one who forbids,
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question expressing astonishment at the person who arrogantly obstructs another from worshipping Allah.

translation: a servant when he prays
interpretation: This refers to a worshipper turning sincerely to Allah in prayer, whose devotion must not be obstructed or treated with contempt.

translation: Have you considered if he is upon guidance?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question calling one to recognize the gravity of opposing or obstructing a person who follows clear guidance from God.

translation: أو يأمر بالتقوى
interpretation: أي: أو كان هذا العبد يدعو إلى خشية الله وطاعته، ويحثّ على الالتزام بما يرضيه.

translation: Have you considered if he denies and turns away?
interpretation: This is a rebuke that draws attention to the grave condition of one who knowingly rejects the truth and refuses to submit to it, exposing the moral danger of denial and deliberate avoidance.

translation: Does he not know that Allah sees?
interpretation: This is a warning to the one who acts arrogantly or persists in wrongdoing: nothing he does is hidden from Allah, whose constant awareness should awaken him to accountability and restrain him from defiance.

translation: No indeed! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock.
interpretation: This is a stern divine warning to the one who persists in arrogance and obstructs obedience: if he refuses to stop, he will be humbled and subjected to God’s punishment, with the forelock representing the person’s complete disgrace and helplessness.

translation: A lying, sinful forelock.
interpretation: This describes the forelock as a metonym for its owner, portraying him as utterly characterized by falsehood and wrongdoing; the mention of the forelock also conveys his humiliation and helplessness before God.

translation: So let him call his assembly.
interpretation: This is a challenge to the arrogant denier: let him summon his supporters and allies for help, yet their combined power cannot protect him from God’s judgment.

translation: We shall call the keepers of Hell.
interpretation: This is a warning that if the denier persists in arrogance and opposition to truth, God will summon the stern angels appointed to punish the wicked.

translation: No! Do not obey him; prostrate yourself and draw near to Allah. ۩
interpretation: This is a decisive command to disregard those who hinder worship and to seek closeness to Allah through sincere prostration and submission.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree.
interpretation: Allah reveals the exalted status of the Qur’an and the sacredness of the Night of Decree, the night in which its revelation began by divine command. Its mention teaches that this night is marked by immense blessing and divine determination, calling believers to honor it through worship and devotion.

translation: And what will make you realize what the Night of Decree is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the extraordinary greatness and profound significance of the Night of Decree, whose true rank surpasses ordinary human understanding.

translation: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.
interpretation: This night possesses immense blessing and honor: worship and righteous deeds performed in it are more virtuous and rewarding than those performed throughout a thousand months without it.

translation: The angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter.
interpretation: This refers to the Night of Decree, when the angels and Gabriel descend by Allah’s command to carry out and oversee the affairs He has decreed for the coming year, making the night one of immense blessing and divine activity.

translation: Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.
interpretation: The Night of Decree is enveloped in divine peace and blessings throughout the night, remaining so until dawn appears.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist until the clear proof came to them.
interpretation: They remained firmly attached to their disbelief and misguided ways, unwilling to abandon them, until Allah sent them a decisive, unmistakable proof: His Messenger bringing the revealed scripture. Through this clear evidence, they could no longer claim that the truth had not been made manifest to them.

translation: A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures.
interpretation: This refers to the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, who conveys revelation preserved from falsehood and corruption, calling people through it to faith and righteousness.

translation: In them are upright scriptures.
interpretation: These scriptures contain truthful, sound teachings that guide people toward faith, righteousness, and obedience to God.

translation: Those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after the clear evidence had come to them.
interpretation: Their disagreement was not caused by a lack of guidance; rather, they divided after the truth had been made clear to them, revealing that stubbornness, rivalry, or personal interests had led them away from sincere adherence to it.

translation: وما أُمِروا إلا أن يعبدوا الله مخلصين له العبادة، مائلين عن الشرك إلى التوحيد، ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة؛ وذلك هو الدين المستقيم.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن جوهر الدين الذي أُمر به الناس هو توحيد الله وإخلاص العبادة له وحده، مع الثبات على الحق وترك الشرك، ويظهر صدق هذا الإخلاص بالمحافظة على الصلاة وأداء الزكاة؛ فهذه هي أصول العبادة والاستقامة التي يقوم عليها الدين القويم.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They are the worst of creation.
interpretation: This verse warns that rejecting faith and persisting in disbelief—whether among those who possess revealed scripture or those who associate partners with God—leads to eternal punishment. Their being described as the worst of creation refers to their deliberate rejection of truth and their refusal to fulfill the purpose for which they were created.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—they are the best of all creation.
interpretation: تبيّن الآية أن الإيمان الحقيقي لا يكتمل بمجرد الاعتقاد، بل يظهر أثره في العمل الصالح؛ فمن جمع بين صدق الإيمان وصلاح العمل استحق منزلة رفيعة، وكان من خير خلق الله.

translation: Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of everlasting residence beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.
interpretation: This verse portrays the ultimate fulfillment granted to those whose reverent awareness of Allah shapes their lives: eternal nearness to Him, complete contentment, and a mutual pleasure in which the servant is accepted by Allah and finds perfect satisfaction in Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the earth is shaken with its final shaking,
interpretation: This portrays the decisive upheaval at the end of the world, when the earth will undergo the immense convulsion decreed by Allah, signaling the onset of the Resurrection and the end of the present order.

translation: And the earth brings forth its burdens.
interpretation: This portrays the earth releasing what lies hidden within it, signifying the disclosure of all buried remains and deeds on the Day of Resurrection, when nothing concealed will remain unseen.

translation: And the human being will say, “What is happening to it?”
interpretation: This portrays humanity’s shock and bewilderment on the Day of Judgment when the earth undergoes its immense transformation, leaving people astonished and asking why it is convulsing and revealing what it conceals.

translation: That Day, it will relate its news.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the earth will testify about the deeds that were carried out upon it, revealing nothing of what people did.

translation: Because your Lord inspired it.
interpretation: The earth will disclose its hidden contents on the Day of Resurrection because Allah will command it to do so and enable it to testify to all that occurred upon it.

translation: On that Day, people will come forth in separate groups so that they may be shown their deeds.
interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, humanity will be gathered and divided according to its circumstances and deeds, and each person will directly encounter the consequences of what they did, with nothing hidden or overlooked.

translation: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.
interpretation: No act of goodness, however small or seemingly unnoticed, is lost before God; its consequence and reward will be made evident to the one who performed it.

translation: And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.
interpretation: No wrong, however tiny or seemingly insignificant, is overlooked by Allah; every deed will be brought before its doer and its consequences made evident.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the galloping horses, breathing heavily,
interpretation: Allah swears by the charging horses whose forceful galloping and heavy breathing convey the intensity, speed, and sacrifice of those striving in His cause, directing attention to the urgency and power with which devotion and obedience should be pursued.

translation: By those that strike sparks with their hooves,
interpretation: This evokes charging horses whose hooves strike stones and flash with sparks, portraying the fierce speed, power, and urgency of their advance.

translation: Then those who launch raids at dawn,
interpretation: This refers to the swift warhorses that charge upon the enemy at daybreak, emphasizing the suddenness, speed, and force of their advance.

translation: Then they raise a cloud of dust with it.
interpretation: The verse portrays the charging horses stirring up dust as they advance swiftly, evoking the intensity, force, and tumult of their movement.

translation: Then they penetrate with it into the midst of the assembly,
interpretation: The verse portrays the charging steeds pressing into the heart of the gathered enemy, expressing decisive courage, force, and determined advance.

translation: Indeed, الإنسان is ungrateful to his Lord.
interpretation: The verse points to the human tendency to overlook Allah’s blessings, deny His favors, and respond with ingratitude rather than obedience and thankfulness.

translation: And indeed, he is certainly a witness to that.
interpretation: The human being himself bears witness to his own ingratitude toward his Lord, revealed through his conduct and denial of the blessings he has received.

translation: And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth.
interpretation: The verse portrays the human being as deeply attached to wealth, an attachment that can become excessive and cause him to neglect gratitude, moral responsibility, and the Hereafter.

translation: Does he not know when what is in the graves is brought forth?
interpretation: This is a warning that every person will one day be resurrected from the grave, when all that was hidden in earthly life becomes subject to God’s judgment.

translation: And what is within the hearts will be brought to light.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the hidden intentions, beliefs, and secrets concealed within people will be exposed, leaving nothing inward undisclosed before God.

translation: Indeed, their Lord, on that Day, is fully aware of them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, nothing about their deeds, intentions, or inner realities will be hidden from Allah; His complete knowledge will govern their accountability and recompense.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The Striking Calamity.
interpretation: “The Striking Calamity” is a powerful name for the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the sudden, overwhelming terror with which it will shake creation and awaken humanity to the ultimate reality of accountability before Allah.

translation: What is the Striking Calamity?
interpretation: إنها استفهام للتعظيم والتهويل، يلفت الانتباه إلى هول يوم القيامة وشدة وقعِه على الخلق.

translation: And what will make you realize what the Striking Calamity is?
interpretation: هذا استفهام للتفخيم والتهويل، يبيّن عِظَم شأن القارعة وهولها، وأن حقيقتها أعظم من أن يحيط بها إدراك الإنسان بسهولة.

translation: يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المتناثر.
interpretation: تصوّر الآية اضطراب الناس وهول الموقف يوم القيامة، إذ يتفرقون ويتحركون في كل اتجاه بلا نظام، كما يتطاير الفراش المتناثر عند اشتداد الفزع.

translation: And the mountains will be like fluffed-up wool.
