interpretation: On the Day of Resurrection, the mountains—despite their seeming solidity and permanence—will be torn apart and scattered, becoming light and unstable like loose, carded wool, demonstrating the overwhelming power of that Day.

translation: As for the one whose scales are heavy,
interpretation: This refers to the person whose righteous deeds, made sincere and accepted by God, outweigh his misdeeds on the Day of Judgment; such weight signifies his success and salvation.

translation: So he will be in a life of contentment.
interpretation: He will enjoy an eternally blessed life in Paradise, free from distress and filled with complete satisfaction.

translation: But as for the one whose scales are light,
interpretation: It refers to the person whose record of righteous deeds is too slight to give weight to their scale on the Day of Judgment.

translation: His abode will be the Abyss.
interpretation: The one whose deeds are too light on the Day of Judgment will find no shelter or destination except the crushing depths of Hell, described as the Abyss.

translation: And what will make you know what it is?
interpretation: This expression emphasizes that the reality of the blazing abyss—into which the one whose deeds are light will fall—is so terrifying and beyond ordinary human understanding that its true nature can only be known through the divine revelation that describes it.

translation: A scorching fire.
interpretation: It depicts a fiercely burning punishment whose intense heat conveys the severity of the torment awaiting those condemned.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. The pursuit of having more has distracted you.
interpretation: Your preoccupation with accumulating wealth, status, possessions, and worldly advantages has diverted you from remembering Allah and fulfilling the purpose of your life.

translation: حتى زرتم المقابر
interpretation: ظل انشغالكم بالتفاخر والتكاثر بالدنيا مستمرًا حتى أدرككم الموت، فصرتم في القبور وانقطع عنكم التمتع بها.

translation: No indeed! You will come to know.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that heedlessness and rivalry will eventually be exposed, and the truth of what was denied will become unmistakably clear.

translation: Then, no! You will soon know.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that worldly distraction and rivalry will not remain without consequence; the truth of what truly matters will become unmistakably clear when people encounter the reality of the Hereafter.

translation: No indeed! If only you knew with certain knowledge.
interpretation: This is a forceful warning that true certainty about the resurrection, judgment, and the consequences of worldly rivalry would prevent people from being deceived by abundance and competition for worldly status.

translation: You will surely see the Hellfire.
interpretation: This is a stern warning that those consumed by worldly rivalry will inevitably confront the reality of Hell, making its threat certain and undeniable.

translation: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.
interpretation: After being informed of the reality of Hell, you will witness it directly and unmistakably, with a certainty based on seeing rather than merely hearing or knowing about it.

translation: Then, on that Day, you will surely be questioned about the blessings you enjoyed.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for how they received, appreciated, and used Allah’s blessings, including their health, wealth, security, and time.

translation: By time,
interpretation: Allah swears by the passage of time, drawing attention to its immense value and to the fact that every moment of human life is steadily being lost.

translation: Indeed, humankind is surely in a state of loss.
interpretation: Human beings are inherently exposed to loss because time continually passes, reducing their opportunity and life unless they preserve themselves through faith, righteous deeds, mutual encouragement to truth, and mutual encouragement to patience.

translation: Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to truth, and urge one another to patience.
interpretation: Human beings are spared from loss when faith becomes a source of righteous conduct, and when they mutually uphold truth and remain steadfast through hardship in obeying God.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Woe to every slanderer and backbiter.
interpretation: This verse sternly condemns the person who habitually disparages others, mocks their faults, or speaks against them behind their backs, warning that such deliberate harm to people’s dignity exposes its perpetrator to Allah’s punishment.

translation: The one who amasses wealth and keeps counting it.
interpretation: This describes a person consumed by hoarding and repeatedly calculating his wealth, treating its accumulation as a source of security and worth while neglecting the temporary nature of worldly possessions.

translation: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal.
interpretation: The verse censures the delusion that accumulated wealth can preserve a person from death or grant lasting life. It exposes the false security of relying on possessions, reminding that wealth is temporary and cannot prevent one’s return to God or the consequences of one’s deeds.

translation: No indeed! He will surely be cast into the Crusher.
interpretation: This is a decisive warning that the one deserving this punishment will be thrown into al-Ḥuṭamah, a blazing torment that crushes and destroys whatever is cast into it.

translation: And what will make you comprehend what the Crusher is?
interpretation: This expresses the terrifying magnitude of the Crusher, a name for Hell that crushes and overwhelms those who deserve its punishment, beyond anything human beings can fully imagine.

translation: The Fire of Allah, kindled.
interpretation: It signifies a fiercely blazing punishment whose intensity and terrifying nature are under Allah’s command, unlike any ordinary earthly fire.

translation: which rises over the hearts.
interpretation: It describes a fire whose torment penetrates to the innermost part of a person, reaching the heart—the seat of feeling, awareness, and intention—so that its punishment is both utterly intense and deeply inward.

translation: Indeed, it will be closed over them.
interpretation: The punishment will completely enclose them, leaving them trapped with no escape or way out.

translation: In extended pillars.
interpretation: It depicts the people of the Fire enclosed within it by elongated pillars, emphasizing their complete confinement and inability to escape.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical reminder of the well-known event in which Allah thwarted the army that came with elephants to destroy the Kaaba, showing that His power protects His sacred signs and overcomes even the greatest forces.

translation: Has He not made their plot go astray?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical affirmation that God rendered the plot of those who sought to harm the Sacred House futile, causing their scheme to fail and leading it away from its intended outcome.

translation: And He sent against them flocks of birds, one after another.
interpretation: This portrays Allah’s intervention against the army that came to attack the Sacred House: He sent hosts of birds in successive groups, demonstrating that even the weakest of His creatures can defeat the mightiest forces by His command.

translation: It pelted them with stones of baked clay.
interpretation: This depicts God’s punishment striking the army through stones of hardened clay cast by the birds, rendering their power helpless before divine judgment.

translation: Then He made them like eaten-up straw.
interpretation: God reduced the invading army to utter ruin, leaving them as worthless and scattered as stalks of grain that have been chewed and discarded.

translation: For the accustomed security of Quraysh,
interpretation: Allah reminds Quraysh of the security and stability He had made familiar to them, particularly in their movements and dealings, so that they would recognize this as a divine favor deserving gratitude and worship.

translation: Their accustomed journeys in winter and summer,
interpretation: This refers to the Quraysh’s regular, secure trade journeys to Yemen in winter and Syria in summer—an enduring blessing that should lead them to recognize Allah’s care and worship Him alone.

translation: So let them worship the Lord of this House,
interpretation: This is a command that they devote their worship exclusively to Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of the Kaʿbah, acknowledging that all blessings and protection come from Him alone.

translation: Who fed them after hunger and granted them security from fear.
interpretation: This verse reminds people that sustenance and safety are divine blessings; therefore, they should recognize Allah’s favor with gratitude and devote themselves to Him alone.

translation: Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment?
interpretation: This is a rhetorical question exposing the moral blindness of the person who rejects accountability before God: such denial is not merely an idea, but a corruption that will appear in the way one treats others and neglects their rights.

translation: That is the one who repulses the orphan.
interpretation: It describes a person whose hardness and lack of compassion lead him to drive away, mistreat, or neglect the orphan instead of protecting and honoring one who is vulnerable.

translation: And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This condemns the person who shows no concern for those in need and neither provides for them nor inspires others to do so, revealing a hard-hearted disregard for social responsibility.

translation: So woe to those who pray,
interpretation: This is a warning that merely performing the outward form of prayer does not suffice when it is accompanied by heedlessness, insincerity, or neglect of its true purpose and obligations.

translation: Those who are heedless of their prayer,
interpretation: This describes people who treat prayer carelessly—neglecting it, delaying it, or performing it without genuine attentiveness and devotion.

translation: Those who act to be seen by others.
interpretation: It refers to people whose acts of worship or goodness are motivated by seeking admiration and recognition from others rather than sincerity toward Allah.

translation: And they withhold the simplest acts of kindness.
interpretation: This condemns those who lack sincere faith and compassion, refusing even minor forms of help or shared benefit that people ordinarily offer one another.

translation: Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar.
interpretation: God assures the Prophet Muhammad that He has bestowed upon him an immeasurable abundance of goodness, honor, blessing, and lasting favor; al-Kawthar also refers to the special river granted to him in Paradise.

translation: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.
interpretation: Devote your worship exclusively to your Lord, expressing gratitude for His blessings through sincere prayer and sacrifice offered only for His sake.

translation: Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off.
interpretation: Allah assures the Prophet that those who despise and oppose him will ultimately be deprived of lasting goodness, honor, and true significance, while his message and remembrance will endure.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say: O disbelievers,
interpretation: Allah commands the Prophet to address those who reject faith openly and directly, establishing that the truth of Islam should not be obscured or compromised by fear of opposition.

translation: I do not worship what you worship.
interpretation: This is a clear declaration of disavowal from worshipping anything besides Allah, rejecting the beliefs and practices of those who associate partners with Him.

translation: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This declares that the beliefs and acts of worship of the disbelievers are fundamentally incompatible with the worship devoted exclusively to Allah, leaving no genuine basis for religious compromise between the two paths.

translation: Nor will I worship what you worship.
interpretation: The Prophet firmly disavows the worship of anything besides Allah, declaring that his devotion cannot be combined with or compromised by the polytheistic worship of others.

translation: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This declares that the worship offered by the believers and the worship offered by the disbelievers are fundamentally incompatible: Allah alone is worshipped with sincere devotion, whereas the other worship is directed elsewhere or mixed with false beliefs, so the two paths cannot be combined.

translation: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.
interpretation: This verse establishes a clear separation between the path of faith chosen by the disbelievers and the worship and belief devoted to Allah. It rejects compromise in matters of worship while affirming that each party bears responsibility for its own religious choice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. When the help of Allah and the victory come,
interpretation: This announces that Allah’s support and the decisive victory He has promised will arrive at the appointed time, establishing the truth and bringing the believers’ struggle to fulfillment.

translation: And you see people entering Allah’s religion in multitudes.
interpretation: This portrays the widespread acceptance of Islam in groups after Allah grants victory, showing that guidance and success come by His support rather than human power alone.

translation: So glorify your Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever accepting of repentance.
interpretation: After witnessing the fulfillment of God’s help and the spread of His religion, the believer is instructed to respond with praise and humility rather than pride, seeking forgiveness for any shortcomings; God continually welcomes those who turn back to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and perish he.
interpretation: This is a divine declaration of Abū Lahab’s ruin: his “hands” signify his power, efforts, and deeds, all of which were doomed to fail because of his persistent hostility toward the truth and his opposition to the Messenger of Allah. The repetition intensifies the certainty and completeness of his destruction.

translation: His wealth and whatever he has earned will not benefit him.
interpretation: Neither his riches nor the gains he accumulated can protect him from God’s judgment or save him from the consequences of his wrongdoing.

translation: He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.
interpretation: This portrays the severe punishment awaiting one who persists in defiance of God, with the blazing fire expressing the intensity and inescapability of that punishment.

translation: And his wife, the carrier of firewood.
interpretation: His wife is portrayed as one who actively supported his hostility and intensified harm against the Prophet, likened to someone gathering fuel to feed the fire of persecution.

translation: Around her neck is a rope of twisted fiber.
interpretation: This portrays the humiliation and punishment awaiting Abū Lahab’s wife: the very adornment and means of harm associated with her are transformed into a binding rope of harsh, twisted fiber around her neck.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say: He is Allah, the One.
interpretation: Allah is uniquely one in His essence, divinity, and perfection; He has no partner, equal, or rival, and worship belongs to Him alone.

translation: Allah is the One upon whom all depend.
interpretation: Allah is perfectly self-sufficient and everlasting, while every created being relies upon Him for existence, provision, and the fulfillment of its needs.

translation: He neither begets nor is born.
interpretation: Allah is utterly unlike His creation: He has no child, parent, lineage, or origin, for He is eternally self-existent and independent.

translation: And there is none comparable to Him.
interpretation: Nothing resembles Allah or equals Him in His essence, attributes, or authority; He is utterly unique and beyond comparison.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say: “I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak.”
interpretation: This verse teaches that protection from every form of visible and hidden harm is sought from Allah alone, the Lord who brings light out of darkness and relief out of hardship.

translation: From the evil of what He has created.
interpretation: This is a prayer for protection from every harm that may arise from any created thing, while recognizing that creation itself belongs to God and that its harmful effects occur only by His permission.

translation: And from the evil of the night when it settles.
interpretation: This is a plea for Allah’s protection from the dangers and harms that may emerge or intensify under the cover of darkness, when what is hidden becomes difficult to perceive.

translation: And from the evil of those who blow upon knots,
interpretation: This is a supplication seeking Allah’s protection from the harm of sorcery and occult practices in which spells are cast through blowing upon tied knots.

translation: And from the evil of an envier when he envies.
interpretation: This is a prayer for protection from the harm that may arise when envy moves beyond an inward feeling and leads a person to act—through hostility, plotting, or attempts to deprive others of their blessings.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Say, “I seek refuge in the Lord of humankind,”
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet—and every believer through him—to turn directly to Allah as the ultimate protector and caretaker of all people, seeking His shelter from every harm, fear, and source of evil.

translation: King of mankind
interpretation: Allah alone possesses absolute sovereignty and authority over all human beings, who depend on Him and are subject to His command.

translation: The God of mankind,
interpretation: Allah is the true Lord and sovereign of all people, to whom humanity belongs and whom it must worship alone.

translation: From the evil of the retreating whisperer.
interpretation: This is a plea for protection from the hidden source of harmful thoughts that insinuates doubt, temptation, and anxiety into a person’s heart, then withdraws when God is remembered.

translation: Who whispers into the hearts of people,
interpretation: It refers to the subtle whisperer who secretly plants doubts, harmful impulses, and thoughts of disobedience within people, seeking to turn them away from truth and righteousness.

translation: From among the jinn and mankind.
interpretation: The evil whisperer may be from either the unseen jinn or human beings who incite others toward doubt, disobedience, and evil.
